Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song to the LORD, saying: "I will sing to the LORD, for He has triumphed gloriously; horse and rider He has hurled into the sea.
The LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation. This is my God, and I will extol Him; my father's God, and I will exalt Him.
The LORD is a warrior; the LORD is His name.
"Pharaoh's chariots and his army He has cast into the sea, and his elite officers have been drowned in the Red Sea.
The depths have covered them; they sank to the bottom like a stone.
Your right hand, O the LORD, is majestic in power; Your right hand, O the LORD, has shattered the enemy.
In the abundance of Your majesty You overthrow those who rise against You; You unleash Your fierce wrath, and it consumes them like stubble.
At the blast of Your nostrils the waters piled up; the floods stood firm like a wall; the depths congealed in the heart of the sea.
"The enemy said, 'I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoils; my appetite shall be sated with them; I will draw my sword; my hand shall destroy them.'
You blew with Your wind; the sea covered them; they sank like lead in the mighty waters.
Who is like You among the gods, O the LORD? Who is like You—majestic in holiness, awesome in praises, working wonders?
You stretched out Your right hand; the earth swallowed them.
In Your steadfast love You have led the people whom You have redeemed; in Your strength You have guided them to Your holy habitation.
The peoples have heard; they tremble; anguish has seized the inhabitants of Philistia.
Then the chiefs of Edom are dismayed; trembling seizes the leaders of Moab; all the inhabitants of Canaan melt away.
Terror and dread fall upon them; by the greatness of Your arm they are still as stone, until Your people pass by, O the LORD, until the people pass by whom You have purchased.
You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of Your inheritance, in the place, O the LORD, that You have made for Your dwelling, in the sanctuary, O Lord, that Your hands have established.
The LORD will reign forever and ever."
For Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and horsemen went into the sea, and the LORD brought the waters of the sea back upon them; but the Israelites walked on dry ground through the midst of the sea.
Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron's sister, took a tambourine in her hand, and all the women went out after her with tambourines and dancing.
And Miriam answered them, "Sing to the LORD, for He has triumphed gloriously; horse and rider He has hurled into the sea."
Then Moses led Israel onward from the Red Sea, and they went out into the Wilderness of Shur; they traveled three days in the wilderness and found no water.
When they came to Marah, they could not drink the water, for it was bitter; therefore its name was called Marah.
And the people grumbled against Moses, saying, "What shall we drink?"
And he cried to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a tree; he cast it into the waters, and the waters became sweet. There He made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there He tested them.

And He said, "If you will diligently listen to the voice of the LORD your God, and do what is right in His eyes, and give ear to His commandments, and keep all His statutes, I will put none of the diseases upon you that I put upon the Egyptians; for I am the LORD who heals you."
Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they encamped there by the waters.
On the fifteenth day of the second month following their exodus from Egypt, the entire congregation of Israel journeyed from Elim and entered the wilderness of Sin, situated between Elim and Sinai.
There, in the desert, the whole congregation murmured against Moses and Aaron,

and the Israelites said to them, "If only we had perished by the hand of the the LORD in Egypt, where we sat beside the fleshpots and ate bread to satiety; for you have brought us into this wilderness to exterminate this whole assembly by famine."

Then the the LORD said to Moses, "Behold, I am about to rain bread from heaven for you, and the people shall go out and gather a day's portion each day, that I may test them, whether they will walk in My law or not.
On the sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, it shall be twice as much as they gather daily."
So Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, "This evening you will know that the the LORD brought you out of the land of Egypt,
and in the morning you will behold the glory of the the LORD, because He has heard your grumbling against Him. For what are we, that you should grumble against us?"

Moses added, "When the the LORD gives you meat to eat in the evening and bread to satiety in the morning, because He has heard your grumbling against Him—what are we? Your grumbling is not against us but against the the LORD."
Then Moses said to Aaron, "Say to the whole congregation of the Israelites, 'Draw near before the the LORD, for He has heard your grumbling.'"
As Aaron addressed the whole congregation, they turned toward the wilderness, and behold, the glory of the the LORD appeared in the cloud.

And the the LORD spoke to Moses, saying, "I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites. Say to them, 'At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread. Then you will know that I am the the LORD your God.'"
In the evening quail ascended and covered the camp, and in the morning a layer of dew lay around the camp.
When the layer of dew evaporated, there upon the surface of the wilderness was a fine, flaky substance, as fine as frost upon the ground.
When the Israelites saw it, they said to one another, "What is it?"—for they did not know what it was. Moses said to them, "It is the bread that the the LORD has given you to eat."

Moses continued, "This is what the the LORD has commanded: 'Gather of it, each according to his eating—an omer for each person, according to the number of your people; let each take for those in his tent.'"
The Israelites did so, and they gathered, some more and some less.
When they measured it by the omer, the one who gathered much had no surplus, and the one who gathered little had no deficit; each had gathered according to his eating.
Moses said to them, "No one is to leave any of it until morning."
But they did not listen to Moses; some left part of it until morning, and it bred worms and became malodorous. So Moses was incensed with them.
Morning by morning they gathered it, each according to his eating; and when the sun grew hot, it melted.
On the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread—two omers for each person—and all the leaders of the congregation came and reported to Moses.

He said to them, "This is what the the LORD has said: 'Tomorrow is a Sabbath rest, a holy Sabbath to the the LORD. Bake what you will bake and boil what you will boil, and lay aside all that remains to be kept until morning.'"
So they laid it aside until morning, as Moses had commanded, and it did not become malodorous, nor were there worms in it.
Moses said, "Eat it today, for today is a Sabbath to the the LORD; today you will not find it in the field.
Six days you shall gather it, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there will be none."
Nevertheless, some of the people went out on the seventh day to gather, but they found none.
And the the LORD said to Moses, "How long will you refuse to keep My commandments and My laws?
See, the the LORD has given you the Sabbath; therefore on the sixth day He gives you bread for two days. Let each of you remain in his place; let no one go out of his place on the seventh day."
So the people rested on the seventh day.
The house of Israel called its name manna. It was like coriander seed, white, and its taste was like wafers made with honey.

Moses said, "This is what the the LORD has commanded: 'Keep an omer of it throughout your generations, so that they may see the bread with which I fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.'"
And Moses said to Aaron, "Take a jar, and put an omer of manna in it, and place it before the the LORD to be kept throughout your generations."
As the the LORD commanded Moses, so Aaron placed it before the testimony to be kept.
The Israelites ate the manna forty years, until they came to an inhabited land; they ate the manna until they reached the border of the land of Canaan.
Now an omer is a tenth of an ephah.

The entire congregation of the Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sin, journeying by stages in accordance with the command of the LORD, and encamped at Rephidim, where no water was available for the people to drink.

Consequently, the people entered into contention with Moses, demanding, “Provide us with water, that we may drink.” Moses answered them, “Why do you contend with me? Why do you put the LORD to the test?”
The people, parched with thirst in that place, murmured against Moses and said, “Why have you brought us up from Egypt, only to put me, my children, and my livestock to death by thirst?”
Moses cried out to the LORD, “What shall I do with this people? They are scarcely a step from stoning me.”
The LORD said to Moses, “Go on ahead of the people, taking with you some of the elders of Israel, and carry in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile; then proceed.”

The LORD said, “Behold, I will stand before you there on the rock at Horeb; strike the rock, and water shall flow from it, that the people may drink.” Moses did so in the presence of the elders of Israel.
He named that place Massah and Meribah, on account of the contention of the Israelites and their testing of the LORD, when they said, “Is the LORD among us, or not?”
Then Amalek came and waged war against Israel at Rephidim.
Moses said to Joshua, “Select men for us and go out to engage Amalek in battle. Tomorrow I will take my stand on the hilltop, the staff of God in my hand.”
Joshua did as Moses had instructed him and fought against Amalek, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the summit of the hill.
So it was that whenever Moses lifted his hand, Israel prevailed, and whenever he lowered his hand, Amalek prevailed.
But when Moses' hands became weary, they took a stone and set it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur upheld his hands, one on either side, so that his hands remained firm until sunset.
Joshua overwhelmed Amalek and his people by the sword.
The LORD said to Moses, “Inscribe this in a book as a memorial, and recite it in Joshua's hearing, for I will utterly efface the memory of Amalek from beneath the heavens.”
Moses then built an altar and called its name, “The LORD is my banner.”
Moses said, “Because a hand has been raised against the throne of the LORD, the LORD will make war upon Amalek from generation to generation.”
Now Jethro, the priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law, had heard of all that God had accomplished for Moses and for His people Israel, and of how the LORD had extricated Israel from Egypt.
After Moses had dismissed his wife Zipporah, his father-in-law Jethro received her and her two sons.
One was named Gershom, for Moses had declared, "I have been a sojourner in an alien land."
The other was named Eliezer, for Moses had declared, "My father's God was my helper; He rescued me from Pharaoh's sword."
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, together with Moses' wife and sons, came to him in the wilderness, where he was encamped at the mountain of God.
He sent word to Moses: "I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you, along with your wife and her two sons."
So Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, bowed in reverence, and kissed him; they exchanged greetings and entered the tent.

Then Moses recounted to his father-in-law all that the LORD had done to Pharaoh and to Egypt on Israel's behalf, together with all the tribulation they had encountered along the journey, and how the LORD had delivered them.
And Jethro rejoiced over all the good that the LORD had done for Israel, whom He had rescued from the power of the Egyptians.
Jethro declared, "Blessed be the LORD, who has delivered you from the power of the Egyptians and from the power of Pharaoh, and who has delivered the people from under the power of the Egyptians.
Now I know that the LORD is greater than all other gods, for He prevailed in the very matter in which they had acted with insolent pride against them."
Then Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God, and Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to partake of a meal with Moses' father-in-law in the presence of God.
The next day Moses took his seat to judge the people, and they stood around him from morning until evening.

When his father-in-law saw all that he was doing for the people, he asked, "What is this you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone, while all the people stand around you from morning until evening?"
Moses answered his father-in-law, "Because the people come to me to seek God's will.
Whenever they have a dispute, it is brought to me, and I decide between the parties and make known to them God's statutes and laws."
Moses' father-in-law replied, "What you are doing is not good.
You and these people who come to you will surely exhaust yourselves, for the matter is too heavy for you. You cannot handle it alone.
"Listen to me; I will give you counsel, and God will be with you. You must be the people's representative before God and bring their disputes to Him.
Teach them the statutes and laws, and show them the path they are to walk and the work they are to perform.
But select capable men from all the people—men who fear God, trustworthy men who hate dishonest gain—and appoint them over the people as officials over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.

"Let them judge the people at all times. Let them bring every major case to you, but let them decide every minor case themselves. In this way they will lighten your load, and they will share it with you.
If you do this, and God so commands you, you will be able to endure, and all these people will return to their homes in peace."
So Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said.
Moses chose capable men from all Israel and made them leaders of the people, officials over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
And they judged the people at all times; they brought the hard cases to Moses, but they judged every minor case themselves.
Then Moses sent his father-in-law on his way, and he returned to his own land.
In the third month after the Israelites' exodus from the land of Egypt—on that very day—they entered the wilderness of Sinai.
Upon departing Rephidim, they came into the wilderness of Sinai and encamped there in the wilderness, opposite the mountain.
Moses ascended to God, and the LORD summoned him from the mountain, saying, "Thus you shall say to the house of Jacob and declare to the sons of Israel:
'You yourselves have witnessed what I wrought upon Egypt, and how I bore you aloft with swift and sheltering deliverance and brought you to Myself.
Now therefore, if you will indeed hearken to My voice and keep My covenant, you shall be My treasured possession among all peoples, for all the earth is Mine.
And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.' These are the words that you shall speak to the Israelites."
So Moses came and summoned the elders of the people, and laid before them all these words that the LORD had enjoined upon him.
And all the people responded in unison, saying, "All that the LORD has spoken we will perform." And Moses conveyed the people's words back to the LORD.

The LORD said to Moses, "Behold, I am about to come to you in a dense cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you, and may also repose enduring trust in you." And Moses reported to the LORD the words of the people.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go to the people and sanctify them today and tomorrow, and let them launder their garments,
and let them be prepared for the third day; for on the third day the LORD will descend upon Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.

And you shall demarcate boundaries for the people round about, saying, 'Take care that you do not ascend the mountain or touch its extremity. Whoever touches the mountain shall assuredly be put to death.

No hand shall touch him, but he shall assuredly be stoned or transfixed with arrows; whether human or beast, he shall not survive. When the trumpet emits a prolonged blast, they may ascend the mountain.'"
So Moses descended from the mountain to the people and sanctified the people, and they laundered their garments.
And he said to the people, "Be prepared for the three days; abstain from sexual relations."
On the third day, at daybreak, there were thunderings and lightnings, and a heavy cloud upon the mountain, and an exceedingly loud trumpet blast, so that all the people in the camp quaked.
Then Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God, and they stationed themselves at the foot of the mountain.
Mount Sinai was altogether enveloped in smoke because the LORD had descended upon it in fire; its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked violently.
And as the trumpet's sound waxed louder and louder, Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
The LORD descended to the summit of Mount Sinai, and the LORD summoned Moses to the summit, and Moses ascended.
And the LORD said to Moses, "Descend and admonish the people, lest they break through to the LORD to gaze, and many of them perish.
Let the priests also, who draw near to the LORD, sanctify themselves, lest the LORD erupt against them."
And Moses said to the LORD, "The people cannot ascend Mount Sinai, for You Yourself admonished us, saying, 'Set boundaries around the mountain and sanctify it.'"
And the LORD said to him, "Go, descend; then you shall ascend, you and Aaron with you; but let not the priests and the people break through to ascend to the LORD, lest He erupt against them."
So Moses descended to the people and addressed them.
Then God spoke all these words, saying:
“I am the LORD, your God, who brought you forth from the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
You shall have no other gods besides Me.
You shall not fashion for yourself a carved image, or any likeness of anything in the heavens above, on the earth beneath, or in the waters under the earth.

You shall not bow down to them, nor render them service, for I, the LORD, your God, am a jealous God, punishing the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate Me,
but showing steadfast love to thousands—to those who love Me and keep My commandments.
You shall not misuse the name of the LORD, your God, for the LORD will not hold guiltless whoever misuses His name.
“Remember the Sabbath day, so as to hallow it.
Six days you shall labor and accomplish all your work,

but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD, your God; on it you shall perform no labor—neither you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your livestock, nor the sojourner residing within your gates.
For in six days the LORD fashioned the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that fills them, and He rested on the seventh day; therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and sanctified it.
“Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be prolonged in the land that the LORD, your God, is bestowing upon you.
You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor.
You shall not covet your neighbor’s house; you shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, or his male servant, or his female servant, or his ox, or his donkey, or anything belonging to your neighbor.”
All the people witnessed the thunder and the lightning, the sound of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking; and the people, seeing it, trembled with fear and stood at a distance.
They said to Moses, “You speak to us, and we will heed; but let not God speak to us, lest we perish.”
Moses said to the people, “Do not be afraid, for God has come to test you, so that the fear of Him may remain before you, and that you may not sin.”
The people remained at a distance, while Moses approached the thick darkness where God was.
Then the LORD said to Moses, “Thus you shall say to the Israelites: ‘You have seen that I have spoken with you from heaven.
You shall not make other gods alongside Me; gods of silver or gold you shall not make for yourselves.

An altar of earth you shall make for Me, and upon it you shall sacrifice your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your sheep and your oxen. In every place where I cause My name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
If you make an altar of stone for Me, you shall not build it of hewn stone, for if you wield your tool upon it, you profane it.
Nor shall you ascend to My altar by steps, lest your nakedness be exposed upon it.’”
These are the ordinances that you shall set before them.
If you acquire a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years, and in the seventh year he shall go out free, without payment.
If he entered alone, he shall go out alone; if he was married, his wife shall go out with him.
If his master gives him a wife, and she bears him sons or daughters, the woman and her children shall belong to their master, and he shall go out alone.
But if the servant declares, “I love my master, my wife, and my children; I do not wish to go free,”
then his master shall bring him before the judges, and he shall bring him to the door or to the doorpost and bore his ear with an awl; thereafter he shall serve his master in perpetuity.
If a man sells his daughter as a maidservant, she shall not go out as the male servants go out.

If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master, who has designated her for himself, he shall let her be redeemed; he shall have no authority to sell her to a foreign people, because he has dealt treacherously with her.
If he designates her for his son, he shall deal with her according to the ordinance for daughters.
If he takes another wife for himself, he shall not diminish her food, her clothing, or her conjugal rights.
If he does not provide her with these three things, she shall go out free, without money.
Whoever strikes a man so that he dies shall surely be put to death.
But if he did not lie in wait, and God caused the man to fall into his hand, then I will appoint for you a place to which he may flee.
But if a man acts with premeditation against his neighbor, to kill him by treachery, he shall be taken from My altar to be put to death.
Whoever strikes his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
Whoever kidnaps a man and sells him, or if the kidnapped man is found in his possession, shall surely be put to death.
Whoever curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
If men quarrel, and one strikes his neighbor with a stone or with his fist, and the man does not die but is confined to bed,
then, if he rises again and walks about outside with his staff, the striker shall be absolved; nevertheless, he shall compensate the injured man for his lost time and provide for his healing.
If a man strikes his male or female servant with a rod, and the servant dies under his hand, vengeance shall surely be taken.
However, if the servant survives a day or two, the owner shall not be punished, because the servant is his property.

If men who are fighting strike a pregnant woman and her children come forth, but there is no injury, the offender shall surely be fined, according to what the woman's husband imposes upon him and as the judges determine.
But if there is an injury, then you shall give life for life,
eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
If a man strikes the eye of his male or female servant and destroys it, he shall send the servant away free in compensation for the eye.
If he knocks out a tooth of his male or female servant, he shall send the servant away free in compensation for the tooth.
If an ox gores a man or a woman to death, the ox shall surely be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the ox shall be acquitted.

If the ox has been accustomed to gore in the past, and its owner has been warned, yet he does not restrain it, and it kills a man or a woman, then the ox shall be stoned and its owner shall also be put to death.
If, however, a ransom is imposed upon him, he shall pay whatever is demanded for the redemption of his life.
Whether the ox gores a son or a daughter, it shall be done to him according to this same ordinance.
If the ox gores a male or female servant, the owner shall give thirty shekels of silver to his master, and the ox shall be stoned.
If a man opens or digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
the owner of the pit shall make restitution; he shall give money to the owner of the animal, and the dead animal shall be his.
If one man's ox injures another man's ox so that it dies, they shall sell the living ox and divide the proceeds, and they shall also divide the dead ox.
But if it was known that the ox had a habit of goring in the past, and its owner did not restrain it, he shall pay ox for ox, and the dead ox shall be his.
Should a man purloin an ox or a sheep and thereafter either slaughter or vend it, he must recompense five head of cattle for the ox and four sheep for the sheep.
If a thief is apprehended in the act of breaking in and is struck down so that he dies, no bloodguilt attaches to the one who struck him.
Yet if the sun has risen upon him, bloodguilt attaches to the slayer; the thief must make full restitution, and should he possess nothing, he himself shall be sold to answer for his theft.
If the stolen property is discovered alive in his possession—whether ox, donkey, or sheep—he shall restore twofold.

If a man permits his livestock to graze a field or vineyard and then lets them stray so that they feed in another's field, he must make restitution from the choicest produce of his own field and vineyard.
If a fire breaks out and spreads among thorns, consuming sheaves, standing grain, or an entire field, the one who kindled it must make full restitution.
If a man entrusts silver or goods to his neighbor for safekeeping, and they are stolen from that neighbor's house, the thief, if apprehended, shall repay twofold.
If the thief is not found, the owner of the house shall be brought before the judges, that it may be determined whether he has laid hands upon his neighbor's goods.

In every case of breach of trust—whether concerning an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost article about which someone asserts, "This is it"—both parties shall bring their dispute before the judges; the one whom the judges condemn must pay double to his neighbor.
If a man entrusts to his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any animal for safekeeping, and it dies, is injured, or is carried off, with no witness to the event,
then an oath by the LORD shall stand between them both, attesting that he has not misappropriated his neighbor's property; the owner shall accept that oath, and no restitution shall be exacted.
But if it was stolen from his keeping, he must make restitution to the owner.
If it was torn by beasts, he shall produce the carcass as evidence and shall not make restitution for the torn animal.
If a man borrows from his neighbor, and the thing is injured or dies while its owner is not present, he must make full restitution.
If the owner is present, no restitution is required; and if the animal was hired, its hire covers the loss.
If a man seduces a virgin who is not betrothed and lies with her, he must pay her bride-price and take her as his wife.
If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he shall pay silver equal to the bride-price of virgins.
You shall not permit a sorceress to live.
Whoever has sexual relations with an animal must surely be put to death.
Whoever sacrifices to any god other than the LORD alone shall be devoted to destruction.
You shall not wrong a sojourner, nor shall you oppress him, for you yourselves were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
You shall not afflict any widow or orphan.
If you do afflict them, and they cry out to Me, I will surely hear their cry.
Then My wrath will burn, and I will slay you with the sword, so that your wives become widows and your children fatherless.
If you lend money to any of My people among you who is poor, you shall not be to him as a creditor, nor shall you charge him interest.
If you ever take your neighbor's garment in pledge, you shall return it to him before the sun goes down.
For that is his only covering; it is his cloak for his body. In what, then, shall he sleep? And if he cries out to Me, I will hear, for I am gracious.
You shall not revile God, nor curse a ruler of your people.
You shall not delay to offer from the fullness of your harvest and from the outflow of your presses; the firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me.
Likewise you shall do with your oxen and with your sheep: seven days it shall be with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it to Me.
You shall be holy men to Me; therefore you shall not eat any flesh torn by beasts in the field; you shall cast it to the dogs.
“You must not propagate a false report, nor place your hand alongside the wicked to serve as a malicious witness.
You shall not follow a multitude into wrongdoing; and when you testify in a dispute, you must not turn aside so as to incline after the crowd.
Neither shall you show partiality to a poor person in his lawsuit.
“If you encounter your enemy’s ox or donkey wandering astray, you must surely return it to him.
If you see the donkey of one who hates you collapsed beneath its load, you must not abandon it to him; rather, you shall surely help him with it.
You shall not pervert the justice due to your poor in his lawsuit.
“Keep far from a false charge, and do not put the innocent and the righteous to death, for I will not acquit the guilty.
Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and subverts the words of the righteous.
Do not oppress a sojourner, for you know the soul of a sojourner, because you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
“For six years you shall sow your land and gather in its yield,

but in the seventh year you shall let it rest and lie fallow, so that the poor among your people may eat; and what they leave the beasts of the field may eat. You shall do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove.
Six days you shall do your work, but on the seventh day you shall rest, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the son of your maidservant and the sojourner may be refreshed.
“Be careful to observe all that I have said to you; do not invoke the names of other gods, and do not let them be heard upon your lips.
Three times a year you shall celebrate a feast to Me.

You shall keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread: as I commanded you, you shall eat unleavened bread for seven days at the appointed time in the month of Abib, because in it you came out of Egypt; and none shall appear before Me empty-handed.
And you shall keep the Feast of Harvest with the firstfruits of your labor, which you sow in the field, and the Feast of Ingathering at the year’s end, when you gather your produce from the field.
“Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Lord, the LORD.
You shall not offer the blood of My sacrifice with leavened bread, nor shall the fat of My feast remain until morning.
You shall bring the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God; and you must not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.
“Behold, I am sending an angel before you to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place that I have prepared.
Pay heed to him and obey his voice; do not rebel against him, for he will not forgive your transgressions, because My Name is in him.
But if you indeed obey his voice and do all that I speak, I will be an enemy to your enemies and an adversary to your adversaries.
For My angel shall go before you and bring you to the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, and I will annihilate them.
Do not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do as they do; rather, you shall utterly demolish them and shatter their sacred pillars.
“You shall serve the LORD your God, and He will bless your bread and your water, and I will remove sickness from your midst.
There shall be no miscarriage or barrenness in your land; I will fulfill the number of your days.
I will send My terror before you and destroy all the people among whom you come; I will make all your enemies turn their backs to you.
I will send the hornet before you to drive out the Hivites, the Canaanites, and the Hittites from before you.
“I will not drive them out before you in a single year, lest the land become desolate and the beasts of the field multiply against you.
Little by little I will drive them out before you, until you have increased and taken possession of the land.

I will set your border from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the Euphrates; for I will give the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you shall drive them out before you.
You shall not make a covenant with them or with their gods.
They must not dwell in your land, lest they cause you to sin against Me; for if you serve their gods, it will be a snare to you.”
Then He said to Moses, “Ascend to the the LORD, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel, and bow down at a distance.”
Moses alone is to draw near to the the LORD, but they shall not draw near, and the people shall not ascend with him.

So Moses came and recounted to the people all the words of the the LORD and all the ordinances; and all the people answered with one voice, saying, “All the words that the the LORD has spoken we will carry out.”
Then Moses wrote down all the words of the the LORD, and rising early in the morning, he erected an altar at the foot of the mountain, together with twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
He sent the young men of the Israelites, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed bulls as peace offerings to the the LORD.
Moses took half of the blood and set it in basins, and the remaining half he sprinkled upon the altar.
Then he took the Book of the Covenant and read it aloud in the hearing of the people; and they said, “All that the the LORD has spoken we will do, and we will heed.”
Moses took the blood and sprinkled it upon the people, and he said, “Behold, the blood of the covenant that the the LORD has made with you in regard to all these words.”
Then Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel went up.
And they beheld the God of Israel; and beneath His feet was something like a pavement of sapphire, as clear as the very heaven.
Yet He did not lay His hand upon the nobles of the Israelites; they saw God, and they ate and drank.

And the the LORD said to Moses, “Ascend to Me on the mountain and remain there, and I will give you the tablets of stone, and the law, and the commandment, which I have written, in order to instruct them.”
So Moses arose, with Joshua his attendant, and Moses went up to the mountain of God.
And to the elders he said, “Tarry here for us until we return to you; and behold, Aaron and Hur are with you. Whoever has a dispute, let him come near to them.”
Then Moses went up the mountain, and the cloud enveloped the mountain.
The glory of the the LORD dwelt upon Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days; and on the seventh day He called to Moses from within the cloud.
The appearance of the glory of the the LORD was like a consuming fire on the summit of the mountain in the sight of the Israelites.
Moses entered the midst of the cloud and ascended the mountain; and Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites, that they bring Me an offering; from every man whose heart moves him you shall take My offering.
And this is the offering that you shall take from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen and goats’ hair;
rams’ skins dyed red, goatskins, and acacia wood;
oil for the lamps, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
onyx stones and stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece.
And let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell in their midst.
According to all that I show you, the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its furnishings, so you shall make it.”
“And they shall make an ark of acacia wood: two and a half cubits shall be its length, a cubit and a half its width, and a cubit and a half its height.
And you shall overlay it with pure gold; inside and outside you shall overlay it, and you shall make upon it a molding of gold all around.
And you shall cast for it four rings of gold and set them upon its four feet, two rings on one side and two rings on the other side.
And you shall make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
And you shall put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark with them.
The poles shall remain in the rings of the ark; they shall not be removed from it.
And you shall put into the ark the testimony that I shall give you.
And you shall make a mercy seat of pure gold: two and a half cubits its length and a cubit and a half its width.
And you shall make two cherubim of gold; of hammered work you shall make them, at the two ends of the mercy seat.
And make one cherub at one end and one cherub at the other end; from the mercy seat you shall make the cherubim at its two ends.
And the cherubim shall stretch out their wings above, overshadowing the mercy seat with their wings, their faces one to another; toward the mercy seat shall be the faces of the cherubim.
And you shall put the mercy seat above upon the ark, and in the ark you shall put the testimony that I shall give you.

And there I will meet with you, and from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim that are upon the ark of the testimony, I will speak with you about all that I will command you for the Israelites.”
“And you shall make a table of acacia wood: two cubits its length, a cubit its width, and a cubit and a half its height.
And you shall overlay it with pure gold, and you shall make for it a molding of gold all around.
And you shall make for it a rim around it, a handbreadth wide, and you shall make a molding of gold for its rim all around.
And you shall make for it four rings of gold, and you shall put the rings on the four corners that are on its four feet.
Close to the rim shall be the rings, as holders for the poles to carry the table.
And you shall make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, and the table shall be carried with them.
And you shall make its plates, its dishes, its bowls, and its pitchers for pouring; of pure gold you shall make them.
And you shall set the bread of the Presence on the table before Me continually.”
“And you shall make a lampstand of pure gold; the lampstand shall be made of hammered work; its base, its shaft, its cups, its calyxes, and its flowers shall be of one piece with it.
And six branches shall go out from its sides: three branches of the lampstand from one side and three branches from the other side.

Three cups made like almond blossoms, each with calyx and flower, on one branch, and three cups made like almond blossoms, each with calyx and flower, on the other branch—so for the six branches going out from the lampstand.
And on the lampstand four cups made like almond blossoms, with their calyxes and their flowers.

And a calyx under two branches of one piece with it, and a calyx under two branches of one piece with it, and a calyx under two branches of one piece with it—for the six branches going out from the lampstand.
Their calyxes and their branches shall be of one piece with it, all of it one hammered piece of pure gold.
And you shall make its seven lamps, and you shall set up its lamps so that they give light in front of it.
And its tongs and its trays shall be of pure gold.
It shall be made, with all these utensils, from a talent of pure gold.
And see that you make them according to the pattern that was shown to you on the mountain.”
You shall make the tabernacle of ten curtains of finely twisted linen, interwoven with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and embroidered with cherubim by the hand of a skilled artisan.
Each curtain shall measure twenty-eight cubits in length and four cubits in breadth, every curtain being of one identical measure.
Five curtains shall be joined together, edge to edge, and five curtains joined together in like manner.

You shall make loops of blue yarn along the edge of the outermost curtain in the first set, at the place of joining, and you shall make corresponding loops along the edge of the outermost curtain in the second set.
You shall make fifty loops upon the one curtain and fifty upon the edge of the curtain in the second set, the loops being disposed opposite one another.
You shall make fifty clasps of gold and join the curtains to one another by means of the clasps, so that the tabernacle becomes a single whole.
You shall make eleven curtains of goats' hair for a tent over the tabernacle.
The length of each curtain shall be thirty cubits, and its breadth four cubits; one measure shall obtain for all eleven curtains.
You shall join five curtains together by themselves, and six together by themselves, and you shall double over the sixth curtain at the front of the tent.
You shall make fifty loops on the edge of the outermost curtain in the first set, and fifty on the edge of the curtain in the second set.
You shall make fifty clasps of bronze, insert the clasps into the loops, and join the tent together so that it becomes one.
The surplus half-curtain of the tent covering shall hang over the rear of the tabernacle.
A cubit on this side and a cubit on that side of the overhanging length shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle, on this side and on that, to cover it.
You shall make a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and above it a covering of fine leather.
You shall make upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
Each frame shall be ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
Each frame shall possess two tenons, fitted together one to the other; you shall make them thus for every frame of the tabernacle.
You shall make twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle.
You shall make forty silver bases beneath the twenty frames: two bases beneath each frame for its two tenons.
For the second side, toward the north, there shall be twenty frames.
Their forty silver bases shall be two beneath each frame.
For the rear of the tabernacle, toward the west, you shall make six frames.
You shall make two frames for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear.
They shall be twinned below and joined together at the top by one ring; so shall it be for both corners.
Thus there shall be eight frames, with sixteen silver bases, two bases beneath each frame.
You shall make five bars of acacia wood for the frames of one side of the tabernacle.
Five bars for the frames of the second side, and five for the frames of the rear toward the west.
The middle bar shall run through the midst of the frames from end to end.
You shall overlay the frames with gold, fashion gold rings to receive the bars, and overlay the bars with gold.
You shall erect the tabernacle according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain.
You shall make a veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, with cherubim skillfully worked into it.
You shall hang it upon four pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold, whose hooks are of gold, standing upon four bases of silver.
You shall hang the veil beneath the clasps and bring the ark of the Testimony there behind the veil; the veil shall separate for you the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.
You shall put the mercy seat upon the ark of the Testimony in the Most Holy Place.
You shall set the table outside the veil on the north side of the tabernacle, and you shall place the lampstand opposite the table on the south side.
You shall make a screen for the entrance of the tent of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer.
You shall make five pillars of acacia wood for the screen, overlay them with gold, fashion their hooks of gold, and cast five bases of bronze for them.
You shall fabricate the altar of acacia timber: the altar shall be square, five cubits in length and five cubits in breadth, and three cubits in height.
You shall fashion its horns upon its four corners; its horns shall be of one piece with it, and you shall overlay it with bronze.
You shall make all its utensils of bronze: its pots for clearing ashes, its shovels, its basins, its flesh-hooks, and its firepans.
You shall make for it a grating, a network of bronze; and upon the four corners of the grating you shall make four bronze rings.
You shall set it beneath the ledge of the altar, so that the netting extends halfway up the altar.
You shall make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with bronze.
Its poles shall be inserted into the rings, so that the poles rest upon the two sides of the altar when it is borne.
You shall fashion it hollow, of planks; as He revealed it to you upon the mountain, so shall it be made.
You shall make the court of the tabernacle: for the south side, southward, the hangings of the court shall be of fine twisted linen, one hundred cubits in length for that side.
Its twenty pillars and their twenty bases shall be of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands shall be of silver.
Likewise for the north side in length: hangings one hundred cubits long, with twenty pillars and twenty bronze bases; the hooks of the pillars and their bands shall be of silver.
For the west side, the hangings of the court shall be fifty cubits in width, with ten pillars and ten bases.
The width of the court on the east side, toward the sunrise, shall be fifty cubits.
The hangings on one side of the gate shall be fifteen cubits, with three pillars and three bases.
And on the other side, hangings of fifteen cubits, with three pillars and three bases.
For the gate of the court there shall be a screen of twenty cubits, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer, with four pillars and four bases.
All the pillars around the court shall be connected with silver; their hooks shall be of silver, and their bases of bronze.
The length of the court shall be one hundred cubits, and the breadth fifty cubits, and the height five cubits, of fine twisted linen, with bases of bronze.
All the utensils of the tabernacle for all its service, and all its tent pegs, and all the pegs of the court, shall be of bronze.
You shall command the children of Israel that they bring to you clear oil of beaten olives for the light, to cause the lamp to burn continually.

In the tent of meeting, outside the veil that is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall tend it from evening to morning before the LORD; it shall be a perpetual statute for their generations among the children of Israel.
You shall bring near unto you your brother Aaron, together with his sons from among the Israelites—Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar—that they may minister to Me as priests.
You shall fashion holy garments for your brother Aaron, garments of glory and beauty.
You shall speak unto all the wise-hearted whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, that they may fashion Aaron’s garments to consecrate him for ministry unto Me.

These are the garments they shall fashion: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a checkered tunic, a turban, and a sash. They shall fashion holy garments for Aaron your brother and for his sons, that they may serve Me as priests.
They shall take gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, together with fine linen.
You shall fashion the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen, the work of a skillful artisan.
It shall possess two shoulder pieces joined to its two ends, and it shall be joined together.
The skillfully woven waistband that is upon it shall be of one workmanship with it—of gold, blue, purple, scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen.
You shall take two onyx stones and engrave upon them the names of the sons of Israel:
six of their names upon one stone, and the remaining six names upon the other, according to their births.
As the work of a stone engraver, like the engravings of a signet, you shall engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Israel; you shall set them in settings of gold.

You shall put the two stones upon the shoulder pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the sons of Israel, and Aaron shall bear their names before the LORD upon his two shoulders for a remembrance.
You shall make settings of gold,
and two chains of pure gold, twisted like cords, and you shall attach the chains to the settings.
You shall make a breastpiece of judgment, the work of a skillful artisan; like the work of the ephod you shall make it, of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen.
It shall be square and doubled, a span in length and a span in width.
You shall set in it a mounting of stones, four rows of stones: the first row a sardius, a topaz, and an emerald;
the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;
the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
and the fourth row a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. They shall be set in gold settings.
The stones shall be twelve, according to the names of the sons of Israel, each like the engraving of a signet, each according to its name, for the twelve tribes.
You shall make on the breastpiece chains like cords, of pure gold, twisted.
You shall make two gold rings for the breastpiece and put them on the two ends of the breastpiece.
You shall put the two gold chains on the two rings at the ends of the breastpiece.
You shall attach the two ends of the chains to the two settings and put them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
You shall make two gold rings and put them on the two ends of the breastpiece, on the edge toward the ephod.
You shall make two gold rings and put them below on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, toward the front, corresponding to its seam, above the waistband of the ephod.
They shall bind the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it may rest on the waistband of the ephod and not swing away from the ephod.
Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel on the breastpiece of judgment over his heart when he enters the holy place, for a remembrance before the LORD continually.

You shall put the Urim and the Thummim into the breastpiece of judgment, and they shall be over Aaron’s heart when he goes before the LORD. Aaron shall bear the judgment of the sons of Israel over his heart before the LORD continually.
You shall make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue.
It shall have an opening for the head in the middle; around the opening there shall be a binding like the neck of a garment, woven, so that it does not tear.
You shall make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet upon its hem all around, and gold bells between them all around.
A gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe.
It shall be upon Aaron when he ministers, and its sound shall be heard when he enters and exits the sanctuary before the LORD, so that he does not die.
You shall make a plate of pure gold and engrave upon it, like the engraving of a signet, “Holy to the LORD.”
You shall put it on a blue cord and set it upon the turban, at the front of the turban.

It shall be upon Aaron’s forehead, and Aaron shall bear the iniquity of the holy things that the Israelites consecrate, all their holy gifts; and it shall be upon his forehead continually, for acceptance before the LORD.
You shall weave the tunic of fine linen and make the turban of fine linen, and you shall make the sash, the work of an embroiderer.
For Aaron’s sons you shall make tunics, sashes, and caps, for glory and for beauty.
You shall clothe Aaron your brother and his sons with him, and you shall anoint them, ordain them, and consecrate them, that they may serve Me as priests.
You shall make linen undergarments to cover the flesh of their nakedness; they shall extend from the hips to the thighs.

They shall be upon Aaron and his sons when they enter the tent of meeting or approach the altar to minister in the holy place, so that they do not bear iniquity and die. It is a statute forever for him and for his descendants.
This is what you are to do to consecrate them, so that they may serve Me as priests: Take a young bull and two rams without blemish,
together with unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil. You shall make them from fine wheat flour,
and you shall put them in a basket and present them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams. “
Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.
Take the garments and dress Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastpiece, fastening the ephod with its woven waistband.
Put the turban on his head and attach the holy crown to the turban.
Then take the anointing oil and pour it on his head to anoint him.
Bring his sons and dress them in tunics.
Wrap the sashes around Aaron and his sons, put headbands on them, and ordain them in this manner; the priesthood shall be theirs by a perpetual statute. Thus you shall ordain Aaron and his sons. “
Bring the bull to the front of the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.
You shall slaughter the bull before the LORD at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
Take some of the blood of the bull and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger; then pour out all the remaining blood at the base of the altar.
Take all the fat that covers the entrails, the lobe of the liver, both kidneys and the fat on them, and burn them on the altar.
But burn the flesh of the bull, its hide, and its dung outside the camp; it is a sin offering. “
Take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.
Slaughter the ram and take its blood and sprinkle it on all sides of the altar.
Cut the ram into pieces, wash its entrails and legs, and place them with its head and the other pieces.
Burn the entire ram on the altar. It is a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD. “
Take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.

Slaughter the ram, take some of its blood, and put it on the right earlobes of Aaron and his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Then sprinkle the blood on all sides of the altar.

Take some of the blood from the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle both on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments. Then he and his garments will be consecrated, along with his sons and their garments. “
Take the fat from the ram—the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails, the lobe of the liver, both kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh, since this is a ram for ordination—
along with one loaf of bread, one cake of bread made with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.
Put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar along with the burnt offering, as a pleasing aroma before the LORD. It is an offering made by fire to the LORD. “
Take the breast of the ram of ordination and wave it before the LORD as a wave offering, and it will be your portion.
Consecrate for Aaron and his sons the breast of the wave offering that is waved and the thigh of the heave offering that is lifted up from the ram of ordination.
This will belong to Aaron and his sons as a perpetual portion from the Israelites, for it is the heave offering that the Israelites present to the LORD from their peace offerings. “
The holy garments that belong to Aaron will belong to his sons after him, so that they may be anointed and ordained in them.
The son who succeeds him as priest and enters the Tent of Meeting to minister in the Holy Place must wear them for seven days.
You are to take the ram of ordination and boil its flesh in a holy place.
At the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, Aaron and his sons are to eat the flesh of the ram and the bread that is in the basket.
They must eat those things by which atonement was made for their ordination and consecration, but no outsider may eat them, because they are holy.
If any of the meat of ordination or any of the bread is left until morning, you are to burn up the remainder; it must not be eaten, because it is holy. “
This is what you are to do for Aaron and his sons, in accordance with all that I have commanded you. You are to ordain them for seven days.
Each day you are to prepare a bull as a sin offering for atonement. Purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
For seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and consecrate it. Then the altar will be most holy; anything that touches it will become holy. “
This is what you are to offer regularly on the altar: two lambs a year old, every day, continually.
Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight.
With the first lamb offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour, mixed with a quarter hin of oil from pressed olives, and a drink offering of a quarter hin of wine.
You shall offer the second lamb at twilight with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, as a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD. “
For the generations to come, this burnt offering shall be made regularly at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting before the LORD, where I will meet with you to speak with you there.
There I will meet with the Israelites, and the place will be consecrated by My glory.
So I will consecrate the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and I will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests.
Then I will dwell among the Israelites and be their God.
And they will know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I might dwell among them. I am the LORD their God.”
You shall make an altar for burning incense; you shall make it of acacia wood.
It shall be square—a cubit long and a cubit wide—and two cubits high; its horns shall be of one piece with it.
Overlay it with pure gold—its top, its sides all around, its walls, and its horns—and make a gold molding around it.
Make two gold rings beneath its molding, on its two opposite sides, to serve as housings for the poles by which it shall be borne.
Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
Place the altar before the veil that is over the ark of the testimony, before the atonement cover that is over the testimony, where I will meet with you.
Aaron shall burn fragrant incense upon it; every morning, when he tends the lamps, he shall burn it.
And when Aaron sets up the lamps at twilight, he shall burn it—a perpetual incense before the LORD throughout your generations.
You shall not offer upon it unauthorized incense, nor burnt offering, nor grain offering; and you shall not pour a drink offering upon it.

Once a year Aaron shall make atonement on its horns; throughout your generations he shall make atonement upon it once a year with the blood of the sin offering of atonement. It is most holy to the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"When you take a census of the Israelites to number them, each man shall give a ransom for his life to the LORD when you number them, so that no plague may come upon them in the numbering.
This is what everyone who is counted shall give: half a shekel, by the sanctuary shekel—twenty gerahs to the shekel—half a shekel as an offering to the LORD.
"Everyone who is counted, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the offering of the LORD.
The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less, than the half shekel, when giving the offering of the LORD to make atonement for your souls.

You shall take the atonement money from the Israelites and devote it to the service of the tent of meeting; it shall be for the Israelites a memorial before the LORD, to make atonement for your souls."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"You shall make a bronze basin with a bronze stand for washing; place it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet from it.
Whenever they enter the tent of meeting or approach the altar to minister, to burn an offering by fire to the LORD, they shall wash with water, lest they die.
They shall wash their hands and their feet, so that they will not die; this shall be a perpetual statute for them, for him and his descendants throughout their generations."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Take for yourself the finest spices: five hundred shekels of liquid myrrh, half as much—two hundred fifty shekels—of fragrant cinnamon, two hundred fifty shekels of fragrant cane,
and five hundred shekels of cassia, all by the sanctuary shekel, together with a hin of olive oil.
Make of these a holy anointing oil, a fragrant compound, the work of a perfumer; it shall be a holy anointing oil.
"With you shall anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the testimony,
the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, and the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand.
Sanctify them, and they shall be most holy; whatever touches them shall be holy.
"You shall anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them to serve as priests to Me.
And you shall say to the Israelites, 'This shall be a holy anointing oil to Me throughout your generations.
It shall not be poured upon ordinary flesh, nor shall you make any other like it in composition; it is holy, and it shall be holy to you.
Whoever compounds any like it, or whoever puts any of it on a stranger, shall be cut off from his people.'"
The LORD said to Moses, "Take for yourself fragrant spices—stacte, onycha, and galbanum—and pure frankincense, all in equal measures.
Prepare them into incense, a fragrant blend, the work of a perfumer, seasoned with salt, pure and holy.
Beat some of it very fine and place it before the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you; it shall be most holy to you.
"You are not to make this incense for yourselves using the same formula. It is to be regarded as holy to the LORD.
Whoever makes any like it, to smell it, shall be cut off from his people."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“See, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
I have filled him with the Spirit of God—with wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and every manner of craftsmanship—
to devise artistic designs, to work in gold, silver, and bronze,
and to cut stones for setting and to carve wood, so that he may execute every kind of work.

“Moreover, I have appointed with him Aholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, and I have endowed every skillful artisan with wisdom of heart, that they may fabricate everything I have commanded you.
They shall make the tent of meeting, the ark of the testimony, the mercy seat that is upon it, and all the furnishings of the tent;
the table with its utensils, the pure lampstand with all its utensils, and the altar of incense;
the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the basin with its stand;
the garments of service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for priestly ministry;
the anointing oil and the fragrant incense for the holy place. They shall do all that I have commanded you.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“You shall speak to the Israelites, saying, ‘You must keep My Sabbaths, for this is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, that you may know that I am the LORD who sanctifies you.
You shall keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you. Everyone who profanes it shall surely be put to death; whoever does any work on it shall be cut off from among his people.
“‘Six days work shall be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of solemn rest, holy to the LORD; whoever does any work on the Sabbath day shall surely be put to death.
Therefore the Israelites shall keep the Sabbath, observing it throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant.
It is a sign between Me and the Israelites forever, for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed.’”
When He had finished speaking with him on Mount Sinai, He gave Moses the two tablets of the testimony, tablets of stone, written with the finger of God.

Perceiving that Moses tarried in descending from the mountain, the people congregated about Aaron and demanded, "Arise and fashion for us deities who shall lead us onward, for this Moses—the man who delivered us from Egyptian bondage—we know not what fate has befallen him."
Aaron replied, "Break off the golden rings that are in the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me."
So all the people broke off the golden earrings from their ears and brought them to Aaron.

He received them from their hand and, fashioning the gold with an engraving tool, made it into a molten calf; whereupon they exclaimed, "These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt."
When Aaron beheld this, he built an altar before it and proclaimed, "Tomorrow shall be a feast to the LORD."
They rose early the next day and presented burnt offerings and peace offerings; then the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to engage in revelry.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Descend at once, for your people, whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves.

They have swiftly turned aside from the way that I commanded them and have made for themselves a molten calf; they have bowed down to it, sacrificed to it, and declared, 'These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.'
I have observed this people, and behold, they are a stiff-necked people.
Now therefore leave Me alone, that My anger may burn against them and consume them; yet I will make of you a great nation."
But Moses implored the LORD his God, saying, "The LORD, why does Your anger burn against Your people, whom You brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand?

Why should the Egyptians say, 'He brought them out to do them harm, to slay them in the mountains, and to annihilate them from the face of the earth'? Turn from Your fierce anger and relent concerning the disaster against Your people.

Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, Your servants, to whom You swore by Yourself and said, 'I will multiply your offspring as the stars of heaven, and all this land of which I have spoken I will give to your offspring, and they shall possess it forever.'
So the LORD relented from the disaster that He had threatened to bring upon His people."
Moses then turned and descended from the mountain, bearing in his hand the two tablets of the testimony—tablets inscribed on both sides, written on one side and on the other.
The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved upon the tablets.
When Joshua heard the noise of the people as they shouted, he said to Moses, "There is a sound of war in the camp."
Moses replied, "It is not the sound of a shout of triumph, nor the sound of a cry of defeat; rather, it is the sound of singing that I hear."
As he drew near to the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses' anger burned; he hurled the tablets from his hands and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.
He seized the calf that they had made, burned it with fire, ground it to powder, scattered it upon the water, and made the Israelites drink it.
Moses demanded of Aaron, "What has this people done to you, that you have brought so great a sin upon them?"
Aaron answered, "Let not the anger of my lord burn hot; you know how predisposed this people is to evil.
They said to me, 'Make us gods to go before us, for as for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we know not what has become of him.'
So I said to them, 'Whoever has gold, let him break it off'; they gave it to me, and I cast it into the fire, and out came this calf."

When Moses saw that the people were running wild—for Aaron had let them get out of control to their disgrace among their foes—he stood at the gate of the camp and said, "Who is on the LORD's side? Let him come to me." And all the sons of Levi gathered to him.

And he said to them, "Thus says the LORD God of Israel, 'Put every man his sword upon his thigh, and go back and forth from gate to gate throughout the camp, and slay every man his brother, every man his companion, and every man his neighbor.'"
The Levites did as Moses had commanded, and about three thousand men of the people fell that day.
For Moses had said, "Consecrate yourselves today to the LORD, for every man has been against his son and against his brother, so that He may bestow upon you a blessing this day."
The next day Moses said to the people, "You have sinned a great sin; yet now I will go up to the LORD; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin."
Moses returned to the LORD and said, "Alas, this people has sinned a great sin and has made for themselves gods of gold.
Yet now, if You will forgive their sin—but if not, blot me, I pray, out of Your book that You have written."

The LORD said to Moses, "Whoever has sinned against Me, him I will blot out of My book. Now go, lead the people to the place that I have spoken to you; behold, My angel will go before you; nevertheless, in the day when I visit, I will visit their sin upon them."
And the LORD struck the people because they had made the calf, the one that Aaron made.
The LORD spoke to Moses: “Go up from here, you and the people whom you brought up from the land of Egypt, to the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, ‘I will give it to your seed.’
I will send an angel before you, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
It is a land flowing with milk and honey; yet I will not go up in your midst, because you are a stiff-necked people, lest I consume you on the way.”
When the people heard this grievous word, they mourned, and no one put on his ornaments.

The LORD said to Moses, “Say to the children of Israel, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. If I should go up in your midst for a single moment, I would consume you. Now take off your ornaments from you, and I will know what I will do to you.’”
So the children of Israel stripped off their ornaments from Mount Horeb.

Moses took the tent and pitched it outside the camp, far from the camp, and called it the tent of meeting. Everyone who sought the LORD would go out to the tent of meeting, which was outside the camp.
Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would rise and stand, each at the entrance of his tent, and they would gaze after Moses until he entered the tent.
When Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would descend and stand at the entrance of the tent, and the LORD would speak with Moses.
When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, all the people would rise and worship, each at the entrance of his tent.
Thus the LORD used to speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks with his friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his young assistant, Joshua son of Nun, did not depart from the tent.

Moses said to the LORD, “See, You say to me, ‘Bring up this people,’ but You have not let me know whom You will send with me. Yet You have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have also found favor in My sight.’
Now therefore, if I have found favor in Your sight, please let me know Your ways, that I may know You and find favor in Your sight. Consider too that this nation is Your people.”
And He said, “My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
And he said to Him, “If Your presence will not go with us, do not bring us up from here.

For how shall it be known that I have found favor in Your sight, I and Your people? Is it not in Your going with us, so that we are distinguished, I and Your people, from all the people who are on the face of the earth?”
And the LORD said to Moses, “I will do this thing that you have spoken, for you have found favor in My sight, and I know you by name.”
And he said, “Please show me Your glory.”

And He said, “I will make all My goodness pass before your face, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before you, and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show mercy to whom I will show mercy.”
But He said, “You cannot see My face, for no man can see Me and live.”
And the LORD said, “Behold, there is a place by Me, and you shall stand upon the rock.
And it will be, while My glory passes by, that I will put you in a cleft of the rock, and I will cover you with My hand until I have passed by.
Then I will take away My hand, and you shall see My back, but My face shall not be seen.”
The LORD said to Moses, "Chisel out two stone tablets like the first ones, and I will inscribe upon them the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.
Be prepared by morning, and ascend Mount Sinai in the morning; station yourself there for Me on the summit.
No one shall ascend with you, nor shall anyone be seen anywhere on the mountain; not even the flocks and herds may graze opposite that mountain."
So Moses chiseled out two stone tablets like the first ones. Rising early in the morning, he took the two tablets in his hand and ascended Mount Sinai, as the LORD had commanded him.
Then the LORD descended in the cloud, stood with him there, and proclaimed the name of the LORD.
The LORD passed before Moses and proclaimed, "The LORD, the LORD, the compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness,

maintaining steadfast love for a thousand generations, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin, yet not acquitting the guilty, but visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children and the children's children, to the third and fourth generation."
Moses hastened to bow low to the earth and worship.
"O Lord," he said, "if I have found favor in Your sight, let the Lord go among us, for this is a stiff-necked people; pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance."

The LORD said, "Behold, I am making a covenant. Before all your people I will perform wonders never before wrought in any nation throughout the earth, so that all the people among whom you live may see the work of the LORD, for what I am doing with you is awesome.
Observe what I command you this day: I will drive out before you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites."
Take heed lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land into which you are entering, lest it become a snare in your midst.
Rather, you shall tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, and cut down their Asherah poles.
For you shall worship no other god, because the LORD—whose name is Jealous—is a jealous God.

Take heed lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, for when they prostitute themselves to their gods and sacrifice to them, they will invite you, and you will eat of their sacrifices.
And when you take some of their daughters for your sons, their daughters will prostitute themselves to their gods and make your sons do likewise.
You shall make no molten gods for yourself."

You shall keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread: for seven days, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, for in the month of Abib you came out of Egypt.
All that opens the womb is Mine, and all your livestock's firstborn males, whether ox or sheep.

You may redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a lamb, but if you do not redeem it, you shall break its neck. You must redeem all the firstborn of your sons. No one shall appear before Me empty-handed.
Six days you shall labor, but on the seventh day you shall rest; even in plowing time and harvest you must rest.
You shall celebrate the Feast of Weeks with the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the Feast of Ingathering at the year's turn.
Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Lord, the LORD, the God of Israel.
For I will drive out nations before you and enlarge your territory, and no one shall covet your land when you go up three times a year to appear before the LORD your God.
You must not offer the blood of My sacrifice with leavened bread, nor shall the sacrifice of the Passover feast remain until morning.
You shall bring the choicest firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk."
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Write down these words, for according to these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel."
So Moses was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights; he ate no bread and drank no water. And He wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments.
When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the Testimony in his hand, he did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had been speaking with the LORD.
When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone, and they were afraid to come near him.
But Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the leaders of the congregation returned to him, and Moses spoke to them.
Afterward all the Israelites drew near, and he commanded them everything the LORD had spoken to him on Mount Sinai.
When Moses finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.
Whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with Him, he would remove the veil until he came out; and when he came out, he would tell the Israelites what he had been commanded.
The Israelites would see that the skin of Moses' face shone, so Moses would put the veil over his face again until he went in to speak with the LORD.
Moses assembled the whole congregation of the Israelites and said to them, “These are the words that the LORD has commanded you to perform:
for six days work may be done, but the seventh day shall be holy to you, a Sabbath of solemn rest to the LORD; whoever performs work on it shall be put to death.
You shall not kindle a fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day.”
Moses also said to the whole congregation of the Israelites, “This is the thing that the LORD has commanded:
Take from among you an offering to the LORD; let everyone whose heart is willing bring the LORD’s offering—gold, silver, and bronze;
blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen and goats’ hair;
rams’ skins dyed red, fine leather, and acacia wood;
oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
onyx stones and stones for setting in the ephod and the breastpiece.
“Let every wise-hearted person among you come and make all that the LORD has commanded:
the tabernacle, its tent and its covering, its clasps, its frames, its bars, its pillars, and its bases;
