the ark with its poles, the mercy seat, and the veil of the screen;
the table with its poles and all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
the lampstand for the light, with its utensils and its lamps, and the oil for the light;
the altar of incense with its poles, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the screen for the doorway at the entrance of the tabernacle;
the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grating, its poles, and all its utensils, the basin and its stand;
the hangings of the court, its pillars and its bases, and the screen for the gate of the court;
the pegs of the tabernacle, the pegs of the court, and their cords;
the woven garments for ministering in the Holy Place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for serving as priests.”
Then all the congregation of the Israelites went out from Moses’ presence.
Everyone whose heart stirred him, and everyone whose spirit moved him, came and brought the LORD’s offering for the work of the tent of meeting, for all its service, and for the holy garments.
Thus men and women alike—all who were willing-hearted—brought brooches, earrings, signet rings, ornaments, and every kind of gold article; everyone who presented a wave offering of gold to the LORD.
Everyone who had in his possession blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, fine linen, goats’ hair, rams’ skins dyed red, and fine leather brought them.
Everyone who could present an offering of silver or bronze brought the LORD’s offering, and everyone who had acacia wood for any work of service brought it.
All the wise-hearted women spun with their hands and brought what they had spun—blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
All the women whose hearts stirred them in wisdom spun the goats’ hair.
The leaders brought onyx stones and stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece,
along with the spice and the oil for the light, the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense.
Every man and woman of the Israelites whose heart was willing brought a freewill offering to the LORD for all the work that the LORD had commanded through Moses to be done.
Moses said to the Israelites, “See, the LORD has called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
He has filled him with the Spirit of God—with wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and every kind of craftsmanship—
to devise artistic designs, to work in gold, silver, and bronze,
to cut stones for setting, to carve wood, and to execute every kind of artistic work.
He has also put it in his heart to teach, both him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

He has filled them with skill of heart to perform every work of the craftsman, the designer, and the embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and in fine linen, and of the weaver—those who do every kind of work and those who devise designs.”

Bezalel, Oholiab, and every artisan of wise heart in whom the LORD had deposited wisdom and understanding—so that they comprehended how to execute the entirety of the work pertaining to the service of the sanctuary—were to act in accordance with all that the LORD had commanded, for the LORD had imparted to them the wisdom and understanding requisite for every task of the sacred labor.
Moses summoned Bezalel, Oholiab, and every wise-hearted person whose heart the LORD had endowed with wisdom—every one whose heart stirred him to draw near and undertake the labor.

They received from Moses all the contribution that the Israelites had brought for the work of the service of making the sanctuary, while the people continued to bring him freewill offerings morning after morning.
All the skilled artisans engaged in the sanctuary work came, each departing from the task at which he was laboring,
and they said to Moses, "The people are bringing far more than is sufficient for the service of the work that the LORD has commanded to be done."
Moses commanded that a proclamation be made throughout the camp: "Let no man or woman perform any further labor for the offering of the sanctuary." Thus the people were restrained from bringing more.
The materials were already sufficient for all the work to be done, and even exceeded what was required.
All the skilled artisans among the workers fashioned the tabernacle from ten curtains of fine twined linen, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, with cherubim skillfully worked into them.
Each curtain measured twenty-eight cubits in length and four cubits in width, all the curtains being of one measure.
Five curtains were joined to one another, and the remaining five curtains were joined to one another.
He fashioned loops of blue along the edge of the one curtain at the end of the first set, and he fashioned them likewise along the edge of the outermost curtain in the second set.
He made fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in the second set, the loops being opposite one another.
He made fifty clasps of gold and coupled the curtains to one another with the clasps, so that the tabernacle became a single whole.
He made curtains of goats' hair for a tent over the tabernacle—eleven curtains in all.
The length of one curtain was thirty cubits, and its width four cubits; all eleven curtains were of one measure.
He joined five curtains by themselves and six curtains by themselves.
He made fifty loops on the edge of the outermost curtain in the one set and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in the second set.
He made fifty bronze clasps to join the tent together, so that it became one.
He made a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and an outer covering of fine leather.
He made the upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
Each frame was ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
Each frame had two tenons, fitted to one another; he did this for all the frames of the tabernacle.
He made twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle, toward the south.
He made forty silver bases beneath the twenty frames: two bases under one frame for its two tenons, and two bases under another frame for its two tenons.
For the second side of the tabernacle, toward the north, he made twenty frames,
with their forty silver bases, two bases under one frame and two bases under another.
For the west side of the tabernacle he made six frames.
He made two frames for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear.
They were coupled beneath and coupled together at the top into one ring; he did this for both of them in the two corners.
There were eight frames with their sixteen silver bases, two bases under each frame.
He made bars of acacia wood: five for the frames of one side of the tabernacle,
five bars for the frames of the other side, and five bars for the frames of the tabernacle at the rear toward the west.
He made the middle bar to pass through the midst of the frames from end to end.
He overlaid the frames with gold and made their rings of gold as holders for the bars, and he overlaid the bars with gold.
He made the veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twined linen, fashioning it with cherubim skillfully worked.
He made four pillars of acacia wood for it and overlaid them with gold; their hooks were of gold, and he cast for them four silver bases.
For the entrance of the tent he made a screen of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twined linen, the work of an embroiderer,
along with its five pillars and their hooks; he overlaid their capitals and their bands with gold, and their five bases were bronze.
Bezalel fabricated the ark from acacia timber, its dimensions being two and a half cubits in length, a cubit and a half in breadth, and a cubit and a half in height.
He sheathed it with pure gold, both within and without, and fashioned a gold molding encircling it.
He cast four gold rings for it and affixed them to its four feet, placing two rings upon one side and two upon the other.
He then fashioned poles of acacia timber and sheathed them with gold.
He inserted the poles into the rings along the ark's sides, thereby equipping it for transport.
He fashioned the mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits in length and a cubit and a half in breadth.
He made two cherubim of hammered gold at the mercy seat's extremities,
one cherub at either end, wrought as one continuous piece with the mercy seat itself.
The cherubim spread their wings upward, overshadowing the mercy seat with their pinions; they faced one another, their gaze directed toward the mercy seat.
He fashioned the table from acacia timber, two cubits in length, a cubit in breadth, and a cubit and a half in height.
He sheathed it with pure gold and fashioned a gold molding encircling it.
He fashioned a rim about it, a handbreadth in width, and set a gold molding upon that rim.
He cast four gold rings for it and fastened them to the four corners at its four legs.
The rings lay adjacent to the rim, serving as housings for the poles by which the table was carried.
He fashioned the poles from acacia timber and sheathed them with gold, so that the table might be borne.
He fashioned the table's utensils—its plates, dishes, bowls, and libation pitchers—out of pure gold.
He fashioned the lampstand of pure gold, hammered work throughout; its base, shaft, cups, buds, and petals were all of one piece.
Six branches extended from its sides—three from one side and three from the other.
On one branch were three cups fashioned like almond blossoms, each with buds and petals, and likewise on the next branch, and so for all six branches extending from the lampstand.
Upon the lampstand itself were four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with buds and petals.
A bud was situated beneath the first pair of branches, a bud beneath the second pair, and a bud beneath the third pair, for the six branches in all.
Their buds and branches were all of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.
He also fashioned seven lamps for it, together with wick trimmers and trays, of pure gold.
He fashioned the lampstand and all its utensils from a talent of pure gold.
He fashioned the altar of incense from acacia timber. It was square, a cubit in length and a cubit in breadth, and two cubits in height; its horns were of one piece with it.
He sheathed it with pure gold—its top, its sides, and its horns—and fashioned a gold molding encircling it.
He made two gold rings below the molding on opposite sides, to hold the poles by which it was carried.
He fashioned the poles from acacia timber and sheathed them with gold.
He also prepared the holy anointing oil and the pure, fragrant incense, the work of a perfumer.
He fashioned the altar of burnt offering from acacia wood: it was square, five cubits in length and five cubits in breadth, and three cubits in height.
He made its horns upon its four corners, the horns being of one piece with it, and he overlaid it with bronze.
He made all the altar’s utensils of bronze—the pots, the shovels, the basins, the forks, and the firepans—and he made all its implements of the same material.
He made for the altar a grating of bronze, a netlike work beneath its ledge, extending halfway down.
He cast four rings at the four corners of the bronze grating, as holders for the poles.
He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze,
and he inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar, so that it might be carried by them; he made it hollow, of boards.
He made the basin of bronze, and its stand of bronze, from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He made the court. On the south side, toward the south, the hangings of the court were of fine twisted linen, one hundred cubits in length;
its twenty pillars had twenty bronze bases, while the hooks and bands of the pillars were silver.
On the north side the arrangement was the same: one hundred cubits of hangings, twenty pillars, twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands for the pillars.
On the west side the hangings were fifty cubits, with ten pillars, ten bases, and silver hooks and bands.
On the east side the width was fifty cubits.
The hangings on one shoulder were fifteen cubits, with three pillars and three bases;
on the other shoulder, on either side of the gate of the court, the hangings were likewise fifteen cubits, with three pillars and three bases.
All the hangings around the court were of fine twisted linen.
The bases of the pillars were bronze, but their hooks, bands, and overlaid capitals were silver; indeed, all the pillars of the court were connected with silver bands.

The screen for the gate of the court was embroidered work in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen; it was twenty cubits long and five cubits high, corresponding to the hangings of the court.
Its four pillars were bronze, with bronze bases, silver hooks and bands, and silver-overlaid capitals.
All the pegs for the tabernacle and for the court round about were bronze.

These are the records of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony, as they were recorded at the command of Moses for the service of the Levites under the hand of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all that the the LORD had commanded Moses;
and with him was Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver, designer, and embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and in fine linen.
All the gold that was offered as a wave offering for the work, for all the work of the sanctuary, amounted to twenty-nine talents and seven hundred thirty shekels, by the sanctuary shekel.
The silver from the census of the congregation was one hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels, by the sanctuary shekel—
a beka per head, that is, half a shekel by the sanctuary shekel, for everyone twenty years old and upward who was numbered, totaling six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty men.
From the one hundred talents of silver were cast the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the veil: one hundred bases from one hundred talents, a talent for each base.
From the one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels he made hooks for the pillars, overlaid their capitals, and joined them with bands.
The bronze offered amounted to seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.
With it he made the bases for the entrance of the tent of meeting, the bronze altar and its bronze grating, all the utensils of the altar,
the bases around the court, the bases of the gate of the court, and all the pegs of the tabernacle and of the court round about.

From the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, the artisans fashioned woven vestments for ministration in the sanctuary, and they likewise fashioned the holy garments for Aaron, precisely as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He fashioned the ephod of gold, together with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen.
They hammered the gold into thin sheets and cut threads from them, weaving them into the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and the fine linen, the labor of a master craftsman.
They made shoulder pieces for the ephod, joining them at its two extremities.
The skillfully woven waistband of the ephod was of one piece with it, wrought in the same manner—gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen—as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They set the onyx stones in gold filigree settings, engraved like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel.
Then they fastened them upon the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He made the breastpiece with the same craftsmanship as the ephod—gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen.
It was square and doubled, a span in length and a span in breadth.
They filled it with four rows of stones: the first row was carnelian, chrysolite, and emerald;
the second row was turquoise, sapphire, and diamond;
the third row was jacinth, agate, and amethyst;
and the fourth row was beryl, onyx, and jasper. These stones were set in gold filigree settings.
The stones corresponded to the names of the twelve sons of Israel, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
For the breastpiece they made braided chains of pure gold, like cords.
They made two gold filigree settings and two gold rings, and they fastened the rings to the two corners of the breastpiece.
Then they attached the two gold chains to the two rings at the corners of the breastpiece,
and they fastened the other ends of the chains to the two filigree settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
They made two gold rings and attached them to the other two corners of the breastpiece, on the inner edge adjacent to the ephod.
They made two more gold rings and attached them to the lower part of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on the front, near the seam just above the woven waistband of the ephod.

Then they tied the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue yarn, so that the breastpiece rested above the waistband of the ephod and would not swing away from the ephod, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth, the work of a weaver,
with an opening in its center like the opening of a collar, and with a band around the opening so that it would not tear.
They made pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen around the lower hem of the robe.
They also made bells of pure gold and set them around the hem between the pomegranates.
A bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate—all around the lower hem of the robe for ministration, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made tunics of fine linen, woven work, for Aaron and his sons,
and the turban of fine linen, the ornate headbands, and the linen undergarments of finely twisted linen,
and the sash of finely twisted linen, embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold and engraved upon it, like the engraving of a seal: HOLY TO the LORD.
They attached to it a blue cord to mount it upon the turban above, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Thus all the work on the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, was completed; the Israelites had done everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then they brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent with all its furnishings, its clasps, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases;
the covering of ram skins dyed red, the covering of fine leather, and the veil of the screen;
the ark of the testimony with its poles and the mercy seat;
the table with all its utensils and the bread of the Presence;
the pure gold lampstand with its lamps, the arranged lamps, and all its utensils, together with the oil for the light;
the gold altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the entrance to the tent;
the bronze altar with its bronze grating, its poles, and all its utensils; the basin with its stand;

the curtains of the courtyard with its posts and bases; the curtain for the gate of the courtyard; its ropes and tent pegs; and all the equipment for the service of the tabernacle, the tent of meeting;
the woven garments for ministration in the sanctuary; the holy garments for Aaron the priest; and the garments for his sons to serve as priests.
The Israelites had done all the work just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
And Moses inspected all the work and saw that they had done it just as the LORD had commanded. So Moses blessed them.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“On the first day of the first month, you shall raise the tabernacle, namely the tent of meeting.
You shall place within it the ark of the testimony, and you shall veil the ark with the curtain.
You shall introduce the table and array its setting, and you shall introduce the lampstand and raise its lamps.
You shall set the golden altar of incense before the ark of the testimony, and you shall establish the screen for the doorway of the tabernacle.
You shall set the altar of burnt offering before the doorway of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting,
and you shall set the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and you shall put water in it.
And you shall erect the court round about it, and you shall hang the screen for the gate of the court.
“Then you shall take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and all that is in it, and you shall consecrate it and all its furnishings; and it shall be holy.
You shall anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and you shall consecrate the altar, so that the altar shall be most holy.
You shall anoint the basin and its stand, and you shall consecrate it.
Then you shall bring Aaron and his sons to the doorway of the tent of meeting, and you shall wash them with water.
And you shall clothe Aaron with the holy garments, and you shall anoint him and consecrate him, that he may serve Me as priest.
You shall bring his sons near and clothe them with tunics,
and anoint them as you anointed their father, that they may serve Me as priests. Their anointing shall be to them for an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.”
Thus Moses did: according to all that the LORD commanded him, so he did.
In the first month of the second year, on the first day of the month, the tabernacle was raised.
Moses raised the tabernacle, set its bases, set up its frames, inserted its bars, and erected its pillars.
He spread the tent over the tabernacle and placed the covering of the tent over it from above, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He took the testimony and placed it within the ark, and he set the poles upon the ark, and he placed the mercy seat above upon the ark.
He brought the ark into the tabernacle and set up the veil of the screen, and he screened the ark of the testimony, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He set the table in the tent of meeting, on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the veil.
He arranged the bread upon it before the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He set the lampstand in the tent of meeting, opposite the table, on the south side of the tabernacle.
He raised the lamps before the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He set the golden altar in the tent of meeting before the veil.
He burned fragrant incense upon it, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He set up the screen for the doorway of the tabernacle.
He set the altar of burnt offering at the doorway of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting, and offered upon it the burnt offering and the grain offering, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He set the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it for washing.
Moses and Aaron and his sons washed their hands and their feet from it.
When they entered the tent of meeting or approached the altar, they washed, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He erected the court all around the tabernacle and the altar, and set up the screen for the gate of the court. So Moses finished the work.
Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
Moses could not enter the tent of meeting because the cloud had settled upon it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
Whenever the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the sons of Israel set out on all their journeys.
But if the cloud was not taken up, then they did not set out until the day it was taken up.
For the cloud of the LORD was on the tabernacle by day, and fire was in it by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.
The LORD summoned Moses and addressed him from the Tent of Meeting, saying,

“Speak to the Israelites and declare to them: Whenever any individual among you presents an offering to the LORD, you shall bring your offering from the domestic livestock—whether from the herd or from the flock.

If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he shall present an unblemished male; he shall bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, so that it may be accepted on his behalf before the LORD.
He shall impose his hand upon the head of the burnt offering, and it shall be accepted on his behalf, to effect atonement for him.
“He shall slaughter the young bull before the LORD, and Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall present the blood and dash it against the altar on every side, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
He shall flay the burnt offering and dissect it into its several portions.
The sons of Aaron the priest shall lay fire upon the altar and arrange wood upon the fire.
Then Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall arrange the portions—the head and the suet—upon the fire that rests upon the wood that rests upon the altar.
Its entrails and its shanks he shall wash with water, and the priest shall incinerate the whole of it upon the altar: a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a fragrance pleasing to the LORD.
“If his offering is a burnt offering from the flock—whether from the sheep or from the goats—he shall present an unblemished male.
He shall slaughter it on the northern side of the altar before the LORD, and Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall dash its blood against the altar on every side.
The priest shall dissect it into its portions and arrange them, together with its head and its fat, upon the fire that is upon the wood that is upon the altar.

The entrails and the shanks he shall wash with water, and the priest shall present the whole and incinerate it upon the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a fragrance pleasing to the LORD.
“If his offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, he shall bring his offering of turtledoves or young pigeons.
The priest shall bring it to the altar, wring off its head, and incinerate it upon the altar; its blood shall be drained against the side of the altar.
He shall remove its crop with its plumage and cast it beside the altar on the east side, at the place of the ashes.

He shall cleave it open by its wings without severing it, and the priest shall incinerate it upon the altar, upon the wood that is upon the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a fragrance pleasing to the LORD.”
Whensoever a person presents an oblation of grain unto the LORD, his offering shall consist of fine flour; he shall pour oil upon it and place frankincense upon it.

He shall bring it unto Aaron’s sons, the priests, and the priest shall take from it a handful of the fine flour and of its oil, together with all the frankincense thereof, and shall burn the memorial portion upon the altar as an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma unto the LORD.
The remainder of the grain offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy portion among the offerings made by fire unto the LORD.
Should you present a grain offering baked in an oven, it shall be unleavened cakes of fine flour mingled with oil, or unleavened wafers anointed with oil.
If your offering is a grain offering upon a griddle, it shall be of fine flour, unleavened, mingled with oil.
You shall crumble it into pieces and pour oil upon it; it is a grain offering.
If your offering is a grain offering cooked in a pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
When you bring unto the LORD the grain offering prepared in any of these manners, you shall present it unto the priest, who shall convey it unto the altar.
The priest shall lift from the grain offering its memorial portion and burn it upon the altar as an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma unto the LORD.
The rest of the grain offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy portion among the offerings made by fire unto the LORD.
No grain offering that you present unto the LORD shall be made with leaven, for you must not burn any leaven or honey as an offering made by fire unto the LORD.
You may present them as an offering of firstfruits unto the LORD, but they shall not be offered upon the altar as a pleasing aroma.
You shall season all your grain offerings with salt; you must not allow the salt of the covenant of your God to be absent from your grain offering; with all your offerings you shall present salt.
If you present a grain offering of firstfruits unto the LORD, you shall offer crushed new grain, roasted in the fire, as the grain offering of your firstfruits.
You shall put oil upon it and place frankincense upon it; it is a grain offering.
The priest shall burn as its memorial portion some of the crushed grain and oil, together with all its frankincense, as an offering made by fire unto the LORD.
If a person’s offering is a sacrifice of peace offerings, let him present it from the herd, whether male or female, unblemished before the LORD.
He shall lay his hand upon the head of his offering and slaughter it at the entrance of the tent of meeting; then Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall throw the blood around against the altar.
From the sacrifice of peace offerings he shall present, as an offering by fire to the LORD, the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is upon the entrails.
He shall also remove the two kidneys with the fat upon them, which is on the loins, together with the lobe of the liver beside the kidneys.
Aaron’s sons shall burn it on the altar upon the burnt offering that is on the wood over the fire, as an offering by fire, a soothing aroma to the LORD.
If his offering for a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD is from the flock, he shall present it, male or female, unblemished.
If he presents a lamb as his offering, he shall bring it before the LORD.
He shall lay his hand upon the head of his offering and slaughter it before the tent of meeting; then Aaron’s sons shall throw its blood around against the altar.

From the sacrifice of peace offerings he shall present, as an offering by fire to the LORD, its fat—the entire fat tail removed close to the backbone—along with the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is upon the entrails.
He shall also remove the two kidneys with the fat upon them, which is on the loins, together with the lobe of the liver beside the kidneys.
The priest shall burn it on the altar as food, an offering by fire to the LORD.
If his offering is a goat, he shall present it before the LORD.
He shall lay his hand upon its head and slaughter it before the tent of meeting; then Aaron’s sons shall throw its blood around against the altar.
From it he shall present his offering, as an offering by fire to the LORD: the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is upon the entrails.
He shall also remove the two kidneys with the fat upon them, which is on the loins, together with the lobe of the liver beside the kidneys.
The priest shall burn them on the altar as bread, an offering by fire, a soothing aroma; all the fat belongs to the LORD.
It is a perpetual statute throughout your generations, in all your dwellings: you shall eat neither fat nor blood.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

“Speak to the Israelites and say: If any person sins unintentionally, transgressing any of the LORD’s commandments concerning things that must never be done, and commits one of those prohibited acts:” “
If the anointed priest sins, bringing guilt upon the people, then he shall offer to the LORD, for the sin he has committed, a young bull without blemish as a sin offering.
He shall bring the bull to the entrance of the tent of meeting before the LORD, lay his hand upon the head of the bull, and slaughter the bull before the LORD. “
The anointed priest shall take some of the blood of the bull and bring it into the tent of meeting.
He shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of it seven times before the LORD, in front of the veil of the sanctuary.

He shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense before the LORD, which stands in the tent of meeting, and pour out all the rest of the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the entrance of the tent of meeting. “
He shall remove all the fat from the bull of the sin offering—the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails—
together with the two kidneys and the fat upon them at the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall remove with the kidneys.
This shall be done just as the fat is removed from the bull of the peace offering; and the priest shall burn these portions on the altar of burnt offering. “
But the hide of the bull and all its flesh, together with its head, its legs, its entrails, and its dung—all the rest of the bull—
he shall carry outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place, to the ash heap, and burn it there on wood with fire; at the place where the ashes are poured out, it shall be burned.” “

If the whole congregation of Israel sins unintentionally, and the matter is hidden from the eyes of the assembly, so that they do any one of the things the LORD has commanded not to be done, and they become guilty—
when the sin they have committed becomes known, the assembly shall offer a young bull as a sin offering and bring it before the tent of meeting.
The elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the head of the bull before the LORD, and the bull shall be slaughtered before the LORD. “
The anointed priest shall bring some of the blood of the bull into the tent of meeting.
He shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD, in front of the veil.

He shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that is before the LORD in the tent of meeting, and pour out all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the entrance of the tent of meeting. “
He shall remove all its fat from it and burn it on the altar.
He shall do with this bull as he did with the bull of the sin offering; thus he shall do with it. And the priest shall make atonement for them, and they shall be forgiven.
He shall carry the bull outside the camp and burn it as he burned the first bull; it is the sin offering for the assembly.” “
When a leader sins and unintentionally does any one of all the things the LORD his God has commanded not to be done, and becomes guilty—
or when his sin which he has committed is made known to him—he shall bring as his offering a male goat without blemish.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the goat and slaughter it in the place where they slaughter the burnt offering before the LORD; it is a sin offering.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering.
He shall burn all its fat on the altar, like the fat of the sacrifice of peace offerings; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin, and he shall be forgiven. “
If any one of the common people sins unintentionally, doing any of the things the LORD has commanded not to be done, and becomes guilty—
or when his sin which he has committed is made known to him—then he shall bring for his offering a female goat without blemish, for the sin he has committed.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter the sin offering at the place of the burnt offering.
The priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out all the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.

He shall remove all its fat, as the fat is removed from the sacrifice of peace offerings, and the priest shall burn it on the altar for a pleasing aroma to the LORD; and the priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be forgiven. “
If he brings a lamb as his offering for a sin offering, he shall bring a female without blemish.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it for a sin offering in the place where they slaughter the burnt offering.
The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out all the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.

He shall remove all its fat, as the fat of the lamb is removed from the sacrifice of peace offerings, and the priest shall burn them on the altar, on the LORD’s offerings by fire; and the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he shall be forgiven.”
Should an individual sin by withholding testimony after having heard a formal adjuration to bear witness, notwithstanding that he has either seen or known the matter, he shall bear his iniquity.

Or if a person touches anything unclean—whether the carcass of an unclean wild animal, or the carcass of unclean livestock, or the carcass of an unclean creeping thing—and the fact is concealed from him, he is nonetheless unclean and incurs guilt.
Or if he touches the uncleanness of a human being, whatever species of impurity renders a person unclean, and it escapes his notice, though he subsequently becomes aware of it, he is guilty.

Or if a person rashly utters an oath with his lips, whether to do good or to do harm, in any matter concerning which one may swear thoughtlessly, and it escapes his notice, then upon discovering it he shall be guilty in one of these respects.
When anyone becomes guilty in any of these ways, he shall confess the sin he has committed.
He shall bring to the LORD his guilt offering for the sin he has committed: a female from the flock, a lamb or a goat, as a sin offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin.

If he cannot afford a lamb, he shall bring to the LORD, as his guilt offering for the sin he has committed, two turtledoves or two young pigeons—one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.
He shall bring them to the priest, who shall first present the one for the sin offering; he shall wring its head from its neck without severing it.
He shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, and the rest of the blood shall be drained out at the base of the altar; it is a sin offering.
He shall then prepare the second bird as a burnt offering according to the prescribed ordinance; thus the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he shall be forgiven.

But if he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he shall bring, as his offering for the sin he has committed, a tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering; he shall put no oil on it and shall add no frankincense to it, because it is a sin offering.
He shall bring it to the priest, who shall take a handful of it as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar, on top of the offerings made by fire to the LORD; it is a sin offering.

In this way the priest shall make atonement for him for any of these sins he has committed, and he shall be forgiven; the remainder of the offering shall belong to the priest, as in the case of the grain offering.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

“If a person acts unfaithfully and sins unintentionally against the LORD’s holy things, he must bring to the LORD as his guilt offering a ram without blemish from the flock, valued according to your valuation in silver shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel; it is a guilt offering.

He must make restitution for the holy thing in which he sinned, add a fifth of its value, and give it to the priest, who shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and he will be forgiven.
“If someone sins and violates any of the LORD’s commandments concerning things not to be done, even though he is unaware of it, he is still guilty and shall bear his iniquity.

He must bring to the priest a ram without blemish from the flock, at the proper valuation, as a guilt offering; the priest shall make atonement for him for the wrong he committed in ignorance, and he will be forgiven.
It is a guilt offering; he is indeed guilty before the LORD.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"If a person sins and acts unfaithfully against the LORD by deceiving his neighbor concerning a deposit, or a pledge, or a stolen thing, or by extorting from his neighbor,
or if he has found what was lost and lied about it, swearing falsely concerning any one of all the things that a person may do and thereby sin—
then, when he has sinned and incurred guilt, he shall restore what he took by robbery, or the thing extorted, or the deposit entrusted to him, or the lost thing that he found.
Or, in regard to anything about which he swore falsely, he shall restore it in full and add a fifth to it; to the one to whom it belongs he shall give it on the day he presents his guilt offering.
And he shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD: a ram without blemish from the flock, according to your valuation, for a guilt offering.
The priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD, and he shall be forgiven for any of the things by which one may incur guilt.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

"Command Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the burnt offering—the burnt offering shall remain on the hearth of the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning on it.
The priest shall put on his linen tunic and linen undergarments on his flesh; he shall remove the ashes from the burnt offering consumed by fire on the altar and place them beside the altar.
Then he shall take off his garments, put on other garments, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.

The fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it; it shall not go out. Every morning the priest shall burn wood on it, arrange the burnt offering on it, and burn the fat of the peace offerings on it.
Fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it shall not go out.
"And this is the law of the grain offering: Aaron's sons shall present it before the LORD in front of the altar.

He shall take from it a handful of the fine flour of the grain offering, together with its oil and all the frankincense on the grain offering, and burn it on the altar as a memorial portion, a soothing aroma to the LORD.
Aaron and his sons shall eat the remainder of it; it shall be eaten unleavened in a holy place, in the court of the tent of meeting.
It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it as their portion from My offerings by fire; it is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
Every male among the sons of Aaron may eat it; it is a perpetual statute throughout your generations from the LORD's offerings by fire. Everyone who touches them shall be holy."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

"This is the offering of Aaron and his sons, which they shall offer to the LORD on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.
It shall be made with oil on a griddle; you shall bring it well stirred; as a grain offering of baked pieces you shall offer it, a soothing aroma to the LORD.
The priest who is anointed in his place from among his sons shall offer it; it is a perpetual statute to the LORD; it shall be wholly burned.
Every grain offering of a priest shall be wholly burned; it shall not be eaten.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the sin offering: In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the sin offering shall be slaughtered before the LORD; it is most holy.
The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it; it shall be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the tent of meeting.
Whatever touches its flesh shall be holy, and when some of its blood is sprinkled on a garment, you shall wash what was sprinkled in a holy place.
An earthenware vessel in which it is boiled shall be broken; and if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, it shall be scoured and rinsed with water.
Every male among the priests may eat it; it is most holy.
But no sin offering may be eaten from which any of its blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the holy place; it shall be burned with fire."
This is the law of the guilt offering, which is most holy:
the guilt offering shall be slaughtered in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and its blood shall be sprinkled round about the altar.
All of its fat shall be offered—namely, the fat tail and the fat enveloping the entrails,
together with the two kidneys and the fat upon them near the loins, and the lobe above the liver, which the priest shall excise along with the kidneys.
The priest shall incinerate them upon the altar as an offering made by fire to the LORD; it is a guilt offering.
Every male among the priests may partake of it; it shall be consumed in a holy place, for it is most holy.
As the sin offering is, so is the guilt offering; one law governs both, and it pertains to the priest who effects atonement thereby.
As for the priest who offers a burnt offering on behalf of another, the hide of the burnt offering he has presented shall accrue to that priest.
Likewise, every grain offering baked in an oven, or prepared upon a griddle or in a pan, shall belong to the priest who presents it.
Every grain offering, whether commingled with oil or dry, shall be apportioned equally among all the sons of Aaron.
This is the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings that one may present to the LORD:

if he presents it as a thanksgiving, then, in conjunction with the sacrifice of thanksgiving, he shall offer unleavened cakes mingled with oil, unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and well-kneaded cakes of fine flour mingled with oil.
With cakes of leavened bread he shall present his offering, together with the sacrifice of his peace offering of thanksgiving.
From these he shall present one cake from each kind as a contribution to the LORD; it shall belong to the priest who sprinkles the blood of the peace offerings.
The flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offering of thanksgiving shall be eaten on the day of his offering; he shall leave none of it until morning.
If, however, the sacrifice of his offering is a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day he presents his sacrifice, and what remains of it may be eaten on the next day.
But the remainder of the flesh of the sacrifice shall be consumed by fire on the third day.

If any of the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings is eaten on the third day, it shall not be accepted, nor shall it be credited to him who offered it; it shall be an abomination, and the person who eats of it shall bear his iniquity.
The flesh that touches anything unclean shall not be eaten; it shall be burned in the fire. As for the flesh, all who are clean may eat of it.
But the person who eats of the flesh of the sacrifice of peace offerings that belong to the LORD, while his uncleanness is upon him, that person shall be cut off from his people.

If a person touches anything unclean—whether human uncleanness, an unclean beast, or any unclean detestable thing—and then eats of the flesh of the sacrifice of peace offerings that belong to the LORD, that person shall be cut off from his people.
“Speak to the Israelites and say: You are not to eat any of the fat of an ox, a sheep, or a goat.
The fat of an animal found dead or torn by beasts may be used for any other purpose, but you must not eat it.
For anyone who eats the fat of an animal from which an offering by fire is presented to the LORD, the person who eats it shall be cut off from his people.
You must not eat the blood of any bird or animal in any of your dwellings.
Whoever eats blood shall be cut off from his people.”
“Speak to the Israelites and say: He who presents the sacrifice of his peace offering to the LORD is to bring to the LORD an offering from it.
With his own hands he is to bring the offerings made by fire to the LORD; he is to bring the fat together with the breast, and wave the breast before the LORD as a wave offering.
The priest shall burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
You are to give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from your peace offerings.
The priest who offers the blood and fat of the peace offering shall have the right thigh as his portion.

I have taken from the Israelites the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution from their peace offerings, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as a perpetual portion from the Israelites.
This is the portion of the offerings made by fire to the LORD that belongs to Aaron and his sons; it has been assigned to them from the day they are presented to the LORD as priests.
On the day he was anointed, the LORD commanded that this be given to them by the Israelites as a perpetual statute for the generations to come.”
This is the law of the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering, and the peace offering,
which the LORD commanded Moses on Mount Sinai on the day He commanded the Israelites to present their offerings to the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai.
“Take Aaron and his sons, together with their garments, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread,
and assemble the entire congregation at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.”
Moses did as the LORD commanded, and the congregation was assembled at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
Moses said to them, “This is what the LORD has commanded to be done.”
Then Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
He clothed Aaron with the tunic, girded him with the sash, invested him with the robe, and placed the ephod upon him; then he girded him with the ephod’s skillfully woven waistband and fastened it.
He set the breastpiece upon him and inserted the Urim and the Thummim into the breastpiece.
He placed the turban on Aaron’s head and affixed the golden plate—the holy crown—on the front of the turban, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle and all that was in it, thereby consecrating them.
He sprinkled some of the oil on the altar seven times, anointing the altar and all its utensils, together with the basin and its stand, to sanctify them.
He poured anointing oil upon Aaron’s head and anointed him, setting him apart as holy.
Moses then brought forward Aaron’s sons, clothed them with tunics, girded them with sashes, and bound headbands upon them, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He brought forward the bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.

Moses slaughtered it, took some of the blood, and with his finger applied it to the horns of the altar on every side, purifying the altar; he poured the remaining blood at the base of the altar and consecrated it, making atonement for it.
Moses also took all the fat that enveloped the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and burned them on the altar.
The bull—its hide, flesh, and offal—he burned outside the camp, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He presented the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
Moses slaughtered the ram and dashed the blood against the altar on every side.
He dismembered the ram and burned the head, the pieces, and the fat.

After washing the entrails and the legs with water, he burned the entire ram on the altar as a burnt offering—a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD—just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He presented the second ram, the ram of ordination, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
Moses slaughtered it, took some of its blood, and put it on the lobe of Aaron’s right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the great toe of his right foot.

He brought forward Aaron’s sons as well and put some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the great toes of their right feet; then he dashed the rest of the blood against the altar on every side.
He took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.

From the basket of unleavened bread that was before the LORD, he took one unleavened cake, one cake of bread made with oil, and one wafer, and he placed them upon the fat portions and the right thigh.
He put all these into the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved them as a wave offering before the LORD.
Moses then took them from their hands and burned them on the altar atop the burnt offering; they were ordination offerings, a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
He also took the breast and waved it as a wave offering before the LORD. It became Moses’ portion from the ram of ordination, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood from the altar and sprinkled them on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments; thus he consecrated Aaron and his garments, together with his sons and their garments.

Moses said to Aaron and his sons, “Boil the meat at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and eat it there with the bread that is in the basket of ordination offerings, as I commanded when I said, ‘Aaron and his sons shall eat it.’
Then burn the remainder of the meat and the bread.
You must not leave the entrance to the Tent of Meeting for seven days, until the days of your ordination are completed; for it will take seven days to ordain you.
What has been done today was commanded by the LORD to make atonement for you.
You must remain at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting day and night for seven days and keep the LORD’s charge, so that you will not die; for this is what I have been commanded.”
So Aaron and his sons did everything the LORD had commanded through Moses.
On the eighth day, Moses summoned Aaron, together with his sons and the elders of Israel.
Moses said to Aaron, “Take a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, both unblemished, and present them before the LORD.
Say to the Israelites, ‘Take a male goat for a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb, each a year old and unblemished, for a burnt offering.
Bring also an ox and a ram for peace offerings, to sacrifice before the LORD, together with a grain offering mixed with oil, for today the LORD will appear to you.’”
They brought what Moses had commanded to the front of the tent of meeting, and the whole congregation drew near and stood before the LORD.
Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you.”

Moses said to Aaron, “Approach the altar and offer your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and for the people; then present the people’s offering and make atonement for them, as the LORD has commanded.”
Aaron approached the altar and slaughtered the calf for his sin offering.
Aaron’s sons brought the blood to him; he dipped his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the altar, and he poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
The fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver from the sin offering he burned on the altar, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The flesh and the hide he burned with fire outside the camp.
He slaughtered the burnt offering, and Aaron’s sons handed him the blood, which he sprinkled all around the altar.
They handed him the burnt offering, cut into its pieces, together with the head, and he burned them on the altar.
He washed the entrails and the legs and burned them on the altar, on top of the burnt offering.
Then he brought the people’s offering: he took the goat of the sin offering for the people, slaughtered it, and offered it for sin, as he had done with the first.
He brought the burnt offering and offered it according to the ordinance.
He brought the grain offering, filled his hand with some of it, and burned it on the altar, in addition to the morning burnt offering.
He slaughtered the ox and the ram for the people as a peace offering; Aaron’s sons handed him the blood, and he sprinkled it around the altar.
They also set forth the fat portions from the ox and the ram: the fat tail, the covering fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver.
They placed the fat portions on the breasts, and he burned the fat portions on the altar.
Aaron waved the breasts and the right thigh as a wave offering before the LORD, as Moses had commanded.
Then Aaron lifted his hands toward the people and blessed them; and, having finished offering the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, he came down.
Moses and Aaron entered the tent of meeting; when they came out, they blessed the people, and the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people.
Fire came out from before the LORD and consumed the burnt offering and the fat on the altar; when all the people saw it, they shouted and fell on their faces.
Aaron’s sons Nadab and Abihu each took his censer, placed fire in it, laid incense upon it, and offered before the LORD an unauthorized fire that He had not commanded them.
Then fire came forth from before the LORD and consumed them, so that they died before the LORD.
Moses said to Aaron, “This is what the LORD has spoken: ‘I will be sanctified among those who are near Me, and I will be glorified before all the people.’” And Aaron remained silent.
Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, Aaron’s uncle, and said to them, “Come near and carry your brothers from before the sanctuary to a place outside the camp.”
They came near and carried them in their tunics outside the camp, just as Moses had commanded.

Moses said to Aaron and to his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, “Do not dishevel your hair, nor tear your garments, lest you die and wrath come upon the whole congregation; but let your brothers, the entire house of Israel, mourn the conflagration that the LORD has kindled.
You shall not go out from the entrance of the tent of meeting, lest you die, for the anointing oil of the LORD is upon you.” And they did as Moses had said.
The LORD spoke to Aaron, saying,

“You and your sons with you shall not drink wine or strong drink when you enter the tent of meeting, lest you die; it shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations, in order to distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the unclean and the clean, and to teach the children of Israel all the statutes that the LORD has spoken to them through Moses.”
Moses spoke to Aaron and to his surviving sons, Eleazar and Ithamar: “Take the grain offering that remains from the LORD’s fire offerings and eat it unleavened beside the altar, for it is most holy.
You shall eat it in a holy place, because it is your portion and your sons’ portion from the LORD’s fire offerings; for so I have been commanded.

You shall eat the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution in a clean place—you and your sons and your daughters with you—for they have been given as your portion and your sons’ portion from the sacrifices of peace offerings of the children of Israel.

They shall bring the thigh of the contribution and the breast of the wave offering together with the fat portions as fire offerings, to wave them as a wave offering before the LORD; and they shall be yours and your sons’ with you as a perpetual portion, as the LORD has commanded.”
Moses diligently inquired about the goat of the sin offering and discovered that it had been burned up; he became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s surviving sons, and said,
“Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy place? It is most holy, and He has given it to you to bear the iniquity of the congregation, to make atonement for them before the LORD.
Behold, its blood was not brought into the inner sanctuary; you certainly should have eaten it in the holy place, as I commanded.”

Aaron answered Moses, “Behold, today they offered their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD, and these calamities have befallen me; if I had eaten the sin offering today, would it have been pleasing in the eyes of the LORD?”
When Moses heard this, it pleased him.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying to them:
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: This is the law concerning all the beasts upon the earth.
Among the beasts, you may eat any creature that has a fully cloven hoof and chews the cud.
"Nevertheless, you shall not eat these among the ruminants or among the cloven-hoofed: the camel, for though it ruminates, it does not divide the hoof; it is unclean to you.
The rock badger, for it ruminates but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean to you.
The hare, for it ruminates but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean to you.
And the swine, for it divides the hoof and is cloven-footed, yet does not ruminate; it is unclean to you.
Their flesh you shall not eat, and their carcasses you shall not touch; they are unclean to you.
"From all that inhabit the waters, in seas and rivers, you may eat these: every creature that possesses fins and scales.
But every creature in seas or rivers that lacks fins and scales—among all swarming aquatic life and every living thing in the waters—is an abomination to you.
They shall remain an abomination to you; you shall not eat their flesh, and their carcasses you shall hold in abhorrence.
Every aquatic creature lacking fins and scales is detestable to you.
"And these you shall hold in abhorrence among the birds; they are not to be eaten, for they are an abomination: the eagle, the bearded vulture, and the black vulture;
the kite and the falcon according to its kind;
every raven according to its kind;
the ostrich, the short-eared owl, the gull, and the hawk according to its kind;
the little owl, the cormorant, and the great owl;
the white owl, the desert owl, and the osprey;
the stork according to its kind, the heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
"Every winged insect that goes upon four legs is an abomination to you.
Yet you may eat these among the winged insects that go upon four legs: those possessing jointed legs above their feet, wherewith to leap upon the earth.
Namely, the locust according to its kind, the katydid according to its kind, the cricket according to its kind, and the grasshopper according to its kind.
But every other winged insect with four feet is detestable to you.
"By these you shall be rendered unclean: whoever touches their carcass shall be unclean until evening.
And whoever bears any part of their carcass shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.
Every beast that has a hoof without a cloven cleft, or that does not ruminate, is unclean to you; whoever touches them becomes unclean.
Every quadruped that walks upon its paws, among all quadrupedal creatures, is unclean to you; whoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.
And he who carries its carcass shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening; they are unclean to you.
"And these are unclean to you among the swarming things that swarm upon the earth: the mole rat, the mouse, and the great lizard according to its kind;
the gecko, the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
These are unclean to you among all swarming things; whoever touches them after they die shall be unclean until evening.

And upon whatever any of them falls when dead, it becomes unclean—whether a wooden vessel, a garment, a skin, or a sack—every vessel employed for work; it must be brought into water and remains unclean until evening, after which it becomes clean.
If one of them falls into an earthen vessel, everything within it becomes unclean, and you shall break the vessel.
Any food that may be eaten, if water has touched it, becomes unclean; and any drink that may be drunk from any vessel becomes unclean.
Moreover, everything upon which a carcass falls becomes unclean; an oven or stove shall be demolished; they are unclean and shall be unclean to you.
Nevertheless, a spring or a cistern of water remains clean, though whoever touches their carcass becomes unclean.
"If a carcass falls upon seed intended for sowing, it remains clean;
but if water has been put upon the seed and a carcass falls upon it, it is unclean to you.
If any beast that you may eat dies, whoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.
And he who eats of its carcass, or carries its carcass, shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.
"Every swarming thing that swarms upon the earth is detestable; it shall not be eaten.
You shall not eat any swarming creature that moves on the earth—whether it creeps upon its belly, walks on four legs, or has many feet—for they are detestable.
Do not render your souls abominable by any swarming creature, nor defile yourselves through them, lest you become defiled.
"For I am the LORD your God. Consecrate yourselves therefore, and be holy, for I am holy; and do not defile yourselves with any swarming thing that moves upon the earth.
For I am the LORD, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God; you shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.
This is the law concerning beasts and birds and every living creature that moves in the waters and every creature that swarms upon the earth,
to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, and between the living thing that may be eaten and the living thing that may not be eaten."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
“Speak to the Israelites and say: ‘When a woman conceives and gives birth to a son, she shall be ceremonially unclean for seven days, as during the days of her menstrual impurity.
On the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.

Then she shall continue in the blood of her purification for thirty-three days; she shall not touch anything holy, nor shall she enter the sanctuary, until the days of her purification have been fulfilled.
But if she gives birth to a daughter, she shall be unclean for two weeks, as during her menstruation, and she shall continue in the blood of her purification for sixty-six days.’”

When the days of her purification have been fulfilled, whether for a son or for a daughter, she shall bring to the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting a year-old lamb for a burnt offering, and a young pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering.

He shall present it before the LORD and make atonement for her, so that she may be cleansed from the flow of her blood. This is the law for the woman who gives birth, whether to a male or to a female child.

If she cannot afford a lamb, then she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering, and the priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,

“When a person develops upon the skin of his body a swelling, an eruption, or a bright spot, and it becomes in the skin of his body an affliction of leprosy, he shall be brought to Aaron the priest, or to one of his sons among the priests.

The priest shall inspect the affliction on the skin of the flesh; and if the hair in the afflicted area has turned white and the affliction appears deeper than the skin of the flesh, it is an affliction of leprosy. Upon inspecting him, the priest shall pronounce him unclean.
“But if the bright spot is white in the skin of his body and does not appear deeper than the skin, and its hair has not turned white, the priest shall confine the afflicted person for seven days.

On the seventh day the priest shall inspect him; and if, in his judgment, the affliction has remained stationary and has not spread in the skin, then the priest shall confine him a second time for seven days.

On the seventh day the priest shall inspect him again; and if the affliction has faded and has not spread in the skin, the priest shall pronounce him clean: it is merely an eruption. He shall wash his garments and be clean.
But if the eruption spreads in the skin after he has presented himself to the priest for his cleansing, he shall present himself again to the priest.
The priest shall look; and if the eruption has spread in the skin, the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is leprosy.
“When a man is afflicted with leprosy, he shall be brought to the priest.
The priest shall inspect him; and if there is a white swelling in the skin that has turned the hair white, with raw flesh in the swelling,
it is chronic leprosy in the skin of his body. The priest shall pronounce him unclean and shall not confine him, for he is unclean.
If the leprosy breaks out abundantly in the skin, so that it covers all the skin of the afflicted person from his head to his feet, so far as the priest can see,
then the priest shall inspect him; and if the leprosy has covered all his flesh, he shall pronounce him clean. Since it has all turned white, he is clean.
But whenever raw flesh appears on him, he shall be unclean.
The priest shall inspect the raw flesh and pronounce him unclean; raw flesh is unclean, for it is leprosy.
If, however, the raw flesh turns again and becomes white, he shall come to the priest,
and the priest shall inspect him; and if the affliction has turned white, the priest shall pronounce the afflicted person clean: he is clean.
“If there is a boil on the skin of a person’s body and it heals,
and in the place of the boil there appears a white swelling or a reddish-white bright spot, it shall be shown to the priest.
The priest shall inspect it; and if it appears deeper than the skin and its hair has turned white, the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is leprosy that has broken out in the boil.
But if the priest examines it and finds no white hair in it, and it is not deeper than the skin but has faded, the priest shall confine him for seven days.
If it spreads in the skin, the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is a disease.
But if the bright spot remains in its place and does not spread, it is the scar of the boil, and the priest shall pronounce him clean.
“Or if the body sustains a burn by fire, and the raw flesh of the burn becomes a reddish-white or white bright spot,

the priest shall inspect it; and if the hair in the bright spot has turned white and it appears deeper than the skin, it is leprosy. It has broken out in the burn, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is an affliction of leprosy.
But if the priest examines it and finds no white hair in the bright spot, and it is not deeper than the skin but has faded, the priest shall confine him for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest shall inspect him; and if it is spreading in the skin, the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is an affliction of leprosy.
But if the bright spot remains in its place and does not spread in the skin, but has faded, it is a swelling from the burn, and the priest shall pronounce him clean, for it is the scar of the burn.”
“When a man or a woman has an affliction on the head or in the beard,

the priest shall inspect the affliction; and if it appears deeper than the skin, with yellow, fine hair in it, the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is a scall, an affliction of leprosy of the head or beard.
If the priest examines the scall and it does not appear deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, the priest shall confine the person with the scall for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest shall inspect the affliction; and if the scall has not spread, and there is no yellow hair in it, and the scall does not appear deeper than the skin,
then he shall shave himself, though he shall not shave the scall, and the priest shall confine the person with the scall for a second period of seven days.

On the seventh day the priest shall inspect the scall; and if the scall has not spread in the skin and does not appear deeper than the skin, the priest shall pronounce him clean. He shall wash his garments and be clean.
“But if the scall spreads in the skin after his cleansing,
the priest shall inspect him; and if the scall has spread in the skin, the priest need not search for yellow hair: he is unclean.
If, however, the scall remains unchanged in his sight and black hair has grown in it, the scall is healed; he is clean, and the priest shall pronounce him clean.
“When a man or a woman has bright spots on the skin of the body, white bright spots,
the priest shall inspect them; and if the bright spots on the skin of the body are of a dull white, it is a benign discoloration that has broken out on the skin: he is clean.
“If a man loses the hair of his head, he is bald; he is clean.
If he loses the hair from the front of his head, he has a bald forehead; he is clean.
But if there is on the bald head or the bald forehead a reddish-white affliction, it is leprosy breaking out on his bald head or forehead.
The priest shall inspect him; and if the swelling of the affliction on his bald head or forehead is reddish-white, like the appearance of leprosy in the skin of the body,
he is a leprous man; he is unclean. The priest shall pronounce him unclean; his affliction is on his head.
“The leper who has the affliction shall wear torn garments, let his hair hang loose, cover his upper lip, and cry out, ‘Unclean, unclean.’
As long as the affliction remains upon him, he is unclean. He is unclean; he shall dwell apart, and his dwelling shall be outside the camp.”
“When an affliction of leprosy appears in a garment, whether a woolen or a linen garment,
or in the warp or the woof of linen or wool, or in a skin, or in anything made of skin,
and if the affliction is greenish or reddish in the garment, in the skin, in the warp, in the woof, or in any article of skin, it is an affliction of leprosy, and it shall be shown to the priest.
The priest shall inspect the affliction and confine the article that bears the affliction for seven days.

On the seventh day he shall inspect the affliction; and if it has spread in the garment, in the warp or the woof, or in the skin—whatever the skin may be used for—the affliction is a persistent leprosy: it is unclean.
He shall burn the garment, the warp, or the woof, whether of wool or linen, or any article of skin in which the affliction is found, for it is a persistent leprosy. It shall be burned in the fire.
“If, however, the priest examines it and the affliction has not spread in the garment, in the warp, or in the woof, or in any article of skin,
the priest shall command that the article bearing the affliction be washed, and he shall confine it for a second period of seven days.

After it has been washed, the priest shall inspect it; and if the appearance of the affliction has not changed, though it has not spread, it is unclean. It shall be burned in the fire; the corruption is on its front or its back.
But if the priest examines it and the afflicted area has faded after washing, he shall tear it out of the garment, the skin, the warp, or the woof.
If it appears again in the garment, the warp, the woof, or any article of skin, it is spreading; the article in which the affliction is found shall be burned in the fire.
But if the affliction departs from the garment, the warp, the woof, or any article of skin when it is washed, it shall be washed a second time and be clean.
This is the law for an affliction of leprosy in a garment of wool or linen, in the warp or the woof, or in any article of skin, for determining whether it is clean or unclean.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“This is the statute governing the leper for the day of his cleansing: he must be conducted to the priest.
The priest shall repair outside the camp and inspect him; and if the leprous malady has been healed in the leper,
“then the priest shall direct that two living, ritually clean birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop be taken for the party undergoing purification.
The priest shall also direct that one of the birds be slain over fresh water in an earthenware vessel.

As for the living bird, he shall take it, together with the cedar wood, the scarlet yarn, and the hyssop, and dip them, along with the living bird, into the blood of the bird that was slain, over the fresh water.
He shall asperse seven times the one being purified from the leprous disease, and shall declare him clean; then he shall set the living bird free over the open country.

“The one being purified shall launder his garments, depilate all his hair, and bathe in water, and he shall be clean; thereafter he may enter the camp, though he shall remain outside his tent for seven days.
On the seventh day he shall remove all his hair—his head, his beard, his eyebrows, and every other hair; he shall wash his garments and bathe his flesh in water, and he shall be clean.
“On the eighth day he shall take two unblemished male lambs, one yearling ewe, three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour commingled with oil as a grain offering, and a log of oil.
The officiating priest shall present the man, together with these offerings, before the the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest shall take one of the lambs and present it as a guilt offering, with the log of oil, and wave them as a wave offering before the the LORD.

He shall slay the lamb at the site where the sin offering and the burnt offering are slaughtered, within the holy place; for the guilt offering, like the sin offering, pertains to the priest and is most holy.
“The priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering and place it on the right earlobe of the one being purified, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall take some of the log of oil and pour it into the hollow of his own left palm.
The priest shall dip his right finger into the oil in his left palm and sprinkle of that oil with his finger seven times before the the LORD.

From the remainder of the oil in his palm, the priest shall place some upon the right earlobe of the one being purified, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, over the blood of the guilt offering.
The leftover oil in the priest's palm he shall apply to the head of the one being purified; and the priest shall make atonement for him before the the LORD.
“Then the priest shall perform the sin offering and effect atonement for the one being purified from his impurity; thereafter he shall slaughter the burnt offering.
The priest shall offer the burnt offering and the grain offering upon the altar; thus the priest shall effect atonement for him, and he shall be clean.

“If, however, he is indigent and his means do not suffice for these provisions, then he shall take one male lamb as a guilt offering, to be waved for his atonement, and one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mingled with oil for a grain offering, together with a log of oil.
And two turtledoves or two young pigeons, according to what he can afford, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.
On the eighth day he shall bring them for his purification to the priest, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the the LORD.
“The priest shall take the lamb of the guilt offering and the log of oil, and wave them as a wave offering before the the LORD.

He shall slaughter the lamb of the guilt offering, and the priest shall take some of its blood and place it on the right earlobe of the one being purified, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall pour some of the oil into the hollow of his own left palm.
The priest shall, with his right finger, sprinkle some of the oil in his left palm seven times before the the LORD.
