“The priest shall put some of the oil that is in his palm on the right earlobe of the one being purified, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on the site of the blood of the guilt offering.
The rest of the oil in the priest's palm he shall put on the head of the one being purified, to make atonement for him before the the LORD.
He shall offer one of the turtledoves or young pigeons, whichever his means allow,
one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, together with the grain offering; and the priest shall make atonement before the the LORD for the one being purified.
This is the statute for the leper afflicted with a leprous disease, whose means do not suffice for the offering customary to his cleansing.”
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
“When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving to you for a possession, and I put a leprous disease in a house in the land of your possession,
then the owner of the house shall come and report to the priest, saying, ‘It appears to me that there is a plague in the house.’
The priest shall direct that the house be emptied before he comes to inspect the plague, lest everything in the house become unclean; then the priest shall come to inspect the house.
“He shall inspect the plague; and if the plague is in the walls of the house as greenish or reddish depressions that appear to sink deeper than the surface of the wall,
then the priest shall withdraw from the house to its doorway and quarantine the house for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest shall return and inspect it; and if the plague has spread in the walls of the house,
then the priest shall order that the stones containing the plague be removed and cast into an unclean place outside the city.
“The interior of the house shall be scraped all around, and the dust scraped off shall be poured out outside the city in an unclean place.
They shall insert other stones in place of the removed stones, and he shall take other mortar and replaster the house.
If the plague breaks out again in the house after he has taken out the stones and after the house has been scraped and plastered,
then the priest shall come and inspect it; and if the plague has spread in the house, it is a malignant leprosy in the house—it is unclean.
“He shall demolish the house—its stones, its timber, and all its mortar—and remove them outside the city to an unclean place.
Furthermore, anyone who enters the house during the whole period of its confinement shall be unclean until evening.
Whoever lies down in the house shall wash his garments, and whoever eats in the house shall wash his garments.
If, however, the priest comes and inspects it and the plague has not spread in the house after it was plastered, then the priest shall declare the house clean, because the plague has healed.
“To purify the house, he shall take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop.
He shall slaughter one of the birds over fresh water in an earthenware vessel.
He shall take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet yarn, and the living bird, dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and in the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
He shall purify the house with the blood of the bird, the fresh water, the living bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the scarlet yarn.
He shall set the living bird free outside the city over the open country; thus he shall make atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.
“This is the statute for every sort of leprous disease and scall,
for the leprosy of a garment and of a house,
and for a swelling, a scab, and a bright spot,
to instruct concerning uncleanness and cleanness. This is the law of leprosy.”
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and declare to them: If any man suffers a morbid discharge from his flesh, that very discharge renders him ritually unclean.
This constitutes his uncleanness in the matter of his discharge: whether his flesh emits the flow or retains it, the condition itself is his uncleanness.
“Every couch upon which the afflicted man lies shall be unclean, and every article upon which he sits shall be unclean.
Anyone who touches his couch shall launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
Anyone who sits upon an article on which the afflicted man has sat shall launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches the flesh of the afflicted man shall launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
If the afflicted man expectorates upon a ritually clean person, the latter shall launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
“Every saddle upon which the afflicted man rides shall be unclean.

Everything beneath him, whatsoever he sits upon, shall impart uncleanness until evening to anyone who touches it; and whoever transports such objects shall launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
Anyone touched by the afflicted man, if he has not rinsed his hands in water, shall launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
Any earthen vessel touched by the afflicted man shall be shattered, whereas any wooden vessel shall be rinsed with water.
“When the afflicted man is cleansed of his discharge, he shall reckon seven days for his purification, launder his garments, bathe his flesh in running water, and thereafter be clean.
On the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, present himself before the the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and deliver them to the priest.
The priest shall render one a sin offering and the other a burnt offering, and shall make atonement for him before the the LORD on account of his discharge.
“If semen is emitted by a man, he shall bathe his entire body in water and remain unclean until evening.
Every garment and every skin upon which semen falls shall be washed in water and remain unclean until evening.
If a woman lies with a man and copulative emission occurs, both shall bathe in water and remain unclean until evening.
“When a woman has a discharge, and her discharge in her flesh is blood, she shall be in her menstrual impurity for seven days; everyone who touches her shall be unclean until evening.
Everything upon which she lies during her menstrual impurity shall be unclean, and everything upon which she sits shall be unclean.
Anyone who touches her bed shall launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches any object upon which she sits shall launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
Whether it is the bed or the object upon which she sits, whoever touches it shall be unclean until evening.
If a man lies with her, her menstrual impurity shall be upon him; he shall be unclean for seven days, and every bed upon which he lies shall be unclean.

“If a woman has a flow of blood for many days outside the time of her menstruation, or if she has a flow beyond her menstrual period, she shall be unclean throughout all the days of her discharge, as in the days of her menstruation.

Every bed upon which she lies during all the days of her discharge shall be to her as the bed of her menstruation, and every object upon which she sits shall be unclean, as in the uncleanness of her menstruation.
Anyone who touches them shall be unclean; he shall launder his garments, bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
If she is cleansed from her discharge, she shall count seven days for herself, and afterward she shall be clean.
On the eighth day she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest shall make one a sin offering and the other a burnt offering, and the priest shall make atonement for her before the the LORD from her discharge.
“Thus you shall separate the Israelites from their uncleanness, lest they die in their uncleanness by defiling My tabernacle that is among them.
This is the law for the one who has a discharge, for the man from whom semen is emitted so that he becomes unclean thereby,
and for the woman in her menstrual impurity, and for the one, male or female, who has a discharge, and for the man who lies with an unclean woman.”
The LORD spoke to Moses after the death of Aaron’s two sons, who had drawn near to the LORD and perished.

The LORD said to Moses, “Tell your brother Aaron that he must not enter the Most Holy Place behind the veil at any time, before the mercy seat that is upon the ark, lest he die; for I will appear in the cloud upon the mercy seat. “
Aaron shall enter the Most Holy Place with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

He shall be vested in the holy linen tunic, with linen undergarments upon his flesh; he shall gird himself with a linen sash and wrap a linen turban about his head. These are the holy garments. He shall bathe his body in water and then put them on.
From the congregation of the Israelites he shall take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
Aaron shall present the bull of the sin offering that is for himself and make atonement for himself and for his household.
He shall take the two goats and set them before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Aaron shall cast lots over the two goats—one lot for the LORD and one lot for Azazel, the scapegoat.
Aaron shall bring the goat upon which the lot for the LORD fell and offer it as a sin offering.
But the goat upon which the lot for Azazel fell shall be presented alive before the LORD, to make atonement over it, that it may be sent away into the wilderness to Azazel. “
Aaron shall bring the bull of the sin offering that is for himself and shall make atonement for himself and for his household, and he shall slaughter the bull of the sin offering that is for himself.
He shall take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD, with his hands full of finely ground sweet incense, and bring them within the veil.
He shall put the incense upon the fire before the LORD, so that the cloud of incense covers the mercy seat that is over the testimony, lest he die.
He shall take some of the blood of the bull and sprinkle it with his finger on the east side of the mercy seat; before the mercy seat he shall sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times.

Then he shall slaughter the goat of the sin offering that is for the people and bring its blood within the veil, and he shall do with its blood as he did with the blood of the bull, sprinkling it upon the mercy seat and before the mercy seat.

Thus he shall make atonement for the sanctuary from the uncleannesses of the Israelites and from their transgressions, for all their sins; and so shall he do for the tent of meeting, which dwells among them in the midst of their uncleanness.

No person shall be in the tent of meeting when he enters to make atonement in the sanctuary until he comes out, having made atonement for himself, for his household, and for all the assembly of Israel.

Then he shall go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it, taking some of the blood of the bull and some of the blood of the goat, and putting it on the horns of the altar all around.
He shall sprinkle some of the blood upon it with his finger seven times, and cleanse it and consecrate it from the uncleannesses of the Israelites. “
When he has finished making atonement for the sanctuary, the tent of meeting, and the altar, he shall bring the live goat.

Aaron shall lay both his hands upon the head of the live goat and confess over it all the iniquities of the Israelites and all their transgressions, even all their sins, putting them upon the head of the goat; and he shall send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a man appointed for the task.
The goat shall bear upon itself all their iniquities to a desolate, uninhabited region; and he shall release the goat in the wilderness.
Then Aaron shall come into the tent of meeting and remove the linen garments that he put on when he went into the sanctuary, and he shall leave them there.

He shall bathe his body in water in a holy place and put on his garments, and he shall come out and offer his burnt offering and the burnt offering of the people, and make atonement for himself and for the people.
The fat of the sin offering he shall burn upon the altar.
He who releases the goat for Azazel shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterward he may come into the camp.

The bull of the sin offering and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the sanctuary, shall be carried outside the camp; their hides, their flesh, and their offal shall be burned with fire.
He who burns them shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterward he may come into the camp. “

This shall be a statute forever for you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you shall deny yourselves and do no work at all, whether the native-born or the foreigner sojourning among you.
For on this day atonement shall be made for you to cleanse you; before the LORD you shall be clean from all your sins.
It is a sabbath of solemn rest for you, and you shall deny yourselves; it is a statute forever.
The priest who is anointed and consecrated to minister in his father’s place shall make atonement, wearing the holy linen garments.
He shall make atonement for the holy sanctuary, for the tent of meeting, for the altar, for the priests, and for all the people of the assembly.”
“This shall be an everlasting statute for you, to make atonement for the Israelites once in the year for all their sins.” And Moses did as the LORD commanded him.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to Aaron, to his sons, and to all the Israelites, and say to them that this is the commandment the LORD has issued:
“Every man of the house of Israel who slaughters an ox, a lamb, or a goat within the camp, or who slaughters it beyond the camp,

yet does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD before the tabernacle of the LORD, that man shall be held guilty of bloodshed; he has shed blood, and he shall be cut off from among his people.

“This provision exists so that the Israelites may bring to the LORD the sacrifices they have been offering in the open field; they shall bring them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting and sacrifice them there as peace offerings to the LORD.
The priest shall sprinkle the blood upon the altar of the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
They shall no longer sacrifice their offerings to the goat demons after which they prostitute themselves. This shall be a perpetual statute for them throughout their generations.
“And you shall say to them: Any man of the house of Israel, or of the strangers who sojourn among them, who offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice,
and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it to the LORD, that man shall be cut off from his people.

“And any man of the house of Israel, or of the strangers sojourning among them, who eats any blood—I will set My face against that person who eats the blood, and I will cut him off from among his people.
For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you upon the altar to make atonement for your souls; for it is the blood that makes atonement for the soul.
“Therefore I said to the Israelites, ‘No person among you shall eat blood, nor shall the stranger who sojourns among you eat blood.’
“And any man of the Israelites, or of the strangers sojourning among them, who hunts down a beast or a bird that may be eaten shall pour out its blood and cover it with earth.
For the life of all flesh is its blood. Therefore I said to the Israelites, ‘You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood; whoever eats it shall be cut off.’

“And every person, whether native or stranger, who eats what dies of itself or what is torn by beasts shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening; then he shall be clean.
But if he does not wash them or bathe his body, he shall bear his iniquity.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them, ‘I am the LORD your God.
You shall not do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you dwelt, nor as they do in the land of Canaan, to which I am bringing you; you shall not walk in their statutes.
You shall follow My ordinances and keep My statutes, walking in them; I am the LORD your God.
You shall keep My statutes and My ordinances, which a person shall do and live by them; I am the LORD.
“None of you shall approach a close relative by blood for sexual relations; I am the LORD.
“You shall not have sexual relations with your mother; she is your mother, and you shall not have sexual relations with her.
You shall not have sexual relations with your father’s wife, for that would expose your father’s nakedness.
You shall not have sexual relations with your sister, whether she is your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter, whether she was raised in the same household or elsewhere.
You shall not have sexual relations with your granddaughter, whether your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter, for their nakedness is your own.
You shall not have sexual relations with the daughter of your father’s wife if she was raised in your father’s household, for she is your sister.
“You shall not have sexual relations with your father’s sister, for she is your father’s close relative.
You shall not have sexual relations with your mother’s sister, for she is your mother’s close relative.
You shall not have sexual relations with your father’s brother—that is, with his wife—for she is your aunt.
You shall not have sexual relations with your daughter-in-law, for she is your son’s wife.
You shall not have sexual relations with your brother’s wife, for she belongs to your brother.

“You shall not marry a woman and her daughter, or her granddaughter through her son or daughter, in order to have sexual relations with them; they are her close relatives, and such a union is depravity.
You shall not marry a woman and then her sister as a rival, having sexual relations with the second while the first is still alive.
You shall not approach a woman to have sexual relations with her during her menstrual uncleanness.
You shall not have sexual relations with your neighbor’s wife, thereby defiling yourself.
You shall not give any of your children to be sacrificed to Molech, nor profane the name of your God; I am the LORD.
You shall not have sexual relations with a man as with a woman; that is detestable.
You shall not have sexual relations with any animal, defiling yourself with it; and no woman shall present herself to an animal for mating, for that is a perversion.
“Do not defile yourselves in any of these ways, for by all these things the nations that I am driving out before you have defiled themselves.
The land became defiled, so I punished its iniquity, and the land vomited out its inhabitants.
“You shall keep My statutes and My ordinances, and you shall not do any of these abominations, whether the native or the resident alien dwelling among you.
For the people of the land who were before you did all these abominations, and the land became defiled.
Otherwise the land will vomit you out when you make it unclean, just as it vomited out the nation that was before you.
For everyone who does any of these abominations shall be cut off from among his people.
So keep My charge, that you do not practice any of these abominable customs that were practiced before you, and that you do not defile yourselves by them; I am the LORD your God.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the entire congregation of the Israelites and say to them, 'You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.
"'Each of you shall revere his mother and his father, and you shall keep My Sabbaths; I am the LORD your God.
Do not turn to idols, nor make for yourselves molten gods. I am the LORD your God.
"'When you offer a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD, you shall offer it for your acceptance.
It shall be eaten the day you offer it and on the morrow; and what remains until the third day shall be burned with fire.
If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is an abomination; it shall not be accepted.
And everyone who eats it shall bear his iniquity, because he has profaned the holy thing of the LORD, and that soul shall be cut off from his people.
"'When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not wholly reap the corner of your field, nor shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest.
And you shall not glean your vineyard, nor shall you gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the poor and the sojourner. I am the LORD your God.
"'You shall not steal; you shall not deal falsely; you shall not lie to one another.
You shall not swear falsely by My name, so as to profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
You shall not oppress your neighbor or rob him. The wages of a hired worker shall not remain with you until morning.
You shall not curse the deaf, nor put a stumbling block before the blind, but you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.
"'You shall do no injustice in judgment; you shall not be partial to the poor, nor defer to the great; but in righteousness you shall judge your neighbor.
You shall not spread slander among your people, and you shall not endanger the life of your neighbor. I am the LORD.
You shall not hate your brother in your heart; you shall surely rebuke your neighbor, and not bear sin because of him.
You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against the children of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
"'You shall keep My statutes. You shall not breed your livestock with a different kind; you shall not sow your field with mixed seed; nor shall a garment of mixed fabrics come upon you.

If a man lies with a woman who is a slave, betrothed to another man and not yet ransomed or given her freedom, there must be due punishment; they shall not be put to death, because she had not been freed.
He shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, a ram for a guilt offering.
And the priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD for the sin which he has committed, and the sin which he has committed shall be forgiven him.
"'When you come into the land and plant all kinds of trees for food, you shall regard their fruit as forbidden; for three years it shall be forbidden to you; it shall not be eaten.
But in the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, a praise offering to the LORD.
And in the fifth year you may eat its fruit, to increase its yield for you. I am the LORD your God.
"'You shall not eat anything with the blood, nor shall you practice divination or sorcery.
You shall not round off the hair at your temples, nor mar the edges of your beard.
You shall not make any cuts in your flesh for the dead, nor tattoo any marks on yourselves. I am the LORD.
Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, lest the land fall into prostitution and the land become full of depravity.
You shall keep My Sabbaths and revere My sanctuary. I am the LORD.
Do not turn to mediums or spiritists; do not seek them out, to be defiled by them. I am the LORD your God.
You shall rise up before the gray-headed and honor the presence of an old man, and you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.
"'When a stranger sojourns with you in your land, you shall not do him wrong.
The stranger who sojourns with you shall be to you as the native among you, and you shall love him as yourself, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
You shall do no wrong in judgment, in measures of length or weight or quantity.
You shall have just balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
And you shall observe all My statutes and all My ordinances and do them. I am the LORD.'"
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

“Say to the Israelites: Any Israelite, or any sojourner dwelling among the Israelites, who offers any of his offspring to Molech shall surely be put to death; the people of the land shall stone him with stones.
“I Myself will set My face against that man and cut him off from among his people, because he has given of his offspring to Molech, thereby defiling My sanctuary and profaning My holy name.
If the people of the land deliberately close their eyes to that man when he gives of his offspring to Molech and do not put him to death,
then I will set My face against that man and against his family, and I will cut him off—together with all who prostitute themselves by following him into Molech's service—from among their people.
“Any person who turns to mediums or to spiritists in order to prostitute himself with them—I will set My face against that person and cut him off from among his people.
“Sanctify yourselves, therefore, and be holy, for I am the LORD your God.
Keep My statutes and practice them; I am the LORD, who sanctifies you.
“Anyone who curses his father or his mother must be put to death; because he has cursed his father or his mother, his blood is upon him.
If a man commits adultery with another man's wife—with the wife of his neighbor—both the adulterer and the adulteress must be put to death.
“If a man lies with his father's wife, he has uncovered his father's nakedness; both of them must be put to death, and their blood is upon them.
If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both must be put to death; they have committed a perversion, and their blood is upon them.
If a man lies with a male as with a woman, both have committed an abomination; they must be put to death, and their blood is upon them.
If a man marries a woman and her mother, that is depravity; he and they shall be burned with fire, so that there may be no depravity among you.
“If a man has sexual relations with an animal, he must be put to death, and you shall kill the animal.
If a woman approaches any animal to mate with it, you shall kill the woman and the animal; they must be put to death, and their blood is upon them.

“If a man takes his sister, whether his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her nakedness, and she sees his nakedness, it is a disgrace; they shall be cut off in the sight of their people. He has uncovered his sister's nakedness and shall bear his iniquity.

If a man lies with a woman during her menstrual flow and uncovers her nakedness—having exposed the source of her flow—and she uncovers the source of her blood, both of them shall be cut off from among their people.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister or of your father's sister, for one who does so has uncovered his near kin; they shall bear their iniquity.
If a man lies with his aunt—that is, his uncle's wife—he has uncovered his uncle's nakedness; they shall bear their sin and die childless.
If a man takes his brother's wife, it is impurity; he has uncovered his brother's nakedness, and they shall be childless.
“You shall keep all My statutes and all My ordinances and do them, so that the land to which I am bringing you to dwell in it will not vomit you out.
You shall not follow the statutes of the nations I am driving out before you, for they did all these things, and I abhorred them.
I have said to you that you shall inherit their land, and I will give it to you to possess—a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the LORD your God, who has separated you from the peoples.

“You shall distinguish between the clean and the unclean among beasts, and between the unclean and the clean among birds; and you shall not make yourselves detestable by beast, by bird, or by anything that creeps on the ground, which I have set apart as unclean for you.
You shall be holy to Me, for I am the LORD, holy, and I have separated you from the peoples to be Mine.
Any man or woman who is a medium or a spiritist must be put to death; they shall be stoned with stones, and their blood is upon them.”
The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to Aaron and his sons and say to them: 'No member of his people may render himself ceremonially unclean for a dead person,
except for his nearest kin—his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, and his brother—or
his sister, a virgin still bound to his household, who has never been given to a husband; on her account he may incur defilement.
He shall not defile himself for a relative by marriage among his people, lest he profane himself.
They shall not tonsure their heads, nor trim the extremities of their beards, nor gash their flesh.
They shall be consecrated unto their God, and they shall not profane the name of their God, because they present the LORD's offerings made by fire, the bread of their God; hence they must be holy.
They shall not take a wife who has been profaned by harlotry, nor one dismissed by her husband, for the priest is consecrated unto his God.
You shall sanctify him, for he presents the bread of your God; he shall be holy unto you, because I, the LORD, am holy, and I am He who sanctifies you.
If a priest's daughter profanes herself by playing the harlot, she profanes her father; she shall be burned with fire. "'
The high priest, preeminent among his brethren, upon whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been consecrated to wear the garments, shall not dishevel his hair nor rend his garments.
He shall not come near any dead body, nor shall he defile himself, even for his father or his mother.
He shall not leave the sanctuary, nor shall he profane the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is upon him. I am the LORD.
He shall take a wife in her virginity.
A widow, or a divorced woman, or one profaned by harlotry—these he shall not take; but he shall take a virgin from his own people as wife,
so that he does not defile his offspring among his people, for I am the LORD who sanctifies him.'"
The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to Aaron and say, '
No man among your descendants throughout their generations who has a blemish shall approach to offer the bread of his God.
For no man who has a blemish shall approach—neither a blind man, nor a lame man, nor a mutilated man, nor a man with a withered limb—
nor a man with a broken foot or a broken hand,
nor a hunchback or a dwarf, nor one with a blemish in his eye, nor one suffering from scabs or scurf, nor one with crushed testicles. "'
No descendant of Aaron the priest who has a blemish shall approach to present the LORD's offerings made by fire; because he has a blemish, he shall not approach to offer the bread of his God.
He may eat the most holy food of his God, as well as the holy food,
but because he has a blemish, he shall not approach the veil nor come near the altar, lest he profane My sanctuaries, for I am the LORD who sanctifies them.'"
So Moses spoke these words to Aaron, to his sons, and to all the Israelites.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to Aaron and his sons, that they separate themselves from the sacred offerings of the sons of Israel, which they consecrate to Me, and that they not desecrate My holy name: I am the LORD.

“Say to them, ‘Throughout your generations, any man among all your descendants who, having an uncleanness upon him, approaches the sacred offerings that the sons of Israel consecrate to the LORD—that person shall be cut off from My presence: I am the LORD.

None of the descendants of Aaron who has a leprous disease or a discharge may partake of the sacred offerings until he is purified. Whoever touches anything unclean through contact with the dead, or a man who has had an emission of semen,
and whoever touches any swarming thing by which he may be made unclean, or a person from whom he may contract uncleanness, according to all his uncleanness—
the person who touches such a thing shall remain unclean until the evening and shall not partake of the sacred offerings unless he has bathed his flesh in water.
At sunset he shall be clean, and thereafter he may partake of the sacred offerings, for it is his food.
He shall not eat that which dies of itself or is torn by beasts, lest he defile himself therewith: I am the LORD.
They shall therefore keep My charge, lest they incur guilt for it and die thereby when they profane it: I am the LORD who sanctifies them.’
“No outsider shall eat of a sacred offering; neither a guest of the priest nor a hired laborer shall eat of a sacred offering.
But if a priest acquires a person with his silver, that person may eat of it, and those born in his house may eat of his food.
If a priest’s daughter is given to a layman, she shall not eat of the sacred contribution.
But if a priest’s daughter is widowed or divorced, having no offspring, and returns to her father’s house as in her youth, she may eat of her father’s food; yet no outsider shall eat of it.
“And if anyone eats of a sacred offering inadvertently, he shall add a fifth of its valuation to it and give the sacred offering to the priest.
They shall not desecrate the sacred offerings of the sons of Israel, which they offer to the LORD,
and so make them bear the iniquity of trespass in their eating of their sacred things: for I am the LORD who sanctifies them.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

“Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the sons of Israel, and say to them, ‘When any man of the house of Israel or of the sojourners in Israel presents his offering to the LORD, whether for any of their vows or for any of their freewill offerings that they offer to the LORD as a burnt offering,
“‘it must be a male without blemish, from the cattle, from the sheep, or from the goats, to be accepted for you.
You shall not offer anything that has a blemish, for it will not be acceptable for you.

And when anyone offers a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD, to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering, from the cattle or from the flock, to be accepted it must be perfect; there shall be no blemish in it.

Beasts that are blind, or fractured, or maimed, or afflicted with a running issue, or scurvy, or scabbed—you shall not offer these to the LORD, nor make of them a fire offering upon the altar to the LORD.
“‘You may offer a bull or a lamb that has an elongated or truncated member as a freewill offering, but for a vow it shall not be accepted.
You shall not offer to the LORD any animal whose testicles are bruised, crushed, torn, or severed; neither shall you do so in your land.
Nor shall you accept from the hand of a foreigner any of these to offer as the bread of your God, because their corruption is in them and a blemish is in them; they shall not be accepted for you.’”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“When an ox or sheep or goat is born, it shall remain seven days with its mother, and from the eighth day onward it shall be accepted as a fire offering to the LORD.
You shall not slaughter an ox or a sheep and its young in one day.
“And when you offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving to the LORD, you shall offer it so that you may be accepted.
It shall be eaten on that day; you shall leave none of it until morning: I am the LORD.
You shall therefore keep My commandments and do them: I am the LORD.
And you shall not desecrate My holy name, that I may be sanctified among the sons of Israel. I am the LORD who sanctifies you,
who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God: I am the LORD.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the Israelites and instruct them: These are My appointed feasts, the holy convocations of the LORD that you are to proclaim at their appointed times.
"For six days labor may be performed, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of solemn rest, a holy convocation. You are not to perform any work; wherever you dwell, it is a Sabbath to the LORD.
"These are the LORD's appointed feasts, the holy convocations that you are to proclaim at their appointed times.
The LORD's Passover begins at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month.
"On the fifteenth day of the same month begins the Feast of Unleavened Bread to the LORD. For seven days you must eat unleavened bread.
On the first day you are to hold a holy convocation; you are not to do any ordinary work.
For seven days you are to present an offering made by fire to the LORD. On the seventh day is a holy convocation; you are not to do any ordinary work."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land I am bestowing upon you and reap its harvest, you are to bring to the priest a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest.
He shall wave the sheaf before the LORD so that it may be accepted on your behalf; the priest is to wave it on the day after the Sabbath.
"On the day you wave the sheaf, you are to offer a year-old lamb without blemish as a burnt offering to the LORD,
along with its grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil—an offering made by fire to the LORD, a pleasing aroma—and its drink offering of a quarter hin of wine.
You must not eat any bread or roasted grain or new grain until the very day you bring this offering to your God. This is to be a perpetual statute for the generations to come, wherever you live.
"From the day after the Sabbath, the day you brought the sheaf of the wave offering, you are to count off seven full weeks.
Count off fifty days up to the day after the seventh Sabbath, and then present an offering of new grain to the LORD.
From wherever you live, you are to bring two loaves of bread as a wave offering, made of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour, baked with leaven, as firstfruits to the LORD.

"Along with the bread you are to present seven unblemished year-old male lambs, one young bull, and two rams. They will be a burnt offering to the LORD, together with their grain offerings and drink offerings—an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
You are also to prepare one male goat as a sin offering and two year-old male lambs as a peace offering.
The priest is to wave the two lambs as a wave offering before the LORD, together with the bread of the firstfruits. The bread and the two lambs shall be holy to the LORD for the priest.
"On that same day you are to proclaim a holy convocation; you are not to do any ordinary work. This is to be a perpetual statute wherever you live for the generations to come.

When you reap the harvest of your land, you are not to reap to the very edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest. Leave them for the poor and the sojourner. I am the LORD your God."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the Israelites and say: On the first day of the seventh month you are to have a day of solemn rest, a holy convocation commemorated with trumpet blasts.
You are not to do any ordinary work, but you are to present an offering made by fire to the LORD."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"The tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. You are to hold a holy convocation and humble yourselves, and present an offering made by fire to the LORD.
On this day you are not to do any work, for it is a Day of Atonement to make atonement for you before the LORD your God.
"If anyone does not humble himself on this day, he must be cut off from his people.
I will destroy anyone who does any work on this day.
"You are not to do any work. This is to be a perpetual statute for the generations to come, wherever you live.
It is a Sabbath of solemn rest for you, and you shall humble yourselves. From the evening of the ninth day of the month until the following evening you are to keep your Sabbath."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Speak to the Israelites and say: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month the Feast of Tabernacles to the LORD begins, and it lasts for seven days.
On the first day there is to be a holy convocation; you are not to do any ordinary work.

For seven days you are to present an offering made by fire to the LORD. On the eighth day you are to hold a holy convocation and present an offering made by fire to the LORD. It is a solemn assembly; you are not to do any ordinary work.

"These are the LORD's appointed feasts, which you are to proclaim as holy convocations for presenting offerings made by fire to the LORD—burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices, and drink offerings, each on its designated day.
These offerings are in addition to the LORD's Sabbaths and in addition to your gifts, your vows, and all your freewill offerings that you give to the LORD.

On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, after you have gathered the produce of the land, you are to celebrate a feast to the LORD for seven days. There shall be complete rest on the first day and complete rest on the eighth day.
"On the first day you are to take the branches of majestic trees—palm branches, boughs of leafy trees, and willows of the brook—and rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.
You are to celebrate this feast to the LORD for seven days each year. This is to be a perpetual statute for the generations to come; you are to celebrate it in the seventh month.
"You are to dwell in booths for seven days. All the native-born of Israel must dwell in booths,
so that your generations may know that I made the Israelites dwell in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God."
So Moses declared to the Israelites the appointed feasts of the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Command the sons of Israel to bring to you clear oil of pressed olives for the light, that the lamp may burn continually.
Outside the veil of the Testimony, in the tent of meeting, Aaron shall arrange it from evening until morning before the LORD continually; it shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations.
He shall arrange the lamps on the pure lampstand before the LORD continually.”
“And you shall take fine flour and bake it into twelve cakes; two-tenths of an ephah shall be in each cake.
You shall set them in two rows, six in a row, on the pure table before the LORD.
You shall put pure frankincense on each row, that it may be a memorial portion for the bread, an offering by fire to the LORD.
Every Sabbath day he shall arrange it before the LORD continually, as a covenant forever from the sons of Israel.
It shall belong to Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat it in a holy place, for it is most holy to them among the offerings by fire to the LORD, a perpetual statute.”
Now the son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the sons of Israel; and the son of the Israelite woman and an Israelite man quarreled in the camp.
The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name and cursed; so they brought him to Moses. His mother was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
They put him in custody, that the adjudication might be declared to them from the mouth of the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Bring the blasphemer outside the camp, and let all who heard him lay their hands on his head; then let all the congregation stone him.
And speak to the sons of Israel, saying, ‘Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin.

Whoever blasphemes the Name of the LORD shall surely be put to death; all the congregation shall stone him. The foreigner and the native-born alike shall be put to death when he blasphemes the Name.’”
“Whoever strikes any person mortally shall surely be put to death.
Whoever strikes an animal shall make restitution for it, life for life.
If a man causes a disfigurement in his neighbor, as he has done, so shall it be done to him:
fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. As he caused a disfigurement in a man, so shall it be given to him.
Whoever strikes an animal shall make restitution for it, and whoever strikes a man shall be put to death.
You shall have one standard of judgment for the foreigner and for the native-born, for I am the LORD your God.”
Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, and they brought the blasphemer outside the camp and stoned him with stones. The sons of Israel did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying,
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land that I am giving to you, the land itself shall observe a Sabbath to the LORD.
For six years you shall sow your field, and for six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather its produce;
but in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land—a Sabbath to the LORD. You shall not sow your field or prune your vineyard.
You shall not reap the aftergrowth of your harvest, nor shall you gather the grapes of your unpruned vines; it shall be a year of solemn rest for the land.

Whatever the land yields during its Sabbath shall be food for you—for yourself, your male and female servants, your hired laborer, and the resident alien who dwells with you—as well as for your livestock and the wild animals in your land; all its yield shall be for food.
All its produce shall be for food.
You shall count seven weeks of years, seven times seven years, so that the seven weeks of years amount to forty-nine years.
Then you shall sound a trumpet blast on the tenth day of the seventh month; on the Day of Atonement you shall sound the trumpet throughout all your land.

You shall consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee for you, when each of you shall return to his property and each of you shall return to his clan.
That fiftieth year shall be a jubilee for you; in it you shall neither sow nor reap the aftergrowth, nor gather the grapes from the unpruned vines.
For it is a jubilee; it shall be holy to you, and you may eat the produce of the field.
In this year of jubilee each of you shall return to his property.
And if you make a sale to your neighbor or buy from your neighbor, you shall not wrong one another.
You shall buy from your neighbor according to the number of years after the jubilee, and he shall sell to you according to the number of years of crops.
If the years are many, you shall increase the price; if the years are few, you shall decrease the price, for it is the number of crops that he is selling to you.
You shall not wrong one another, but you shall fear your God, for I am the LORD your God.
Therefore you shall carry out My statutes, keep My ordinances, and perform them, so that you may dwell securely in the land.
The land will yield its fruit, and you will eat your fill and dwell securely upon it.
And if you ask, "What shall we eat in the seventh year, since we may not sow or gather our crop?"
I will command My blessing upon you in the sixth year, so that it produces a crop sufficient for three years.
When you sow in the eighth year, you will still be eating from the old crop; you shall eat the old until the ninth year, when its crop comes in.
The land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is Mine; for you are strangers and sojourners with Me.
In all the land of your possession, you shall provide for the redemption of the land.
If your brother becomes poor and sells part of his property, then his nearest redeemer shall come and redeem what his brother has sold.

If a man has no one to redeem it, yet his hand attains enough and he finds sufficient for its redemption, he shall calculate the years since its sale and repay the balance to the man to whom he sold it, and so return to his property.
He shall calculate the years of its sale and restore the surplus to the man to whom he sold it, and then he shall return to his property.

But if his hand has not attained enough to recover it, then what he sold shall remain in the hand of the buyer until the year of jubilee; in the jubilee it shall be released, and he shall return to his property.
If a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, he may redeem it until the end of the year of its sale; for a full year he shall have the right of redemption.
If it is not redeemed within a full year, then the house in the walled city shall belong permanently to the buyer and his descendants; it shall not be released in the jubilee.
But the houses in villages that have no wall around them shall be reckoned with the fields of the land; they may be redeemed, and they shall be released in the jubilee.
As for the cities of the Levites, the houses in the cities of their possession may be redeemed by the Levites at any time.

If one of the Levites redeems a house, then in the jubilee the sold house shall be released and he shall return to his possession, because the houses in the Levites' cities are their possession among the Israelites.
But the fields of pastureland belonging to their cities may not be sold, for that is their perpetual possession.
If your brother becomes poor and cannot maintain himself with you, you shall support him as a stranger and a sojourner, and he shall live with you.
You shall take no interest or profit from him, but you shall fear your God, so that your brother may live with you.
You shall not lend him your money at interest, nor give him your food for profit.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
If your brother becomes poor beside you and sells himself to you, you shall not make him serve as a slave;
he shall be with you as a hired worker and as a sojourner. He shall serve with you until the year of jubilee.
Then he and his children with him shall go out from you and return to his clan and to the possession of his fathers.
For they are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt; they shall not be sold as slaves.
You shall not rule over him ruthlessly, but you shall fear your God.
As for your male and female slaves whom you may have, you may buy male and female slaves from the nations around you.
You may also buy them from the strangers who sojourn with you and from their clans born in your land, and they may be your property.
You may bequeath them to your children after you to inherit as property. You may make them serve you forever. But as for your brothers, the Israelites, no one shall rule over his brother ruthlessly.
If a stranger or sojourner with you becomes rich, and your brother beside him becomes poor and sells himself to the stranger or sojourner with you, or to a member of the stranger's clan,
then after he is sold he may be redeemed. One of his brothers may redeem him,
or his uncle or his cousin may redeem him, or a close relative from his clan may redeem him; or if he grows rich, he may redeem himself.

He shall calculate with his buyer from the year he sold himself to him until the year of jubilee, and the price of his sale shall be according to the number of years; he shall be counted with him as a hired worker.
If there are still many years left, he shall pay for his redemption in proportion to them from the money of his sale.
If there are few years left until the year of jubilee, he shall calculate and pay for his redemption in proportion to the years.
He shall be with him as a worker hired year by year; he shall not be ruled over ruthlessly in your sight.
And if he is not redeemed by these means, then he and his children with him shall go out in the year of jubilee.
For to Me the Israelites are servants; they are My servants whom I brought out of the land of Egypt: I am the LORD your God."

You shall not fabricate idols for yourselves, nor shall you erect a carved image or a sacred pillar; neither shall you install a sculpted stone within your land so as to prostrate yourselves before it, for I am the LORD your God.
You shall keep My Sabbaths and hold My sanctuary in awe, for I am the LORD.
If you walk according to My statutes, observe My commandments, and carry them into practice,
I will grant your rains in their due season, so that the land yields its produce and the trees of the field give their fruit.
Your harvests shall be so abundant that threshing overtakes vintage and vintage overtakes sowing; you shall eat your bread to fullness and dwell securely in your land.
I will establish peace in the land, so that you lie down without fear; I will rid the land of dangerous beasts, and no sword shall traverse your land.
You shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sword.
Five of you shall put a hundred to flight, and a hundred of you ten thousand; and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.
I will turn My regard toward you, make you fruitful, multiply you, and establish My covenant with you.
You shall eat grain long stored, and you shall clear out the old to make way for the new.
I will set My dwelling in your midst, and My soul shall not abhor you.
I will walk among you and be your God, and you shall be My people.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you should not remain their slaves; I shattered the bars of your yoke and caused you to walk upright.
But if you do not listen to Me and do not perform all these commandments,
and if you spurn My statutes and your soul abhors My ordinances, so that you fail to perform all My commandments and thereby break My covenant,

then I will do this to you: I will appoint over you sudden terror, wasting disease, and burning fever, which shall waste the eyes and consume the soul; you shall sow your seed in vain, and your enemies shall devour it.
I will set My face against you, and you shall be smitten before your enemies; those who hate you shall dominate you, and you shall flee though no one pursues.
And if, in spite of these things, you do not listen to Me, I will chastise you sevenfold for your sins.
I will break the pride of your power and make your heavens like iron and your earth like bronze.
Your strength shall be expended in vain, for your land shall not yield its produce, and the trees of the land shall not bear their fruit.
And if you persist in opposing Me and refuse to listen to Me, I will multiply plagues upon you sevenfold, according to your sins.
I will send wild beasts among you, which shall rob you of your children, destroy your cattle, diminish you, and leave your roads desolate.
And if by these things you are not corrected by Me, but persist in opposing Me,
then I too will oppose you and strike you sevenfold for your sins.
I will bring upon you a sword that avenges the covenant; you shall be gathered into your cities, and I will send pestilence among you, and you shall be delivered into the enemy's hand.
When I withhold the bread that sustains you, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven and shall return your bread by weight; you shall eat and not be satisfied.
And if, notwithstanding this, you will not listen to Me, but persist in opposing Me,
then I will oppose you in furious wrath, and I too will chastise you sevenfold for your sins.
You shall eat the flesh of your sons and the flesh of your daughters.
I will destroy your high places, cut down your incense altars, and cast your corpses upon the corpses of your idols, and My soul shall abhor you.
I will reduce your cities to ruins and desolate your sanctuaries, and I will take no delight in the fragrance of your offerings.
I Myself will desolate the land, so that your enemies who dwell in it shall be appalled at it.
I will scatter you among the nations and draw out the sword after you; your land shall become a desolation, and your cities shall become ruins.
Then the land shall enjoy its Sabbaths throughout the days of its desolation, while you are in your enemies' land; then the land shall rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
Throughout all the days of its desolation it shall rest, because it did not rest during your Sabbaths when you dwelt upon it.

As for those who survive among you, I will send faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies; the sound of a driven leaf shall put them to flight, and they shall flee as from the sword and fall though no one pursues.
They shall stumble, one over another, as before the sword, though no one pursues; and you shall have no power to stand before your enemies.
You shall perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies shall devour you.
Those who survive among you shall waste away in their iniquity in the lands of your enemies, and they shall also waste away in the iniquities of their fathers with them.
They shall confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers, in the treachery by which they betrayed Me, and also that they persisted in opposing Me.
So I also persisted in opposing them and brought them into the land of their enemies—if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled and they accept the punishment of their iniquity,
then I will remember My covenant with Jacob, and also My covenant with Isaac, and also My covenant with Abraham will I remember, and I will remember the land.

The land shall be abandoned by them and shall enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies desolate without them; and they shall accept the punishment of their iniquity, because they rejected My ordinances and their soul abhorred My statutes.
Yet even so, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or abhor them so as to destroy them utterly and break My covenant with them, for I am the LORD their God.
But I will remember for them the covenant of their forefathers, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be their God: I am the LORD.
These are the statutes and the ordinances and the laws which the LORD made between Him and the children of Israel on Mount Sinai by the hand of Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: If anyone makes a special vow to the LORD, involving the valuation of persons,
then your valuation of a male from twenty to sixty years of age shall be fifty shekels of silver, according to the shekel of the sanctuary.
And if it is a female, your valuation shall be thirty shekels.
“If the person is from five to twenty years old, your valuation for the male shall be twenty shekels, and for the female ten shekels.
If the person is from one month to five years old, your valuation for the male shall be five shekels of silver, and for the female three shekels of silver.
And if the person is sixty years old or more, your valuation for the male shall be fifteen shekels, and for the female ten shekels.

But if he is too impoverished to meet your valuation, then he shall present himself before the priest, and the priest shall value him; according to what the one making the vow can afford, the priest shall value him.
“If the vowed gift is an animal that may be brought as an offering to the LORD, everything of it that is given to the LORD shall be holy.
He shall not exchange it or substitute for it, good for bad or bad for good; and if he does substitute one animal for another, then both it and its substitute shall be holy.
“If it is any unclean animal that may not be offered as an offering to the LORD, then he shall present the animal before the priest.
And the priest shall value it, whether it is good or bad; as the priest values it, so it shall be.
But if he wishes to redeem it, he shall add a fifth to your valuation.
“When a man dedicates his house as holy to the LORD, the priest shall value it, whether it is good or bad; as the priest values it, so it shall stand.
And if he who dedicated it wishes to redeem his house, he shall add a fifth of the valuation in silver, and it shall become his again.
“If a man dedicates to the LORD part of the field of his possession, then your valuation shall be in proportion to its seed: a homer of barley seed shall be valued at fifty shekels of silver.
If he dedicates his field from the Year of Jubilee, according to your valuation it shall stand.

But if he dedicates his field after the Jubilee, then the priest shall calculate the price for him according to the years remaining until the Year of Jubilee, and a deduction shall be made from your valuation.
And if he who dedicated the field wishes to redeem it, he shall add a fifth of the value in silver, and it shall be restored to him.
“But if he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed any further.
But when the field is released in the Jubilee, it shall be holy to the LORD, like a devoted field; the priest shall take possession of it.
If he dedicates to the LORD a field which he has bought, which is not of the field of his possession,
then the priest shall calculate for him the amount of your valuation up to the Year of Jubilee, and he shall give the valuation on that day as holy to the LORD.
In the Year of Jubilee the field shall return to him from whom it was bought, to whom the land belonged as a possession.
Every valuation shall be according to the shekel of the sanctuary: twenty gerahs to the shekel.
“But the firstborn among animals, which as a firstborn belongs to the LORD, no one shall dedicate; whether ox or sheep, it belongs to the LORD.
And if it is an unclean animal, then he shall redeem it according to your valuation, and shall add a fifth to it; or if it is not redeemed, then it shall be sold according to your valuation.
But anything that a man devotes to the LORD, of all that he has, whether man or beast, or of the field of his possession, shall not be sold or redeemed; every devoted thing is most holy to the LORD.
No person devoted to destruction among humankind shall be redeemed; he shall surely be put to death.
“Every tithe of the land, whether of the seed of the land or of the fruit of the trees, is the LORD's; it is holy to the LORD.
If a man redeems any of his tithe, he shall add a fifth to it.
And every tithe of the herd or flock, every tenth that passes under the rod, shall be holy to the LORD.
He shall not inquire whether it is good or bad, nor shall he exchange it; and if he does exchange it, then both it and its substitute shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.”
These are the commandments which the LORD commanded Moses for the sons of Israel on Mount Sinai.
On the first day of the second month, in the second year after Israel's departure from Egypt, the LORD addressed Moses within the tent of meeting in the wilderness of Sinai, declaring,
“Take a census of the entire congregation of the sons of Israel, organized by their clans and patriarchal houses, reckoning every male by name and by head.
You and Aaron shall enumerate those twenty years of age and older, every man fit to march in Israel's host, mustering them according to their military divisions.
And with you there shall be one man from each tribe, each the head of his patriarchal house.
“These are the names of the men who shall stand with you: from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;
from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;
from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;
from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;
from the sons of Joseph—from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud, and from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;
from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
from Asher, Pagiel son of Ochran;
from Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel;
from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.”
These were the men summoned from the congregation—leaders of their ancestral tribes and heads of Israel's thousands.
Moses and Aaron took these men, who had been designated by name,

and on the first day of the second month they convened the whole congregation; the people registered themselves by clans and patriarchal houses, by the number of names, from twenty years old and upward, head by head.
Thus he enumerated them in the wilderness of Sinai, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The descendants of Reuben, Israel's firstborn, were recorded by their generations, clans, and patriarchal houses, every male from twenty years old and upward who could go out to war.
The enumeration of the tribe of Reuben amounted to forty-six thousand five hundred.
The descendants of Simeon were recorded by their generations, clans, and patriarchal houses, every male from twenty years old and upward who could go out to war.
The enumeration of the tribe of Simeon amounted to fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
The descendants of Gad were recorded by their generations, clans, and patriarchal houses, every male from twenty years old and upward who could go out to war.
The enumeration of the tribe of Gad amounted to forty-five thousand six hundred fifty.
The descendants of Judah were recorded by their generations, clans, and patriarchal houses, every male from twenty years old and upward who could go out to war.
The enumeration of the tribe of Judah amounted to seventy-four thousand six hundred.
The descendants of Issachar were recorded by their generations, clans, and patriarchal houses, every male from twenty years old and upward who could go out to war.
The enumeration of the tribe of Issachar amounted to fifty-four thousand four hundred.
The descendants of Zebulun were recorded by their generations, clans, and patriarchal houses, every male from twenty years old and upward who could go out to war.
The enumeration of the tribe of Zebulun amounted to fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
The descendants of Joseph—namely, the descendants of Ephraim—were recorded by their generations, clans, and patriarchal houses, every male from twenty years old and upward who could go out to war.
The enumeration of the tribe of Ephraim amounted to forty thousand five hundred.
The descendants of Manasseh were recorded by their generations, clans, and patriarchal houses, every male from twenty years old and upward who could go out to war.
The enumeration of the tribe of Manasseh amounted to thirty-two thousand two hundred.
The descendants of Benjamin were recorded by their generations, clans, and patriarchal houses, every male from twenty years old and upward who could go out to war.
The enumeration of the tribe of Benjamin amounted to thirty-five thousand four hundred.
The descendants of Dan were recorded by their generations, clans, and patriarchal houses, every male from twenty years old and upward who could go out to war.
The enumeration of the tribe of Dan amounted to sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
The descendants of Asher were recorded by their generations, clans, and patriarchal houses, every male from twenty years old and upward who could go out to war.
The enumeration of the tribe of Asher amounted to forty-one thousand five hundred.
The descendants of Naphtali were recorded by their generations, clans, and patriarchal houses, every male from twenty years old and upward who could go out to war.
The enumeration of the tribe of Naphtali amounted to fifty-three thousand four hundred.
These were the men who were enumerated—whom Moses and Aaron enumerated together with the leaders of Israel, twelve men, each representing his patriarchal house.
All the enumerated among the sons of Israel, from twenty years old and upward, every man able to go to war in Israel—
their total was six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty.
But the Levites were not enumerated among them by their fathers' tribe.
Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Only the tribe of Levi you shall not enumerate, nor take their sum among the sons of Israel.

Instead, appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of the testimony, over all its furnishings, and over everything belonging to it; they shall carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings, minister to it, and encamp around the tabernacle.
When the tabernacle sets out, the Levites shall take it down; when it is to be pitched, they shall erect it; and any unauthorized person who approaches shall be put to death.
“The sons of Israel shall encamp by their armies, each man by his own camp and each man by his own standard.

But the Levites shall encamp around the tabernacle of the testimony, so that wrath may not fall upon the congregation of the sons of Israel; and the Levites shall keep the charge of the tabernacle of the testimony.”
Thus the sons of Israel did according to all that the LORD had commanded Moses; so they did.
The LORD addressed Moses and Aaron, saying,

“The Israelites shall encamp around the Tent of Meeting, setting themselves over against it at a distance; every man shall take his place by his standard, beneath the ensigns of his ancestral house; and they shall encamp facing it on all sides.”
Eastward, in the direction of the sunrise, the standard of the camp of Judah shall be pitched according to their hosts; and the leader of the sons of Judah shall be Nahshon son of Amminadab.
His host, those of them who were mustered, shall number seventy-four thousand six hundred.
Adjacent to him shall encamp the tribe of Issachar, whose leader shall be Nethanel son of Zuar.
His host, those of them who were mustered, shall number fifty-four thousand four hundred.
Likewise the tribe of Zebulun shall encamp, whose leader shall be Eliab son of Helon.
His host, those of them who were mustered, shall number fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
The total of those mustered in the camp of Judah shall be one hundred eighty-six thousand four hundred, according to their hosts; and they shall set out first.
Southward, the standard of the camp of Reuben shall be pitched according to their hosts; and the leader of the sons of Reuben shall be Elizur son of Shedeur.
His host, those of them who were mustered, shall number forty-six thousand five hundred.
Adjacent to him shall encamp the tribe of Simeon, whose leader shall be Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
His host, those of them who were mustered, shall number fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
And the tribe of Gad shall encamp, whose leader shall be Eliasaph son of Reuel.
His host, those of them who were mustered, shall number forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.
The total of those mustered in the camp of Reuben shall be one hundred fifty-one thousand four hundred and fifty, according to their hosts; and they shall set out second.
Then the Tent of Meeting shall set out, with the camp of the Levites in the midst of the camps; as they encamp, so shall they set out, each man in his place, by their standards.
Westward, the standard of the camp of Ephraim shall be pitched according to their hosts; and the leader of the sons of Ephraim shall be Elishama son of Ammihud.
His host, those of them who were mustered, shall number forty thousand five hundred.
Adjacent to him shall encamp the tribe of Manasseh, whose leader shall be Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
His host, those of them who were mustered, shall number thirty-two thousand two hundred.
And the tribe of Benjamin shall encamp, whose leader shall be Abidan son of Gideoni.
His host, those of them who were mustered, shall number thirty-five thousand four hundred.
The total of those mustered in the camp of Ephraim shall be one hundred eight thousand one hundred, according to their hosts; and they shall set out third.
Northward, the standard of the camp of Dan shall be pitched according to their hosts; and the leader of the sons of Dan shall be Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
His host, those of them who were mustered, shall number sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
Adjacent to him shall encamp the tribe of Asher, whose leader shall be Pagiel son of Ocran.
His host, those of them who were mustered, shall number forty-one thousand five hundred.
And the tribe of Naphtali shall encamp, whose leader shall be Ahira son of Enan.
His host, those of them who were mustered, shall number fifty-three thousand four hundred.
The total of those mustered in the camp of Dan shall be one hundred fifty-seven thousand six hundred, according to their hosts; and they shall set out last, by their standards.
These are the numbered of the sons of Israel by their fathers' houses; all the numbered of the camps by their hosts were six hundred three thousand five hundred and fifty.
But the Levites were not numbered among the sons of Israel, as the LORD commanded Moses.
Thus the sons of Israel did according to all that the LORD commanded Moses: they encamped by their standards, and so they set out, each man by his family, according to his father's house.
These are the genealogies of Aaron and Moses on the day when the LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.
These are the names of the sons of Aaron: Nadab the firstborn, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
These are the names of the sons of Aaron—the anointed priests whose hands had been consecrated to priestly service.

But Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no sons; therefore Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests in the presence of Aaron their father.
And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Bring the tribe of Levi near and set it before Aaron the priest, that it may minister to him.
They shall keep his charge and the charge of the entire congregation before the tent of meeting, to perform the service of the tabernacle.
They shall keep all the utensils of the tent of meeting and the charge of the sons of Israel, to perform the service of the tabernacle.
And you shall give the Levites to Aaron and to his sons; they are wholly given to him from among the sons of Israel.
And you shall appoint Aaron and his sons, and they shall keep their priesthood; but any outsider who approaches shall be put to death.”
And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Behold, I have taken the Levites from among the sons of Israel in place of every firstborn that opens the womb among the sons of Israel; and the Levites shall be Mine.

For every firstborn is Mine: on the day that I struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to Myself every firstborn in Israel, from human being to beast; they shall be Mine. I am the LORD.”
And the LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying,
“Take a census of the sons of Levi by their ancestral houses and by their clans; every male from one month old and upward you shall number.”
So Moses numbered them in accordance with the LORD's command, as he had been instructed.
And these were the sons of Levi by their names: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
And these are the names of the sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei.
And the sons of Kohath by their clans: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
And the sons of Merari by their clans: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites by their ancestral houses.
For Gershon: the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites; these are the Gershonite clans.
Those of them who were numbered, all males from one month old and upward, were seven thousand five hundred.
The Gershonite clans shall encamp behind the tabernacle on the west.
And the head of the ancestral house of the Gershonites was Eliasaph son of Lael.
And the custody of the sons of Gershon in the tent of meeting was the tabernacle and the tent, its covering, and the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting,
together with the hangings of the court, the screen for the entrance of the court that surrounds the tabernacle and the altar, and its cords, for all its service.
And for Kohath: the clan of the Amramites, the clan of the Izharites, the clan of the Hebronites, and the clan of the Uzzielites; these are the Kohathite clans.
In number, all males from one month old and upward, eight thousand six hundred, guardians of the charge of the sanctuary.
The clans of the sons of Kohath shall encamp on the south side of the tabernacle.
And the head of the ancestral house of the Kohathites, by their clans, was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
And their custody was the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary with which they minister, together with the veil and all its service.
And the chief over the chiefs of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, with oversight of the guardians of the charge of the sanctuary.
For Merari: the clan of the Mahlites and the clan of the Mushites; these are the Merarite clans.
And those of them who were numbered, all males from one month old and upward, were six thousand two hundred.
And the head of the ancestral house of the Merarites, by their clans, was Zuriel son of Abihail; they shall encamp on the north side of the tabernacle.
And the appointed custody of the sons of Merari was the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, its pillars, its bases, all its vessels, and all its service,
together with the pillars of the court all around, their bases, their pegs, and their cords.

And those encamping eastward, before the tabernacle toward the sunrise—Moses and Aaron and his sons—were guardians of the charge of the sanctuary for the charge of the sons of Israel; and any outsider who approached was to be put to death.
All the numbered of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron numbered at the LORD's command by their clans, all males from one month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand.
And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying, “Number all the firstborn males among the sons of Israel from one month old and upward, and take the number of their names.

And you shall take the Levites for Me—I am the LORD—in place of all the firstborn among the sons of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the cattle of the sons of Israel.”
So Moses numbered all the firstborn among the sons of Israel, as the LORD had commanded him.
And all the firstborn males, by the number of their names, from one month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand two hundred seventy-three.
And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the sons of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites in place of their cattle; and the Levites shall be Mine. I am the LORD.
And as for the redemption of the two hundred seventy-three of the firstborn of the sons of Israel who are in excess over the Levites,
you shall take five shekels apiece; by the shekel of the sanctuary you shall take them—twenty gerahs to the shekel—
and give the money to Aaron and to his sons as the redemption price for those who are in excess among them.”
So Moses took the redemption money from those who were in excess of the number redeemed by the Levites;
from the firstborn of the sons of Israel he took the money: one thousand three hundred sixty-five shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary.
And Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and to his sons, according to the word of the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
“Take a census of the Kohathites among the Levites, by their clans and ancestral houses,
from thirty years of age and upward to fifty, every man who enters upon service to perform work in the Tent of Meeting.”
This is the service of the Kohathites in the Tent of Meeting: the most holy objects.
When the camp prepares to set out, Aaron and his sons shall go in and remove the veil of the screen and cover the ark of the testimony with it.
They shall place over it a covering of fine leather, spread over it a cloth wholly of blue, and insert its poles.
Over the table of the Presence they shall spread a blue cloth and place upon it the dishes, the pans, the bowls, and the pitchers for the drink offering; the perpetual bread shall be upon it.
They shall spread over these a scarlet cloth, cover them with a fine-leather covering, and insert its poles.
They shall take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand for the light, its lamps, its tongs, its snuffers, and all its oil vessels with which they serve it.
They shall put it and all its vessels in a fine-leather covering and place them on the carrying frame.
