Over the golden altar they shall spread a blue cloth, cover it with a fine-leather covering, and insert its poles.
They shall take all the service vessels with which they serve in the sanctuary, put them in a blue cloth, cover them with a fine-leather covering, and place them on the carrying frame.
They shall remove the ashes from the altar and spread a purple cloth over it.
They shall place upon it all its vessels—the firepans, the forks, the shovels, and the basins, all the vessels of the altar—and spread over it a fine-leather covering and insert its poles.

When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the sanctuary and all its vessels, as the camp sets out, the Kohathites shall come to carry them; but they must not touch the holy things, lest they die. These are the Kohathites' burden in the Tent of Meeting.

Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has oversight of the oil for the light, the spices, the continual incense, the anointing grain offering, and the oil for the whole Tabernacle and everything in it, in the sanctuary and its vessels.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
“Do not let the Kohathite clans be cut off from among the Levites.
Do this for them, that they may live and not die when they approach the most holy objects: Aaron and his sons shall go in and assign each man to his service and burden.
But they must not go in to look at the holy things even for a moment, lest they die.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Take a census of the Gershonites also, by their ancestral houses and clans,
from thirty years of age and upward to fifty, every man who enters upon service to perform work in the Tent of Meeting.
This is the service of the Gershonite clans, in work and in carrying burdens:
they shall carry the curtains of the Tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting with its covering, the fine-leather covering above it, the screen for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,

the hangings of the courtyard, the screen for the entrance of the courtyard gate that is around the Tabernacle and the altar, their cords, and all the equipment for their service; and they shall perform all the work connected with these things.
All the service of the Gershonites, their carrying burdens and all their work, shall be under the direction of Aaron and his sons; and you shall assign to them all their duties as a charge.
This is the service of the Gershonite clans in the Tent of Meeting, and their charge is under the supervision of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.”
“The Merarites you shall number by their clans and ancestral houses,
from thirty years of age and upward to fifty, every man who enters upon service to perform work in the Tent of Meeting.
This is their charge for all their service in the Tent of Meeting: the frames of the Tabernacle, its bars, its pillars, and its bases;
the pillars of the courtyard all around, their bases, their pegs, and their cords, with all their equipment and all their service; and you shall assign by name the vessels of their charge.
This is the service of the Merarite clans, their entire service in the Tent of Meeting, under the supervision of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.”
Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of the congregation numbered the Kohathites by their clans and ancestral houses,
from thirty years of age and upward to fifty, every man who entered the service for work in the Tent of Meeting.
Their numbered men by clans were 2,750.
These were the numbered men of the Kohathite clans, everyone who served in the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron numbered at the LORD's command through Moses.
The numbered men of the Gershonites by their clans and ancestral houses,
from thirty years of age and upward to fifty, every man who entered the service for work in the Tent of Meeting,
were 2,630 by their clans and ancestral houses.
These were the numbered men of the Gershonite clans, everyone who served in the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron numbered at the LORD's command.
The numbered men of the Merarites by their clans and ancestral houses,
from thirty years of age and upward to fifty, every man who entered the service for work in the Tent of Meeting,
These were the numbered men of the Merarite clans, whom Moses and Aaron numbered at the LORD's command through Moses.
All the numbered men of the Levites, whom Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel numbered by their clans and ancestral houses,
from thirty years of age and upward to fifty, every man who came to do the service of ministry and the service of carrying burdens in the Tent of Meeting,
According to the LORD's command, they were numbered by Moses, each man assigned to his service and burden; thus they were numbered by him, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Command the Israelites to send out of the camp every leper, every person with a discharge, and everyone defiled by contact with a corpse.
Both male and female shall be sent out; they shall be removed outside the camp, so that they do not defile the camps in whose midst I dwell among them.”
The Israelites did so: they sent them outside the camp, just as the LORD had spoken to Moses, so the Israelites did.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites: When a man or woman commits any of the transgressions by which mortals offend the LORD, and thereby incurs guilt,
they shall confess the sin they have committed, make full restitution for their guilt, add one-fifth to it, and give it to the person against whom they have offended.

But if the injured party has no kinsman-redeemer to whom restitution may be made, the restitution due to the LORD shall be given to the priest, in addition to the ram of atonement by which atonement is made for the offender.
Every contribution of sacred things that the Israelites present to the priest shall belong to him.
Each person's consecrated gifts shall remain his own, but whatever anyone gives to the priest shall become the priest's.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them: If any man's wife goes astray and acts unfaithfully against him,
and another man lies with her carnally, and the matter is hidden from her husband's eyes, and she is defiled, and there is no witness against her, nor was she apprehended,
and a spirit of jealousy comes upon him, so that he is jealous of his wife, whether she is defiled or not,

then the man shall bring his wife to the priest and bring her offering for her: a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He shall pour no oil upon it and put no frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance, recalling iniquity.
The priest shall bring her near and set her before the LORD.
The priest shall take holy water in an earthen vessel and take some of the dust from the floor of the tabernacle and put it into the water.

The priest shall set the woman before the LORD, uncover her head, and place in her hands the grain offering of remembrance, that is, the grain offering of jealousy; and the priest shall hold in his hand the water of bitterness that brings a curse.

“Then the priest shall make her swear and say to her: ‘If no man has lain with you, and if you have not gone astray to uncleanness while under your husband, be free from this water of bitterness that brings a curse.’
But if you have gone astray while under your husband, and if you are defiled, and a man other than your husband has lain with you,

then the priest shall make the woman swear by the oath of the curse, and the priest shall say to her: ‘May the LORD make you a curse and an oath among your people, when the LORD causes your belly to swell and you to miscarry.’
“These waters of bitterness that bring a curse shall enter your bowels, to make your belly swell and cause you to miscarry. And the woman shall say, ‘Amen, Amen.’
“Then the priest shall write these curses in a book and wash them off into the water of bitterness.
He shall make the woman drink the water of bitterness that brings a curse, and the water that brings a curse shall enter her for bitterness.
The priest shall take the grain offering of jealousy from the woman's hand, wave it before the LORD, and bring it to the altar.
The priest shall take a handful of the grain offering, its memorial portion, and burn it on the altar; afterward he shall make the woman drink the water.

When he has made her drink the water, then, if she is defiled and has acted unfaithfully against her husband, the water that brings a curse shall enter her for bitterness, her belly shall swell, she shall miscarry, and the woman shall become a curse among her people.
But if the woman is not defiled, but is clean, she shall be free and shall conceive offspring.
“This is the law of jealousy, when a wife goes astray while under her husband and is defiled,
or when a spirit of jealousy comes upon a man and he is jealous of his wife. Then he shall set the woman before the LORD, and the priest shall do to her according to all this law.
The man shall be free from iniquity, and that woman shall bear her iniquity.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them, ‘When either a man or a woman makes a special vow—the vow of a Nazirite—to consecrate himself to the LORD,
he shall abstain from wine and fermented drink; he shall not drink vinegar made from wine or vinegar made from fermented drink; and he shall not eat fresh grapes or dried grapes.
Throughout all the days of his separation, he shall eat nothing produced by the grapevine, from the seeds even to the skin. “‘

All the days of his vow of separation no razor shall touch his head; until the days are fulfilled in which he has separated himself to the LORD, he shall be holy, and he shall let the hair of his head grow long.
All the days that he separates himself to the LORD he shall not go near a corpse.
He shall not defile himself for his father or his mother, his brother or his sister, when they die, because the consecration of his God is upon his head.
Throughout all the days of his separation he is holy to the LORD. “‘
If someone dies very suddenly beside him and defiles his consecrated head, then he shall shave his head on the day of his purification; on the seventh day he shall shave it.
On the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest, to the entrance of the tent of meeting.

The priest shall offer one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering, and shall make atonement for him, because he incurred guilt on account of the dead person; and he shall reconsecrate his head that same day.
He shall rededicate to the LORD the days of his separation and bring a male lamb a year old for a guilt offering; but the former days shall be forfeited, because his consecration was defiled. “‘
This is the law of the Nazirite: when the days of his separation are fulfilled, he shall be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting.

He shall present his offering to the LORD: one male lamb a year old without blemish for a burnt offering, one ewe lamb a year old without blemish for a sin offering, and one ram without blemish for a peace offering;
together with a basket of unleavened bread—cakes of fine flour mixed with oil and unleavened wafers anointed with oil—along with their grain offering and their drink offerings.
The priest shall bring them before the LORD and shall offer his sin offering and his burnt offering.
He shall offer the ram for a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD, with the basket of unleavened bread; the priest shall offer also its grain offering and its drink offering. “‘
The Nazirite shall shave his consecrated head at the entrance of the tent of meeting and shall take the hair of his consecrated head and place it on the fire beneath the sacrifice of peace offerings.

The priest shall take the boiled shoulder of the ram, one unleavened cake from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and shall put them upon the hands of the Nazirite after he has shaved his consecrated head.

The priest shall wave them as a wave offering before the LORD; it is a holy portion for the priest, together with the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution; and after that the Nazirite may drink wine.

This is the law of the Nazirite who vows his offering to the LORD for his consecration, in addition to whatever else his means allow; according to the vow he has vowed, so he must act, in accordance with the law of his consecration.’”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying, ‘Thus you shall bless the Israelites: say to them,
“The LORD bless you and keep you.
The LORD make His face shine upon you and be gracious to you.
The LORD lift up His countenance upon you and give you peace.”
And they shall put My name upon the Israelites, and I will bless them.’”

On the day Moses finished erecting the tabernacle, he anointed and consecrated it, together with all its furnishings, the altar, and every utensil thereof; he anointed them and set them apart as holy.
The leaders of Israel—heads of their ancestral houses, chieftains of the tribes, those who presided over the enumeration—brought an offering.
They brought before the LORD six covered carts and twelve oxen, one cart for every two leaders and one ox for each, and presented them before the tabernacle.
Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Accept these from them, that they may be employed in the service of the tent of meeting, and give them to the Levites, to each according to his service."
So Moses took the carts and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.
He gave two carts and four oxen to the sons of Gershon, according to their service;
and four carts and eight oxen to the sons of Merari, according to their service, under the supervision of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
But to the sons of Kohath he gave none, because the service of the holy things was theirs to carry on their shoulders.
The leaders brought the dedication offering for the altar on the day it was anointed, and they presented their offering before the altar.
And the LORD said to Moses, "One leader shall present his offering each day for the dedication of the altar."
On the first day Nahshon son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl of seventy shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, of the tribe of Issachar, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl of seventy shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.
On the third day Eliab son of Helon, of the tribe of Zebulun, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl of seventy shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Eliab son of Helon.
On the fourth day Elizur son of Shedeur, of the tribe of Reuben, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl of seventy shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Elizur son of Shedeur.
On the fifth day Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai, of the tribe of Simeon, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl of seventy shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
On the sixth day Eliasaph son of Deuel, of the tribe of Gad, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl of seventy shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Eliasaph son of Deuel.
On the seventh day Elishama son of Ammihud, of the tribe of Ephraim, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl of seventy shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;

and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Elishama son of Ammihud.
On the eighth day Gamaliel son of Pedahzur, of the tribe of Manasseh, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl of seventy shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;

His offering was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl of seventy shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;

On the tenth day Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai, of the tribe of Dan, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl of seventy shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;

and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
On the eleventh day Pagiel son of Ochran, of the tribe of Asher, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl of seventy shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Pagiel son of Ochran.
On the twelfth day Ahira son of Enan, of the tribe of Naphtali, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing one hundred thirty shekels, and one silver bowl of seventy shekels, both by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old, for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Ahira son of Enan.
This was the dedication offering of the leaders of Israel for the altar on the day it was anointed: twelve silver plates, twelve silver bowls, and twelve gold dishes.
Each silver plate weighed one hundred thirty shekels, and each bowl seventy, so that all the silver vessels amounted to two thousand four hundred shekels by the sanctuary shekel.
The twelve gold dishes, filled with incense, weighed ten shekels each by the sanctuary shekel, so that all the gold of the dishes amounted to one hundred twenty shekels.
All the animals for the burnt offering were twelve bulls, twelve rams, and twelve male lambs a year old, with their grain offering, together with twelve male goats for a sin offering.
All the animals for the sacrifice of peace offerings were twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats, and sixty male lambs a year old. This was the dedication of the altar after it was anointed.

When Moses entered the tent of meeting to speak with Him, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat that is on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim; and He spoke to him.
“Speak to Aaron and tell him, ‘When you kindle the seven lamps, they are to cast their radiance before the lampstand.’”
Aaron did precisely so, setting up the lamps before the lampstand, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The lampstand itself was a work of beaten gold, wrought from its base to its blossoms, according to the pattern that the LORD had shown Moses.
Then the LORD said to Moses,
“Take the Levites from among the Israelites and purify them.
Thus you shall deal with them in order to cleanse them: sprinkle upon them the water of purification; have them shave their whole body and launder their garments, and so let them purify themselves.
Then let them take a young bull, together with its grain offering of fine flour mingled with oil, and you are to take a second young bull for a sin offering.
Bring the Levites before the Tent of Meeting and assemble the entire congregation of the Israelites.
You are to present the Levites before the LORD, and the Israelites shall lay their hands upon them.
Aaron shall present the Levites before the LORD as a wave offering from the Israelites, so that they may be consecrated to the service of the LORD.
Then the Levites shall lay their hands on the heads of the bulls, and you are to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the LORD, to make atonement for the Levites.
You are to have the Levites stand before Aaron and his sons, and then present them as a wave offering to the LORD.
In this way you shall separate the Levites from the rest of the Israelites, and the Levites shall be Mine.
After you have cleansed them and presented them as a wave offering, they are to come and perform their service at the Tent of Meeting.
For they are wholly given to Me from among the Israelites; I have taken them for Myself in place of every firstborn among the Israelites, that is, the first issue of every womb.
For every firstborn in Israel is Mine, whether human or animal; I consecrated them to Myself on the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt.
But I have taken the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the Israelites.

And I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons from among the Israelites, to carry out the service of the Israelites at the Tent of Meeting, and to make atonement for the Israelites, so that no plague may afflict the Israelites when they approach the sanctuary.”
So Moses, Aaron, and the entire congregation of the Israelites did for the Levites everything that the LORD had commanded Moses.
The Levites purified themselves and laundered their garments, and Aaron presented them as a wave offering before the LORD; Aaron also made atonement for them to cleanse them.
Afterward the Levites came to perform their service at the Tent of Meeting before Aaron and his sons; they did exactly as the LORD had commanded Moses concerning the Levites.
“This is what pertains to the Levites: from twenty-five years of age and upward they shall enter to perform the work of service in the Tent of Meeting.
But at the age of fifty they shall withdraw from the company of those who serve and shall labor no more.
They may, however, assist their brothers in the Tent of Meeting by keeping guard, though they shall not perform the work. This is how you are to administer the Levites with respect to their duties.”
In the first month of the second year after the Israelites had departed from the land of Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying:
“Command the Israelites to observe the Passover at its appointed time.
You are to observe it at the appointed time, at twilight on the fourteenth day of this month, in accordance with all its statutes and ordinances.”
So Moses instructed the Israelites to observe the Passover,
and they did so in the wilderness of Sinai at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. The Israelites executed everything precisely as the LORD had commanded Moses.

Yet certain men had become unclean through contact with a human corpse, and therefore could not observe the Passover on that day. They accordingly presented themselves before Moses and Aaron on that same day
and said to Moses, “We are unclean because of a dead body; but why should we be excluded from presenting the LORD’s offering among the Israelites at its appointed time?”
Moses replied to them, “Remain here, and I will ascertain what the LORD commands concerning you.”
Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
“Tell the Israelites: ‘When any one of you or your descendants is unclean because of a dead body, or is on a distant journey, he may nevertheless observe the Passover to the LORD.
Such persons shall observe it at twilight on the fourteenth day of the second month; they shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
They shall leave none of it until morning, nor break any of its bones; they shall observe the Passover in accordance with all its statutes.

But if a man is clean and is not on a journey, yet neglects to observe the Passover, that person shall be cut off from his people, because he did not present the LORD’s offering at its appointed time; that man shall bear his iniquity.

If an alien sojourning among you wishes to observe the Passover to the LORD, he shall do so according to the statute and ordinance of the Passover. You shall have one statute for the alien and for the native of the land.’”
On the day the tabernacle was erected, the cloud enveloped the tabernacle—the Tent of the Testimony—and from evening until morning the cloud above the tabernacle had the appearance of fire.
Thus it was continually: the cloud covered it by day, and by night it had the appearance of fire.
Whenever the cloud was lifted from above the Tent, the Israelites would set out; and wherever the cloud settled, there the Israelites would encamp.
At the command of the LORD the Israelites set out, and at the command of the LORD they encamped. As long as the cloud rested over the tabernacle, they remained encamped.
Even when the cloud lingered over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites kept the charge of the LORD and did not set out.
Sometimes the cloud remained over the tabernacle for only a few days; at the command of the LORD they would encamp, and at the command of the LORD they would set out.
Sometimes the cloud remained only from evening until morning, and when it lifted in the morning, they set out. Whether by day or by night, whenever the cloud lifted, they set out.
Whether the cloud lingered for two days, a month, or longer, the Israelites remained encamped and did not set out as long as the cloud rested over the tabernacle; but when it lifted, they set out.
They encamped at the command of the LORD and set out at the command of the LORD. They kept the charge of the LORD, according to the command of the LORD through Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Make for yourself two silver trumpets of hammered work; they shall be for you for summoning the congregation and for breaking camp.
When they are blown, the whole congregation shall assemble before you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
If only one is blown, then the leaders, the heads of the thousands of Israel, shall assemble before you.
When you blow an alarm, the camps encamped on the east shall set out.
When you blow an alarm a second time, the camps encamped on the south shall set out; an alarm shall be blown for their departures.
But when you assemble the assembly, you shall blow without sounding an alarm.
The sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets; this shall be a perpetual statute for you throughout your generations.
When you go to war in your land against an enemy who oppresses you, you shall sound an alarm on the trumpets, and you shall be remembered before the LORD your God and be saved from your enemies.

On the day of your gladness, at your appointed festivals, and at the beginnings of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and your peace offerings; they shall serve as a memorial for you before your God. I am the LORD your God.”
On the twentieth day of the second month in the second year, the cloud rose from above the tabernacle of the testimony.
Then the Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sinai according to their journeys, and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.
They set out for the first time at the command of the LORD through Moses.
In the first place, according to their companies, the standard of the camp of Judah set out, with Nahshon son of Amminadab over its host;
Nethanel son of Zuar over the host of Issachar;
and Eliab son of Helon over the host of Zebulun.
Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari set out, carrying the tabernacle.
Next the standard of the camp of Reuben set out, according to its companies, with Elizur son of Shedeur over its host;
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai over the host of Simeon;
and Eliasaph son of Deuel over the host of Gad.
Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things, and the tabernacle was erected before their arrival.
After them the standard of the camp of Ephraim set out, according to its companies, with Elishama son of Ammihud over its host;
Gamaliel son of Pedahzur over the host of Manasseh;
and Abidan son of Gideoni over the host of Benjamin.
Finally, the standard of the camp of Dan set out, as the rear guard of all the camps, with Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai over its host;
Pagiel son of Ochran over the host of Asher;
and Ahira son of Enan over the host of Naphtali.
These were the journeys of the Israelites according to their companies, and so they set out.

Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We are journeying to the place of which the LORD said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will do you good, for the LORD has spoken good concerning Israel.”
Hobab said to him, “I will not go; I will return to my own land and to my kindred.”
Moses replied, “Please do not forsake us, for you know how we camp in the wilderness, and you shall be eyes for us.
If you go with us, then the good that the LORD does for us, we will do for you.”
They set out from the mountain of the LORD on a three days’ journey, with the ark of the covenant of the LORD going before them for three days to seek out a resting place for them.
The cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.
Whenever the ark set out, Moses said, “Rise up, O LORD! Let Your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate You flee before You.”
And when it came to rest, he said, “Return, O LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel.”

Now the people were like those who complain bitterly, acting wickedly in the hearing of the LORD; and when the LORD heard, His anger was kindled, and fire from the LORD burned among them and consumed the outskirts of the camp.
Then the people cried out to Moses, and Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire subsided.
So he named that place Taberah, because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.
Meanwhile, the rabble among them craved a craving; the Israelites also turned back and wept, saying, “Who will feed us meat?
We remember the fish that we ate in Egypt for nothing—the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic.
But now our appetite is dried up; there is nothing at all except this manna before our eyes.”
Now the manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance was like the appearance of bdellium.
The people went about and gathered it, ground it in hand mills or crushed it in mortars, boiled it in pots, and made cakes of it; and its taste was like the taste of cakes baked with oil.
When the dew fell upon the camp by night, the manna fell with it.
Moses heard the people weeping throughout their families, each man at the entrance of his tent; and the anger of the LORD burned fiercely, and Moses was also displeased.
So Moses said to the LORD, “Why have You treated Your servant so badly? Why have I not found favor in Your eyes, that You have laid the burden of all this people upon me?
“Did I conceive all this people? Did I give birth to them, that You should say to me, ‘Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries a nursing child, to the land You swore to their fathers’?
“Where am I to get meat to give to all this people? For they weep before me, saying, ‘Give us meat, that we may eat.’
“I am not able to carry all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me.
“If You are going to deal with me like this, please kill me now—if I have found favor in Your eyes—and do not let me see my own ruin.”

Then the LORD said to Moses, “Gather to Me seventy men from the elders of Israel whom you know to be elders and officers of the people; bring them to the Tent of Meeting, and let them take their stand there with you.

“I will come down and speak with you there, and I will take some of the Spirit that is upon you and put it upon them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with you, so that you will not bear it alone.

“And say to the people, ‘Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, for you shall eat meat, because you have wept in the hearing of the LORD, saying, “Who will feed us meat? For it was better for us in Egypt!” Therefore the LORD will give you meat, and you shall eat.’
“You shall eat not one day, nor two days, nor five days, nor ten days, nor twenty days,

“but a whole month—until it comes out of your nostrils and becomes loathsome to you—because you have rejected the LORD, who is among you, and have wept before Him, saying, ‘Why did we ever leave Egypt?’”
But Moses said, “I am among six hundred thousand men on foot, and You have said, ‘I will give them meat, that they may eat for a whole month!’
“Are all the flocks and herds to be slaughtered for them, or are all the fish of the sea to be gathered for them, that it might suffice for them?”
Then the LORD said to Moses, “Is the LORD’s power insufficient? Now you shall see whether My word will come to pass for you or not.”
So Moses went out and spoke the words of the LORD to the people; and he gathered the seventy elders of the people and stationed them around the tent.

Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and He took some of the Spirit that was upon Moses and put it upon the seventy elders; and when the Spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, but they did not do so again.

Now two men had remained in the camp—one named Eldad and the other Medad—and the Spirit rested upon them; they were among those enrolled, but they had not gone out to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp.
And a young man ran and told Moses, saying, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”
Then Joshua son of Nun, the attendant of Moses from his youth, answered and said, “My lord Moses, restrain them!”
But Moses said to him, “Are you jealous on my behalf? Would that all the LORD’s people were prophets, that the LORD would put His Spirit upon them!”
Then Moses returned to the camp, he and the elders of Israel.

Then a wind went out from the LORD and drove quail in from the sea, and scattered them over the camp to a depth of about two cubits on the ground, for about a day’s journey in every direction around the camp.

And the people rose up all that day and all that night and all the next day and gathered the quail; the one who gathered least gathered ten homers; and they spread them out for themselves all around the camp.
While the meat was still between their teeth, before it was consumed, the anger of the LORD burned against the people, and the LORD struck the people with a very great plague.
So the name of that place was called Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved.
From Kibroth-hattaavah the people journeyed to Hazeroth, and they remained at Hazeroth.
Miriam and Aaron began to speak against Moses on account of the Cushite woman whom he had married—for he had indeed taken a Cushite wife.
They said, "Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Has He not spoken through us as well?" And the LORD heard it.
Now Moses was preeminently meek, surpassing every other human being upon the face of the earth.
Suddenly the LORD said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, "You three come out to the tent of meeting." So the three of them went out.
Then the LORD descended in a pillar of cloud, stood at the entrance of the tent, and called Aaron and Miriam; and the two of them came forward.
He said, "Listen now to My words: If there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, make Myself known to him in a vision; I speak with him in a dream.
Not so with My servant Moses; he is faithful in all My house.
With him I speak directly and plainly, not in riddles, and he beholds the form of the LORD. Why then were you not afraid to speak against My servant Moses?"
The anger of the LORD was kindled against them, and He departed.
When the cloud withdrew from above the tent, behold, Miriam was leprous, white as snow; and Aaron turned toward Miriam, and behold, she was leprous.
Then Aaron said to Moses, "Please, my lord, do not lay upon us the sin we have so foolishly committed.
Do not let her be like a stillborn infant whose flesh is half consumed when it emerges from its mother's womb."
So Moses cried out to the LORD, "O God, please heal her!"

The LORD replied to Moses, "If her father had but spat in her face, would she not be disgraced for seven days? Let her be confined outside the camp for seven days, and afterward she may be brought back in."
So Miriam was confined outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not set out until Miriam was brought back in.
Afterward the people set out from Hazeroth and encamped in the Wilderness of Paran.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Send men to spy out the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites; from each ancestral tribe you shall send one leader.”
At the LORD's command Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran; all of them were men and heads of the Israelites.
From the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;
from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;
from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
from the tribe of Manasseh, that is, of Joseph, Gaddi son of Susi;
from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;
from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;
and from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.
These are the names of the men whom Moses sent to spy out the land. And Moses called Hoshea son of Nun Joshua.
Moses sent them to spy out the land of Canaan and said to them, “Go up by way of the Negev, and then ascend into the hill country.
See what the land is like, and whether the people who dwell in it are strong or weak, few or many.
And see what the land is like in which they dwell, whether good or bad; and what the cities are like in which they dwell, whether in camps or in fortified places.

And see what the land is like, whether rich or poor; whether there is timber in it or not. Take courage and bring back some of the fruit of the land.” Now the season was that of the first ripe grapes.
So they went up and spied out the land from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob, near Lebo-hamath.
They went up into the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai—the descendants of Anak—were. (Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.)
They reached the Valley of Eshcol and cut down from there a branch bearing a single cluster of grapes; they carried it on a pole between two of them, and they also brought some pomegranates and figs.
That place was called the Valley of Eshcol because of the cluster the Israelites cut down from there.
At the end of forty days they returned from spying out the land.

They came to Moses and Aaron and to the whole congregation of the Israelites in the wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh; they brought back word to them and to the whole congregation, and showed them the fruit of the land.
They told him, “We came to the land to which you sent us; it indeed flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
Nevertheless, the people who inhabit the land are strong, and its cities are fortified and exceedingly large; moreover, we saw the descendants of Anak there.
Amalek dwells in the land of the Negev; the Hittites, the Jebusites, and the Amorites dwell in the hill country; and the Canaanites dwell by the sea and along the Jordan.”
Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said, “Let us go up at once and take possession of it, for we are well able to overcome it.”
But the men who had gone up with him said, “We are not able to go up against the people, for they are stronger than we.”

And they brought an evil report to the Israelites concerning the land they had spied out, saying, “The land through which we passed to spy it out is a land that devours its inhabitants; and all the people we saw in it are of great stature.
Moreover, we saw the Nephilim there—the sons of Anak, who descend from the Nephilim—and we seemed to ourselves like grasshoppers, and so we seemed to them.”
That very night the whole assembly raised a clamorous cry, and the people wept bitterly.
All the Israelites murmured against Moses and Aaron, and the entire assembly said to them, “Would that we had perished in Egypt, or that we had met our end in this wilderness!
Why has the LORD brought us into this land only to fall by the sword, so that our wives and little ones become plunder? Would it not be better for us to return to Egypt?”
And they said to one another, “Let us appoint a captain and go back to Egypt.”
Then Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces before the whole assembly of the congregation of the Israelites.
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had spied out the land, tore their garments,
and they said to the whole assembly of the Israelites, “The land through which we passed to spy it out is an exceedingly good land.
If the LORD takes delight in us, He will bring us into this land and give it to us—a land flowing with milk and honey.
Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not fear the people of the land, for they are bread for us; their protection has departed from them, and the LORD is with us. Do not fear them.”
But the whole assembly was about to stone them, when the glory of the LORD appeared at the tent of meeting to all the Israelites.
And the LORD said to Moses, “How long will this people despise Me, and how long will they refuse to believe in Me, notwithstanding all the signs that I have performed in their midst?
I will strike them with pestilence and disinherit them, and I will make of you a nation greater and mightier than they.”
But Moses said to the LORD, “Then the Egyptians will hear of it, for by Your might You brought up this people from among them,

and they will tell the inhabitants of this land. They have heard that You, the LORD, are in the midst of this people, whom You have let be seen face to face, and that Your cloud stands over them, and that You go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and in a pillar of fire by night.
Now if You put this people to death all at once, then the nations who have heard the report of You will say,
‘Because the LORD was not able to bring this people into the land that He swore to give them, He has slaughtered them in the wilderness.’ “
And now, I pray, let the power of my Lord be great, even as You have spoken, saying,

‘The LORD is slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, forgiving iniquity and transgression, yet by no means clearing the guilty, but visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation.’
Pardon, I pray, the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of Your steadfast love, just as You have forgiven this people from Egypt until now.”
Then the LORD said, “I have pardoned, according to your word;
but truly, as I live, and as all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the LORD, “
none of the men who have seen My glory and My signs, which I wrought in Egypt and in the wilderness, and yet have put Me to the test these ten times and have not obeyed My voice,
shall see the land that I swore to give to their fathers; none of those who despised Me shall see it.
But My servant Caleb, because he had a different spirit with him and has followed Me fully, I will bring him into the land into which he went, and his descendants shall possess it.
Now, since the Amalekites and the Canaanites dwell in the valley, turn back tomorrow and set out into the wilderness by the way to the Red Sea.”
And the LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying, “How long shall this wicked congregation murmur against Me?
I have heard the murmurings of the Israelites, which they murmur against Me. “
Say to them, ‘As I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you just as you have spoken in My hearing:
your corpses shall fall in this wilderness, and all of you who were numbered, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward, who have murmured against Me,
shall by no means enter the land concerning which I swore to make you dwell in it, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
But your little ones, whom you said would become a prey, I will bring in, and they shall know the land that you have despised. “‘
But as for you, your corpses shall fall in this wilderness;
and your children shall be shepherds in the wilderness forty years, and shall bear your unfaithfulness, until your corpses are consumed in the wilderness.
According to the number of the days in which you spied out the land, forty days, a year for each day, you shall bear your iniquity forty years, and you shall know My displeasure.
I, the LORD, have spoken; surely thus will I do to all this wicked congregation that is gathered together against Me: in this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die.’”
And the men whom Moses had sent to spy out the land, who returned and made the whole congregation murmur against him by bringing up an evil report about the land—
those men who brought up the evil report of the land died by the plague before the LORD.
But Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive, of those men who went to spy out the land.
When Moses spoke these words to all the Israelites, the people mourned greatly.
And they rose early in the morning and went up to the top of the mountain, saying, “Behold, we are here, and we will go up to the place that the LORD has promised, for we have sinned.”
But Moses said, “Why now are you transgressing the commandment of the LORD? It will not prosper.
Do not go up, lest you be struck down before your enemies, for the LORD is not among you.
For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there before you, and you shall fall by the sword; because you have turned back from following the LORD, the LORD will not be with you.”
But they presumed to go up to the top of the mountain, although neither the ark of the covenant of the LORD nor Moses departed from the midst of the camp.
Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites who dwelt in that mountain came down and defeated them and pursued them as far as Hormah.
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘When you enter the land I am giving you as your dwelling,

and you present to the LORD an offering by fire—whether a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow, as a freewill offering, or at your appointed times—to produce a pleasing aroma to the LORD, from the herd or from the flock,
then the one presenting his offering to the LORD shall also present a grain offering of one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with one-fourth of a hin of oil.
With the burnt offering or sacrifice of each lamb, you are to prepare one-fourth of a hin of wine as a drink offering.
Or for a ram, you shall prepare a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with one-third of a hin of oil,
and one-third of a hin of wine as a drink offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
“‘When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a peace offering to the LORD,
you shall present with it a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with one-half of a hin of oil,
and one-half of a hin of wine as a drink offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
This is to be done for each bull, ram, lamb, or goat.
You shall prepare them in proportion to the number you offer.
Every native-born Israelite shall do these things in this way when presenting an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
And if a sojourner resides among you, or whoever is among you throughout your generations, and he wishes to present an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, he shall do as you do.

As for the assembly, there shall be one statute for you and for the sojourner who resides among you, a perpetual statute throughout your generations; as you are, so shall the sojourner be before the LORD.
There is to be one law and one ordinance for you and for the sojourner who resides among you.’”
Then the LORD said to Moses,
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘When you enter the land to which I am bringing you,
and you eat of the bread of the land, you shall lift up an offering to the LORD.
From the first of your dough you shall lift up a cake as an offering; you shall lift it up as an offering from the threshing floor.
Throughout your generations, you shall give this offering to the LORD from the first of your dough.
“‘And if you stray inadvertently and do not obey all these commandments that the LORD has spoken to Moses—
all that the LORD has commanded you through Moses, from the day the LORD gave the commandments and onward throughout your generations—

and if it is done inadvertently without the knowledge of the congregation, then the whole congregation shall offer one young bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, with its grain offering and its drink offering according to the ordinance, and one male goat as a sin offering.

The priest shall make atonement for the whole congregation of Israel, so that they may be forgiven, for it was inadvertent, and they have brought their offering, an offering by fire to the LORD, and their sin offering before the LORD for their inadvertent sin.
Then the whole congregation of Israel and the sojourner who resides among them shall be forgiven, because all the people acted inadvertently.
“‘Also, if one person sins inadvertently, he shall present a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
The priest shall make atonement before the LORD for the person who erred, when he sinned inadvertently, to make atonement for him, and he shall be forgiven.
You shall have one law for the native-born and for the sojourner who resides among you, for anyone who acts inadvertently.
But the person who acts defiantly, whether native-born or sojourner, blasphemes the LORD; that person shall be cut off from among his people.
Because he has despised the word of the LORD and broken His commandment, that person shall be utterly cut off; his guilt remains upon him.’”
While the Israelites were in the wilderness, a man was found gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
Those who found him gathering wood brought him before Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation.
They put him in custody, because it had not been declared what should be done to him.
Then the LORD said to Moses, “The man must be put to death; the whole congregation must stone him outside the camp.”
So the whole congregation took him outside the camp and stoned him to death, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then the LORD said to Moses,
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘Throughout your generations, you are to make tassels on the corners of your garments, with a blue cord on each tassel.

These will serve as tassels for you to look at, so that you may remember all the commandments of the LORD and do them, and not stray after your own heart and your own eyes, by which you are led astray.
Then you will remember and obey all My commandments, and you will be holy to your God.
I am the LORD your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God.’”

Now Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, together with Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, descendants of Reuben, took certain Israelite men and set themselves in open defiance;
they presented themselves before Moses with two hundred fifty leaders of the congregation—men of renown, regularly summoned to the assembly.

They said to Moses and Aaron, “You have carried your presumption too far, for the entire congregation is holy, every one of them, and the LORD dwells among them. Why then do you exalt yourselves above the assembly of the LORD?”
When Moses heard this, he fell upon his face.

Then he spoke to Korah and to all his faction, saying, “In the morning the LORD will make known who belongs to Him and who is holy, and He will bring that one near to Himself; indeed, the one whom He chooses He will bring near to Himself.
Do this: take censers for yourselves, Korah and all your faction,
put fire in them, and lay incense upon them before the LORD tomorrow. The man whom the LORD chooses shall be the holy one. You Levites have carried your presumption too far!
Hear now, you sons of Levi:

is it too small a thing for you that the God of Israel has set you apart from the congregation of Israel, to bring you near to Himself for the service of the tabernacle of the LORD and to stand before the congregation to minister to them?
He has brought you near, along with all your brothers, the sons of Levi, and now you seek the priesthood as well.
Therefore you and all your faction are gathered together against the LORD; and what is Aaron, that you murmur against him?”
Moses sent to summon Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and they replied, “We will not come up.
Is it a trivial matter that you brought us up from a land of abundant prosperity only to kill us in the wilderness, and now you would also lord it over us?
Besides, you have not brought us into a land of abundant prosperity or given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Would you blind these men? We will not come up.”
Moses was exceedingly angry, and he said to the LORD, “Do not regard their offering. I have not taken one donkey from them, nor have I wronged a single one of them.”
Then Moses said to Korah, “You and all your faction must appear before the LORD tomorrow—you, they, and Aaron.
Let each man take his censer, put incense on it, and bring it before the LORD—two hundred fifty censers in all; you and Aaron shall each bring his own.”
So each man took his censer, put fire in it, laid incense on it, and stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, together with Moses and Aaron.
Korah assembled the whole congregation against them at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD appeared to the entire congregation.
Then the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
“Separate yourselves from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment.”
But they fell upon their faces and said, “O God, God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and will You be angry with the entire congregation?”
Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the congregation, saying, ‘Withdraw from the dwelling of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.’”
So Moses rose and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him.
He warned the congregation, “Depart, I beg you, from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing that belongs to them, lest you be swept away in all their sin.”

Thus they withdrew from around the dwelling of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram; and Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrances of their tents, with their wives, their sons, and their little ones.
And Moses said, “By this you shall know that the LORD has sent me to do all these works, for I have not acted of my own accord.
If these men die the common death of all men, or if they suffer the ordinary fate of all mankind, then the LORD has not sent me.

But if the LORD creates something new, and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them up, with all that belongs to them, so that they descend alive into Sheol, then you shall understand that these men have despised the LORD.”
As soon as he finished speaking all these words, the ground beneath them split open.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up, together with their households and all the people who belonged to Korah, along with all their possessions.
They and all that belonged to them went down alive into Sheol; the earth closed over them, and they perished from the midst of the assembly.
All Israel around them fled at their outcry, for they said, “Lest the earth swallow us up as well.”
Then fire came out from the LORD and consumed the two hundred fifty men who had offered the incense.
Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to remove the censers from the burning and scatter the fire abroad, for they are holy.

As for the censers of these sinners against their own lives, let them be hammered into plates as a covering for the altar, because they were offered before the LORD and are holy; thus they shall serve as a sign to the children of Israel.”
So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers that had been offered by those who were burned, and they were hammered into a covering for the altar,

as a memorial to the children of Israel, so that no outsider who is not of the seed of Aaron might draw near to offer incense before the LORD, lest he become like Korah and his faction, just as the LORD had spoken to him through Moses.
But on the next day the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying, “You have killed the people of the LORD.”
And when the congregation assembled against Moses and Aaron, they turned toward the tent of meeting, and behold, the cloud covered it, and the glory of the LORD appeared.
Then Moses and Aaron came to the front of the tent of meeting.
Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Get away from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment.” And they fell upon their faces.

And Moses said to Aaron, “Take the censer, put fire on it from the altar, lay incense on it, and hurry to the congregation and make atonement for them; for wrath has gone out from the LORD—the plague has begun.”
So Aaron took it, as Moses had spoken, and ran into the midst of the assembly; and behold, the plague had already begun among the people. He put on the incense and made atonement for the people.
He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was arrested.
Those who died by the plague were fourteen thousand seven hundred, besides those who died on account of Korah.
Then Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the plague was arrested.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

"Speak to the Israelites and take from them twelve rods, one rod for each ancestral household, from all their chieftains according to their fathers’ houses; let every man inscribe his name upon his rod.
Inscribe Aaron’s name upon the rod of Levi, for one rod is to represent the head of their ancestral house.
You shall deposit them in the tent of meeting before the testimony, the place where I shall meet with you.
The rod of the man whom I select shall blossom, and I shall quell, before Me, the Israelites’ grumblings, by which they murmur against you."
Moses conveyed this to the Israelites, and their chieftains furnished him with rods—one for each chieftain, according to their ancestral houses—twelve rods in total; Aaron’s rod lay among them.
Moses deposited the rods before the LORD in the tent of the testimony.
On the morrow, Moses entered the tent of the testimony, and behold, Aaron’s rod—pertaining to the Levitical house—had sprouted, put forth buds, blossomed into flowers, and produced almonds.
Moses brought forth all the rods from before the LORD to the Israelites; they inspected them, and each man reclaimed his own rod.
The LORD said to Moses, "Return Aaron’s rod before the testimony, that it be preserved as a sign against the rebellious; and their grumblings shall be removed from before Me, lest they die."
Moses complied; exactly as the LORD had commanded him, so he acted.
The Israelites addressed Moses, saying, "Behold, we are perishing; we are ruined—all of us are ruined.
Everyone who approaches, who draws near to the tabernacle of the LORD, shall die. Will death consume us all?"
The LORD said to Aaron, "You and your sons, together with your ancestral house, shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary; and you and your sons with you shall bear the iniquity of your priesthood. "
Bring near to you also your brothers—the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father—that they may join you and minister to you while you and your sons stand before the tent of testimony.
They shall keep your charge and the charge of the whole tent, yet they shall not approach the holy vessels or the altar, lest they die—both they and you.
They shall be joined to you and shall keep the charge of the tent of meeting for all its service, and no outsider shall come near you.
You shall keep the charge of the sanctuary and of the altar, so that wrath may not again fall upon the children of Israel. "
Behold, I have taken your brothers the Levites from among the children of Israel; they are a gift to you, given to the LORD to perform the service of the tent of meeting.

You and your sons with you shall keep your priesthood for everything concerning the altar and within the veil, and you shall serve. I give the priesthood as a gift, and the outsider who approaches shall be put to death." "
Behold, I have given you the charge of My contributions; all the consecrated things of the children of Israel I have given to you and to your sons as a portion, as a perpetual statute.

This shall be yours from the most holy things, reserved from the fire: every offering of theirs, every grain offering, sin offering, and guilt offering that they render to Me shall be most holy for you and your sons.
In a most holy place you shall eat it; every male may eat it; it shall be holy to you.

This also is yours: the contribution of their gift, all the wave offerings of the children of Israel; I have given them to you, to your sons, and to your daughters with you, as a perpetual statute. Everyone who is clean in your house may eat it.
All the best of the oil, all the best of the new wine and the grain—their firstfruits, which they give to the LORD—I have given to you.
The firstfruits of all that is in their land, which they bring to the LORD, shall be yours; everyone who is clean in your house may eat it. "
Every devoted thing in Israel shall be yours.

Everything that opens the womb of all flesh, which they offer to the LORD—whether of man or beast—shall be yours. Nevertheless, you shall surely redeem the firstborn of man, and you shall redeem the firstborn of an unclean beast.
And their redemption, from a month old, you shall redeem, according to your valuation: five shekels of silver, according to the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs.

But the firstborn of an ox, a sheep, or a goat you shall not redeem; they are holy. You shall sprinkle their blood upon the altar and burn their fat as an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
Their flesh shall be yours, as the breast of the wave offering and the right thigh are yours.

All the contributions of holy things that the children of Israel present to the LORD I have given to you, to your sons, and to your daughters with you, as a perpetual statute. It is a covenant of salt forever before the LORD for you and your offspring with you."
The LORD said to Aaron, "You shall have no inheritance in their land, neither shall you have a portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the children of Israel.
To the sons of Levi, behold, I have given every tithe in Israel for an inheritance, in return for the service that they render, the service of the tent of meeting.
The children of Israel shall no longer come near the tent of meeting, lest they bear sin and die.

The Levites shall perform the service of the tent of meeting, and they shall bear their iniquity. It shall be a statute forever throughout your generations, and among the children of Israel they shall have no inheritance.

For the tithe of the children of Israel, which they present to the LORD as a contribution, I have given to the Levites for an inheritance. Therefore I have said to them that among the children of Israel they shall have no inheritance."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying, "

Moreover, you shall speak to the Levites and say to them, 'When you take from the children of Israel the tithe that I have given you from them for your inheritance, you shall present a contribution from it to the LORD, a tithe of the tithe.
Your contribution shall be reckoned to you as though it were the grain of the threshing floor and as the produce of the winepress.
So you shall present a contribution to the LORD from all your tithes, which you take from the children of Israel; and from it you shall give the LORD’s contribution to Aaron the priest.
Out of all your gifts you shall present every contribution to the LORD, from all the best thereof, the hallowed part of it.'
Therefore say to them, 'When you have set apart the best of it, then the rest shall be reckoned to the Levites as the produce of the threshing floor and as the produce of the winepress.
You may eat it in any place, you and your households, because it is your reward in return for your service in the tent of meeting.
You shall bear no sin by reason of it, when you have set apart the best of it. Neither shall you profane the holy things of the children of Israel, lest you die.'"
Then the LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

“This constitutes the statutory ordinance of the law that the LORD has enjoined: instruct the Israelites to bring to you a red heifer—immaculate, devoid of every blemish, and never subjected to a yoke.
You shall consign it to Eleazar the priest, who shall remove it beyond the encampment and slaughter it in his presence.
Eleazar the priest shall take of its blood with his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the tent of meeting.
The heifer must be incinerated under his supervision—its hide, flesh, blood, and even its dung being consumed by fire.
“The priest shall take cedar timber, hyssop, and scarlet wool, and cast them into the midst of the heifer’s conflagration.
Thereafter the priest shall launder his garments and bathe his person in water; only then may he reenter the camp, though he remains ritually unclean until evening.
Likewise, whoever incinerates the heifer must launder his garments, bathe his person in water, and remain unclean until evening.

“Then a man in a state of ritual purity shall gather the ashes of the heifer and deposit them in a ceremonially clean place beyond the camp; they are to be preserved for the congregation of the Israelites for the water of purification, since it is a sin offering.

The man who gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his garments and remain unclean until evening. This ordinance shall be an everlasting statute for the Israelites and for the sojourner residing among them.
“Anyone who touches the corpse of any human being shall be ritually unclean for seven days.

He must purify himself with this water on the third day and again on the seventh day; then he shall be clean. If, however, he fails to purify himself on both the third and the seventh days, he shall not be clean.

Anyone who touches a human corpse and does not purify himself defiles the tabernacle of the LORD; that person shall be cut off from Israel, because the water of purification has not been sprinkled upon him. He remains unclean, and his impurity abides upon him.
“This is the law when a man dies in a tent: everyone who enters the tent, as well as everyone already present within it, shall be unclean for seven days.
Furthermore, every open vessel lacking a securely fastened lid is unclean.
Likewise, anyone in the open field who touches one slain by the sword, or a corpse, or a human bone, or a grave, shall be unclean for seven days.
“For the unclean person, they shall take some of the ashes of the purification offering, place them in a vessel, and pour living water over them.

Then a clean person shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it upon the tent, upon all the vessels, upon the persons who were present, and upon anyone who touched a bone, a slain person, a corpse, or a grave.

The clean person shall sprinkle the unclean on the third day and on the seventh day. On the seventh day he shall complete the purification; then the one being cleansed shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and he shall be clean by evening.

“But if an unclean person does not purify himself, that individual shall be cut off from the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD. The water of purification has not been sprinkled upon him; he remains unclean.
This shall be an everlasting statute for them: the one who sprinkles the water of purification must wash his garments, and whoever touches the water of purification shall be unclean until evening.
Furthermore, whatever the unclean person touches becomes unclean, and anyone who touches him shall be unclean until evening.”
In the first month, the entire congregation of the Israelites entered the wilderness of Zin and encamped at Kadesh. There Miriam died and was buried.
Now the congregation lacked water, whereupon they gathered in opposition to Moses and Aaron.
"Would that we had expired when our brethren expired before the the LORD!
Why have you brought the congregation of the the LORD into this wilderness, that we and our beasts should perish here?
Why have you raised us out of Egypt only to bring us to this execrable place? It affords no grain, figs, vines, or pomegranates, nor water to drink."
Moses and Aaron withdrew from the presence of the assembly to the entrance of the tent of meeting and fell upon their faces; then the glory of the the LORD appeared to them.
The LORD then addressed Moses, saying,

"Take the staff, and assemble the congregation—you and your brother Aaron—and speak to the rock before their eyes, that it may give forth its water. Thus you shall bring water out of the rock for them and give drink to the congregation and their livestock."
So Moses took the staff from before the the LORD, as He had commanded him.
Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly before the rock, and he said to them, "Listen, you rebels: shall we bring water for you out of this rock?"
Then Moses lifted up his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff; water gushed out abundantly, and the congregation and their livestock drank.

The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "Because you did not believe in Me, so as to sanctify Me before the eyes of the Israelites, therefore you shall not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them."
These are the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites contended with the the LORD, and He manifested His holiness among them.
From Kadesh, Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom: "Thus says your brother Israel: You know all the hardship that has befallen us.
Our ancestors descended into Egypt, and we sojourned there for many days; the Egyptians mistreated us and our fathers. "
We cried to the the LORD, and He heard our voice and sent an angel, and brought us out of Egypt. And behold, we are at Kadesh, a city at the extremity of your territory.

Please let us pass through your land. We will not pass through field or vineyard, nor drink water from a well; we will travel the king's highway, and we will not turn aside to the right or to the left until we have passed through your territory."
But Edom said to him, "You shall not pass through me, lest I come out against you with the sword."
The Israelites said to him, "We will go up by the highway; and if we drink your water, I and my livestock, then I will pay its price. Only let me pass through on foot—nothing more."
But he said, "You shall not pass through." And Edom came out against them with a massive people and a strong hand.
Thus Edom refused to let Israel pass through his territory; so Israel turned away from him.
They set out from Kadesh, and the Israelites, the whole congregation, came to Mount Hor.
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom, saying,
"Let Aaron be gathered to his people, for he shall not enter the land that I have given to the Israelites, because you rebelled against My command at the waters of Meribah.
Take Aaron and his son Eleazar, and bring them up Mount Hor.
Strip Aaron of his garments and put them on his son Eleazar; and Aaron shall be gathered to his people and die there."
Moses did as the the LORD commanded; and they went up Mount Hor in the sight of the whole congregation.
Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on his son Eleazar; and Aaron died there on the top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
When the whole congregation saw that Aaron had breathed his last, all the house of Israel wept for Aaron thirty days.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who dwelt in the Negev, heard that Israel had come by the way of Atharim; he fought against Israel and took some of them captive.
Israel vowed a solemn vow to the LORD, saying, “If You will indeed give this people into my hand, then I will utterly destroy their cities.”
The LORD heeded Israel’s voice and delivered up the Canaanite; Israel devoted them and their cities to destruction, and called the name of that place Hormah.
They set out from Mount Hor by the way of the Red Sea, to skirt the land of Edom, and the people grew disheartened on the way.

The people spoke contemptuously against God and against Moses: “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? For there is no bread and no water, and our souls are utterly revolted by this wretched fare.”
Then the LORD sent fiery serpents among the people; they bit the people, and many of the Israelites died.

The people came to Moses and said, “We have sinned, for we have spoken against the LORD and against you. Pray to the LORD, that He may remove the serpent from us.” Moses prayed to the LORD on behalf of the people.
The LORD said to Moses, “Make a fiery serpent and set it on a standard; everyone who is bitten, when he looks at it, shall live.”
So Moses made a bronze serpent and set it on the standard; and if a serpent bit anyone, he looked at the bronze serpent and lived.
The Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim in the wilderness that lies before Moab toward the sunrise.
From there they set out and camped in the Valley of Zered.
From there they set out and camped beyond the Arnon, which is in the wilderness extending from the territory of the Amorites; for the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
Therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of the LORD: “Waheb in Suphah, and the valleys of the Arnon,
and the slope of the valleys that stretches toward the settlement of Ar, and leans upon the border of Moab.”
From there they went to Beer; that is the well of which the LORD said to Moses, “Gather the people, and I will give them water.”
Then Israel sang this song: “Spring up, O well! Sing to it!
The well that the princes dug, that the nobles of the people hollowed out with the scepter, with their staffs.
And from the wilderness to Mattanah, from Mattanah to Nahaliel, from Nahaliel to Bamoth,
and from Bamoth to the valley that is in the field of Moab, to the top of Pisgah, which looks down upon the wasteland.”
Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,
“Let me pass through your land. We will not turn aside into field or vineyard; we will not drink water from a well. We will go along the king’s highway until we have passed through your territory.”
But Sihon would not allow Israel to pass through his territory. Sihon gathered all his people and went out against Israel into the wilderness, and came to Jahaz, and fought against Israel.
Israel struck him with the sword and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the border of the Ammonites, for the Ammonite frontier was strong.
Israel took all these cities, and Israel settled in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon and in all its outlying villages.
For Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab and had taken all his land from his hand as far as the Arnon.
Therefore the proverb-makers say, “Come to Heshbon; let it be rebuilt; let the city of Sihon be established.
For fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from the city of Sihon; it consumed Ar of Moab, and the lords of the heights of the Arnon.
Woe to you, Moab! You are undone, O people of Chemosh! he has given his sons as fugitives, and his daughters into captivity, to Sihon king of the Amorites.
But we have overthrown them; Heshbon is destroyed as far as Dibon; we have laid waste as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba.”
Thus Israel settled in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to spy out Jazer, and they captured its villages and dispossessed the Amorites who were there.
Then they turned and went up by the way of Bashan. Og king of Bashan came out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.

The LORD said to Moses, “Do not fear him, for I have given him into your hand, and all his people and his land; and you shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon.”
They struck him and his sons and all his people, until no survivor was left to him, and they took possession of his land.
