The Israelites journeyed onward and encamped on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
Balak son of Zippor beheld all that Israel had wrought against the Amorites.
Moab was seized with profound dread of the people, for they were numerous, and Moab was sick with anxiety on account of the Israelites.
Moab said to the elders of Midian, "This multitude will now devour all that surrounds us, as an ox consumes the grass of the field." At that time Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab.

Balak dispatched messengers to Balaam son of Beor, at Pethor beside the River, in the land of his people, to summon him with these words: "Behold, a people has emerged from Egypt; it covers the face of the earth and is encamped opposite me.

Come, I pray, and curse this people for me, for they are too mighty for me. Perhaps I may then be able to smite them and expel them from the land, for I know that whomever you bless is blessed, and whomever you curse is accursed."
So the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian set out, bearing fees for divination, and came to Balaam and delivered Balak's message to him.
Balaam said to them, "Remain here tonight, and I shall return to you with whatever answer the LORD gives me." So the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.
Then God came to Balaam and asked, "Who are these men with you?"
Balaam said to God, "Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent to me, saying, 'Behold, the people that has come out of Egypt covers the face of the earth.
Come now, curse them for me; perhaps I may be able to fight against them and drive them out.'"
God said to Balaam, "You shall not go with them; you shall not curse the people, for they are blessed."
Balaam rose in the morning and said to Balak's princes, "Go back to your own land, for the LORD has refused to let me go with you."
So the princes of Moab rose, came to Balak, and said, "Balaam refuses to come with us."
Balak sent again, dispatching princes more numerous and more distinguished than the former.
They came to Balaam and said, "Thus says Balak son of Zippor: 'Please do not let anything prevent you from coming to me.
For I will honor you greatly, and whatever you say to me I will do; come, therefore, and curse this people for me.'"
Balaam replied to Balak's servants, "Even if Balak were to give me his house filled with silver and gold, I could not transgress the word of the LORD my God, by doing anything, small or great.
Now, please remain here tonight as well, so that I may learn what further the LORD will say to me."
God came to Balaam by night and said to him, "If the men have come to summon you, arise and go with them; yet you shall do only what I speak to you."
Balaam rose in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the princes of Moab.
But God's anger was kindled because he went, and the Angel of the LORD took His stand in the road as an adversary against him. Balaam was riding his donkey, with his two servants beside him.

The donkey saw the Angel of the LORD standing in the road with His drawn sword in His hand, and she turned aside from the road and went into the field. Balaam struck the donkey to turn her back onto the road.
Then the Angel of the LORD stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, with a wall on either side.
When the donkey saw the Angel of the LORD, she pressed against the wall and crushed Balaam's foot against it, so he struck her again.
The Angel of the LORD went further and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn, either to the right or to the left.
When the donkey saw the Angel of the LORD, she lay down under Balaam; Balaam's anger burned, and he struck the donkey with his staff.
Then the LORD opened the donkey's mouth, and she said to Balaam, "What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?"
Balaam answered the donkey, "Because you have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you on the spot."
The donkey said to Balaam, "Am I not your donkey, the one you have ridden all your life until today? Have I ever treated you this way before?" Balaam said, "No."
Then the LORD opened Balaam's eyes, and he saw the Angel of the LORD standing in the road with His sword drawn. Balaam bowed down and fell on his face.
The Angel of the LORD said to him, "Why have you struck your donkey these three times? Behold, I have come out to oppose you, because your path is crooked before me.
The donkey saw me and turned aside from me these three times. If she had not turned aside, I would have killed you and spared her."
Balaam said to the Angel of the LORD, "I have sinned, for I did not know that you were standing in the road against me. Now, if it is displeasing in your sight, I will turn back."
The Angel of the LORD said to Balaam, "Go with the men, but speak only the word that I tell you." So Balaam went with Balak's princes.
When Balak heard that Balaam had come, he went out to meet him at the Moabite city on the Arnon, at the frontier of his territory.
Balak said to Balaam, "Did I not send to summon you? Why did you not come to me? Am I not able to honor you?"
Balaam replied, "Behold, I have come to you. But do I now have any power to say anything? I can speak only the word that God puts in my mouth."
Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.
Balak sacrificed oxen and sheep, and sent portions to Balaam and to the princes who were with him.
In the morning Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal, and from there Balaam saw the outskirts of the people.
Balaam instructed Balak, “Erect seven altars for me upon this height, and make ready seven bulls and seven rams.”
Balak discharged that injunction with scrupulous fidelity, and the two of them presented a bull and a ram upon every altar.

Balaam then said to Balak, “Remain here beside your burnt offering while I withdraw to a solitary eminence; perhaps the LORD will vouchsafe an encounter with me, and whatever He discloses I shall report to you.” So he ascended to a barren height.
God encountered him, and Balaam said, “I have arrayed seven altars, and upon each I have offered a bull and a ram.”
Then the LORD implanted a word in Balaam’s mouth and commanded, “Return to Balak and deliver this message.”
Accordingly, he returned to Balak, who stood beside his burnt offering in the company of all the princes of Moab.
And Balaam lifted up his oracle, declaring, “Balak has summoned me from Aram—the king of Moab from the mountains of the east—saying, ‘Come, curse Jacob on my behalf; come, denounce Israel!’
How, then, shall I execrate those whom God has not execrated? How shall I denounce those whom the LORD has not denounced?
For from the summit of the rocks I behold them, and from the hills I survey them: behold, a people dwelling in seclusion, not reckoned among the nations.
Who can enumerate the dust of Jacob, or tally the fourth part of Israel? Let my soul perish among the righteous, and let my final estate be commensurate with theirs!”
Balak said to Balaam, “What have you wrought against me? I brought you to curse my adversaries, yet—behold—you have blessed them abundantly!”
He answered, “Am I not constrained to utter precisely what the LORD places in my mouth?”
Balak said to him, “I entreat you to accompany me to another prospect, from which you shall descry but a portion of them—not their totality—and from that station curse them on my behalf.”
So he conducted him to the field of Zophim, to the summit of Pisgah, where he erected seven altars and offered a bull and a ram upon each.
Balaam said to Balak, “Station yourself here beside your burnt offering while I encounter the LORD yonder.”
The LORD encountered Balaam and placed a word in his mouth, commanding, “Return to Balak and deliver this message.”
He returned to Balak, who stood beside his burnt offering with the princes of Moab, and Balak demanded, “What has the LORD spoken?”
Then Balaam lifted up his oracle, saying, “Arise, Balak, and attend; give ear to me, son of Zippor.
God is not a man, that He should prevaricate, nor a son of man, that He should relent. Has He declared and not executed? Has He spoken and not established it?
Behold, I have received a mandate to bless; He has blessed, and I cannot revoke it.
He has discerned no iniquity in Jacob, nor perceived perversity in Israel. The LORD his God is with him, and the acclamation of a king resounds among them.
God brought them forth from Egypt; He possesses strength like that of a wild ox.
There is no augury in Jacob, no divination in Israel; at the appointed time it shall be proclaimed concerning Jacob and Israel, ‘What has God wrought!’
Behold, the people rise like a lioness and rouse themselves like a lion; they will not recline until they have devoured the prey and drunk the blood of the slain.”
Balak said to Balaam, “Utter no curse against them, and no blessing either!”
Balaam answered Balak, “Did I not admonish you that whatever the LORD speaks, I am obliged to perform?”
Balak said to Balaam, “Pray, come—I shall conduct you to yet another site; perhaps it will commend itself to God, and from there you may curse them on my behalf.”
So Balak led Balaam to the summit of Peor, which overlooks the wasteland.
Balaam said to Balak, “Construct seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams.”
Balak complied with Balaam’s instruction and offered a bull and a ram upon each altar.
When Balaam perceived that it pleased the the LORD to bless Israel, he did not resort to sorcery as he had at other times, but turned his gaze toward the wilderness.
When Balaam raised his eyes and saw Israel encamped tribe by tribe, the Spirit of God came upon him,
and he uttered his oracle: “The oracle of Balaam son of Beor, the oracle of the man whose eye has been opened—
the oracle of one who hears the words of God, who beholds the vision of the Almighty, who falls down with eyes uncovered:
‘How lovely are your tents, O Jacob, your dwellings, O Israel!
They spread like valleys, like gardens beside a river, like aloes the the LORD has planted, like cedars beside the waters.
Water shall overflow from his buckets, and his seed shall have abundant water; his king shall be exalted above Agag, and his kingdom shall be lifted high.
God brought him out of Egypt; he has the strength of a wild ox. He shall devour hostile nations and crush their bones; with his arrows he shall pierce them.
He crouches and lies down like a lion, like a lioness—who dares rouse him? Blessed are those who bless you, and cursed are those who curse you!’”
Then Balak’s anger blazed against Balaam; he clapped his hands in fury and said to Balaam, “I summoned you to curse my enemies, yet behold, you have blessed them three times over.
Now flee to your own place! I said I would reward you richly, but the the LORD has withheld honor from you.”
Balaam replied to Balak, “Did I not tell the messengers you sent to me,

‘If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not transgress the command of the the LORD by doing anything of my own accord, good or evil; I must speak only what the the LORD speaks’?
And now I am returning to my people; but come, let me advise you what this people will do to your people in the latter days.”
Then he uttered his oracle: “The oracle of Balaam son of Beor, the oracle of the man whose eye has been opened—
the oracle of one who hears the words of God and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who beholds the vision of the Almighty, who falls down with eyes uncovered:
‘I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star shall proceed from Jacob, and a scepter shall rise from Israel; he shall crush the temples of Moab and lay waste all the sons of Sheth.
Edom shall become a possession, and Seir—his enemy—shall become a possession, while Israel performs valiantly.
A ruler shall arise from Jacob and destroy the remnant of the city.’”
Then Balaam saw Amalek and uttered his oracle: “Amalek is the first of the nations, but its end shall be utter destruction.”
Then he saw the Kenites and uttered his oracle: “Your dwelling is secure, and your nest is set in the rock;
yet the Kenite shall be consumed until Asshur takes you captive.”
Then he uttered his oracle: “Alas, who shall live when God ordains this?
Ships shall come from Kittim and subdue Asshur and subdue Eber, but he too shall come to ruin.”
Then Balaam arose and departed to his own place, and Balak also went his way.
While Israel was sojourning in Shittim, the people began to prostitute themselves with the daughters of Moab.
The Moabite women invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to those gods.
Thus Israel devoted itself to Baal of Peor, and the anger of the LORD blazed against Israel.
The LORD said to Moses, “Take all the leaders of the people and execute them in broad daylight before the LORD, so that the fierce anger of the LORD may be turned away from Israel.”
So Moses said to the judges of Israel, “Let every one of you put to death those among his people who have devoted themselves to Baal of Peor.”

Then, behold, an Israelite man came and brought a Midianite woman to his kinsmen in the sight of Moses and the whole congregation of the Israelites, while they were weeping at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
When Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw this, he rose from the midst of the congregation, seized a spear in his hand,
pursued the Israelite man into the tent, and thrust both of them through—the Israelite man and the woman—right through her belly, so that the plague was stayed from the Israelites.
Those who died in the plague numbered twenty-four thousand.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned My wrath away from the Israelites, because he was zealous with My zeal among them, so that I did not destroy the Israelites in My zeal.
Therefore declare: Behold, I am giving him My covenant of peace.
It shall be to him and to his descendants after him a covenant of perpetual priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites.”
Now the name of the slain Israelite man who was slain with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, a leader of a Simeonite ancestral house.
And the name of the slain Midianite woman was Cozbi daughter of Zur, a tribal chief of a clan in Midian.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Harass the Midianites and strike them down,

for they are harassing you with their wiles, with which they have beguiled you in the affair of Peor and in the affair of Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite leader, their sister, who was slain on the day of the plague because of Peor.”
After the plague had run its course, the LORD spoke to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, saying,
“Take a census of the whole congregation of the Israelites according to their ancestral houses, counting every male twenty years of age and older who is able to bear arms in Israel.”
This took place on the plains of Moab beside the Jordan near Jericho, where Moses and Eleazar the priest addressed the people, saying,
“Count those twenty years old and upward, just as the LORD commanded Moses concerning the Israelites who came out of Egypt.”
Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, comprised four clans: the Hanochites, from Hanoch; the Palluites, from Pallu;
the Hezronites, from Hezron; and the Carmiites, from Carmi.
whose sons were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram—the same Dathan and Abiram summoned by the assembly, who contended against Moses and Aaron in Korah’s company when they rebelled against the LORD.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them along with Korah, while the company perished as fire consumed 250 men, so that they became a warning.
The sons of Korah, however, did not die.
The Simeonites by their clans were the Nemuelites, from Nemuel; the Jaminites, from Jamin; the Jachinites, from Jachin;
the Zerahites, from Zerah; and the Shaulites, from Shaul.
The Gadites by their clans were the Zephonites, from Zephon; the Haggites, from Haggi; the Shunites, from Shuni;
the Oznites, from Ozni; the Erites, from Eri;
the Arodites, from Arod; and the Areelites, from Areli.
Judah’s sons Er and Onan died in Canaan.
The Judahite clans were the Shelanites, from Shelah; the Perezites, from Perez; and the Zerahites, from Zerah.
The Perezites comprised the Hezronites, from Hezron, and the Hamulites, from Hamul.
The Issacharites by their clans were the Tolaites, from Tola; the Punites, from Puvah;
the Jashubites, from Jashub; and the Shimronites, from Shimron.
The Zebulunites by their clans were the Seredites, from Sered; the Elonites, from Elon; and the Jahleelites, from Jahleel.
Joseph’s descendants were Manasseh and Ephraim.
The Manassites by their clans were the Machirites, from Machir; Machir fathered Gilead, and the Gileadites descended from Gilead.
Gilead’s sons included the Iezerites, from Iezer; the Helekites, from Helek;
the Asrielites, from Asriel; the Shechemites, from Shechem;
the Shemidaites, from Shemida; and the Hepherites, from Hepher.
Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, only daughters—Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
The Ephraimites by their clans were the Shuthelahites, from Shuthelah; the Becherites, from Becher; and the Tahanites, from Tahan.
Shuthelah’s son was Eran, ancestor of the Eranites.
These were Joseph’s descendants by their clans; the Ephraimite enrollment was 32,500.
The Benjaminites by their clans were the Belaites, from Bela; the Ashbelites, from Ashbel; and the Ahiramites, from Ahiram.
They also included the Shuphamites, from Shupham, and the Huphamites, from Hupham.
Bela’s sons were Ard and Naaman, ancestors of the Ardites and the Naamites.
The Danites by their clans were the Shuhamites, from Shuham.
The Asherites by their clans were the Imnites, from Imnah; the Ishvites, from Ishvi; and the Beriites, from Beriah.
Beriah’s descendants were the Heberites, from Heber, and the Malchielites, from Malchiel.
Asher had a daughter named Serah.
The Naphtali clans by their families were the Jahzeelites, from Jahzeel; the Gunites, from Guni;
the Jezerites, from Jezer; and the Shillemites, from Shillem.
Thus the total enrollment of the Israelites was 601,730.
Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“This land is to be divided among them as an inheritance, in proportion to the number of names.
To the more numerous you shall give a larger inheritance, and to the fewer a smaller one; each tribe’s inheritance shall correspond to its enrollment.
Nevertheless, the land must be divided by lot; they shall inherit according to the names of their ancestral tribes.
Whether the group is large or small, its inheritance shall be determined by lot.”
The Levites were counted by their clans: the Gershonites, from Gershon; the Kohathites, from Kohath; and the Merarites, from Merari.
The Levite families included the Libnites, the Hebronites, the Mahlites, the Mushites, and the Korahites. Kohath fathered Amram,
whose wife was Jochebed, a daughter of Levi who had been born to Levi in Egypt; she bore Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam.
To Aaron were born Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD.
The Levite enrollment was 23,000, counting every male one month old and older; they were not included among the Israelites, for no inheritance was allotted to them among the Israelites.
These are the enrollments that Moses and Eleazar the priest recorded when they counted the Israelites on the plains of Moab beside the Jordan at Jericho.
Among them there was not one man from the earlier enrollment that Moses and Aaron the priest had made in the Wilderness of Sinai,
for the LORD had said that they would surely die in the wilderness. Not one of them survived except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
The daughters of Zelophehad—Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah—descended from Hepher, Gilead, Machir, and Manasseh, and thus belonged to the families of Manasseh son of Joseph.
They drew near to the entrance of the tent of meeting and stood before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, before the leaders, and before the whole congregation, and they said: “
Our father died in the wilderness, though he was not among the company of Korah that gathered against the LORD; rather, he died for his own sin, and he left no sons.
Why should our father’s name be expunged from his clan merely because he had no son? Grant us a possession among our father’s brothers.”
Moses brought their case before the LORD.
“The daughters of Zelophehad speak rightly. You must certainly give them a possession as an inheritance among their father’s brothers, and you must transfer their father’s inheritance to them. “
Moreover, speak to the Israelites and say: If a man dies leaving no son, then you must transfer his inheritance to his daughter.
If he has no daughter, you must give his inheritance to his brothers.
If he has no brothers, you must give his inheritance to his father’s brothers.

And if his father has no brothers, you must give his inheritance to his nearest kinsman within his clan, who shall take possession of it. This shall be a statutory ordinance for the Israelites, as the LORD has commanded Moses.”
The LORD said to Moses, “Go up into this Mount Abarim and survey the land that I have given to the Israelites.
When you have seen it, you too shall be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron was gathered,

because you rebelled against My word in the wilderness of Zin during the congregation’s contention, failing to sanctify Me at the waters before their eyes”—those waters being the waters of Meribah Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.
Moses spoke to the LORD, saying,
“the LORD, God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation
who shall go out before them and come in before them, who shall lead them out and bring them in, so that the congregation of the LORD may not be like sheep without a shepherd.”
The LORD said to Moses, “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hand upon him.
Stand him before Eleazar the priest and before the whole congregation, and commission him in their sight.
Invest him with some of your authority, so that the entire congregation of the Israelites may obey.

He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall inquire for him by the judgment of the Urim before the LORD; at his word they shall go out, and at his word they shall come in—he and all the Israelites with him, even the whole congregation.”
Moses did as the LORD had commanded him: he took Joshua and stood him before Eleazar the priest and before the whole congregation.
He laid his hands upon him and commissioned him, exactly as the LORD had spoken through Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying, "
Command the Israelites and say to them, 'You shall be careful to present to Me, at its appointed time, My offering—My food for My fire offerings—a pleasing aroma to Me.' "
And you shall say to them, 'This is the fire offering that you shall offer to the LORD: two unblemished, year-old male lambs, each day as a perpetual burnt offering.
You shall offer one lamb in the morning and the other between the two evenings.
A tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a grain offering, mixed with a quarter of a hin of beaten oil, shall accompany it.
It is a perpetual burnt offering, ordained at Mount Sinai, a pleasing aroma—an offering by fire to the LORD.
Its libation shall be a quarter of a hin for each lamb; pour out a libation of fermented drink to the LORD in the sanctuary.
And you shall offer the second lamb between the two evenings; like the morning grain offering and its libation, you shall offer it as an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.' "
On the Sabbath day, two unblemished year-old male lambs, together with two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and its libation.
This is the burnt offering for every Sabbath, in addition to the perpetual burnt offering and its libation.
On the first day of each month, you shall present to the LORD a burnt offering: two young bulls, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old male lambs.
With each bull, three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering; with the ram, two-tenths of an ephah;
and with each lamb, a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil. It is a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma—an offering by fire to the LORD.
Their libations shall be half a hin of wine for a bull, a third of a hin for a ram, and a quarter of a hin for a lamb. This is the burnt offering for each month throughout the months of the year.
And one male goat shall be offered as a sin offering to the LORD, in addition to the perpetual burnt offering and its libation. "
On the fourteenth day of the first month is the LORD’s Passover.
On the fifteenth day of this month there is a feast; for seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten.
On the first day there shall be a holy convocation; you shall not do any ordinary work.
You shall present to the LORD an offering by fire, a burnt offering: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old male lambs; they shall be unblemished for you.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for a bull, and two-tenths for a ram.
A tenth of an ephah for each of the seven lambs.
And one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
You shall offer these in addition to the morning burnt offering, which is the perpetual burnt offering.
In the same way you shall offer daily, for seven days, the food of an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD. It shall be offered in addition to the perpetual burnt offering and its libation.
On the seventh day you shall have a holy convocation; you shall not do any ordinary work. "
On the day of the firstfruits, when you present a new grain offering to the LORD at your Feast of Weeks, you shall have a holy convocation; you shall not do any ordinary work.
You shall present a burnt offering as a pleasing aroma to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old male lambs.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for each bull, two-tenths for the one ram.
A tenth of an ephah for each of the seven lambs.
With one male goat to make atonement for you.
You shall offer them, together with their libations, in addition to the perpetual burnt offering and its grain offering; they shall be unblemished for you."
On the first day of the seventh month, you are to observe a sacred convocation; you must perform no laborious work, for it shall be a day of trumpet blasts for you.
You shall present to the LORD a burnt offering—one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished—as a fragrant and pleasing aroma.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mingled with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for the bull, two-tenths for the ram,
and one-tenth for each of the seven lambs.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.

These are in addition to the monthly burnt offering and its grain offering, the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and their libations, as ordained—a fire offering, a soothing aroma to the LORD.
On the tenth day of this seventh month, you shall have a sacred convocation; you must humble yourselves and do no work.
You shall present to the LORD a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma: one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mingled with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for the bull, two-tenths for the ram,
and one-tenth for each of the seven lambs.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the sin offering of atonement and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and their libations.
On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, you shall have a sacred convocation; you must perform no laborious work, and you shall celebrate a feast to the LORD for seven days.
You shall present a fire offering, a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD: thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mingled with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for each of the thirteen bulls, two-tenths for each of the two rams,
and one-tenth for each of the fourteen lambs.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and its libation.
On the second day, you shall present twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished.
Their grain offering and their libations for the bulls, rams, and lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and its libations.
On the third day, you shall present eleven young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished.
Their grain offering and their libations for the bulls, rams, and lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and its libation.
On the fourth day, you shall present ten young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished.
Their grain offering and their libations for the bulls, rams, and lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and its libation.
On the fifth day, you shall present nine young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished.
Their grain offering and their libations for the bulls, rams, and lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and its libation.
On the sixth day, you shall present eight young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished.
Their grain offering and their libations for the bulls, rams, and lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and its libations.
On the seventh day, you shall present seven young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished.
Their grain offering and their libations for the bulls, rams, and lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and its libation.
On the eighth day, you shall have a solemn assembly; you must perform no laborious work.
You shall present a fire offering, a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD: one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished.
Their grain offering and their libations for the bull, ram, and lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and its libation.

You shall present these to the LORD at your appointed feasts, besides your vow offerings and your freewill offerings—for your burnt offerings, your grain offerings, your libations, and your peace offerings.
Thus Moses spoke to the Israelites according to all that the LORD had commanded him.
Then Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the Israelites, saying, “This is the thing that the LORD has commanded:”
When a man vows a vow to the LORD, or swears an oath to bind himself by a pledge, he shall not violate his word; he shall perform all that proceeds from his mouth.
If a woman, while in her father's house in her youth, vows a vow to the LORD and binds herself by a pledge,

and her father hears her vow and her pledge by which she bound herself, and her father remains silent toward her, then all her vows shall stand, and every pledge by which she bound herself shall stand.
But if her father prohibits her on the day he hears, none of her vows or pledges by which she bound herself shall stand; and the LORD will forgive her, because her father prohibited her.
If she is married to a husband while her vows are upon her, or while a rash utterance of her lips by which she bound herself is upon her,
and her husband hears and remains silent toward her on the day he hears, then her vows shall stand, and her pledges by which she bound herself shall stand.
But if her husband prohibits her on the day he hears, he nullifies her vow that is upon her and the rash utterance of her lips by which she bound herself; and the LORD will forgive her.
Every vow of a widow or a divorced woman, by which she has bound herself, shall stand against her.
If she vowed in her husband's house, or bound herself by an oath,
and her husband heard and remained silent toward her and did not prohibit her, then all her vows shall stand, and every pledge by which she bound herself shall stand.

But if her husband indeed nullifies them on the day he hears, then whatever proceeded from her lips concerning her vows or concerning the binding of her soul shall not stand; her husband has nullified them, and the LORD will forgive her.
Every vow and every binding oath to afflict her soul—her husband may confirm it, or her husband may nullify it.

But if her husband is wholly silent toward her from day to day, then he confirms all her vows or all her pledges that are upon her; he has confirmed them, because he was silent toward her on the day he heard.
But if he nullifies them after he has heard, then he shall bear her guilt.
These are the statutes that the LORD commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, between a father and his daughter in her youth in her father's house.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Avenge the Israelites upon the Midianites; afterward you shall die.”
Moses spoke to the people, saying, “Arm men from among you for the war, that they may go against Midian to execute the LORD’s vengeance upon Midian.
You shall send a thousand from each tribe of Israel to the war.”
So from the thousands of Israel they furnished a thousand from each tribe—twelve thousand men armed for war.
Moses sent them to the war, a thousand from each tribe, along with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest; he took with him the holy vessels and the trumpets for the alarm.
They made war against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and killed every male.
They also killed the kings of Midian—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian—and Balaam son of Beor they slew with the sword.
The Israelites took captive the women of Midian and their little ones, and they plundered all their cattle, all their flocks, and all their goods.
They burned with fire all their cities where they dwelt, and all their encampments.
They took all the spoil and all the prey, both of man and of beast.
They brought the captives, the prey, and the spoil to Moses and to Eleazar the priest, and to the congregation of the Israelites, at the camp on the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the congregation went out to meet them outside the camp.
Moses was angry with the officers of the host—the commanders of thousands and of hundreds who were returning from the war.
Moses said to them, “Have you allowed all the women to live?
See, it was these who, on Balaam’s counsel, caused the Israelites to trespass against the LORD in the matter of Peor, so that the plague came upon the congregation of the LORD.
“Now therefore kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman who has known a man by lying with him.
But keep alive for yourselves all the young girls who have not known a man by lying with him.

And you shall camp outside the camp seven days; everyone who has killed any person and everyone who has touched any slain person shall purify yourselves and your captives on the third day and on the seventh day.
You shall also purify every garment, every article of skin, everything made of goats’ hair, and every article of wood.”
Eleazar the priest said to the men of war who had gone to the battle, “This is the statute of the law that the LORD has commanded Moses:
only the gold, the silver, the bronze, the iron, the tin, and the lead—

everything that can withstand fire, you shall pass through the fire, and it shall be clean; nevertheless it shall be purified with the water of purification; and everything that cannot withstand fire you shall pass through water.
You shall wash your clothes on the seventh day, and you shall be clean; and afterward you may come into the camp.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Take the sum of the prey that was taken, both of man and of beast—you and Eleazar the priest and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the congregation—
and divide the prey into two parts, between the men of war who went out to battle and all the congregation.
And levy a tribute for the LORD from the men of war who went out to battle: one soul out of five hundred, both of persons and of cattle, of donkeys and of sheep.
From their half you shall take it and give it to Eleazar the priest as the LORD’s heave offering.

And from the half of the Israelites you shall take one portion of fifty, of persons, of cattle, of donkeys, and of sheep, of all the beasts, and give them to the Levites who keep charge of the tabernacle of the LORD.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The prey that remained from the spoil taken by the men of war amounted to 675,000 sheep,
and 32,000 persons in all—every woman who had not known a man by lying with him.
The half, the portion of those who went out to war, numbered 337,500 sheep;
the LORD’s tribute from the sheep was 675;
the cattle were 36,000, of which the LORD’s tribute was 72;
the donkeys were 30,500, of which the LORD’s tribute was 61;
and the persons were 16,000, of which the LORD’s tribute was 32 persons.
Moses gave the tribute, the LORD’s heave offering, to Eleazar the priest, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
From the half belonging to the Israelites, which Moses had divided off from the men who had gone to war—
Moses took one portion of fifty from the Israelites’ half, of persons and of beasts, and gave them to the Levites who kept charge of the tabernacle of the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The officers over the thousands of the army, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, came near to Moses
and said to him, “Your servants have taken a count of the men of war under our command, and not one of us is missing.
So we have brought an offering to the LORD—what each man found: gold articles, anklets, bracelets, rings, earrings, and pendants—to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from them—all the crafted articles.
The gold of the heave offering that the commanders of thousands and of hundreds offered to the LORD was 16,750 shekels.
The men of war had each taken plunder for himself.
Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD.

The Reubenites and Gadites possessed an exceedingly great abundance of livestock, and when they surveyed the lands of Jazer and Gilead, they perceived that the region was eminently suited to pastoral husbandry.
Accordingly, the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben approached Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the congregation, and said,
"Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon—
the land that the LORD subdued before the congregation of Israel is a land for livestock, and your servants possess livestock in abundance.
If we have found favor in your sight, let this land be granted to your servants as a possession, and do not compel us to cross the Jordan."
Moses said to the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben, "Shall your brothers go to war while you remain here?
Why would you dishearten the Israelites from crossing into the land that the LORD has given them?
This is precisely what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to survey the land.
They ascended to the Valley of Eshcol, saw the land, and then discouraged the Israelites so that they would not enter the land that the LORD had given them.
On that day the LORD's anger was kindled, and He swore an oath, saying,
'Surely none of the men who came up from Egypt, from twenty years old and upward, shall see the land I swore to give Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they have not wholly followed Me,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, for they have wholly followed the LORD.
The LORD's anger burned against Israel, and He made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until the entire generation that had done evil in the LORD's sight was consumed.
And now you have arisen in your fathers' place, a brood of sinful men, only to add still more to the LORD's fierce anger against Israel.
For if you turn away from following Him, He will again abandon this people to the wilderness, and you will bring ruin upon all this people.'"
Then they came near to him and said, "We will build sheepfolds here for our livestock and cities for our children.

But we ourselves will go armed and march in the vanguard before the Israelites until we have brought them to their place, while our children remain in fortified cities, safe from the inhabitants of the land.
We will not return to our homes until every Israelite has received his inheritance.
For we shall not share in their inheritance west of the Jordan and beyond; our inheritance has fallen to us east of the Jordan."
Moses said to them, "If you do this—if you arm yourselves before the LORD for war,
and every armed man among you crosses the Jordan before the LORD until He has driven out His enemies from before Him,
and the land is subdued before the LORD—then afterward you may return, and you will be blameless before the LORD and before Israel, and this land shall be your possession before the LORD.
But if you do not do so, behold, you have sinned against the LORD; and be assured that your sin will find you out.
Build cities for your children and folds for your flocks, and do as you have promised."
The sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben said to Moses, "We, your servants, will do as my lord commands.
Our children, our wives, our livestock, and all our beasts will remain in the cities of Gilead.
But your servants will cross over, every man armed for battle, before the LORD to wage war, as my lord has spoken."
Moses commanded them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the heads of the fathers' houses of the tribes of Israel.

Moses said to them, "If the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben cross the Jordan with you, every man armed for battle before the LORD, and the land is subdued before you, then you shall give them the land of Gilead as a possession.
But if they do not cross over armed with you, then they shall receive possessions among you in the land of Canaan."
The sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben answered, "What the LORD has spoken to your servants, so we will do.
We will cross over armed before the LORD into Canaan, and our inherited possession shall remain with us on this side of the Jordan."

Moses gave to them—to the sons of Gad, the sons of Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph—the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan: the land with its cities and the surrounding territories.
The sons of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
Beth-nimrah, and Beth-haran—fortified cities and sheepfolds.
The Reubenites built Heshbon, Elealeh, and Kiriathaim,
along with Nebo, Baal-meon (whose names were changed), and Sibmah; and they gave names to the cities they built.
Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, captured it, and dispossessed the Amorites who were in it.
Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled there.
Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their villages, calling them Havvoth-jair.
Nobah went and captured Kenath with its villages, and called it Nobah after his own name.
These are the stages of the Israelites' march out of Egypt, proceeding by their divisions under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
At the the LORD's command, Moses recorded their points of departure according to their stages; and these are their stages according to their points of departure.
They set out from Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the day after the Passover, the Israelites went out triumphantly in full view of all the Egyptians,
while the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn, whom the the LORD had struck down among them; and the the LORD executed judgments against their gods.
The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.
They set out from Etham and turned back toward Pi-hahiroth, which is opposite Baal-zephon, and camped before Migdol.
They set out from before Pi-hahiroth and passed through the sea into the wilderness; they traveled three days' journey in the wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.
They set out from Marah and came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.
They set out from Elim and camped by the Red Sea.
They set out from the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.
They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
They set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah.
They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shapher.
They set out from Mount Shapher and camped at Haradah.
They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
They set out from Tahath and camped at Terah.
They set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.
They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
They set out from Ezion-geber and camped in the wilderness of Zin, that is, Kadesh.
They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the edge of the land of Edom.
At the the LORD's command, Aaron the priest ascended Mount Hor and died there in the fortieth year after the Israelites had come out of Egypt, on the first day of the fifth month.
Aaron was one hundred twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the south of the land of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming.
They set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.
They set out from Iyim and camped at Dibon-gad.
They set out from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, before Nebo.
They set out from the mountains of Abarim and camped in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
They camped by the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim in the plains of Moab.
The LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
you must drive out before you all the inhabitants of the land, destroy all their carved images and all their molten images, and demolish all their high places.
You shall take possession of the land and dwell in it, for I have given you the land to possess.

"You are to apportion the land by lot as an inheritance among your clans: to a more numerous clan give a larger inheritance, and to a smaller clan a smaller one; wherever the lot falls for anyone, that shall be his. You shall inherit according to the tribes of your fathers.

But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land before you, then those you allow to remain will become barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides, and they will harass you in the land where you live.
And I will do to you what I had planned to do to them."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
"Command the Israelites and say to them, 'When you are entering the land of Canaan, this is the land that shall fall to you as an inheritance—the land of Canaan according to its borders.'
Your southern side shall be from the wilderness of Zin along the border of Edom, and your southern boundary shall be from the end of the Salt Sea eastward.
"Your border shall turn from the south to the ascent of Akrabbim and pass on to Zin, and its exits shall be from the south to Kadesh-barnea; and it shall go out to Hazar-addar and pass on to Azmon.
Then the border shall turn from Azmon to the Brook of Egypt, and its exits shall be to the sea.
For the western border, you shall have the Great Sea and its coast; this shall be your western border.
"This shall be your northern border: from the Great Sea you shall mark out for yourselves Mount Hor.
From Mount Hor you shall mark out to the entrance to Hamath, and the exits of the border shall be to Zedad.
Then the border shall go out to Ziphron, and its exits shall be at Hazar-enan. This shall be your northern border.
"You shall mark out for yourselves your eastern border from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
The border shall descend from Shepham to Riblah on the east side of Ain, and the border shall descend and reach the eastern shore of the Sea of Chinnereth eastward.
The border shall descend to the Jordan, and its exits shall be at the Salt Sea. This shall be your land according to its borders all around."
Moses commanded the Israelites, saying, "This is the land that you shall inherit by lot, which the LORD has commanded to give to the nine tribes and to the half-tribe.

For the tribe of the children of Reuben, according to their ancestral houses, and the tribe of the children of Gad, according to their ancestral houses, have received their inheritance; and the half-tribe of Manasseh has received its inheritance.
The two and a half tribes have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan at Jericho, eastward, toward the sunrise."
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
"These are the names of the men who shall apportion the land for you: Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun.
You shall take one leader from each tribe to apportion the land.
These are the names of the men: for the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
for the tribe of the sons of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud;
for the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon;
for the tribe of the sons of Dan, Bukki son of Jogli;
for the sons of Joseph—for the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, Hanniel son of Ephod,
and for the tribe of the sons of Ephraim, Kemuel son of Shiphtan;
for the tribe of the sons of Zebulun, Elizaphan son of Parnach;
for the tribe of the sons of Issachar, Paltiel son of Azzan;
for the tribe of the sons of Asher, Ahihud son of Shelomi;
and for the tribe of the sons of Naphtali, Pedahel son of Ammihud.
These are the ones whom the LORD has commanded to apportion the inheritance to the Israelites in the land of Canaan."
The LORD spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, saying, “

Command the Israelites to give the Levites, out of the inheritance of their holdings, cities in which to dwell, together with pasturelands surrounding them, and you shall give the pasturelands to the Levites.
The cities shall be theirs to dwell in, and their pasturelands shall be for their cattle, their property, and all their animals.
The pasturelands of the cities that you give to the Levites shall extend a thousand cubits outward from the wall of each city in every direction.

You shall measure outside the city: on the east side two thousand cubits, on the south side two thousand cubits, on the west side two thousand cubits, and on the north side two thousand cubits, with the city in the center; this shall constitute the pasturelands of their cities.
The cities that you give to the Levites shall be the six cities of refuge, which you shall designate so that the manslayer may flee to them, and besides these you shall give forty-two cities.
All the cities that you give to the Levites shall be forty-eight, together with their pasturelands.

As for the cities that you give from the possession of the Israelites, from the larger tribe you shall give many, and from the smaller tribe you shall give few; each tribe shall give cities to the Levites in proportion to the inheritance it receives.”
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying, “
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
you shall designate cities to be cities of refuge for you, so that the manslayer who kills a person unintentionally may flee to them.
The cities shall be a refuge for you from the avenger of blood, so that the manslayer does not die until he stands before the congregation for judgment.
The cities that you give shall be six cities of refuge.
You shall provide three cities beyond the Jordan and three cities in the land of Canaan; they shall be cities of refuge.
These six cities shall be a refuge for the Israelites, for the sojourner, and for the temporary resident among them, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.
“If he strikes him with an iron implement and he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer shall be put to death.
If he strikes him with a stone in his hand that can kill, and he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer shall be put to death.
If he strikes him with a wooden implement in his hand that can kill, and he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer shall be put to death.
The avenger of blood himself shall put the murderer to death; when he encounters him, he shall put him to death.
If he pushes him in hatred, or throws something at him with intent, and he dies,
or if he strikes him in enmity with his hand so that he dies, the striker shall be put to death; he is a murderer. The avenger of blood shall put the murderer to death when he encounters him.
But if he pushes him suddenly without enmity, or throws any object at him without intent,
or if, without seeing him, he drops a stone on him that could kill, and he dies, though he was not his enemy and did not seek his harm,
then the congregation shall judge between the striker and the avenger of blood according to these ordinances.

The congregation shall rescue the manslayer from the hand of the avenger of blood and return him to his city of refuge, where he had fled, and he shall dwell there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
But if the manslayer goes beyond the boundary of his city of refuge to which he fled,
and the avenger of blood finds him outside the boundary of his city of refuge and kills the manslayer, the avenger shall incur no bloodguilt.
For he must remain in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest; after the death of the high priest, the manslayer may return to the land of his possession.
“These things shall be a statute of judgment for you throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
If anyone kills a person, the murderer shall be put to death on the evidence of witnesses; but no one shall be put to death on the testimony of a single witness.
Moreover, you shall not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty of death, but he shall surely be put to death.
Nor shall you accept a ransom for one who has fled to his city of refuge, so that he may return to dwell in the land before the death of the high priest.
You shall not pollute the land in which you are, for blood pollutes the land, and no expiation can be made for the land for the blood that is shed in it except by the blood of the one who shed it.
You shall not defile the land in which you dwell, in which I, the LORD, dwell among you, for I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites.”

The patriarchal chieftains of the clan of Gilead—son of Machir, son of Manasseh—drawn from the Josephite houses, approached Moses and the leaders, namely the heads of the ancestral houses of the Israelites, and spoke before them.

They said, "The LORD commanded our lord to apportion the land as an inheritance to the Israelites by lot, and our lord was commanded by the LORD to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

Now, should those daughters marry into one of the tribes of the Israelites, their inheritance will be alienated from our ancestral estate and annexed to the estate of the tribe into which they marry; thus our allotted portion will be diminished.

Moreover, when the jubilee arrives for the Israelites, their estate will be permanently incorporated into the tribe to which they have married and thereby subtracted from the estate of our paternal tribe."
Moses then instructed the Israelites in accordance with the word of the LORD, saying, "The tribe of Joseph has spoken justly."

He further declared that this is the ordinance the LORD has decreed concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: they may marry whomever they deem suitable, provided they marry within the clan of their father's tribe.
Hence no Israelite inheritance shall circulate from tribe to tribe, since each Israelite must remain tenaciously attached to the patrimony of his ancestral tribe.
Furthermore, every daughter who inherits property among the Israelites must marry within her father's tribal clan, so that the Israelites may each retain the patrimony of his forefathers.
No estate, therefore, shall pass from one tribe to another, because each Israelite tribe must hold fast to its own allotment.
Zelophehad's daughters complied exactly with what the LORD had commanded through Moses.
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah—the daughters of Zelophehad—married their paternal cousins.
They married within the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained with their father's tribal house.
These are the statutes and ordinances the LORD enjoined upon the Israelites through Moses on the plains of Moab beside the Jordan across from Jericho.
These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel in the wilderness, beyond the Jordan, in the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
It is an eleven days' journey from Horeb by way of Mount Seir to Kadesh-barnea.
In the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Moses spoke to the Israelites according to all that the LORD had commanded him concerning them,
after he had defeated Sihon, king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, who dwelt in Ashtaroth in Edrei.
Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses undertook to expound this law, saying:
The LORD our God spoke to us at Horeb, saying, “You have remained at this mountain long enough.

Turn and set out for yourselves, and go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all their neighboring peoples in the Arabah, in the hill country, in the lowlands, in the Negev, along the seacoast, in the land of the Canaanites, and in Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates.
See, I have set the land before you. Enter and take possession of the land that the LORD swore to give to your fathers—to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—and to their descendants after them.”
At that time I said to you, “I cannot bear you by myself.
The LORD your God has multiplied you, and behold, you are today as numerous as the stars of heaven.
May the LORD, the God of your fathers, increase you a thousand times more than you are, and bless you, as He has promised you.
How can I alone bear your load, your burden, and your disputes?
Choose for yourselves wise, discerning, and reputable men from your tribes, and I will appoint them as your heads.”
And you answered me and said, “What you have proposed is good.”
So I took the heads of your tribes, wise and respected men, and appointed them as leaders over you—commanders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, and officers for your tribes.
And I charged your judges at that time, saying, “Hear the cases between your brothers, and judge righteously between a man and his brother or the foreigner residing among you.

You shall not show partiality in judgment; you shall hear the small and the great alike. You shall not be intimidated by anyone, for judgment belongs to God. And bring to me any case that is too difficult for you, and I will hear it.”
And I commanded you at that time all the things that you should do.

Then we set out from Horeb and went through all that great and terrifying wilderness that you saw, on the way to the hill country of the Amorites, as the LORD our God had commanded us. We came to Kadesh-barnea.
And I said to you, “You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.
See, the LORD your God has set the land before you. Go up and take possession, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has told you. Do not fear or be dismayed.”
Then all of you came to me and said, “Let us send men ahead of us to spy out the land and bring back a report to us concerning the way by which we should go up and the cities that we shall enter.”
The proposal seemed good to me, so I took twelve men from among you, one man from each tribe.
They turned and went up into the hill country and came to the Valley of Eshcol and spied it out.
And they took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us, and they brought back a report and said, “It is a good land that the LORD our God is giving us.”
Yet you would not go up, but rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.
And you grumbled in your tents and said, “Because the LORD hated us, He brought us out of the land of Egypt to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us.

Where are we going up? Our brothers have made our hearts melt, saying, ‘The people are greater and taller than we are; the cities are great and fortified up to heaven; and moreover we have seen the sons of the Anakim there.’”
Then I said to you, “Do not be terrified or afraid of them.
The LORD your God, who goes before you, He will fight for you, just as He did for you in Egypt before your eyes,
and in the wilderness, where you have seen how the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, all the way that you went until you came to this place.”
Yet in this matter you did not believe the LORD your God,
who goes before you on the way to seek out a place for you to camp, in fire by night and in cloud by day, to show you the way in which you should go.
And the LORD heard the sound of your words and was angry, and He swore, saying, “
Not one of these men of this evil generation shall see the good land that I swore to give to your fathers.
Except Caleb the son of Jephunneh; he shall see it, and to him and to his sons I will give the land on which he has trodden, because he has wholly followed the LORD.”
The LORD was angry with me also because of you, and He said, “You also shall not go in there.
Joshua the son of Nun, who stands before you, he shall go in there. Encourage him, for he shall cause Israel to inherit it.

And as for your little ones, whom you said would become a prey, and your children who today have no knowledge of good or evil, they shall go in there, and to them I will give it, and they shall possess it.”
But as for you, turn and set out for the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea.

Then you answered and said to me, “We have sinned against the LORD. We will go up and fight, according to all that the LORD our God commanded us.” And every man of you girded on his weapons of war and rashly undertook to go up into the hill country.
And the LORD said to me, “Tell them: Do not go up, and do not fight, for I am not among you, lest you be defeated before your enemies.”
So I spoke to you, but you would not listen. You rebelled against the command of the LORD, and you presumptuously went up into the hill country.
Then the Amorites who lived in that hill country came out against you and chased you as bees do, and beat you down in Seir as far as Hormah.
And you returned and wept before the LORD, but the LORD would not listen to your voice or give ear to you.
So you remained at Kadesh many days, the days that you remained.
Then we turned and journeyed into the wilderness by way of the Red Sea, just as the LORD had spoken to me, and for many days we circled Mount Seir.
Then the LORD said to me,
“You have circled this mountain long enough; turn northward.
Give this charge to the people: ‘You are passing through the territory of your brothers, the sons of Esau, who inhabit Seir; they will be exceedingly afraid of you, so guard yourselves carefully.’
Do not provoke them, for I will not give you any of their land, not even a footstep's breadth, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as an inheritance.
You must buy food from them with silver so that you may eat, and you must also purchase water from them with silver so that you may drink.

For the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has watched over your journey through this vast wilderness. The LORD your God has been with you; you have lacked nothing these forty years.”

So we passed by our brothers, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. We turned from the Arabah road, which comes from Elath and Ezion-geber, and traveled along the road through the wilderness of Moab.

Then the LORD said to me, “Do not harass Moab or provoke them to war, for I will not give you any of their land as an inheritance, because I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as an inheritance.”
The Emim had formerly lived there—a people great and numerous and tall, like the Anakim.
They too were regarded as Rephaim, like the Anakim, but the Moabites called them Emim.

The Horites also formerly inhabited Seir, but the descendants of Esau drove them out and annihilated them before them and settled in their place, just as Israel did in the land the LORD gave them as a possession.
“Now arise and cross the Brook Zered.” So we crossed the Brook Zered.

The days we spent traveling from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the Brook Zered were thirty-eight years, until the entire generation of men of war had perished from the camp, as the LORD had sworn to them.
Indeed, the hand of the LORD was against them, to destroy them from the camp until they were consumed.
When all the men of war had died off from among the people,
“Today you are to pass by the border of Moab at Ar.

When you come near the Ammonites, do not distress them or provoke them to war, for I will not give you any of the land of the Ammonites as an inheritance, because I have given it to the descendants of Lot as an inheritance.”
It too is regarded as a land of the Rephaim; the Rephaim formerly dwelt there, but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim—
a people great and numerous and tall, like the Anakim; yet the LORD destroyed them before the Ammonites, who then dispossessed them and settled in their place,
just as He did for the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir, when He destroyed the Horites before them; they drove them out and settled in their place, and they remain there to this day.
As for the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, the Caphtorim, who came from Caphtor, destroyed them and settled in their place.
“Arise, set out, and cross the Arnon Valley. See, I have delivered Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land into your hand. Begin to take possession of it, and engage him in battle.
This day I will begin to put the dread and fear of you upon all the peoples under heaven, so that when they hear the report of you, they will tremble and be in anguish before you.”
From the wilderness of Kedemoth I sent messengers with words of peace to Sihon king of Heshbon, saying,
“Let me pass through your land. I will travel only along the road; I will not turn aside to the right or to the left.
Sell me food for silver so that I may eat, and give me water for silver so that I may drink. Only let me pass through on foot,
just as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land the LORD our God is giving us.”

But Sihon king of Heshbon was unwilling to let us pass through, because the LORD your God had hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, in order to deliver him into your hand, as is now the case.
Then the LORD said to me, “See, I have begun to deliver Sihon and his land over to you. Begin to take possession of his land.”
Then Sihon and all his people came out to meet us in battle at Jahaz.
The LORD our God delivered him over to us, and we struck him down, along with his sons and all his people.
At that time we captured all his cities and devoted to destruction every city—men, women, and children—leaving no survivor.
We took only the livestock and the spoil of the cities we had captured as our own.
From Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley, and from the city that is in the valley, as far as Gilead, there was no city too strong for us; the LORD our God delivered all of them over to us.
But you did not go near the land of the Ammonites—anywhere along the Jabbok River, the cities of the hill country, or anything else the LORD our God had commanded.
Then we turned and ascended by the road to Bashan, and Og, king of Bashan, came out against us with all his people to wage war at Edrei.

The LORD said to me, “Do not fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand, together with all his people and his land; and you shall deal with him as you dealt with Sihon, king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon.”
So the LORD our God also delivered Og, king of Bashan, and all his people into our hands, and we struck him down until no survivor remained.
At that time we captured all his cities; there was not a single city that we did not take from them—sixty cities in all, the whole region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All these were fortified cities, with high walls, gates, and bars, besides a great many unwalled villages.
We devoted them to destruction, just as we had done to Sihon, king of Heshbon, destroying every city—men, women, and children.
But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we plundered for ourselves.
Thus, at that time, we took from the two kings of the Amorites the land beyond the Jordan, from the Valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon—
the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir—
all the cities of the plain, all Gilead, and all Bashan, as far as Salcah and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

For Og, king of Bashan, alone remained of the remnant of the Rephaim; behold, his bed was a bed of iron—was it not in Rabbah of the Ammonites?—nine cubits long and four cubits wide, by the cubit of a man.
This land we possessed at that time: from Aroer, which is by the Valley of the Arnon, and half the hill country of Gilead with its cities, I gave to the Reubenites and the Gadites.
The rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh—the whole region of Argob, all Bashan. That land is called the land of the Rephaim.

Jair, son of Manasseh, took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and he called those villages of Bashan after his own name, Havvoth-jair, as they are called to this day.
To the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave from Gilead to the Valley of the Arnon—the middle of the valley as a boundary—and as far as the Jabbok, the river that forms the border of the Ammonites;
the Arabah also, with the Jordan as its boundary, from Chinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, beneath the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
At that time I commanded you, saying, “The LORD your God has given you this land to possess; all you men of valor shall cross over armed before your brothers, the children of Israel.
Only your wives, your little ones, and your livestock—I know that you have much livestock—shall remain in the cities that I have given you,

until the LORD gives rest to your brothers, as He has to you, and they too possess the land that the LORD your God is giving them beyond the Jordan; then each man shall return to his possession that I have given you.”

And I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, “Your eyes have seen all that the LORD your God has done to these two kings; so the LORD will do to all the kingdoms into which you are crossing over there.
You shall not fear them, for the LORD your God—He Himself is the One fighting for you.”
At that time I pleaded with the LORD, saying,
“O Lord, the LORD, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your mighty hand; for what god is there in heaven or on earth who can do according to Your works and according to Your might?
Please let me cross over and see the good land beyond the Jordan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon.”
But the LORD was angry with me for your sake and would not listen to me; and the LORD said to me, “Enough! Do not speak to Me anymore about this matter.
Go up to the top of Pisgah and lift up your eyes westward, northward, southward, and eastward, and look with your eyes; for you shall not cross this Jordan.
But command Joshua, strengthen him, and encourage him, for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land that you will see.”
So we stayed in the valley opposite Beth-peor.

And now, O Israel, give heed to the statutes and the ordinances that I am instructing you to observe, that you may live and enter to possess the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, is bestowing upon you.
You shall not add to the word that I command you, nor diminish from it, that you may keep the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you.
Your eyes have seen what the LORD did at Baal-peor; for the LORD your God destroyed from your midst all the men who followed Baal-peor.
But you who cleaved to the LORD your God are all alive this day.
Behold, I have taught you statutes and ordinances, as the LORD my God commanded me, to perform them in the midst of the land into which you are entering to possess it.

Therefore observe and perform them, for this shall be your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the peoples, who, when they hear all these things, shall say, "Surely this great nation is a wise and discerning people."
For what great nation is there that has a god so near to it as the LORD our God is to us, whenever we call upon Him?
And what great nation is there that has statutes and ordinances so righteous as all this law that I am setting before you today?

Only take heed to yourself, and guard your soul diligently, lest you forget the things that your eyes have seen, and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life; and make them known to your children and to your children's children.

The day when you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, when the LORD said to me, "Assemble the people to Me, that I may let them hear My words, so that they may learn to fear Me all the days that they live upon the earth, and that they may teach their children."
And you drew near and stood under the mountain, while the mountain burned with fire unto the heart of heaven, with darkness, cloud, and thick gloom.
Then the LORD spoke to you out of the midst of the fire: you heard the sound of words, but you saw no form; there was only a voice.
And He declared to you His covenant, which He commanded you to perform—the Ten Commandments—and He wrote them upon two tablets of stone.
And the LORD commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and ordinances, that you might perform them in the land whither you are passing over to possess.
Therefore guard yourselves exceedingly, for you saw no form on the day that the LORD spoke to you out of the midst of the fire at Horeb,
lest you corrupt yourselves and make for yourselves a graven image, the likeness of any figure, the form of male or female,
the form of any beast that is on the earth, the form of any winged bird that flies in the heavens,
the form of anything that creeps upon the ground, the form of any fish that is in the waters beneath the earth.

And lest, when you lift up your eyes to heaven, and see the sun and the moon and the stars, all the host of heaven, you be drawn away and bow down to them and serve them—things that the LORD your God has allotted to all the peoples under the whole heaven.
But the LORD has taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be to Him a people of inheritance, as it is this day.
Moreover, the LORD was incensed against me on account of your words, and He swore that I should not cross the Jordan, nor enter the good land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
For I am to die in this land; I shall not cross the Jordan; but you shall cross over and possess that good land.

Take heed to yourselves, lest you forget the covenant of the LORD your God, which He made with you, and make for yourselves a graven image in the likeness of anything that the LORD your God has forbidden you.
For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.

When you beget children and children's children, and have grown old in the land, if you act corruptly and make a graven image in the likeness of anything, and do evil in the sight of the LORD your God, so as to provoke Him to anger,

I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that you shall quickly perish from the land into which you are crossing the Jordan to possess; you shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall be utterly destroyed.
And the LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and you shall be left few in number among the nations whither the LORD will lead you.
And there you shall serve gods of wood and stone, the work of men's hands, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.
But from there you shall seek the LORD your God, and you shall find Him, if you seek Him with all your heart and with all your soul.
When you are in tribulation, and all these things have come upon you, in the latter days you shall return to the LORD your God and hearken unto His voice.
For the LORD your God is a merciful God; He will not fail you nor destroy you, nor forget the covenant with your fathers that He swore to them.

For ask now of the former days, which were before you, since the day that God created man upon the earth, and ask from one end of heaven to the other, whether so great a thing as this has ever happened, or anything like it has ever been heard.
Did any people ever hear the voice of God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as you have heard, and live?

Or has God ever attempted to go and take for Himself a nation from the midst of another nation, by trials, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, and by great terrors, according to all that the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?
