To you it was shown, that you might know that the LORD is God; there is none else besides Him.
Out of heaven He made you hear His voice, that He might instruct you; and upon earth He showed you His great fire, and you heard His words out of the midst of the fire.
And because He loved your fathers, He chose their seed after them, and brought you out of Egypt in His presence, with His great power,
to drive out from before you nations greater and mightier than you, to bring you in, to give you their land for an inheritance, as it is this day.
Know therefore this day, and lay it to your heart, that the LORD is God in heaven above and upon the earth beneath; there is none else.

And you shall keep His statutes and His commandments, which I command you this day, that it may be well with you and with your children after you, and that you may prolong your days upon the land that the LORD your God is giving you for all days.
Then Moses set apart three cities beyond the Jordan, toward the rising of the sun,
that the manslayer might flee thither, who should kill his neighbor unawares, and hated him not in time past; and that, fleeing unto one of these cities, he might live.
Bezer in the wilderness, upon the tableland, for the Reubenites; and Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
And this is the law which Moses set before the children of Israel.
These are the testimonies, and the statutes, and the ordinances, which Moses spoke unto the children of Israel, when they came forth out of Egypt,

beyond the Jordan, in the valley over against Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt at Heshbon, whom Moses and the children of Israel smote, when they came forth out of Egypt;
and they took possession of his land, and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites, who were beyond the Jordan toward the rising of the sun;
from Aroer, which is on the bank of the river Arnon, even unto Mount Sirion, which is Hermon;
and all the Arabah beyond the Jordan eastward, even unto the sea of the Arabah, under the slopes of Pisgah.
Moses summoned all Israel and declared to them: “Hear, O Israel, the statutes and ordinances that I am proclaiming in your hearing this day; learn them and be scrupulous to observe them.
The LORD our God cut a covenant with us at Horeb.
The LORD did not make this covenant with our ancestors, but with us—every one of us who is alive here today.
The LORD spoke with you face to face on the mountain, from the midst of the fire.
I stood between the LORD and you at that time to convey to you the word of the LORD, because you were terrified by the fire and did not ascend the mountain, saying:
“I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
You shall have no other gods before Me.
You shall not make for yourself a carved image, or any likeness of what is in the heavens above, or on the earth beneath, or in the waters beneath the earth.

You shall not bow down to them or serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me,
but showing steadfast love to thousands, to those who love Me and keep My commandments. “
You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not hold guiltless anyone who takes His name in vain.
Observe the Sabbath day, to keep it holy, as the LORD your God has commanded you.
Six days you shall labor and do all your work,

but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God; on it you shall not do any work—neither you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your ox, nor your donkey, nor any of your livestock, nor the foreigner within your gates—so that your male servant and your female servant may rest as you do.

Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out of there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm; therefore the LORD your God has commanded you to keep the Sabbath day. “
Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God has commanded you, so that your days may be prolonged and that it may go well with you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife; you shall not desire your neighbor’s house, his field, his male servant, his female servant, his ox, his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.”

The LORD spoke these words to your whole assembly on the mountain, out of the midst of the fire, the cloud, and the thick darkness, with a loud voice, and He added nothing more; then He wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.
When you heard the voice out of the midst of the darkness, while the mountain was blazing with fire, you drew near to me—all the heads of your tribes and your elders—

and you said, “Behold, the LORD our God has shown us His glory and His greatness, and we have heard His voice out of the midst of the fire; today we have seen that God speaks with a human being and yet that person lives.
Now, therefore, why should we die? For this great fire will consume us, and we shall die. If we hear the voice of the LORD our God any longer, we shall die.
For what mortal being has ever heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the midst of fire, as we have, and survived?
You go near and hear all that the LORD our God says; then speak to us all that the LORD our God speaks to you, and we will hear and do it.”

The LORD heard the voice of your words when you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me, “I have heard the voice of the words of this people, which they have spoken to you; they have done well in all that they have spoken.
Oh, that they had such a heart as to fear Me and keep all My commandments always, so that it might be well with them and with their children forever!
Go and say to them, ‘Return to your tents.’

But as for you, stand here by Me, and I will speak to you all the commandments, statutes, and ordinances that you are to teach them, so that they may observe them in the land I am giving them to possess.”
So be careful to do as the LORD your God has commanded you; do not turn aside to the right or to the left.
Walk in all the way that the LORD your God has commanded you, so that you may live and prosper, and prolong your days in the land that you will possess.

And this constitutes the commandment—the statutes and the judgments—that the LORD your God has commanded to be taught to you, that you may perform them in the land into which you are crossing to take possession of it.

So that you may fear the LORD your God—you, your son, and your grandson—all the days of your life, and keep all His statutes and His commandments that I am commanding you, so that your days may be prolonged.

Hear, O Israel, and carefully perform them, that it may be well with you and that you may multiply greatly, in a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has spoken to you.
Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one.
And you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might.
And these words that I am commanding you today shall be upon your heart.
And you shall teach them diligently to your children, and you shall speak of them when you sit in your house, when you walk along the road, when you lie down, and when you rise.
And you shall bind them as a sign upon your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes.
And you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
And it shall be, when the LORD your God brings you into the land that He swore to your fathers—to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob—to give you great and good cities that you did not build,
and houses full of all good things that you did not fill, and cisterns hewn that you did not hew, vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant; and you shall eat and be satisfied.
Beware, lest you forget the LORD, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
You shall fear the LORD your God, and Him you shall serve, and by His name you shall swear.
You shall not go after other gods, of the gods of the peoples who are around you.
For the LORD your God in your midst is a jealous God, lest the anger of the LORD your God be kindled against you, and He destroy you from the face of the earth.
You shall not test the LORD your God as you tested Him at Massah.
You shall diligently keep the commandments of the LORD your God, and His testimonies and His statutes that He has commanded you.
And you shall do what is right and good in the sight of the LORD, that it may go well with you and that you may go in and take possession of the good land that the LORD swore to your fathers,
to drive out all your enemies before you, as the LORD has spoken.
When your son asks you in time to come, saying, "What are these testimonies and statutes and judgments that the LORD our God has commanded you?"
And you shall say to your son, "We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt, and the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
And the LORD showed great and severe signs and wonders in Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his house, before our eyes.
And He brought us out from there, to bring us in, to give us the land that He swore to our fathers. "
And the LORD commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God, for our good always, that He might preserve us alive, as at this day.
And it shall be righteousness for us, if we are careful to do all this commandment before the LORD our God, as He has commanded us."

When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are entering to possess, and He drives out before you many nations—the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites—seven nations greater and mightier than you;
and when the LORD your God delivers them over to you, and you defeat them, then you shall devote them to utter destruction. You shall make no covenant with them and show them no mercy.
You shall not intermarry with them: you shall not give your daughter to his son, nor take his daughter for your son;
for they will turn your sons away from following Me, so that they serve other gods; then the anger of the LORD your God will be kindled against you, and He will swiftly annihilate you.
But this is what you shall do to them: you shall tear down their altars, shatter their sacred pillars, cut down their Asherim, and burn their carved images in the fire.
For you are a holy people to the LORD your God; the LORD your God has chosen you from among all the peoples on the face of the earth to be His own people, a treasured possession.
The LORD did not set His love upon you or choose you because you were more numerous than any other people, for you are the fewest of all peoples.

Rather, because the LORD loved you and kept the oath that He swore to your fathers, He brought you out with a mighty hand and redeemed you from the house of bondage, from the hand of Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
Know, therefore, that the LORD your God is God: He is the faithful God, who keeps covenant and steadfast love with those who love Him and keep His commandments, to a thousand generations,
and who repays to their face those who hate Him, bringing them to ruin; He will not delay, but will repay to their face the one who hates Him.
Therefore you shall keep the commandment, the statutes, and the ordinances that I command you this day, to do them.

And it shall come to pass, because you listen to these ordinances and you keep and do them, that the LORD your God will keep with you the covenant and the steadfast love that He swore to your fathers.

He will love you, bless you, and multiply you; He will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground—your grain, your new wine, and your oil—the increase of your cattle and the young of your flock, in the land that He swore to your fathers to give you.
You shall be blessed above all peoples; there shall be no barren man or woman among you, nor among your livestock.
The LORD will remove from you every sickness; He will not lay upon you any of the evil diseases that you knew in Egypt, but He will lay them upon all who hate you.
You shall devour all the peoples whom the LORD your God is giving you; your eye shall not pity them, neither shall you serve their gods, for that would be a snare to you.
If you should say in your heart, “These nations are too many for me; how can I dispossess them?”
You shall not be afraid of them; you shall remember well what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt—

the great trials that your eyes saw, the signs and wonders, the mighty hand and outstretched arm by which the LORD your God brought you out. The LORD your God will do likewise to all the peoples whom you fear.
Moreover, the LORD your God will send the hornet among them, until those who are left and hide themselves from you have perished.
You shall not be terrified of them, for the LORD your God is in your midst—a great and awesome God.
The LORD your God will drive out those nations before you little by little; you will not be able to destroy them all at once, lest the beasts of the field multiply against you.
But the LORD your God will deliver them over to you and will throw them into great panic until they are destroyed.
He will give their kings into your hand, and you shall blot out their name from under heaven; no one shall be able to stand before you, until you have destroyed them.

The carved images of their gods you shall burn with fire; you shall not covet the silver or gold that is upon them, nor take it for yourself, lest you be snared by it, for it is an abomination to the LORD your God.
And you shall not bring an abomination into your house, lest you become devoted to destruction like it; you shall utterly detest and abhor it, for it is devoted to destruction.
Be scrupulously observant of the entire commandment that I am enjoining upon you this day, so that you may live, multiply, enter, and possess the land that the LORD swore to your fathers.

Remember the whole trajectory through which the LORD your God guided you during these forty years in the wilderness, in order to humble you and to assay you, discerning what lay within your heart—whether you would keep His commandments or not.

He humbled you and caused you to hunger, then nourished you with manna—something neither you nor your ancestors had ever known—in order to teach you that humankind does not subsist on bread alone, but that humankind lives by every utterance that proceeds from the mouth of the LORD.
Throughout these forty years, your garments did not wear out upon you, nor did your feet become swollen.
Know, then, in your heart, that as a father disciplines his son, so the LORD your God disciplines you.
Therefore keep the commandments of the LORD your God, walking in His ways and revering Him.
For the LORD your God is conducting you into a bountiful land—a land of watercourses, springs, and subterranean depths issuing forth in valleys and mountains—
a land of wheat and barley, of vines, fig trees, and pomegranates, of olive oil and honey,
a land where you will eat bread without privation, where you will want for nothing—a land whose stones are iron and whose mountains yield copper to be mined.
When you have eaten your fill and are satisfied, you shall bless the LORD your God for the good land that He has bestowed upon you.
Take heed, lest you forget the LORD your God, by failing to observe His commandments, ordinances, and statutes, which I am enjoining upon you this day.
Otherwise, after you have eaten and are sated, and have built stately houses and settled in them,
and when your cattle and flocks have proliferated, and your silver and gold have increased, and everything in your possession has multiplied,
then your heart will become exalted, and you will forget the LORD your God, who delivered you from the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.
He guided you through that vast and terrifying wilderness, with its venomous serpents and scorpions and its parched, waterless terrain, and brought forth water for you from the flinty rock.
He sustained you in the wilderness with manna unknown to your ancestors, in order to humble and test you, so that He might ultimately do you good.
You may say in your heart, “My own power and the vigor of my hand have secured this prosperity for me.”
But you must remember the LORD your God, for it is He who grants you the capacity to acquire wealth, thereby establishing His covenant, which He swore to your fathers, as is evident this day.
If you forget the LORD your God and pursue other gods, serving and prostrating yourself before them, I solemnly testify against you today that you will utterly perish.
Just as the nations that the LORD is destroying before you, so you too will perish, because you would not heed the voice of the LORD your God.
Hear, O Israel: today you are crossing the Jordan to enter and dispossess nations greater and mightier than you, with cities great and fortified up to the heavens,
a people great and tall, the descendants of the Anakim, whom you know, and of whom you have heard it said, ‘Who can withstand the sons of Anak?’

Know therefore today that the LORD your God is He who goes before you as a consuming fire; He will destroy them and subdue them before you, so that you may drive them out and annihilate them swiftly, just as the LORD has promised you.

When the LORD your God has thrust them out before you, do not say in your heart, ‘Because of my righteousness the LORD has brought me in to possess this land,’ for it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD is driving them out before you.

Not by your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart are you entering to possess their land, but because of the wickedness of these nations the LORD your God is driving them out before you, and in order to fulfill the word that the LORD swore to your fathers—to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
Know therefore that it is not by your righteousness that the LORD your God is giving you this good land to possess, for you are a stiff-necked people.

Remember; do not forget how you provoked the LORD your God to wrath in the wilderness. From the day you came out of the land of Egypt until you came to this place, you have been rebellious against the LORD.
Even at Horeb you provoked the LORD to wrath, and the LORD was incensed with you to destroy you.

When I ascended the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant that the LORD made with you, I remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights; I neither ate bread nor drank water.

And the LORD gave me the two tablets of stone written with the finger of God, and upon them were all the words that the LORD had spoken with you on the mountain out of the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly.
And at the end of forty days and forty nights the LORD gave me the two tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant.

And the LORD said to me, ‘Arise, go down quickly from here, for your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. They have turned aside quickly from the way that I commanded them; they have made for themselves a molten image.’
Furthermore the LORD spoke to me, saying, ‘I have seen this people, and behold, it is a stiff-necked people.
Leave Me alone, that I may destroy them and blot out their name from under heaven; and I will make of you a nation mightier and greater than they.’
So I turned and descended from the mountain, while the mountain was burning with fire, with the two tablets of the covenant in my two hands.
And I looked, and behold, you had sinned against the LORD your God; you had made for yourselves a molten calf; you had turned aside quickly from the way that the LORD had commanded you.
So I seized the two tablets and cast them from my two hands, and I shattered them before your eyes.

Then I prostrated myself before the LORD forty days and forty nights, as at the first; I neither ate bread nor drank water, because of all your sin that you had committed in doing evil in the sight of the LORD, to provoke Him.
For I was afraid of the anger and hot displeasure with which the LORD was angry against you to destroy you; but the LORD listened to me that time also.
And the LORD was exceedingly angry with Aaron to destroy him; so I prayed for Aaron also at that time.

Then I took your sin, the calf that you had made, and burned it with fire and crushed it, grinding it very fine until it was as fine as dust; and I cast its dust into the brook that descended from the mountain.
And at Taberah and at Massah and at Kibroth-hattaavah you provoked the LORD to wrath.

And when the LORD sent you from Kadesh-barnea, saying, ‘Go up and possess the land that I have given you,’ you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God; you neither believed Him nor listened to His voice.
You have been rebellious against the LORD from the day I knew you.
So I prostrated myself before the LORD forty days and forty nights, because the LORD had said He would destroy you.
And I prayed to the LORD and said, ‘O Lord GOD, do not destroy Your people and Your inheritance, whom You have redeemed through Your greatness, whom You brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
Remember Your servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; do not regard the stubbornness of this people, nor their wickedness, nor their sin.

Otherwise the people of the land from which You brought us may say, “Because the LORD was not able to bring them into the land that He had promised them, and because He hated them, He brought them out to slay them in the wilderness.”
Yet they are Your people and Your inheritance, whom You brought out by Your mighty power and outstretched arm.’
At that time the LORD said to me, “Carve for yourself two stone tablets like the former ones, and ascend to Me upon the mountain, and fashion for yourself an ark of wood.
And I will inscribe upon the tablets the words that were upon the first tablets, which you shattered, and you shall deposit them in the ark.”
So I fashioned an ark of acacia wood, and I carved two stone tablets like the first ones, and I ascended the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.

And He inscribed upon the tablets according to the first writing the Ten Commandments, which the LORD had spoken to you on the mountain out of the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly; and the LORD gave them to me.
Then I turned and descended from the mountain, and I placed the tablets in the ark that I had made, as the LORD had commanded me, and there they remain.
Now the Israelites journeyed from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah; there Aaron died and was buried, and Eleazar his son ministered as priest in his stead.
From there they traveled to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of watercourses.
At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to bear the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD to minister to Him and to bless in His name, unto this day.
Therefore Levi has no portion or inheritance among his brothers; the LORD is his inheritance, as the LORD your God spoke to him.
And I remained upon the mountain forty days and forty nights, as at the first time; and the LORD hearkened to me that time also, and the LORD would not destroy you.
Then the LORD said to me, “Arise, proceed on your journey before the people, that they may enter and possess the land that I swore to their fathers to give them.”

And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God require of you, but to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, and to love Him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
to keep the commandments of the LORD and His statutes, which I am enjoining upon you today, for your well-being?
Behold, to the LORD your God belong the heavens, even the highest heavens, and the earth with all that is therein.
Yet the LORD set His love upon your fathers to love them, and He chose their offspring after them—you—above all peoples, as it is this day.
Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be obstinate no longer.
For the LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, the mighty, and the awesome God, who shows no favoritism and accepts no bribe.
He executes justice for the orphan and the widow, and loves the sojourner, giving him food and clothing.
So you must love the sojourner, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
You shall fear the LORD your God; you shall serve Him, and to Him you shall cleave, and by His name you shall swear.
He is your praise and He is your God, who has wrought for you these great and awesome things that your eyes have beheld.
Your fathers descended into Egypt with seventy persons, and now the LORD your God has made you as numerous as the stars of heaven.
You shall love the LORD your God all the days, and keep His charge, His statutes, His judgments, and His commandments.
Know today that it is not your children—those who have neither known nor beheld the discipline of the LORD your God, His greatness, His mighty hand, and His outstretched arm—
together with His signs and His deeds, which He performed in the midst of Egypt against Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and against all his land;

and what He did to the Egyptian host, to its horses and chariots, when He made the waters of the Red Sea surge over their faces as they pursued you, and how the LORD annihilated them even to this day;
and what He did for you in the wilderness until you came to this place;

and what He did in the midst of all Israel to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, son of Reuben, when the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their households, their tents, and every living thing that stood upon their feet;
for your eyes have seen all the great work that the LORD has done.
You shall keep the whole commandment that I command you today, so that you may be strong and go in and possess the land that you are crossing over to possess,
and so that you may prolong your days upon the land that the LORD swore to your fathers to give to them and to their offspring, a land flowing with milk and honey.
For the land you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt, from which you came out, where you sowed your seed and watered it by foot, like a vegetable garden.
But the land you are crossing over to possess is a land of hills and valleys; it drinks water from the rain of heaven,
a land that the LORD your God tends; the eyes of the LORD your God are always upon it, from the beginning to the end of the year.
If you will diligently listen to my commandments that I command you today, to love the LORD your God and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul,
then I will give the rain of your land in its season, the early rain and the latter rain, and you shall gather in your grain, your new wine, and your oil.
I will give grass in your field for your cattle, and you shall eat and be satisfied.
Take heed for yourselves, lest your heart be deceived, and you turn aside and serve other gods and worship them.

Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and He will shut up the heavens so that there will be no rain, and the ground will not yield its produce, and you will perish quickly from off the good land that the LORD gives you.
You shall therefore lay up these words of mine in your heart and in your soul, and you shall bind them as a sign upon your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes.
You shall teach them to your children, speaking of them when you sit in your house, when you walk by the way, when you lie down, and when you rise up.
You shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
so that your days and the days of your children may be multiplied upon the land that the LORD swore to your fathers to give them, like the days of heaven upon the earth.
If you keep all these commandments that I command you, to do them, to love the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, and to cling to Him,
then the LORD will drive out all these nations before you, and you shall possess nations greater and mightier than yourselves.
Every place where the sole of your foot treads shall be yours; your border shall be from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the river Euphrates to the western sea.
No man shall be able to stand against you; the LORD your God will put the dread of you and the fear of you upon all the land that you tread, as He has spoken to you.
See, I am setting before you today blessing and curse:
the blessing, if you obey the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you today;
and the curse, if you do not obey the commandments of the LORD your God, but turn aside from the way that I command you today, to go after other gods that you have not known.
When the LORD your God brings you into the land that you are going in to possess, you shall put the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
Are they not beyond the Jordan, toward the setting of the sun, in the land of the Canaanites who dwell in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, beside the oaks of Moreh?
For you are crossing the Jordan to go in to possess the land that the LORD your God gives you, and you shall possess it and dwell in it.
You shall keep and do all the statutes and judgments that I am setting before you today.

These are the statutes and judgments that you shall be scrupulous to observe throughout all the days that you live upon the earth, in the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, has granted to you to possess.
You shall utterly destroy all the places where the nations whom you are dispossessing served their gods—upon the high mountains, upon the hills, and beneath every verdant tree.
You shall tear down their altars, smash their pillars, burn their Asherah poles with fire, hew down the carved images of their gods, and obliterate their name from that place.
You shall not do thus unto the LORD your God.
Rather, you shall seek the place that the LORD your God will choose from among all your tribes, to establish His name there as His dwelling; thither you shall go.

And there you shall bring your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution of your hand, your vows and your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock.
There, before the LORD your God, you and your households shall eat and rejoice in all your undertakings, inasmuch as the LORD your God has blessed you.
You shall not do according to all that we are doing here today, each doing whatever is right in his own eyes.
For you have not yet come to the rest and to the inheritance that the LORD your God is giving you.
But when you cross the Jordan and dwell in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to inherit, and when He gives you rest from all your enemies round about, so that you dwell in security,

then to the place that the LORD your God will choose, to make His name dwell there, you shall bring all that I command you: your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution of your hand, and all the choicest of your vow offerings that you vow to the LORD.
And you shall rejoice before the LORD your God—you, your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levite within your gates—because he has no portion or inheritance with you.
Take heed to yourself, lest you offer your burnt offerings in any place that you see;
but only in the place that the LORD will choose in one of your tribes shall you do all that I command you.

Nevertheless, you may slaughter and eat meat within any of your gates, according to all your soul's desire, as the LORD your God has blessed you; the clean and the unclean alike may eat it, as the gazelle and as the deer.
Only you shall not eat the blood; you shall pour it out on the earth like water.

You may not eat within your gates the tithe of your grain, or of your wine, or of your oil, or the firstborn of your herd or of your flock, or any of your vows that you vow, or your freewill offerings, or the contribution of your hand;

but you shall eat them before the LORD your God in the place that the LORD your God will choose—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, and the Levite within your gates—and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God in all your undertakings.
Take heed to yourself, lest you forsake the Levite all your days upon your land.
When the LORD your God enlarges your territory, as He has promised you, and you say, 'I will eat meat,' because your soul craves meat, you may eat meat, according to all your soul's desire.

If the place that the LORD your God chooses to put His name there is too far from you, then you may slaughter from your herd and from your flock, which the LORD has given you, as I have commanded you, and you may eat within your gates, according to all your soul's desire.
Just as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so you may eat of it; the unclean and the clean alike may eat of it.
Only be resolute not to eat the blood, for the blood is the life, and you shall not eat the life with the flesh.
You shall not eat it; you shall pour it out on the earth like water.
You shall not eat it, that it may go well with you and with your children after you, when you do what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
But the holy things that are yours, and your vows, you shall take and go to the place that the LORD will choose;

and you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood, upon the altar of the LORD your God; and the blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out upon the altar of the LORD your God, but the flesh you may eat.
Observe and hear all these words that I command you, that it may go well with you and with your children after you forever, when you do what is good and right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
When the LORD your God cuts off from before you the nations that you are entering to dispossess, and you dispossess them and dwell in their land,

take heed to yourself, lest you be ensnared after them, after they are destroyed from before you, and lest you inquire concerning their gods, saying, 'How did these nations serve their gods? I too will do likewise.'
You shall not do so to the LORD your God, for every abomination that the LORD hates they have done for their gods; for they even burn their sons and their daughters in the fire to their gods.
Everything that I command you, you shall be careful to do; you shall not add to it, nor shall you take away from it.
If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams should arise in your midst and give you a sign or a wonder,
and the sign or wonder of which he spoke to you comes to pass, while he says, “Let us follow other gods whom you have not known, and let us serve them,”

you shall not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams, for the the LORD your God is testing you, to ascertain whether you love the the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
You shall walk after the the LORD your God and fear Him and keep His commandments and obey His voice; you shall serve Him and cling to Him.

But that prophet or that dreamer of dreams shall be put to death, because he has spoken rebellion against the the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery, in order to turn you aside from the way in which the the LORD your God commanded you to walk. Thus shall you purge the evil from your midst.

If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or your daughter or the wife of your bosom or your friend who is as your own soul secretly entices you, saying, “Let us go and serve other gods,” which neither you nor your fathers have known—
gods of the peoples around you, whether near you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other—
you shall not yield to him or listen to him, nor shall your eye pity him, nor shall you spare him, nor shall you conceal him.
Rather, you shall surely kill him; your hand shall be first against him to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people.
You shall stone him to death with stones, because he sought to draw you away from the the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
Then all Israel shall hear and fear, and they shall never again perpetrate such wickedness among you.
If you hear in one of your cities, which the the LORD your God is giving you to dwell in,
that worthless men have gone out from among you and have drawn away the inhabitants of their city, saying, “Let us go and serve other gods,” which you have not known,
then you shall inquire and search diligently and ask carefully; and behold, if the matter proves true and certain, that such an abomination has been committed among you,
you shall surely strike the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, devoting it and all that is in it, including its livestock, to utter destruction by the sword.

You shall gather all its spoil into the midst of its open square and burn the city and all its spoil with fire as a whole burnt offering to the the LORD your God; it shall remain a perpetual ruin, never to be rebuilt.

None of the devoted things shall cling to your hand, so that the the LORD may turn from the fierceness of His anger and grant you mercy and have compassion on you and multiply you, as He swore to your fathers.
If you obey the voice of the the LORD your God, keeping all His commandments that I am commanding you today, and doing what is right in the eyes of the the LORD your God.
You are sons of the LORD your God. You shall not lacerate yourselves, nor shall you create a tonsured baldness between your eyes as a funerary lamentation.
For you are a holy people to the LORD your God, and the LORD has chosen you to be a people for His own possession out of all the peoples who are upon the face of the earth.
You shall not eat any detestable thing.
These are the animals that you may eat: the ox, the sheep, and the goat;
the deer, the gazelle, the roebuck, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope, and the mountain sheep.
And every beast that has a divided hoof and is cloven-footed and chews the cud among the beasts, that you may eat.

Nevertheless, of those that chew the cud or have the hoof divided, you shall not eat these: the camel, the hare, and the rock badger, because they chew the cud but do not divide the hoof; they are unclean to you.
And the pig, because it divides the hoof but does not chew the cud, is unclean to you. You shall not eat their flesh, and you shall not touch their carcasses.
These you may eat of all that are in the waters: all that have fins and scales you may eat.
But all that have not fins and scales you shall not eat; they are unclean to you.
Every clean bird you may eat.
But these are those that you shall not eat: the eagle, the vulture, and the black vulture;
the red kite, the falcon, and the buzzard of any kind;
the ostrich, the short-eared owl, the gull, and the hawk of any kind;
the little owl, the great owl, and the white owl;
the pelican, the Egyptian vulture, and the cormorant;
the stork, the heron of any kind, the hoopoe, and the bat.
And every winged swarming thing is unclean to you; they shall not be eaten.
Every clean flying creature you may eat.

You shall not eat any carcass. You may give it to the sojourner who is within your gates, that he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner. For you are a holy people to the LORD your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.
You shall surely tithe all the yield of your seed that goes out of the field year by year.

And you shall eat before the LORD your God, in the place that He will choose to make His name dwell there, the tithe of your grain, your wine, and your oil, and the firstborn of your herd and flock, that you may learn to fear the LORD your God all your days.

And if the way is too long for you, so that you are not able to carry it, because the place is too far from you which the LORD your God chooses, to set His name there, when the LORD your God blesses you,
then you shall turn it into money, and bind the money in your hand, and go to the place that the LORD your God chooses.

And you shall spend the money for whatever your soul desires—oxen, sheep, wine, strong drink, or whatever your soul asks—and you shall eat there before the LORD your God and rejoice, you and your household.
And you shall not forsake the Levite who is within your gates, for he has no portion or inheritance with you.
At the end of every three years you shall bring out all the tithe of your produce in that year and lay it up within your gates.

And the Levite, because he has no portion or inheritance with you, and the sojourner, the fatherless, and the widow who are within your gates, shall come and eat and be satisfied, that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands that you do.
At the expiration of every seventh year, you shall institute a remission.

And this is the statute governing the release: every holder of a debt shall remit the obligation his hand has extended to his neighbor; he shall not press his neighbor, even his brother, for repayment, because the LORD’s release has been proclaimed.
You may exact a debt from an alien, yet whatever claim you hold against your brother, your hand shall relinquish.
Nevertheless, there shall be no indigent among you, for the LORD will surely bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess.
If only you diligently heed the voice of the LORD your God, observing carefully to perform all this commandment that I am enjoining upon you this day.
For the LORD your God will bless you, as He promised you; and you shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow; and you shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you.

If there is among you an indigent person, one of your brothers, in any of your towns within the land that the LORD your God is giving you, you shall not harden your heart nor close your hand against your indigent brother.
Rather, you shall open your hand liberally to him and lend him whatever suffices for his need, namely, whatever he lacks.

Beware lest a base thought arise in your heart, and you say, “The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand,” and your eye look upon your indigent brother with grudging ill will, so that you give him nothing; then he will cry out to the LORD against you, and guilt shall be upon you.

You shall give to him ungrudgingly, and your heart shall not be grieved when you give to him, because on account of this very matter the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in every undertaking of your hand.
For the indigent will never cease from the midst of the land; therefore I command you, saying, “You shall open your hand wide to your brother, to your afflicted, and to your indigent in your land.”
If your brother, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, is sold to you, he shall serve you six years, and in the seventh year you shall send him forth free from you.
And when you send him forth free from you, you shall not send him away empty-handed.
You shall furnish him liberally from your flock, from your threshing floor, and from your winepress; as the LORD your God has blessed you, you shall give to him.
And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you; therefore I command you this matter today.
But if he says to you, “I will not go out from you,” because he loves you and your household, and because it is well with him with you,
then you shall take an awl and thrust it through his ear into the door, and he shall be your servant forever; and to your maidservant you shall do likewise.

It shall not be grievous in your eyes when you send him away free from you, for he has served you six years at half the cost of a hired worker; and the LORD your God will bless you in all that you do.

Every firstborn male that is born among your herd and among your flock you shall consecrate to the LORD your God; you shall do no work with the firstborn of your herd, nor shear the firstborn of your flock.
You shall eat it, you and your household, before the LORD your God year by year at the place that the LORD will choose.
But if there is in it a blemish—if it is lame or blind or has any serious defect—you shall not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
You shall eat it within your towns; the unclean and the clean alike may eat it, as the gazelle and as the deer.
Only you shall not eat its blood; you shall pour it out on the earth like water.
Observe the month of Abib and celebrate the Passover to the LORD your God, for in the month of Abib the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
You shall sacrifice the Passover to the LORD your God—sheep or cattle—at the place that the LORD will choose as a dwelling for His name.

You shall eat no leavened bread with it; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, the bread of affliction, because you departed from Egypt in haste, so that you may remember the day of your departure from Egypt throughout all the days of your life.
No leaven shall be seen with you in any of your territory for seven days, nor shall any of the flesh that you sacrifice on the evening of the first day remain until morning.
You may not sacrifice the Passover within any of your towns that the LORD your God is giving you.
Rather, you shall sacrifice the Passover at the place that the LORD your God will choose to establish His name, in the evening at sunset, at the appointed time of your departure from Egypt.
You shall cook it and eat it at the place that the LORD your God will choose, and in the morning you may turn and go to your tents.
For six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a solemn assembly to the LORD your God; you shall do no work.
You shall count seven weeks for yourself; begin counting the seven weeks from the moment the sickle is first put to the standing grain.
Then you shall celebrate the Feast of Weeks to the LORD your God with a freewill offering from your hand, in proportion to how the LORD your God has blessed you.

You shall rejoice before the LORD your God at the place that He will choose to establish His name—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, the Levite within your towns, and the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow who are among you.
You shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and you shall be careful to observe these statutes.
You shall celebrate the Feast of Booths for seven days when you gather in your threshing floor and your winepress.
You shall rejoice in your feast—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, the Levite, and the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow within your towns.

For seven days you shall celebrate to the LORD your God at the place that He will choose, because the LORD your God will bless you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, and you shall be wholly joyful.

Three times a year all your males shall appear before the LORD your God at the place that He will choose—at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, at the Feast of Weeks, and at the Feast of Booths—and none shall appear before the LORD empty-handed.
Each shall give as he is able, according to the blessing that the LORD your God has given you.
You shall appoint judges and officers for your tribes in all your towns that the LORD your God is giving you, and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.
You shall not pervert justice; you shall not show partiality; and you shall not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and subverts the words of the righteous.
Justice, and only justice, you shall pursue, so that you may live and possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
You shall not plant for yourself any tree as an Asherah beside the altar of the LORD your God that you are making.
You shall not set up for yourself a sacred pillar, which the LORD your God hates.
You shall not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or a sheep that bears a blemish or any other defect, for such an offering is an abomination to the LORD your God.
If, within one of the towns that the LORD your God gives you, there is found a man or a woman who does what is evil in the sight of the LORD your God by transgressing His covenant,
and if that person has gone and served other gods and worshiped them, or the sun, or the moon, or any of the host of heaven—which I have not commanded—

and if the matter is reported to you and you hear of it, then you must investigate it diligently; and if the report proves true and well established—that this abomination has indeed been perpetrated in Israel—
then you shall bring out to your gates that man or that woman who has committed this wicked deed, and you shall stone them with stones so that they die.
On the testimony of two or three witnesses the condemned person shall be put to death, but no one shall be put to death on the testimony of a single witness.
The hands of the witnesses shall be the first to put the offender to death, and afterward the hands of all the people; thus you shall purge the evil from your midst.

If a case is too difficult for you to adjudicate—matters of bloodshed, of legal claims, or of bodily injury—within your towns, then you shall arise and go up to the place that the LORD your God will choose.
You shall come to the Levitical priests and to the judge who is in office in those days, inquire of them, and they shall declare to you the verdict of the case.
You shall act according to the decision that they render for you from that place which the LORD will choose, and you must be careful to do all that they instruct you.

According to the law that they teach you and according to the judgment that they pronounce for you, you shall act; you shall not deviate to the right or to the left from the decision that they declare to you.
And the person who acts presumptuously, refusing to heed the priest who stands there to minister before the LORD your God or the judge—that person shall die, and you shall purge the evil from Israel.
Then all the people shall hear and fear, and they shall not act presumptuously again.
When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, take possession of it, and settle in it, and you say, “I will set a king over me, like all the nations around me,”
you must surely set over you a king whom the LORD your God chooses. From among your brothers you shall set a king over you; you may not appoint over you a foreigner who is not your brother.
He must not acquire many horses for himself, nor lead the people back to Egypt in order to acquire more horses, for the LORD has declared to you, “You shall never return that way again.”
He must not take many wives, lest his heart be led astray, nor may he amass for himself an excessive store of silver and gold.
When he is seated upon the throne of his kingdom, he shall write for himself a transcript of this law in a scroll, in the presence of the Levitical priests.

It shall remain with him, and he shall read from it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God, to observe all the words of this law and these statutes, and to carry them out,

so that his heart does not become haughty toward his brothers and he does not turn aside from the commandment to the right or to the left, in order that he and his sons may prolong their days over his kingdom in the midst of Israel.

The Levites—the entire tribe of Levi—shall possess no allotment or inheritance among the Israelites; rather, they shall subsist upon the offerings made by fire to the LORD, for that constitutes their inheritance.
They shall have no inheritance among their kinsmen, since the LORD Himself is their inheritance, exactly as He has promised them.
This, moreover, shall be the priests' due from the people, from those who present a sacrifice, whether ox or sheep: they shall give to the priest the shoulder, the jowls, and the stomach.
You shall give him the firstfruits of your grain, your new wine, and your oil, together with the first shearing of your flock,
for the LORD your God has chosen him and his descendants from all your tribes to stand and minister in the name of the LORD for all time.
If a Levite comes from one of your towns anywhere in Israel where he has been residing, and comes, whenever he desires, to the place the LORD will choose,
he may minister in the name of the LORD his God, like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the LORD.
He shall receive an equal portion of food, apart from what he obtains by selling his ancestral estate.
When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, you must not learn to practice the abominations of those nations.
No one among you shall be found who passes his son or daughter through the fire, or who practices divination, soothsaying, augury, or sorcery,
or who casts spells, consults a medium or spiritist, or seeks guidance from the dead.
For everyone who does these things is an abomination to the LORD, and on account of these abominations the LORD your God will drive out those nations before you.
You must be blameless before the LORD your God.
For those nations that you will dispossess listen to soothsayers and diviners, but the LORD your God has not permitted you to do so.
The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among you, from your brothers; you shall listen to him.

This accords with everything you requested of the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, when you said, "Let us not hear the voice of the LORD our God, nor see this great fire any longer, lest we die."
And the LORD said to me, "They have spoken well.
I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their brothers, and I will put My words in his mouth, and he will speak to them everything that I command him.
And if anyone does not listen to My words that he speaks in My name, I will require it of him.
But if a prophet presumes to speak in My name a word that I have not commanded him to speak, or speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die."
You may say in your heart, "How shall we know that the word has not been spoken by the LORD?"
If the prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the word does not come to pass, then the LORD has not spoken that word; the prophet has spoken presumptuously. You need not fear him.
When the LORD your God cuts off the nations whose land the LORD your God gives you, and you dispossess them and dwell in their cities and houses,
set apart for yourself three cities in the midst of your land that the LORD your God gives you to possess.
Prepare the way for yourself, and divide into three parts the territory of your land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, so that any manslayer may flee there.
This is the matter concerning the manslayer who flees there and lives: whoever strikes his neighbor without prior knowledge, not having hated him before.

For instance, if a man goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut wood, and as his hand swings the axe to fell a tree, the iron head slips from the handle and strikes his neighbor so that he dies, he may flee to one of these cities and live.

Otherwise, the avenger of blood might pursue the manslayer while his heart is hot, overtake him because the distance is great, and strike him dead, though he does not deserve death, since he did not hate his neighbor previously.
Therefore I command you, saying, “Set apart for yourself three cities.”
And if the LORD your God enlarges your border, as He swore to your fathers, and gives you all the land that He promised to give your fathers,

provided that you keep all this commandment that I command you today—to love the LORD your God and to walk in His ways all your days—then you shall add three more cities for yourself besides these three,
so that innocent blood will not be shed in the midst of your land that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance, and bloodguilt will not be upon you.
But if a man hates his neighbor and lies in wait for him, rises against him, and strikes him so that he dies, and he flees to one of these cities,
then the elders of his city shall send and take him from there and deliver him into the hand of the avenger of blood, that he may die.
Your eye shall not pity him, but you shall purge the innocent blood from Israel, that it may go well with you.
You shall not move your neighbor's landmark, which the ancestors have set in your inheritance that you will inherit in the land that the LORD your God gives you to possess.
A single witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity or sin in any offense he may commit; a matter shall be established only by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
If a malicious witness rises up against a man to accuse him of wrongdoing,
then both men who have the dispute shall stand before the LORD, before the priests and judges who are in those days.
The judges shall inquire diligently, and if the witness proves to be a false witness who has testified falsely against his brother,
then you shall do to him as he had intended to do to his brother, and you shall purge the evil from your midst.
The rest shall hear and fear, and they shall never again do such an evil thing among you.
Your eye shall not pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

When you march out to war against your enemies and perceive horses and chariots and a people more numerous than you, do not dread them, for the LORD your God, Who brought you up from the land of Egypt, is with you.
And when you draw near to battle, the priest shall approach and speak to the people,
saying, “Hear, O Israel: Today you are drawing near to battle against your enemies. Let not your hearts grow faint; do not be afraid, do not panic, and do not be terrified before them.
For the LORD your God goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.”

Then the officers shall speak to the people, saying, “Who is the man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in battle and another man dedicate it.
And who is the man who has planted a vineyard and has not yet partaken of its produce? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in battle and another man partake of its produce.
And who is the man who has betrothed a woman and has not taken her in marriage? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in battle and another man marry her.
And who is the man who is fearful and fainthearted? Let him go and return to his house, lest his comrades’ courage fail as his own.”
And when the officers have finished speaking to the people, they shall appoint commanders of the armies to lead the people.
When you approach a city to fight against it, you shall proclaim peace to it.
And if it answers you with peace and opens to you, then all the people found in it shall become forced labor for you and shall serve you.
But if it does not make peace with you, but makes war against you, then you shall besiege it.
And when the LORD your God delivers it into your hand, you shall strike every male in it with the edge of the sword.

Only the women, the little ones, the livestock, and all that is in the city—all its spoil—you shall take as plunder for yourself, and you shall eat the spoil of your enemies, which the LORD your God has given you.
Thus you shall do to all the cities that are very far from you, which are not of the cities of these nations.
But of the cities of these peoples that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance, you shall not leave alive anything that breathes.
Rather, you shall utterly destroy them—the Hittite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite—just as the LORD your God has commanded you,
so that they may not teach you to do according to all their abominations, which they have done for their gods, and so you sin against the LORD your God.

When you besiege a city for a long time, fighting against it to capture it, you shall not destroy its trees by laying an axe to them, for you may eat from them, but you shall not cut them down. For the tree of the field is not a man, that it should be drawn into your siege.
Only a tree that you know is not a tree for food you may destroy and cut down, and you shall build siege works against the city that makes war with you, until it falls.
Should a slain man be discovered fallen in the open country of the land that the LORD your God is granting you to possess, and his killer remain unknown,
then your elders and your judges shall go out and measure the distances from the corpse to the cities encircling it.
The elders of the city nearest the slain man shall take a heifer from the herd that has neither been worked nor drawn under a yoke.
The elders of that city shall bring the heifer down to a rugged valley—one that has neither been plowed nor sown—and there they shall break the heifer’s neck.

Then the priests, the sons of Levi, shall approach, for the LORD your God has chosen them to minister to Him and to bless in the name of the LORD; and by their pronouncement every dispute and every act of violence shall be adjudicated.
All the elders of the city nearest the slain man shall wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley.
and they shall declare, “Our hands did not shed this blood, nor did our eyes witness it.
Atone, O the LORD, for Your people Israel, whom You have redeemed, and do not charge innocent blood to Your people Israel.” Then the bloodguilt shall be atoned for them.
Thus you shall purge the shedding of innocent blood from your midst, when you do what is right in the sight of the LORD.
When you go out to war against your enemies, and the LORD your God delivers them into your hand and you take captives,
and you see among the captives a woman of beautiful form, and you desire her and would take her as your wife,
then you shall bring her into your house; she shall shave her head and trim her nails,

and she shall remove the garments of her captivity, remain in your house, and mourn her father and mother for a full month; thereafter you may go in to her and become her husband, and she shall be your wife.
But if you no longer delight in her, you shall let her go wherever she wishes; you shall not sell her for silver, nor treat her as merchandise, because you have humbled her.
If a man has two wives, one beloved and the other unloved, and both bear him sons, and the firstborn son is the child of the unloved wife,
then on the day he apportions his inheritance among his sons he may not grant the son of the beloved wife the rights of the firstborn in preference to the firstborn son of the unloved wife.

Rather, he shall acknowledge the firstborn, the son of the unloved wife, by giving him a double portion of all that he possesses, for he is the firstfruits of his vigor, and the right of the firstborn is his.
If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who will not obey his father’s voice or his mother’s voice, and though they discipline him he still does not listen,
then his father and mother shall seize him and bring him out to the elders of his city and to the gate of his place.
They shall say to the elders of his city, “This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious; he will not obey our voice; he is a glutton and a drunkard.”
Then all the men of his city shall stone him to death, so that you purge the evil from your midst, and all Israel shall hear and fear.
If a man has committed a capital offense and is to be put to death, and you hang him on a tree,

his corpse shall not remain on the tree overnight; you shall surely bury him that same day, for a hanged man is accursed of God, so that you do not defile your land, which the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
Should you discern your brother's ox or sheep wandering astray, you must not avert your gaze from them; rather, you shall diligently restore them to your brother.

If your brother does not dwell nearby, or you are unacquainted with him, then you shall bring the beast into your own dwelling, where it shall remain in your custody until your brother inquires after it; thereupon, you shall restore it to him.
You shall extend the same care to his donkey, his garment, or any lost possession of your brother that you happen to find; you may not turn away from it.
Should you observe your brother's donkey or ox collapsed upon the roadway, you must not disregard them; you shall assuredly assist him in raising them.
No woman shall don the apparel of a man, nor shall any man array himself in woman's attire, for all who perpetrate such acts constitute an abomination to the LORD your God.

Should you chance upon a bird's nest containing fledglings or eggs, whether in a tree or upon the ground, while the mother broods over the young or the eggs, you shall not seize the mother together with her offspring.
You shall assuredly release the mother, yet you may take the young for your own use, so that prosperity may attend you and your days may be prolonged.
When you erect a new dwelling, you shall construct a parapet upon its roof, lest you incur bloodguilt within your household should someone fall from it.
You shall not sow your vineyard with heterogeneous seed, lest the entire harvest be forfeited—both the seed you have sown and the produce of the vineyard.
You shall not yoke an ox and a donkey together in plowing.
You shall not wear a garment woven of wool and linen combined.
You shall fashion tassels upon the four corners of the cloak with which you cover yourself.
Should a man take a wife, consummate the marriage, and thereafter come to despise her,
and should he fabricate allegations against her, impugning her reputation by declaring, “I espoused this woman, and upon approaching her I discovered that she was not a virgin,”
then the young woman's father and mother shall take the tokens of her virginity and exhibit them before the elders of the city at the gate.
The father of the young woman shall then address the elders, saying, “I gave my daughter to this man in marriage, and he has grown to hate her;

and behold, he has imputed to her baseless charges, asserting, ‘I did not find your daughter a virgin.’ Yet these are the tokens of my daughter's virginity.” Then they shall spread the cloth before the elders of the city.
Then the elders of that city shall seize the man and chastise him,

and they shall impose upon him a fine of one hundred shekels of silver, which they shall give to the father of the young woman, because he has defamed a virgin of Israel. She shall remain his wife; he shall not be at liberty to divorce her for the remainder of his days.
But if the accusation proves true, and the tokens of virginity are not found in the young woman,

then they shall bring the young woman to the entrance of her father's house, and the men of her city shall stone her to death, because she has committed a scandalous act in Israel by playing the harlot in her father's house. Thus shall you purge the evil from your midst.
If a man is discovered lying with another man's wife, both of them—the man who lay with the woman and the woman herself—shall die; thus shall you purge the evil from Israel.
If a betrothed virgin is encountered by a man in the city, and he lies with her,

then you shall bring them both to the gate of that city and stone them to death—the young woman because she did not cry out for help though she was in the city, and the man because he violated his neighbor's wife. Thus shall you purge the evil from your midst.
But if a man encounters a betrothed young woman in the open country, seizes her, and lies with her, then only the man who lay with her shall die.
You shall do nothing to the young woman, for she has committed no capital sin; this matter is analogous to a man rising against his neighbor and murdering him.
For he found her in the open country, and though the betrothed young woman cried for help, no one was present to rescue her.
If a man finds an unbetrothed virgin, seizes her, and lies with her, and the matter comes to light,

then the man who lay with her shall give the father of the young woman fifty shekels of silver, and she shall become his wife, because he has humbled her; he shall not be permitted to divorce her throughout all his days.
No man shall take his father's wife, lest he expose his father's nakedness.
No man whose testicles have been crushed or whose genital member has been severed may be admitted to the assembly of the the LORD.
No child of an illicit union shall enter the assembly of the the LORD; not even in the tenth generation shall any descendant of such a one be admitted to the assembly of the the LORD.
No Ammonite or Moabite shall enter the assembly of the the LORD; even to the tenth generation, none of them shall ever be admitted to the assembly of the the LORD.
This is because they did not meet you with bread and water on the road when you departed from Egypt, and because they hired against you Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Aram-naharaim to curse you.
Yet the the LORD your God refused to heed Balaam; instead, the the LORD your God transformed the curse into a blessing for you, because the the LORD your God loved you.
You shall never seek their peace or prosperity for all your days, forever.
You must not despise an Edomite, for he is your brother; nor shall you despise an Egyptian, because you were an alien in his land.
The third generation of children born to them may enter the assembly of the the LORD.
When you march out with your host against your enemies, you must keep yourself from every evil.
If there is among you a man who is not clean because of a nocturnal emission, he shall go outside the camp and shall not enter the midst of the camp.
Toward evening he shall bathe in water, and at sunset he may come into the midst of the camp.
You shall have a place outside the camp, and you shall go out there.
You shall have a trowel among your equipment, and when you sit down outside, you shall dig with it and then cover your excrement.

For the the LORD your God walks in the midst of your camp, to deliver you and to give your enemies before you, so that your camp may be holy; and He shall see no indecent thing in you and turn away from following you.
You shall not hand over to his master a slave who has escaped from his master to you.
He shall dwell with you, in your midst, in the place that he chooses within one of your gates, wherever it seems best to him; you shall not oppress him.
There shall be no cult prostitute among the daughters of Israel, and no cult prostitute among the sons of Israel.
You shall not bring the hire of a harlot or the wages of a dog into the house of the the LORD your God for any vow, for both are an abomination to the the LORD your God.
You shall not charge interest to your brother—interest on money, interest on food, interest on any thing that is lent.

You may charge interest to a foreigner, but to your brother you shall not charge interest, so that the the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hand in the land that you are entering to possess.
When you make a vow to the the LORD your God, you shall not delay to pay it, for the the LORD your God will surely require it of you, and it would be sin in you.
But if you refrain from vowing, it is no sin in you.
You shall be careful to perform what goes out of your lips, just as you have freely vowed to the the LORD your God, promising with your mouth.
When you enter your neighbor's vineyard, you may eat grapes to your satisfaction, as many as you desire, but you shall not put any in your container.
When you enter your neighbor's standing grain, you may pluck the heads with your hand, but you shall not put a sickle to your neighbor's standing grain.

When a man marries a woman and she becomes his wife, yet she fails to find favor in his eyes because he has discovered in her some shameful matter, he may write her a certificate of divorce, place it in her hand, and dismiss her from his house.
After she has left his house, she may go and become another man's wife.

If the subsequent husband likewise comes to despise her and writes her a bill of divorce, placing it in her hand and sending her away from his house—or if that latter husband dies, the one who took her as wife—

then her first husband, who dismissed her, may not take her back as his wife after she has been defiled, for such a reunion is an abomination before the LORD; nor shall you bring sin upon the land that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance.

When a man marries a new wife, he shall not march out with the army, nor shall any civic burden be imposed upon him; for one year he shall be exempt for his household, and he shall bring joy to the wife he has taken.
No one shall take a pair of millstones, nor even the upper stone, as security, for that would be to take a life in pledge.
If a man is found to have kidnapped one of his brothers among the Israelites, whether to enslave him or to sell him, that thief shall die, and you shall purge the evil from your midst.
In a case of leprous disease, be exceedingly careful to observe and do all that the Levitical priests instruct you, as I have commanded them; so you shall be careful to do.
Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the way, when you came out of Egypt.
When you make a loan of any kind to your neighbor, you shall not enter his house to take his pledge.
You shall stand outside, and the man to whom you lend shall bring the pledge out to you.
If he is a poor man, you shall not go to sleep while his pledge remains in your possession.
You shall surely return his pledge to him by sunset, so that he may sleep in his garment and bless you; and it shall be righteousness for you before the LORD your God.
You shall not oppress a hired servant who is poor and needy, whether he is one of your brothers or a sojourner residing in your land within your towns.
You shall give him his wages on the day they are due, before sunset, because he is poor and sets his heart upon them, lest he cry out against you to the LORD, and it be sin to you.
Fathers shall not be put to death for their sons, nor sons for their fathers; each man shall be put to death for his own sin.
You shall not pervert justice for the sojourner or the orphan, nor take a widow's garment as a pledge.
You shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you from there; therefore I command you to do this thing.

When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in the field, you shall not return to take it; it shall belong to the sojourner, the orphan, and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you beat your olive tree, you shall not go over the boughs again; it shall be for the sojourner, the orphan, and the widow.
When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you shall not glean after you; it shall be for the sojourner, the orphan, and the widow.
You shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt; therefore I command you to do this thing.
If a dispute arises between men and they come before the court for judgment, the judges shall justify the righteous and condemn the wicked.
If the wicked man deserves to be beaten, the judge shall cause him to lie down and be beaten in his presence, with the number of stripes proportioned to his wickedness.
He may give him forty stripes, but no more, lest, in your sight, your brother be degraded should he receive an excessive beating beyond these.
You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads out the grain.

If brothers dwell together and one of them dies without a son, the wife of the deceased shall not be given in marriage to a stranger outside; her husband's brother shall go in to her, take her to himself as wife, and perform the duty of a brother-in-law to her.
The first son she bears shall rise up in the name of his dead brother, so that his name may not be blotted out from Israel.

But if the man does not desire to take his brother's widow, then his brother's widow shall go up to the gate, to the elders, and say, “My husband's brother refuses to raise up a name for his brother in Israel; he will not perform the duty of a brother-in-law to me.”
Then the elders of his city shall call him and speak to him, and he shall stand and say, “I do not desire to take her.”

Then his brother's widow shall come near to him in the sight of the elders, remove his sandal from his foot, spit in his face, and answer and say, “Thus shall it be done to the man who does not build up his brother's house.”
And his name shall be called in Israel, “The house of the man whose sandal was removed.”

When men strive together, a man and his brother, and the wife of one draws near to rescue her husband from the hand of the one who strikes him, and she puts out her hand and seizes him by his genitals,
then you shall cut off her hand; your eye shall not pity.
You shall not have in your bag two different stones, a large and a small.
You shall not have in your house two different ephahs, a large and a small.
A perfect and just stone you shall have; a perfect and just ephah you shall have, that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God gives you.
For all who do such things, all who act unjustly, are an abomination to the LORD your God.
Remember what Amalek did to you on the way when you came out of Egypt,
how he met you on the way and attacked you when you were faint and weary, cutting off all the stragglers behind you, and he did not fear God.

When the LORD your God gives you rest from all your enemies around you in the land that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance to possess, you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven; you shall not forget.
When you have entered the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and you have taken possession of it and settled there,

you shall take some of the firstfruits of all the produce of the soil that you bring from your land, which the LORD your God is giving you, and place it in a basket, and journey to the place that the LORD your God will choose to make His Name dwell there.
You shall approach the priest then in office and say to him, “I have declared today to the LORD your God that I have come into the land that the LORD swore to our fathers to give us.”
The priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it before the altar of the LORD your God.

You shall answer and say before the LORD your God, “My father was a wandering Aramean, and he descended into Egypt and resided there as an alien, few in number, and there he became a nation, great, mighty, and populous.
The Egyptians dealt harshly with us, afflicted us, and imposed upon us brutal servitude.
Then we cried out to the LORD, the God of our fathers, and the LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, our toil, and our oppression.
And the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, and with signs and wonders.
And He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And now, behold, I have brought the firstfruits of the soil that You, O the LORD, have given me, and I have set it before the LORD your God and worshiped before the LORD your God.”
