And you shall rejoice in all the good that the LORD your God has given to you and to your house, you and the Levite and the foreigner who is among you.

When you have finished tithing all the tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of tithing, and have given it to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, so that they may eat within your gates and be filled,

you shall say before the LORD your God, “I have removed the sacred portion from my house, and moreover I have given it to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, in accordance with every commandment that You have given me. I have not transgressed any of Your commandments, nor have I forgotten them.

I have not eaten of it while in mourning, nor have I removed any of it while unclean, nor have I given any of it for the dead. I have obeyed the voice of the LORD my God. I have done according to all that You have commanded me.
Look down from Your holy habitation, from heaven, and bless Your people Israel and the land that You have given us, as You swore to our fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.”
The LORD your God enjoins upon you this day to observe these statutes and judgments; therefore you shall keep and do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
You have declared today that the LORD is your God, and that you will walk in His ways and keep His statutes and His commandments and His judgments, and obey His voice.
And the LORD has declared today that you are His treasured people, as He promised you, and that you are to keep all His commandments,
and that He will exalt you above all nations that He has made, to the praise, renown, and glory of His people, and that you shall be a holy people to the LORD your God, as He has spoken.
Moses, together with the elders of Israel, commanded the people, saying, "Observe the entire commandment that I am enjoining upon you this day."
And it shall be, on the day you cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, that you shall set up great stones and plaster them with plaster.

And you shall inscribe upon them all the words of this law when you cross over, so that you may enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the LORD, the God of your fathers, spoke to you.
And when you have crossed the Jordan, you shall set up these stones on Mount Ebal, as I command you this day, and you shall plaster them with plaster.
And there you shall build an altar to the LORD your God, an altar of stones; you shall not lift iron upon them.
Of whole stones you shall build the altar of the LORD your God, and you shall offer burnt offerings on it to the LORD your God.
And you shall sacrifice peace offerings, and you shall eat, and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God.
And you shall inscribe upon the stones all the words of this law with conspicuous clarity."
Then Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel, saying, "Be silent and hear, O Israel: this day you have become a people to the LORD your God.
You shall therefore obey the voice of the LORD your God, and perform His commandments and His statutes, which I am commanding you this day."
And Moses commanded the people that day, saying,
"When you cross the Jordan, these shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
And these shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali."
Then the Levites shall speak with a loud voice to every man of Israel:
"Cursed is the man who fashions a carved image or a molten image, an abomination to the LORD, the work of a craftsman's hands, and sets it up in secret"; and all the people shall respond, Amen.
"Cursed is he who treats with contempt his father or his mother"; and all the people shall respond, Amen.
"Cursed is he who displaces his neighbor's boundary marker"; and all the people shall respond, Amen.
"Cursed is he who misguides the blind along the road"; and all the people shall respond, Amen.
"Cursed is he who distorts justice for the sojourner, the fatherless, and the widow"; and all the people shall respond, Amen.
"Cursed is he who has sexual relations with his father's wife, for he has violated his father's marriage bed"; and all the people shall respond, Amen.
"Cursed is he who has sexual relations with any beast"; and all the people shall respond, Amen.
"Cursed is he who has sexual relations with his sister, whether the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother"; and all the people shall respond, Amen.
"Cursed is he who has sexual relations with his mother-in-law"; and all the people shall respond, Amen.
"Cursed is he who assaults his neighbor covertly"; and all the people shall respond, Amen.
"Cursed is he who accepts a bribe to slay an innocent person"; and all the people shall respond, Amen.
"Cursed is everyone who does not uphold the words of this law by doing them"; and all the people shall respond, Amen.

If you diligently heed the voice of the LORD your God, scrupulously keeping and performing all His commandments that I enjoin upon you this day, then the LORD your God will exalt you above all the nations of the earth.
All these blessings shall come upon you and overtake you, provided that you heed the voice of the LORD your God.
You shall be blessed in the city, and blessed shall you be in the field.
Blessed shall be the fruit of your womb, the produce of your ground, and the offspring of your beasts, the increase of your herds and the young of your flocks.
Blessed shall be your basket and your kneading bowl.
You shall be blessed in your coming in, and blessed shall you be in your going out.
The LORD will cause your enemies who rise against you to be struck down before you; they shall come out against you by one road and flee before you by seven roads.
The LORD will command the blessing upon your storehouses and upon all the labor of your hands, and He will bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
The LORD will establish you as a people holy to Himself, as He swore to you, if you keep the commandments of the LORD your God and walk in His ways.
Then all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the LORD is proclaimed over you, and they shall stand in awe of you.

Moreover, the LORD will make you abound in prosperity—in the fruit of your womb, in the offspring of your beasts, and in the produce of your ground—in the land that the LORD swore to your fathers to give you.
The LORD will open to you His good treasury, the heavens, to give rain upon your land in its season and to bless all the work of your hands; you shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow.

The LORD will make you the head and not the tail; you shall be only above and never below, if you obey the commandments of the LORD your God, which I command you this day, being careful to observe them.
And do not turn aside, to the right or to the left, from all the words that I command you this day, to go after other gods and serve them.

But if you do not heed the voice of the LORD your God, to keep and perform all His commandments and statutes that I enjoin upon you this day, then all these curses shall come upon you and overtake you.
You shall be cursed in the city, and cursed shall you be in the field.
Cursed shall be your basket and your kneading bowl.
Cursed shall be the fruit of your womb, the produce of your ground, the increase of your herds and the young of your flocks.
You shall be cursed in your coming in, and cursed shall you be in your going out.

The LORD will send upon you the curse, confusion, and rebuke in every undertaking of your hand, until you are destroyed and perish swiftly, because of the evil of your deeds, whereby you have forsaken Me.
The LORD will make pestilence cling to you until He has consumed you from the land that you are entering to possess.
The LORD will smite you with consumption, fever, inflammation, burning heat, sword, blight, and mildew; they shall pursue you until you perish.
Your heavens shall be brass, and the earth beneath you iron.
The LORD will make the rain of your land powder and dust; from heaven it shall descend upon you until you are destroyed.

The LORD will give you up to be defeated before your enemies; you shall go out against them by one road and flee before them by seven roads, and you shall become a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
Your carcass shall be food for every bird of the heavens and for the beasts of the earth, with none to frighten them away.
The LORD will smite you with the boils of Egypt, with tumors, scabs, and itch, from which you cannot be healed.
The LORD will smite you with madness, blindness, and dismay of heart.
You shall grope at noonday as the blind grope in darkness, and you shall not prosper in your ways; you shall be only oppressed and robbed continually, and there shall be no one to save you.
You shall betroth a wife, but another man shall violate her; you shall build a house, but you shall not dwell in it; you shall plant a vineyard, but you shall not enjoy its fruit.

Your ox shall be slaughtered before your eyes, but you shall not eat of it; your donkey shall be seized from before you and shall not be restored to you; your sheep shall be given to your enemies, and there shall be no one to save you.
Your sons and daughters shall be given to another people, while your eyes look on and fail with longing for them all day long, but your hand shall be powerless.
A people whom you have not known shall eat the fruit of your ground and all your labor, and you shall be only oppressed and crushed continually.
You shall be driven mad by the sight that your eyes shall see.
The LORD will smite you with an incurable boil upon your knees and upon your legs, from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head.
The LORD will drive you and the king whom you set over you to a nation that neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you shall serve other gods, of wood and stone.
You shall become a horror, a proverb, and a byword among all the peoples to whom the LORD shall lead you.
You shall carry much seed out into the field, but you shall gather in little, for the locust shall consume it.
You shall plant vineyards and dress them, but you shall neither drink the wine nor gather the grapes, for the worm shall eat them.
You shall have olive trees throughout all your territory, but you shall not anoint yourself with the oil, for your olives shall drop off.
You shall beget sons and daughters, but they shall not be yours, for they shall go into captivity.
The cricket shall possess all your trees and the fruit of your ground.
The sojourner who is among you shall rise above you higher and higher, while you sink lower and lower.
He shall lend to you, but you shall not lend to him; he shall be the head, and you shall be the tail.

All these curses shall come upon you and pursue you and overtake you, until you are destroyed, because you did not heed the voice of the LORD your God, to keep His commandments and statutes that He commanded you.
They shall be a sign and a wonder upon you and upon your descendants forever.
Because you did not serve the LORD your God with joyfulness and gladness of heart, when all things abounded,

therefore you shall serve your enemies whom the LORD shall send against you, in hunger and thirst, in nakedness and in want of all things; and He shall put an iron yoke upon your neck until He has destroyed you.
The LORD will bring against you a nation from afar, from the end of the earth, swooping down like an eagle, a nation whose language you do not understand.
A nation of fierce countenance that does not regard the person of the old or show favor to the young.

It shall eat the fruit of your beasts and the produce of your ground until you are destroyed, leaving you neither grain, nor wine, nor oil, nor the increase of your herds nor the young of your flocks, until it has caused you to perish.

It shall besiege you in all your gates, throughout all your land, until your high and fortified walls, in which you trust, come down; it shall besiege you in all your gates throughout all the land that the LORD your God has given you.
You shall eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of your sons and daughters, whom the LORD your God has given you, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy shall distress you.
The man who is tender and very delicate among you shall have an evil eye toward his brother, toward the wife of his bosom, and toward the remnant of his children whom he has spared.

So that he will not give to any of them any of the flesh of his children that he eats, because nothing else is left to him, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy shall distress you in all your gates.

The woman who is tender and delicate, who would not venture to set the sole of her foot upon the ground out of delicacy and tenderness, shall have an evil eye toward the husband of her bosom, toward her son, and toward her daughter.

And toward her afterbirth that comes out from between her feet, and toward her children whom she bears, because she shall eat them secretly for want of all things, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy shall distress you in your gates.
If you do not carefully observe all the words of this law that are written in this book, to fear this glorious and awesome Name, the LORD your God,
then the LORD will make your plagues and the plagues of your descendants extraordinary—great and enduring plagues, and severe and enduring sicknesses.
He will bring back upon you all the diseases of Egypt, of which you were afraid, and they shall cling to you.
The LORD will also bring upon you every sickness and every plague that is not written in the book of this law, until you are destroyed.
Whereas you were as numerous as the stars of heaven, you shall be left few in number, because you did not obey the voice of the LORD your God.

And just as the LORD rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so the LORD will rejoice over you to destroy you and to bring you to nothing; and you shall be plucked up from the land that you are entering to possess.
The LORD will scatter you among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other, and there you shall serve other gods, of wood and stone, which neither you nor your fathers have known.
Among those nations you shall find no ease, and there shall be no rest for the sole of your foot; but the LORD will give you there a trembling heart, failing eyes, and a despairing soul.
Your life shall hang in doubt before you; you shall fear night and day and shall have no assurance of your life.

In the morning you shall say, “Would that it were evening!” and in the evening, “Would that it were morning!”—because of the dread of your heart that you shall dread, and because of the sight of your eyes that you shall see.

The LORD will bring you back to Egypt in ships, by the way of which I said to you, “You shall never see it again”; and there you shall offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, but there shall be no buyer.
These are the words of the covenant that the LORD commanded Moses to make with the sons of Israel in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant He had made with them at Horeb.
Moses summoned all Israel and said to them, “You have seen all that the LORD accomplished before your eyes in the land of Egypt—to Pharaoh, to all his servants, and to all his land.
Your eyes saw the great trials, the signs, and those great wonders.
Yet to this day the LORD has not granted you a heart to know, eyes to see, or ears to hear. “
I have led you forty years through the wilderness; your garments have not worn out upon you, nor have your sandals worn off your feet.
You have eaten no bread and drunk neither wine nor strong drink, so that you might know that I am the LORD your God. “
When you arrived at this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out against us to battle, and we defeated them.
We seized their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
Therefore observe the words of this covenant and put them into practice, that you may prosper in all that you do. “
You are all standing today before the LORD your God—your heads, your tribes, your elders, and your officers, every man in Israel—
your little ones, your wives, and the resident alien in the midst of your camps, from the hewer of wood to the drawer of water,
to enter into the covenant of the LORD your God and into His oath, which the LORD your God is making with you today,
that He may establish you today as His people and be your God, just as He spoke to you and as He swore to your fathers—to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob. “
And it is not with you alone that I am making this covenant and this oath,
but with him who stands here with us today before the LORD our God and with him who is not here with us today. “
For you know how we dwelt in the land of Egypt and how we passed through the midst of the nations through which you passed.
You saw their abominations and their idols—wood and stone, silver and gold—that were among them.

Lest there be among you a man or woman, or family or tribe, whose heart turns away today from the LORD our God to go and serve the gods of those nations; lest there be among you a root bearing poisonous fruit and wormwood.

And when such a one hears the words of this curse, he blesses himself in his heart, saying, ‘I shall have peace, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart,’ thereby bringing disaster upon the watered land as well as the dry. “

The LORD will not consent to forgive him; rather, the anger of the LORD and His jealousy will burn against that man, and all the curse written in this book will settle upon him, and the LORD will blot out his name from under heaven.
The LORD will single him out for disaster from all the tribes of Israel, in accordance with all the curses of the covenant written in this Book of the Law. “

And the generation to come—your children who rise after you, and the foreigner who comes from a distant land—will say, when they see the plagues of that land and the diseases that the LORD has inflicted upon it,

‘Its whole land is sulfur and salt, a burnt wasteland, unsown and unproductive, where no grass grows, like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in His anger and wrath.’ “
All nations will say, ‘Why has the LORD done thus to this land? What is the meaning of this great and burning anger?’
Then they will say, ‘Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD, the God of their fathers, which He made with them when He brought them out of the land of Egypt.
They went and served other gods and worshiped them—gods they did not know and that He had not allotted to them.
Therefore the anger of the LORD burned against this land, to bring upon it every curse written in this book.
The LORD uprooted them from their land in anger, wrath, and great indignation, and cast them into another land, as it is this day.’ “
The secret things belong to the LORD our God, but the things revealed belong to us and to our children forever, that we may do all the words of this law.”
When all these things have come upon you—the blessing and the curse that I have set before you—and you call them to mind among all the nations to which the LORD your God has driven you,
you and your children shall return to the LORD your God and obey His voice with all your heart and all your soul, in accordance with all that I command you this day.
Then the LORD your God will restore you from captivity and have compassion on you, gathering you again from all the peoples among whom the LORD your God has scattered you.
Even if your exiles are at the ends of heaven, from there the LORD your God will gather you, and from there He will take you.
the LORD your God will bring you into the land your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it; He will prosper you and multiply you beyond your fathers.
the LORD your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your descendants, so that you love the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul, and thereby live.
the LORD your God will place all these curses upon your enemies and those who hate you, who have persecuted you.
You shall turn again and obey the voice of the LORD, doing all His commandments that I command you this day.

the LORD your God will make you abundantly prosperous in all the work of your hands, in the fruit of your womb, your livestock, and your soil, for good; for the LORD will once more rejoice over you for good, as He rejoiced over your fathers.

This is contingent upon your obeying the voice of the LORD your God by keeping His commandments and statutes written in this Book of the Law, and upon your returning to the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul.
For this commandment that I am commanding you today is not too abstruse for you, nor is it remote.
It is not in heaven, that you should say, "Who will ascend to heaven for us and bring it to us, that we may hear it and do it?"
Neither is it beyond the sea, that you should say, "Who will cross the sea for us and bring it to us, that we may hear it and do it?"
Rather, the word is very near you—in your mouth and in your heart—so that you may do it.
See, I have set before you today life and good, death and evil.

If you heed what I command you today—loving the LORD your God, walking in His ways, and keeping His commandments, statutes, and judgments—then you shall live and multiply, and the LORD your God will bless you in the land you are entering to possess.
But if your heart turns away and you do not listen, and you are drawn away to bow down to other gods and serve them,
I declare to you today that you shall surely perish. You shall not prolong your days upon the land that you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess.
I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse; therefore choose life, that you and your descendants may live,

by loving the LORD your God, obeying His voice, and clinging to Him, for He is your life and the length of your days, that you may dwell in the land that the LORD swore to your fathers—to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—to give them.
Moses went forth and proclaimed these words to the whole of Israel.

He said to them, “I have attained the age of one hundred twenty years this day; I am no longer capable of active leadership. Furthermore, the the LORD has declared to me, ‘You shall not cross this Jordan.’

The The LORD your God—He Himself is crossing over before you; He will annihilate these nations from before your face, and you shall take possession of their land. Joshua, too, is crossing over before you, just as the the LORD has spoken.
The The LORD will deal with them as He dealt with Sihon and Og, kings of the Amorites, and with their land, which He laid waste.
The The LORD will deliver them before you, and you shall treat them in accordance with every commandment I have enjoined upon you.
Be strong and courageous; do not fear, nor be dismayed before them, for the the LORD your God is the One who goes with you. He will not fail you, nor will He forsake you.”
Moses wrote down this law and delivered it to the Levitical priests who bear the ark of the covenant of the the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel.
Moses charged them, saying, “At the end of every seven years, at the designated time of the year of release, during the Feast of Tabernacles,
when all Israel assembles to appear before the the LORD your God in the place He will choose, you shall read this law aloud in the hearing of all Israel.
Assemble the people—men, women, and children—and the sojourner within your gates, so that they may hear, learn, and fear the the LORD your God, and carefully observe all the words of this law,
and that their children who have not known it may hear and learn to fear the the LORD your God for as long as you live upon the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”

The The LORD said to Moses, “Behold, the days of your death draw near. Summon Joshua and present yourselves in the tent of meeting, that I may commission him.” So Moses and Joshua went and took their stand in the tent of meeting.
The The LORD appeared in the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood at the entrance of the tent.

The The LORD said to Moses, “You are about to die and be gathered to your fathers. This people will then arise and turn to idolatry, pursuing the foreign gods of the land they are entering, living in its midst; they will forsake Me and violate the covenant I have made with them.

In that day My anger will be kindled against them; I will forsake them and hide My face from them, so that they will be consumed. Many evils and troubles will befall them, and they will say in that day, ‘Have not these calamities come upon us because our God is not in our midst?’
I will surely hide My face in that day on account of all the evil they have committed, for they will have turned to other gods.”

The The LORD said, “Now, therefore, write this song for yourselves and teach it to the children of Israel; place it upon their lips, so that this song may stand as a witness for Me against the children of Israel.

For when I bring them into the land I swore to their fathers—a land flowing with milk and honey—and they eat their fill and grow prosperous, they will turn to other gods, serve them, provoke Me, and break My covenant.

And when many evils and troubles befall them, this song will testify against them as a witness, for it will not be forgotten from the mouths of their descendants. I know the inclination of their hearts even now, before I bring them into the land I have sworn to give them.”
So Moses wrote this song that very day and taught it to the children of Israel.
The The LORD then commissioned Joshua son of Nun, saying, “Be strong and courageous, for you shall lead the children of Israel into the land I swore to them, and I will be with you.”
When Moses had finished writing all the words of this law in a book, to their very completion,
Moses commanded the Levites who bear the ark of the covenant of the the LORD, saying,
“Take this book of the law and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the the LORD your God, so that it may remain there as a witness against you.
For I know your rebellion and your stiff neck. Even while I am alive with you today, you have been rebellious against the the LORD; how much more so after my death!
Assemble before me all the elders of your tribes and your officers, that I may speak these words in their hearing and call heaven and earth to witness against them.

For I know that after my death you will utterly corrupt yourselves and turn aside from the way I have commanded you. In the latter days evil will befall you, because you will do what is evil in the sight of the the LORD, provoking Him to anger by the work of your hands.”
Moses then recited the words of this song in the hearing of the whole assembly of Israel, until he had finished.
Give ear, O heavens, and I shall speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
My instruction shall drip like rain, my discourse shall distill like dew, like gentle rain upon the tender grass and like showers upon the herb.
For I will proclaim the name of the LORD; ascribe greatness to our God.
The Rock—His work is perfect, for all His ways are justice; a God of faithfulness, without iniquity, righteous and upright is He.
They have dealt corruptly toward Him; to their shame, they are no longer His children—a perverse and crooked generation.
Do you thus repay the LORD, you foolish and senseless people? Is He not your Father who created you, who made you and established you?
Remember the days of old; consider the years of many generations; ask your father, and he will show you; your elders, and they will tell you.
When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when He separated the sons of men, He set the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel.
For the LORD’s portion is His people; Jacob is the lot of His inheritance.
He found him in a desert land, in the howling waste of the wilderness; He encircled him, He instructed him, He kept him as the apple of His eye.
Like an eagle that stirs up its nest, that flutters over its young, spreading out its wings, catching them and bearing them on its pinions—
the LORD alone led him, and no foreign god was with him.
He made him ride on the high places of the earth, and he ate the produce of the fields; He nursed him with honey from the rock and oil from the flinty crag.
Curds from the herd and milk from the flock, with fat of lambs, rams of Bashan and goats, with the finest of the wheat—and you drank wine from the blood of the grape.
But Jeshurun grew fat and kicked; you grew fat, you grew thick, and you became sleek; then he forsook God who made him and scorned the Rock of his salvation.
They provoked Him to jealousy with strange gods; with abominations they provoked Him to anger.
They sacrificed to demons, not God—to gods they had not known, to new gods that had come recently, which your fathers had not dreaded.
You forgot the Rock who begot you, and forgot God who formed you.
The LORD saw it and spurned them, because of the provocation of His sons and daughters.
And He said, “I will hide My face from them; I will see what their end will be, for they are a perverse generation, children in whom is no faithfulness.

They have made Me jealous with that which is not God; they have provoked Me to anger with their idols. So I will make them jealous with a people that is not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.
For a fire is kindled in My anger, and it burns to the depths of Sheol, devours the earth and its increase, and sets on fire the foundations of the mountains.
I will heap disasters upon them; I will spend My arrows on them.
“They shall be wasted with hunger, and devoured by plague and bitter destruction; I will send the teeth of beasts against them, with the venom of things that crawl in the dust.
Outdoors the sword shall bereave, and indoors terror, for young man and virgin, the nursing child with the man of gray hairs.
I would have said, ‘I will scatter them afar; I will make the memory of them cease from among mankind’—
had I not feared the provocation of the enemy, lest their adversaries misunderstand, lest they say, ‘Our hand is exalted, and the LORD has not done all this.’”
For they are a nation void of counsel, and there is no understanding in them.
If they were wise, they would understand this; they would discern their latter end.
How could one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them, and the LORD had given them up?
For their rock is not as our Rock, even our enemies themselves being judges.
For their vine comes from the vine of Sodom and from the fields of Gomorrah; their grapes are grapes of gall, their clusters are bitter.
Their wine is the venom of serpents, and the cruel poison of asps.
“Is not this laid up in store with Me, sealed in My treasuries?
Vengeance is Mine, and recompense, for the time when their foot shall slip; for the day of their calamity is at hand, and their doom hastens.”
For the LORD will judge His people and have compassion on His servants, when He sees that their power is gone and there is none remaining, bond or free.
“And He will say, ‘Where are their gods, the rock in which they took refuge,
who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their drink offering? Let them rise up and help you; let them be your protection!’”
“See now that I am He, and there is no god besides Me; I kill and I make alive; I wound and I heal; and there is none that can deliver out of My hand.
For I lift up My hand to heaven and swear, As I live forever,
if I sharpen My flashing sword and My hand takes hold on judgment, I will render vengeance to My adversaries and repay those who hate Me.
I will make My arrows drunk with blood, and My sword shall devour flesh, with the blood of the slain and the captives, from the heads of the leaders of the enemy.”
Rejoice, O nations, with His people, for He avenges the blood of His servants and renders vengeance to His adversaries, and makes atonement for His land, for His people.
So Moses, together with Joshua the son of Nun, came and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people.
And when Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
he said to them, “Set your hearts to all the words that I am testifying against you today, that you may command your sons to observe and to do all the words of this law.
For it is not an empty word for you, but it is your life, and by this word you shall prolong your days in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”
The LORD spoke to Moses that very day, saying,
“Go up this mountain of the Abarim, Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab, opposite Jericho, and view the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the sons of Israel for a possession.
And die on the mountain that you are ascending, and be gathered to your people, as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people.”
“Because you broke faith with Me in the midst of the sons of Israel at the waters of Meribah-kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin, and because you did not sanctify Me in the midst of the sons of Israel.
For you shall see the land from a distance, but you shall not enter there, into the land that I am giving to the sons of Israel.”
This is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the children of Israel before his death.
He said, "The LORD came from Sinai and dawned upon them from Seir; He shone forth from Mount Paran. He came with myriads of holy ones, and from His right hand issued a flaming law for them.
Indeed, He loves the peoples—all His holy ones are in Your hand. They bow at Your feet and receive Your words.
Moses commanded us a law, an inheritance for the assembly of Jacob.
He was king in Jeshurun when the heads of the people assembled, the tribes of Israel together.
"Let Reuben live and not die, nor let his people be few.
"And this for Judah: 'Hear, O the LORD, the voice of Judah, and bring him to his people. Let his hands be sufficient for him, and be a help against his adversaries.'
"And of Levi he said: 'Your Thummim and Urim belong to Your godly one, whom You tested at Massah and contended with at the waters of Meribah.
He said of his father and mother, 'I have not seen them,' and did not acknowledge his brothers or know his own children, for they kept Your word and guarded Your covenant.
They shall teach Jacob Your ordinances and Israel Your law. They shall put incense before You and whole burnt offerings on Your altar.
Bless, O the LORD, his substance, and accept the work of his hands. Crush the loins of those who rise against him and of those who hate him, so that they rise no more.'
"And of Benjamin he said: 'The beloved of the LORD shall dwell in safety by Him; He shelters him all the day, and he dwells between His shoulders.'
"And of Joseph he said: 'Blessed by the LORD is his land, with the choicest gifts of heaven, with the dew, and with the deep that lies beneath,
with the choicest fruits of the sun and the finest yield of the months,
with the best of the ancient mountains and the choicest gifts of the everlasting hills,
with the choice things of the earth and its fullness, and the favor of Him who dwelt in the bush. May these rest on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the one set apart among his brothers.

His firstborn ox has majesty, and his horns are the horns of a wild ox; with them he shall gore the peoples, all at once, to the ends of the earth. They are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.'
"And of Zebulun he said: 'Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents.
They shall call peoples to the mountain; there they shall offer sacrifices of righteousness, for they shall suck the abundance of the seas and the hidden treasures of the sand.'
"And of Gad he said: 'Blessed be he who enlarges Gad! He dwells like a lion and tears off arm and scalp.
He chose the best for himself, for there a commander's portion was reserved; and he came with the heads of the people. He executed the righteousness of the LORD and His judgments with Israel.'
"And of Dan he said: 'Dan is a lion's cub; he shall leap from Bashan.'
"And of Naphtali he said: 'Naphtali, satisfied with favor and full of the blessing of the LORD, take possession of the west and the south.'
"And of Asher he said: 'Most blessed of sons is Asher; let him be favored by his brothers, and let him dip his foot in oil.
Your bars shall be iron and bronze, and as your days, so shall your strength be.'
"There is none like God, O Jeshurun, who rides through the heavens to your help, and in His majesty through the skies.
The eternal God is your refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms. He will drive out the enemy before you and say, 'Destroy!'
So Israel shall dwell in safety, the fountain of Jacob alone, in a land of grain and new wine; yes, his heavens shall drop down dew.

Happy are you, O Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD, the shield of your help and the sword of your majesty! Your enemies shall cower before you, and you shall tread upon their high places."
Then Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the summit of Pisgah, which faces Jericho. And the LORD showed him the whole land—from Gilead to Dan—
all of Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the Western Sea,
the Negev, and the region of the Jordan Valley, with Jericho, the City of Palms, as far as Zoar.

And the LORD said to him, “This is the land that I swore to give Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob when I said, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’ I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you shall not cross over into it.”
So Moses, the servant of the LORD, died there in the land of Moab, as the LORD had said.
And He buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth-peor, but to this day no one knows the location of his grave.
Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died, yet his eyes were not dim, nor had his vigor faded.
The Israelites lamented Moses in the plains of Moab for thirty days, until the period of weeping and mourning for Moses had come to an end.
Now Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hands on him; so the Israelites obeyed him and did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Since then, no prophet has arisen in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face,
in all the signs and wonders that the LORD sent him to perform in the land of Egypt against Pharaoh and all his officials and all his land,
and in all the mighty acts and all the great and terrifying deeds that Moses performed in the sight of all Israel.
After the death of Moses, the servant of the LORD, the LORD addressed Joshua son of Nun, Moses’ attendant, with these words:
“Moses My servant is dead. Now, therefore, arise—you together with all this people—and cross this Jordan into the land that I am granting to the children of Israel.
Every place where the sole of your foot treads I have given to you, just as I promised Moses.
Your border shall extend from the wilderness and this Lebanon to the great river, the Euphrates—that is, all the land of the Hittites—and as far as the Great Sea toward the setting of the sun.
“No one shall be able to withstand you throughout all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I shall be with you; I will neither abandon you nor forsake you.
Be strong and courageous, for you shall apportion to this people the land that I swore to their ancestors to give them.

Only be very strong and courageous, taking care to observe the whole law that Moses My servant commanded you. Do not turn aside from it to the right or to the left, so that you may prosper wherever you go.

“This Book of the Law must not depart from your mouth; meditate upon it day and night, so that you may be careful to do all that is written in it. Then you will prosper and succeed in all that you do.
Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be terrified or dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.”
Joshua then commanded the officers of the people,

“Go throughout the camp and instruct the people: ‘Prepare your provisions, for within three days you will cross this Jordan to enter and take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.’”
Moreover, Joshua addressed the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh:
“Remember the word that Moses, the servant of the LORD, commanded you when he said, ‘The LORD your God is giving you rest and has given you this land.’

Your wives, your little ones, and your livestock shall remain in the land that Moses gave you beyond the Jordan, but all your valiant men, armed, shall cross over before your brothers and assist them,

“until the LORD has given your brothers rest, as He has given you, and they also have taken possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving them. Then you may return to your own land and possess it—the land that Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave you beyond the Jordan, toward the sunrise.”
They answered Joshua, “All that you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go.
“Just as we obeyed Moses in all things, so we will obey you. May the LORD your God be with you, as He was with Moses.
Whoever rebels against your command and does not obey your words in all that you command him shall be put to death. Only be strong and courageous!”

Joshua son of Nun clandestinely dispatched two men from Shittim to spy out the land, saying, "Go, reconnoiter the land, especially Jericho." So they went and entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab and lodged there.
It was reported to the king of Jericho, "Behold, men from among the Israelites have come here tonight to search out the land."
Then the king of Jericho sent word to Rahab, saying, "Bring out the men who came to you, who entered your house, for they have come to search out all the land."
But the woman had taken the two men and concealed them. She said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know whence they came.
When dusk fell and the gate was being shut, the men went out. I do not know where the men went. Pursue them quickly; you may overtake them."
But she had brought them up to the roof and hidden them among the stalks of flax she had arranged in order on the roof.
So the men pursued them along the way to the fords of the Jordan; and as soon as the pursuers had gone out, the gate was shut behind them.
Before the spies had lain down, she came up to them on the roof.
She said to the men, "I know that the the LORD has given you the land, and that dread of you has fallen upon us, and all the inhabitants of the land are overcome with dread before you.

For we have heard how the the LORD dried up the waters of the Red Sea before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, whom you devoted to destruction.
When we heard these things, our courage failed, and no one retained any resolve because of you; for the the LORD your God, He is God in heaven above and on earth beneath.
Now therefore swear to me by the the LORD that, since I have dealt kindly with you, you will deal kindly with my father's house, and give me a trustworthy pledge.
Spare my father and mother, my brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them, and deliver our lives from death."
The men said to her, "We pledge our lives for yours, provided you do not disclose this business of ours. And when the the LORD gives us the land, we will deal with you in kindness and truth."
Then she let them down by a rope through the window, for her house was built into the city wall, and she dwelt in the wall.
She said to them, "Go to the hill country, lest the pursuers meet you; hide there three days until the pursuers have returned, and afterward go your way."
The men said to her, "We will be innocent of this oath that you have made us swear,

provided that, when we come into the land, you tie this scarlet cord in the window through which you let us down, and gather into your house your father and mother, your brothers, and all your father's household.

Whoever goes out of the doors of your house into the street, his blood shall be upon his own head, and we shall be innocent; but if anyone with you in the house is harmed, his blood shall be upon our heads.
But if you disclose this business of ours, we shall be innocent of the oath you made us swear."
She said, "According to your words, so be it." Then she sent them away, and they departed; and she tied the scarlet cord in the window.
They went and came to the hill country and remained there three days, until the pursuers had returned. The pursuers searched all along the road but did not find them.
Then the two men returned and came down from the hill country, crossed over, and came to Joshua son of Nun, and told him all that had happened to them.
They said to Joshua, "Truly the the LORD has given all the land into our hand; indeed, all the inhabitants of the land are overcome with dread before us."
At dawn Joshua arose, and he together with all the Israelites set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan, where they encamped before crossing.
After three days the officers passed through the midst of the camp.
They commanded the people, saying, "When you see the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God being carried by the Levitical priests, you shall set out from your place and follow after it.

Nevertheless, let there be a distance of about two thousand cubits between you and it; do not draw near to it, so that you may know the way by which you must go, for you have not passed this way before."
Joshua said to the people, "Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the LORD will perform wonders among you."
Joshua said to the priests, "Take up the ark of the covenant and pass on before the people." So they took up the ark of the covenant and went before the people.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Today I will begin to exalt you in the sight of all Israel, so that they may know that, just as I was with Moses, so I will be with you.
You shall command the priests who bear the ark of the covenant, 'When you come to the brink of the waters of the Jordan, you shall stand still in the Jordan.'"
Joshua said to the Israelites, "Come near here and hear the words of the LORD your God.

By this you shall know that the living God is among you, and that He will surely dispossess before you the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Hivite, the Perizzite, the Girgashite, the Amorite, and the Jebusite.
Behold, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is crossing before you into the Jordan.
Now take for yourselves twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one man from each tribe.

And it shall be that, as soon as the soles of the feet of the priests bearing the ark of the LORD—the Lord of all the earth—rest in the waters of the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan flowing down from above shall be cut off and shall stand in one heap."
So when the people set out from their tents to cross the Jordan, the priests bearing the ark of the covenant went before the people.

Now the Jordan overflows all its banks throughout the days of harvest; and as soon as those bearing the ark came to the Jordan, and the feet of the priests bearing the ark were dipped in the edge of the water,

the waters coming down from above stood still and rose up in one heap, a great distance away at Adam, the city beside Zarethan, while the waters flowing down toward the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, were completely cut off; and the people crossed over opposite Jericho.

The priests bearing the ark of the covenant of the LORD stood firmly on dry ground in the midst of the Jordan, and all Israel passed over on dry ground until the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan.
Upon the completion of the entire nation’s passage across the Jordan, the LORD spoke to Joshua, saying,
“Appropriate for yourselves twelve men from the people—one representative from each tribe—

and charge them thus: ‘Take up for yourselves twelve stones from this place, from the very midst of the Jordan, from the locus where the priests’ feet stood firm; transport them with you and deposit them in the encampment where you lodge this night.’”
So Joshua summoned the twelve men whom he had appointed from among the Israelites—one man from each tribe.

And Joshua said to them, “Cross over before the ark of the LORD your God into the midst of the Jordan, and let each man hoist a stone upon his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Israel,
that this may serve as a sign among you; when your children inquire tomorrow, saying, ‘What mean these stones to you?’

then you shall answer them, ‘Because the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD; when it crossed over in the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off. And these stones shall be for a memorial to the sons of Israel forever.’”

And the sons of Israel did so as Joshua commanded: they lifted twelve stones out of the midst of the Jordan, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Israel, as the LORD had spoken to Joshua; and they carried them over with them to the encampment and laid them down there.
Joshua also erected twelve stones in the midst of the Jordan, at the place where the feet of the priests bearing the ark of the covenant had stood; and they remain there to this day.

For the priests bearing the ark stood in the midst of the Jordan until everything was finished that the LORD commanded Joshua to speak to the people, according to all that Moses had commanded Joshua; and the people hastened and crossed over.
And when all the people had finished crossing, the ark of the LORD crossed over, and the priests, before the people.
The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over in martial array before the Israelites, as Moses had spoken to them,
about forty thousand equipped for battle crossing over before the LORD to the plains of Jericho.
On that day the LORD exalted Joshua in the sight of all Israel, and they revered him, as they had revered Moses, all the days of his life.
Then the LORD spoke to Joshua, saying,
“Command the priests bearing the ark of the testimony to ascend out of the Jordan.”
So Joshua commanded the priests, saying, “Ascend out of the Jordan.”

And when the priests bearing the ark of the covenant of the LORD came up out of the midst of the Jordan, and the soles of the priests’ feet were lifted up to the dry ground, the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and surged over all its banks as before.
The people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and encamped at Gilgal on the eastern edge of Jericho.
And those twelve stones which they had taken out of the Jordan Joshua set up at Gilgal.
And he said to the sons of Israel, “When your children ask their fathers tomorrow, saying, ‘What are these stones?’
then you shall make known to your children, saying, ‘Israel crossed over this Jordan on dry land,
because the LORD your God dried up the waters of the Jordan from before you until you crossed over, as the LORD your God did to the Red Sea, which He dried up from before us until we crossed over,
so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the hand of the LORD is mighty, that you may fear the LORD your God forever.’”

When all the Amorite kings who were beyond the Jordan to the west, together with all the Canaanite kings who were by the sea, heard that the LORD had dried up the waters of the Jordan before the children of Israel until we had passed over, their hearts melted, and no spirit remained in them any longer because of the children of Israel.
At that time the LORD said to Joshua, “Make flint knives for yourself, and circumcise the children of Israel a second time.”
So Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the children of Israel at the Hill of the Foreskins.
Now this is the reason Joshua circumcised them: all the males who had come out of Egypt, all the men of war, had died in the wilderness along the way after they came out of Egypt.
For although all the people who came out had been circumcised, none of those born in the wilderness along the way after they left Egypt had been circumcised.

For the children of Israel traveled in the wilderness forty years, until the whole nation of men of war who came out of Egypt was consumed, because they did not obey the voice of the LORD; to them the LORD had sworn that He would not let them see the land that the LORD had sworn to their fathers to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
So He raised up their children in their place, and Joshua circumcised these, for they were uncircumcised because they had not been circumcised on the journey.
When the whole nation had finished being circumcised, they remained in their places in the camp until they were healed.
The LORD said to Joshua, “Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you.” Therefore the name of that place is called Gilgal to this day.
The children of Israel camped at Gilgal and observed the Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day of the month in the plains of Jericho.
On the day after the Passover, on that very day, they ate unleavened bread and roasted grain from the produce of the land.
The manna ceased on the day after they ate from the produce of the land, and the children of Israel no longer had manna; instead, they ate from the produce of the land of Canaan that year.

Now when Joshua was near Jericho, he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a man was standing opposite him with his sword drawn in his hand. Joshua went to him and said, “Are you for us, or for our adversaries?”
“No,” he replied, “but as Commander of the army of the LORD I have now come.” Then Joshua fell on his face to the ground and worshiped, and said to him, “What does my Lord say to His servant?”
The Commander of the army of the LORD said to Joshua, “Take off your sandal from your foot, for the place where you are standing is holy.” And Joshua did so.
Now Jericho was shut up and closely barred because of the Israelites: no one went out, and no one came in.
the LORD said to Joshua, “See, I have given Jericho into your hand, together with its king and its mighty men of valor.
You shall march around the city, all the men of war circling it once; thus you shall do for six days.
Seven priests shall carry before the ark seven trumpets of rams’ horns; on the seventh day you shall encircle the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the trumpets.

When they make a long blast with the ram’s horn, and when you hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people shall shout with a great shout; then the wall of the city shall fall down flat, and the people shall go up, every man straight ahead.”
Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, “Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests carry seven trumpets of rams’ horns before the ark of the LORD.”
He said to the people, “Pass on, and march around the city, and let the armed men pass on before the ark of the LORD.”

So, when Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests bearing the seven trumpets of rams’ horns before the LORD passed on and blew the trumpets; the ark of the covenant of the LORD followed them.
The armed men went before the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rear guard came after the ark, while the priests kept blowing the trumpets as they went.
Joshua commanded the people, saying, “You shall not shout, nor make your voice heard, and no word shall come out of your mouth, until the day I tell you to shout; then you shall shout.”
Thus he made the ark of the LORD go around the city, circling it once; then they returned to the camp and lodged there.
Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of the LORD.

The seven priests bearing the seven trumpets of rams’ horns went on continually before the ark of the LORD, blowing the trumpets; the armed men went before them, and the rear guard followed the ark of the LORD, while the priests blew the trumpets.
On the second day they marched around the city once and returned to the camp; they did so for six days.
On the seventh day they rose early at dawn and marched around the city in the same manner seven times; on that day only they encircled the city seven times.
At the seventh time, when the priests blew the trumpets, Joshua said to the people, “Shout, for the LORD has given you the city.
The city and everything in it shall be devoted to the LORD for destruction; only Rahab the prostitute, and all who are with her in the house, shall live, because she hid the messengers we sent.
But you, keep yourselves from the devoted thing, lest you make yourselves accursed by taking from it and so make the camp of Israel accursed and bring trouble upon it.
Yet all the silver and gold, and the vessels of bronze and iron, are holy to the LORD; they shall go into the treasury of the LORD.”

So the people shouted, and the priests blew the trumpets; and when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, they shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell down flat, so that the people went up into the city, every man straight ahead, and they captured the city.
They devoted to destruction by the edge of the sword all that was in the city, both men and women, young and old, oxen, sheep, and donkeys.
Joshua said to the two men who had spied out the land, “Go into the prostitute’s house and bring out the woman and all that she has, as you swore to her.”

So the young men who had been spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father, her mother, her brothers, and all that she had; all her relatives they brought out and set them outside the camp of Israel.
They burned the city with fire, and all that was in it; only the silver, the gold, and the vessels of bronze and iron they put into the treasury of the house of the LORD.
Thus Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, her father’s household, and all that she had; and she has lived among Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

At that time Joshua charged them with an oath, saying, “Cursed be the man before the LORD who rises up and rebuilds this city Jericho: he shall lay its foundation at the cost of his firstborn, and at the cost of his youngest son shall he set up its gates.”
So the LORD was with Joshua, and his fame spread throughout all the land.

But the Israelites acted unfaithfully concerning the devoted things: Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of what had been devoted, and the LORD's wrath ignited against the Israelites.
Joshua, meanwhile, dispatched men from Jericho to Ai, which lies near Beth-aven, east of Bethel, and instructed them, "Ascend and reconnoiter the land." The men ascended and reconnoitered Ai.

Upon their return to Joshua, they reported, "Let not the whole people ascend; rather, let about two or three thousand men go up and strike Ai, so that you do not weary the entire people, for the men of Ai are few."
So roughly three thousand men went up, yet they fled before the men of Ai.
The men of Ai struck down about thirty-six of them and pursued them from the gate as far as Shebarim, striking them down on the descent; and the courage of the people melted and became as water.
Then Joshua tore his garments and fell on his face to the earth before the ark of the LORD until evening, he and the elders of Israel, and they put dust upon their heads.

Joshua said, "Ah, the LORD, why did You ever bring this people across the Jordan, only to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites for destruction? Would that we had been content to remain beyond the Jordan!
O the LORD, what shall I say, now that Israel has turned its back before its enemies?
When the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land hear of it, they will surround us and cut off our name from the earth; and what will You do for Your great name?"
The LORD said to Joshua, "Rise! Why have you fallen on your face?
Israel has sinned; they have transgressed My covenant that I commanded them; they have taken some of the devoted things; they have stolen, acted deceitfully, and placed them among their own baggage.

Therefore the Israelites cannot stand before their enemies; they turn their backs before their enemies, because they have become devoted to destruction. I will no longer be with you unless you destroy the devoted things from among you.

Rise, consecrate the people, and say, 'Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, for thus says the LORD God of Israel: There is a devoted thing in your midst, O Israel; you cannot stand before your enemies until you remove the devoted thing from your midst.'

In the morning you shall come near by your tribes; and the tribe that the LORD takes shall come near by families; and the family that the LORD takes shall come near by households; and the household that the LORD takes shall come near man by man.

And he who is taken with the devoted thing shall be burned with fire, he and all that belongs to him, because he has transgressed the covenant of the LORD and committed a disgraceful thing in Israel."
So Joshua rose early in the morning and brought Israel near by tribes, and the tribe of Judah was taken.
He brought near the clan of Judah, and the clan of the Zerahites was taken; then he brought near the clan of the Zerahites man by man, and Zabdi was taken.
He brought near his household man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken.
Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory to the LORD God of Israel and give Him praise. Tell me now what you have done; do not hide it from me."
Achan answered Joshua, "Truly I have sinned against the LORD God of Israel, and this is what I did:

I saw among the spoil a sumptuous Shinar cloak, two hundred shekels of silver, and a gold bar weighing fifty shekels; I coveted them and took them. Behold, they are hidden in the earth in the midst of my tent, with the silver beneath it."
Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent; and behold, it was hidden in his tent, with the silver beneath it.
They took them from the tent and brought them to Joshua and all Israel, and laid them out before the LORD.

Joshua and all Israel with him took Achan son of Zerah, the silver, the cloak, the gold bar, his sons, his daughters, his ox, his donkey, his sheep, his tent, and all that he had, and brought them up to the Valley of Achor.
Joshua said, "Why have you brought trouble upon us? The LORD will trouble you this day." And all Israel stoned him with stones and burned them with fire.
They raised over him a great heap of stones, which remains to this day. Then the LORD turned from the fierceness of His anger. Therefore that place has been called the Valley of Achor to this day.

Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid, nor be dismayed; take all your fighting force and ascend against Ai. Behold, I have delivered into your hand the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his territory.
You shall deal with Ai and its king as you dealt with Jericho and its king, except that you may plunder its spoil and livestock for yourselves. Deploy an ambush behind the city.”
So Joshua, together with the entire martial host, arose to ascend against Ai; and Joshua chose thirty thousand men of valor and sent them out under cover of night.
He charged them, “Behold, you are to lie in ambush behind the city; do not withdraw very far from it, and let all of you be prepared.
I, with all the people accompanying me, will approach the city; and when they sally forth against us, as formerly, we shall flee before them.
They will pursue us until we have drawn them away from the city, for they will say, ‘They are fleeing before us, as at first’; and we shall flee before them.
Then you shall rise from the ambush and dispossess the city, for the LORD your God will deliver it into your hand.
When you have seized the city, you shall set it ablaze; according to the word of the LORD you shall act. Behold, I have commanded you.”
Joshua then sent them forth, and they proceeded to the place of ambush, taking position between Bethel and Ai, westward of Ai; but Joshua lodged that night among the people.
Joshua rose early in the morning, mustered the people, and he and the elders of Israel went up before the people to Ai.
All the fighting men with him went up, drew near to the city, and encamped north of Ai, with the valley between them and Ai.
He had taken about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.
So they stationed the whole camp north of the city and its rearguard west of the city; and that night Joshua went into the midst of the valley.

When the king of Ai saw this, he and all his people hastened and rose early in the morning to meet Israel in battle at the appointed place before the Arabah; yet he did not know that an ambush had been set against him behind the city.
Joshua and all Israel feigned retreat before them and fled toward the wilderness.
All the men of Ai were summoned to pursue them, and they pursued Joshua, being drawn away from the city.
Not a man remained in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel; they left the city unguarded and pursued Israel.
Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Extend toward Ai the javelin in your hand, for I will give it into your hand.” So Joshua extended toward the city the javelin in his hand.
As soon as he extended his hand, the ambush arose quickly from its place, ran into the city, captured it, and hastily set the city ablaze.

The men of Ai turned and saw the smoke of the city ascending to heaven, and they had no power to flee this way or that; and the people who had been fleeing toward the wilderness turned back against their pursuers.
When Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had captured the city and that smoke was ascending, they turned back and struck down the men of Ai.
The ambush also came out of the city against them, so they were caught in the middle, with Israelites on both sides; and Israel struck them down until no survivor or fugitive remained.
But they took the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

When Israel had finished slaying all the inhabitants of Ai in the open country and in the wilderness where they had pursued them, and all had fallen by the edge of the sword, all Israel returned to Ai and put it to the sword.
All who fell that day, from man to woman, were twelve thousand—every inhabitant of Ai.
For Joshua did not withdraw the hand with which he had extended the javelin until he had devoted to destruction all the inhabitants of Ai.
Only the livestock and the spoil of that city Israel took as plunder for themselves, according to the word of the LORD, which He had commanded Joshua.
Joshua burned Ai and made it an everlasting heap of ruins, a desolation to this day.

He hanged the king of Ai on a tree until evening; and at sunset Joshua commanded that his corpse be taken down from the tree and cast at the entrance of the city gate, and they raised over him a great heap of stones, which remains to this day.
Then Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal.

as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the children of Israel, as it is written in the Book of the Law of Moses: an altar of whole stones, upon which no iron tool had been wielded. They offered burnt offerings to the LORD and sacrificed peace offerings.
There, in the presence of the children of Israel, he wrote on the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he had written.

All Israel, with their elders, officers, and judges, stood on either side of the ark of the covenant of the LORD, facing the Levitical priests who bore the ark—half of them before Mount Gerizim and half before Mount Ebal—as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded at first, to bless the people of Israel.
Afterward he read all the words of the law, the blessing and the curse, according to all that is written in the Book of the Law.
There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded that Joshua did not read before the whole assembly of Israel, together with the women, the little ones, and the sojourners who walked among them.

When all the kings who held sway on the western bank of the Jordan—in the hill country, in the lowlands, and along the entire littoral of the Great Sea opposite Lebanon, namely the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites—learned of these events,
they coalesced into a single coalition to wage war against Joshua and against Israel.
But when the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had wrought against Jericho and Ai, they too resorted to artifice.
They set out bearing provisions, loading their donkeys with frayed sacks and with wineskins that were antiquated, fissured, and patched.
Their sandals were worn and patched upon their feet, their garments were threadbare, and all their victuals consisted of dry bread that had become crumbled and moldy.
They repaired to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal and said to him and to the men of Israel, "We have journeyed from a far country; therefore now ratify a covenant with us."
The Israelites said to the Hivite, "Perhaps you dwell in our midst; how then could we ratify a covenant with you?"
"We are your servants," they replied to Joshua. Joshua said to them, "Who are you, and from what land have you come?"
Your servants have come from an exceedingly distant land, on account of the name of the LORD your God, for we have heard the report of Him and all that He did in Egypt,
and all that He did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan—to Sihon king of Heshbon and to Og king of Bashan, who reigned at Ashtaroth.

Therefore our elders and all the inhabitants of our land said to us, "Take provisions in your hand for the journey, go to meet them, and say to them, 'We are your servants; now make a covenant with us.'"
This bread of ours was warm when we took it from our houses on the day we set out to come to you; but now, behold, it is dry and crumbled.
And these wineskins were new when we filled them; behold, they have burst; and these garments and sandals of ours have become exceedingly worn because of the very long journey."
The men took some of their provisions, yet they did not seek counsel from the LORD.
Joshua made peace with them and entered into a covenant with them to preserve their lives; and the leaders of the congregation swore an oath to them.
At the end of three days, after they had entered into a covenant with them, it was discovered that they were near and were dwelling in their midst.
The Israelites set out and reached their cities on the third day—Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.
Yet the Israelites did not smite them, because the leaders of the congregation had sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel; and the whole congregation murmured against the leaders.
All the leaders said to the whole congregation, "We have sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel, and now we cannot touch them.
This is what we will do to them: we will let them live, lest wrath come upon us because of the oath that we swore to them."
The leaders said to them, "Let them live." So they became hewers of wood and drawers of water for the whole congregation, just as the leaders had spoken to them.

Joshua summoned them and said to them, "Why have you deceived us, saying, 'We are very far from you,' when in fact you dwell among us? Now therefore you are accursed, and servitude shall never be lifted from you: you shall be hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of my God."

They answered Joshua, "Because it was surely told to your servants that the LORD your God had commanded His servant Moses to give you all the land and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land before you; therefore we were exceedingly afraid for our lives because of you, and we have done this thing.
And now, behold, we are in your hand; deal with us as seems good and right in your eyes."
So he did to them and delivered them out of the hand of the Israelites, so that they did not put them to death.
That day Joshua appointed them hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and for the altar of the LORD, in the place that He would choose, to this day.

When Adoni-zedek, king of Jerusalem, heard that Joshua had captured Ai and had devoted it to destruction, treating Ai and its king exactly as he had treated Jericho and its king, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living among them,
he was seized with great fear, because Gibeon was a great city, comparable to one of the royal cities, and because it was larger than Ai, while all its men were mighty warriors.
Therefore Adoni-zedek, king of Jerusalem, sent to Hoham, king of Hebron, to Piram, king of Jarmuth, to Japhia, king of Lachish, and to Debir, king of Eglon, saying,
"Come up to me and help me, and let us strike Gibeon, for it has made peace with Joshua and with the people of Israel."

So the five kings of the Amorites—the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon—gathered together, went up with all their forces, encamped against Gibeon, and made war on it.

Then the men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal, saying, "Do not withdraw your hand from your servants; come up to us quickly and save us and help us, for all the kings of the Amorites who dwell in the hill country have gathered against us."
So Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the people of war with him, and all the mighty men of valor.
And the the LORD said to Joshua, "Do not fear them, for I have given them into your hand. Not one of them shall stand before you."
Joshua therefore came upon them suddenly, having marched up all night from Gilgal.

And the the LORD threw them into confusion before Israel, who struck them with a great blow at Gibeon and pursued them by the way of the ascent of Beth-horon, striking them as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

And as they fled before Israel, while they were descending the ascent of Beth-horon, the the LORD cast down great stones from heaven upon them as far as Azekah, and they died. Indeed, those who died by the hailstones were more numerous than those whom the sons of Israel killed with the sword.

At that time Joshua spoke to the the LORD on the day when the the LORD gave the Amorites over to the sons of Israel, and he said in the sight of Israel, "Sun, stand still at Gibeon, and moon, in the Valley of Aijalon."

And the sun stood still, and the moon stopped, until the nation took vengeance on its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? The sun stopped in the midst of heaven and did not hasten to go down for about a whole day.
There has been no day like it before or since, when the the LORD listened to the voice of a man, for the the LORD fought for Israel.
So Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.
Now these five kings had fled and hidden themselves in the cave at Makkedah.
And it was told to Joshua, "The five kings have been found hidden in the cave at Makkedah."
And Joshua said, "Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave and set men by it to guard them,
but do not stay there yourselves; pursue your enemies; attack their rear guard. Do not let them enter their cities, for the the LORD your God has given them into your hand."
When Joshua and the sons of Israel had finished striking them with a very great blow, until they were wiped out, and when the remnant that remained had entered the fortified cities,
then all the people returned safe to Joshua in the camp at Makkedah. Not a man moved his tongue against any of the sons of Israel.
Then Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me from the cave."
And they did so, and brought the five kings out to him from the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.

And when they brought the kings out to Joshua, Joshua summoned all the men of Israel and said to the commanders of the men of war who had gone with him, "Come near; put your feet on the necks of these kings." Then they came near and put their feet on their necks.
And Joshua said to them, "Do not be afraid or dismayed; be strong and courageous. For thus the the LORD will do to all your enemies against whom you fight."
And afterward Joshua struck them and put them to death, and he hanged them on five trees. And they hung on the trees until evening.

And at the time of the going down of the sun, Joshua commanded, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden, and they put large stones against the mouth of the cave, which remain to this very day.

As for Makkedah, Joshua captured it that day and struck it, and its king, with the edge of the sword. He devoted to destruction every person in it; he left none remaining. And he did to the king of Makkedah just as he had done to the king of Jericho.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him passed on from Makkedah to Libnah and fought against Libnah.

And the the LORD gave it also and its king into the hand of Israel. And he struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person in it; he left none remaining in it. And he did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him passed on from Libnah to Lachish and laid siege to it and fought against it.
And the the LORD gave Lachish into the hand of Israel, and he captured it on the second day and struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person in it, as he had done to Libnah.
Then Horam, king of Gezer, came up to help Lachish. And Joshua struck him and his people, until he left none remaining.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him passed on from Lachish to Eglon. And they camped against it and fought against it.
And they captured it that day, and struck it with the edge of the sword. And he devoted to destruction that day every person in it, as he had done to Lachish.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him went up from Eglon to Hebron and fought against it.

And they captured it and struck it with the edge of the sword, and its king and all its cities and every person in it. He left none remaining, as he had done to Eglon, and devoted it to destruction, and every person in it.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him turned back to Debir and fought against it.

And he captured it with its king and all its cities. And they struck them with the edge of the sword and devoted to destruction every person in it; he left none remaining. Just as he had done to Hebron and to Libnah and its king, so he did to Debir and its king.

So Joshua struck the whole land, the hill country and the Negev and the lowland and the foothills, and all their kings. He left none remaining, but devoted to destruction all that breathed, just as the the LORD God of Israel commanded.
And Joshua struck them from Kadesh-barnea as far as Gaza, and all the country of Goshen, as far as Gibeon.
And Joshua captured all these kings and their land at one time, because the the LORD God of Israel fought for Israel.
