So Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

When Jabin, monarch of Hazor, received intelligence of these developments, he dispatched envoys to Jobab, monarch of Madon, and to the monarchs of Shimron and Achshaph, and to the sovereigns of the northern territories in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Chinnereth, in the lowland, and in the elevations of Dor by the sea,
and to the Canaanites on the east and on the west, and to the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, and the Jebusites in the hill country, and to the Hivites beneath Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
They emerged with all their hosts, a people as innumerable as the sand upon the seashore, accompanied by horses and chariots in prodigious abundance.
All these monarchs convened and encamped together at the waters of Merom to prosecute war against Israel.

And the LORD declared to Joshua, "Do not be apprehensive of them, for tomorrow at this hour I shall deliver all of them slain before Israel; you shall hamstring their horses and incinerate their chariots with fire."
Accordingly, Joshua and all the martial host with him descended upon them precipitously at the waters of Merom and fell upon them.
The LORD delivered them into Israel's hand, and they smote them and pursued them as far as Great Sidon and Misrephoth-maim, eastward to the valley of Mizpeh, smiting them until no survivor remained.
Joshua then executed against them precisely what the LORD had prescribed: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
At that juncture Joshua turned and seized Hazor, striking its king with the sword, for Hazor had formerly been the paramount power among all those kingdoms.
They struck down every inhabitant with the edge of the sword, devoting them to utter destruction; no breathing soul was left, and he burned Hazor with fire.
Joshua captured all these cities and their kings and struck them with the edge of the sword; he devoted them to destruction, as Moses, the servant of the LORD, had enjoined.
Yet Israel did not incinerate any of the cities that stood upon their mounds, save Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.

All the spoil of these cities and the livestock the Israelites appropriated as plunder; but every person they struck down with the edge of the sword until they were annihilated, leaving no one breathing.
As the LORD had commanded Moses His servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and Joshua complied; he left nothing unfulfilled of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
Thus Joshua annexed all that land: the hill country, all the Negev, all the land of Goshen, the lowland, the Arabah, the hill country of Israel and its lowland,
from Mount Halak, which ascends toward Seir, to Baal-gad in the valley of Lebanon beneath Mount Hermon; and he captured all their kings, struck them, and put them to death.
Joshua protracted war against all these kings for an extended duration.
No city sought accommodation with the Israelites except the Hivites inhabiting Gibeon; all the others were seized in battle.
For the LORD hardened their hearts to confront Israel in battle, so that they might be devoted to destruction and receive no quarter, but be annihilated, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

At that time Joshua advanced and extirpated the Anakim from the hill country—from Hebron, Debir, and Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah and all the hill country of Israel—and devoted them and their cities to destruction.
No Anakim survived in the land of the Israelites except in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod, where remnants persisted.

So Joshua took possession of the entire land in accordance with all that the LORD had spoken to Moses; and Joshua allotted it as an inheritance to Israel according to their tribal divisions; and the land enjoyed respite from war.

Here are set forth the kings of the land whom the Israelites subdued, whose territories they appropriated east of the Jordan, extending from the gorge of the Arnon to Mount Hermon and encompassing the whole eastern Arabah.

Sihon, king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, ruled from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon gorge, through the midst of that gorge, as far as the Jabbok gorge, the frontier of the Ammonites, together with half of Gilead.
The eastern Arabah extended to the Sea of Chinnereth and to the Sea of the Arabah—that is, the Salt Sea—eastward along the route toward Beth-jeshimoth, and southward beneath the slopes of Pisgah.
The domain of Og, king of Bashan—one of the last survivors of the Rephaim—who held court at Ashtaroth and Edrei,
included Mount Hermon, Salcah, and all of Bashan, reaching to the frontier of the Geshurites and Maacathites, as well as half of Gilead up to the border of Sihon, king of Heshbon.

Moses, the servant of the the LORD, together with the Israelites, vanquished them; and Moses, the servant of the the LORD, allotted their land as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

These are the kings whom Joshua and the Israelites struck down west of the Jordan, from Baal-gad in the valley of Lebanon to Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, distributed according to their tribal allotments; Joshua assigned their territories as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel.
The lands comprised the hill country, the Shephelah, the Arabah, the slopes, the wilderness, and the Negev, inhabited by the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
The king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, near Bethel, one;
the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one.
The king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
the king of Aphek, one; the king of Sharon, one;
the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
the king of Shimron-meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;
the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
the king of Dor in Naphath-dor, one; the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one;
the king of Tirzah, one—thirty-one kings in all.

Now Joshua was old and advanced in years, and the LORD said to him, “You are old and advanced in years, and very much of the land remains to be possessed—this is the land that remains: all the districts of the Philistines and all the Geshurites,

from the Shihor, which lies before Egypt, to the border of Ekron northward (this is reckoned as Canaanite territory)—that of the five Philistine rulers of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron, together with the Avvites;
from the south, all the land of the Canaanites, from Mearah of the Sidonians to Aphek, as far as the border of the Amorites;
and the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon to the east, from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath.
As for all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim—all the Sidonians—I Myself will drive them out before the Israelites.
Be sure to allot this land as an inheritance to Israel, as I have commanded you.”
Now, therefore, apportion this land as an inheritance among the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
The Reubenites and the Gadites, together with the half-tribe of Manasseh, had already received the inheritance that Moses, the servant of the LORD, had given them east of the Jordan.
Their territory extended from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley, along with the city in the middle of the valley, and all the tableland from Medeba to Dibon;
and all the cities of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, to the border of the Ammonites;
and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan to Salecah;
all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei—he was one of the last of the Rephaim—and Moses struck them down and dispossessed them.
Yet the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites, so Geshur and Maacath dwell among the Israelites to this day.
To the tribe of Levi, however, Moses gave no inheritance; the fire offerings of the LORD, the God of Israel, are his inheritance, as He had spoken to him.
Moses gave the following inheritance to the clans of the tribe of Reuben:
their territory extended from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley, along with the city in the middle of the valley, and all the tableland near Medeba;
Heshbon and all its cities on the plateau—Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon,
Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-shahar on the hill in the valley,
Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah, and Beth-jeshimoth;

all the cities of the plateau and the whole kingdom of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who had reigned in Heshbon. Moses struck him down, along with the chiefs of Midian—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba—princes of Sihon who had lived in the land.
The Israelites also killed Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, along with the others they put to the sword.
The border of the Reubenites was the Jordan. These were the cities and villages given as an inheritance to the Reubenites, according to their clans.
This is what Moses had given to the clans of the tribe of Gad:
their territory included Jazer, all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites as far as Aroer, near Rabbah;
and from Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir;

and in the valley, Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon—the rest of the kingdom of Sihon, king of Heshbon. The Jordan River was the border, extending to the edge of the Sea of Chinnereth on the east side of the Jordan.
These were the cities and villages given as an inheritance to the Gadites, according to their clans.
This is what Moses had given to the clans of the half-tribe of Manasseh:
their territory included Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og, king of Bashan, and all the towns of Jair in Bashan—sixty cities;
half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan. These were allotted to the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh—to half the clan of Machir.
These are the portions Moses had given them on the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho.
To the tribe of Levi, however, Moses had given no inheritance. The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as He had promised them.

These are the territories that the Israelites inherited in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the Israelite tribes apportioned to them.
Their inheritance was determined by lot, exactly as the LORD had commanded through Moses, for the nine and one-half tribes.
For Moses had already granted an inheritance to the two and one-half tribes beyond the Jordan, yet he had granted no inheritance among them to the Levites.

The sons of Joseph had become two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim, and the Levites received no share in the land except cities in which to dwell, together with their pasturelands for livestock and property.
Thus the Israelites acted precisely as the LORD had commanded Moses, and they partitioned the land.

Then the sons of Judah approached Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, “You know the word that the LORD spoke to Moses, the man of God, at Kadesh-barnea, concerning you and me.
“I was forty years old when Moses, the servant of the LORD, sent me from Kadesh-barnea to reconnoiter the land, and I brought back a report precisely as I had perceived it in my heart.
“Yet my brothers who went up with me demoralized the people, whereas I unreservedly followed the LORD my God.

“Therefore on that day Moses swore, saying, ‘Surely the land upon which your foot has trodden shall be an inheritance for you and your children forever, because you have unreservedly followed the LORD my God.’

“And now, mark well that the LORD has preserved me alive, just as He promised, these forty-five years since the LORD spoke this word to Moses, while Israel wandered in the wilderness; and now, mark well that I am eighty-five years old today.
“I am today as vigorous as on the day Moses sent me; my strength then is my strength now, for warfare and for every undertaking of life.

“Now, therefore, grant me this mountainous region that the LORD promised on that day; for you heard on that day that the Anakim were there, with great fortified cities. Perhaps the LORD will be with me, and I shall dispossess them, just as the LORD said.”
So Joshua blessed him and gave Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh as an inheritance.
Therefore Hebron has remained the inheritance of Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite to this day, because he unreservedly followed the LORD, the God of Israel.
Now the name of Hebron formerly was Kiriath-arba; Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim. And the land had rest from war.
The allotment for the clans of the tribe of Judah reached the territory of Edom, to the Wilderness of Zin toward the south, at the farthest extremity of the south.
Their southern boundary began at the tongue of the Salt Sea, at the inlet facing southward.
It issued southward toward the Ascent of Akrabbim, crossed Zin, ascended south of Kadesh-barnea, passed Hezron, ascended to Addar, and bent toward Karka.
It passed Azmon, reached the Brook of Egypt, and discharged toward the sea; this formed their southern frontier.
The eastern frontier was the Salt Sea to the mouth of the Jordan; the northern frontier began at the bay of the sea at the mouth of the Jordan.
It ascended to Beth-hoglah, passed north of Beth-arabah, and ascended to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.

Then the boundary ascended to Debir from the Valley of Achor, turning north toward Gilgal, which lies opposite the Ascent of Adummim south of the valley; it continued to the waters of En-shemesh and ended at En-rogel.

It ascended the Valley of Ben-hinnom to the southern shoulder of the Jebusite city—that is, Jerusalem—then ascended to the summit of the mountain west of the Valley of Hinnom, at the northern extremity of the Valley of Rephaim.
From the summit the boundary curved to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah and issued to the cities of Mount Ephron; then it curved to Baalah, that is, Kiriath-jearim.
From Baalah it turned westward to Mount Seir, passed along the northern shoulder of Mount Jearim—that is, Chesalon—descended to Beth-shemesh, and crossed to Timnah.
Then it went out to the northern shoulder of Ekron, curved to Shikkeron, passed along to Mount Baalah, and issued to Jabneel; the boundary ended at the sea.
The western frontier was the coast of the Great Sea. These were the boundaries encircling the clans of the sons of Judah.
By the LORD’s command to Joshua, he gave Caleb son of Jephunneh a portion among the sons of Judah—Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, the city of Arba, father of Anak.
Caleb drove out from there the three sons of Anak—Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, descendants of Anak.
From there he went up against the inhabitants of Debir, formerly Kiriath-sepher.
And Caleb said, “Whoever attacks Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give him my daughter Achsah as a wife.”
So Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s brother, captured it, and Caleb gave his daughter Achsah to him as a wife.
When she came, she urged him to request a field from her father; and as she alighted from the donkey, Caleb asked her, “What do you want?”
“Give me a blessing,” she answered. “Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me also springs of water.” So Caleb gave her the upper and lower springs.
This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Judah. The cities of the south were:
Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon—twenty-nine cities with their villages.
Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim—fourteen cities with their villages;
Gederoth, Beth-dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah—sixteen cities with their villages;
Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah—nine cities with their villages;
Ekron with its towns and villages;
from Ekron westward, all that lay beside Ashdod, with their villages;
Ashdod with its towns and villages; Gaza with its towns and villages; to the Brook of Egypt and the Great Sea with its coastline.
Goshen, Holon, and Giloh—eleven cities with their villages;
Humtah, Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), and Zior—nine cities with their villages.
Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah—ten cities with their villages;
Maarath, Beth-anoth, and Eltekon—six cities with their villages;
Kiriath-baal (that is, Kiriath-jearim) and Rabbah—two cities with their villages;
in the wilderness: Beth-arabah, Middin, and Secacah;
Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En-gedi—six cities with their villages.
But the descendants of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites, inhabitants of Jerusalem; so the Jebusites dwell with the descendants of Judah in Jerusalem to this day.
The lot for the sons of Joseph extended from the Jordan at Jericho to the waters of Jericho on the east, traversing the wilderness that ascends from Jericho into the hill country of Bethel.
From Bethel it passed to Luz, skirted the border of the Archites at Ataroth,
and descended westward to the border of the Japhletites, reaching as far as the border of Lower Beth-horon and as far as Gezer, with its termini toward the sea.
Thus Manasseh and Ephraim, the sons of Joseph, received their inheritance.
The boundary of the Ephraimites, according to their clans, extended eastward from Ataroth-addar to Upper Beth-horon.
It proceeded toward the sea to Michmethah on the north, then curved eastward to Taanath-shiloh, passing it on the east to Janohah.
From Janohah it descended to Ataroth and Naarath, reached Jericho, and terminated at the Jordan.
The boundary went out from Tappuah westward to the Wadi Kanah, with its outlets at the sea; this constituted the inheritance of the tribe of Ephraim according to its families.
The Ephraimites also possessed distinct cities situated within the inheritance of the Manassites, together with their villages.
They did not dispossess the Canaanites dwelling in Gezer; rather, the Canaanites continued to reside among the Ephraimites to this day, though they were subjected to forced labor.

The lot was assigned to the tribe of Manasseh, for he was Joseph’s firstborn—namely Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh and progenitor of Gilead, a warrior; consequently, Gilead and Bashan were conferred upon him.

The allotment likewise pertained to the remaining posterity of Manasseh, according to their clans: the clans of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, enumerated by their families.
Now Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, but daughters only; and these are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

They presented themselves before Eleazar the priest, before Joshua son of Nun, and before the leaders, saying, “The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers.” Accordingly, Joshua granted them an inheritance among their father’s brothers, in accordance with the command of the LORD.
Thus ten portions fell to Manasseh, apart from the land of Gilead and Bashan beyond the Jordan,
because the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance among his sons, whereas the land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the sons of Manasseh.
The boundary of Manasseh extended from Asher to Michmethath, east of Shechem; it then turned southward toward the inhabitants of En-tappuah.
The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah itself, situated on the border of Manasseh, belonged to the Ephraimites.

From there the boundary descended into the Kanah Valley. These cities, though reckoned among the cities of Manasseh, belonged to Ephraim; and the border of Manasseh lay on the northern side of the valley, terminating at the sea.
Ephraim’s territory lay to the south, and Manasseh’s to the north, with the sea as its western limit; and they abutted Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.

Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh also possessed Beth-shean and its dependent towns, Ibleam and its dependent towns, the inhabitants of Dor and its dependent towns, the inhabitants of Endor and its dependent towns, the inhabitants of Taanach and its dependent towns, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its dependent towns—three Naphoth.
Yet the descendants of Manasseh were unable to dispossess these cities, because the Canaanites were resolutely determined to remain in that land.
But when the Israelites grew strong, they reduced the Canaanites to compulsory servitude and did not expel them entirely.
Then the descendants of Joseph addressed Joshua, saying, “Why have you given us only one allotment and one portion? We are a populous people, because the LORD has blessed us abundantly.”

Joshua answered them, “If you are a populous people, ascend into the forest and hew out a place for yourself there in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too constricted for you.”

The descendants of Joseph replied, “The hill country is insufficient for us, and all the Canaanites who dwell in the valley possess iron chariots—both those in Beth-shean and its villages and those in the valley of Jezreel.”
Then Joshua said to the house of Joseph—to Ephraim and Manasseh—“You are a populous and mighty people; you will have not only one allotment,
but the hill country as well. It is a forest, and you will clear it, and its farthest borders will be yours. Although the Canaanites have iron chariots and are strong, you can drive them out.”
The whole congregation of the Israelites assembled at Shiloh and erected the Tent of Meeting there, for the land had been subjugated before them.
Seven tribes among the Israelites had not yet obtained their inheritance.
Joshua remonstrated with the Israelites, saying, “How long will you remain indolent in going to take possession of the land that the LORD God of your fathers has given you?
Designate for yourselves three men from each tribe, and I will send them; let them arise, traverse the land, record it according to their inheritances, and return to me.
They shall partition it into seven allotments: Judah shall maintain its southern frontier, and the house of Joseph shall maintain its northern frontier.
You shall inscribe the seven portions of the land and bring them here to me, and I will cast lots on your behalf here before the LORD our God.

For the Levites possess no allotment among you, since the priesthood of the LORD constitutes their inheritance; and Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already secured their inheritance east of the Jordan, which Moses, the servant of the LORD, bestowed upon them.”

The men arose and went, and Joshua charged those tasked with surveying the land, saying, “Traverse the land, record it, and return to me, so that I may cast lots for you here before the LORD in Shiloh.”
The men therefore passed through the land and recorded it in a scroll, enumerating the cities into seven allotments, and returned to Joshua in the camp at Shiloh.
Joshua cast lots for them before the LORD in Shiloh, and there he distributed the land to the Israelites according to their divisions.
The allotment for the tribe of Benjamin, by its clans, came up, and their territory fell between the Judahites and the Josephites.
Their northern boundary began at the Jordan, ascended to the shoulder of Jericho on the north, climbed westward into the hill country, and terminated in the wilderness of Beth-aven.
From there the boundary passed to Luz, to the south side of Luz (that is, Bethel), and descended to Ataroth-addar upon the hill south of Lower Beth-horon.

The boundary then arced southward from the hill confronting Beth-horon on the south, and its extremities reached Kiriath-baal—that is, Kiriath-jearim—a city of the Judahites; this constituted the western frontier.
The southern side began at the extremity of Kiriath-jearim and extended westward, emerging at the spring of Nephtoah.

The boundary descended to the terminus of the mountain overlooking the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, situated in the Valley of Rephaim to the north, and descended the Valley of Hinnom to the southern flank of the Jebusite, finally reaching En-rogel.
It curved northward, emerged at En-shemesh, extended to Geliloth opposite the Ascent of Adummim, and descended to the stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
It continued northward over against the Arabah and descended into the Arabah.
The boundary proceeded northward to the shoulder of Beth-hoglah, and its termini reached the northern gulf of the Salt Sea at the southern extremity of the Jordan; this was the southern frontier.
The Jordan formed its eastern limit. Such was the inheritance of the Benjamites according to their clans, bounded on every side.
The cities of the Benjamites, according to their clans, were Jericho, Beth-hoglah, the Valley of Keziz,
Chephar-ammoni, Ophni, and Geba—twelve cities with their villages—
Zelah, Eleph, the Jebusite city (that is, Jerusalem), Gibeath, and Kiriath—fourteen cities with their villages. This was the inheritance of the Benjamites.
The second lot issued for the clans of Simeon, and their inheritance fell within the territory already assigned to Judah.
Their allotment comprised Beersheba (also called Sheba), Moladah,
Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen—thirteen cities, together with their villages.
It further included Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan—four cities with their villages—
along with all the surrounding villages as far as Baalath-beer (Ramath of the Negev). Such was the inheritance of the Simeonite clans.
Because Judah's portion proved disproportionately extensive, Simeon's inheritance was taken from within Judah's territory; thus the Simeonites received their portion in the midst of Judah's land.
The third lot came up for the Zebulunites according to their clans, and the boundary of their inheritance extended to Sarid.
From there it ascended to the sea, reaching Maralah; it touched Dabbasheth and extended to the brook east of Jokneam.
Turning east from Sarid toward the sunrise, it reached the border of Chisloth-tabor, extended to Daberath, and ascended to Japhia.
Thence it crossed eastward to Gath-hepher and Eth-kazin, came out at Rimmon, and turned toward Neah.
The border then curved northward around Hannathon, and its termini were the Valley of Iphtah-el.
The inheritance further included Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem—twelve cities with their villages.
These cities and villages constituted the inheritance of the Zebulunites according to their clans.
The fourth lot issued for Issachar, for its clans.
Their territory embraced Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem,
The boundary touched Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth-shemesh, and its terminus was the Jordan—sixteen cities with their villages.
These cities and villages were the inheritance of the Issacharites according to their clans.
The fifth lot came out for the tribe of Asher according to its clans.
Their territory included Helkath, Hali, Beten, and Achshaph;
Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal. On the west it touched Carmel and Shihor-libnath.
Turning eastward toward Beth-dagon, it touched Zebulun and the Valley of Iphtah-el on the north, then Beth-emek and Neiel, and extended to Cabul on the left.
It further reached Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Greater Sidon.
The boundary then turned to Ramah and the fortified city of Tyre; turning again to Hosah, it terminated at the sea in the region of Achzib,
together with Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob—twenty-two cities with their villages.
These cities and villages were the inheritance of the Asherites according to their clans.
The sixth lot issued for the Naphtalites according to their clans.
Their boundary ran from Heleph, from the oak at Zaanannim, through Adami-nekeb and Jabneel, to Lakkum, and its terminus was the Jordan.
The boundary then turned westward to Aznoth-tabor and went out to Hukkok; it touched Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan on the east.
The fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Chinnereth,
Iron, Migdal-el, Horem, Beth-anath, and Beth-shemesh—nineteen cities with their villages.
These cities and villages were the inheritance of the Naphtalites according to their clans.
The seventh lot came out for the tribe of Dan according to its clans.
The territory of their inheritance included Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir-shemesh,
Me-jarkon and Rakkon, with the territory facing Joppa.

When the territory of the Danites proved too small for them, they went up and fought against Leshem, captured it, struck it with the sword, took possession of it, settled in it, and called Leshem Dan, after the name of their ancestor Dan.
These cities and villages were the inheritance of the Danites according to their clans.
When the Israelites had finished allotting the land according to its boundaries, they gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them.
By the command of the LORD, they gave him the city he requested—Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He rebuilt the city and settled in it.

These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the Israelite tribes allotted by lot at Shiloh before the LORD, at the entrance to the tent of meeting. Thus they finished dividing the land.
Then the the LORD spoke to Joshua, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and declare, ‘Appoint for yourselves the cities of refuge, concerning which I spoke to you through Moses,
so that the manslayer who strikes down a life inadvertently, without knowledge, may flee thither; and they shall constitute for you an asylum from the avenger of blood.

He shall flee to one of these cities, take his stand at the portal of the city gate, and plead his case in the hearing of that city’s elders; then they shall receive him into the city, allot him a dwelling, and he shall reside among them.
Should the avenger of blood pursue him, they must not surrender the manslayer into his hand, because he struck his neighbor unwittingly and had not been his enemy beforehand.

He shall dwell in that city until he stands in judgment before the congregation, and until the death of the high priest who shall serve in those days; thereafter the manslayer may return to his own city and house, to the city from which he fled.’”
They consecrated Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba—that is, Hebron—in the hill country of Judah.

Beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho, they gave Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau, from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.

These cities were designated for all the Israelites and for the resident alien dwelling among them, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally might flee there and not die at the hand of the avenger of blood before standing before the congregation.
Then the heads of the ancestral houses of the Levites approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the Israelite tribes.
At Shiloh in the land of Canaan they said to them, “The LORD commanded through Moses that cities be given to us for habitation, together with their pasturelands for our livestock.”
So, by the command of the LORD, the Israelites gave the Levites these cities and their pasturelands out of their own inheritance.

The first lot fell to the Kohathite families; the descendants of Aaron the priest, who were among the Levites, received by lot from the tribe of Judah, from the tribe of Simeon, and from the tribe of Benjamin thirteen cities.
The remaining Kohathites received by lot, from the families of the tribe of Ephraim, from the tribe of Dan, and from the half-tribe of Manasseh, ten cities.
The Gershonites received by lot, from the families of the tribe of Issachar, from the tribe of Asher, from the tribe of Naphtali, and from the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities.
The Merarites, according to their families, received from the tribe of Reuben, from the tribe of Gad, and from the tribe of Zebulun twelve cities.
Thus the Israelites gave these cities and their pasturelands to the Levites by lot, exactly as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
From the tribe of Judah and from the tribe of Simeon they gave these cities, which are designated by name,
to the descendants of Aaron, who belonged to the Kohathite clans of Levi, because the first lot had fallen to them.
They assigned them Kiriath-arba—Arba being the father of Anak—which is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, together with the pasturelands around it.
But the city’s fields and its outlying villages were given to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his possession.
To the descendants of Aaron the priest they gave Hebron—the city of refuge for the manslayer—with its pasturelands, and Libnah with its pasturelands,
Jattir with its pasturelands, Eshtemoa with its pasturelands,
Holon with its pasturelands, Debir with its pasturelands,
Ain with its pasturelands, Juttah with its pasturelands, and Beth-shemesh with its pasturelands—nine cities from these two tribes.
From the tribe of Benjamin: Gibeon with its pasturelands, Geba with its pasturelands,
Anathoth with its pasturelands, and Almon with its pasturelands—four cities.
All the cities of the descendants of Aaron the priests were thirteen cities with their pasturelands.
The rest of the Kohathite families among the Levites had cities allotted to them from the tribe of Ephraim.
They were given Shechem—the city of refuge for the manslayer—in the hill country of Ephraim, with its pasturelands, and Gezer with its pasturelands,
Kibzaim with its pasturelands, and Beth-horon with its pasturelands: four cities.
From the tribe of Dan: Eltekeh with its pasturelands, Gibbethon with its pasturelands,
Aijalon with its pasturelands, Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands: four cities.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh: Tanach with its pasturelands, and Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands: two cities.
All the cities for the rest of the Kohathite families were ten, with their pasturelands.

To the Gershonites among the Levitical families, from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan—the city of refuge for the manslayer—with its pasturelands, and Be-eshterah with its pasturelands: two cities.
From the tribe of Issachar: Kishion with its pasturelands, Daberath with its pasturelands,
Jarmuth with its pasturelands, En-gannim with its pasturelands: four cities.
From the tribe of Asher: Mishal with its pasturelands, Abdon with its pasturelands,
Helkath with its pasturelands, Rehob with its pasturelands: four cities.
From the tribe of Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee—the city of refuge for the manslayer—with its pasturelands, Hammoth-dor with its pasturelands, and Kartan with its pasturelands: three cities.
All the cities of the Gershonites by their families were thirteen, with their pasturelands.
To the remaining Levites, the families of the Merarites: from the tribe of Zebulun, Jokneam with its pasturelands, Kartah with its pasturelands,
Dimnah with its pasturelands, Nahalal with its pasturelands: four cities.
From the tribe of Reuben: Bezer with its pasturelands, Jahaz with its pasturelands,
Kedemoth with its pasturelands, Mephaath with its pasturelands: four cities.
From the tribe of Gad: Ramoth in Gilead—the city of refuge for the manslayer—with its pasturelands, Mahanaim with its pasturelands,
Heshbon with its pasturelands, Jazer with its pasturelands: four cities.
All the cities for the Merarite families, which remained of the Levitical families, were twelve.
All the cities of the Levites within the possession of the Israelites were forty-eight cities with their pasturelands.
Each of these cities had its pasturelands around it; so it was with all these cities.
Thus the LORD gave Israel all the land that He had sworn to give to their fathers; they took possession of it and settled in it.
And the LORD gave them rest on every side, just as He had sworn to their fathers; no man among all their enemies could stand against them, and the LORD delivered all their enemies into their hand.
Not one of all the good promises that the LORD had spoken to the house of Israel failed; everything came to pass.
Then Joshua summoned the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh,
and said to them, "You have kept all that Moses, the servant of the LORD, commanded you, and you have obeyed my voice in all that I commanded you.
You have not deserted your brothers these many days; rather, you have kept the charge of the commandment of the LORD your God.

And now the LORD your God has given rest to your brothers, as He promised them. So now turn and go to your tents, to the land of your possession, which Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave you beyond the Jordan.

Above all, be exceedingly vigilant to observe the commandment and the law that Moses, the servant of the LORD, commanded you: to love the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, to keep His commandments, to hold fast to Him, and to serve Him with all your heart and all your soul."
So Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their tents.

To the half-tribe of Manasseh Moses had given an inheritance in Bashan, while Joshua gave the other half an inheritance west of the Jordan among their brothers. When Joshua sent them to their tents, he blessed them,
saying, "Return to your tents with great wealth—with very many livestock, with silver, gold, bronze, iron, and an abundance of garments. Share the spoils of your enemies with your brothers."

Thus the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh departed from the Israelites at Shiloh in Canaan and set out for Gilead, the land of their possession, which they had acquired in accordance with the command of the LORD through Moses.
When they came to Geliloth of the Jordan in Canaan, the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar there by the Jordan—an altar of formidable size and imposing appearance.
The Israelites heard that the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had built an altar on the border of Canaan at Geliloth of the Jordan, on the Israelite side.
When the whole congregation of Israel heard of it, they assembled at Shiloh to march against them in war.
The Israelites sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to Gilead, to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh,
together with ten leaders—one leader from each ancestral house, a leader for every tribe of Israel, each the head of an ancestral house among the clans of Israel.
They went to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead and spoke to them, saying:

"Thus says the whole congregation of the LORD: What is this treachery that you have committed today against the God of Israel by turning away from the LORD and building an altar for yourselves, so that you might rebel against the LORD?
Is the iniquity of Peor not enough for us—a sin from which we have not been cleansed to this day, even though a plague struck the congregation of the LORD?
And now you would turn away from the LORD? If you rebel against the LORD today, He will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel tomorrow.

If, however, the land of your possession is unclean, then cross over into the land of the LORD's possession, where the LORD's tabernacle dwells, and take possession among us. But do not rebel against the LORD, nor against us, by building an altar for yourselves besides the altar of the LORD our God.
Did not Achan son of Zerah commit a trespass in the devoted things, so that wrath fell upon the whole congregation of Israel? And he was but one man; yet he did not perish alone for his iniquity."
Then the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the leaders of the clans of Israel:
"The LORD, the God of gods—the LORD, the God of gods—He knows, and Israel will know. If this was rebellion or breach of faith against the LORD, do not spare us today.

If we have built this altar in order to turn away from the LORD, or to offer burnt offerings or grain offerings upon it, or to sacrifice fellowship offerings upon it, then let the LORD Himself require it.
"But we did it out of anxious solicitude, fearing that in days to come your descendants might say to our descendants, 'What claim do you have upon the LORD, the God of Israel?

For the LORD has made the Jordan a boundary between us and you, O Reubenites and Gadites! You have no portion in the LORD.' So your descendants might cause our descendants to abandon the fear of the LORD.
"Therefore we said, 'Let us build an altar—not for burnt offerings or sacrifices—

but as a witness between us and you and the generations after us, that we may perform the service of the LORD in His presence with our burnt offerings, sacrifices, and peace offerings, so that your descendants will not say to our descendants in the future, "You have no portion in the LORD." '.

"And we thought, 'If they ever say this to us or to our descendants, we will reply, "Look at the pattern of the LORD's altar that our fathers made—not for burnt offerings or sacrifices, but as a witness between us and you."'

Far be it from us to rebel against the LORD or to turn away from Him today by building an altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings, or sacrifices, other than the altar of the LORD our God that stands before His tabernacle."

When Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the congregation and the heads of the clans of Israel who were with him heard the words that the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had spoken, it pleased them.

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, "Today we know that the LORD is among us, because you have not committed this breach of faith against the LORD. Now you have delivered the Israelites from the LORD's wrath."
Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders returned from Gilead to Canaan, to the Israelites, and reported to them.
The matter pleased the Israelites, and they praised God; and they did not speak of going up against them in war to destroy the land in which the Reubenites and Gadites dwelt.
The Reubenites and Gadites named the altar "Witness," for they said, "It is a witness between us that the LORD is God."
After a long time had passed since the LORD had granted Israel repose from all their surrounding enemies, Joshua had grown old and advanced in years.
Joshua summoned all Israel—its elders, leaders, judges, and officers—and addressed them: “I have grown old and advanced in years.
“You have witnessed everything the LORD your God has wrought upon all these nations for your sake; indeed, it is the LORD your God who has waged war on your behalf.
“Behold, I have apportioned to you, by your tribes, the surviving nations together with all the peoples I have extirpated from the Jordan to the Great Sea in the west.
“The LORD your God Himself will drive them out before you and dispossess them; you shall inherit their land, precisely as the LORD your God has pledged to you.
“Be exceedingly steadfast, then, in observing and performing all that is inscribed in the Book of the Law of Moses, so that you do not turn aside from it either to the right or to the left.
“Do not commingle with these surviving nations that dwell among you; do not invoke the names of their deities, nor swear by them, nor render them service, nor bow down to them.
“Rather, cleave to the LORD your God, as you have done hitherto.
“For the LORD has dispossessed before you nations great and formidable; to this day no human being has withstood you.
“A single one of you shall put a thousand to flight, because the LORD your God Himself is the One who wages war on your behalf, just as He has declared to you.
“Be exceedingly vigilant over your souls, then, in loving the LORD your God.
“For if you turn back and attach yourselves to the remnant of these nations that still dwell among you, and contract marriages with them, entering into their midst as they enter into yours,

“then know with certainty that the LORD your God will no longer dispossess these nations before you; instead, they shall become a snare and a trap to you, a scourge at your sides and barbs in your eyes, until you vanish from this good land that the LORD your God has bestowed upon you.

“Behold, I am this day proceeding along the way of all the earth; and you know, with all your heart and all your soul, that not a single word among all the good promises the LORD your God spoke concerning you has failed—every one of them has been fulfilled for you; not one has fallen.

“And just as every good thing the LORD your God promised you has come to pass, so too will the LORD bring upon you every calamity He has threatened, until He has eradicated you from this good land that the LORD your God has granted you.

“If you violate the covenant of the LORD your God that He enjoined upon you, and go to serve other gods and bow down to them, then the LORD's wrath will blaze against you, and you will swiftly perish from the good land He has given you.”
Then Joshua assembled all the tribes of Israel at Shechem. He summoned the elders, leaders, judges, and officers of Israel, and they presented themselves before God.

Joshua said to all the people, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Long ago your fathers, including Terah, the father of Abraham and Nahor, lived beyond the Euphrates and worshiped other gods.
‘But I took your father Abraham from beyond the Euphrates and led him throughout all the land of Canaan and multiplied his descendants. I gave him Isaac,
and to Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Seir to possess, but Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
‘Then I sent Moses and Aaron, and I afflicted the Egyptians by what I did there, and afterward I brought you out.
When I brought your fathers out of Egypt and you came to the sea, the Egyptians pursued them with chariots and horsemen as far as the Red Sea.

So your fathers cried out to the LORD, and He put darkness between you and the Egyptians; He brought the sea over them and covered them. Your own eyes saw what I did to the Egyptians. Then you lived in the wilderness for a long time.

‘Later I brought you to the land of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan. They fought against you, but I gave them into your hands, so that you took possession of their land and destroyed them before you.
Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, set out to fight against Israel. He sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse you,
but I refused to listen to Balaam. So he blessed you again and again, and I delivered you from his hand.

‘Then you crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The citizens of Jericho fought against you, as did the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites, but I gave them into your hands.
I sent the hornet ahead of you, and it drove out the two Amorite kings before you—not by your sword or bow.
I gave you a land on which you did not toil and cities you did not build, and you live in them; you are eating from vineyards and olive groves you did not plant.’ ”
“Now therefore fear the LORD and serve Him in sincerity and truth. Put away the gods your fathers served beyond the Euphrates and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.

But if it is unpleasing in your sight to serve the LORD, then choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve, whether the gods your fathers served beyond the Euphrates, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you live. But as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.”
The people answered, “Far be it from us to forsake the LORD to serve other gods!

For the LORD our God is He who brought us and our fathers up out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, and performed these great signs before our eyes. He protected us on our entire journey and among all the nations through which we traveled.
And the LORD drove out before us all the peoples, including the Amorites who lived in the land. We too will serve the LORD, because He is our God.”
But Joshua said to the people, “You are not able to serve the LORD, for He is a holy God; He is a jealous God; He will not forgive your rebellion or your sins.
If you forsake the LORD and serve foreign gods, He will turn and bring disaster on you and consume you, after He has been good to you.”
“No!” the people replied. “We will serve the LORD.”
Then Joshua said to the people, “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen to serve the LORD.” “We are witnesses!” they replied.
“Now, then,” Joshua said, “get rid of the foreign gods among you and incline your hearts to the LORD, the God of Israel.”
The people said to Joshua, “We will serve the LORD our God and obey His voice.”
On that day Joshua made a covenant for the people and established for them a statute and ordinance at Shechem.
Joshua recorded these things in the Book of the Law of God. Then he took a large stone and set it up there under the oak that was by the sanctuary of the LORD.

And Joshua said to all the people, “Behold, this stone will be a witness against us, for it has heard all the words the LORD spoke to us. Therefore it will be a witness against you, so that you do not deny your God.”
Then Joshua dismissed the people, each to his own inheritance.
After these things, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of one hundred and ten.
They buried him in the territory of his inheritance at Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
Israel served the LORD throughout the lifetime of Joshua and of the elders who outlived him and who had known all the works that the LORD had done for Israel.

And the bones of Joseph, which the Israelites had brought up from Egypt, were buried at Shechem in the plot of ground that Jacob had bought from the sons of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for a hundred pieces of silver. And it became an inheritance of Joseph’s descendants.
Eleazar son of Aaron died, and they buried him at Gibeah, which had been given to his son Phinehas, in the hill country of Ephraim.
After Joshua's death, the Israelites sought direction from the LORD, saying, "Who shall first ascend on our behalf against the Canaanites to wage war against them?"
The LORD replied, "Judah shall go up; behold, I have consigned the land into his hand."

Judah said to Simeon his brother, "Ascend with me into my allotted inheritance, and let us make war upon the Canaanites; I, in turn, will accompany you into your allotted inheritance." So Simeon went with him.
Judah ascended, and the LORD delivered the Canaanite and the Perizzite into their hand; they struck down ten thousand men at Bezek.
They found Adoni-bezek at Bezek, fought against him, and struck the Canaanite and the Perizzite.
Adoni-bezek fled, but they pursued and apprehended him, and amputated the thumbs of his hands and his great toes.

Adoni-bezek said, "Seventy kings, with the thumbs of their hands and their great toes amputated, used to scavenge scraps beneath my table. As I have done, so God has requited me." Then they brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
The sons of Judah fought against Jerusalem, captured it, struck it with the edge of the sword, and consigned the city to fire.
Afterward the sons of Judah descended to fight against the Canaanites dwelling in the hill country, the Negev, and the Shephelah.
Judah went against the Canaanites dwelling in Hebron (formerly Kiriath-arba) and struck Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
From there he went against the inhabitants of Debir (formerly Kiriath-sepher).
Caleb said, "Whoever strikes Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give him my daughter Achsah as wife."
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, captured it; and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as wife.
When she arrived, she incited him to ask her father for a field; and as she dismounted from the donkey, Caleb said to her, "What is your request?"
She said to him, "Grant me a favor: since you have given me land in the Negev, give me also springs of water." So Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.

The descendants of Moses' father-in-law, the Kenite, ascended with the sons of Judah from the City of Palms into the wilderness of Judah, which lies in the Negev of Arad; and they went and dwelt among the people.
Judah went with Simeon his brother; they struck the Canaanites inhabiting Zephath and devoted it to destruction, calling the city Hormah.
Judah captured Gaza and its territory, Ashkelon and its territory, and Ekron and its territory.
The LORD was with Judah, and he took possession of the hill country; yet he could not dispossess the inhabitants of the plain, because they possessed iron chariots.
They gave Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had spoken, and he drove out from there the three sons of Anak.
The sons of Benjamin did not dispossess the Jebusites inhabiting Jerusalem; so the Jebusites dwell with the sons of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
The house of Joseph also ascended against Bethel, and the LORD was with them.
The house of Joseph spied out Bethel (formerly called Luz).
The spies saw a man emerging from the city and said to him, "Show us the entrance to the city, and we will deal kindly with you."
He showed them the entrance, and they struck the city with the edge of the sword; yet they spared the man and all his family.
The man went to the land of the Hittites, built a city, and named it Luz; that remains its name to this day.
Manasseh did not dispossess Beth-shean and its towns, Taanach and its towns, Dor and its towns, Ibleam and its towns, or Megiddo and its towns; the Canaanites persisted in dwelling in that land.
When Israel grew strong, they subjected the Canaanites to forced labor, but they did not utterly dispossess them.
Ephraim did not dispossess the Canaanites dwelling in Gezer; the Canaanites dwelt among them in Gezer.
Zebulun did not dispossess the inhabitants of Kitron and Nahalol; the Canaanites dwelt among them and became forced labor.
Asher did not dispossess the inhabitants of Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob.
The Asherites dwelt among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, for they did not dispossess them.

Naphtali did not dispossess the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath; Naphtali dwelt among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, and the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath became forced labor for them.
The Amorites confined the Danites to the hill country and would not permit them to descend into the plain.
The Amorites persisted in dwelling in Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim; yet the house of Joseph prevailed, and they became forced labor.
The border of the Amorites ran from the ascent of Akrabbim, from the rock, and upward.

The Angel of the LORD ascended from Gilgal to Bochim and declared, “I brought you up out of Egypt and brought you into the land that I swore to your fathers, and I said, ‘I will never break My covenant with you.’
You shall make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land; you shall tear down their altars. But you have not obeyed My voice. What is this that you have done?
So I also said, ‘I will not drive them out before you; instead, they shall be a continual source of distress to you, and their gods shall become a snare for you.’”
When the Angel of the LORD spoke these words to all the Israelites, the people raised a great cry and wept.
Accordingly, they named that place Bochim, and there they offered sacrifice to the LORD.
Upon Joshua's dismissal of the people, the Israelites departed, each to his own inheritance, to take possession of the land.
The people served the LORD throughout the days of Joshua and throughout the days of the elders who survived Joshua, those who had witnessed all the great works that the LORD had wrought for Israel.
Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of one hundred and ten years.
They interred him within the bounds of his inheritance at Timnath-heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
That entire generation was gathered to its fathers, and a subsequent generation arose that knew neither the LORD nor the work that He had accomplished for Israel.
The Israelites perpetrated evil in the sight of the LORD and served the Baals.

They abandoned the LORD, the God of their fathers, who had led them out of the land of Egypt, and pursued other gods from among the gods of the neighboring peoples, prostrating themselves before them; thus they provoked the LORD.
They abandoned the LORD and served Baal and the Ashtoreths.

Therefore the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and He delivered them into the hands of plunderers, who despoiled them; He sold them into the hands of their enemies on every side, so that they could no longer withstand their foes.
Wherever they marched forth, the hand of the LORD was against them for calamity, as the LORD had declared and as He had sworn to them; and they were sorely distressed.
Then the LORD raised up judges, who delivered them from the hand of those who plundered them.

Yet they did not heed their judges, for they were unfaithful, pursuing other gods and bowing down to them; they swiftly deviated from the path their fathers had trodden in obeying the commandments of the LORD; they did not act accordingly.

Whenever the LORD raised up a judge for them, the LORD was with that judge and delivered them from the hand of their enemies throughout the judge's days; for the LORD was moved to pity by their groaning on account of those who oppressed and crushed them.

But upon the judge's death, they reverted and behaved even more corruptly than their fathers, going after other gods to serve them and bow down to them; they did not relinquish any of their practices or their obstinate course.
So the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and He said, “Because this nation has transgressed My covenant that I commanded their fathers and has not obeyed My voice,
I will no longer expel before them any of the nations that Joshua left when he died,
in order to test Israel, whether they will preserve the way of the LORD by walking in it, as their fathers preserved it.”
Thus the LORD left those nations, not expelling them at once, and He did not deliver them into Joshua's hand.
These are the nations that the the LORD left in place to test Israel through them—namely, all who had not known the entirety of Canaan's wars.
He did so only that the successive generations of Israel's sons might acquire martial knowledge, instructing those who had not previously known such conflicts.
These included the five Philistine lords, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites inhabiting Mount Lebanon from Mount Baal-hermon to the approach to Hamath.
They remained to test Israel, to ascertain whether Israel would heed the commandments of the the LORD, which He had enjoined upon their ancestors through Moses.
The Israelites settled among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
They married the daughters of those peoples and gave their own daughters to the sons of those peoples, and thereby served their gods.
The Israelites perpetrated evil in the the LORD's estimation: they forgot the the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs.
Consequently the the LORD's anger burned against Israel, and He sold them into the power of Cushan-rishathaim, king of Aram-naharaim; the Israelites served him for eight years.
When the Israelites cried out to the the LORD, He raised up a deliverer for them—Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother—who saved them.
The Spirit of the the LORD came upon him; he judged Israel and went out to battle. The the LORD gave Cushan-rishathaim, king of Aram, into his hand, and his hand overpowered Cushan-rishathaim.
The land then enjoyed rest for forty years, until Othniel son of Kenaz died.
The Israelites once more perpetrated evil in the the LORD's estimation; therefore the the LORD emboldened Eglon, king of Moab, against Israel, because they had done evil in the the LORD's estimation.
He mustered the Ammonites and Amalekites, marched against Israel, defeated them, and occupied the City of Palms.
Thus the Israelites served Eglon, king of Moab, for eighteen years.
When the Israelites cried out to the the LORD, He raised up a deliverer for them—Ehud son of Gera, a Benjamite, a left-handed man—and through him the Israelites sent tribute to Eglon, king of Moab.
Ehud fashioned for himself a double-edged dagger roughly a cubit in length and secured it beneath his clothing upon his right thigh.
He presented the tribute to Eglon, king of Moab, who was an exceedingly corpulent man.
When he had finished presenting the tribute, he dismissed the men who had carried it.
He, however, turned back from the carved images near Gilgal and said, “I have a confidential message for you, O king.” The king replied, “Silence,” and all his attendants withdrew.
Ehud approached him while he was sitting alone in his private, cool upper chamber, and said, “I have a message from God for you.” The king rose from his seat.
Ehud extended his left hand, drew the dagger from his right thigh, and plunged it into Eglon's abdomen.
Even the hilt followed the blade into the wound, and the fat closed over it, so that he could not extract the weapon from his belly; and Eglon's bowels discharged.
Ehud then exited through the vestibule, closed the doors of the upper chamber behind him, and locked them.
After he had gone out, his servants arrived and found the doors of the chamber locked; they surmised that he was relieving himself in the cool room.
They waited until embarrassment overcame them, but he did not open the chamber doors; so they took the key, opened them, and discovered their lord fallen dead upon the floor.
Ehud escaped while they delayed; he passed beyond the carved images and fled to Seirah.
When he arrived, he sounded the trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim; the Israelites descended with him from the hill, with him leading them.

He said to them, “Follow me, for the the LORD has delivered your enemies, the Moabites, into your hand.” They descended after him, seized the fords of the Jordan against Moab, and allowed no one to cross.
At that time they struck down about ten thousand Moabites, all robust and valiant men; not one escaped.
Thus Moab was subdued under Israel's hand that day, and the land enjoyed rest for eighty years.
After him came Shamgar son of Anath, who struck down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad and likewise delivered Israel.
After Ehud died, the Israelites again acted wickedly in the sight of the LORD.
So the LORD delivered them into the power of Jabin, king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; the commander of his army was Sisera, who dwelt in Harosheth-hagoyim.
Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, for Jabin possessed nine hundred iron chariots and had cruelly oppressed the Israelites for twenty years.
At that time Deborah, a prophetess and the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel.
She used to sit beneath the palm of Deborah, between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites would come up to her for judgment.

She sent for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali and said to him, “Has not the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded you: ‘Go, advance toward Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun’?”
“I will draw Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, with his chariots and his multitude, to you at the Brook Kishon, and I will deliver him into your hand.”
Barak said to her, “If you go with me, I will go; but if you do not go with me, I will not go.”

She replied, “I will surely go with you; nevertheless, the honor of the journey you are undertaking will not be yours, for the LORD will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.” Then Deborah arose and went with Barak to Kedesh.
Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali at Kedesh, and ten thousand men went up after him; Deborah went up with him.
Now Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites, the descendants of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law, and had pitched his tent as far as the oak in Zaanannim, near Kedesh.
When Sisera was told that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor,
he summoned all his chariots—nine hundred iron chariots—and all the people with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the Brook Kishon.

Deborah said to Barak, “Arise, for this is the day the LORD has given Sisera into your hand. Has not the LORD gone out before you?” So Barak went down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men following him.
The LORD routed Sisera and all his chariots and army before Barak by the sword, and Sisera alighted from his chariot and fled on foot.
Barak pursued the chariots and the army to Harosheth-hagoyim, and all of Sisera's army fell by the sword; not one survived.
Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
Jael went out to meet Sisera and said to him, “Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me; do not be afraid.” So he turned aside to her into the tent, and she covered him with a blanket.
He said to her, “Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty.” So she opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him.
He said to her, “Stand at the entrance of the tent, and if anyone comes and asks you, ‘Is there a man here?’ you shall say, ‘No.’”
He was sound asleep and exhausted. Then Jael, Heber's wife, took a tent peg and a hammer in her hand, went stealthily to him, drove the peg into his temple until it sank into the ground, and he died.
As Barak pursued Sisera, Jael came out to meet him and said, “Come, and I will show you the man you are seeking.” He went in to her, and there lay Sisera dead, with the tent peg in his temple.
Thus on that day God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the Israelites.
The hand of the Israelites pressed ever harder against Jabin king of Canaan until they had destroyed Jabin king of Canaan.
On that very day Deborah and Barak, son of Abinoam, intoned this canticle, declaring:
“When the chieftains take the vanguard in Israel, and the populace freely consecrates itself to the fray, extol the LORD.
Hear, O kings; give ear, O rulers! I myself will sing to the LORD; I will make melody to the LORD, the God of Israel.”
“The LORD, when You went out from Seir, when You marched from the field of Edom, the earth trembled, the heavens dripped, and even the clouds poured down water.
The mountains quaked before the LORD, indeed, this Sinai before the LORD, the God of Israel.”
“In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were deserted, and travelers walked by crooked paths.
The villages failed in Israel; they failed until I, Deborah, arose—until I arose as a mother in Israel.”
“When they chose new gods, warfare reached the city gates, and neither shield nor spear appeared among forty thousand in Israel.
My heart is with the commanders of Israel, who offered themselves willingly among the people. Bless the LORD!”
“You who ride upon white donkeys, You who repose upon saddle carpets, and You who traverse the road—give voice!

At the sound of archers among the watering places, there they recount the righteous acts of the LORD, the righteous acts of His rural folk in Israel. Then the people of the LORD came down to the gates.”
“Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, utter a song! Arise, Barak, and lead away your captives, son of Abinoam.
Then the remnant came down to the nobles; the people of the LORD came down for me against the mighty.”
“From Ephraim came those whose root is in Amalek; after you, Benjamin, amid your clans. From Machir came down commanders, and from Zebulun those who bear the marshal's staff.
The princes of Issachar were with Deborah; yes, Issachar was with Barak, sent into the valley at his feet. Among the clans of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.
Why did you sit among the sheepfolds, to hear the whistling for the flocks? Among the clans of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.”
“Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan; and Dan—why did he linger by the ships? Asher sat still at the coast of the sea, dwelling by its inlets.
Zebulun was a people who jeopardized their lives unto death, and Naphtali upon the high places of the field.”
“The kings came and fought; then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo; they seized no silver as spoil.
From heaven the stars fought; from their courses they fought against Sisera.
The torrent Kishon swept them away, the ancient torrent, the torrent Kishon. O my soul, march on in strength!
Then the horses' hooves thundered from the galloping, the galloping of his chargers.
The angel of the LORD pronounces a bitter curse upon Meroz and its inhabitants, because they did not come to the help of the LORD, to the help of the LORD among the mighty.”
“Most blessed among women is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite; blessed is she in the tent above women.
He asked for water, and she gave him milk; she brought him curds in a princely bowl.
She put her hand to the tent peg, and her right hand to the workmen's hammer; she struck Sisera, she crushed his head, she shattered and pierced his temple.
Between her feet he bowed, he fell, he lay; between her feet he bowed, he fell; where he bowed, there he fell down ruined.”

The song then turns to Sisera's mother, who looks out through the window and cries through the lattice: “Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why tarry the hoofbeats of his chariots?” Her wise attendants answer, and she herself replies:
“Are they not finding and dividing the plunder—a girl or two for every warrior; dyed garments for Sisera, embroidered garments for the necks of the captives?”
The song concludes: “So may all Your enemies perish, O the LORD! But may those who love You be like the sun when it rises in its might.” And the land had rest for forty years.
Again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD, so the LORD gave them into the hand of Midian for seven years.
The hand of Midian prevailed against Israel; and because of the Midianites the Israelites made for themselves the dens that are in the mountains, and the caves and the strongholds.
Whenever Israel sowed, the Midianites, the Amalekites, and the sons of the East would come up against them.
They would encamp against them as far as Gaza and destroy the produce of the land, leaving Israel no sustenance—neither sheep, nor ox, nor donkey.
For they came up with their livestock and their tents in such multitudes as locusts, and both they and their camels were without number; and they entered the land to despoil it.
Thus Israel was brought very low because of Midian, and the Israelites cried out to the LORD.
When the Israelites cried out to the LORD because of Midian,
the LORD sent a prophet to the Israelites, who said to them, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'I brought you up from Egypt and brought you out of the house of slavery.
I delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all your oppressors; I drove them out before you and gave you their land.
I said to you, "You shall not fear the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell," but you have not listened to My voice.'"
The angel of the LORD came and sat under the oak in Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite, while his son Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress to hide it from the Midianites.
The angel of the LORD appeared to him and said, "The LORD is with you, O mighty man of valor."

Gideon said to him, "Please, my lord, if the LORD is with us, why then has all this happened to us? And where are all His wondrous works that our fathers recounted to us, saying, 'Did not the LORD bring us up from Egypt?' But now the LORD has forsaken us and given us into the hand of Midian."
Then the LORD turned to him and said, "Go in this strength of yours and deliver Israel from the hand of Midian. Have I not sent you?"
He said to Him, "Please, my Lord, how can I save Israel? Behold, my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house."
The LORD said to him, "Surely I will be with you, and you shall strike the Midianites as one man."
Gideon said to Him, "If now I have found favor in Your sight, then show me a sign that it is You who speak with me.
Please do not depart from here until I come to You and bring out my offering and set it before You." And He said, "I will stay until you return."

So Gideon went in and prepared a young goat and unleavened cakes from an ephah of flour; he put the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot, and brought them out to Him under the oak and presented them.
The angel of God said to him, "Take the meat and the unleavened cakes and lay them on this rock, and pour out the broth." And he did so.

Then the angel of the LORD stretched out the tip of the staff that was in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened cakes; and fire sprang up from the rock and consumed the meat and the cakes, and the angel of the LORD disappeared from his sight.
When Gideon perceived that it was the angel of the LORD, he said, "Alas, O Lord, the LORD! For now I have seen the angel of the LORD face to face."
The LORD said to him, "Peace be to you; do not fear; you shall not die."
So Gideon built an altar there to the LORD and called it, "The LORD Is Peace." To this day it stands in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
That night the LORD said to him, "Take your father's bull, the second bull seven years old, and pull down the altar of Baal that your father has, and cut down the Asherah that is beside it.
Then build an altar to the LORD your God on the top of this stronghold in due order, and take the second bull and offer it as a burnt offering with the wood of the Asherah that you cut down."

So Gideon took ten men from among his servants and did as the LORD had told him; but because he feared his father's household and the men of the city, he could not do it by day, so he did it by night.
When the men of the city arose early in the morning, behold, the altar of Baal was torn down, the Asherah beside it was cut down, and the second bull was offered on the altar that had been built.
They said to one another, "Who has done this thing?" And when they inquired and searched, they said, "Gideon the son of Joash has done this thing."
Then the men of the city said to Joash, "Bring out your son, that he may die, because he has broken down the altar of Baal and because he has cut down the Asherah that was beside it."

But Joash said to all who stood against him, "Will you contend for Baal? Or will you save him? Whoever contends for him shall be put to death by morning. If he is a god, let him contend for himself, because his altar has been broken down."
Therefore on that day Gideon was called Jerubbaal, that is to say, "Let Baal contend against him," because he had broken down his altar.
Now all the Midianites and the Amalekites and the sons of the East gathered together; and they crossed over and encamped in the Valley of Jezreel.
But the Spirit of the LORD clothed Gideon, and he blew the trumpet, and the Abiezrites rallied to him.
He sent messengers throughout all Manasseh, and they too were gathered after him; he also sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they came up to meet them.
Then Gideon said to God, "If You will save Israel by my hand, as You have spoken,

behold, I am laying a fleece of wool on the threshing floor: if there is dew on the fleece alone, and it is dry on all the ground, then I shall know that You will save Israel by my hand, as You have spoken."
And it was so; for when he rose early the next morning and squeezed the fleece, he wrung out dew from the fleece, a bowlful of water.
Then Gideon said to God, "Let not Your anger burn against me, but let me speak once more: please let it be dry on the fleece alone, and on all the ground let there be dew."
And God did so that night; it was dry on the fleece alone, and on all the ground there was dew.
Jerubbaal—that is, Gideon—and all the troops accompanying him rose early and encamped beside the spring of Harod, while the Midianite host lay to the north in the valley near the hill of Moreh.
Then the LORD said to Gideon, "The people with you are too numerous for Me to deliver Midian into your hand, lest Israel vaunt itself against Me, saying, 'My own hand has saved me.'"

Now therefore proclaim in the hearing of the people, "Whoever is fearful and trembling, let him turn back and depart from Mount Gilead." So twenty-two thousand of the people returned, and ten thousand remained.

And the LORD said to Gideon, "The people are still too many; bring them down to the water, and I will test them for you there. Everyone of whom I say, 'This one shall go with you,' shall go with you, and everyone of whom I say, 'This one shall not go with you,' shall not go."

So he brought the people down to the water, and the LORD said to Gideon, "Everyone who laps the water with his tongue, as a dog laps, you shall set apart by himself; likewise everyone who kneels down to drink."
The number of those who lapped, putting their hand to their mouth, was three hundred men; but all the rest of the people knelt down to drink water.
Then the LORD said to Gideon, "With the three hundred men who lapped I will save you, and I will give Midian into your hand; let all the other people go, each to his own place."

So the people took provisions in their hands, and their trumpets; and he sent all the rest of Israel away, each to his tent, but retained the three hundred men. Now the camp of Midian lay below him in the valley.
That same night the LORD said to him, "Arise, go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand."
But if you are afraid to go down, go down to the camp with Purah your servant,
and you shall hear what they say; then your hands will be strengthened, and you shall go down against the camp." So he went down with Purah his servant to the outposts of the armed men in the camp.
Now Midian and Amalek and all the sons of the East lay in the valley like locusts in multitude, and their camels were without number, like the sand on the seashore in multitude.

When Gideon came, behold, a man was telling a dream to his companion, and he said, "Behold, I dreamed a dream, and behold, a cake of barley bread tumbled into the camp of Midian and came to the tent; it struck the tent so that it fell, overturned it, and the tent lay flat."
His companion answered, "This is nothing other than the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, a man of Israel; God has given Midian and all the camp into his hand."

As soon as Gideon heard the telling of the dream and its interpretation, he worshipped; and he returned to the camp of Israel and said, "Arise, for the LORD has given the camp of Midian into your hand."
And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put a trumpet into the hand of each of them, and empty jars, with torches inside the jars.
And he said to them, "Watch me and do as I do; when I come to the edge of the camp, do as I do.
When I blow the trumpet, I and all who are with me, then you also blow the trumpets around the whole camp and shout, 'For the LORD and for Gideon!'"

So Gideon and the hundred men who were with him came to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, just as they had posted the watchmen; and they blew the trumpets and broke the jars that were in their hands.
