The servants of the king of Aram said to him, “Their god is a god of the hills; therefore they were stronger than we. But let us fight against them in the plain, and surely we shall be stronger than they.”
“Do this,” they advised: “remove the kings from their commands and appoint governors in their place.

Muster for yourself an army like the army that you lost, horse for horse and chariot for chariot, and fight against them in the plain; surely then you will be stronger than they.” He listened to their counsel and did so.
At the return of the year Ben-Hadad mustered Aram and went up to Aphek to fight against Israel.
The Israelites were mustered and provisioned, and they went to meet them; the Israelites encamped before them like two little flocks of goats, while Aram filled the land.

Then the man of God drew near to the king of Israel and said, “Thus says the the LORD: ‘Because Aram has said, “The the LORD is a god of the hills and not a god of the valleys,” I will give all this great multitude into your hand, and you shall know that I am the the LORD.’”
They encamped opposite one another for seven days, and on the seventh day the battle was joined; the Israelites struck down one hundred thousand foot soldiers of Aram in a single day.
The rest fled into the city of Aphek, and the wall fell upon twenty-seven thousand of those who remained. Ben-Hadad fled into the city and hid himself in an inner chamber.

His servants said to him, “Behold, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful kings. Let us put sackcloth on our loins and ropes on our heads and go out to the king of Israel; perhaps he will spare your life.”

So they girded sackcloth on their loins and put ropes on their heads, and they came to the king of Israel and said, “Your servant Ben-Hadad says, ‘Please let me live.’” He said, “Is he still alive? He is my brother.”

The men took it as a favorable omen and quickly seized upon his words, saying, “Yes, your brother Ben-Hadad.” Then he said, “Go, bring him.” Ben-Hadad came out to him, and Ahab had him mount the chariot.

Ben-Hadad said to him, “I will restore the cities that my father took from your father, and you shall have streets for yourself in Damascus, as my father had in Samaria; and I will let you go upon this covenant.” So Ahab made a covenant with him and let him go.
By the word of the the LORD, one of the sons of the prophets said to his companion, “Strike me, please.” But the man refused to strike him.

Then he said to him, “Because you did not obey the voice of the the LORD, behold, as soon as you depart from me a lion shall strike you down.” As soon as he departed from him, a lion found him and struck him down.
He found another man and said, “Strike me, please.” The man struck him and wounded him.
Then the prophet went and stood by the road, waiting for the king, having disguised himself with a bandage over his eyes.

As the king passed by, he cried out to the king, “Your servant went out into the midst of the battle, and behold, a man turned aside and brought a man to me and said, ‘Guard this man; if he is missing, your life shall be for his life, or else you shall pay a talent of silver.’”
“While your servant was busy here and there, he was gone.” The king of Israel said to him, “So shall your judgment be; you yourself have decided it.”
Then he hastily removed the bandage from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized him as one of the prophets.
He said to him, “Thus says the the LORD: ‘Because you have let go out of your hand the man whom I devoted to destruction, your life shall be for his life, and your people for his people.’”
The king of Israel went to his house sullen and vexed, and he came to Samaria.
Following these events, Naboth the Jezreelite possessed a vineyard in Jezreel, situated adjacent to the palace of Ahab, king of Samaria.

Ahab said to Naboth, "Grant me your vineyard, that I may convert it into a vegetable garden, for it lies near, beside my house; and I will give you a superior vineyard in exchange, or, if you prefer, I will remunerate you with its price in silver."
Naboth replied to Ahab, "The LORD forbid that I should surrender to you the inheritance of my fathers."

So Ahab entered his house sullen and resentful because of the word that Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him; he said, "I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers." Then he lay upon his bed, turned away his face, and refused to eat.
His wife Jezebel came to him and said, "Why is your spirit so dejected that you refuse food?"

He said to her, "Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him, 'Give me your vineyard for silver, or, if you prefer, I will give you another vineyard in its place,' and he said, 'I will not give you my vineyard.'"
Jezebel his wife said to him, "Do you now exercise sovereignty over Israel? Arise, eat, and let your heart be glad. I myself will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite."
Accordingly, she wrote letters in Ahab's name, sealed them with his seal, and dispatched them to the elders and nobles residing in Naboth's city.
In the letters she wrote, "Proclaim a fast, and set Naboth at the head of the people.
Set two scoundrels before him to testify against him, saying, 'You have cursed God and the king.' Then bring him out and stone him to death."
The men of his city, the elders and nobles who dwelt in his city, did as Jezebel had instructed them, precisely as it was written in the letters she had sent them.
They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people.

Then two scoundrels entered and sat opposite him; and these scoundrels testified against Naboth before the people, saying, "Naboth cursed God and the king." Thereupon they carried him outside the city and stoned him to death.
They sent word to Jezebel, saying, "Naboth has been stoned and is dead."

When Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and was dead, she said to Ahab, "Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for silver; for Naboth is no longer alive—he is dead."
When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he arose to go down and take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.
Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
"Arise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria; behold, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone down to take possession of it.

You shall speak to him, saying, 'Thus says the LORD: Have you murdered and also taken possession?' And you shall speak to him, saying, 'Thus says the LORD: In the place where the dogs licked the blood of Naboth, the dogs shall lick your blood—even yours.'"
Ahab said to Elijah, "Have you found me, O my enemy?" And he answered, "I have found you, because you have sold yourself to do evil in the sight of the LORD."
"Behold, I will bring disaster upon you, and I will utterly sweep you away, and I will cut off from Ahab every male in Israel, whether slave or free.

And I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, for the provocation with which you have provoked Me to anger, and for having made Israel sin.
And concerning Jezebel the LORD also said, 'The dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.'
Whoever belongs to Ahab and dies in the city, the dogs shall eat; and whoever dies in the field, the birds of the sky shall eat."
There was no one like Ahab, who sold himself to do evil in the sight of the LORD, because Jezebel his wife incited him.
He acted very abominably in going after idols, according to all that the Amorites had done, whom the LORD drove out before the children of Israel.
When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes, put sackcloth upon his flesh, fasted, lay in sackcloth, and went about quietly.
Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

"Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before Me? Because he has humbled himself before Me, I will not bring the disaster in his days; but in the days of his son I will bring the disaster upon his house."
Three full years elapsed in which no hostilities disturbed the peace between Aram and Israel.
In the third year, Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, descended to the king of Israel.
The king of Israel said to his servants, "Are you aware that Ramoth-gilead is ours, yet we remain passive, failing to reclaim it from the king of Aram?"
He said to Jehoshaphat, "Will you accompany me to wage war at Ramoth-gilead?" Jehoshaphat replied to the king of Israel, "I am as you are; my people are as your people; my horses are as your horses."
Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Please inquire today for the word of the LORD."

The king of Israel gathered the prophets—about four hundred men—and said to them, "Shall I march against Ramoth-gilead in battle, or shall I forbear?" They answered, "Go up, for the Lord will give it into the king's hand."
Jehoshaphat said, "Is there no longer a prophet of the LORD here, that we might consult him?"

The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There remains one man through whom we may inquire of the LORD—Micaiah son of Imlah—but I detest him, for he never prophesies prosperity for me, only calamity." Jehoshaphat said, "Let not the king say so."
The king of Israel called one of his officials and said, "Fetch Micaiah son of Imlah without delay."

Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting each upon his throne, robed in regalia, at the threshing floor beside the gate of Samaria, while all the prophets prophesied before them.
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah fashioned iron horns for himself and declared, "Thus says the LORD: With these you shall gore the Arameans until you make an end of them."
All the prophets prophesied likewise, saying, "Ascend to Ramoth-gilead and prosper, for the LORD will deliver it into the king's hand."

The messenger who had gone to summon Micaiah said to him, "Now observe: the prophets speak with one accord in the king's favor. Please let your word be like the word of one of them, and speak favorably."
Micaiah said, "As the LORD lives, only what the LORD speaks to me will I utter."

When he came to the king, the king said to him, "Micaiah, shall we march against Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall we desist?" He answered, "Go up and prosper, for the LORD will deliver it into the king's hand."
The king said to him, "How many times must I make you swear that you will speak to me nothing but the truth in the name of the LORD?"
He said, "I saw all Israel dispersed upon the mountains, like sheep without a shepherd; and the LORD said, 'These have no master; let each return to his own house in peace.'"
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not tell you that he would prophesy no good concerning me, but only evil?"
Micaiah said, "Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD seated upon His throne, and all the host of heaven standing beside Him, on His right and on His left."
And the LORD said, "Who will persuade Ahab to go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?" One spoke in this manner, and another in that.
Then a spirit came out and stood before the LORD and said, "I will entice him." And the LORD said to him, "By what means?"
He said, "I will go forth and become a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets." And He said, "You shall entice him, and you shall also succeed; go forth and do so."
Now, then, behold: the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, and the LORD has decreed disaster concerning you."
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came near and struck Micaiah on the cheek, saying, "By what way did the Spirit of the LORD pass from me to speak to you?"
Micaiah said, "Behold, you will see on that day when you enter an inner room to hide yourself."
The king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and return him to Amon the ruler of the city and to Joash the king's son,
and say, 'Thus says the king: Imprison this man and feed him on bread of affliction and water of affliction until I return in peace.'"
Micaiah said, "If you indeed return in peace, the LORD has not spoken by me." Then he said, "Hear, all peoples!"
So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and enter the battle, but you wear your robes." And the king of Israel disguised himself and went into the battle.
The king of Aram commanded the thirty-two captains of his chariots, "Do not engage small or great, but the king of Israel alone."
When the chariot captains saw Jehoshaphat, they said, "Surely that is the king of Israel." They turned aside to attack him, and Jehoshaphat cried out.
But when the chariot captains saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.
But a man drew his bow at a venture and struck the king of Israel between the scale armor and the breastplate. He said to his charioteer, "Turn about and carry me out of the camp, for I am wounded."
The battle intensified that day, and the king was held upright in his chariot facing the Arameans, while the blood of the wound ran into the floor of the chariot; he died at evening.
As the sun was setting, a cry went through the camp: "Every man to his city, and every man to his land!"
The king died and was brought to Samaria, where they buried him.
They washed the chariot at the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked up his blood, while the prostitutes bathed, in accordance with the word of the LORD that He had spoken.
Now the rest of the acts of Ahab, and all that he did, and the ivory house that he built, and all the cities that he built—are they not recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Ahab slept with his fathers, and his son Ahaziah reigned in his place.
In the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel, Jehoshaphat son of Asa began to reign over Judah.
Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah, daughter of Shilhi.

He walked in all the way of Asa his father and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD. Yet the high places were not removed; the people continued to sacrifice and burn incense on the high places.
Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, and his might that he displayed, and his wars—are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
He also removed from the land the rest of the male shrine prostitutes who had survived from the days of his father Asa.
There was no king in Edom; a deputy reigned.
Jehoshaphat constructed a fleet of Tarshish ships to fetch gold from Ophir, but they never sailed, for the ships were wrecked at Ezion-geber.
Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, "Let my servants sail with your servants in the ships." But Jehoshaphat refused.
Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers and was buried with them in the city of David his father; his son Jehoram reigned in his stead.
In the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, Ahaziah son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned over Israel two years.
He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD and walked in the way of his father and mother and in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin.
He served Baal and worshiped him, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger, just as his father had done.
After the death of Ahab, Moab rebelled against Israel.

Ahaziah fell through the lattice of his upper chamber in Samaria and was grievously injured; whereupon he dispatched messengers with the instruction: “Go, inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I shall recover from this malady.”

Yet the angel of the LORD spoke to Elijah the Tishbite: “Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and speak to them, ‘Is it because there is no God in Israel that you go to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?’ Therefore thus says the LORD: ‘You shall not descend from the bed to which you have ascended, but you shall surely die.’” And Elijah went.
When the messengers returned to him, he said to them, “Why have you returned?”

They replied, “A man came up to meet us and said to us, ‘Go, return to the king who sent you, and speak to him, “Thus says the LORD: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you send to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore you shall not descend from the bed to which you have ascended, but you shall surely die.”’”
He asked them, “What was the appearance of the man who came up to meet you and uttered these words to you?”
They answered, “He was a hirsute man, girded with a leather belt about his loins.” And he said, “It is Elijah the Tishbite.”

Thereupon the king sent to him a captain of fifty with his fifty men, and he ascended to him; and behold, Elijah was seated upon the summit of the hill. And he said to him, “O man of God, the king says, ‘Come down.’”
Elijah answered the captain of fifty, “If I am indeed a man of God, let fire descend from heaven and consume you and your fifty.” Then fire descended from heaven and consumed him and his fifty.
Again he sent another captain of fifty with his fifty. He approached and said to him, “O man of God, thus says the king: ‘Come down quickly.’”
Elijah answered, “If I am a man of God, let fire descend from heaven and consume you and your fifty.” Then the fire of God descended from heaven and consumed him and his fifty.

So he sent yet a third captain of fifty with his fifty. The third captain of fifty ascended, came, and fell upon his knees before Elijah, and supplicated him, saying, “O man of God, pray let my life, and the life of these fifty servants of your, be precious in your eyes.
Behold, fire descended from heaven and consumed the two former captains and their fifties; but now let my life be precious in your eyes.”
Then the angel of the LORD said to Elijah, “Go down with him; do not fear him.” So he arose and went down with him to the king.

And he said to him, “Thus says the LORD: ‘Because you have sent messengers to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron—is it because there is no God in Israel?—therefore you shall not descend from the bed to which you have ascended, but you shall surely die.’”
So he died in accordance with the word of the LORD that Elijah had spoken. Because he had no son, Jehoram reigned in his stead, in the second year of Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.
Now the rest of the acts of Ahaziah that he performed, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
When the the LORD was about to bear Elijah heavenward in a tempest, Elijah and Elisha departed from Gilgal.

Elijah said to Elisha, “Remain here, I pray, for the the LORD has commissioned me as far as Bethel.” But Elisha replied, “As the the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I shall not abandon you.” Thus they descended to Bethel.

The sons of the prophets at Bethel came forth to Elisha and said to him, “Do you know that the the LORD will remove your master from above your head this day?” He answered, “Indeed, I know; be still.”

Elijah said to him, “Elisha, abide here, I pray, for the the LORD has sent me to Jericho.” But he said, “As the the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not forsake you.” So they came to Jericho.
The sons of the prophets at Jericho drew near to Elisha and said to him, “Do you know that the the LORD will remove your master from above your head this day?” He replied, “Yes, I know; be silent.”

Elijah said to him, “Remain here, I pray, for the the LORD has dispatched me to the Jordan.” But he answered, “As the the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, I will not abandon you.” So the two of them continued onward.
Fifty men from the company of prophets went and stood at a distance, while the two of them stood by the Jordan.
Elijah took his mantle, rolled it up, and struck the waters, so that they parted to this side and that, and the two crossed over on dry ground.
When they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, “Ask what I should do for you before I am taken from you.” And Elisha said, “Please let a twofold portion of your spirit be upon me.”
He said, “You have asked a hard thing. Nevertheless, if you see me when I am taken from you, it shall be so for you; but if not, it shall not be.”
As they walked and conversed, behold, a fiery chariot and fiery horses separated them, and Elijah ascended in the whirlwind to heaven.
Elisha saw it and cried out, “My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and its horsemen!” He saw him no more; then he seized his garments and tore them in two.
He also took up Elijah’s mantle that had fallen from him, returned, and stood by the bank of the Jordan.

He took the mantle of Elijah that had fallen from him and struck the waters, saying, “Where is the the LORD, the God of Elijah?” When he had struck the waters, they parted to this side and that, and Elisha crossed over.
When the prophetic disciples at Jericho saw him from afar, they said, “The spirit of Elijah rests upon Elisha.” They came to meet him and prostrated themselves to the ground before him.

They said to him, “Behold, your servants have fifty able men; let them go, we pray, and search for your master, lest the Spirit of the the LORD has carried him away and cast him upon some mountain or into some valley.” He said, “You shall not send.”
But they pressed him until he was ashamed, and he said, “Send them.” So they sent fifty men, who searched for three days but did not find him.
When they returned to him while he was residing at Jericho, he said to them, “Did I not say to you, ‘Do not go’?”
Then the men of the city said to Elisha, “Behold, the site of this city is pleasant, as my lord sees; but the water is bad, and the land is barren.”
He said, “Bring me a new flask and put salt in it.” So they brought it to him.
Then he went out to the spring of the waters and threw salt there, and said, “Thus says the the LORD, ‘I have healed these waters; from there shall be no more death or barrenness.’”
So the waters were healed to this day, according to the word of Elisha that he spoke.
Then he went up from there to Bethel; and as he was going up along the road, young boys came out of the city and jeered at him, saying, “Go up, you baldhead; go up, you baldhead!”
When he turned around and saw them, he cursed them in the name of the the LORD. Then two she-bears came out of the forest and tore forty-two of the boys.
He went from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.
In the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat’s reign over Judah, Jehoram son of Ahab became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria twelve years.
He perpetrated evil in the sight of the LORD, though not to the degree of his father and mother, for he removed the sacred pillar of Baal that his father had erected.
Nevertheless, he adhered to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which that king had led Israel into sin, and he did not depart from them.
Now Mesha, king of Moab, was a sheep breeder, and he rendered to the king of Israel a tribute of one hundred thousand lambs and one hundred thousand rams, together with their wool.
But upon Ahab’s death, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
At that juncture King Jehoram marched out of Samaria and mustered all Israel.

He sent to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, saying, “Moab has rebelled against me. Will you accompany me in war against Moab?” Jehoshaphat replied, “I am as you are; my people are as your people; my horses are as your horses.”
Jehoshaphat asked, “By which route shall we ascend?” Jehoram answered, “Through the wilderness of Edom.”
So the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom set out; they circled about for seven days, and no water was found for the army or for the beasts that accompanied them.
Then the king of Israel exclaimed, “Alas! For the LORD has summoned these three kings only to deliver them into the hand of Moab.”

But Jehoshaphat said, “Is there no prophet of the LORD here, through whom we may inquire of the LORD?” One of the servants of the king of Israel answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here—the one who poured water upon Elijah’s hands.”
Jehoshaphat said, “The word of the LORD is with him.” So the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom descended to him.

Elisha said to the king of Israel, “What have I to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father and to the prophets of your mother.” The king of Israel said, “No, for the LORD has called these three kings to deliver them into the hand of Moab.”
Elisha said, “As the LORD of hosts lives, before whom I stand, were it not that I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, I would not look upon you or acknowledge you.”
“But now bring me a musician.” And when the musician played, the hand of the LORD came upon him.
And he said, “Thus says the LORD: Make this valley full of trenches.
For thus says the LORD: You shall not see wind, nor shall you see rain; yet this valley shall be filled with water, so that you may drink—you, your livestock, and your beasts.
This is a trifling matter in the sight of the LORD; He will also deliver Moab into your hand.
And you shall strike every fortified city and every choice city, and you shall fell every good tree, and stop up all springs of water, and mar every good piece of land with stones.”
In the morning, when the grain offering was being offered, behold, water came by way of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
When all Moab heard that the kings had come up to fight against them, they summoned all who could bear arms, from the least to the greatest, and took their stand on the border.
They rose early in the morning, and the sun shone upon the water; and Moab, looking from the opposite side, saw the water red as blood.
They said, “This is blood! The kings have surely slain one another. Now, Moab, to the spoil!”
When they came to the camp of Israel, Israel rose up and struck Moab, so that they fled before them; and they pursued them into the land, striking Moab as they went.

They demolished the cities, and every man cast a stone upon every good field until it was filled; they stopped up all the springs of water and felled all the good trees, until only Kir-hareseth remained, with its stones; and the slingers surrounded it and struck it.
When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too strong for him, he took seven hundred swordsmen to break through to the king of Edom, but they could not.

Then he took his firstborn son, who was to reign in his place, and offered him as a burnt offering upon the wall; and great wrath came upon Israel, so they withdrew from him and returned to their own land.

Now a wife from among the company of the prophets appealed to Elisha, saying, “My husband, your servant, has perished, and you know that I stood in awe of the LORD. Moreover, the creditor has arrived to confiscate my two sons and reduce them to servitude.”
Elisha said to her, “How am I to assist you? Tell me, what possessions remain in your household?” She answered, “I have nothing in the house save a flask of oil.”
He said, “Go and procure empty containers from all your neighbors; do not limit yourself to a scant few.”
He added, “Then enter, shut the door behind you and your sons, pour the oil into all these vessels, and remove each one once it is filled.”
So she departed from him and shut the door behind her and her sons. They brought the vessels to her, and she poured.
When the vessels were full, she said to her son, “Bring me another vessel.” He said, “No further vessel remains.” Then the oil ceased to flow.
She came and reported to the man of God. He said, “Go, sell the oil and satisfy your debt, and you and your sons shall subsist upon the surplus.”
One day Elisha went to Shunem, where a woman of distinction resided, and she importuned him to dine. So whenever he traveled that route, he would break his journey there for a meal.
She said to her husband, “Behold, I perceive that this man who continually passes by us is a holy man of God.
Let us make a modest chamber on the roof and furnish it for him with a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp, so that whenever he comes to us he may lodge there.”
One day he came there, withdrew to the upper chamber, and lay down there.
He said to Gehazi his servant, “Summon this Shunammite.” So he called her, and she stood before him.

He said to him, “Say now to her, ‘You have extended to us such meticulous solicitude; what is to be done for you? Would you have me speak on your behalf to the king or to the commander of the army?’” She answered, “I dwell among my own people.”
He said, “What further benefaction might be rendered to her?” Gehazi answered, “She has no son, and her husband is aged.”
He said, “Call her.” So he called her, and she stood at the door.
He said, “By this time next year you shall be cradling a son.” She said, “No, my lord, man of God, do not delude me.”
But the woman conceived and bore a son at that season the next year, exactly as Elisha had spoken to her.
When the child had grown, one day he went out to his father among the harvesters.
He said to his father, “My head, my head!” His father said to a servant, “Convey him to his mother.”
The servant carried him to his mother; he rested upon her knees until noon, and then he died.
She went up and placed him upon the prophet’s couch, shut the door upon him, and went out.
She called to her husband and said, “Please send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, that I may hasten to the man of God and return.”
He said, “Why do you repair to him this day? It is neither the new moon nor the Sabbath.” She said, “It is well.”
Then she saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Drive on; do not slacken the pace for me unless I tell you.”
So she set out and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her from a distance, he said to Gehazi his servant, “Behold, the Shunammite approaches.”
He said, “Run now to meet her, and say to her, ‘Is all well with you? Is all well with your husband? Is all well with the child?’” She answered, “It is well.”

When she reached the man of God on the mountain, she seized his feet. Gehazi came near to push her away, but the man of God said, “Leave her alone, for her spirit is embittered, and the LORD has concealed the matter from me and has not disclosed it to me.”
She said, “Did I ask my lord for a son? Did I not say, ‘Do not delude me’?”
He said to Gehazi, “Brace yourself, take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him; if anyone greets you, do not answer; and lay my staff on the child’s face.”
The mother of the child said, “As the LORD lives, and as you live, I will not leave you.” So he arose and followed her.
Gehazi went on before them and laid the staff on the child’s face, but there was no sound and no response. So he returned to meet him and reported, “The child has not awakened.”
When Elisha entered the house, the child lay dead upon his bed.
He went in and shut the door behind the two of them and prayed to the LORD.
He went up and lay upon the child, placing his mouth to his mouth, his eyes to his eyes, and his hands to his hands; and as he stretched himself over him, the flesh of the child grew warm.
Then he returned and paced back and forth in the house; then he went up and stretched himself over him again. The child sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
He called Gehazi and said, “Summon this Shunammite.” So he called her, and she came to him. Then he said, “Take up your son.”
She came in, fell at his feet, bowed to the ground, and then took up her son and went out.

Elisha returned to Gilgal, and there was a famine in the land. The sons of the prophets were sitting before him. He said to his servant, “Set the large pot on the fire, and prepare a pottage for the sons of the prophets.”

One of them went out into the field to gather herbs. He found a wild vine and gathered from it as many wild gourds as his cloak could hold; then he came and sliced them into the pot of stew, not knowing what they were.
They served it to the men to eat. But as they were eating the stew, they cried out, “There is poison in the pot, man of God!” And they could not eat it.
He said, “Then fetch meal.” He threw it into the pot and said, “Serve it to the people, that they may eat.” And there was nothing noxious in the pot.
A man came from Baal-shalishah, bringing to the man of God twenty loaves of barley bread from the firstfruits, and fresh grain in his bag. Elisha said, “Give it to the people, that they may eat.”
His servant said, “How am I to present this before a hundred men?” But Elisha said, “Give it to the people, that they may eat, for thus says the LORD, ‘They shall eat and have a surplus.’”
So he set it before them, and they ate and had a surplus, in accordance with the word of the LORD.

Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a man of great consequence before his master and highly honored, because through him the the LORD had granted deliverance to Aram; he was a mighty man of valor, yet the man was leprous.
Now the Arameans had gone out in raiding bands and had taken captive a little girl from the land of Israel, and she served before Naaman's wife.
She said to her mistress, “Oh, that my master might stand before the prophet who is in Samaria; then he would recover him from his leprosy.”
He went in and told his master, saying, “Thus and thus has the girl from the land of Israel spoken.”
The king of Aram said, “Go now, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel.” So he departed, taking in his hand ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of garments.
He brought the letter to the king of Israel, which read, “Now, when this letter reaches you, behold, I have sent to you Naaman my servant, that you may cure him of his leprosy.”

When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his garments and said, “Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man sends to me to cure a man of leprosy? Consider now, and see that he seeks an occasion against me.”

When Elisha, the man of God, heard that the king of Israel had torn his garments, he sent to the king, saying, “Why have you torn your garments? Let him come now to me, that he may know that there is a prophet in Israel.”
So Naaman came with his horses and chariot and stood at the door of Elisha's house.
Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, “Go and wash in the Jordan seven times, and your flesh shall be restored to you, and you shall be clean.”

But Naaman was wroth and went away, saying, “Behold, I thought that he would surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the the LORD his God, and wave his hand over the place, and cure the leper.”
“Are not Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean?” So he turned and went away in rage.
His servants came near and spoke to him, “My father, if the prophet had spoken to you a great thing, would you not have done it? How much more, then, when he says to you, ‘Wash, and be clean’?”
So he went down and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the word of the man of God; his flesh returned like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.

Then he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and stood before him and said, “Behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth but in Israel; now, therefore, please accept a blessing from your servant.”
Elisha said, “As the the LORD lives, before whom I stand, I will take nothing.” And he urged him to take it, but he refused.
Naaman said, “If not, then please let two mule-loads of earth be given to your servant, for your servant will no longer offer burnt offering or sacrifice to other gods, but to the the LORD.

In this matter may the the LORD pardon your servant: when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leans on my hand, and I bow myself in the house of Rimmon—when I bow myself in the house of Rimmon, may the the LORD pardon your servant in this matter.”
He said to him, “Go in peace.” So he departed from him a little way.

Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, “Behold, my master has spared this Aramean, Naaman, by not receiving from his hand what he brought. As the the LORD lives, I will run after him and take something from him.”
Gehazi pursued after Naaman. When Naaman saw him running after him, he alighted from the chariot to meet him and said, “Is all well?”

Gehazi said, “All is well. My master has sent me, saying, ‘Behold, now two young men of the sons of the prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of garments.’”

Naaman said, “Be pleased to take two talents.” He urged him, and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of garments, and gave them to two of his servants; and they carried them before him.
When he came to the hill, he took them from their hand and deposited them in the house, and sent the men away, and they departed.
When he had come in and stood before his master, Elisha said to him, “Where have you been, Gehazi?” And he said, “Your servant has not gone anywhere.”

Elisha said, “Did not my heart go with you when the man turned from his chariot to meet you? Is it now a time to take silver, and to take garments, and olive groves, and vineyards, and sheep, and oxen, and male servants, and female servants?”
“Therefore the leprosy of Naaman shall cling to you and to your seed forever.” And he went out from his presence a leper, white as snow.
The sons of the prophets said to Elisha, "The quarters in which we reside under your tutelage have grown excessively cramped."
"Let us go, I pray, to the Jordan; there let each man take a beam, that we may construct for ourselves a place in which to dwell." And Elisha said, "Go."
Then one of them said, "Please consent to accompany your servants." And he said, "I will go."
So he went with them. They came to the Jordan and felled trees.
As one of them was felling a beam, the iron axehead fell into the water, and he cried out, "Alas, my lord! It was borrowed."
The man of God asked, "Where did it fall?" When he showed him the place, he hewed a stick, cast it there, and the iron floated.
Then he said, "Lift it out for yourself." So he reached out his hand and took it.
Now the king of Aram was at war with Israel. He took counsel with his servants, saying, "My encampment shall be at such-and-such a place."
But the man of God sent word to the king of Israel, "Beware lest you pass by this place, for the Arameans are descending there."
The king of Israel therefore sent to the place of which the man of God had warned him; having been forewarned, he kept vigilant there, not merely once or twice.
The king of Aram was enraged over this, and he summoned his servants and demanded, "Will you not disclose to me which among us is in league with the king of Israel?"
One of his servants replied, "No, my lord the king; but Elisha, the prophet who is in Israel, tells the king of Israel the very words you speak in your bedchamber."
He said, "Go and see where he is, that I may send and seize him." And they reported, "Behold, he is in Dothan."
So he sent horses and chariots and a substantial force. They came by night and surrounded the city.
When the servant of the man of God rose early and went out, behold, an army with horses and chariots was surrounding the city. His servant said, "Alas, my master! What shall we do?"
He said, "Do not be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them."

Then Elisha prayed, "The LORD, I pray, open his eyes that he may see." And the LORD opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw; and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.
As they came down to him, Elisha prayed to the LORD, "Strike this people with blindness, I pray." And the LORD struck them with blindness according to the word of Elisha.
Then Elisha said to them, "This is not the way, and this is not the city; follow me, and I will lead you to the man whom you seek." And he led them to Samaria.
When they had entered Samaria, Elisha said, "The LORD, open the eyes of these, that they may see." And the LORD opened their eyes, and they saw; and behold, they were in the midst of Samaria.
When the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha, "My father, shall I strike them down? Shall I strike them down?"

He answered, "You shall not strike them. Would you strike those whom you have taken captive with your sword and your bow? Set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink and return to their master."
So he prepared a great feast for them; and after they had eaten and drunk, he sent them away, and they went to their master. And the raiding bands of Aram no longer came into the land of Israel.
Afterward Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered all his army and went up and besieged Samaria.
There was a great famine in Samaria; and behold, they besieged it until a donkey's head was sold for eighty shekels of silver, and a quarter of a kab of dove's dung for five shekels.
As the king of Israel was passing by upon the wall, a woman cried out to him, "Save me, my lord the king!"
He said, "If the LORD does not save you, how can I save you? From the threshing floor or from the winepress?"
And the king said to her, "What troubles you?" She answered, "This woman said to me, 'Give your son, that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.
"So we boiled my son and ate him. And I said to her the next day, 'Give your son, that we may eat him,' but she hid her son."
When the king heard the woman's words, he tore his garments as he passed along upon the wall; and the people saw that he wore sackcloth beneath upon his flesh.
Then he said, "May God do so to me, and more also, if the head of Elisha the son of Shaphat remains on him today."

Now Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. He sent a man from before him, but before the messenger came to him, he said to the elders, "Do you see how this son of a murderer has sent to take away my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door and hold him fast at the door. Is not the sound of his master's feet behind him?"
While he was still speaking with them, behold, the messenger came down to him, and he said, "Behold, this evil is from the LORD; why should I wait for the LORD any longer?"

Elisha said, “Hear the word of the LORD. This is what the LORD says: ‘At this time tomorrow, a seah of fine flour will be sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria.’”

But the officer upon whose arm the king leaned answered the man of God, “Look—even if the LORD were to open the floodgates of heaven, could such a thing come to pass?” “You shall see it with your own eyes,” Elisha replied, “but you will not eat of it.”
Now four men afflicted with leprosy were stationed at the entrance to the city gate, and they said to one another, “Why do we linger here until we die?

If we propose to enter the city, the famine is there, and we shall perish; if we remain here, we shall perish all the same. Come, then—let us defect to the Aramean camp. If they spare us, we shall live; if they put us to death, we shall die.”
So they rose at twilight and made their way toward the Aramean camp, and when they reached its outskirts, they discovered that no one was there.

For the Lord had caused the Aramean camp to hear the sound of chariots, horses, and a mighty host, so they said to one another, “Behold, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to come upon us.”
Thus they rose and fled in the twilight, abandoning their tents, their horses, and their donkeys, leaving the camp exactly as it stood, and fled for their lives.

When these lepers reached the outskirts of the camp, they entered a tent, ate and drank, and carried away silver, gold, and garments, which they hid. Then they returned, entered another tent, took what was in it, and hid that as well.

Then they said to one another, “We are not acting rightly. This day is a day of good tidings, and we are holding our peace. If we wait until morning light, retribution will overtake us. Come, then—let us go and report this to the king’s household.”

So they went and called to the gatekeepers of the city, saying, “We went to the Aramean camp, and behold, no one is there—not even the voice of a man—only horses and donkeys tethered, and the tents just as they were.”
The gatekeepers proclaimed the news, and it was reported to the king’s household.

Then the king rose in the night and said to his servants, “Let me tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know that we are famished, so they have left the camp to conceal themselves in the fields, thinking, ‘When they come out of the city, we will capture them alive and enter the city.’”

One of his servants answered, “Please, let some men take five of the horses that remain in the city. Their plight is the same as that of all the Israelites who remain; their plight is the same as that of all the Israelites who have perished. Let us send them and see.”
So they took two chariots with horses, and the king sent them after the Aramean army, saying, “Go and see.”

They pursued them as far as the Jordan, and indeed the whole way was littered with garments and equipment that the Arameans had cast away in their haste. So the messengers returned and reported to the king.
Then the people went out and plundered the Aramean camp, and a seah of fine flour sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, according to the word of the LORD.

Now the king had put the officer upon whose arm he leaned in charge of the gate, and the people trampled him in the gateway, and he died, just as the man of God had said when the king came down to him.
It happened just as the man of God had told the king: “At this time tomorrow, two seahs of barley will sell for a shekel, and a seah of fine flour for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria.”

And the officer had answered the man of God, “Look—even if the LORD were to open the floodgates of heaven, could such a thing come to pass?” “You shall see it with your own eyes,” Elisha had replied, “but you will not eat of it.”
And so it befell him: the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.

Elisha had spoken to the woman whose son he had restored to life, saying, “Arise, go you and your household, and sojourn wherever you are able to sojourn, for the LORD has summoned a famine, and it is coming upon the land for seven years.”
The woman arose and acted in accordance with the word of the man of God; she departed with her household and sojourned in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
When the seven years had run their course, the woman returned from the land of the Philistines and went out to the king to cry out concerning her house and her field.
Now the king was speaking to Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, saying, “Please recount to me all the great deeds that Elisha has performed.”

While he was recounting to the king how he had restored the dead to life, behold, the woman whose son he had restored to life came crying to the king about her house and her field. Gehazi said, “My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha restored to life.”

The king inquired of the woman, and she recounted it to him; then the king appointed to her a certain officer, saying, “Restore to her all that was hers, together with all the produce of the field, from the day she left the land until now.”
Elisha went to Damascus while Ben-hadad, king of Aram, was ill, and it was reported to him, saying, “The man of God has come here.”
The king said to Hazael, “Take a gift in your hand and go to meet the man of God, and inquire of the LORD through him, saying, ‘Shall I recover from this sickness?’”

So Hazael went to meet him, taking in his hand a gift of forty camel-loads and every good thing of Damascus, and he came and stood before him and said, “Your son Ben-hadad, king of Aram, has sent me to you, saying, ‘Shall I recover from this sickness?’”
Elisha said to him, “Go, say to him, ‘You shall certainly recover,’ but the LORD has shown me that he shall surely die.”
He fixed his gaze upon him and held it until he was ashamed, and the man of God wept.

Hazael said, “Why does my lord weep?” He said, “Because I know the evil that you will do to the children of Israel: you will set their fortresses on fire, you will slay their young men with the sword, you will dash their little ones to pieces, and you will rip open their pregnant women.”
Hazael said, “But what is your servant, this dog, that he should do so great a thing?” Elisha said, “The LORD has shown me that you are to be king over Aram.”
So he departed from Elisha and came to his master, who said to him, “What did Elisha say to you?” And he said, “He said to me, ‘You shall certainly recover.’”
On the next day he took the thick cloth and dipped it in water and spread it over his face, so that he died; and Hazael reigned in his place.
In the fifth year of Joram the son of Ahab, king of Israel—Jehoshaphat being then king of Judah—Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat began to reign over Judah.
He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did what was evil in the sight of the LORD.
Yet the LORD was unwilling to destroy Judah, for the sake of David His servant, as He had promised to give him a lamp for his sons always.
In his days Edom revolted from under Judah’s rule and set up a king over themselves.
Then Joram crossed over to Zair with all his chariots; by night he arose and struck down the Edomites who surrounded him and the commanders of the chariots, but the troops fled to their tents.
So Edom has remained in revolt against Judah to this day, and at the same time Libnah revolted.
As for the rest of the acts of Joram, and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
Joram slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David; and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
In the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah the son of Jehoram, king of Judah, began to reign.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri, king of Israel.
He walked in the way of the house of Ahab and did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, like the house of Ahab, for he was son-in-law to the house of Ahab.
He went with Joram the son of Ahab to war against Hazael, king of Aram, at Ramoth-gilead, and the Arameans wounded Joram.

King Joram returned to Jezreel to be healed of the wounds that the Arameans had inflicted on him at Ramah when he fought against Hazael, king of Aram; and Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to Jezreel to see Joram son of Ahab, because he was sick.
Elisha the prophet summoned one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, "Prepare for action, take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead.
When you arrive there, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi; then bring him away from his brothers and take him into an inner room.
Take the flask of oil, pour it on his head, and say, 'Thus says the LORD: I have anointed you king over Israel.' Then open the door and flee; do not wait."
So the young prophet went to Ramoth-gilead.
When he arrived, the commanders of the army were sitting together, and he said, "I have a message for you, commander." Jehu said, "For which of us?" He answered, "For you, commander."
He arose, entered the house, poured the oil on his head, and said, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I have anointed you king over the people of the LORD, over Israel.
You shall strike down the house of Ahab your lord, and I will avenge the blood of My servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of the LORD at the hand of Jezebel.
The whole house of Ahab shall perish; I will cut off from Ahab every male, both bond and free, in Israel.
I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.
The dogs shall eat Jezebel in the plot of Jezreel, and no one shall bury her." Then he opened the door and fled.
Jehu went out to the servants of his lord, and they said to him, "Is all well? Why did this madman come to you?" He said, "You know the man and his rant."
They said, "That is a lie; tell us now." He said, "Thus and thus he said to me: 'Thus says the LORD: I have anointed you king over Israel.'"
They hurried, each man took his garment and placed it beneath him on the bare steps; they blew the trumpet and said, "Jehu is king."
Thus Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. Now Joram with all Israel had been guarding Ramoth-gilead against Hazael king of Aram.

But King Joram had returned to Jezreel to be healed of the wounds that the Arameans had inflicted on him while he fought Hazael king of Aram. Jehu said, "If you are willing, let no fugitive leave the city to go and report in Jezreel."
Then Jehu rode and went to Jezreel, for Joram was lying there; and Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to visit Joram.
The watchman standing on the tower in Jezreel saw the company of Jehu as he came and said, "I see a company." Joram said, "Take a horseman and send him to meet them and say, 'Is it peace?'"

So the horseman went to meet him and said, "Thus says the king: 'Is it peace?'" Jehu said, "What have you to do with peace? Turn behind me." The watchman reported that the messenger had reached them but did not return.
Then he sent a second horseman, who came to them and said, "Thus says the king: 'Is it peace?'" Jehu answered, "What have you to do with peace? Turn behind me."
The watchman reported, "He reached them, but he is not coming back; and the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he drives furiously."

Joram said, "Harness." So they harnessed his chariot. Then Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his chariot, and they went to meet Jehu and found him in the plot of Naboth the Jezreelite.
When Joram saw Jehu, he said, "Is it peace, Jehu?" He answered, "What peace, so long as the whoredoms of your mother Jezebel and her sorceries are so many?"
Joram turned his horses and fled, and said to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"
Jehu drew his bow and struck Joram between his shoulders; the arrow pierced his heart, and he sank down in his chariot.

Jehu said to Bidkar his officer, "Take him up and throw him into the field of Naboth the Jezreelite. Remember how you and I rode side by side behind Ahab his father, and the LORD laid this burden on him:

'Surely I have seen the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons,' says the LORD, 'and I will repay you in this very plot,' says the LORD. Now take him up and throw him into the plot, according to the word of the LORD."

When Ahaziah king of Judah saw this, he fled by the way of Beth-haggan. Jehu pursued him and said, "Strike him down too," in the chariot. At the ascent of Gur, which is by Ibleam, he fled to Megiddo and died there.
His servants carried him to Jerusalem and buried him with his fathers in his tomb in the city of David.
In the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab, Ahaziah had begun to reign over Judah.
Jehu came to Jezreel, and Jezebel heard of it. She painted her eyes, adorned her head, and looked out of the window.
As Jehu entered the gate, she said, "Is it peace, Zimri, murderer of your master?"
He lifted his face toward the window and said, "Who is with me? Who?" Then two or three eunuchs looked out at him.
He said, "Throw her down." So they threw her down, and some of her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses, and they trampled her underfoot.
He went in, ate and drank, and said, "Attend to this cursed woman and bury her, for she is a king's daughter."
When they went to bury her, they found no more of her than the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands.
They returned and told him, and he said, "This is the word of the LORD that He spoke by His servant Elijah the Tishbite: 'In the plot of Jezreel the dogs shall eat the flesh of Jezebel,
and her corpse shall be as dung on the surface of the field in the plot of Jezreel, so that no one will say, "This is Jezebel."'"
Now Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. Jehu composed letters and sent them to Samaria, addressing the officials of Jezreel, the elders, and the guardians of Ahab’s sons, with this message:
“When this letter reaches you, since your master’s sons are with you, and you possess chariots, horses, a fortified city, and weapons,
choose the best and most upright among your master’s sons, set him upon his father’s throne, and fight on behalf of your master’s house.”
They were terrified—indeed, exceedingly so—and said, “Behold, two kings could not withstand him; how then shall we stand?”

The steward of the household, the city overseer, the elders, and the guardians sent word to Jehu: “We are your servants; whatever you command we will do, and we will install no man as king. Do what seems good in your eyes.”

He then wrote a second letter to them: “If you are mine and will obey my voice, take the heads of your master’s sons and come to me at Jezreel by this time tomorrow.” Now the king’s sons, seventy in number, were with the great men of the city, who were raising them.
When the letter reached them, they seized the king’s sons, slaughtered seventy men, placed their heads in baskets, and sent them to him at Jezreel.
A messenger came and reported, “They have brought the heads of the king’s sons.” He replied, “Lay them in two heaps at the gate’s entrance until morning.”
In the morning he went out, stood before all the people, and said, “You are righteous. Behold, I conspired against my master and killed him; but who struck down all these?
Know, then, that not one word of the LORD that the LORD spoke concerning the house of Ahab shall fall to the ground, for the LORD has accomplished what He spoke through His servant Elijah.”
Jehu struck down everyone remaining of Ahab’s house in Jezreel, together with all his great men, his intimates, and his priests, until he left him no survivor.
Then he rose, departed, and went toward Samaria; along the way, at Beth-eked of the Shepherds,

Jehu encountered the brothers of Ahaziah, king of Judah, and asked, “Who are you?” They replied, “We are brothers of Ahaziah; we have come down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother.”
He commanded, “Take them alive.” They seized them alive and slaughtered them at the pit of Beth-eked—forty-two men—and left not one of them.

He left that place and found Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. He greeted him and asked, “Is your heart upright, as my heart is toward your heart?” Jehonadab answered, “It is.” “If it is,” Jehu said, “give me your hand.” He gave his hand, and Jehu took him up into the chariot.
He said, “Come with me and witness my zeal for the LORD.” So they made him ride in his chariot.
When he reached Samaria, he killed all who remained to Ahab in Samaria until he had annihilated them, in accordance with the word of the LORD spoken to Elijah.
Jehu assembled all the people and said to them, “Ahab served Baal but little; Jehu will serve him much.”

“Now summon to me all the prophets of Baal, all his servants, and all his priests; let none be absent, for I intend a great sacrifice to Baal. Whoever is absent shall not live.” Jehu, however, acted deceitfully, in order to destroy the worshippers of Baal.
He said, “Consecrate a solemn assembly for Baal.” And they proclaimed it.
Jehu sent throughout all Israel; all the worshippers of Baal came, so that not one was left who did not come. They entered the house of Baal, and it was filled from end to end.
He said to the keeper of the wardrobe, “Bring out garments for all the worshippers of Baal.” So he brought out garments for them.

Jehu went in with Jehonadab son of Rechab into the house of Baal and said to the worshippers of Baal, “Search and see that none of the servants of the LORD is here with you, but only worshippers of Baal.”

They went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed eighty men outside and said, “If any of the men whom I bring into your hands escapes, the one who lets him escape shall forfeit his life in exchange for the fugitive’s.”

As soon as he finished offering the burnt offering, Jehu commanded the guards and the officers, “Go in and strike them down; let no one get out.” The guards and officers struck them with the edge of the sword, cast the bodies out, and proceeded to the city of the house of Baal.
They brought out the sacred pillars of the house of Baal and burned them.
They demolished the pillar of Baal and tore down the house of Baal, making it a latrine to this day.
Thus Jehu eradicated Baal from Israel.
Yet Jehu did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he had caused Israel to sin—the golden calves at Bethel and at Dan.

The LORD said to Jehu, “Because you have acted well in doing what is right in My eyes, and have carried out against the house of Ahab all that was in My heart, your sons shall sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation.”
But Jehu was not careful to walk in the law of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart; he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam, by which he had caused Israel to sin.
In those days the LORD began to cut Israel down, and Hazael defeated them throughout all the territory of Israel:
from the Jordan eastward, all the land of Gilead—the Gadites, the Reubenites, and the Manassites—from Aroer by the Arnon Valley, including Gilead and Bashan.
Now the rest of the acts of Jehu, all that he did and all his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Jehu slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria. His son Jehoahaz reigned in his place.
The time that Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria was twenty-eight years.
When Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, perceived that her son had perished, she arose and annihilated every scion of the royal house.

Yet Jehosheba, daughter of King Joram and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash, the son of Ahaziah, and surreptitiously removed him from among the king's sons who were being put to death; with his nurse she hid him in the bedchamber, concealing him from Athaliah so that he was not slain.
He remained hidden with her in the house of the LORD for six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.

In the seventh year, Jehoiada sent and took the captains of the hundreds of the Carites and the runners; he brought them to himself in the house of the LORD, and there, within the house of the LORD, he made a covenant with them, bound them by oath, and showed them the king.
He commanded them, saying, "This is the thing that you shall do: one third of you, those coming on the Sabbath, shall keep watch over the king's house;
another third shall be at the gate of Sur, and another third at the gate behind the runners; you shall keep watch over the house.
Your two divisions that go out on the Sabbath shall keep watch over the house of the LORD for the king.
You shall surround the king on every side, each man with his weapons in his hand; whoever approaches the ranks shall be put to death. Be with the king in his going out and in his coming in."

The captains of the hundreds did all that Jehoiada the priest commanded; each took his men, those coming on the Sabbath together with those going off on the Sabbath, and they came to Jehoiada the priest.
The priest gave to the captains of the hundreds the spears and shields of King David that were in the house of the LORD.
The runners stood, each man with his weapons in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, by the altar and by the house, surrounding the king.
Then he brought out the king's son, set the crown upon him, and gave him the testimony; they made him king, anointed him, clapped their hands, and said, "Long live the king!"
When Athaliah heard the sound of the runners and of the people, she came to the people in the house of the LORD.

She looked, and there stood the king by the pillar according to custom, with the captains and the trumpeters beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets; then Athaliah tore her garments and cried, "Treason! Treason!"

Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of the hundreds, the commanders of the host, and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks; whoever follows her, kill with the sword," for the priest had said, "She shall not be put to death in the house of the LORD."
So they laid hands on her, and she went by the way of the horses' entrance to the king's house, and there she was put to death.
Jehoiada made a covenant between the LORD and the king and the people, that they should be the LORD's people; and between the king and the people.

All the people of the land went to the house of Baal and tore it down; they thoroughly broke its altars and its images in pieces; they killed Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. The priest appointed officers over the house of the LORD.

He took the captains of the hundreds, the Carites, the runners, and all the people of the land; they brought the king down from the house of the LORD and came by the way of the gate of the runners to the king's house. He sat on the throne of the kings.
All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; Athaliah they put to death with the sword at the king's house.
Joash was seven years old when he began to reign.
In the seventh year of Jehu, Joash became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem; his mother was Zibiah of Beersheba.
Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD throughout all his days, because Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
Nevertheless, the high places were not removed; the people continued to sacrifice and burn incense on the high places.

Joash said to the priests, “All the money brought into the house of the LORD as sacred offerings—the money collected in the census, each man’s assessed valuation, and every voluntary contribution that anyone decides to bring into the house of the LORD—
let each priest receive it from his acquaintances and apply it to repairing every defect found in the house.”
Yet by the twenty-third year of King Joash, the priests had not repaired the damage to the house.

So King Joash summoned Jehoiada the priest and his fellow priests and said to them, “Why have you not repaired the damage to the house? Now, therefore, take no more money from your acquaintances, but hand it over for the repair of the house.”
The priests agreed that they would collect no more money from the people and would no longer repair the damage to the house.

Then Jehoiada the priest took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and set it beside the altar on the right side, as one enters the house of the LORD. The priests who guarded the threshold put into it all the money brought into the house of the LORD.
Whenever they saw that there was a great deal of money in the chest, the king’s secretary and the high priest would come up, count the money found in the house of the LORD, and tie it up in bags.
They then gave the counted money to those supervising the work on the house of the LORD, who disbursed it to the carpenters and builders working on the house.
It went to the masons and stonecutters, and for the purchase of timber and hewn stone to repair the damage to the house, and for every other expense incurred in restoring the house.
However, no silver basins, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or any articles of gold or silver were made from the money brought into the house of the LORD.
Instead, it was given to the workmen, and they used it to repair the house of the LORD.
Moreover, no accounting was demanded from the men into whose hands the money was entrusted for disbursement to the workmen, because they acted faithfully.
The money from guilt offerings and sin offerings was not brought into the house of the LORD; it belonged to the priests.
At that time Hazael king of Aram went up and fought against Gath and captured it; then Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.

Joash king of Judah took all the sacred objects that his ancestors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, kings of Judah, had consecrated, together with his own sacred objects and all the gold found in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and of the royal palace, and sent them to Hazael king of Aram, who then withdrew from Jerusalem.
The rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
His servants conspired against him and struck Joash down at Beth-millo, on the road that descends to Silla.
His servants Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer struck him, and he died; they buried him with his ancestors in the City of David, and his son Amaziah reigned in his place.
In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu ascended the throne over Israel in Samaria, and his reign endured seventeen years.
He wrought evil in the sight of the LORD, walking in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, wherewith he had caused Israel to sin, and he did not turn away from them.
Therefore the wrath of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and He delivered them into the hand of Hazael king of Aram, and into the hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael, throughout all those days.
Then Jehoahaz sought the LORD’s favor, and the LORD hearkened unto him, for He saw the oppression of Israel, because the king of Aram oppressed them.
So the LORD granted Israel a deliverer, and they went forth from under the hand of Aram; and the children of Israel dwelt in their tents as aforetime.
Nevertheless they did not depart from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, wherein he had caused Israel to sin, but walked therein; and the Asherah remained standing in Samaria.
For Jehoahaz was left with no host save fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen, because the king of Aram had destroyed them and ground them to dust for threshing.
Now the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and his might, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
And Jehoahaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria; and Joash his son reigned in his stead.
In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned sixteen years.
And he did evil in the sight of the LORD; he did not depart from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, wherewith he had caused Israel to sin, but walked in them.
Now the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, and his might wherewith he warred against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
And Joash slept with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat upon his throne; and Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

Now Elisha had fallen sick of the sickness whereof he was to die. And Joash king of Israel came down to him, and wept over his face, and said, “My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen!”
And Elisha said to him, “Take a bow and arrows.” So he took a bow and arrows.
Then he said to the king of Israel, “Lay your hand upon the bow.” And he laid his hand upon it; and Elisha laid his hands upon the king’s hands.

And he said, “Open the east window.” And he opened it. Then Elisha said, “Shoot!” And he shot. And he said, “The arrow of the LORD’s salvation, even the arrow of salvation against Aram; for you shall smite the Arameans at Aphek until you have made an end of them.”
Then he said, “Take the arrows.” And he took them. Then he said to the king of Israel, “Strike the ground.” And he struck thrice and stopped.

And the man of God was wroth with him, and said, “You should have struck five or six times; then you would have struck Aram until you had made an end of it; but now you will strike Aram only three times.”
And Elisha died, and they buried him. Now bands of Moabites invaded the land at the turn of the year.

And it came to pass, as they were burying a man, that, behold, they spied a band of raiders; and they cast the man into the sepulcher of Elisha. And when the man touched the bones of Elisha, he revived and stood upon his feet.
Now Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

But the LORD was gracious unto them, and had compassion on them, and turned unto them, because of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and would not destroy them, nor cast them away from His presence, until now.
And Hazael king of Aram died; and Ben-hadad his son reigned in his stead.

And Jehoash son of Jehoahaz retook from the hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael the cities which he had taken from Jehoahaz his father by war. Jehoash struck him thrice, and recovered the cities of Israel.
In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; his mother was Jehoaddan, from Jerusalem.
He did what was upright in the eyes of the LORD, though not with the wholehearted fidelity of his ancestor David; rather, he conducted himself in every respect as his father Joash had done.
Yet the high places were not removed, and the people continued to sacrifice and to burn incense upon them.
When the kingdom was firmly established in his hand, he put to death the servants who had assassinated his father the king.

But he did not execute the children of the murderers, in accordance with what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, wherein the LORD commanded, “Fathers shall not be put to death because of their children, nor shall children be put to death because of their fathers; each shall die for his own sin.”
He struck down ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt, seized Sela in battle, and renamed it Joktheel, a name it bears to this day.
Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, “Come, let us confront one another face to face.”

Jehoash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, “The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son for a wife’; but a wild beast that was in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
You have indeed struck Edom, and your heart has lifted you up. Glory in it and stay at home; why should you stir up trouble so that you fall, you and Judah with you?”
But Amaziah would not listen, so Jehoash king of Israel advanced; he and Amaziah king of Judah confronted one another at Beth-shemesh in Judah.
Judah was routed before Israel, and every man fled to his tent.

Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Jehoash son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh; then he came to Jerusalem and tore down the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate—a breach of four hundred cubits.
He carried off all the gold and silver and all the vessels found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the royal palace, together with hostages, and returned to Samaria.
The rest of the acts of Jehoash—what he did, his might, and his war with Amaziah king of Judah—are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Jehoash slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel; his son Jeroboam reigned in his place.
Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
The rest of the acts of Amaziah—are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
A conspiracy was formed against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; but they sent men after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
They brought him back on horses and buried him in Jerusalem with his fathers in the City of David.
Then all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
He rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king had been laid to rest with his fathers.
In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash became king of Israel in Samaria, and he reigned forty-one years.
He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD; he did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he had made Israel sin.

He restored the border of Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, in accordance with the word that the LORD, the God of Israel, had spoken through His servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath-hepher.
For the LORD saw the very bitter affliction of Israel: there was no one, whether confined or at large, and no helper for Israel.
Yet the LORD had not decreed that He would blot out the name of Israel from under heaven, so He saved them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash.

The rest of the acts of Jeroboam—all that he did, his might, how he waged war, and how he recovered Damascus and Hamath, which had belonged to Judah, for Israel—are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Jeroboam slept with his fathers, with the kings of Israel; his son Zechariah reigned in his place.
In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam’s dominion over Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah assumed the kingship of Judah.
He was sixteen years old at his accession and occupied the throne for fifty-two years in Jerusalem; his mother was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
He acted uprightly in the sight of the LORD, conforming entirely to the conduct of his father Amaziah.
Only the high places remained unabolished; the populace continued to slaughter sacrificial victims and burn incense upon them.

The LORD afflicted the king with leprosy, which persisted until his death, so that he dwelt in secluded quarters, while Jotham, the king’s son, administered the palace and governed the people of the land.
As for the remaining exploits of Azariah and the totality of his accomplishments, are they not inscribed in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
Azariah died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David, and his son Jotham succeeded him as king.
In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah, king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and his reign endured but six months.
He acted wickedly in the sight of the LORD, as his fathers had done; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he caused Israel to sin.
Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him, struck him down before the people, put him to death, and seized the throne in his stead.
The remaining acts of Zechariah are indeed recorded—behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
This fulfilled the word of the LORD, which He spoke to Jehu: “Your sons shall occupy the throne of Israel to the fourth generation.” And so it happened.
In the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah, king of Judah, Shallum son of Jabesh began to reign, and he reigned one month in Samaria.
Menahem son of Gad went up from Tirzah, entered Samaria, struck down Shallum son of Jabesh there, killed him, and reigned in his place.
