The remaining acts of Shallum, together with the conspiracy he formed, are recorded—behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

Then Menahem attacked Tiphsah and all within it and its surrounding territory, extending from Tirzah; because its inhabitants refused to open to him, he devastated the city and ripped open all its pregnant women.
In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah, king of Judah, Menahem son of Gad began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and his reign lasted ten years.
He acted wickedly in the sight of the LORD; throughout his days he never turned from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he caused Israel to sin.
Pul, king of Assyria, invaded the land, and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver so that Pul would support him and secure his hold on the kingdom.

Menahem raised the silver from Israel—levying it upon all the men of substance, fifty shekels from each—to give to the king of Assyria; consequently, the king of Assyria withdrew and did not remain in the land.
The remaining acts of Menahem, and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
Menahem died, and his son Pekahiah succeeded him as king.
In the fiftieth year of Azariah, king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned two years.
He acted wickedly in the sight of the LORD; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he caused Israel to sin.

Pekah son of Remaliah, his commander, conspired against him; with Argob and Arieh and fifty men of the Gileadites, he struck Pekahiah down in the citadel of the royal palace in Samaria, killed him, and reigned in his place.
The remaining acts of Pekahiah, and all that he did, are recorded—behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
In the fifty-second year of Azariah, king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned twenty years.
He acted wickedly in the sight of the LORD; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he caused Israel to sin.

During Pekah’s reign over Israel, Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, invaded and captured Ijon, Abel-beth-maachah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee, and the whole land of Naphtali; he deported the inhabitants to Assyria.
Hoshea son of Elah conspired against Pekah son of Remaliah, struck him down and killed him, and reigned in his place in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
The remaining acts of Pekah, and all that he did, are recorded—behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah began to reign as king of Judah.
He was twenty-five years old at his accession and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; his mother was Jerusha, daughter of Zadok.
He acted uprightly in the sight of the LORD, in accordance with all that his father Uzziah had done.
Only the high places were not removed; the people continued to sacrifice and burn incense on them. He also built the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD.
The remaining acts of Jotham, and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
In those days the LORD began to send Rezin, king of Aram, and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.
Jotham died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David, his father, and his son Ahaz succeeded him as king.
In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham ascended the throne of Judah.
Ahaz was twenty years old at his accession and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; nevertheless, he did not do what was right in the sight of the LORD his God, as David his father had done.

He emulated the conduct of the kings of Israel, and he even consigned his own son to the fire, in conformity with the abominable practices of the nations that the LORD had dispossessed before the Israelites.
He offered sacrifices and burned incense upon the high places, upon the hills, and beneath every verdant tree.
At that juncture Rezin, king of Aram, and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, marched against Jerusalem to wage war; they besieged Ahaz, yet proved unable to subdue him.
Concurrently, Rezin king of Aram recovered Elath for Aram, expelling the Judahites from Elath; the Arameans occupied Elath and remain there to this day.

Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, “I am your servant and your son. Ascend and deliver me from the power of the king of Aram and from the power of the king of Israel, who have risen up against me.”
Ahaz further appropriated the silver and gold discovered in the house of the LORD and in the royal treasuries, dispatching them as tribute to the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria hearkened to him: he ascended against Damascus, seized it, deported its inhabitants to Kir, and executed Rezin.

King Ahaz journeyed to Damascus to greet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria; upon beholding the altar in Damascus, he transmitted to Uriah the priest a delineation of the altar and a model thereof, in accordance with all its craftsmanship.
Uriah the priest constructed the altar precisely in accordance with all that King Ahaz had sent from Damascus, and he completed it before King Ahaz returned from Damascus.
Upon the king’s return from Damascus, when he saw the altar, he drew near to it and ascended upon it.
He burned his burnt offering and his grain offering, poured out his libation, and sprinkled upon the altar the blood of his peace offerings.
He relocated the bronze altar that stood before the LORD from its position in front of the temple—between the new altar and the house of the LORD—and stationed it on the north side of the new altar.

King Ahaz commanded Uriah the priest, “Burn upon the great altar the morning burnt offering and the evening burnt offering, the king’s burnt offering and his grain offering, the burnt offering of all the people of the land, and their grain offerings and their drink offerings; sprinkle upon it all the blood of the burnt offering and all the blood of the sacrifice. But the bronze altar shall be mine for consultation.”
Uriah the priest executed all that King Ahaz had commanded.
King Ahaz dismantled the frames of the stands and removed the basin from them; he took down the Sea from the bronze oxen beneath it and placed it upon a stone pavement.
He also removed from the house of the LORD the Sabbath canopy that had been erected there, together with the king’s outer entrance, because of the king of Assyria.
The remainder of the deeds of Ahaz, are they not inscribed in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
Ahaz lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David; and his son Hezekiah reigned in his stead.
In the twelfth year of the reign of Ahaz over Judah, Hoshea son of Elah ascended the throne of Israel in Samaria, and his reign endured nine years.
He perpetrated evil in the sight of the LORD, though not to the same degree as the kings of Israel who had preceded him.
Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, advanced against him; Hoshea became his vassal and rendered tribute.

Yet the king of Assyria detected a conspiracy in Hoshea, who had dispatched envoys to So, king of Egypt, and who had ceased to remit the annual tribute. Accordingly, the king of Assyria seized him and incarcerated him in a prison house.
Then the king of Assyria overran the entire country, ascended to Samaria, and besieged it for three years.
In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria and deported Israel to Assyria, resettling them in Halah, in Gozan by the Habor River, and in the cities of the Medes.

All this calamity befell Israel because the Israelites had sinned against the LORD their God, who had liberated them from the land of Egypt and from the domination of Pharaoh, king of Egypt; moreover, they had venerated other gods.
They had conformed to the statutes of the nations whom the LORD had dispossessed before the Israelites, and to the innovations introduced by the kings of Israel.
The Israelites surreptitiously perpetrated deeds contrary to the LORD their God; from watchtower to fortified city, they erected high places in every one of their cities.
They raised up sacred pillars and Asherah poles upon every lofty hill and beneath every luxuriant tree.
They burned incense at every high place, emulating the nations that the LORD had expelled before them, and they committed iniquitous acts that provoked the LORD.
They served idols, although the LORD had admonished them, “You shall not do this thing.”

Yet the LORD had admonished Israel and Judah through all His prophets and seers, declaring, “Turn back from your evil ways, and observe My commandments and statutes in accordance with the entire Law that I commanded your fathers and transmitted to you through My servants the prophets.”
Nevertheless, they refused to hearken, and they stiffened their necks like their fathers, who had not placed faith in the LORD their God.

They spurned His statutes and the covenant He had ratified with their fathers, along with the decrees He had given them; they pursued vain idols and thereby became vain themselves, imitating the surrounding nations, although the LORD had commanded them not to emulate them.

They abandoned all the commandments of the LORD their God and fashioned for themselves two calves of molten metal; they fabricated an Asherah, prostrated themselves before the entire host of heaven, and served Baal.
They consigned their sons and daughters to the fire, practiced divination and sorcery, and sold themselves to perpetrate evil in the sight of the LORD, thereby provoking His wrath.
Therefore the LORD was exceedingly incensed with Israel and banished them from His presence; only the tribe of Judah remained.
Yet even Judah did not observe the commandments of the LORD their God, but walked in the customs that Israel had instituted.
Consequently, the LORD rejected the whole line of Israel, afflicted them, and delivered them into the hand of plunderers, until He had cast them out of His presence.
For when He had rent Israel from the house of David, they elevated Jeroboam son of Nebat to kingship; Jeroboam diverted Israel from following the LORD and induced them to commit a grave sin.
The Israelites persisted in all the sins that Jeroboam had committed; they did not desist from them.

until the LORD finally removed Israel from His presence, precisely as He had foretold through all His servants the prophets. Thus Israel was exiled from its native soil to Assyria, where it remains to this day.

Thereafter the king of Assyria imported people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim and settled them in the cities of Samaria in lieu of the Israelites; they took possession of Samaria and dwelt in its cities.
At the inception of their residence, they did not revere the LORD, so the LORD dispatched lions among them, and the beasts slew some of them.

So they addressed the king of Assyria, saying, “The people you have resettled in the cities of Samaria are ignorant of the law of the god of the land; hence He has sent lions among them, for they are ignorant of the law of the god of the land.”
Then the king of Assyria issued a command: “Send one of the priests you carried off from there; let him go and reside there, and instruct them in the law of the god of the land.”
So one of the priests who had been carried away from Samaria came and took up residence in Bethel, and he instructed them how to revere the LORD.
Nevertheless, every nation continued to fabricate its own gods and installed them in the shrines that the Samaritans had constructed on the high places, each nation in the cities where it dwelt.
The Babylonians made Succoth-benoth, the Cuthites made Nergal, and the Hamathites made Ashima.
The Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak, while the Sepharvites burned their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
Thus they revered the LORD, yet they also appointed priests from their own ranks to officiate for them in the shrines of the high places.
They revered the LORD, but they also served their own gods in accordance with the customs of the nations from which they had been deported.

To this day they persist in their former practices: they do not revere the LORD, nor do they observe the statutes, ordinances, laws, or commandments that the LORD gave to the descendants of Jacob, whom He designated Israel.
When the LORD covenanted with them, He charged them: “Do not revere other gods, nor bow down to them, nor serve them, nor sacrifice to them.
Rather, revere the LORD, who brought you up from the land of Egypt with great power and an outstretched arm; bow down to Him and sacrifice to Him.
And you must meticulously observe the statutes, ordinances, laws, and commandments that He inscribed for you; do not revere other gods.
Do not forget the covenant that I have made with you, and do not revere other gods.
Rather, revere the LORD your God, and He will rescue you from the hand of all your enemies.”
But they did not hearken; instead, they persisted in their ancestral customs.
So these nations revered the LORD, yet they also served their carved images; to this day, their children and grandchildren continue to act as their fathers did.
In the third regnal year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz ascended the throne of Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; his mother’s name was Abi, daughter of Zechariah.
He executed what was upright in the sight of the LORD, precisely as David, his father, had done.

He extirpated the high places, shattered the sacred pillars, hewed down the Asherah, and pulverized the bronze serpent that Moses had fashioned, for up to that time the sons of Israel had been offering incense to it; and it was called Nehushtan.
He reposed his trust in the LORD, the God of Israel; among all the kings of Judah who preceded or succeeded him, none was comparable to him.
He adhered steadfastly to the LORD, never deviating from His pursuit, and observed the commandments that the LORD had enjoined upon Moses.
The LORD was with him; wherever he marched, he prospered. He defied the king of Assyria and refused to render him homage.
He smote the Philistines even unto Gaza and its borders, from watchtower to fortified city.
In the fourth year of King Hezekiah—which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel—Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, ascended against Samaria and invested it.
At the close of three years they seized it; in the sixth year of Hezekiah—that is, the ninth year of Hoshea, king of Israel—Samaria fell.
The king of Assyria deported Israel to Assyria and resettled them in Halah, along the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.
Because they had not hearkened to the voice of the LORD their God, but had transgressed His covenant and all that Moses, the servant of the LORD, had commanded; they neither listened nor executed.
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib, king of Assyria, advanced against all the fortified cities of Judah and subdued them.

Hezekiah, king of Judah, dispatched envoys to the king of Assyria at Lachish, saying, “I have transgressed; withdraw from me; whatever tribute you impose upon me, I shall discharge.” And the king of Assyria exacted from Hezekiah, king of Judah, three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
Hezekiah surrendered all the silver found in the house of the LORD and in the royal treasuries.
At that juncture Hezekiah stripped the gold from the doors of the temple of the LORD and from the doorposts that Hezekiah, king of Judah, had overlaid, and delivered it to the king of Assyria.

The king of Assyria dispatched Tartan, Rab-saris, and Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah with a formidable host against Jerusalem. They ascended and arrived at Jerusalem, and took position by the conduit of the upper pool, which is on the highway to the Fuller’s Field.
They summoned the king; and Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was superintendent of the household, together with Shebna the scribe and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, went out to meet them.
Rabshakeh said to them, “Pray, convey to Hezekiah: Thus speaks the great king, the king of Assyria: ‘What is this confidence upon which you rely?’
‘You assert—though it is but empty rhetoric—counsel and martial prowess. Now upon whom do you rely, that you have rebelled against me?’

‘Now observe: you have placed your confidence in Egypt, that splintered reed, this staff of cane; should a man lean upon it, it will penetrate his palm and lacerate it. Thus Pharaoh, king of Egypt, is to all who trust in him.’

‘Yet if you say to me, “We trust in the LORD our God,” is it not He whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, while he enjoined Judah and Jerusalem, “You shall prostrate yourselves before this altar in Jerusalem”?’
‘Now, then, strike a bargain with my lord the king of Assyria: I shall furnish you two thousand horses, if you can, on your side, mount riders upon them.’
‘How then could you repel even a single captain among the least of my master’s servants? Yet you have trusted in Egypt for chariots and cavalry.’
‘Have I, perchance, ascended against this place to devastate it apart from the LORD? The LORD Himself said to me, “Ascend against this land and ravage it.”’”

Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebna, and Joah said to Rabshakeh, “Pray, address your servants in Aramaic, for we comprehend it; do not speak with us in the Judean tongue within earshot of the people upon the wall.”

Rabshakeh replied, “Has my master dispatched me to utter these words to your master and to you alone, and not to the men seated upon the wall, who with you shall eat their own dung and drink their own urine?”
Rabshakeh then stood and cried with a loud voice in the Judean language, saying, “Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria.
Thus says the king: Let not Hezekiah beguile you, for he is powerless to deliver you from his hand.
Nor let Hezekiah induce you to trust in the LORD by saying, ‘The LORD will certainly rescue us; this city shall not be surrendered into the hand of the king of Assyria.’
Do not heed Hezekiah; for thus says the king of Assyria: Conclude peace with me and surrender to me, and each of you shall eat of his own vine and fig tree and drink from his own cistern.

Until I arrive and remove you to a land resembling your own—a land of grain and new wine, of bread and vineyards, of olive oil and honey—so that you may live and not perish. Do not heed Hezekiah when he deludes you, saying, ‘The LORD will deliver us.’
Has any god of the nations ever delivered his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Did they deliver Samaria from my hand?
Who among all the gods of the lands has delivered his land from my hand, that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem from my hand?”
But the people held their peace and did not reply to him a single word, for the king’s injunction was, “Do not answer him.”
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah with their garments rent, and reported to him the words of Rabshakeh.
When King Hezekiah received these tidings, he rent his garments, invested himself in sackcloth, and entered the house of the LORD.
He then dispatched Eliakim, the steward of the household, Shebna the scribe, and the senior priests, arrayed in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
They said to him, “Thus says Hezekiah: ‘This day is a day of anguish, chastisement, and blasphemy; for the children have arrived at the birthstool, yet there is no vigor to bring them forth.’

Perchance the LORD your God has heeded all the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master, the king of Assyria, dispatched to revile the living God, and will rebuke the words that the LORD your God has heard. Therefore you shall offer supplication for the remnant that is found.”
So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
Isaiah said to them, “Thus you shall say to your master: Thus says the LORD: Be not dismayed by the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed Me.
Behold, I will instill a spirit in him, so that he shall hear a report and return to his own land, and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.”
When the Rabshakeh learned that the king of Assyria had withdrawn from Lachish, he returned and found him campaigning against Libnah.
Moreover, he heard concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, “Behold, he has marched forth to make war against you,” so he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
“Thus you shall say to Hezekiah king of Judah: ‘Do not let your God, in whom you trust, delude you by asserting, “Jerusalem shall not be delivered into the hand of the king of Assyria.”
Behold, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, devoting them to utter destruction; and shall you be delivered?
Did the gods of the nations deliver those whom my fathers destroyed—Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the sons of Eden who were in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?’”
Hezekiah received the letters from the hand of the messengers and read them; then he ascended to the house of the LORD and spread them out before the LORD.
Hezekiah prayed before the LORD and said, “O LORD, God of Israel, who are enthroned upon the cherubim, You alone are God of all the kingdoms of the earth; You have made heaven and earth.
Incline Your ear, O LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, O LORD, and see; and hear the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to revile the living God.
Truly, O LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste the nations and their lands.
And they have cast their gods into the fire; for they were no gods, but the work of men's hands, wood and stone, so they destroyed them.
Now, therefore, O LORD our God, deliver us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone are the LORD God.”
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Because you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria, I have heard.”
“This is the word that the LORD has spoken concerning him: The virgin daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you; the daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head in derision at you.
Whom have you reproached and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel!

By your messengers you have reproached the Lord, and you have said, ‘With my many chariots I have ascended the heights of the mountains, the farthest reaches of Lebanon; I have felled its tall cedars and its choicest cypresses; I have penetrated its farthest lodging, the forest of its Carmel.’
I have dug and drunk strange waters, and with the soles of my feet I have dried up all the streams of Egypt.”
“Have you not heard? Long ago I ordained it; from ancient days I planned it; now I have brought it to pass, that you should reduce fortified cities to heaps of ruins.

Therefore their inhabitants were bereft of strength; they were dismayed and confounded; they were like grass of the field and tender herb, like grass upon the housetops, blighted before it reaches maturity.
But I know your sitting down and your going out and your coming in, and your raging against Me.
Because you have raged against Me and your arrogance has ascended into My ears, behold, I will put My hook in your nose and My bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way that you came.”

“And this shall be the sign to you: this year you shall eat what grows of itself, and in the second year you shall eat what springs from that; but in the third year sow and reap, and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
And the surviving remnant of the house of Judah shall again strike roots beneath and bear fruit above.
For out of Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and out of Mount Zion survivors; the zeal of the LORD shall accomplish this.”
“Therefore thus says the LORD concerning the king of Assyria: He shall not enter this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor advance against it with a shield, nor raise a siege rampart against it.
By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and he shall not enter this city, says the LORD.
For I will defend this city to deliver it, for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.”
And that night the angel of the LORD went out and struck down 185,000 in the camp of the Assyrians. When people arose early in the morning, behold, all were corpses.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria decamped and went and returned and dwelt in Nineveh.

And as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer, his sons, struck him down with the sword; and they fled into the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son reigned in his stead.
In those days Hezekiah fell gravely ill. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and declared, “Thus says the LORD: ‘Put your affairs in order, for you are about to die; you shall not recover.’”
Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall and prayed to the LORD, saying,
“Please, O the LORD, remember how I have walked before You in truth and with an undivided heart, and have done what is pleasing in Your sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Before Isaiah had gone out into the middle court, the word of the LORD came to him:

“Return and tell Hezekiah, the leader of My people, ‘Thus says the LORD, the God of your father David: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. Behold, I will heal you; on the third day you shall ascend to the house of the LORD.
I will add fifteen years to your life; I will deliver you and this city from the grasp of the king of Assyria; and I will shield this city for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.’”
Then Isaiah said, “Bring a poultice of figs.” So they brought it and applied it to the boil, and he recovered.
Hezekiah asked Isaiah, “What sign will the LORD give that He will heal me and that I shall go up to the house of the LORD on the third day?”
Isaiah replied, “This is the sign from the LORD that He will accomplish what He has promised: shall the shadow advance ten steps, or retreat ten steps?”
Hezekiah said, “It is a trivial matter for the shadow to advance ten steps; no, let the shadow retreat ten steps.”
Then Isaiah the prophet cried out to the LORD, and He caused the shadow to retreat ten steps along the steps by which it had descended—the stairway of Ahaz.
At that time Berodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent envoys with letters and a gift to Hezekiah, because he had heard that Hezekiah had been ill.

Hezekiah welcomed them and showed them his entire treasury—silver, gold, spices, precious oil, his armory, and everything found in his storehouses. There was nothing in his palace or throughout his realm that he did not display to them.
Then the prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and asked, “What did these men say, and from where did they come to you?” Hezekiah replied, “They have come from a distant land—from Babylon.”
Isaiah asked, “What have they seen in your house?” Hezekiah said, “They have seen everything in my house; there is nothing among my treasures that I have not shown them.”
Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the LORD.”
“Behold, days are coming when everything in your house, and all that your fathers have laid up until this day, shall be carried off to Babylon; nothing shall remain, says the LORD.
Some of your own sons, born to you, shall be taken away and made eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good,” for he thought, “Why not, if there will be peace and truth in my days?”
The rest of the deeds of Hezekiah, all his might, and how he made the pool and the conduit and brought water into the city—are they not recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
Hezekiah passed away, joining his ancestors, and his son Manasseh reigned in his place.
Manasseh was twelve years of age when he assumed the throne, and he reigned in Jerusalem for fifty-five years; his mother was Hephzibah.
He perpetrated what was evil in the sight of the the LORD, emulating the abominations of the nations that the the LORD had dispossessed before the Israelites.

He restored the high places that his father Hezekiah had demolished, erected altars to Baal, fashioned an Asherah after the manner of Ahab, king of Israel, and prostrated himself before them in worship and service.
He likewise constructed altars within the house of the the LORD, concerning which the the LORD had declared that He would establish His Name in Jerusalem.
In the two courts of the the LORD’s house he erected altars to the entire celestial host.
He even sacrificed his son by fire, practiced sorcery and divination, consulted mediums and spiritists, and thereby multiplied evil in the sight of the the LORD, provoking Him to anger.

He installed the carved image of the Asherah that he had fabricated within the house concerning which the the LORD had said to David and to Solomon his son, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel, I will put My Name forever.

I will not again cause the feet of Israel to wander from the land that I gave to their fathers, provided they are meticulous in doing all that I have commanded them and all the law that My servant Moses commanded them."
Nevertheless, they did not listen; Manasseh led them astray, so that they acted more wickedly than the nations whom the the LORD had destroyed before the Israelites.
The the LORD spoke through His servants the prophets, saying,
"Because Manasseh, king of Judah, has committed these abominations—acting more wickedly than the Amorites who preceded him—and has caused Judah to sin through his idols,
therefore thus says the the LORD, the God of Israel: Behold, I am bringing calamity upon Jerusalem and Judah, so dreadful that every hearer’s ears will tingle.
I will stretch over Jerusalem the measuring line of Samaria and the plumb line of the house of Ahab, and I will wipe out Jerusalem as one wipes a dish—wiping it and turning it upside down.
I will forsake the remnant of My inheritance and deliver them into the hand of their enemies, so that they become plunder and spoil to all their adversaries.
For they have done evil in My eyes and have provoked Me from the day their fathers departed from Egypt until this day."
Moreover, Manasseh spilled so much innocent blood that he filled Jerusalem from one end to the other, apart from the sin whereby he caused Judah to sin, doing evil in the sight of the the LORD.
As for the remaining acts of Manasseh, all that he did and the sin he committed, are they not recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
Manasseh died and was buried with his fathers in the garden of his house, the garden of Uzza; and his son Amon reigned in his stead.
Amon was twenty-two years of age when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem for two years. His mother was Meshullemeth, daughter of Haruz of Jotbah.
He did evil in the sight of the the LORD, as his father Manasseh had done.
He walked in every way his father had walked, serving the idols his father had served and bowing down to them.
He abandoned the the LORD, the God of his fathers, and did not walk in the way of the the LORD.
The servants of Amon conspired against him and assassinated the king in his own house.
But the people of the land struck down all who had conspired against King Amon, and the people installed his son Josiah as king in his place.
As for the remaining acts of Amon, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
He was buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and his son Josiah reigned in his place.
Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem; his mother was Jedidah, daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath.
He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, walking in all the way of David his father, and he did not turn aside to the right or to the left.
In the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sent Shaphan son of Azaliah son of Meshullam, the scribe, to the house of the LORD, saying,
“Go up to Hilkiah the high priest, and let him total the silver that has been brought into the house of the LORD, which the keepers of the threshold have gathered from the people.
Let it be placed in the hand of the overseers appointed over the work in the house of the LORD, and let them give it to the workmen who are repairing the damage to the house—
to the carpenters, the builders, and the masons—and for the purchase of timber and hewn stone with which to repair the house.
Yet no reckoning shall be required of them for the silver entrusted to their hands, for they are acting in good faith.”
Then Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the scribe, “I have found the book of the Law in the house of the LORD.” Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.

Shaphan the scribe came to the king and reported the matter, saying, “Your servants have poured out the silver that was found in the house and have delivered it into the hand of the overseers of the work, those appointed in the house of the LORD.”
Moreover, Shaphan the scribe told the king, “Hilkiah the priest has given me a book,” and he read it before the king.
When the king heard the words of the book of the Law, he tore his garments.
The king commanded Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king’s servant,

“Go, inquire of the LORD for me, for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that has been found; for great is the wrath of the LORD that is kindled against us, because our fathers did not obey the words of this book, so as to do according to all that is written concerning us.”

So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went and spoke to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum son of Tikvah son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe; she dwelt in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter, and they spoke to her.
She said to them, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Tell the man who sent you to Me,
‘Thus says the LORD: Behold, I am bringing evil upon this place and upon its inhabitants—all the words of the book that the king of Judah has read—

because they have forsaken Me and have burned incense to other gods, provoking Me to anger with all the work of their hands. Therefore My wrath is kindled against this place, and it shall not be quenched.’”
“But to the king of Judah who sent you to inquire of the LORD, thus shall you say to him: ‘Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning the words that you have heard:

Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before the LORD when you heard what I spoke against this place and against its inhabitants, that they should become a desolation and a curse, and because you tore your garments and wept before Me, I also have heard you, declares the LORD.

Therefore, behold, I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace; your eyes shall not see all the evil that I am bringing upon this place.’” And they brought back word to the king.
The king dispatched emissaries, whereupon all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem were convoked before him.

He then ascended to the house of the LORD, accompanied by every man of Judah and every inhabitant of Jerusalem, together with the priests, the prophets, and all the people, from the least to the greatest; and in their hearing he recited the entirety of the words of the book of the covenant discovered in the house of the LORD.

Standing beside the pillar, the king solemnized a covenant before the LORD: that he would walk after the LORD and keep His commandments, testimonies, and statutes with all their heart and soul, thereby establishing the words of this covenant inscribed in the book. And all the people acceded to the covenant.

The king then instructed Hilkiah the high priest, the priests of the second order, and the doorkeepers to remove from the temple of the LORD every vessel fashioned for Baal, for Asherah, and for all the host of heaven; he burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron and conveyed their ashes to Bethel.

He deposed the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed to offer incense upon the high places throughout the cities of Judah and in the environs of Jerusalem; likewise those who burned incense to Baal, to the sun, to the moon, to the constellations, and to all the host of heaven.
He removed the Asherah from the house of the LORD to the Kidron brook outside Jerusalem, burned it there, pulverized it to dust, and scattered that dust upon the graves of the common people.
He demolished the quarters of the cult prostitutes that stood by the house of the LORD, where women wove hangings for Asherah.

He convened all the priests from the cities of Judah and defiled the high places where they had burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba; he also demolished the high places at the gates, including the one at the entrance of the gate of Joshua, the city governor, situated on the left as one entered the city gate.
Yet the priests of the high places were not permitted to ascend to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem; instead, they partook of unleavened bread among their brethren.
He desecrated Topheth in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, so that no one could cause his son or daughter to pass through the fire to Molech.

He removed the horses that the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun at the entrance to the house of the LORD, near the chamber of Nathan-melech the eunuch, which lay in the precincts; and he burned the sun chariots with fire.

The king tore down the altars upon the roof of Ahaz’s upper chamber, which the kings of Judah had erected, as well as the altars Manasseh had built in the two courts of the house of the LORD; he pulverized them and cast their dust into the Kidron brook.

He defiled the high places on the right side of the Mount of Corruption, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Sidonians, for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, and for Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
He shattered the sacred pillars, cut down the Asherim, and filled their sites with human bones.

Furthermore, he demolished the altar at Bethel and the high place that Jeroboam son of Nebat—who had caused Israel to sin—had erected; he burned the high place, reduced it to powder, and incinerated the Asherah.

As Josiah turned, he noticed the tombs on the hill; he sent for the bones, removed them from the tombs, and burned them upon the altar, thereby defiling it, in fulfillment of the word of the LORD proclaimed by the man of God who had foretold these deeds.

He asked, “What monument is that which I behold?” The men of the city replied, “It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and proclaimed the very deeds you have performed against the altar of Bethel.”
He said, “Leave him undisturbed; let no one displace his bones.” So they spared his bones, together with those of the prophet who had come from Samaria.
Josiah likewise removed all the shrines of the high places in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had built to provoke the LORD to anger, and he treated them as he had treated Bethel.
He slaughtered all the priests of the high places upon their altars and burned human bones upon them; then he returned to Jerusalem.
The king commanded all the people, “Observe the Passover to the LORD your God, as it is prescribed in this book of the covenant.”
Indeed, no Passover like it had been observed since the days of the judges who judged Israel, nor throughout the reigns of the kings of Israel and Judah.
Only in the eighteenth year of King Josiah was this Passover celebrated to the LORD in Jerusalem.

Moreover, Josiah eradicated the mediums, the spiritists, the household gods, the idols, and every abomination discerned in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, so that he might fulfill the words of the law written in the book Hilkiah the priest had found in the house of the LORD.
Before him there had been no king like him, who turned to the LORD with all his heart, soul, and might, in accordance with the whole law of Moses; nor did any arise after him who resembled him.
Nevertheless, the LORD did not turn from the fierceness of His great wrath, which had been kindled against Judah because of all the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked Him.
The LORD declared, “I will remove Judah from My sight as I removed Israel; I will reject this city Jerusalem, which I chose, and the house concerning which I said, ‘My name shall be there.’”
The remaining deeds of Josiah, and all that he accomplished, are they not recorded in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
In his days Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt, marched against the king of Assyria at the Euphrates; King Josiah went out to oppose him and was slain at Megiddo as soon as he saw him.

His servants conveyed him dead in a chariot from Megiddo, brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his own tomb. Then the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah, anointed him, and enthroned him in his father’s place.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king; he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, following all that his fathers had done.
Pharaoh Neco imprisoned him at Riblah in the land of Hamath, preventing his reign in Jerusalem, and imposed upon the land a tribute of one hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of his father Josiah, changed his name to Jehoiakim, and carried Jehoahaz away; he went to Egypt and died there.

Jehoiakim paid the silver and gold to Pharaoh; yet to raise the money he taxed the land according to Pharaoh’s demand, exacting from each person according to his assessment in order to remit it to Pharaoh Neco.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king; he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother was Zebudah daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.
He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done.
During Jehoiakim's reign, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, advanced against the land; Jehoiakim served as his vassal for three years, after which he defected and rebelled.

The LORD, in His wrath, dispatched against him bands of Chaldeans, Arameans, Moabites, and Ammonites, and sent them against Judah to destroy it, in fulfillment of the word the LORD had spoken through His servants the prophets.
This calamity befell Judah solely by the LORD's decree, so that He might expel them from His presence, on account of the sins of Manasseh and all that he had wrought.
Moreover, there was the innocent blood he had spilled—Jerusalem itself had been saturated with it—and the LORD was unwilling to forgive.
As for the remaining deeds of Jehoiakim and all that he accomplished, are they not recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
Jehoiakim then died and was gathered to his ancestors, and his son Jehoiachin succeeded him upon the throne.
Nor did the king of Egypt venture forth from his own territory again, for the king of Babylon had seized everything from the Brook of Egypt to the Euphrates that had once belonged to Egypt.
Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he ascended the throne, and he reigned in Jerusalem for three months. His mother was Nehushta, daughter of Elnathan, from Jerusalem.
He practiced what was evil in the sight of the LORD, emulating in every respect the conduct of his father.
It was in those days that the officers of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, advanced against Jerusalem, and the city was subjected to siege.
Nebuchadnezzar himself then marched against the city while his forces maintained the siege.

Whereupon Jehoiachin, king of Judah, surrendered to the king of Babylon—together with his mother, his courtiers, his officials, and his eunuchs—and the king of Babylon took him captive in the eighth year of that monarch's reign.

He stripped from that place all the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the royal palace, and he hacked to pieces all the gold vessels that Solomon, king of Israel, had fashioned for the temple of the LORD, just as the LORD had foretold.
He exiled the entire populace of Jerusalem—its princes, its warriors of valor, its artisans and smiths, some ten thousand captives in all—leaving behind only the most destitute of the land.
He carried Jehoiachin off to Babylon, along with the queen mother, the king’s wives, his officials, and the leading men of the land; these he led into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.
There were seven thousand fighting men, together with a thousand craftsmen and smiths—all of them valiant men trained for war—and the king of Babylon brought them all captive to Babylon.
The king of Babylon then installed Mattaniah, Jehoiachin’s uncle, as king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
He, too, did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, following in all respects the pattern set by Jehoiakim.
For it was through the LORD’s anger that events unfolded in Jerusalem and Judah until He cast them from His presence; and Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

In the ninth year of his reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, advanced against Jerusalem with his entire host; he encamped against the city and constructed siege works encircling it.
The city remained under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
By the ninth day of the fourth month, famine had become severe in the city, and the people had no bread.

Then the city wall was breached, and all the men of war fled by night through the gate between the two walls near the king’s garden, though the Chaldeans surrounded the city; they took the road toward the Arabah.
The Chaldean army pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and all his troops deserted him.
They seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where judgment was pronounced upon him.
They slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes, then blinded Zedekiah, bound him in bronze shackles, and carried him off to Babylon.

In the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month—it was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon—Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard and a servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
He burned the house of the LORD, the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem; every great house he consumed with fire.
The whole Chaldean army under the captain of the guard tore down the walls surrounding Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, carried into exile the rest of the people who remained in the city, the deserters who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude.
But the captain of the guard left some of the poorest of the land to be vinedressers and plowmen.
The Chaldeans broke in pieces the bronze pillars, the stands, and the bronze sea that were in the house of the LORD, and carried their bronze to Babylon.
They also took the pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the spoons, and all the bronze vessels used in the temple service.
The captain of the guard took the firepans and the bowls, together with whatever vessels were of gold or of silver.
As for the two pillars, the one sea, and the stands that Solomon had made for the house of the LORD, the bronze of all these vessels was beyond weighing.

The height of one pillar was eighteen cubits, its bronze capital was three cubits high, and a network with pomegranates of bronze encircled the capital all around; the second pillar was the same, with its network.
The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold.

From the city he took one officer who had been in command of the men of war, five men of the king’s council who were found in the city, the scribe of the commander of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.
Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
The king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was carried away from its land into exile.
Over the people who remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, he appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan.

When all the commanders of the armies and their men heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah, they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, and their men.
Gedaliah swore to them and their men and said, “Do not fear the servants of the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be well with you.”

But in the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama, of the royal family, came with ten men and struck down Gedaliah, so that he died, together with the Jews and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
Then all the people, from the least to the greatest, and the commanders of the armies, arose and went to Egypt, for they were afraid of the Chaldeans.

In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Judah, on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of prison.
He spoke kindly to him and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
He changed Jehoiachin’s prison garments, and he ate bread continually in the king’s presence all the days of his life.
And his allowance, a regular allowance from the king, was given to him daily, for all the days of his life.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Diphath, and Togarmah.
The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.
The sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca; the sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
Cush fathered Nimrod, who began to be a mighty warrior on the earth.
Mizraim fathered the Ludim, the Anamim, the Lehabim, and the Naphtuhim,
the Pathrusim, the Casluhim (from whom the Philistines came), and the Caphtorim.
Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn, and Heth,
and the Jebusite, the Amorite, the Girgashite,
the Hivite, the Arkite, the Sinite,
the Arvadite, the Zemarite, and the Hamathite.
The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.
Arphaxad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
To Eber were born two sons: one was named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided; and his brother was named Joktan.
Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab; all these were the sons of Joktan.
The sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael.
These are their generations: Nebaioth the firstborn of Ishmael, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, and Tema,
Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah; these are the sons of Ishmael.
The sons of Keturah, Abraham's concubine: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah; the sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.
The sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah; all these were the sons of Keturah.
Abraham fathered Isaac; the sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel.
The sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.
The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
The sons of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
The sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam; and Timna was Lotan's sister.
The sons of Shobal: Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam; the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah.
The sons of Anah: Dishon; the sons of Dishon: Hamran, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan; the sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the Israelites: Bela son of Beor, whose city was named Dinhabah.
When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his place.
When Jobab died, Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.
When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place; the name of his city was Avith.
When Hadad died, Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.
When Samlah died, Shaul of Rehoboth on the River reigned in his place.
When Shaul died, Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place.
When Baal-hanan died, Hadad reigned in his place; the name of his city was Pai, and his wife's name was Mehetabel daughter of Matred, daughter of Mezahab.
When Hadad died, the chiefs of Edom were Chief Timna, Chief Aliah, Chief Jetheth,
Chief Oholibamah, Chief Elah, Chief Pinon,
Chief Kenaz, Chief Teman, Chief Mibzar,
Chief Magdiel, and Chief Iram; these are the chiefs of Edom.
These are the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun;
Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
The sons of Judah were Er, Onan, and Shelah—three born to him by Bath-shua the Canaanite. Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the LORD, so He put him to death.
His daughter-in-law Tamar bore him Perez and Zerah, so that Judah had five sons in all.
The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Zerah were Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara—five in all.
The sons of Carmi were Achar, the troubler of Israel, who violated the devoted thing.
The son of Ethan was Azariah.
The sons born to Hezron were Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb.
Ram fathered Amminadab, and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, the prince of the sons of Judah.
Nahshon fathered Salma, and Salma fathered Boaz.
Boaz fathered Obed, and Obed fathered Jesse.
Jesse fathered Eliab his firstborn, Abinadab the second, and Shimea the third;
Nethanel the fourth and Raddai the fifth;
Ozem the sixth and David the seventh.
Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. The sons of Zeruiah were Abishai, Joab, and Asahel—three in all.
Abigail bore Amasa, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.
Caleb son of Hezron had children by his wife Azubah and by Jerioth; these were her sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
When Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath, who bore him Hur.
Hur fathered Uri, and Uri fathered Bezalel.
Afterward Hezron married the daughter of Machir, the father of Gilead, whom he took when he was sixty years old, and she bore him Segub.
Segub fathered Jair, who possessed twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.
Geshur and Aram took the towns of Jair from them, together with Kenath and its villages—sixty towns in all. All these were descendants of Machir, the father of Gilead.
After Hezron died at Caleb-ephrathah, Abijah, Hezron’s wife, bore him Ashhur, the father of Tekoa.
The sons of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron, were Ram the firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
Jerahmeel had another wife named Atarah; she was the mother of Onam.
The sons of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel, were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
The sons of Onam were Shammai and Jada. The sons of Shammai were Nadab and Abishur.
The name of Abishur’s wife was Abihail, and she bore him Ahban and Molid.
The sons of Nadab were Seled and Appaim; Seled died without children.
The son of Appaim was Ishi; the son of Ishi was Sheshan; and the son of Sheshan was Ahlai.
The sons of Jada, the brother of Shammai, were Jether and Jonathan; Jether died without children.
The sons of Jonathan were Peleth and Zaza. These were the sons of Jerahmeel.
Sheshan had no sons, only daughters; but he had an Egyptian servant named Jarha.
Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant as a wife, and she bore him Attai.
Attai fathered Nathan; Nathan fathered Zabad.
Zabad fathered Ephlal; Ephlal fathered Obed.
Obed fathered Jehu; Jehu fathered Azariah.
Azariah fathered Helez; Helez fathered Eleasah.
Eleasah fathered Sismai; Sismai fathered Shallum.
Shallum fathered Jekamiah; Jekamiah fathered Elishama.
The sons of Caleb, the brother of Jerahmeel, were Mesha his firstborn, who was the father of Ziph, and the sons of Mareshah, the father of Hebron.
The sons of Hebron were Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
Shema fathered Raham, the father of Jorkoam; Rekem fathered Shammai.
The son of Shammai was Maon, and Maon was the father of Beth-zur.
Caleb’s concubine Ephah bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez; Haran fathered Gazez.
The sons of Jahdai were Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
Caleb’s concubine Maacah bore Sheber and Tirhanah.
She also bore Shaaph, the father of Madmannah, and Sheva, the father of Machbenah and the father of Gibea; and Caleb’s daughter was Achsah.
These were the sons of Caleb. The sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, were Shobal, the father of Kiriath-jearim;
Salma, the father of Bethlehem; and Hareph, the father of Beth-gader.
Shobal, the father of Kiriath-jearim, had sons: Haroeh and half of the Menuhoth.
The families of Kiriath-jearim were the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites; from them came the Zorathites and the Eshtaolites.
The descendants of Salma were Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth-beth-joab, half of the Manahathites, and the Zorites.
The families of scribes who dwelt at Jabez were the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. These are the Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.
Now these were the sons of David born to him in Hebron: Amnon the firstborn, by Ahinoam the Jezreelitess; Daniel the second, by Abigail the Carmelitess;
Absalom the third, son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; and Adonijah the fourth, son of Haggith.
Shephatiah the fifth, by Abital; and Ithream the sixth, by his wife Eglah.
Six were born to him in Hebron, where he reigned seven years and six months; he reigned in Jerusalem thirty-three years.
These were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon—four by Bath-shua daughter of Ammiel;
Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet—nine in all.
All these were sons of David, besides the sons of his concubines; and Tamar was their sister.
Solomon’s son was Rehoboam; Abijah was his son, Asa his son, and Jehoshaphat his son.
Jehoram was his son, Ahaziah his son, and Joash his son.
Amaziah was his son, Azariah his son, and Jotham his son.
Ahaz was his son, Hezekiah his son, and Manasseh his son.
Amon was his son, Josiah his son.
The sons of Josiah were Johanan the firstborn, Jehoiakim the second, Zedekiah the third, and Shallum the fourth.
The sons of Jehoiakim were Jeconiah his son and Zedekiah his son.
The sons of Jeconiah the captive were Shealtiel his son;
and Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
The sons of Pedaiah were Zerubbabel and Shimei. The sons of Zerubbabel were Meshullam and Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister.
And Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-hesed—five in all.
The sons of Hananiah were Pelatiah and Jeshaiah, and the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, and the sons of Shecaniah.
The sons of Shecaniah were Shemaiah. The sons of Shemaiah were Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat—six in all.
The sons of Neariah were Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam—three in all.
The sons of Elioenai were Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani—seven in all.
Judah’s sons were Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
Reaiah, the son of Shobal, fathered Jahath; Jahath, in turn, fathered Ahumai and Lahad, and these men constituted the clans of the Zorathites.
Etam’s sons were Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash, and their sister was Hazzelelponi.
Penuel fathered Gedor, whereas Ezer fathered Hushah; these were Hur’s sons, Hur being Ephrathah’s firstborn and Bethlehem’s progenitor.
Ashhur, Tekoa’s father, had two wives, Helah and Naarah.
Naarah bore him Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari, and these were Naarah’s sons.
Helah’s sons were Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan.
Koz fathered Anub and Zobebah, along with the clans of Aharhel, Harum’s son.
Jabez surpassed his brothers in honor, and his mother named him Jabez, declaring, “Because I bore him in pain.”

Jabez invoked the God of Israel, saying, “If You will indeed bless me and enlarge my territory, and if Your hand will accompany me, and if You will preserve me from harm so that I might not suffer pain.” And God granted his petition.
Chelub, Shuhah’s brother, fathered Mehir, who became Eshton’s father.
Eshton fathered Beth-rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah, Ir-nahash’s father; these were Recah’s men.
Kenaz’s sons were Othniel and Seraiah, and Othniel’s son was Hathath.
Meonothai fathered Ophrah, and Seraiah fathered Joab, Ge-harashim’s father, because they were artisans.
Caleb, Jephunneh’s son, had sons Iru, Elah, and Naam, and Elah’s son was Kenaz.
Jehallelel’s sons were Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
Ezrah’s sons were Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon; Mered’s wife, Bithiah, Pharaoh’s daughter, bore Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah, Eshtemoa’s father.
His Judean wife bore Jered, Gedor’s father; Heber, Soco’s father; and Jekuthiel, Zanoah’s father. These were the sons of Bithiah, Pharaoh’s daughter, whom Mered married.
The sons of Hodiah’s wife, Naham’s sister, were the fathers of Keilah the Garmite and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.
Shimon’s sons were Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan, and Tilon; Ishi’s sons were Zoheth and Ben-zoheth.
Shelah, Judah’s son, had sons Er, Lecah’s father; Laadah, Mareshah’s father; and the families of the linen workers at Beth-ashbea.
Jokim, the men of Cozeba, Joash, and Saraph—who ruled in Moab—and Jashubi-lehem: these are matters of antiquity.
They were potters and residents of Netaim and Gederah, and they dwelt there in royal service.
Simeon’s sons were Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
Shallum was his son, Mibsam his son, and Mishma his son.
Mishma’s sons were Hammuel his son, Zaccur his son, and Shimei his son.
Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, though his brothers did not have numerous children, and their entire family did not multiply as abundantly as Judah’s sons.
They settled in Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar-shual,
Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susim, Beth-biri, and Shaaraim; these were their cities until David reigned.
Their villages included Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan—five cities—together with
all their surrounding villages as far as Baal. These were their settlements, and they maintained their genealogical registers.
Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah the son of Amaziah,
Joel, Jehu the son of Joshibiah, the son of Seraiah, the son of Asiel,
Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,
and Ziza the son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemaiah.
These named individuals were clan leaders, and their ancestral houses increased prodigiously.
They journeyed to Gedor’s entrance, east of the valley, seeking pasture for their flocks.
They discovered rich, excellent pasture, and the land was broad, tranquil, and secure, because Hamites had previously inhabited it.

These men, recorded by name, acted in Hezekiah’s reign, king of Judah; they attacked their tents and the Meunites found there, devoted them to destruction to this day, and occupied their place, since pasture for their flocks was there.
Five hundred of them—men of the Simeonites—went to Mount Seir, led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, sons of Ishi.
They struck down the remnant of the Amalekites who had escaped, and they have resided there to this day.

The sons of Reuben, Israel's firstborn—for he indeed was the firstborn—suffered the forfeiture of his primogeniture because he defiled his father's conjugal couch; consequently, his birthright was transferred to the sons of Joseph, son of Israel, and his lineage was not reckoned according to the rights of the firstborn.
For Judah prevailed over his brethren and produced the ruler, although the birthright itself remained Joseph's.
The sons of Reuben, Israel's firstborn, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
The descendants of Joel were Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, and Shimei his son;
his son was Micah, his son was Reaiah, his son was Baal;
his son was Beerah, whom Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, carried into exile, and he was a chieftain of the Reubenites.
His kinsmen, according to their clans and as registered in their genealogies, were Jeiel the chief and Zechariah.
Bela, son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel, dwelt in Aroer, extending as far as Nebo and Baal-meon.
He also settled eastward to the entrance of the wilderness, from the Euphrates River, because their herds had multiplied in the land of Gilead.
In the days of Saul they waged war against the Hagrites, who fell into their power; and they occupied their tents throughout the whole eastern expanse of Gilead.
The sons of Gad dwelt opposite them in the land of Bashan, as far as Salecah.
Joel was the chief, Shapham the second, and Janai and Shaphat were in Bashan.
Their kinsmen according to their fathers' houses were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber—seven in all.
These were the sons of Abihail, son of Huri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz.
Ahi, son of Abdiel, son of Guni, was chief of their fathers' houses.
They settled in Gilead, in Bashan and its towns, and throughout all the pasturelands of Sharon, to their outer limits.
All of these were enrolled in the days of Jotham, king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam, king of Israel.

The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had valiant warriors—men bearing shield and sword, drawing the bow, and trained in war—forty-four thousand seven hundred sixty, who went out to battle.
They waged war against the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.

They were helped against them, and the Hagrites and all who were with them were delivered into their hand, because they cried out to God in the battle; and He was entreated by them, because they trusted in Him.
They seized their livestock—fifty thousand camels, two hundred fifty thousand sheep, two thousand donkeys—and one hundred thousand captives.
For many fell slain, because the warfare was of God; and they dwelt in their place until the exile.
The sons of the half-tribe of Manasseh dwelt in the land; they were numerous from Bashan to Baal-hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.
These were the heads of their fathers' houses: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel—mighty men of valor, men of renown, heads of their fathers' houses.
But they transgressed against the God of their fathers, and gave themselves to the gods of the peoples of the land, whom God had destroyed before them.

So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul, king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, and he carried them away—the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh—and brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river Gozan, to this day.
The sons of Levi were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Amram were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam; and the sons of Aaron were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Eleazar fathered Phinehas, and Phinehas fathered Abishua.
Abishua fathered Bukki, and Bukki fathered Uzzi.
Uzzi fathered Zerahiah, and Zerahiah fathered Meraioth.
Meraioth fathered Amariah, and Amariah fathered Ahitub.
Ahitub fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Ahimaaz.
Ahimaaz fathered Azariah, and Azariah fathered Johanan.
Johanan fathered Azariah, who served as priest in the house that Solomon built in Jerusalem.
Azariah fathered Amariah, and Amariah fathered Ahitub.
Ahitub fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Shallum.
Shallum fathered Hilkiah, and Hilkiah fathered Azariah.
Azariah fathered Seraiah, and Seraiah fathered Jehozadak.
Jehozadak went into exile when the LORD carried Judah and Jerusalem into exile by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.
The sons of Levi were Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.
These are the names of the sons of Gershom: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to their fathers’ houses.
For Gershom: Libni his son, Jahath his son, Zimmah his son,
Joah his son, Iddo his son, Zerah his son, and Jeatherai his son.
The sons of Kohath: Amminadab his son, Korah his son, and Assir his son;
Elkanah his son, Ebiasaph his son, and Assir his son;
Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uzziah his son, and Saul his son.
The sons of Elkanah were Amasai and Ahimoth.
From Ahimoth the line ran Elkanah, Zophai, and Nahath;
The sons of Samuel were Vashni the firstborn and Abijah.
The sons of Merari: Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, and Uzzah his son;
Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, and Asaiah his son.
These are the men David appointed to direct the music in the house of the LORD after the ark came to rest.
They ministered with song before the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, until Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, and thereafter they served according to their prescribed order.

Among the sons of the Kohathites stood Heman the singer, son of Joel, son of Samuel, son of Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Eliel, son of Toah, son of Zuph, son of Elkanah, son of Mahath, son of Amasai, son of Elkanah, son of Joel, son of Azariah, son of Zephaniah, son of Tahath, son of Assir, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, son of Israel.

His brother Asaph stood at his right hand: Asaph, son of Berechiah, son of Shimea, son of Michael, son of Baaseiah, son of Malchijah, son of Ethni, son of Zerah, son of Adaiah, son of Ethan, son of Zimmah, son of Shimei, son of Jahath, son of Gershom, son of Levi.

On the left stood their brothers, the sons of Merari: Ethan, son of Kishi, son of Abdi, son of Malluch, son of Hashabiah, son of Amaziah, son of Hilkiah, son of Amzi, son of Bani, son of Shemer, son of Mahli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Levi.
Their fellow Levites were assigned to all the service of the tabernacle of the house of God,

while Aaron and his sons were charged with the work of the most holy place: they offered on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense, and they made atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses, the servant of God, had commanded.
The sons of Aaron were Eleazar, Phinehas, Abishua, Bukki, Uzzi, Zerahiah, Meraioth, Amariah, Ahitub, Zadok, and Ahimaaz.

These were their settlements within their territories: to the sons of Aaron of the Kohathite families, for the lot fell to them, they gave Hebron in the land of Judah with its surrounding pasturelands.
The fields and villages of that city, however, were given to Caleb son of Jephunneh.
To the sons of Aaron they gave the city of refuge, Hebron, together with Libnah, Jattir, Eshtemoa, and their pasturelands,
Ashan, and Beth-shemesh with their pasturelands.
From the tribe of Benjamin they gave Geba, Alemeth, and Anathoth with their pasturelands—thirteen cities in all for their families.
The remaining sons of Kohath received by lot ten cities from the half-tribe of Manasseh.
The sons of Gershom received thirteen cities by families from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Manasseh in Bashan.
The sons of Merari received twelve cities by lot from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
Thus the Israelites gave the Levites these cities and their pasturelands.
They allotted by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin the cities named above.
Some of the Kohathite families had cities in the territory of Ephraim:
Shechem, a city of refuge, with its pasturelands in the hill country of Ephraim, together with Gezer and its pasturelands,
Jokmeam and its pasturelands, Beth-horon and its pasturelands,
Aijalon and its pasturelands, and Gath-rimmon and its pasturelands.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh they gave to the remaining Kohathite families Aner and its pasturelands and Bileam and its pasturelands.
To the sons of Gershom from the family of the half-tribe of Manasseh they gave Golan in Bashan and its pasturelands and Ashtaroth and its pasturelands.
From Issachar they gave Kedesh, Daberath, Ramoth, and Anem with their pasturelands;
from Asher, Mashal, Abdon, Hukok, and Rehob with their pasturelands;
and from Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kiriathaim with their pasturelands.
To the remaining sons of Merari from Zebulun they gave Rimmono and Tabor with their pasturelands.
From Reuben, east of the Jordan at Jericho, they gave Bezer in the wilderness, Jahzah, Kedemoth, and Mephaath with their pasturelands.
From Gad they gave Ramoth in Gilead, Mahanaim, Heshbon, and Jazer with their pasturelands.
The sons of Issachar were Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron—four in all.

The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Samuel—heads of their ancestral houses belonging to Tola—were mighty men of valor according to their generations; in the days of David their number was twenty-two thousand six hundred.
The sons of Uzzi: Izrahiah; and the sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah—all five of them chiefs.
With them, by their generations, according to their ancestral houses, were companies of the household: thirty-six thousand troops for war, because they had many wives and sons.
Their kinsmen of all the families of Issachar—mighty men of valor, every one of them—numbered eighty-seven thousand by genealogical reckoning.
The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, and Jediael—three.
The sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri—five heads of ancestral houses; mighty men of valor; and their genealogical enumeration was twenty-two thousand thirty-four.
The sons of Becher: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth—all these were sons of Becher.
Their genealogy by their generations, as heads of their ancestral houses, mighty men of valor, was twenty thousand two hundred.
The sons of Jediael: Bilhan; and the sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
All these were sons of Jediael, by the heads of their fathers' houses, mighty men of valor—seventeen thousand two hundred who went out to war.
Shuppim and Huppim were sons of Ir; Hushim was a son of Aher.
The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum—the sons of Bilhah.
The sons of Manasseh: Asriel, whom his Aramean concubine bore; she also bore Machir, the father of Gilead.
Machir took a wife for Huppim and for Shuppim; his sister's name was Maacah; and the second was named Zelophehad, who had daughters.
Maacah, Machir's wife, bore a son and called his name Peresh; his brother's name was Sheresh; and his sons were Ulam and Rakem.
The sons of Ulam: Bedan. These were the sons of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh.
His sister Hammoleketh bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
The sons of Shemida were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
The sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah; Bered was his son; Tahath was his son; Eleadah was his son; Tahath was his son.
Zabad was his son; Shuthelah was his son; Ezer and Elead were his sons; and men of Gath who were born in the land killed them, because they came down to take their livestock.
Their father Ephraim mourned for many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.
He went in to his wife, and she conceived and bore a son; he named him Beriah, because tragedy had befallen his house.
His daughter Sheerah built Lower Beth-horon and Upper Beth-horon, and also Uzzen-sheerah.
Rephah was his son; Resheph was his son; Telah was his son; Tahan was his son.
Laadan was his son; Ammihud was his son; Elishama was his son.
Nun was his son; Joshua was his son.
Their possessions and settlements were Bethel and its towns, Naaran to the east, Gezer and its towns to the west, and Shechem and its towns as far as Ayyah and its towns.
Along the borders of Manasseh: Beth-shean and its towns, Taanach and its towns, Megiddo and its towns, and Dor and its towns. In these the sons of Joseph son of Israel dwelt.
The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and their sister Serah.
The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel, who was the father of Birzaith.
Heber begot Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham, and their sister Shua.
The sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath—these were the sons of Japhlet.
The sons of Shemer: Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram.
The sons of Helem his brother: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
The sons of Zophah: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, and Imrah.
Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
The sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
The sons of Ulla: Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
All these were sons of Asher, heads of their fathers' houses, chosen mighty men of valor, heads of princes, numbered for war in the army—twenty-six thousand; and their genealogy.
Benjamin fathered Bela, his firstborn, together with Ashbel, the second, and Aharah, the third;
Nohah, the fourth, and Rapha, the fifth, complete the enumeration of his principal sons.
Bela's progeny included Addar, Gera, and Abihud;
These were the sons of Ehud, who constitute the ancestral heads of the inhabitants of Geba and who were deported to Manahath.
Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera effected that deportation, and Gera fathered Uzza and Ahihud.
Shaharaim fathered children in the territory of Moab after having dismissed his wives Hushim and Baara.
By his wife Hodesh he fathered Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, and Malcham, together with Jeuz, Sachiah, and Mirmah—these being his sons and heads of ancestral houses.
From Hushim he also fathered Abitub and Elpaal.
Elpaal's sons were Eber, Misham, and Shemed, who built Ono and Lod, including its dependent settlements.
Beriah and Shema served as ancestral heads of the inhabitants of Aijalon and routed the inhabitants of Gath.
The register proceeds with Ahio, Shashak, and Jeremoth;
then Michael, Ishpah, and Joha, the sons of Beriah;
then Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, and Heber;
then Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab, the sons of Elpaal;
and finally Elienai, Zillethai, and Eliel.
Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath were the sons of Shimei;
then Iphdeiah and Penuel, the sons of Shashak;
and then Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri, the sons of Jeroham.
These were the chiefs of their ancestral houses, enumerated according to their generations, and they resided in Jerusalem.
The father of Gibeon resided in Gibeon, and his wife's name was Maacah.
His firstborn was Abdon, followed by Zur, Kish, Baal, and Nadab;
Mikloth fathered Shimeah. These men dwelt over against their kinsmen in Jerusalem, together with those kinsmen.
Ner fathered Kish; Kish fathered Saul; and Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
Jonathan's son was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal fathered Micah.
Micah's sons were Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz fathered Jehoaddah; Jehoaddah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri fathered Moza.
