Moza fathered Binea, whose son was Raphah, whose son was Eleasah, whose son was Azel.
Azel had six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan.
The sons of his brother Eshek were Ulam the firstborn, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third.
Ulam's sons were mighty men of valor and archers; they were prolific in sons and grandsons, one hundred fifty in all, and all these were descendants of Benjamin.
Thus all Israel was enrolled by genealogies, and behold, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah; Judah, however, was carried away to Babylon for its unfaithfulness.
The first inhabitants who dwelt in their holdings in their cities were Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the Nethinim.
From among the descendants of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh, some dwelt in Jerusalem.
Uthai son of Ammihud, son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani, of the sons of Perez son of Judah.
Of the Shilonites, Asaiah the firstborn and his sons.
Of the sons of Zerah, Jeuel, together with his brethren, six hundred and ninety.
Of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Hodaviah, son of Hassenuah.
Ibneiah son of Jeroham; Elah son of Uzzi, son of Michri; and Meshullam son of Shephatiah, son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah.
Nine hundred and fifty-six, together with their brethren according to their generations—all these men being heads of ancestral houses for their respective clans.
Of the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin.
Azariah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, chief officer of the house of God.
Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah; and Maasai son of Adiel, son of Jahzerah, son of Meshullam, son of Meshillemith, son of Immer.
One thousand seven hundred and sixty, together with their brethren, heads of their ancestral houses—valiant men engaged in the service of the house of God.
Of the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari.
Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zichri, son of Asaph.
Obadiah son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah son of Asa, son of Elkanah, who dwelt in the villages of the Netophathites.
The gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, and Ahiman, with their brethren; Shallum was the chief.
To this day they are gatekeepers at the king’s gate on the east, for the camp of the sons of Levi.

Shallum son of Kore, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, and his brethren of the Korahite house, were over the work of the service, keepers of the thresholds of the tent; their fathers had been keepers of the entrance to the camp of the the LORD.
In former times Phinehas son of Eleazar had been their chief, and the the LORD was with him.
Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was gatekeeper at the door of the tent of meeting.

All these, selected as gatekeepers at the thresholds, numbered two hundred and twelve. They were enrolled by genealogy in their villages, for David and Samuel the seer had appointed them to their trusted office.
They and their sons were in charge of the gates of the house of the the LORD, that is, the house of the tent, according to their watches.
The gatekeepers were stationed on the four sides—east, west, north, and south.
Their brethren in their villages were to come in at appointed times, seven days at a time, to serve with them.
For the four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites, were over the chambers and treasuries of the house of God.
They lodged round about the house of God, because the watch was committed to them; they were in charge of the key and opened it morning by morning.
Some of them were in charge of the vessels of service, for they brought them in and took them out by count.
Some were appointed over the vessels and over all the holy vessels, and over the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the frankincense, and the spices.
Some of the sons of the priests compounded the ointment of spices.
Mattithiah, one of the Levites—the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite—was entrusted with the making of the baked cakes.
Some of the sons of the Kohathites, their brethren, were over the showbread, to prepare it Sabbath by Sabbath.
These are the singers, heads of the Levitical ancestral houses, who lodged in the chambers and were free from other duty, because they were engaged in their work day and night.
These were heads of the fathers of the Levites, according to their generations, chief men; these dwelt at Jerusalem.
Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, dwelt in Gibeon; his wife’s name was Maacah.
His firstborn son was Abdon, and then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, and Nadab.
Mikloth fathered Shimeam. These too dwelt alongside their brethren in Jerusalem, opposite their kinsmen.
Ner fathered Kish, Kish fathered Saul, and Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
The son of Jonathan was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal fathered Micah.
The sons of Micah were Pithon, Melech, and Tarea.
Ahaz fathered Jarah, Jarah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; Zimri fathered Moza.
Moza fathered Binea; Rephaiah was his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.
Azel had six sons, whose names were Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan; these were the sons of Azel.
The Philistines arrayed themselves for battle against Israel, whereupon the Israelites fled before them and fell slain upon Mount Gilboa.
The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons, striking down Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul.
The fighting pressed sorely upon Saul, and the archers overtook him and wounded him.

Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised men come and abuse me.” Yet his armor-bearer refused, being seized with great fear; so Saul took up the sword and fell upon it.
When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he likewise fell upon his sword and died.
Thus Saul died, together with his three sons and his entire household.
When all the Israelites in the valley saw that their army had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their cities, and the Philistines came and occupied them.
On the following day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, they found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
They stripped him, took his head and his armor, and sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to proclaim the tidings of victory to their idols and to the people.
They placed his armor in the temple of their gods and fastened his head in the temple of Dagon.
When all the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,
all the valiant men rose up, took away the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons, brought them to Jabesh, buried their bones beneath the oak in Jabesh, and observed a seven-day fast.
Thus Saul died because of his unfaithfulness, which he committed against the LORD in that he did not keep the word of the LORD, and because he consulted a medium, seeking guidance from her.
He did not inquire of the LORD; therefore the LORD put him to death and transferred the kingdom to David, the son of Jesse.
All Israel mustered to David at Hebron and declared, “Behold, we are your own kin.”

Even in former days, while Saul still reigned, you were the one who led Israel forth and brought them in; and the LORD your God said to you, “You shall shepherd My people Israel, and you shall be ruler over My people Israel.”

So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and David covenanted with them there before the LORD; and they anointed David king over Israel, in accordance with the word of the LORD given through Samuel.
Then David and all Israel marched on Jerusalem—that is, Jebus—where the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, dwelt.
The inhabitants of Jebus said to David, “You shall not come in here.” Yet David captured the stronghold of Zion, that is, the City of David.
David declared, “Whoever first strikes down the Jebusites shall be chief and commander.” Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and thereby became chief.
David took up residence in the stronghold; hence they called it the City of David.
He rebuilt the city all around, from the Millo to the surrounding wall, and Joab restored the remainder of the city.
David grew ever greater, for the LORD of Hosts was with him.

Now these are the heads of the mighty men who stood with David and lent him strong support in his kingdom, together with all Israel, to make him king, according to the word of the LORD concerning Israel.
This is the roster of David’s mighty men: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the thirty, who brandished his spear against three hundred men slain in a single encounter.
After him stood Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men.
He was with David at Pas-dammim, where the Philistines had gathered for battle on a field full of barley; the people fled before the Philistines.
But they took their stand in the midst of the field, defended it, struck down the Philistines, and the LORD wrought a great deliverance.
Three of the thirty chief men went down to David at the rock, to the cave of Adullam, while the Philistine host was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.
David was then in the stronghold, and a Philistine garrison held Bethlehem.
David longed and said, “Who will give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem by the gate?”
So the three broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well of Bethlehem by the gate, carried it, and brought it to David; but David refused to drink it and poured it out to the LORD.

He said, “Far be it from me before my God to do this. Shall I drink the blood of these men, who brought it at the risk of their lives?” Therefore he would not drink it. These are the deeds the three mighty men performed.
Abishai, Joab’s brother, was chief of the three; he wielded his spear against three hundred and slew them, winning a name among the three.
He was doubly honored among the three and became their commander, though he did not attain to the first three.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada, a valiant man from Kabzeel, renowned for great deeds, struck down two sons of Ariel of Moab; he also descended into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.

He slew an Egyptian of imposing stature, five cubits tall; the Egyptian bore a spear like a weaver’s beam, yet Benaiah went down to him with a staff, seized the spear from the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.
These were the exploits of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he won a name among the three mighty men.
He was honored among the thirty, though he did not reach the first three; David appointed him over his bodyguard.
Now the mighty men of the forces were: Asahel, Joab’s brother; Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem;
Shammoth the Harorite; Helez the Pelonite;
Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; Abiezer the Anathothite;
Sibbecai the Hushathite; Ilai the Ahohite;
Maharai the Netophathite; Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite;
Ithai son of Ribai of Gibeah of the Benjamites; Benaiah the Pirathonite;
Hurai of the brooks of Gaash; Abiel the Arbathite;
Azmaveth the Baharumite; Eliahba the Shaalbonite;
the sons of Hashem the Gizonite; Jonathan son of Shageh the Hararite;
Ahiam son of Sacar the Hararite; Eliphal son of Ur;
Hepher the Mecherathite; Ahijah the Pelonite;
Hezro the Carmelite; Naarai son of Ezbai;
Joel the brother of Nathan; Mibhar son of Hagri;
Zelek the Ammonite; Naharai the Beerothite, the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah;
Ira the Ithrite; Gareb the Ithrite;
Uriah the Hittite; Zabad son of Ahlai;
Adina son of Shiza the Reubenite, a chief of the Reubenites, with thirty men under his command;
Hanan son of Maacah; and Joshaphat the Mithnite;
Uzzia the Ashterathite; Shama and Jeiel, sons of Hotham the Aroerite;
Jediel son of Shimri, and Joha his brother, the Tizite;
Eliel the Mahavite; Jeribai and Joshaviah, sons of Elnaam; and Ithmah the Moabite;
Eliel, and Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.
These are the men who rallied to David at Ziklag while he was still constrained on account of Saul son of Kish; they ranked among the mighty men, auxiliaries in war.
They were archers, adept with either hand at hurling stones and shooting arrows from the bow—kinsmen of Saul from Benjamin.
Ahiezer the chief, and Joash, sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; Jeziel and Pelet, sons of Azmaveth; Beracah and Jehu the Anathothite;
Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the thirty and over the thirty; Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad the Gederathite;
Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite;
Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam the Korahites;
Joelah and Zebadiah, sons of Jeroham of Gedor.

From Gad there defected to David at the stronghold in the wilderness mighty men of valor, men of the army, bearing shield and spear, whose faces were like the faces of lions and who were swift as gazelles upon the mountains:
Ezer the chief, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third;
Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth;
Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh;
Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth;
Jeremiah the tenth, Machbannai the eleventh.
These were of the sons of Gad, captains of the host: the least of them could confront a hundred, and the greatest a thousand.
These are they who crossed the Jordan in the first month, when it overflowed all its banks, and put to flight all the inhabitants of the valleys, both eastward and westward.
Moreover, men of Benjamin and Judah came to David at the stronghold.

David went out before them and answered, "If you have come to me peaceably to help me, my heart shall be knit to you; but if you have come to betray me to my adversaries, though no violence is in my hands, may the God of our fathers see and judge."

Then the Spirit clothed Amasai, chief of the thirty, and he said, "We are yours, David, and with you, son of Jesse: peace, peace to you, and peace to your helpers, for your God helps you." David received them and appointed them captains of the troop.

Some of Manasseh defected to David when he came with the Philistines against Saul to battle, yet they did not assist them, for the Philistine lords, upon deliberation, sent him away, saying, "At the peril of our heads he will fall to his master Saul."
As he journeyed to Ziklag, there joined him of Manasseh Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zilthai, captains of thousands in Manasseh.
They helped David against the band, for all were mighty men of valor and captains in the army.
For day by day men came to David to help him, until the camp had become a great host, like the host of God.
These are the numbers of the heads of men armed for war who came to David at Hebron, to transfer the kingdom of Saul to him, according to the word of the LORD.
The sons of Judah: 6,800, equipped with shield and spear.
From the sons of Simeon: 7,100 mighty men of valor for the war.
Zadok, a young mighty man of valor, with twenty-two commanders from his father's house.
From the sons of Benjamin, Saul's kinsmen: 3,000, the majority of whom until that time had kept charge of the house of Saul.
From the sons of Ephraim: 20,800 mighty men of valor, famous men in their fathers' houses.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh: 18,000, designated by name to come and make David king.
From the sons of Issachar: 200 chiefs, men endowed with discernment of the times, knowing what Israel ought to do, and all their brethren at their command.
From Zebulun: 50,000 who went out to the army, arrayed for battle with all the implements of war, single-minded in their support.
From Naphtali: 1,000 commanders, with 37,000 men bearing shield and spear.
From Asher: 40,000 who went out to the army, to set the battle in array.
From beyond the Jordan—Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh: 120,000, with all the implements of war.
All these men of war, keeping ranks, came to Hebron with a perfect heart to make David king over all Israel; and all the rest of Israel were of one heart to make David king.
They remained there with David three days, eating and drinking, for their brethren had prepared for them.

Moreover, those near them, as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, brought bread on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen, together with food, flour, fig cakes, raisin cakes, wine, oil, oxen, and sheep in abundance, for there was joy in Israel.
David conferred with all his leaders—the commanders of thousands and of hundreds.

David said to the whole assembly of Israel, “If it seems good to you, and if this proceeds from the LORD our God, let us send word throughout to our brothers who remain in all the territories of Israel, together with the priests and Levites in their cities and pasturelands, that they may assemble with us.
And let us bring back the ark of our God to us, for we did not seek Him in the days of Saul.”
The whole assembly consented to act, for the matter seemed right in the eyes of all the people.
David assembled all Israel—from the Shihor of Egypt to Hamath—to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim.
David and all Israel went up to Baalah, that is, to Kiriath-jearim in Judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, the LORD, who is enthroned between the cherubim—the ark that is called by the Name.
They conveyed the ark of God from the house of Abinadab on a new cart, while Uzzah and Ahio guided the cart.
David and all Israel celebrated before God with all their might, with songs and with harps, lyres, tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
When they reached the threshing floor of Kidon, Uzzah stretched out his hand to steady the ark, for the oxen had stumbled.
Then the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and He struck him down because he had laid his hand upon the ark; so he died there before God.
David was incensed because the LORD had broken out against Uzzah, and he called that place Perez-uzzah, as it is still known today.
David feared God that day and said, “How, then, shall I bring the ark of God to me?”
So David did not remove the ark to the City of David; instead, he turned it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
The ark of God remained in the house of Obed-edom for three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household.
Hiram, king of Tyre, dispatched envoys to David, together with cedar timber, masons, and carpenters, to erect a residence for him.
David perceived that the LORD had established him as king over Israel, for his kingdom had been exalted on high for the sake of His people Israel.
David took additional wives in Jerusalem and fathered still more sons and daughters.
The children born to him in Jerusalem were Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon;
When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, they all went up to seek him; but David heard of their advance and marched out to confront them.
The Philistines came and deployed themselves in the Valley of Rephaim.
David inquired of God, saying, “Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will You deliver them into my hand?” The LORD said to him, “Go up, and I will deliver them into your hand.”
They ascended to Baal Perazim, where David struck them down. Then David said, “God has broken through my enemies by my hand, like a breach of waters.” Therefore that place was called Baal Perazim.
They abandoned their gods there, and David gave orders, so that they were burned with fire.
The Philistines made yet another incursion and spread themselves in the valley.
David inquired of God again, and God said to him, “Do not go up after them; turn away from them, and come upon them opposite the balsam trees.
When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then you shall go out to battle, for God has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines.”
David did as God commanded him, and they struck the camp of the Philistines from Gibeon to Gezer.
The fame of David went out into all lands, and the LORD put the dread of him upon all the nations.
David built houses for himself in the City of David, and he prepared a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it.
Then David said, "No, only the Levites may carry the ark of God, for the LORD chose them to carry the ark of the LORD and to serve Him forever."
David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the LORD to the place he had prepared for it.
David gathered the sons of Aaron and the Levites.
For the Kohathites: Uriel the chief, with one hundred twenty of his kinsmen;
for the Merarites: Asaiah the chief, with two hundred twenty;
for the Gershonites: Joel the chief, with one hundred thirty;
for the Elizaphanites: Shemaiah the chief, with two hundred;
for the Hebronites: Eliel the chief, with eighty;
and for the Uzzielites: Amminadab the chief, with one hundred twelve.
David summoned the priests Zadok and Abiathar, and the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.
He said to them, "You are heads of the Levite fathers; you and your kinsmen sanctify yourselves and bring up the ark of the LORD God of Israel to the place I prepared for it.
Because you did not carry it the first time, the LORD our God broke out against us, since we did not seek Him according to the ordinance."
So the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves to bring up the ark of the LORD God of Israel.
The Levites carried the ark of God on their shoulders with poles, as Moses had commanded according to the word of the LORD.
David told the chiefs of the Levites to appoint their fellow Levites as singers, to raise their voices with joy, accompanied by musical instruments—lyres, harps, and cymbals—sounding aloud.
The Levites appointed Heman son of Joel; from his kinsmen, Asaph son of Berechiah; and from the sons of Merari, Ethan son of Kushaiah.
With them were their kinsmen of the second rank: Zechariah, Ben, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel, the gatekeepers.
The singers Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were to sound the bronze cymbals.
Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah were to play lyres on Alamoth;
Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah were to play harps on the Sheminith, to lead.
Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was in charge of the singing; he directed the singing because he was skillful.
Berechiah and Elkanah were gatekeepers for the ark.
Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer, the priests, blew trumpets before the ark of God; and Obed-edom and Jehiah were gatekeepers for the ark.
So David, the elders of Israel, and the commanders of thousands went to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the house of Obed-edom with rejoicing.
Because God helped the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, they offered seven bulls and seven rams.
David was clothed in a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who carried the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah, the leader of the singing of the singers; David also wore a linen ephod.
Thus all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of the LORD with shouting, with the sound of the horn, with trumpets, and with cymbals, sounding aloud with lyres and harps.
When the ark of the covenant of the LORD came to the City of David, Michal daughter of Saul looked out through the window and saw King David dancing and playing, and she despised him in her heart.
They brought the ark of God and set it in the midst of the tent that David had pitched for it, and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.
When David had finished offering the burnt offering and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD.
He distributed to every Israelite, man and woman alike, a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a raisin cake.
He appointed some of the Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD, to invoke, to give thanks, and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel.
Asaph was the chief, then Zechariah, Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel, with harps and lyres; and Asaph sounded the cymbals.
Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests were to blow trumpets continually before the ark of the covenant of God.
On that day David first committed to Asaph and his brothers the task of thanking the LORD.
Give thanks to the LORD; call upon His name; make known His deeds among the peoples.
Sing to Him, sing praises to Him; recount all His wondrous works.
Glory in His holy name; let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice.
Seek the LORD and His strength; seek His face continually.
Remember the wonders He has done, His marvels and the judgments of His mouth.
O offspring of Israel, His servant, children of Jacob, His chosen ones,
He is the LORD our God; His judgments are in all the earth.
Remember His covenant forever, the word He commanded for a thousand generations,
the covenant He made with Abraham, and His oath to Isaac,
which He established for Jacob as a statute, and for Israel as an everlasting covenant, saying, "To you I will give the land of Canaan as the portion of your inheritance,"
when you were few in number, indeed very few, and sojourners in it,
wandering from nation to nation and from one kingdom to another people.
He allowed no one to oppress them; He rebuked kings on their behalf,
saying, "Do not touch My anointed ones; do My prophets no harm."
Sing to the LORD, all the earth; proclaim His salvation from day to day.
Declare His glory among the nations, His marvelous works among all the peoples.
For great is the LORD and greatly to be praised; He is to be revered above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
Splendor and majesty are before Him; strength and joy are in His place.
Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
Ascribe to the LORD the glory due His name; bring an offering and come before Him; worship the LORD in the splendor of holiness.
Tremble before Him, all the earth; the world is firmly established and cannot be moved.
Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice; let them say among the nations, "The LORD reigns."
Let the sea roar and all that fills it; let the field exult and everything in it.
Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD, for He comes to judge the earth.
Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His steadfast love endures forever.
And say, "Save us, O God of our salvation, and gather us and deliver us from the nations, that we may give thanks to Your holy name and glory in Your praise."
Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.
And all the people said, "Amen!" and praised the LORD.
So he left Asaph and his brothers there before the ark of the covenant of the LORD to minister before the ark continually, as the daily service required.
Obed-edom and his brothers, sixty-eight, together with Obed-edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah, served as gatekeepers.
Zadok the priest and his brothers the priests served before the tabernacle of the LORD at the high place in Gibeon,
to offer burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering regularly, morning and evening, and to do all that is written in the Law of the LORD, which He commanded Israel.
With them were Heman and Jeduthun and the rest who were chosen and expressly named to give thanks to the LORD, because His steadfast love endures forever.
Heman and Jeduthun had trumpets and cymbals and the other instruments for the songs of God, and the sons of Jeduthun were at the gate.
Then all the people departed, each to his own home, and David went home to bless his household.
Now when David had taken up residence in his house, David said to Nathan the prophet, “Behold, I dwell in a house of cedars, but the ark of the covenant of the LORD is beneath tent curtains.”
Nathan said to David, “Do all that is in your heart, for God is with you.”
And it came to pass that night that the word of God came to Nathan, saying,
“Go and say to My servant David, ‘Thus says the LORD: You shall not build Me the house to dwell in.
For I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought up Israel until this day, but I have gone from tent to tent and from tabernacle.
In all places where I walked with all Israel, did I speak a word to any of the judges of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd My people, saying, “Why have you not built Me a house of cedars?”
And now thus you shall say to My servant David: Thus says the LORD of hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be leader over My people Israel.
And I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you; and I will make for you a name like the name of the great ones who are in the earth.

And I will appoint a place for My people Israel, and I will plant them, and they shall dwell in their place and be disturbed no more; and the sons of wickedness shall not oppress them again, as at the beginning and as since the day I appointed judges over My people Israel.
I will subdue all your enemies. Moreover, I declare to you that the LORD will build you a house.
And it shall be when your days are fulfilled to go with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you, who will be from your sons, and I will establish his kingdom.
He shall build Me a house, and I will establish his throne forever.
I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to Me a Son; and I will not take My steadfast love from him, as I removed it from the one who was before you.
And I will establish him in My house and in My kingdom forever, and his throne shall be established forever.’”
According to all these words and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.
Then King David went in and sat before the LORD and said, “Who am I, O the LORD God, and what is my house, that You have brought me thus far?
And this was a small thing in Your eyes, O God; and You have spoken concerning Your servant’s house for a great while to come, and have regarded me according to the manner of man, O the LORD God?
What more can David add to You for honoring Your servant? For You know Your servant.
O the LORD, for Your servant’s sake and according to Your heart, You have done all this greatness, to make known all these great things.
O the LORD, there is none like You, and there is no God besides You, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

And who is like Your people Israel, the one nation on earth whom God went to redeem for Himself a people, to make for Yourself a name of greatness and awesomeness, by driving out nations from before Your people whom You redeemed from Egypt?
And You made Your people Israel Your own people forever, and You, O the LORD, became their God.
And now, O the LORD, let the word that You have spoken concerning Your servant and concerning his house be established forever, and do as You have spoken.
And let Your name be established and magnified forever, saying, ‘The the LORD of hosts is the God of Israel, even a God to Israel, and the house of Your servant David is established before You.’
For You, my God, have revealed to Your servant that You will build him a house; therefore Your servant has found courage to pray before You.
And now, O the LORD, You are God, and You have promised this good thing to Your servant.
And now be pleased to bless the house of Your servant, that it may be before You forever; for You, O the LORD, have blessed, and it is blessed forever.”
Subsequent to these events, David vanquished the Philistines, reduced them to submission, and wrested from their control Gath together with its outlying villages.
He likewise overcame the Moabites, who thereupon entered into vassalage to David and rendered him tribute.
Furthermore, David defeated Hadadezer, king of Zobah, as far as Hamath, while the latter was advancing to establish his dominion at the Euphrates River.
From him David seized a thousand chariots, seven thousand mounted warriors, and twenty thousand infantrymen; he hamstrung all the chariot horses, preserving only a hundred.
When the Arameans of Damascus advanced to succor Hadadezer, king of Zobah, David slew twenty-two thousand of their men.
David then stationed garrisons in Aram of Damascus; the Arameans became subject to him and paid him tribute. Thus the LORD granted David victory in every campaign he undertook.
David also seized the golden shields borne by Hadadezer’s officers and conveyed them to Jerusalem.

From Tibhath and Cun, cities belonging to Hadadezer, David carried off an immense quantity of bronze, which Solomon subsequently employed in fashioning the bronze Sea, the pillars, and sundry bronze vessels.
When Tou, king of Hamath, learned that David had annihilated the whole host of Hadadezer, king of Zobah,

he dispatched his son Hadoram to King David to offer salutations and benedictions, for David had waged war against Hadadezer and vanquished him; indeed, Hadadezer had been hostile to Tou. Hadoram brought articles of every kind in gold, silver, and bronze.
King David consecrated these, together with the silver and gold he had despoiled from all the nations—Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, and Amalek—to the LORD.
Moreover, Abishai, son of Zeruiah, struck down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
He installed garrisons throughout Edom, and all the Edomites were brought under David’s sway. Thus the LORD granted David victory in every campaign.
Thus David reigned over all Israel, dispensing justice and righteousness to all his people.
Joab, son of Zeruiah, commanded the army; Jehoshaphat, son of Ahilud, served as recorder;
Zadok, son of Ahitub, and Abimelech, son of Abiathar, were priests; Shavsha was scribe;
and Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, was over the Cherethites and Pelethites; David’s sons were chief officials in attendance upon the king.
After these things, Nahash, king of the Ammonites, died, and his son succeeded him.

David resolved, “I will show steadfast love to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed steadfast love to me.” Therefore David dispatched messengers to console him concerning his father; and David’s servants came into the land of the Ammonites, to Hanun, to comfort him.

But the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun, “Do you suppose that David is honoring your father because he has sent comforters to you? Have not his servants come to you in order to explore the land, to spy it out, and to overthrow it?”
So Hanun seized David’s servants, shaved them, cut off their garments at the middle, even to their posteriors, and sent them away.
When some went and reported to David concerning the men, he sent to meet them, for the men were deeply humiliated. The king said, “Remain at Jericho until your beards have grown, and then return.”

When the Ammonites perceived that they had made themselves abhorrent to David, Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim, from Aram-maacah, and from Zobah.
They hired thirty-two thousand chariots, together with the king of Maacah and his people, who came and encamped before Medeba; and the Ammonites gathered from their cities and came to the battle.
When David heard of it, he sent Joab and the whole host of the mighty men.
The Ammonites came out and drew up in battle array at the entrance of the city, while the kings who had come were by themselves in the open country.
When Joab saw that the battle was set against him both in front and in the rear, he chose some of the choice men of Israel and arrayed them against the Arameans;
the rest of the people he placed under the command of Abishai his brother, and they arrayed themselves against the Ammonites.
He said, “If the Arameans prove too strong for me, then you shall be my deliverance; but if the Ammonites prove too strong for you, then I will deliver you.
Be strong, and let us be courageous for our people and for the cities of our God; and may the LORD do what is good in His eyes.”
So Joab and the people with him drew near to battle against the Arameans, and they fled before him.
When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they too fled before Abishai and entered the city. Then Joab returned to Jerusalem.

When the Arameans saw that they had been defeated before Israel, they sent messengers and brought out the Arameans who were beyond the River, with Shophach, commander of Hadadezer’s army, at their head.
When this was reported to David, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, came to them, and drew up in battle array against them; David drew up for battle and fought against them.
The Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed seven thousand charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers of the Arameans; he also put to death Shophach, the commander of the army.
When the servants of Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated before Israel, they made peace with David and served him; nor would Aram any longer help the Ammonites.

In the springtime, when monarchs customarily take the field, Joab led forth the army, laid waste the territory of the Ammonites, advanced upon Rabbah, and besieged it, while David remained in Jerusalem; Joab then struck Rabbah and overthrew it.

David seized the crown of their king from his head; finding it to weigh a talent of gold and to be set with a precious stone, he placed it upon his own head, and he carried away from the city an exceedingly great quantity of spoil.

He brought out the inhabitants and consigned them to compulsory labor with saws, iron picks, and axes; he dealt thus with every city of the Ammonites, and then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
Afterward war arose with the Philistines at Gezer, and Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Sippai, one of the descendants of the giants, so that the Philistines were subdued.
War flared again with the Philistines, and Elhanan son of Jair struck down Lahmi, brother of Goliath the Gittite, whose spear shaft resembled a weaver's beam.
Another battle took place at Gath, where a man of prodigious stature—bearing six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in all—also descended from the giants.
When he reviled Israel, Jonathan, son of Shimea (David's brother), struck him down.
These men, descendants of the giants in Gath, fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.
Satan stood against Israel and incited David to number Israel.
David said to Joab and to the commanders of the people, “Go, number Israel from Beersheba to Dan, and bring me their count, that I may know it.”
Joab said, “May the LORD multiply His people a hundredfold. Are they not all, my lord the king, your servants? Why then does my lord require this? Why should it become a guilt for Israel?”
Nevertheless, the king’s word prevailed against Joab; and Joab departed and went throughout all Israel, and came to Jerusalem.
Joab gave David the number of the muster of the people: all Israel had 1,100,000 men who drew the sword, and Judah had 470,000 men who drew the sword.
But Levi and Benjamin he did not number among them, for the king’s command was abhorrent to Joab.
And this thing was evil in the sight of God, and He struck Israel.
David said to God, “I have sinned greatly in that I have done this thing; but now, I pray You, take away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly.”
The LORD spoke to Gad, David’s seer, saying,
“Go and speak to David, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD: I am offering you three things; choose one of them for yourself, that I may do it to you.’”
Gad came to David and said to him, “Thus says the LORD: ‘Choose for yourself.

If three years of famine; or three months to be swept away before your foes, while the sword of your enemies overtakes you; or three days of the sword of the LORD, even pestilence in the land, with the angel of the LORD destroying throughout all the territory of Israel—now consider what answer I shall return to Him who sent me.’”
David said to Gad, “I am in great distress. Let me, I pray, fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are very great; but let me not fall into the hand of man.”
So the LORD sent a pestilence upon Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.

God sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem; and as he was destroying, the LORD saw, and He relented of the calamity, and said to the destroying angel, “It is enough; now withdraw your hand.” The angel of the LORD was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

David lifted up his eyes and saw the angel of the LORD standing between earth and heaven, with his drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem. David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell upon their faces.

David said to God, “Was it not I who commanded the people to be numbered? I indeed have sinned and done wickedly; but these sheep, what have they done? O the LORD my God, let Your hand, I pray, be against me and against my father’s house, but not against Your people, that there be a plague.”
Then the angel of the LORD commanded Gad to say to David that David should go up and raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
So David went up at the word of Gad, which he had spoken in the name of the LORD.
Now Ornan was threshing wheat; and Ornan turned back and saw the angel, and his four sons with him hid themselves.
As David came to Ornan, Ornan looked and saw David, and went out from the threshing floor and bowed down to David with his face to the ground.
David said to Ornan, “Give me the site of the threshing floor, that I may build an altar to the LORD on it; give it to me at the full price, that the plague may be restrained from the people.”

Ornan said to David, “Take it, my lord the king, and do what is good in your eyes. See, I give the oxen for burnt offerings, and the threshing sledges for wood, and the wheat for the grain offering; I give it all.”
King David said to Ornan, “No, but I will surely buy it for the full price; for I will not take what is yours for the LORD, nor offer a burnt offering without cost.”
So David gave Ornan six hundred shekels of gold by weight for the site.
David built an altar to the LORD there, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and called on the LORD; and He answered him with fire from heaven upon the altar of burnt offering.
The LORD spoke to the angel, and he put his sword back into its sheath.
At that time, when David saw that the LORD had answered him at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he sacrificed there.
Now the tabernacle of the LORD, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering, were at that time at the high place in Gibeon.
But David could not go before it to inquire of God, for he was afraid because of the sword of the angel of the LORD.
Then David declared, “This is the house of the LORD God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel.”
David gave orders to assemble the resident aliens in Israel, and from among them he appointed stonecutters to quarry dressed stone for building the house of God.
He provided iron in abundance for nails for the doors of the gates and for the fittings, and bronze beyond measure.
He also procured cedar timber without stint, for the Sidonians and the Tyrians conveyed an immense quantity of cedar to David.

David said, “My son Solomon is youthful and unseasoned, and the house to be built for the the LORD must be exceedingly magnificent—renowned and resplendent among all the nations. I shall now make provision for it.” So David made copious preparations before his death.
Then he summoned his son Solomon and charged him to build a house for the the LORD, the God of Israel.
David said to Solomon, “My son, it was my heartfelt resolve to build a house for the Name of the the LORD my God.

But the word of the the LORD came to me, saying, “‘You have effused abundant blood and waged mighty wars; you shall not erect a house for My Name, because you have poured out much blood upon the earth in My sight.

Behold, a son shall be born to you; he shall be a man of repose, and I will grant him respite from all his surrounding foes. His name shall be Solomon, and I will bestow upon Israel tranquility and security throughout his days.
He it is who shall build a house for My Name. He shall be My son, and I shall be his Father; I will establish the throne of his kingship over Israel in perpetuity.’
“Now then, my son, may the the LORD be with you, that you may thrive and erect the house of the the LORD your God, according to His word concerning you.
May the the LORD endow you with discernment and understanding, and commission you over Israel, that you may observe the law of the the LORD your God.

Then you shall prosper, provided you are meticulous in observing the statutes and ordinances that the the LORD enjoined upon Moses for Israel. Be resolute and valiant; do not succumb to fear or dismay.

Now behold, in my affliction I have prepared for the house of the the LORD one hundred thousand talents of gold, one million talents of silver, and bronze and iron beyond measure. I have likewise furnished timber and stone, and you may augment them.
Moreover, abundant workmen are with you—stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and artisans skilled in every material—
gold, silver, bronze, and iron beyond enumeration. Arise, then, and execute the work, and may the the LORD be with you.”
David moreover enjoined all the leaders of Israel to assist his son Solomon.

“Is not the the LORD your God with you? Has He not granted you repose on every side? For He has delivered the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land is subdued before the the LORD and before His people.

Now devote your heart and your soul to seeking the the LORD your God. Arise and construct the sanctuary of the the LORD God, that you may convey the ark of the covenant of the the LORD and the sacred vessels of God into the house erected for the Name of the the LORD.”
When David had grown old and reached the fullness of his days, he installed his son Solomon as king over Israel.
He gathered all the leaders of Israel, together with the priests and the Levites.
The Levites—those thirty years of age and older—were enumerated, and their number, reckoned by individual heads, came to thirty-eight thousand men.
Of these, twenty-four thousand were appointed to oversee the work of the house of the LORD, while six thousand served as officers and judges.
Four thousand were gatekeepers, and four thousand praised the LORD with the instruments that David had fashioned for praise.
David then organized them into divisions corresponding to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The Gershonites comprised Laadan and Shimei.
The sons of Laadan were Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel—three in all.
The sons of Shimei were Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran—three—these being the heads of the fathers' houses belonging to Laadan.
The sons of Shimei were Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah—four.
Jahath was the chief and Zizah the second; Jeush and Beriah did not produce many sons, so they were reckoned as one father's house.
The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel—four.
The sons of Amram were Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart to consecrate the most holy things forever: to burn incense before the LORD, to minister to Him, and to bless in His name forever.
Moses, the man of God, had his sons counted among the tribe of Levi.
The sons of Moses were Gershom and Eliezer.
The son of Gershom was Shebuel the chief.
The son of Eliezer was Rehabiah the chief; Eliezer had no other sons, but the descendants of Rehabiah were exceedingly numerous.
The son of Izhar was Shelomith the chief.
The sons of Hebron were Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel were Micah the chief and Isshiah the second.
The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi; the sons of Mahli were Eleazar and Kish.
Eleazar died without sons, having only daughters; their kinsmen, the sons of Kish, married them.
The sons of Mushi were Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth—three.

These were the sons of Levi according to their fathers' houses—the heads of the fathers' houses—as they were registered by name, from twenty years old and upward, those who performed the work for the service of the house of the LORD.
For David had declared, "The LORD, the God of Israel, has given rest to His people, and He dwells in Jerusalem forever."
Therefore the Levites no longer needed to carry the tabernacle or any of its vessels for its service.
For by David's final instructions, the Levites were numbered from twenty years old and upward.

Their station was beside the sons of Aaron for the service of the house of the LORD—over the courts, the chambers, the purification of all holy things, and the work of the service of the house of God—
namely, the arrangement of the showbread, the fine flour for the grain offering, the unleavened wafers, the pan, the mixed offering, and every measure and quantity,
and to stand every morning to give thanks and to praise the LORD, and likewise at evening,
and for all the burnt offerings offered to the LORD on Sabbaths, new moons, and appointed feasts, according to the prescribed number, continually before the LORD.
Thus they kept the charge of the tent of meeting, the charge of the holy place, and the charge of their brothers, the sons of Aaron, for the service of the house of the LORD.
These were the divisions of Aaron's sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu predeceased their father, leaving no sons; therefore Eleazar and Ithamar alone discharged the priestly office.
David, in concert with Zadok—descended from Eleazar—and Ahimelech—descended from Ithamar—organized them for their service according to their assigned duties.
Because the leaders among Eleazar's descendants outnumbered those among Ithamar's, the allotment yielded sixteen patriarchal heads for Eleazar's house and eight for Ithamar's.
They were distributed by lot, impartially, the one group alongside the other, since sacred officials and officials of God were found among both Eleazar's and Ithamar's descendants.

Shemaiah son of Nethanel, the Levite scribe, recorded them before the king, the officials, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the heads of the priestly and Levitical families, assigning one father's house to Eleazar and one to Ithamar.

The lot fell in this order: first to Jehoiarib, second to Jedaiah, third to Harim, fourth to Seorim, fifth to Malchijah, sixth to Mijamin, seventh to Hakkoz, eighth to Abijah, ninth to Jeshua, tenth to Shecaniah, eleventh to Eliashib, twelfth to Jakim, thirteenth to Huppah, fourteenth to Jeshebeab, fifteenth to Bilgah, sixteenth to Immer, seventeenth to Hezir, eighteenth to Happizzez, nineteenth to Pethahiah, twentieth to Jehezkel, twenty-first to Jachin, twenty-second to Gamul, twenty-third to Delaiah, and twenty-fourth to Maaziah.

These were their appointments for ministry, by which they entered the house of the the LORD, in accordance with the ordinance established for them by their father Aaron, as the the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him.
As for the remaining Levites: from Amram's sons, Shubael; from Shubael's sons, Jehdeiah.
From Rehabiah's line, Isshiah was the first.
From the Izharites, Shelomoth; from Shelomoth's sons, Jahath.
The sons of Hebron were Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
From Uzziel's sons, Micah; from Micah's sons, Shamir.
Micah's brother was Isshiah; from Isshiah's sons, Zechariah.
Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi; Jaaziah's son was Beno.
From Merari through Jaaziah came Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
Mahli had Eleazar, who had no sons.
Mushi's sons were Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the Levites according to their ancestral houses.

They too cast lots, just as their kinsmen the Aaronites had done, before King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the priestly and Levitical families, treating the elder house and the younger house alike.

David, together with the military commanders, set apart for service the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, who prophesied with harps, lyres, and cymbals; the number of those assigned to the work of their service was established.
Among the sons of Asaph were Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah, under Asaph's direction, prophesying under the king's supervision.
The sons of Jeduthun were Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah—six in all—under their father Jeduthun's direction, prophesying with the harp in thanksgiving and praise to the LORD.
The sons of Heman were Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
All these were Heman's sons, Heman being the king's seer in the words of God, appointed to exalt his power; and God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

All of them served under their father's direction in the song of the house of the LORD, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, for the service of the house of God, Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman being under the king's supervision.
Together with their brothers, all trained in singing to the LORD—skillful men—they numbered two hundred eighty-eight.
They cast lots for their duties, without distinction between the lesser and the greater, teacher and pupil alike.
The first lot, designated for Asaph, fell to Joseph; the second to Gedaliah, together with his sons and brothers, twelve in number.
The third fell to Zaccur, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The fourth to Izri, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The fifth to Nethaniah, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The sixth to Bukkiah, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The seventh to Jesarelah, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The eighth to Jeshaiah, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The ninth to Mattaniah, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The tenth fell to Shimei, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The eleventh to Azarel, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The thirteenth to Shubael, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The fourteenth to Mattithiah, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The fifteenth to Jeremoth, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The sixteenth to Hananiah, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The seventeenth to Joshbekashah, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The eighteenth fell to Hanani, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The nineteenth to Mallothi, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The twentieth to Eliathah, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The twenty-first to Hothir, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The twenty-second to Giddalti, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The twenty-third to Mahazioth, his sons and brothers, twelve.
The twenty-fourth to Romamti-ezer, his sons and brothers, twelve.

The gatekeeping corps was divided as follows: among the Korahites, Meshelemiah son of Kore—one of the sons of Asaph—presided over a division; and Meshelemiah's sons were, in birth order, Zechariah, Jediael, Zebadiah, Jathniel, Elam, Jehohanan, and Elioenai.
Obed-edom's sons were, likewise in birth order, Shemaiah, Jehozabad, Joah, Sacar, Nethanel, Ammiel, Issachar, and Peullethai, for God had blessed him.
To Shemaiah were born sons who wielded authority within their father's household, being mighty men of valor.
Shemaiah's sons were Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad, while his brothers Elihu and Semachiah were likewise valorous men.
All of these derived from the sons of Obed-edom—themselves, their sons, and their brothers—men of strength and valor, sixty-two in all, for the service.
Meshelemiah also had sons and brothers, valorous men, eighteen in all.

From the sons of Merari, Hosah had sons: Shimri the chief—for although he was not the firstborn, his father designated him chief—followed by Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, and Zechariah the fourth.
Hosah had thirteen sons and brothers in total.
These divisions of the gatekeepers, corresponding to their chief men, were charged with ministering in the house of the LORD, even as their brothers were;
and they cast lots, the lesser and the greater alike, according to their ancestral houses, for every gate.
The lot for the east fell to Shelemiah; and for his son Zechariah, a counselor of discernment, they cast lots, and the north fell to him.
To Obed-edom fell the south, and to his sons the storehouse.
To Shuppim and Hosah fell the west, by the Shallecheth Gate on the ascending road, guard corresponding to guard.
On any given day six Levites stood guard on the east, four on the north, four on the south, and two by two at the storehouse; on the west, at the Parbar, four stood on the road and two at the Parbar.
These were the divisions of the gatekeepers among the sons of Korah and the sons of Merari.
Among the Levites, Ahijah presided over the treasuries of the house of God and over the treasuries of the dedicated things.
The sons of Ladan—the Gershonite descendants of Ladan, and the heads of the ancestral houses of Ladan the Gershonite—were Jehieli;
and the sons of Jehieli, Zetham and his brother Joel, presided over the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
From the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites came Shebuel son of Gershom, son of Moses, who was chief over the treasuries.
His relatives through Eliezer were Rehabiah his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son.

This Shelomith and his brothers were charged with all the treasuries of the dedicated things that King David and the heads of the fathers' houses—the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the commanders of the army—had dedicated.
From the spoil of their battles they dedicated these things to maintain the house of the LORD.
All that Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah had dedicated—everything so dedicated—was placed in the custody of Shelomith and his brothers.
Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were assigned to outside duties for Israel, serving as officers and judges.
Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers—1,700 able men—were in charge of Israel's affairs west of the Jordan, for all the work of the LORD and for the service of the king.

Of the Hebronites, Jerijah was chief according to the genealogies of his fathers; in the fortieth year of David's reign they were sought out, and men of valor were found among them at Jazer in Gilead.

His brothers were 2,700 men of valor, heads of fathers' houses, whom King David appointed over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, for every matter pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king.

The sons of Israel were enumerated according to their number—heads of ancestral houses, commanders of thousands and hundreds, and officers who served the king in every matter concerning the divisions that came in and went out month by month throughout all the months of the year—each division comprising twenty-four thousand men.
Jashobeam son of Zabdiel was over the first division for the first month, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
He was descended from Perez and served as chief of all the army commanders for the first month.
Dodai the Ahohite was over the division for the second month, with Mikloth as leader; and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The third commander, for the third month, was Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
This Benaiah was a mighty man among the Thirty and was over the Thirty, and his son Ammizabad was in charge of his division.
The fourth, for the fourth month, was Asahel, Joab’s brother, with Zebadiah his son succeeding him; and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The fifth, for the fifth month, was Shamhuth the Izrahite, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, of the Ephraimites, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, of the Benjamites, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zerahites, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the Ephraimites, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel, and his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Furthermore, over the tribes of Israel: Eliezer son of Zichri was chief officer of the Reubenites; Shephatiah son of Maacah, of the Simeonites;
Hashabiah son of Kemuel, of the Levites; Zadok, of Aaron;
Elihu, one of David’s brothers, of Judah; Omri son of Michael, of Issachar;
Ishmaiah son of Obadiah, of Zebulun; Jerimoth son of Azriel, of Naphtali;
Hoshea son of Azaziah, of the Ephraimites; Joel son of Pedaiah, of the half-tribe of Manasseh;
Iddo son of Zechariah, of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead; Jaasiel son of Abner, of Benjamin;
Azarel son of Jeroham, of Dan. These were the princes of the tribes of Israel.
But David did not number those twenty years old and under, because the LORD had said He would multiply Israel like the stars of heaven.
Joab son of Zeruiah began to number them but did not finish, for wrath came upon Israel; nor was the total recorded in the chronicles of King David.
Over the king’s treasuries was Azmaveth son of Adiel; over the storehouses in the fields, in the cities, in the villages, and in the towers was Jonathan son of Uzziah;
over those who did the work of the field in tilling the ground was Ezri son of Chelub;
over the vineyards was Shimei the Ramathite; over the produce of the vineyards for the wine cellars was Zabdi the Shiphmite;
over the olive trees and the sycamore trees in the Shephelah was Baal-hanan the Gederite; over the storehouses of oil was Joash;
over the cattle that fed in Sharon was Shitrai the Sharonite; over the cattle in the valleys was Shaphat son of Adlai;
over the camels was Obil the Ishmaelite; over the donkeys was Jehdeiah the Meronothite;
over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite. All these were the officials of King David.
Jonathan, David’s uncle, was also a counselor—a man of understanding and a scribe—and Jehiel son of Hachmoni was with the king’s sons.
Ahithophel was the king’s counselor, and Hushai the Archite was the king’s friend.
After Ahithophel came Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar. The commander of the king’s army was Joab.

David assembled all the officials of Israel at Jerusalem: the officials of the tribes, the commanders of the divisions serving the king, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officials in charge of all the property and livestock of the king and his sons, together with the court officials, the mighty men, and all the valiant warriors.

David rose to his feet and said, “Hear me, my brothers and my people. I had it in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and for the footstool of our God, and I made preparations to build.
But God said to me, ‘You shall not build a house for My name, because you are a man of war and have shed blood.’

Yet the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me from all my father’s house to be king over Israel forever. For He chose Judah as leader, and from the house of Judah He chose my father’s house, and from my father’s sons He was pleased to make me king over all Israel.
And of all my sons—for the LORD has given me many sons—He has chosen my son Solomon to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel. “
He said to me, ‘Solomon your son is the one who will build My house and My courts, for I have chosen him to be My son, and I will be his Father.
I will establish his kingdom forever, if he is steadfast to observe My commandments and My ordinances, as he is this day.’

So now, in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD, and in the hearing of our God, observe and seek out all the commandments of the LORD your God, so that you may possess the good land and leave it as an inheritance to your children after you forever.

And you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father, and serve Him with a whole heart and a willing mind, for the LORD searches all hearts and understands the intent of every thought. If you seek Him, He will be found by you; but if you forsake Him, He will reject you forever.
Consider now that the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong and do it.”
Then David gave to his son Solomon the plan of the portico and its buildings, its treasuries, its upper rooms, its inner chambers, and the room for the mercy seat;

and the plan of all that he had in mind for the courts of the house of the LORD, for all the surrounding chambers, for the treasuries of the house of God, and for the treasuries of the dedicated things;
and for the divisions of the priests and the Levites, and for all the work of the service of the house of the LORD, and for all the utensils of service in the house of the LORD.
for the gold by weight for all the articles for every kind of service, and for all the silver articles by weight for every kind of service;

the weight of the gold lampstands and their lamps, including the weight of each lampstand and its lamps; and the weight of the silver lampstands and their lamps, according to the use of each lampstand;
the weight of gold for the tables of the showbread, for each table, and the weight of silver for the silver tables;
the pure gold for the forks, the bowls, and the pitchers; the weight of each gold dish; and the silver for each silver dish and its kind.
and for the altar of incense, refined gold by weight; and gold for the chariot of the cherubim that spread their wings and overshadow the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
“All this,” David said, “The LORD made me understand in writing by His hand upon me, all the works of this pattern.”

David said to Solomon, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Do not be afraid or dismayed, for the LORD God, my God, is with you. He will not leave you or forsake you until all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished.

And behold, the divisions of the priests and the Levites are for all the service of the house of God, and with you in all the work will be every willing man skilled in any craft; also the officials and all the people will be at your every command.”
King David said to all the assembly, “My son Solomon, whom God has chosen alone, is young and inexperienced, and the task is great, for the temple is not for man but for the LORD God.

Now with all my strength I have prepared for the house of my God: gold for the gold work, silver for the silver work, bronze for the bronze work, iron for the iron work, and wood for the wood work; onyx stones, stones for settings, antimony, colored stones, every kind of precious stone, and marble stones in abundance.
Moreover, because I delight in the house of my God, I now give my personal treasures of gold and silver to the house of my God, in addition to all that I have already provided for the holy temple:
three thousand talents of gold from Ophir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver for overlaying the walls of the buildings.
for the gold work and the silver work, and for all the work to be done by the craftsmen. Now who is willing to consecrate himself to the LORD today?”
Then the leaders of the fathers’ houses, the leaders of the tribes of Israel, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the officials in charge of the king’s work gave willingly.

They gave for the service of the house of God five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and one hundred thousand talents of iron.
Those who had precious stones gave them to the treasury of the house of the LORD, under the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite.
Then the people rejoiced because they had given willingly, for with a whole heart they had offered freely to the LORD; and King David also rejoiced with great joy.
Then David blessed the LORD before all the assembly, saying, “Blessed are You, O the LORD, the God of our father Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.

Yours, O the LORD, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the victory and the majesty, for all that is in heaven and on earth is Yours. Yours, O the LORD, is the kingdom, and You are exalted as head over all.
Both riches and honor come from You, and You rule over all. In Your hand are power and might, and in Your hand it is to make great and to strengthen all.
Now therefore, our God, we give thanks to You and praise Your glorious name. “
But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to give as generously as this? For everything comes from You, and we have given You only what comes from Your hand.
For we are strangers and sojourners before You, as all our fathers were; our days on earth are like a shadow, with no hope.
O the LORD our God, all this abundance that we have prepared to build You a house for Your holy name comes from Your hand and belongs to You.

I know, my God, that You test the heart and delight in uprightness. In the uprightness of my heart I have willingly offered all these things, and now I have seen with joy Your people who are present here offering willingly to You.
O the LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our fathers, keep this forever in the imagination of the thoughts of the heart of Your people, and direct their heart toward You.
Give to my son Solomon a perfect heart to keep Your commandments, Your testimonies, and Your statutes, and to do them all, and to build the palace that I have prepared.”
Then David said to all the assembly, “Bless the LORD your God.” So all the assembly blessed the LORD, the God of their fathers, and bowed down and worshiped the LORD and the king.

On the next day they offered sacrifices to the LORD and offered burnt offerings to the LORD: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, a thousand lambs, with their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
They ate and drank that day before the LORD with great joy, and they made Solomon the son of David king a second time, and they anointed him to the LORD as prince, and Zadok as priest.
So Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king in place of David his father, and he prospered, and all Israel obeyed him.
All the leaders and mighty men, and also all the sons of King David, pledged their allegiance to King Solomon.
The LORD highly exalted Solomon in the sight of all Israel and bestowed on him royal majesty such as had not been on any king before him in Israel.
Thus David son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
The length of his reign over Israel was forty years: he reigned seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
He died at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor; and Solomon his son reigned in his place.
Now the acts of King David, first and last, are written in the records of Samuel the seer, Nathan the prophet, and Gad the seer,
with all his reign and his might, and the times that passed over him, and over Israel, and over all the kingdoms of the lands.
Solomon, the son of David, consolidated his authority over the kingdom, and the LORD his God was with him and exalted him mightily.
Then Solomon addressed all Israel—the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, the judges, and every leader throughout Israel, the patriarchal heads.

Solomon, together with the whole assembly, repaired to the high place at Gibeon, because the tent of meeting of God was located there, the very tabernacle that Moses, the servant of the LORD, had constructed in the wilderness.
David, however, had conveyed the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim to the site he had prepared for it, having pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.
The bronze altar fashioned by Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, stood there before the tabernacle of the LORD; and Solomon, with the assembly, sought Him there.
Solomon ascended to the bronze altar before the LORD at the tent of meeting and offered upon it a thousand burnt offerings.
That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask what I shall give you."
Solomon replied to God, "You have dealt with my father David in great and steadfast love, and You have enthroned me in his stead.
Now, O the LORD God, let Your word to my father David be established, for You have installed me as king over a people as innumerable as the dust of the earth.
Now grant me wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people, for who is capable of judging this great people of Yours?"

God said to Solomon, "Because this purpose was in your heart, and you did not request riches, wealth, or honor, nor the life of those who hate you, nor did you request longevity, but you requested wisdom and knowledge for yourself, that you might judge My people over whom I have made you king—
wisdom and knowledge are conferred upon you. I will also give you riches, wealth, and honor, such as no king before you has possessed and none after you will possess."
So Solomon returned to Jerusalem from the high place at Gibeon, from before the tent of meeting, and he reigned over Israel.
Solomon amassed chariots and horsemen: fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
The king made silver and gold as plentiful in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as abundant as the sycamores in the foothills.
Solomon's horses were brought from Egypt and from Kue; the king's merchants procured them from Kue at a fixed price.
A chariot was imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty, and they likewise furnished all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
Solomon resolved to build a house for the name of the LORD and a royal palace for his dominion.
Solomon assigned seventy thousand men to bear burdens, eighty thousand to hew stone in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred to serve as overseers superintending them.
Solomon sent to Hiram, king of Tyre, with this message: “You once dealt kindly with my father David and sent him cedars for the house in which he was to dwell.

Behold, I am building a house for the name of the LORD my God, to consecrate it to Him, to burn fragrant incense before Him, to keep the bread of the Presence in perpetual array, and to offer burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, at the new moons, and at the appointed feasts of the LORD our God. This is an ordinance for Israel forever.
The house that I am building is great, for our God is greater than all gods.
Yet who is able to build Him a house, when heaven itself, even the highest heaven, cannot contain Him? Who am I, then, that I should build Him a house, except to burn incense before Him?

Send me, therefore, a man skillful in working gold, silver, bronze, iron, purple, crimson, and blue, who knows how to execute engravings, to work alongside the skilled artisans who are with me in Judah and Jerusalem, whom my father David provided.
Send me also cedar, cypress, and algum timber from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut the timber of Lebanon; and behold, my servants will be with your servants,
to prepare timber for me in abundance, for the house I am building is to be great and wondrous.

And behold, I will give to your servants, the woodcutters who fell the timber, twenty thousand cors of ground wheat, twenty thousand cors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil.”
Hiram, king of Tyre, replied in writing and sent his answer to Solomon: “Because the LORD loves His people, He has made you king over them.

Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who has given King David a wise son, endowed with discretion and understanding, to build a house for the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
And now I have sent you Huram-abi, a skillful man endowed with understanding,

the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, whose father was a Tyrian, skilled to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, timber, purple, blue, fine linen, and crimson, and to engrave any engraving, and to devise any design that may be assigned to him, together with your wise men and the wise men of my lord David your father.
Now therefore the wheat, the barley, the oil, and the wine of which my lord has spoken, let him send to his servants.
And we will cut wood from Lebanon according to all your need, and bring it to you in rafts by sea to Joppa, and you shall carry it up to Jerusalem.”

Solomon numbered all the resident aliens who were in the land of Israel, after the census that David his father had taken of them, and there were found to be one hundred fifty-three thousand six hundred.
He made seventy thousand of them bearers of burdens, eighty thousand hewers in the mountain, and three thousand six hundred overseers, to set the people to work.

Solomon commenced the erection of the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, upon Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to David, his father, in the place that David had prepared upon the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
He began this work on the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.
These, then, are the foundations that Solomon laid for the construction of the house of God: a length of sixty cubits and a breadth of twenty cubits.

The portico that stood before the temple corresponded in length to the breadth of the house, measuring twenty cubits, while its height reached one hundred twenty cubits; and he overlaid its interior with pure gold.
The greater house he paneled with cypress timber and overlaid with fine gold, embellishing it with carved palm trees and chains.
Moreover, he adorned the temple with precious stones for beauty, and its gold was the gold of Parvaim.
He overlaid the beams, thresholds, walls, and doors with gold, and he carved cherubim upon the walls.

He fashioned the Most Holy Place, whose length, measured against the breadth of the house, was twenty cubits, and whose breadth was likewise twenty cubits; and he overlaid it with six hundred talents of fine gold.
The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold, and he overlaid the upper chambers with gold.
Within the Most Holy Place he made two cherubim of sculptured work and overlaid them with gold.

The wings of the cherubim extended twenty cubits: the wing of the first measured five cubits and reached to the wall of the house, while the other wing, likewise five cubits, touched the wing of the second cherub.
The wing of the second cherub measured five cubits and reached to the wall of the house, while its other wing, five cubits, was joined to the wing of the first.
Thus the wings of these cherubim were spread abroad for twenty cubits; they stood upon their feet, and their faces were turned toward the house.
He made the veil of blue, purple, and crimson yarn and fine linen, with cherubim worked into it.
Before the temple he made two pillars, thirty-five cubits in height, each crowned with a capital of five cubits.
He fashioned chains for the inner sanctuary and placed them upon the tops of the pillars; he made one hundred pomegranates and affixed them to the chains.
He erected the pillars before the temple, one on the right and one on the left; the right-hand pillar he named Jachin, and the left-hand pillar he named Boaz.
