He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
Jotham died and was buried in the City of David; his son Ahaz succeeded him as king.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; yet he did not do what was right in the sight of the LORD, as David his father had done.
Instead, he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel and even cast molten images for the Baals.
He burned incense in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom and consigned his sons to the fire, emulating the abominations of the nations whom the LORD had dispossessed before the Israelites.
He sacrificed and burned incense upon the high places, upon the hills, and beneath every verdant tree.

Consequently, the LORD his God delivered him into the hand of the king of Aram; the Arameans struck him and carried away a great multitude of captives to Damascus. He was likewise delivered into the hand of the king of Israel, who inflicted upon him a devastating defeat.
For in a single day Pekah son of Remaliah slew one hundred twenty thousand valiant men of Judah, because they had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers.
Moreover, Zichri, a mighty warrior of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king's son, Azrikam the palace steward, and Elkanah the king's second-in-command.
The Israelites also took captive two hundred thousand of their kinsmen—women, sons, and daughters—and plundered from them an immense spoil, which they conveyed to Samaria.

Now there was a prophet of the LORD named Oded, and he went out before the army as it came to Samaria and said to them, "Because the LORD, the God of your fathers, was wrathful against Judah, He delivered them into your hand, and you have slain them in a fury of unparalleled ferocity.
And now you purpose to subjugate the people of Judah and Jerusalem, reducing them to male and female slaves; yet are you not yourselves laden with transgressions against the LORD your God?
Heed me, therefore, and restore the captives whom you have taken from your brethren, for the fierce wrath of the LORD rests upon you."

Then certain men among the chiefs of Ephraim—Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai—rose up against those returning from the campaign.

They said to them, "You must not bring the captives here, lest you heap further guilt upon us from the LORD, adding to our sins and our trespasses; for our guilt is already great, and fierce wrath is upon Israel."
So the armed men relinquished the captives and the plunder before the princes and the whole assembly.

Then the men who were designated by name arose, took charge of the captives, and from the spoil clothed all who were naked; they clothed them, shod them, fed them, gave them drink, anointed them, and conveyed every enfeebled person upon donkeys, bringing them to Jericho, the city of palms, near their kinsmen; then they returned to Samaria.
At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria to solicit their aid.
For the Edomites had again invaded and struck Judah, carrying away captives.

The Philistines likewise made raids upon the cities of the Shephelah and the Negev of Judah; they seized Beth-shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco and its villages, Timnah and its villages, and Gimzo and its villages, and settled there.
For the LORD humbled Judah on account of Ahaz king of Israel, because he had cast off restraint in Judah and had been exceedingly unfaithful to the LORD.
Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria came against him and oppressed him rather than strengthening him.
For Ahaz had despoiled the house of the LORD and the house of the king and of the princes, and had given the proceeds to the king of Assyria, but it did not avail him.
In the time of his distress, King Ahaz trespassed yet more against the LORD.

He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus who had defeated him, reasoning that since the gods of the kings of Aram helped them, he would sacrifice to them that they might help him; but they proved to be the downfall of him and of all Israel.
Ahaz gathered the vessels of the house of God, cut the vessels of the house of God in pieces, shut the doors of the house of the LORD, and made altars for himself in every corner of Jerusalem.
In every city of Judah he made high places to burn incense to other gods, provoking the LORD, the God of his fathers.
Now the rest of his acts and all his ways, from first to last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
Ahaz died and was buried in the city, in Jerusalem, but they did not bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel; and Hezekiah his son succeeded him.
Hezekiah was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Abijah, the daughter of Zechariah.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that David his father had done.
In the first month of the first year of his reign, he opened the doors of the house of the LORD and repaired them.
He brought in the priests and the Levites, and gathered them into the eastern square.
“Listen to me, Levites! Consecrate yourselves now, and consecrate the house of the LORD, the God of your fathers, and carry the defilement out of the holy place.
For our fathers acted treacherously and did evil in the sight of the LORD our God; they forsook Him, averted their faces from the dwelling of the LORD, and turned their backs upon Him.
They also shut the doors of the portico and put out the lamps, and they did not burn incense or offer burnt offerings in the sanctuary to the God of Israel.
Therefore the wrath of the LORD came upon Judah and Jerusalem, and He made them an object of horror, desolation, and scorn, as you see with your own eyes.
Behold, our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons, daughters, and wives have gone into captivity because of this.
Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with the LORD, the God of Israel, that His fierce anger may turn away from us.
My sons, do not now be negligent, for the LORD has chosen you to stand before Him, to minister to Him, and to be His ministers who burn incense.”

Then the Levites arose: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah of the Kohathites; and of the sons of Merari, Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel; and of the Gershonites, Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah;
and of the sons of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeuel; and of the sons of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah;
and of the sons of Heman, Jehiel and Shimei; and of the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
They gathered their brethren and consecrated themselves, and went in, according to the king’s command by the words of the LORD, to cleanse the house of the LORD.

The priests went into the inner precincts of the house of the LORD to cleanse it, and they brought out all the defilement that they found in the temple of the LORD into the courtyard of the house of the LORD; and the Levites received it and carried it out to the Kidron Valley.

They began to consecrate on the first day of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they came to the portico of the LORD; they consecrated the house of the LORD in eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.
“We have cleansed all the house of the LORD, the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the table of the bread of the Presence with all its utensils.
Moreover, all the utensils that King Ahaz cast aside during his reign in his treachery, we have prepared and consecrated; and behold, they stand before the altar of the LORD.”
Then King Hezekiah rose early and gathered the officials of the city, and went up to the house of the LORD.

They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats for a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Judah. And he said to the priests, the sons of Aaron, “Offer them on the altar of the LORD.”

So they slaughtered the bulls, and the priests received the blood and sprinkled it on the altar; they slaughtered the rams and sprinkled the blood on the altar; and they slaughtered the lambs and sprinkled the blood on the altar.
Then they brought the male goats for the sin offering before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands upon them.
The priests slaughtered them and made atonement with their blood upon the altar, to make atonement for all Israel; for the king had said, “The burnt offering and the sin offering are for all Israel.”

He stationed the Levites in the house of the LORD with cymbals, harps, and lyres, according to the commandment of David, and of Gad the king’s seer, and of Nathan the prophet; for the commandment was from the LORD through His prophets.
The Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.

Hezekiah gave the command to offer the burnt offering upon the altar; and when the burnt offering began, the song of the LORD began also, with the trumpets and the instruments of David king of Israel.
All the assembly worshiped, and the singers sang, and the trumpeters sounded; all this continued until the burnt offering was finished.
When the offering was finished, the king and all who were present with him bowed themselves and worshiped.

Then King Hezekiah and the officials said to the Levites, “Sing praise to the LORD with the words of David and of Asaph the seer.” So they sang praises with gladness, and they bowed down and worshiped.

Then Hezekiah said, “You have now consecrated yourselves to the LORD. Come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings into the house of the LORD.” So the assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and all who were of a willing heart brought burnt offerings.
The number of the burnt offerings that the assembly brought was seventy bulls, a hundred rams, and two hundred lambs; all these were for a burnt offering to the LORD.
The consecrated gifts were six hundred bulls and three thousand sheep.

But the priests were too few and could not skin all the burnt offerings, so their brethren the Levites helped them until the work was finished and until the priests had consecrated themselves; for the Levites were more upright in heart to consecrate themselves than the priests.
The burnt offerings were also in abundance, together with the fat of the peace offerings and the drink offerings for the burnt offerings. Thus the service of the house of the LORD was restored.
Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced, because God had provided for the people; for the matter came about suddenly.

Hezekiah dispatched messengers throughout all Israel and Judah, and he likewise inscribed letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, summoning them to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, there to celebrate the Passover unto the LORD, the God of Israel.
For the king, together with his officials and the whole assembly in Jerusalem, had resolved to observe the Passover in the second month—
because they could not keep it at the appointed time, the priests not having consecrated themselves in sufficient numbers, nor had the people assembled in Jerusalem.
The plan commended itself to the king and to the entire assembly.

They therefore decreed that a proclamation be carried throughout all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, bidding the people come and keep the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel, at Jerusalem, since they had not observed it in the prescribed fullness.

So, in accordance with the king's command, couriers traversed all Israel and Judah bearing letters from the king and his officials, proclaiming: “People of Israel, return to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, that He may turn in mercy to the remnant of you who have escaped the hand of the kings of Assyria.
Do not resemble your fathers and your brothers, who acted treacherously toward the LORD, the God of their fathers, so that He consigned them to desolation, as you see.

Do not now stiffen your necks, as your fathers did, but yield yourselves to the LORD and enter His sanctuary, which He has consecrated forever, and serve the LORD your God, that His fierce anger may turn away from you.

For if you return to the LORD, your brothers and your children will find compassion in the sight of their captors and return to this land; for the LORD your God is gracious and merciful, and He will not turn His face away from you, if you return to Him.”
Thus the couriers passed from city to city through the country of Ephraim and Manasseh, even as far as Zebulun; yet the people there ridiculed and mocked them.
Nevertheless, certain men of Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.
Moreover, the hand of God was upon Judah, granting them one heart to execute the command of the king and of the officials according to the word of the LORD.
A very great assembly gathered in Jerusalem in the second month to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
They rose up and removed the altars that were in Jerusalem, and every incense altar they carried away and cast into the Kidron Valley.

On the fourteenth day of the second month they slaughtered the Passover, while the priests and the Levites, ashamed of their unreadiness, consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings into the house of the LORD.
They took their stations according to their appointed order, in accordance with the Law of Moses, the man of God; the priests sprinkled the blood received from the hand of the Levites.
For many in the assembly had not consecrated themselves, so the Levites were charged with slaughtering the Passover lambs for everyone who was not clean, thereby consecrating them to the LORD.

For a great multitude of the people—many from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun—had not purified themselves, yet they ate the Passover otherwise than prescribed. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, “May the LORD, who is good, pardon every one
who sets his heart to seek God, the LORD God of his fathers, even though he is not cleansed according to the sanctuary's purity.”
And the LORD heard Hezekiah and healed the people.

The Israelites who were present in Jerusalem kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great gladness; and the Levites and the priests praised the LORD day by day, singing with all their might to the LORD.

Hezekiah encouraged all the Levites who showed skillful understanding in the service of the LORD. Thus for seven days they ate the festival food, offering peace offerings and giving thanks to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
Then the whole assembly resolved to keep the feast for another seven days, and they did so with gladness.

For Hezekiah king of Judah contributed to the assembly one thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep, and the officials contributed one thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep; and a great number of priests consecrated themselves.
The whole assembly of Judah, together with the priests, the Levites, the whole assembly that had come from Israel, the sojourners from the land of Israel, and the inhabitants of Judah, rejoiced.
So there was great joy in Jerusalem, for since the days of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel, there had been nothing like this in Jerusalem.
Then the priests and the Levites arose and blessed the people, and their voice was heard, and their prayer ascended to His holy dwelling in heaven.

After all these events, once every Israelite who could be found had completed the celebration, they went out to the cities of Judah and shattered the sacred pillars, cut down the Asherah poles, and demolished the high places and altars throughout Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh until they had utterly destroyed them; then all Israel returned to their own cities, each to his own possession.

Hezekiah reestablished the divisions of the priests and Levites according to their divisions, assigning each to his proper service, for the priests and Levites were to present burnt offerings and peace offerings, to minister, to give thanks, and to praise within the gates of the the LORD.

The king also set aside from his own property a portion for the burnt offerings—those offered morning and evening—and for the burnt offerings of the Sabbaths, the new moons, and the appointed feasts, as it is written in the law of the the LORD.
He commanded the people, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to give the priests and Levites their portion so that they might devote themselves with renewed strength to the law of the the LORD.

When the command spread abroad, the Israelites brought in abundance the firstfruits of grain, new wine, oil, honey, and every product of the field; indeed, they brought in a tithe of everything in great abundance.

The Israelites and the Judahites who dwelt in the cities of Judah likewise brought tithes of cattle and sheep, together with tithes of the holy things consecrated to the the LORD their God, and they laid them heap upon heap.
They began laying the foundations of these heaps in the third month and completed them in the seventh month.
When Hezekiah and the officials came and saw the heaps, they blessed the the LORD and His people Israel.
Hezekiah then inquired of the priests and Levites concerning the heaps,

and Azariah, the chief priest of the house of Zadok, answered him, “Since the contributions began to be brought into the house of the the LORD, the people have eaten and been satisfied, with a great abundance left over, because the the LORD has blessed His people; indeed, this vast remainder is still here.”
Hezekiah commanded that chambers be prepared in the house of the the LORD, and they prepared them.
They brought the contributions, the tithes, and the consecrated things in faithfully; Conaniah the Levite was the overseer over them, and his brother Shimei was second.

Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah were supervisors under Conaniah and Shimei, by the appointment of King Hezekiah and of Azariah, the chief priest of the house of God.
Kore son of Imnah the Levite, the gatekeeper on the east, was over the freewill offerings of God, to distribute the contribution of the the LORD and the most holy things.

Under his authority were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah, acting in faithfulness to distribute to their brothers in the priestly cities, according to their divisions, to great and small alike.

In addition to those enrolled by genealogy, males from three years old and upward—everyone who entered the house of the the LORD daily for service—were included in these allotments, according to the duties of their divisions.
The priests were enrolled according to their fathers’ houses, and the Levites from twenty years old and upward according to their duties and divisions.
They enrolled their entire assembly—their little ones, wives, sons, and daughters—for in faithfulness they had consecrated themselves as holy.

For the sons of Aaron, the priests in the pasturelands of their cities, in every city, men were designated by name to give portions to every male among the priests and to all the Levites who were enrolled.
Thus Hezekiah acted throughout all Judah, and he did what was good, right, and true before the the LORD his God.
In every work that he began in the service of the house of God, in the law and the commandment, to seek his God, he prospered.
After these deeds of fidelity, Sennacherib, king of Assyria, invaded Judah, invested its fortified cities, and resolved to appropriate them for himself.
When Hezekiah perceived that Sennacherib had arrived and was intent upon making war against Jerusalem,
he took counsel with his officials and warriors concerning the stoppage of the springs outside the city, and they rendered him assistance.

A great throng of people assembled and stopped up all the springs and the stream that coursed through the midst of the land, saying, "Why should the kings of Assyria come and discover abundant water?"

Thereafter Hezekiah fortified himself and rebuilt the entire broken wall; he elevated towers upon it, constructed another wall beyond it, strengthened the Millo in the City of David, and fabricated weapons and shields in profusion.
He appointed commanders of war over the people, assembled them in the plaza at the city gate, and exhorted them, saying,
"Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or dismayed before the king of Assyria and before all the multitude that is with him, for there are more with us than with him.
With him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God, to help us and to fight our battles." And the people took confidence in the words of Hezekiah, king of Judah.

Afterward, while Sennacherib, king of Assyria, was besieging Lachish with all his dominion, he dispatched his servants to Jerusalem to Hezekiah, king of Judah, and to all Judah who were in Jerusalem, saying,
"Thus says Sennacherib, king of Assyria: 'On what are you trusting, that you remain under siege in Jerusalem?
Is not Hezekiah misleading you, to give you over to die by famine and thirst, saying, "The The LORD our God will deliver us from the hand of the king of Assyria"?
Did not Hezekiah himself remove his high places and altars and command Judah and Jerusalem, saying, "You shall worship before one altar and burn incense upon it"?
Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of the lands at all able to deliver their land from my hand?
Who among all the gods of these nations that my fathers devoted to destruction was able to deliver his people from my hand, that your God should be able to deliver you from my hand?

Now therefore do not let Hezekiah deceive you or mislead you in this manner, and do not believe him, for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to deliver his people from my hand and from the hand of my fathers. How much less will your God deliver you from my hand!"'
His servants spoke further against the the LORD God and against His servant Hezekiah.

He also wrote letters to insult the the LORD, the God of Israel, and to speak against Him, saying, "As the gods of the nations of the lands have not delivered their people from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah will not deliver His people from my hand."
They called out with a loud voice in the language of Judah to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, to frighten them and terrify them, that they might capture the city.
And they spoke against the God of Jerusalem as against the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of men's hands.
Then King Hezekiah and Isaiah the prophet, son of Amoz, prayed and cried out to heaven.

And the the LORD sent an angel, who cut off every mighty warrior, commander, and officer in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returned to his own land in disgrace. And when he entered the house of his god, some of his own offspring struck him down there with the sword.
Thus the the LORD saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib, king of Assyria, and from the hand of all others, and He gave them rest on every side.
And many brought gifts to Jerusalem to the the LORD and precious things to Hezekiah, king of Judah, so that he was exalted in the sight of all nations after that.
In those days Hezekiah became mortally ill; he prayed to the the LORD, and He spoke to him and gave him a sign.
But Hezekiah did not repay according to the benefit done to him, for his heart was proud; therefore wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem.
But Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the the LORD did not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah.
And Hezekiah had very great riches and honor; he made treasuries for silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and all kinds of valuable articles;
storehouses for the produce of grain, wine, and oil; and stalls for all kinds of cattle and flocks.
He made cities for himself, and he had flocks and herds in abundance, for God had given him very great wealth.
This same Hezekiah also stopped up the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon and directed them down to the west side of the City of David. And Hezekiah prospered in all his works.
But when envoys of the princes of Babylon were sent to him to inquire about the sign that had been done in the land, God left him to test him, that He might know all that was in his heart.
Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his deeds of lovingkindness, behold, they are written in the vision of Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, and in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

And Hezekiah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the upper part of the tombs of the sons of David; and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem honored him at his death. And Manasseh his son reigned in his place.
Manasseh ascended the throne at twelve years of age and reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
He perpetrated evil in the sight of the LORD, emulating the abominations of the nations that the LORD had dispossessed before the Israelites.
He rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had demolished, erected altars to the Baals, fashioned Asherahs, and bowed down to and served the entire host of heaven.
He even constructed altars within the house of the LORD, concerning which the LORD had declared, “My Name shall be in Jerusalem forever.”
In the two courtyards of the LORD’s house he built altars to the whole host of heaven.

He consigned his sons to the flames in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom, practiced soothsaying, divination, and sorcery, and consulted mediums and spiritists; by these and kindred abominations he provoked the LORD to anger.

He placed the carved image of the idol he had fashioned in the house of God, concerning which God had said to David and to his son Solomon, “In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will establish My Name forever.

I will never again uproot Israel from the land I gave to your fathers, provided that you are careful to observe all that I commanded them through Moses—the whole law, the statutes, and the ordinances.”
Thus Manasseh led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem into such delusion that they did more evil than the nations the LORD had destroyed before the Israelites.
The LORD spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they refused to listen.
Therefore the LORD brought against them the commanders of the Assyrian king’s army; they captured Manasseh with hooks, bound him in bronze shackles, and carried him off to Babylon.
In his affliction he earnestly sought the favor of the LORD his God and humbled himself profoundly before the God of his fathers.
He prayed to Him, and the LORD was moved by his plea; He heard his supplication and restored him to Jerusalem and to his kingdom. Then Manasseh recognized that the LORD is God.

Afterward he built an outer wall for the City of David on the west side of Gihon, in the valley, extending to the entrance of the Fish Gate and surrounding the Ophel; he raised it to a great height. He also posted military commanders in all the fortified cities of Judah.
He removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the LORD, together with all the altars he had built on the temple mount and in Jerusalem, and he cast them outside the city.
He restored the altar of the LORD and offered on it sacrifices of peace offerings and thank offerings; he also commanded Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.
Nevertheless, the people continued to sacrifice at the high places, though only to the LORD their God.

As for the rest of Manasseh’s acts, his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, they are recorded in the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

His prayer and God’s gracious response to it, along with all his sin and treachery, and the sites where he had built high places and erected Asherahs and carved images before his humiliation—all of this is recorded in the records of the seers.
Manasseh died and was buried with his ancestors, and his son Amon succeeded him as king.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
He did evil in the sight of the LORD, just as his father Manasseh had done; Amon sacrificed to all the carved images his father Manasseh had made, and he served them.
Unlike his father Manasseh, he did not humble himself before the LORD; instead, Amon increased his guilt.
His servants conspired against him and assassinated him in his own house.
But the people of the land struck down all who had conspired against King Amon, and they made his son Josiah king in his place.
Josiah ascended the throne at eight years of age, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
He comported himself with rectitude before the LORD, walking in the ways of his father David and deviating neither to the right nor to the left.

In the eighth year of his reign, though still a youth, he began to seek the God of his father David; and in the twelfth year he initiated the purification of Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, the Asherim, the graven images, and the molten idols.

Before him they demolished the altars of the Baals, and he hewed down the incense altars that stood above them; he shattered the Asherim, the graven images, and the molten idols, pulverized them, and scattered the dust upon the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
He likewise incinerated the bones of the priests upon their altars, thereby purifying Judah and Jerusalem.
He executed the same reforms in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon, and as far as Naphtali, even amid their surrounding ruins.

Throughout the land of Israel he demolished the altars, beat the Asherim and graven images to pieces, ground the idols to powder, and cut down every incense altar; thereafter he returned to Jerusalem.

In the eighteenth year of his reign, having purified both the land and the temple, he dispatched Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder, to restore the house of the LORD his God.

They came to Hilkiah the high priest and delivered the funds that had been brought into the house of God, which the Levites who guarded the threshold had amassed from Manasseh, Ephraim, and all the remnant of Israel, as well as from all Judah and Benjamin and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
They committed these resources to the overseers of the work on the house of the LORD, who in turn allocated them to the artisans laboring in the house of the LORD, both to repair and to fortify it.

They also gave them to the carpenters and builders for the purchase of quarried stone and timber for joinery and roofing, in order to restore the buildings that the kings of Judah had reduced to ruin.

The men discharged their labor with fidelity. Over them were appointed as supervisors Jahath and Obadiah, Levites of the sons of Merari, together with Zechariah and Meshullam, Levites of the sons of Kohath; all the Levites were proficient in instrumental music.
They were likewise placed in charge of the porters and of all who supervised every species of work, while some of the Levites served as scribes, officials, and gatekeepers.
As they extracted the money that had been brought into the house of the LORD, Hilkiah the priest discovered the Book of the Law of the LORD given through Moses.
Hilkiah said to Shaphan the scribe, “I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD.” And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan.
Shaphan conveyed the book to the king and rendered an additional report, saying, “Your servants are executing all that has been committed to their charge.
They have melted down the money that was found in the house of the LORD and have consigned it to the custody of the supervisors and the workmen.”
Shaphan the scribe informed the king, “Hilkiah the priest has entrusted me with a book.” Then Shaphan read it aloud in the king’s presence.
When the king heard the words of the Law, he rent his garments.
The king charged Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king’s servant,

“Proceed and consult the LORD on my behalf and on behalf of the surviving remnant in Israel and Judah concerning the words of the book that has been found, for formidable is the wrath of the LORD that has been unleashed upon us, inasmuch as our ancestors failed to observe the word of the LORD so as to do all that is prescribed in this book.”

So Hilkiah and those whom the king had commissioned repaired to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum son of Tokhath, son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe—she resided in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter—and they communicated to her the king’s charge.
She said to them, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Convey to the man who dispatched you to Me,
‘Thus says the LORD: Behold, I am inflicting calamity upon this place and upon its inhabitants—all the imprecations inscribed in the book that they read before the king of Judah.

Because they have abandoned Me and offered incense to alien deities, provoking Me to anger with all the works of their hands, My wrath shall be effused upon this place and shall not be extinguished.’”
“But to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the LORD, you shall respond thus: Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning the words that you have heard:
Because your heart was pliant and you abased yourself before Me, rent your garments, and you wept before Me, I too have hearkened to you, declares the LORD.

Behold, I will gather you to your ancestors, and you shall be gathered to your sepulcher in peace; your eyes shall not behold all the evil that I am bringing upon this place and upon its inhabitants.” And they relayed the response to the king.
Thereupon the king sent and convened all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

The king ascended to the house of the LORD, accompanied by all the men of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests, the Levites, and all the people, from the most eminent to the least significant; and he read aloud in their presence all the words of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.

The king took his station and ratified a covenant before the LORD to walk in the LORD’s ways, to observe His commandments, His testimonies, and His statutes with entire heart and soul, and to execute the terms of the covenant written in this book.

He also obliged all who were present in Jerusalem and Benjamin to stand in assent; and the inhabitants of Jerusalem conducted themselves in conformity with the covenant of God, the God of their fathers.

Josiah eradicated every abomination from all the territories of the Israelites and constrained all who were found in Israel to serve the LORD their God. Throughout his days they did not deviate from following the LORD, the God of their fathers.
In Jerusalem, Josiah observed the Passover to the LORD, and the paschal victim was slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the first month.
He stationed the priests at their posts and strengthened them for the service of the house of the LORD.

To the Levites, who instructed all Israel and were consecrated to the LORD, he said, “Place the holy ark in the house that Solomon son of David, king of Israel, built; you shall no longer carry it on your shoulders. Now serve the LORD your God and His people Israel.”
Prepare yourselves according to your ancestral houses, in your divisions, according to the written ordinance of David, king of Israel, and the written ordinance of Solomon his son.
Stand in the holy place according to the divisions of the ancestral houses of your brothers, the sons of the people, and according to the division of the ancestral house of the Levites.
Slaughter the Passover, consecrate yourselves, and prepare it for your brothers, that you may carry out the word of the LORD given through Moses.
From his own flock Josiah contributed thirty thousand lambs and kids and three thousand cattle; all of these were for the Passover offerings for the people who were present.
His officials likewise contributed willingly: Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, the rulers of the house of God, gave the priests two thousand six hundred Passover offerings and three hundred cattle.

Conaniah, together with his brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, and Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, the leaders of the Levites, contributed to the Levites five thousand Passover offerings and five hundred cattle.
The service was thus prepared: the priests stood in their places and the Levites in their divisions, according to the king's command.
They slaughtered the Passover; the priests sprinkled the blood, while the Levites flayed the victims.

They set aside the burnt offerings to distribute them by divisions of the ancestral houses of the people, so that they might be offered to the LORD, as it is written in the Book of Moses; and they did the same with the cattle.
They roasted the Passover over the fire according to the ordinance, boiled the holy portions in pots, cauldrons, and pans, and then quickly distributed them to all the people.

Afterward they prepared for themselves and for the priests, because the priests, the sons of Aaron, were occupied until nightfall in offering the burnt offerings and the fat; so the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.

The singers, the sons of Asaph, stood at their stations according to the command of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, the king's seer; the gatekeepers were at each gate. They did not need to leave their service, because their brothers the Levites prepared everything for them.
Thus all the service of the LORD was prepared that day: the Passover was kept and the burnt offerings were offered on the altar of the LORD, according to the command of King Josiah.
The Israelites who were present kept the Passover at that time and then celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.

No Passover like it had been kept in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet; none of the kings of Israel had kept a Passover such as Josiah kept, with the priests, the Levites, all Judah and Israel who were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
In the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign this Passover was observed.
After all this, when Josiah had prepared the temple, Neco, king of Egypt, came up to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to meet him.

Neco sent messengers to him, saying, “What have you to do with me, king of Judah? I am not coming against you today, but against the house with which I am at war; God has commanded me to hurry. Stop opposing God, who is with me, so that He does not destroy you.”

But Josiah would not turn away from him; instead, he disguised himself in order to fight, and he did not heed the words of Neco, which came from the mouth of God. So he came to fight in the valley of Megiddo.
The archers shot King Josiah, and the king said to his servants, “Carry me away, for I am severely wounded.”

His servants carried him out of the chariot, placed him in the second chariot that he had, and brought him to Jerusalem, where he died and was buried in the tombs of his fathers. All Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.

Jeremiah also lamented for Josiah, and all the male and female singers speak of Josiah in their laments to this day; they established them as an ordinance in Israel, and they are written in the Laments.
The rest of the acts of Josiah, and his good deeds in accordance with the Law of the LORD,
and his earlier and later deeds, are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
The people of the land took Jehoahaz, son of Josiah, and enthroned him in Jerusalem in his father's stead.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.
The king of Egypt deposed him in Jerusalem and levied upon the land a tribute of one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
Then the king of Egypt made Eliakim, his brother, king over Judah and Jerusalem, and changed his name to Jehoiakim; he also took Jehoahaz, his brother, and carried him away to Egypt.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; he did what was evil in the sight of the LORD his God.
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came up against him, bound him in bronze fetters, and carried him to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar also brought some of the vessels of the house of the LORD to Babylon and placed them in his temple.

The remaining acts of Jehoiakim, together with the abominations he committed and what was found against him, are recorded in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah; Jehoiachin, his son, reigned in his stead.
Jehoiachin was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem; he did what was evil in the sight of the LORD.
At the turn of the year, King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him to Babylon, along with the precious vessels of the house of the LORD, and made Zedekiah, his brother, king over Judah and Jerusalem.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD his God and did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke from the mouth of the LORD.
He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God; he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against turning to the LORD, the God of Israel.
Moreover, all the chief priests and the people grew increasingly unfaithful after all the abominations of the nations, and they defiled the house of the LORD that He had consecrated in Jerusalem.
The LORD, the God of their fathers, persistently sent word to them through His messengers, because He had compassion on His people and on His dwelling place.
But they mocked the messengers of God, despised His words, and scoffed at His prophets, until the wrath of the LORD rose against His people, until there was no remedy.

Therefore He brought against them the king of the Chaldeans, who slew their young men with the sword even in the sanctuary and showed no compassion to young man or maiden, to the old or the aged; He gave all into his hand.
All the articles of the house of God, great and small, and the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king and his officials, he brought to Babylon.
They burned the house of God, broke down the wall of Jerusalem, burned all its palaces with fire, and destroyed all its precious vessels.
Those who escaped the sword he carried away to Babylon, where they became servants to him and to his sons until the reign of Persia.
Thus the land enjoyed its Sabbaths; throughout all the days of its desolation it kept Sabbath, to fulfill the word of the LORD spoken by Jeremiah, until seventy years were completed.

In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, in order that the word of the LORD spoken by Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom and also committed it to writing:

"Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: 'The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has charged me to build Him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Whoever among you of all His people—the LORD his God be with him—let him go up.'"

In the first year of Cyrus, king of Persia, that the word of the LORD spoken by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the LORD stirred the spirit of Cyrus, king of Persia, so that he caused a proclamation to pass throughout all his kingdom—and also committed it to writing—saying:
“Thus says Cyrus, king of Persia: ‘The The LORD God of heaven has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has charged me to build for Him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.
Who among you is of all His people? May his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel—He is the God who is in Jerusalem.

And as for every survivor in whatever place he sojourns, let the men of that place support him with silver and gold, with goods and with beasts, in addition to the freewill offering for the house of God that is in Jerusalem.’”

Then the heads of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin, together with the priests and the Levites—everyone whose spirit God had stirred—arose to go up and build the house of the LORD that is in Jerusalem.
And all who were around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, with beasts, and with costly wares, besides all that was freely offered.
King Cyrus also brought out the vessels of the house of the LORD, which Nebuchadnezzar had brought out from Jerusalem and placed in the house of his god.
Cyrus, king of Persia, brought them out under the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, who numbered them to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah.
And this is their number: thirty basins of gold, a thousand basins of silver, twenty-nine knives;
thirty bowls of gold, four hundred ten bowls of silver, and a thousand other vessels.
All the vessels of gold and of silver were five thousand four hundred. Sheshbazzar brought all these up, together with the exiles who were brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem.

These are the people of the province who ascended from the captivity of the exile, whom Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had carried away to Babylon; they returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own city.
They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah. The roster of the men of the people of Israel is as follows:
Descendants of Pahath-moab, belonging to the lines of Jeshua and Joab: 2,812.
People of Kiriath-arim, Chephirah, and Beeroth: 743.
People of Lod, Hadid, and Ono: 725.
The priests: descendants of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua: 973.
The Levites: descendants of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the line of Hodaviah: 74.
The gatekeepers: descendants of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai: 139.
The Nethinim: descendants of Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth,
The descendants of Solomon's servants: Sotai, Hassophereth, Peruda,
The Nethinim and the descendants of Solomon's servants totaled 392.
These also went up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer, though they could not prove their ancestral houses or their lineage, whether they were of Israel:
the descendants of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda: 652.
And among the priests: the descendants of Habaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai, who had married one of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
These sought their registration among those enrolled by genealogy, but they were not found; therefore they were excluded from the priesthood.
The governor said to them, "You shall not eat of the most holy things until a priest arises with Urim and Thummim."
The whole assembly, as one body, numbered 42,360,
besides 7,337 male and female servants; they also had 200 male and female singers.
Their horses numbered 736 and their mules 245.
Their camels numbered 435 and their donkeys 6,720.
When they came to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, some of the heads of the ancestral houses gave freewill offerings to erect the house of God upon its foundation.
According to their ability, they gave to the treasury of the work 61,000 darics of gold, 5,000 minas of silver, and 100 priestly garments.
The priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, Nethinim, and some of the people settled in their towns, and all Israel in their towns.
In the seventh month, after the Israelites had settled in their cities, the people gathered at Jerusalem as a single body.

Then Jeshua son of Jozadak, with his priestly brethren, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, with his associates, arose and built the altar of the God of Israel, so that they might offer burnt offerings upon it, as it is written in the Law of Moses, the man of God.
They established the altar upon its bases, and although they were in dread of the peoples of the lands, they offered burnt offerings upon it to the LORD, both morning and evening burnt offerings.
They kept the Feast of Booths, as it is written, and offered the daily burnt offerings in their prescribed number, according to the ordinance for each day.

Afterward they offered the continual burnt offering, together with the offerings of the new moons and of all the the LORD's appointed holy convocations, as well as every freewill offering willingly presented to the LORD.
From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to the LORD, although the foundation of the LORD's temple had not yet been laid.

Then they gave silver to the stonecutters and carpenters, and food, drink, and oil to the Sidonians and Tyrians, so that cedar timber from Lebanon might be conveyed by sea to Joppa, in accordance with the authorization of Cyrus, king of Persia.

In the second month of the second year after their arrival at the house of God in Jerusalem, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Jeshua son of Jozadak, and the rest of their brethren—the priests, the Levites, and all who had come from the captivity to Jerusalem—began the work and appointed the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, to oversee the work of the house of the LORD.

Then Jeshua with his sons and brethren, Kadmiel with his sons, the sons of Judah, and the sons of Henadad with their sons and brethren, the Levites, stood as one to supervise the workmen in the house of God.

When the builders laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, the priests stood in their vestments with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the LORD, according to the ordinance of David, king of Israel.

They sang in praise and thanksgiving to the LORD, “He is good, for His loving devotion to Israel endures forever,” and all the people shouted with a great shout of praise to the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD had been laid.

Yet many of the aged priests, Levites, and heads of fathers' houses, who had seen the first house, wept with a loud voice when this house was founded before their eyes, while many others shouted aloud for joy.
Thus the people could not distinguish the sound of the joyful shout from the sound of the weeping, for the people shouted with a great shout, and the sound was heard afar off.
When the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin ascertained that the returned exiles were erecting a temple unto the LORD, the God of Israel,

they drew near to Zerubbabel and the chiefs of the ancestral houses and said to them, “Let us build with you, for we seek your God even as you do, and we have been sacrificing to Him since the days of Esarhaddon, king of Assyria, who transported us hither.”

But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the remaining chiefs of Israel’s ancestral houses replied to them, “You have no share with us in building a house for our God; we ourselves will build it for the LORD, the God of Israel, as King Cyrus of Persia has enjoined upon us.”
Thereupon the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah and terrified them from building,
and they also suborned counselors against them to frustrate their design throughout the days of Cyrus, king of Persia, and until the reign of Darius, king of Persia.
In the commencement of the reign of Ahasuerus, they composed an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
And in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of their colleagues wrote to Artaxerxes, king of Persia; the letter was written in Aramaic and translated.
Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes in these terms: “

Rehum the chancellor, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates—the Dinaites, the Apharsathchites, the Tarpelites, the Apharsites, the Archevites, the Babylonians, the Susanchites, the Dehavites, and the Elamites—
together with the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Asnappar deported and settled in the city of Samaria and elsewhere in the province Beyond the River—and now— “
this is a copy of the letter that they sent to him—to King Artaxerxes—from your servants, the men of the province Beyond the River: Peace to you. And now—

let it be known to the king that the Jews who came up from you to us have arrived at Jerusalem. They are rebuilding that rebellious and deleterious city; they are completing its walls and repairing its foundations. “
Now let it be known to the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, they will render no tribute, custom, or toll, and the royal revenues will be diminished.

Now, because we are in the king’s service and are bound by fealty to the crown, it is not seemly that we should behold the king’s dishonor; therefore we send this notification and make it known to the king, “

that an inquiry may be made in the book of the records of your fathers. In that record you will discover and learn that this city is a rebellious city, injurious to kings and provinces, and that sedition has been fomented within it from days of old; for this cause the city was devastated.
We make known to the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are completed, you will have no share beyond the River.” “
The king sent this reply: “To Rehum the chancellor, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates dwelling in Samaria and elsewhere in the province Beyond the River: Peace to you. And now— “
The letter that you sent to us has been read distinctly before me.
And I issued a decree, and a search has been made, and it has been found that this city from ancient times has risen up against kings, and that rebellion and sedition have been committed in it. “
And mighty kings have been over Jerusalem, who ruled over all the province Beyond the River, and to whom tribute, custom, and toll were paid.
Therefore issue a decree that these men be stopped, and that this city not be rebuilt until a decree is issued by me. “
And be diligent not to be remiss in this matter. Why should damage increase to the detriment of the kings?”
Then, when the copy of King Artaxerxes’ letter was read before Rehum, Shimshai, and their associates, they hastened to Jerusalem against the Jews and stopped them by force and might.
Then the work on the house of God in Jerusalem was suspended, and it remained suspended until the second year of the reign of Darius, king of Persia.
The prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo prophesied to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel concerning them.
Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak arose and began to rebuild the house of God in Jerusalem, while the prophets of God stood with them and sustained them in the work.

At that time Tattenai, governor of the region west of the Euphrates, together with Shethar-bozenai and their associates, came to them and said, “Who issued you a decree to build this temple and to finish this structure?”
They also asked, “What are the names of the men who are constructing this building?”
Yet the eye of their God was upon the elders of the Jews, so that they were not halted until a report could reach Darius and a written answer be returned concerning this matter.

This is the text of the letter that Tattenai, governor of the region west of the Euphrates, and Shethar-bozenai with his associates, the officials in the region west of the Euphrates, sent to King Darius.
They sent a report to him, written as follows: “To King Darius: All peace.

Let it be known to the king that we went to the province of Judah, to the house of the great God. It is being built with cut stones, and timber is being placed in the walls; the work is being carried out diligently and is prospering in their hands. “
We questioned the elders and asked, ‘Who issued you a decree to build this temple and to finish this structure?’
We also asked for their names, so that we might write down the names of their leaders for your information. “
This is the answer they gave: ‘We are servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding the temple that was built many years ago, which a great king of Israel built and completed.
But because our fathers angered the God of heaven, He delivered them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, who destroyed this temple and carried the people away to Babylon.
Yet in the first year of his reign, Cyrus king of Babylon issued a decree to rebuild this house of God.

He also removed from the temple in Babylon the gold and silver articles of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon. King Cyrus gave these articles to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he had appointed governor,
and he told him, “Take these articles, go, and deposit them in the temple in Jerusalem; and let the house of God be rebuilt on its original site.”
So this Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the house of God in Jerusalem, and from that time until now it has been under construction, but it is not yet completed.’ “

Now, therefore, if it pleases the king, let a search be made in the royal archives in Babylon to see whether King Cyrus indeed issued a decree to rebuild this house of God in Jerusalem; and let the king send us his decision in this matter.”
Then King Darius promulgated a decree, whereupon a search was conducted in the archival repository in which the treasures were deposited at Babylon.
A scroll was discovered at Ecbatana, the citadel of the province of Media, bearing a memorandum inscribed thus:

"In the first year of King Cyrus, Cyrus the king issued a decree concerning the house of God at Jerusalem: let the house be rebuilt as a locus of sacrifice, and let its foundations be firmly established; its height and its breadth shall each be sixty cubits,
with three courses of massive stones and one course of fresh timber, the expense being defrayed from the royal treasury.

Moreover, the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar carried away from the temple in Jerusalem and transported to Babylon, shall be restored and brought back to the temple in Jerusalem, to their proper place, and deposited in the house of God."
"Now then, Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and your associates, the Apharsachites who are in Beyond the River—withdraw yourselves utterly from that place.
Desist from interfering with the work on this house of God; let the governor and elders of the Jews erect it upon its original site.

I further decree that the full expense for these elders of the Jews in building this house of God be disbursed to these men without delay from the royal revenue, from the tribute of Beyond the River, so that the labor is not interrupted.

And whatever is requisite—young bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, together with wheat, salt, wine, and oil, according to the specification of the priests in Jerusalem—let it be furnished to them day by day without remission,
that they may present acceptable sacrifices to the God of heaven and intercede for the life of the king and his sons.

I also decree that if any man shall tamper with this edict, a beam shall be extracted from his dwelling and he shall be impaled thereupon, while his house shall be reduced to a dunghill on account of this.

May the God who has caused His name to dwell there overthrow every king or people who stretches forth a hand to alter or destroy this house of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued the decree; let it be executed with all diligence."
Then Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates executed the decree with all diligence, precisely as King Darius had dispatched it.

The elders of the Jews built and prospered through the prophetic ministrations of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo; they finished and built it in accordance with the commandment of the God of Israel and the decrees of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
This house was completed on the third day of the month Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
The Israelites—the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the exiles—celebrated the dedication of this house of God with exultation.

For the dedication of this house of God they offered one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and, as a sin offering for all Israel, twelve male goats according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
They appointed the priests to their divisions and the Levites to their courses for the liturgical service of God in Jerusalem, as it is written in the Book of Moses.
On the fourteenth day of the first month, the exiles celebrated the Passover.
The priests and the Levites had purified themselves in unison, and all were ceremonially clean; they slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the exiles, for their priestly brethren, and for themselves.
The Israelites who had returned from exile ate it, together with everyone who had segregated himself from the impurity of the peoples of the land in order to seek the the LORD God of Israel.

They kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days in joy, because the the LORD had gladdened them and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, to fortify their hands in the labor of the house of God, the God of Israel.
Subsequent to these occurrences, during the reign of Artaxerxes, king of Persia, Ezra—son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest—ascended from Babylon.

This Ezra undertook the ascent from Babylon as a scribe preeminently proficient in the law of Moses, which the LORD, the God of Israel, had given; and the king granted him every petition, in accordance with the hand of the LORD his God upon him.
Moreover, certain of the Israelites, together with priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants, ascended to Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.
He reached Jerusalem in the fifth month, in the seventh year of the king.
For he had commenced the ascent from Babylon on the first day of the first month, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, by the gracious hand of his God upon him.
For Ezra had devoted his heart to studying the law of the LORD, to practicing it, and to teaching in Israel statutes and ordinances.
This is a copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe—a scribe of the words of the commandments of the LORD and of His statutes for Israel:
“Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, scribe of the Law of the God of heaven: Greetings.
I hereby decree that anyone of the people of Israel within my realm, including their priests and Levites, who freely volunteers to accompany you to Jerusalem, may go.
“For you are sent by the king and his seven counselors to investigate Judah and Jerusalem according to the Law of your God that is in your hand,
and to convey the silver and gold that the king and his counselors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,

together with all the silver and gold that you may find throughout the province of Babylon, along with the freewill offerings of the people and of the priests who freely offer for the house of their God in Jerusalem.

“With this money, therefore, you shall diligently purchase bulls, rams, and lambs, together with their grain offerings and drink offerings, and you shall offer them on the altar of the house of your God in Jerusalem.
Whatever seems good to you and to your brothers to do with the remaining silver and gold, you may do according to the will of your God.
“The vessels that are given to you for the service of the house of your God, deliver in full before the God of Jerusalem.
Whatever else is needed for the house of your God that you may need to provide, provide it from the royal treasury.

“And I, King Artaxerxes, issue a decree to all the treasurers in the province Beyond the River: Whatever Ezra the priest, scribe of the Law of the God of heaven, asks of you, let it be done diligently,
up to one hundred talents of silver, one hundred cors of wheat, one hundred baths of wine, one hundred baths of oil, and salt without prescribed limit.
“Whatever is commanded by the God of heaven, let it be done with diligence for the house of the God of heaven, lest wrath fall upon the realm of the king and his sons.
We also inform you that it shall not be lawful to impose tribute, custom, or toll upon any of the priests, Levites, singers, doorkeepers, temple servants, or other servants of this house of God.

“And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God that is in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges to judge all the people in the province Beyond the River—all who know the laws of your God—and instruct those who do not know them.
Whoever will not obey the law of your God and the law of the king, let judgment be executed upon him diligently, whether by death, banishment, confiscation of goods, or imprisonment.”
Blessed be the LORD, the God of our fathers, who put such a thing into the heart of the king, to adorn the house of the LORD that is in Jerusalem,

and who extended covenant mercy to me before the king, his counselors, and all the king's mighty nobles. Thus I was strengthened according to the hand of the LORD my God upon me, and I gathered the principal men of Israel to go up with me.
These are the heads of their ancestral households, together with the genealogical register of those who ascended with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes.
Of the sons of Phinehas, Gershom; of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel; of the sons of David, Hattush.
Of the sons of Shecaniah, of the sons of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him were registered one hundred fifty males.
Of the sons of Pahath-moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred males.
Of the sons of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel, and with him three hundred males.
Of the sons of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him fifty males.
Of the sons of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, and with him seventy males.
Of the sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him eighty males.
Of the sons of Joab, Obadiah son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred eighteen males.
Of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and with him one hundred sixty males.
Of the sons of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight males.
Of the sons of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him one hundred ten males.
Of the last sons of Adonikam, these are their names: Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah, and with them sixty males.
Of the sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zabbud, and with them seventy males.
I gathered them at the river that flows to Ahava, and we encamped there three days. When I examined the people and the priests, I found no Levites there.
Then I sent for Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam, who were leaders, and for Joiarib and Elnathan, who were men of understanding.

I dispatched them to Iddo, the chief at Casiphia, and I put in their mouths the words they were to speak to Iddo and his brothers, the temple servants at Casiphia, that they might bring us servants for the house of our God.
By the good hand of our God upon us, they brought us Sherebiah, a man of discernment, of the sons of Mahli son of Levi son of Israel, with his sons and his brothers, eighteen men.
They also brought Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari, his brothers and their sons, twenty men.
And from the temple servants whom David and the officials had appointed for the service of the Levites came two hundred twenty, all of them designated by name.
Then I proclaimed a fast there at the river Ahava, that we might humble ourselves before our God, to seek from Him a safe way for us, for our little ones, and for all our possessions.

For I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to protect us from enemies on the way, because we had said to the king, “The hand of our God is for good upon all who seek Him, but His power and His wrath are against all who forsake Him.”
So we fasted and sought our God concerning this matter, and He answered us.
Then I set apart twelve of the leading priests, along with Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers.
I weighed out to them the silver, the gold, and the vessels—the offering for the house of our God that the king, his counselors, his princes, and all Israel present there had offered.
I weighed into their hands six hundred fifty talents of silver, silver vessels worth one hundred talents, and one hundred talents of gold,
twenty gold bowls worth a thousand darics, and two vessels of fine bronze, precious as gold.
And I said to them, “You are holy to the LORD, and the vessels are holy, and the silver and the gold are a freewill offering to the LORD, the God of your fathers.
Watch and keep them until you weigh them before the leading priests, the Levites, and the heads of the fathers’ households of Israel at Jerusalem, in the chambers of the house of the LORD.”
So the priests and the Levites received the weighed silver, gold, and vessels to bring them to Jerusalem, to the house of our God.

On the twelfth day of the first month we set out from the river Ahava to go to Jerusalem. The hand of our God was upon us, and He delivered us from the hand of the enemy and from ambushes along the way.
We arrived at Jerusalem and rested there three days.

On the fourth day, in the house of our God, the silver, gold, and vessels were weighed into the hands of Meremoth son of Uriah the priest; with him was Eleazar son of Phinehas, and with them were the Levites Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.
Everything was accounted for by number and by weight, and the total weight was recorded at that time.

Then the exiles who had returned from captivity offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering. All this was a burnt offering to the LORD.
They also delivered the king’s commissions to the king’s satraps and governors of the province Beyond the River, who supported the people and the house of God.

Once these matters had been brought to completion, the leaders drew near to me and declared, “Neither the people of Israel nor the priests and the Levites have kept themselves distinct from the peoples of the lands in respect to their abominations—namely, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.”

For they have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and for their sons, so that the holy lineage has become commingled with the peoples of the lands; indeed, the hand of the officials and governors has been foremost in this trespass.
When I heard this report, I tore my garment and my robe, plucked hair from my head and my beard, and sat down in stunned desolation.
Then all who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered to me because of the unfaithfulness of the exiles, while I remained seated in appalled silence until the evening oblation.
At the time of the evening oblation, I arose from my fasting, with my garment and robe torn, fell upon my knees, and spread out my hands to the LORD my God.
I said, “My God, I am ashamed and abashed to lift up my face before You, my God, for our iniquities have multiplied beyond measure and our guilt has ascended to the heavens.

From the days of our ancestors to this very day we have been in great guilt; and because of our iniquities, we—our kings and our priests—have been delivered into the hand of the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder, and to open disgrace, as is evident this day.

Yet now, for a brief moment, grace has been shown us by the LORD our God, leaving us a remnant and granting us a secure foothold in His holy place, so that our God may afford us a modest measure of revival in our servitude.

For although we are servants, our God has not forsaken us in our bondage; rather, He has extended steadfast love before the kings of Persia, granting us preservation, restoring the house of our God, repairing its ruins, and establishing a protective bulwark in Judah and Jerusalem.”
“And now, our God, what can we say after all this? For we have forsaken Your commandments.

which You commanded through Your servants the prophets, saying, ‘The land that you are entering to possess is a land polluted by the impurity of the peoples of the lands, by their abominations with which they have filled it from end to end in their uncleanness.’

Therefore do not give your daughters to their sons, nor take their daughters for your sons, and never seek their welfare or prosperity, so that you may grow strong and enjoy the good of the land and leave it as an inheritance to your sons forever.
After all that has come upon us because of our evil deeds and our great guilt, You, our God, have punished us less than our iniquities deserve and have given us such a remnant as this.
Shall we again break Your commandments and intermarry with the peoples who practice these abominations? Would You not then be angry with us until You had consumed us, leaving no remnant or survivor?
The LORD, the God of Israel, You are righteous, for we are left a remnant as we are this day. Behold, we stand before You in our guilt, for no one can stand in Your presence on account of this.”

While Ezra was praying and confessing, weeping and prostrating himself before the house of God, an exceedingly great assembly of Israelites—men, women, and children—gathered to him; and the people wept with exceeding bitterness.

Then Shecaniah son of Jehiel, of the sons of Elam, answered Ezra: “We have been unfaithful to our God and have taken foreign wives from the peoples of the land; yet even now there is hope for Israel in this matter.

Now therefore let us make a covenant with our God to put away all the wives and the children born to them, according to the counsel of my lord and of those who tremble at the commandment of our God; and let it be done according to the Law.
Arise, for this matter is your responsibility, and we are with you; be strong and act.”
Then Ezra arose and made the priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear that they would do according to this word; and they swore.

Ezra then withdrew from before the house of God and went to the chamber of Johanan son of Eliashib; and while there he neither ate bread nor drank water, for he was mourning over the unfaithfulness of the exiles.
And a proclamation was issued throughout Judah and Jerusalem to all the exiles, that they should assemble at Jerusalem,
and that whoever did not come within three days, according to the counsel of the officials and elders, all his property should be forfeited and he himself separated from the assembly of the exiles.

So all the men of Judah and Benjamin assembled at Jerusalem within the three days; it was the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month. And all the people sat in the open square before the house of God, trembling because of this matter and because of the heavy rain.
Then Ezra the priest stood up and said to them, “You have been unfaithful and have married foreign women, thereby adding to the guilt of Israel.
Now therefore make confession to the the LORD, the God of your fathers, and do His will; separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign wives.”
Then all the assembly answered with a loud voice, “As you have said, so it is our duty to do.
But the people are many, and it is the rainy season; we cannot stand outside, nor is this the work of one or two days, for we have greatly transgressed in this matter.

Let our leaders stand for the whole assembly, and let all in our cities who have married foreign women come at appointed times, together with the elders and judges of each city, until the fierce wrath of our God is turned away from us in this matter.”
Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah opposed this, with Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite supporting them.
The exiles did so. Ezra the priest selected men who were heads of fathers’ houses, all designated by name, and they sat down on the first day of the tenth month to examine the matter.
They finished with all the men who had married foreign women by the first day of the first month.
Among the sons of the priests who had married foreign women were found: of the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and his brothers—Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah.
They pledged to put away their wives, and, being guilty, they offered a ram of the flock for their guilt.
Of the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
Of the sons of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
Of the sons of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
Of the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (that is, Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
Of the singers: Eliashib. Of the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
And of Israel: of the sons of Parosh—Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah.
Of the sons of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah.
Of the sons of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.
Of the sons of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.
Of the sons of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Jeremoth.
Of the sons of Pahath-moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.
Of the sons of Harim: Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, and Shimeon;
Of the sons of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.
Of the sons of Bani: Maadai, Amram, and Uel;
Of the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah.
All these had married foreign women, and some of them had wives by whom they had children.
The words of Nehemiah son of Hachaliah. In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, I was in the citadel at Susa.
Hanani, one of my brothers, came with some men from Judah, and I questioned them about the Jews who had survived the exile and about Jerusalem.
They said to me, “Those who survived the exile and remain in the province are in great distress and disgrace; the wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire.”
When I heard these words, I sat down and wept; I mourned for days, and I fasted and prayed before the God of heaven.
I said, “I implore the LORD, God of heaven, the great and awesome God, who keeps covenant and steadfast love with those who love Him and keep His commandments,

let Your eyes be open and Your ear attentive to hear the prayer of Your servant that I am praying before You day and night for Your servants, the children of Israel, confessing the sins of the children of Israel, which we have sinned against You; both I and my father’s house have sinned.
We have acted very corruptly against You and have not kept the commandments, statutes, and ordinances that You commanded Your servant Moses.
“Remember, I pray, the word that You commanded Your servant Moses, saying, ‘If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the peoples;
