The LORD said to the Adversary, "Have you considered My servant Job? For there is no one like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man who fears God and turns away from evil."
The Adversary answered the LORD and said, "Does Job fear God for nothing?
Have You not made a hedge about him and his house and all that he has, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions have increased in the land.
But now stretch out Your hand and touch all that he has, and he will surely curse You to Your face."
The LORD said to the Adversary, "Behold, all that he has is in your hand; only do not stretch out your hand against him." So the Adversary went out from the presence of the LORD.
Now on the day when his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their firstborn brother,
a messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were plowing and the donkeys feeding beside them,
and the Sabeans fell upon them and seized them; they struck down the servants with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you."
While he was still speaking, another came and said, "The fire of God fell from heaven and burned up the sheep and the servants, and I alone have escaped to tell you."

While he was still speaking, another came and said, "The Chaldeans formed three bands and raided the camels and took them, and struck down the servants with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you."
While he was still speaking, another came and said, "Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their firstborn brother,
and behold, a great wind came from across the wilderness and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young people, and they died; and I alone have escaped to tell you."
Then Job arose and tore his robe and shaved his head, and he fell to the ground and worshiped.
He said, "Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked shall I return there. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away; Blessed be the name of the LORD."
In all this Job did not sin, nor did he charge God with wrongdoing.
Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came among them to present himself before the LORD.
The LORD said to Satan, "From where do you come?" Satan answered the LORD and said, "From roaming the earth and walking about in it."

The LORD said to Satan, "Have you considered My servant Job? For there is no one like him on earth—a man blameless and upright, who fears God and shuns evil. He still holds fast his integrity, though you have incited Me against him to destroy him without cause."
Satan answered the LORD, "A man will relinquish all his possessions to preserve his own life. But stretch out Your hand and strike his bone and his flesh, and he will surely curse You to Your face."
The LORD said to Satan, "Very well, he is in your hand; only spare his life."
So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD and afflicted Job with grievous boils from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.
He took a potsherd with which to scrape himself while he sat among the ashes.
Then his wife said to him, "Do you still hold fast your integrity? Curse God and die!"
He said to her, "You speak as one of the witless women speaks. Shall we receive good from God and not receive adversity?" In all this Job did not sin with his lips.

Now when Job's three friends heard of all the calamity that had befallen him, each came from his own place—Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. They arranged to meet together to go and mourn with him and to comfort him.
When they lifted up their eyes from afar, they did not recognize him; they raised their voices and wept, and each tore his robe and cast dust heavenward upon his head.
They sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his suffering was exceedingly great.
Afterward Job opened his mouth and cursed his day.
Let the day perish on which I was born, and the night that declared a male child had been conceived.
Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from on high, and let not light shine upon it.
Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it.
Let thick darkness seize that night; let it not rejoice among the days of the year; let it not be numbered among the months.
Behold, let that night be barren; let no cry of joy enter it.
Let those who execrate the day execrate it, even those prepared to rouse Leviathan.
Let the stars of its twilight be dark; let it wait for light, but have none; and let it never behold the dawning of the morning.
For it did not shut the doors of my mother’s womb, nor hide trouble from my eyes.” “
Why did I not die at birth? Why did I not perish when I came from the womb?
Why did knees receive me, or breasts, that I might nurse?
For then I would have lain down and been quiet; I would have slept, and then I would have been at rest,
with kings and counselors of the earth, who built for themselves places now in ruins,
or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver;
or I would have been hidden like a stillborn child, like infants who never saw light.
There the wicked cease from turmoil, and there the weary are at rest.
There prisoners are at ease together; they do not hear the voice of the oppressor.
The small and the great are there, and the servant is free from his master.” “
Why is light given to one in misery, and life to the bitter in soul,
who long for death, but it does not come, and seek it more eagerly than buried treasure,
who rejoice exceedingly and are glad when they find the grave?
To a man whose way is hidden, and whom God has hedged in?
For my sighing comes in place of my bread, and my groanings are poured out like water.
For the thing I feared has come upon me, and what I dreaded has befallen me.
I am not at ease, nor am I quiet, and I have no rest; but trouble comes.”
“If one should presume to address you, would you grow weary? Yet who could restrain himself from speaking?
Surely you have instructed multitudes and fortified their faltering hands.
Your words have sustained those who were stumbling, and you have strengthened knees that were buckling.
But now adversity comes to you, and you are wearied; it touches you, and you are dismayed.
Is not your reverence your confidence, and the integrity of your ways your hope?
“Remember now, who has ever perished while innocent? Or where have the upright been destroyed?
As I have seen, those who plow iniquity and sow trouble reap the same.
By the breath of God they perish, and by the blast of His anger they are consumed.
The roar of the lion and the voice of the fierce lion are silenced, and the teeth of the young lions are broken.
The old lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.
“Now a word was brought to me stealthily, and my ear caught a whisper of it.
In disquieting dreams in the night, when deep sleep falls upon men,
fear and trembling seized me and made all my bones shudder.
Then a spirit glided past my face, and the hair of my flesh stood on end.
It stood still, but I could not discern its form; a figure was before my eyes, and I heard a hushed voice:
“‘Can a mortal be more righteous than God, or a man more pure than his Maker?
If God places no trust in His servants and charges even His angels with error,
how much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundations rest upon dust and who are crushed like a moth!
They are shattered from morning to evening; without anyone's notice, they perish forever.
Are not their tent cords pulled up, so that they die devoid of wisdom?’”
Call out now: is there anyone who will answer you? And to which of the holy ones will you turn?
For indignation slays the fool, and jealousy destroys the simple.
I have observed the fool taking root, yet suddenly I pronounced a curse upon his dwelling.
His sons are driven far from deliverance, crushed at the gate, with no one to rescue them.
The hungry devour his harvest, snatching it even from among thorns, while the thirsty pant after his wealth.
For misfortune does not spring from the dust, nor does toil burgeon from the soil;
rather, man is born to hardship, as sparks inevitably soar upward.
But I, for my part, would seek God and entrust my case to God,
who accomplishes great and unsearchable things, wonders beyond numbering;
who gives rain upon the earth and sends waters across the fields;
who exalts the lowly and raises mourners to deliverance;
who frustrates the schemes of the crafty, so that their hands cannot bring their designs to completion;
who ensnares the wise in their own cunning, while the counsel of the perverse is precipitated into ruin.
They meet with darkness in the daytime and grope at noon as though it were night.
Yet He delivers the needy from the sword, from their devouring words, and from the hand of the mighty.
Thus the poor retain hope, while injustice closes its mouth.
Observe: blessed is the mortal whom God reproves; therefore do not despise the discipline of the Almighty,
for He wounds yet binds up, He shatters yet His hands heal.
He will deliver you from six calamities; indeed, in seven no harm shall touch you.
In famine He will redeem you from death, and in war from the power of the sword.
You will be sheltered from the lash of the tongue, and you will not fear devastation when it arrives.
You will laugh at devastation and famine, and you will not fear the beasts of the earth.
For you will be allied with the stones of the field, and the beasts of the field will be at peace with you.
You will know that your tent is secure; you will survey your homestead and lack nothing.
You will also know that your progeny will be numerous and your descendants like the grass of the earth.
You will come to your grave in ripe old age, as a sheaf is gathered in its season.
Observe, we have searched this out; it is true. Hear it and know it for yourself.
“Oh, that my vexation were weighed, and my calamity laid in the balances together!
For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas; therefore my words have been rash.
For the arrows of the Almighty are in me; my spirit drinks their venom; the terrors of God are arrayed against me.
Does the wild donkey bray over grass, or the ox low over its fodder?
Can tasteless food be eaten without salt, or is there flavor in the white of an egg?
My soul refuses to touch them; they are as loathsome food to me.
“Oh, that my request might come to pass, and that God would grant my desire!
That it would please God to crush me, that He would loose His hand and cut me off!
Then I would still have comfort; I would exult in pain unsparing, for I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should prolong my life?
Is my strength the strength of stones, or is my flesh bronze?
Is there no help within me, and has sound wisdom been driven from me?
“He who withholds kindness from a friend forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
My brothers have dealt treacherously like a torrent, like the torrents of wadis that pass away.
They are darkened because of ice; snow is hidden upon them.
When they are scorched, they vanish; when it is hot, they disappear from their place.
The caravans turn aside from their course; they go up into the waste and perish.
The caravans of Tema looked; the travelers of Sheba hoped in them.
They were ashamed because they trusted; they came there and were confounded.
For now you are nothing; you see a dreadful sight and are afraid.
“Did I say, ‘Give me something,’ or, ‘From your wealth offer a bribe on my behalf’?
Or, ‘Deliver me from the hand of the adversary,’ or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the ruthless’?
Teach me, and I will be silent; show me how I have gone astray.
How forceful are upright words! But what does your reproof prove?
Do you intend to reprove mere words, the speeches of a despairing man that are but wind?
You would even gamble away an orphan and barter over your friend.
But now be pleased to look at me; I will not lie to your face.
Reconsider, I pray; let there be no injustice; reconsider, for my righteousness is still at stake.
Is there injustice on my tongue? Can my palate not discern calamity?”
Is not human existence upon earth an arduous campaign, and are not one’s days like those of a hired laborer?
Like a bondservant panting for the shade, and like a wage-earner awaiting his stipend,
I have been bequeathed months of futility, and nights of affliction have been apportioned to me.
When I lie down, I think, “When shall I arise?” The night drags on, and I am saturated with restlessness until dawn.
My flesh is arrayed in worms and clods of dust; my skin crusts over, only to fester anew.
My days pass more swiftly than a weaver’s shuttle, and they are consumed in hopelessness.
Remember that my life is but a breath; my eye will never again behold prosperity.
The eye that now beholds me will behold me no more; when Your eyes seek me, I shall be no more.
As a cloud dissipates and passes away, so he who descends to Sheol does not ascend again.
He shall never return to his house, nor shall his dwelling place acknowledge him again.
Accordingly, I shall not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit, and I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
Am I the sea, or some leviathan, that You should station a guard over me?
When I say, “My bed will comfort me; my couch will bear my lament,”
then You frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions,
so that my very soul prefers strangulation and death rather than these bones.
I despise it; I would not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.
What is man that You should magnify him, and that You should set Your heart upon him,
that You visit him each morning and test him every instant?
How long will You not look away from me, nor release me even long enough to swallow my saliva?
If I have sinned, what have I done to You, O Watcher of men? Why have You made me Your mark, so that I have become a burden to myself?
And why do You not pardon my transgression and remove my iniquity? For now I shall lie down in the dust; You will seek me, but I shall be no more.
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said: “
How long will you persist in this torrent of verbiage, while the words of your mouth remain a blustering wind?
Does God pervert justice, or does the Almighty distort righteousness?
If your children sinned against Him, He consigned them to the power of their transgression. “
If you seek God with earnest diligence and supplicate the Almighty,
if you are pure and upright, surely now He will rouse Himself on your behalf and bring to completion the dwelling of your righteousness.
Though your beginning was diminutive, your latter end will increase immeasurably. “
I pray you, inquire of the former generation, and attend to the investigations of their fathers.
For we are but of yesterday and know nothing, for our days upon the earth are a shadow.
Will they not teach you and say to you, and bring forth words from their inmost being? “
Can the papyrus thrust itself upward without a marsh? Can reeds flourish in the absence of water?
While it is still verdant and uncut, it withers before every other plant.
So are the paths of all who forget God, and the hope of the hypocrite perishes.
Whose confidence is severed, and whose trust is a spider's web.
He leans upon his house, yet it does not stand; he clings to it, yet it does not endure.
He is luxuriant before the sun, and his shoots spread forth over his garden.
His roots entwine the heap of stones; he seeks a dwelling among the rocks.
If he is swept away from his place, it disowns him, saying, 'I have not seen you.'
Behold, this is the joy of his way; and from the dust others will arise. “
Behold, God does not reject a blameless man, nor does He strengthen the hand of evildoers.
He will yet fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with shouts of joy.
Those who hate you will be clothed with shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.”
"Indeed, I know that it is so; yet how can a mortal be vindicated before God?
If he should wish to contend with Him, he could not answer Him once in a thousand times.
Wise in heart and mighty in strength is He; who has hardened himself against Him and prospered?
"He removes mountains, and they know it not, overturning them in His anger.
He shakes the earth from its place, so that its pillars tremble.
He commands the sun, and it does not rise; He seals up the stars.
He alone stretches out the heavens and treads upon the heights of the sea.
He made the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the constellations of the south.
"He performs great things beyond searching out, and wonders without number.
If He passes by me, I do not see Him; if He moves on, I do not perceive Him.
If He snatches away, who will turn Him back? Who will say to Him, 'What are You doing?'
"God will not turn back His anger; beneath Him the champions of Rahab are brought low.
How much less, then, can I answer Him, choosing my words before Him?
Though I were righteous, I could not answer Him; I could only plead for mercy to my Judge.
If I summoned Him and He answered, I would not believe that He was listening to my voice.
"For He crushes me with a tempest and multiplies my wounds without cause.
He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
If it is a matter of strength, behold, He is mighty; if of justice, who can summon Him?
Though I be righteous, my own mouth would condemn me; though I be blameless, it would prove me perverse.
I am blameless—I do not even know my own soul—I loathe my life.
"It is all one; therefore I say, 'He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.'
When the scourge strikes suddenly, He mocks the plight of the innocent.
The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He covers the faces of its judges. If it is not He, then who is it?
"My days are swifter than a runner; they flee away and see no good.
They pass by like skiffs of reed, like an eagle swooping down upon prey.
"If I say, 'I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad countenance and be cheerful,'
I am afraid of all my sorrows; I know that You will not hold me innocent.
I am guilty; why then should I labor in vain?
If I wash myself with snow and cleanse my hands with lye,
then You would plunge me into the pit, and my own clothes would abhor me.
"For He is not a man, as I am, that I should answer Him, that we should come together in judgment.
There is no arbiter between us, to lay his hand upon us both.
Let Him take His rod away from me, and let not His terror make me afraid;
then I would speak and not fear Him, for I am not such within myself."
My soul is repulsed by my very existence; I shall therefore relinquish all restraint upon my grievance and speak from the acrimony of my spirit.
I will say to God, “Do not condemn me; disclose to me why You contend with me.
Is it consonant with Your justice to oppress, to spurn the work of Your hands, while You lavish favor upon the machinations of the wicked?”
Do You possess eyes of flesh? Do You see as a mortal sees?
Are Your days like those of a mortal, or Your years like those of a man,
that You should investigate my iniquity and search out my sin?
Although You know that I am not guilty, no one can deliver me from Your hand.
Your hands fashioned and knit me together on every side, yet You consume me.
Remember, I implore You, that You made me from clay; will You return me to dust?
Did You not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?
You clothed me with skin and flesh and knit me together with bones and sinews.
You granted me life and steadfast love, and Your providence guarded my spirit.
Yet You concealed these purposes within Your heart; I know that this design is with You.
If I sin, You mark me, and You will not acquit me of my iniquity.
If I am wicked, woe to me; and if I am righteous, I cannot lift up my head, for I am glutted with ignominy and conscious of my affliction.
Should I presume to raise my head, You stalk me like a lion and once more unleash Your wonders against me.
You renew Your witnesses against me and multiply Your wrath toward me; successive calamities and warfare are arrayed against me.
Why then did You bring me forth from the womb? Would that I had perished unseen!
I would have been as though I had never existed, carried from the womb to the grave.
Are not my days few? Then cease, and leave me alone, that I may find a little respite
before I go to the place from which I shall not return, to the land of darkness and deep shadow—
a land of gloom, like thick darkness, of deep shadow without order, where light itself is as darkness.
Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
“Shall an abundance of words go unanswered, or shall a man of mere lips be vindicated?
Your empty talk silences men, and you scoff, and no one puts you to shame.
You say, ‘My teaching is pure, and I am clean in Your eyes.’
“But oh, that God would speak, and open His lips with you!
And that He would show you the secrets of wisdom—for sound wisdom is twofold—know then that God exacts from you less than your iniquity deserves.
“Can you fathom the deep things of God? Can you discover the limit of the Almighty?
It is higher than heaven—what can you do? Deeper than Sheol—what can you know?
Its measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea.
If He passes by, shuts up, and summons to judgment, who can turn Him back?
For He knows worthless men; He sees iniquity as well, and will He not take note?
But a man empty of understanding will never truly become wise—just as a wild donkey’s colt cannot be born human.
“If you prepare your heart and stretch out your hands to Him,
if you put away the iniquity in your hand and do not let unrighteousness dwell in your tents,
then surely you will lift up your face without blemish; you will be secure and not fear.
For you will forget your misery; you will remember it as waters that have passed away.
And your life will be brighter than noonday; darkness will be like the morning.
You will be secure, because there is hope; you will dig, and lie down in safety.
You will lie down, and no one will make you afraid; many will entreat your favor.
But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and they will find no escape; their hope will end in a dying breath.”
“Truly you are the people, and wisdom will perish with you!
But I too possess understanding, no less than you; I am not inferior to you. Who, after all, does not know such things?
I have become a byword of derision among my companions, though I invoked God and received answer—a righteous and blameless man reduced to mockery.
Ease breeds contempt for calamity, yet calamity stands poised for those whose step falters.
The dwellings of marauders enjoy repose, and those who defy God remain secure, as though their deity were but an artifact borne in their own hand.
“But inquire now of the beasts, and they will instruct you; of the birds of heaven, and they will declare to you.
Or commune with the earth, and it will instruct you; and the fish of the sea will recount to you.
Which of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has accomplished this?
In His hand rests the life of every living thing and the breath of all humankind.
Does not the ear assay words, as the palate discerns food?
With the aged dwells wisdom, and understanding with length of days.
“With Him reside wisdom and might; counsel and understanding are His.
What He demolishes shall not be rebuilt; whom He confines shall not be released.
If He withholds the waters, they languish; if He releases them, they overwhelm the earth.
To Him belong strength and sound wisdom; the deceived and the deceiver are His alike.
He leads counselors away despoiled and renders judges witless.
He unbinds the authority of kings and girds their loins with a loincloth.
He leads priests away despoiled and subverts the established.
He deprives the trustworthy of speech and takes discernment from elders.
He pours contempt upon nobles and loosens the belt of the mighty.
He unveils profundities hidden in darkness and brings the shadow of death into light.
He magnifies nations, then annihilates them; He enlarges nations, then disperses them.
He strips the leaders of the earth of their discernment and causes them to wander in a pathless waste.
They grope in darkness without light, and He makes them stagger as drunkards.”
Indeed, my eye has seen all this, and my ear has heard and understood it.
According to your knowledge, I too possess knowledge; I am by no means inferior to you.
Yet I would speak to the Almighty, and I am eager to argue my case with God.
But you are forgers of falsehood, and all of you are physicians of no value.
Would that you might keep absolute silence; then would wisdom be yours.
Hear now my reproof, and give heed to the contentions of my lips.
Will you utter iniquity for God, and speak deceit on His behalf?
Will you show Him favoritism? Will you plead God's cause?
Would it be well for Him to scrutinize you? Or will you mock Him as one mocks a mortal?
He will surely reprove you if you show partiality in secret.
Will not His exaltation affright you, and His terror descend upon you?
Your remembered sayings are proverbs of ashes, and your bulwarks are bulwarks of clay.
Hold your peace before me, and let me speak; then let what may come upon me.
Why should I endanger my own flesh and place my life at hazard?
Though He slay me, I will still hope in Him; yet I will defend my ways before Him.
He Himself shall be my salvation, for no godless man shall come into His presence.
Hear diligently my speech, and let my declaration reach your ears.
Behold, I have ordered my case; I know that I shall be justified.
Who is he that will strive with me? For now, if I hold my peace, I shall expire.
Only do not two things unto me; then will I not hide myself from You.
Withdraw Your hand far from me, and let not Your dread make me afraid.
Then summon me, and I will answer; or let me speak, and do You reply.
How many are my iniquities and sins? Make me know my transgression and my sin.
Why do You hide Your face and regard me as Your enemy?
Will You terrorize a windblown leaf and pursue dry chaff?
For You write bitter things against me and make me inherit the sins of my youth.
You put my feet in the stocks and observe all my paths; You inscribe a mark upon the soles of my feet.
And he wastes away like a rotten thing, like a garment that moths have consumed.
A mortal, begotten of woman, endures but a truncated span and is saturated with turmoil.
He blossoms like a flower and is cut down; he flees like a shadow and leaves no enduring trace.
Do You open Your eyes upon such a one and bring me into judgment alongside You?
Who can distill purity from impurity? No one.
If his days are predetermined, the enumeration of his months resides with You; You have fixed his terminus, which he cannot transgress.
Avert Your gaze from him and let him rest, until, like a hired laborer, he completes his allotted day.
For a tree retains hope: if it is felled, it will sprout anew, and its tender shoots will not languish.
Though its root ages in the earth and its stump dies in the ground,
at the scent of water it will bud and put forth branches like a newly planted shoot.
Yet a mortal perishes and is laid low; he expires, and whither has he gone?
As water vanishes from the sea and a river wastes and desiccates,
so a man lies down and does not rise again; until the heavens are no more, he will not awaken or be roused from his slumber.
Oh, that You would conceal me in Sheol, that You would hide me until Your wrath subsides, that You would appoint me a fixed term and remember me!
If a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my service I will wait until my renewal comes.
You would call, and I would answer You; You would yearn for the work of Your hands.
For now You tally my steps, yet You do not keep watch over my sin.
My transgression is sealed in a pouch, and You fasten my iniquity upon me.
But a mountain collapses and erodes, and a rock is displaced from its site;
water abrades stones, and torrents wash away the soil of the earth, so You annihilate the hope of a mortal.
You subdue him in perpetuity, and he passes away; You alter his countenance and send him away.
His sons are honored, but he remains ignorant; they are brought low, but he is oblivious.
He experiences only the pain of his own flesh and mourns solely for himself.
Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
“Should a wise man answer with vacuous counsel, or sate his belly with hollow wind?
Should he contend with unprofitable discourse, or with words that yield no benefit?
Indeed, you even undermine piety and diminish devotion before God.
For your transgression tutors your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty.
Your own mouth condemns you, not I; your own lips testify against you.”
“Were you the firstborn of mankind? Were you brought forth before the hills?
Do you listen in on God’s council, and confine wisdom to yourself?
What do you know that we do not? What do you understand that is absent from us?
Both the gray-haired and the aged are on our side—men far older than your father.
Are God’s consolations too slight for you, or the gentle word addressed to you?
Why does your heart carry you away, and why do your eyes flash with defiance,
so that you turn your spirit against God and pour forth such words from your mouth?
What is man, that he should be pure, or one born of woman, that he should be righteous?
If God places no trust in His holy ones, and the heavens are not pure in His sight,
how much less man, who is vile and corrupt, who drinks iniquity like water!”

“Listen to me; I will explicate to you; what I have seen I will declare—what wise men have declared, concealing nothing received from their fathers—to whom alone the land was given, when no foreigner passed among them.
The wicked man writhes in pain all his days; the span of years allotted to the ruthless remains hidden.
Sounds of terror are in his ears; in his prosperity the destroyer attacks him.
He does not believe he will return from darkness; he is marked for the sword.
He wanders about for food, saying, ‘Where is it?’ He knows that a day of darkness is at hand.
Distress and anguish terrify him; they overwhelm him, like a king poised for battle.
For he has stretched out his hand against God and vaunts himself against the Almighty,
rushing headlong at Him with his thick, embossed shield.
Though his face is covered with fat and his waist bulges with flesh,
he will dwell in ruined cities, in houses not his own, which are destined to become rubble.
He will not grow rich; his wealth will not endure; his possessions will not overspread the land.
He will not escape the darkness; a flame will wither his shoots, and the breath of God's mouth will carry him away.
Let him not deceive himself by trusting in emptiness, for emptiness will be his recompense.
It will be paid in full before his time, and his branch will not flourish.
He will be like a vine stripped of its unripe grapes, like an olive tree casting off its blossoms.
For the company of the godless will be barren, and fire will consume the tents of bribery.
They conceive trouble and give birth to iniquity; their womb prepares deceit.”
"I have heard many such utterances; you are all grievous comforters.
Is there no terminus to these blustering words? What provokes you, that you should retort?
I, too, could discourse as you do, were your soul in my soul's stead; I could marshal words against you and wag my head at you.
I would encourage you with my mouth, and the consolation of my lips would bring you relief.
If I speak, my anguish is not diminished; if I refrain, what is lifted from me?
"Yet now He has worn me out; you have made desolate all my company.
You have shriveled me, and it has become a witness; my gauntness rises up against me and testifies to my face.
His wrath has torn me, and He has hated me; He gnashes His teeth against me; my adversary sharpens his eyes upon me.
They gape at me with their mouths; they strike my cheek with derision; they are filled with contempt together against me.
"God delivers me to the perverse, and casts me into the hands of the wicked.
I was at ease, and He shattered me; He seized me by the neck and dashed me to pieces; He set me up as His target.
His archers surround me; He pierces my kidneys without mercy and pours out my gall upon the ground.
He breaks me with breach upon breach; He rushes upon me like a warrior.
"I have sewn sackcloth over my skin and have thrust my horn into the dust.
My face is inflamed with weeping, and the shadow of death lies upon my eyelids.
Though there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.
O earth, do not cover my blood, and let my outcry find no resting place.
Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and my advocate is on high.
My friends are my mockers; my eyes pour out tears to God,
that He would plead a man's cause with God, and a son of man's cause with his neighbor.
For when a few years have passed, I shall go by a path from which I shall not return."
My spirit is shattered; my days have been extinguished; the grave stands ready for me.
Surely mockers surround me, while my eyes remain fixed upon their defiance.
Please grant me a pledge with You, for who else will stand surety for me?
For You have concealed their hearts from discernment; therefore You will not exalt them.
Whoever denounces his friends for a share of the spoils will see his children's eyes fail.
He has made me a byword among the peoples, so that I have become one at whom they spit.
My eyes have dimmed with grief, and all my frame has dwindled to a shadow.
The upright are appalled at this, and the innocent rouses himself against the godless.
Yet the righteous will hold fast to his course, and the one whose hands are clean will grow ever stronger.
But come now, all of you; I shall not find a wise man among you.
My days have passed; my plans have been severed, even the desires of my heart.
They turn night into day, saying, "Light is near at hand, notwithstanding the darkness."
If I look to Sheol as my home, and spread my couch in the darkness,
I have said to corruption, "You are my father," and to the worm, "You are my mother and my sister."
Where, then, is my hope? Who could possibly discern it?
Will it descend to the bars of Sheol, when together we sink into the dust?
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
“How long will you continue to set bounds to words? Attain understanding, and then we shall speak.
Why are we reckoned as beasts? Why are we esteemed unclean in your eyes?
He tears himself in his anger; shall the earth be forsaken for your sake, or the rock be removed from its place?
“Indeed, the light of the wicked is extinguished, and the spark of his fire does not shine.
The light in his tent is darkened, and his lamp above him is extinguished.
His vigorous steps are shortened, and his own counsel casts him down.
For he is thrust into a net by his own feet, and he walks upon a snare.
A trap seizes him by the heel, and a snare holds him fast.
A noose is hidden for him in the ground, and a trap lies in his path.
Terrors frighten him on every side and harass him at every step.
His strength is famished, and calamity stands ready at his side.
It devours portions of his skin; the firstborn of death devours his limbs.
“He is torn from the security of his tent and marched to the king of terrors.
Nothing of his remains in his tent; brimstone dwells therein, and sulfur is scattered over his dwelling.
His roots dry up below, and his branches wither above.
His memory perishes from the earth, and he has no name in the street.
He is driven from light into darkness and banished from the world.
He has no offspring or posterity among his people, and no survivor in his dwellings.
Those who come after are appalled at his fate, and those who went before are seized with horror.
Surely such are the dwellings of the wicked, and this is the place of one who does not know God.”
"How long will you vex my soul and crush me with words?
You have now reproached me ten times over, and you are not ashamed to assail me.
If I have truly gone astray, my error remains my own concern.
If you truly magnify yourselves against me and adduce my disgrace as testimony against me,
then know that God has wronged me and ensnared me in His net.
"Though I cry out, 'Violence!' I receive no answer; though I appeal for justice, none is granted.
He has walled up my way so that I cannot pass, and He has shrouded my paths in darkness.
He has stripped me of my honor and removed the crown from my head.
He tears me down on every side until I am undone; He uproots my hope as though it were a tree.
His wrath burns against me, and He counts me among His enemies.
His troops advance in concert; they raise a siege ramp against me and encamp around my tent.
"He has estranged my brothers from me, and my acquaintances have deserted me.
My kinsmen have failed me, and my friends have forgotten me.
My guests and maidservants regard me as a stranger; in their eyes I am a foreigner.
I summon my servant, yet he does not answer; I must entreat him with my own mouth.
My breath has become offensive to my wife, and I am loathsome to my own children.
Even the young boys despise me; whenever I rise, they speak against me.
All my intimate friends abhor me, and those I cherished have turned against me.
My bones cleave to my skin and flesh, and I have barely escaped with my life.
"Have compassion on me, my friends, have compassion, for the hand of God has struck me.
Why do you pursue me as God does? Will you never be satisfied with my flesh?
"Oh, that my words were recorded, that they were inscribed in a book,
that with an iron stylus and lead they were engraved in rock forever!
But I know that my Redeemer lives, and that in the end He will stand upon the dust.
Even after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God.
I will see Him for myself; my eyes will behold Him, and not as a stranger. My innermost being is consumed with longing.
"If you say, 'How shall we persecute him, since the root of the matter is found in him?'
then be afraid of the sword yourselves, for wrath brings the punishment of the sword, so that you may know there is a judgment."
Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
“Therefore my reflections impel me to reply, because of the agitation within me.
I hear a reproof that dishonors me, and my understanding spirit compels my answer.
Do you not know this from antiquity, from the time humanity was established upon the earth,
that the triumph of the wicked is brief and the joy of the godless but momentary?
Though his exaltation ascend to the heavens and his head touch the clouds,
he perishes forever like his own refuse; those who beheld him ask, ‘Where is he?’
He flies away like a dream and is not found; he is driven off like a vision of the night.
The eye that saw him sees him no more, and his place no longer beholds him.
“His children conciliate the impoverished, and his hands restore his ill-gotten wealth.
His bones, though full of youthful vigor, lie down with him in the dust.
Though evil is sweet in his mouth and he hides it beneath his tongue,
though he savors it and will not relinquish it, but keeps it in the roof of his mouth,
his food turns in his entrails and becomes the venom of asps within him.
He swallows riches and vomits them up; God expels them from his belly.
He suckles the poison of asps; the viper’s tongue slays him.
He does not behold the streams, the rivers flowing with honey and curds.
He returns the fruit of his labor without consuming it, and he cannot exult in the wealth of his exchange.
“For he has crushed and abandoned the poor; he has seized a house he did not build.
Because he knew no quietude in his belly, he retains nothing he desires.
Nothing remains for him to devour; therefore his prosperity does not endure.
In the fullness of his sufficiency he is in straits, and every hand of misery comes against him.
When he fills his belly, God sends His fierce anger upon him and rains it upon his flesh.
He may flee from the iron weapon, but the bronze bow pierces him.
He draws it forth, and it comes out of his back; the glittering point emerges from his gall; terrors come upon him.
All darkness is reserved for his treasures; an unfanned fire consumes him and devours the remnant in his tent.
The heavens reveal his iniquity, and the earth rises up against him.
The increase of his house departs; it flows away in the day of His anger.
This is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the heritage decreed to him by God.”
“Listen attentively to my discourse, and let this serve as your consolation.
Bear with me while I speak, and after I have finished, mock on.
Is my complaint directed against a mortal? If so, why should my spirit not chafe?
Turn toward me and be appalled; place a hand over the mouth.
Even when I recall these things, I am seized with terror, and trembling grips my flesh.
Why do the wicked continue to live, grow old, and even wax mighty in power?
Their progeny stand secure before them, and their descendants are before their eyes.
Their households are secure from dread, and the rod of God is not upon them.
Their bull breeds without failure, and their cow calves without miscarriage.
They send out their little ones like a flock, and their children skip about.
They lift up the tambourine and lyre, and make merry to the sound of the pipe.
They spend their days in prosperity, and in a moment they descend to Sheol.
Yet they say to God, “Depart from us, for we do not desire knowledge of Your ways.
What is the Almighty, that we should serve Him? What profit would we gain if we entreat Him?”
Behold, their prosperity is not in their own hand; the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
How often is the lamp of the wicked extinguished, and how often does their calamity come upon them? God distributes sorrows in His anger.
They become like stubble before the wind, and like chaff swept away by a storm.
God stores up his iniquity for his children; He repays him, and he shall know it.
His own eyes will see his destruction, and he will drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
For what delight has he in his household after him, when the number of his months has been cut off?
Shall anyone teach God knowledge, seeing that He judges those who are exalted?
One man dies in his full vigor, wholly at ease and secure;
his frame is well nourished, and the marrow of his bones is moistened.
Another dies in bitterness of soul, having never tasted prosperity.
Together they lie down in the dust, and worms cover them.
Behold, I know your thoughts and the schemes you devise against me.
For you say, “Where is the house of the nobleman, and where are the tents of the wicked?”
Have you not inquired of those who travel the road, and do you not recognize their signs?
For the wicked is spared for the day of calamity; he is led away to the day of wrath.
Who will declare his way to his face, and who will repay him for what he has done?
Yet he is carried to the grave, and a watch is kept over his tomb.
The clods of the valley are sweet to him; all humanity follows after him, and innumerable precede him.
How then can you comfort me with emptiness, when your answers leave nothing but falsehood?
Can a mortal man be of service to God? Surely the discerning man profits himself.
Is it any pleasure to the Almighty that you are righteous, or any gain to Him that you make your ways blameless?
Is it on account of your piety that He reproves you, and brings you into judgment? “
Is not your wickedness great, and is there no end to your iniquities?
For you have exacted sureties from your brothers without cause, and stripped the naked of their garments.
You have not given water to the faint to drink, and you have withheld bread from the famished.
The earth was the domain of the powerful, and the man of distinction dwelt in it.
You have sent widows away empty-handed, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken. “
Therefore snares encircle you, and sudden dread terrifies you;
or darkness, so that you cannot see, and a deluge of waters covers you. “
Is not God in the loftiness of heaven? Behold the summit of the stars, how exalted they are!
Yet you say, ‘What does God know? Can He judge through the dark cloud?’
Thick clouds are a hiding place for Him, so that He does not see; and He walks upon the vault of heaven.
Will you keep to the ancient way that wicked men have trodden—
those who were snatched away before their time, whose foundation was swept away like a river?
They said to God, ‘Depart from us,’ and, ‘What can the Almighty do to us?’
Yet He filled their houses with good; but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
The righteous see it and rejoice, and the innocent mock them.
Surely our adversaries are cut off, and fire consumes their remnant. “
Acquaint yourself with Him, and be at peace; thereby good shall come to you.
Receive instruction from His mouth, and lay up His words in your heart.
If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored; if you remove iniquity far from your tent,
and lay your gold in the dust, and the gold of Ophir among the stones of the brooks,
then the Almighty will be your gold, and you will have abundant silver.
For then you will delight yourself in the Almighty, and lift up your face to God.
You will pray to Him, and He will hear you; and you will pay your vows.
You will also decree a thing, and it will be established for you; and light will shine upon your ways.
When men are brought low, you will say, ‘There is exaltation’; and He will save the one with downcast eyes.
He will deliver even the guilty one; and he will be delivered by the purity of your hands.”
“Even today my complaint is bitter; my affliction outweighs my groaning.
If only I knew where to find Him, that I might come to His seat.
I would set my case in order before Him and fill my mouth with arguments.
I would know the words with which He would answer me, and discern what He would say to me.
Would He contend with me in His great power? No—He would pay heed to me.
There the upright could reason with Him, and I should be delivered forever from my Judge.
“If I go east, He is not there; if I go west, I cannot discern Him.
When He works in the north, I cannot behold Him; when He turns to the south, I cannot see Him.
Yet He knows the way I have taken; when He has tested me, I shall come forth as gold.
My feet have held fast to His steps; I have kept His way and have not turned aside.
I have not departed from the command of His lips; I have treasured the words of His mouth more than my daily bread.
“But He is unchangeable, and who can turn Him back? He does whatever His soul desires.
For He carries out what He has decreed for me, and He has many such designs.
Therefore I am dismayed in His presence; when I ponder this, I dread Him.
God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has terrified me.
For I am not silenced by the darkness, nor by the thick darkness that covers my face.”
Why does the Almighty not reserve times for judgment? Why do those who know Him not see His days?
Some displace boundary markers and pasture stolen flocks.
They drive off the orphan’s donkey and seize the widow’s ox as collateral.
They thrust the indigent from the road, and the afflicted of the land are forced into concealment.
Behold, like wild asses in the wilderness, they go forth to their labor, foraging for prey; the wasteland itself becomes sustenance for their children.
By night they reap in the field, and they glean the vineyard of the wicked.
Without raiment they lie down naked, having no covering against the cold.
Drenched by mountain torrents, they cling to the rock for want of shelter.
They tear the orphan from the breast and exact a pledge from the poor.
Naked and unclothed, they wander about; famished, they carry sheaves of grain.
They press oil within their enclosures and tread the winepresses, yet they thirst.
From the city the dying groan, and the souls of the wounded cry out, yet God charges no one with wrongdoing.
Then there are those who rebel against the light; they do not know its ways or stay on its paths.
At dawn the murderer rises; he slays the poor and needy, and by night he is like a thief.
The adulterer’s eye waits for twilight, saying, “No eye will see me,” and he conceals his face.
In darkness they break into houses; by day they seal themselves in; they never see the light.
For to them, deep darkness is morning; they are friends with the terrors of darkness.
They are but foam upon the surface of the water; their portion of the land is cursed, so that no one turns toward their vineyards.
As drought and heat consume the snow waters, so Sheol consumes those who have sinned.
The womb forgets them; worms feed sweetly upon them; they are no longer remembered, and wickedness is broken like a tree.
They prey upon the barren and childless, and show no kindness to the widow.
Yet God, by His power, sustains the mighty; they rise up, though they do not trust in their own life.
He grants them security, and they rest in it, but His eyes are upon their ways.
They are exalted for a moment, then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.
If this is not so, then who can prove me a liar and reduce my words to nothing?
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
“Dominion and dread attend Him; He establishes tranquility in His exalted realms.
His hosts are beyond numbering, and His light shines upon all
“How, then, can mortal man be justified before God? How can one born of woman attain purity?
Behold, even the moon lacks luster, and the stars are not spotless in His sight.
How much less, then, is man, who is but a maggot, and the son of man, who is but a worm!”
“How you have helped the powerless! How you have saved the arm that has no strength!
How you have counseled the unwise and abundantly declared sound wisdom!
To whom have you uttered words? Whose spirit has gone forth from you? “
The shades of the dead shudder beneath the waters, together with those who dwell therein.
Sheol lies bare before Him, and Abaddon is without any covering. “
He stretches the north over the void; He suspends the earth upon nothing.
He confines the waters within His clouds, yet the cloud is not rent asunder beneath them.
He veils the face of the full moon, spreading His cloud over it.
He has traced a circle upon the face of the waters, at the boundary between light and darkness.
The pillars of heaven quake and are astounded at His rebuke.
By His power He calmed the sea; by His understanding He shattered Rahab.
By His breath the skies are cleared; His hand has pierced the fleeing serpent. “
Indeed, these are but the outskirts of His ways; how faint a whisper of Him is heard! Who, then, can comprehend the thunder of His power?”
Job resumed his discourse and said: “
As God lives, who has deprived me of justice, and the Almighty, who has embittered my soul—
so long as breath still animates me, and the spirit of God remains in my nostrils—
my lips shall not articulate wickedness, nor shall my tongue promulgate deceit. “
Far be it from me to vindicate you; I shall not relinquish my integrity until I expire.
I cleave to my righteousness and will not let it go; throughout my days my conscience shall not reproach me. “
May my enemy be reckoned among the wicked, and my adversary among the unrighteous.
For what hope has the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his soul?
Will God heed his outcry when distress overtakes him?
Will he find delight in the Almighty? Will he invoke God continually? “
I shall instruct you concerning the hand of God; I shall not conceal what pertains to the Almighty.
Behold, you all have seen; why then do you utter such vanity? “
This is the portion allotted to the wicked by God, and the inheritance the ruthless receive from the Almighty:
if his sons proliferate, it is for the sword, and his offspring shall not be sated with bread.
His survivors shall be buried in death, and his widows shall not lament. “
Though he amass silver like dust and prepare garments like clay,
he may accumulate them, yet the righteous shall wear them, and the innocent shall apportion the silver.
He builds his house like a moth’s web, and like a shelter a watchman erects.
He lies down wealthy, yet he shall not be gathered; he opens his eyes, and he is gone. “
Terrors assail him like waters; a tempest snatches him away in the night.
The east wind bears him off, and he vanishes; it whirls him from his place.
It hurls itself upon him without pity; he seeks to escape its force.
It claps its hands at him and hisses at him from its own place.”
Indeed, silver possesses its source, and gold has its appointed place of refinement.
Iron is wrested from the dust, and copper is smelted from the rock.
He imposes an end upon darkness and probes to the utmost extremity every stone shrouded in gloom and the shadow of death.
He cuts a shaft far from human habitation, in regions forgotten by the foot; there men dangle and sway, far from their fellows.
Bread comes forth from the earth, yet beneath it the ground is upheaved as though by fire.
Its stones are the very seat of sapphires, and its dust contains gold.
No bird of prey knows that path, and no falcon's eye has beheld it.
The proud beasts have not trodden it, nor has the lion passed over it.
He lays his hand upon the flint and overturns mountains from their roots.
He hews channels through the rock, and his eye discerns every precious thing.
He dams the streams so that they do not trickle, and brings the hidden thing into the light.
Yet where shall wisdom be found, and where is the place of understanding?
Mortals do not know its worth, nor is it found in the land of the living.
The deep says, "It is not in me." And the sea says, "It is not with me."
It cannot be bought with gold, nor can silver be weighed out as its price.
It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, with precious onyx, or with sapphire.
Gold and glass cannot equal it, nor can it be exchanged for vessels of fine gold.
Coral and crystal are not to be mentioned; the price of wisdom exceeds that of pearls.
The topaz of Cush cannot be compared with it, nor can it be valued in pure gold.
Whence, then, comes wisdom, and where is the place of understanding?
It is concealed from the eyes of all the living and hidden from the birds of the heavens.
Abaddon and Death say, "We have heard a rumor of it with our ears."
God understands its way, and He knows its place.
For He looks to the ends of the earth and sees all that is beneath the heavens.
When He assigned weight to the wind and measured out the waters,
when He made a decree for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,
then He saw it and declared it; He established it and investigated it.
And He said to man, "Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding."
Job again took up his discourse and said,
“Would that I might be restored to the months of old, to the days when God kept watch over me,
when His lamp shone above my head and by His light I walked through darkness,
as in the days of my prime, when the intimate counsel of God rested upon my tent,
while the Almighty remained in my company and my children encircled me,
when my steps were bathed in cream and the rock poured out for me rivers of oil.
“When I proceeded to the city gate and established my seat in the square,
the young men perceived me and withdrew, while the elders rose and stood;
nobles restrained their speech and placed their hands over their mouths;
the voices of leaders were subdued, and their tongues adhered to their palates.
For the ear that heard me pronounced me blessed, and the eye that beheld me bore witness on my behalf.
“Because I rescued the afflicted in his outcry, and the orphan bereft of any helper;
the benediction of the perishing came upon me, and I caused the widow’s heart to exult.
I arrayed myself in righteousness, and it invested me; my justice was as a robe and a turban.
I served as eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.
I was a father to the indigent, and I investigated the plea of one unknown to me.
I shattered the jaws of the wicked and wrested the prey from between his teeth.
“Then I concluded, ‘I shall expire in my nest, and I shall multiply my days like the sand,’
my roots extending to the waters, while the dew lodged upon my branches throughout the night.
My glory was renewed within me, and my bow was perpetually renewed in my hand.
Men hearkened unto me and waited expectantly, and they fell silent for my counsel.
After my words, they spoke no further, and my discourse distilled upon them.
They awaited me as for rain, and opened their mouths as for the latter rain.
I smiled upon them, yet they could scarcely credit it, and they did not suffer the radiance of my countenance to be cast down.
I selected their path and sat at their head; I dwelt as a king amid his troops, like one who consoles mourners.”
Yet now they deride me—young men whose days are fewer than mine, and whose fathers I should have scorned to rank even with the dogs that guarded my flock.
Of what avail to me was the strength of their hands, seeing that their vigor had already decayed?
Gaunt with deprivation and famine, they gnawed the parched earth in a desolate and ruinous wasteland;
they gathered mallow from the scrub and made the roots of the broom shrub their sustenance.
They were expelled from human society, and men shouted after them as though pursuing a thief.
They took refuge in the clefts of ravines, in subterranean cavities and among the rocks;
they brayed among the scrub and huddled together beneath the nettles.
A brood of fools and of men without name, they were driven from the land.
And now I have become their taunt; I am a byword among them.
They hold me in abomination and keep aloof; they do not scruple to spit in my face.
Because He has unstrung my bow and afflicted me, they have cast off restraint in my presence.
On my right the rabble rise up; they thrust aside my feet and cast up against me their paths of destruction.
They destroy my path; they further my ruin, and they need no accomplice.
They advance as through a wide breach; amid the ruin they surge forward.
Terrors are turned upon me; my dignity is driven away like the wind; my deliverance has vanished like a cloud.
And now my life is poured out within me; days of affliction have seized me.
Night pierces my bones, and my gnawing pains know no rest.
By His great power He seizes my garment; He chokes me with the collar of my tunic.
He has cast me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.
I cry out to You, but You do not answer; I stand, and You merely look at me.
You have turned cruel toward me; with the might of Your hand You persecute me.
You lift me to the wind and drive me before it; You dissolve me in the storm.
For I know that You will bring me to death, to the house appointed for all the living.
Yet would He not stretch out His hand against a heap of ruins, when one cries for help in his destruction?
Did I not weep for those in trouble? Was I not grieved for the needy?
Yet when I hoped for good, evil came; when I looked for light, darkness fell.
My insides churn and find no rest; days of affliction confront me.
I go about darkened, though not by the sun; I rise in the assembly and cry for help.
I have become a brother to jackals and a companion to ostriches.
My skin grows black and peels; my bones burn with fever.
My lyre is tuned to mourning, and my pipe to the sound of weeping.
I have entered into a covenant with my eyes; wherefore should I fix my gaze upon a maiden?
What allotment does God possess from above, or what heritage does the Almighty hold from the heights?
Is not calamity the portion of the unrighteous, and disaster the lot of workers of iniquity?
Does He not observe my ways and enumerate all my steps?
If I have walked in falsehood, and my foot has hastened unto deceit,
let Him weigh me in the scales of justice, and let God acknowledge my integrity.
If my step has deviated from the path, and my heart has followed my eyes, and if any stain has adhered to my hands,
then let another consume what I have sown, and let my descendants be rooted out.
If my heart has been seduced by a woman, or if I have lain in ambush at my neighbor’s doorway,
then let my wife grind for another, and let strangers bow down upon her.
For that would constitute a heinous crime, an iniquity adjudicable by judges.
For it is a fire consuming unto Abaddon, and it would extirpate all my increase.
If I have spurned the cause of my male or female servant when they contended with me,
what then shall I do when God arises? When He scrutinizes, what answer shall I return to Him?
Did not He who fashioned me in the womb fashion him? And did not One form us in the womb?
If I have withheld from the poor their desire, or caused the widow’s eyes to fail,
or eaten my morsel alone while the orphan did not partake of it—
for from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, and from my mother’s womb I have guided her—
if I have seen anyone perishing without raiment, or the needy without covering,
if his loins have not blessed me, and if he was not warmed by the fleece of my sheep;
if I have lifted my hand against the fatherless because I perceived my succor in the gate,
then let my shoulder blade fall from my shoulder, and let my arm be broken from its socket.
For calamity from God was a dread to me, and because of His majesty I could not endure.
If I have made gold my confidence, or said to fine gold, “You are my trust”;
if I have rejoiced because my wealth was abundant, and because my hand had acquired much;
if I have beheld the sun when it shone, or the moon progressing in splendor,
and my heart has been secretly enticed, and my mouth has kissed my hand,
this too would be an iniquity for judges, for I would have denied God above.
If I have rejoiced at the destruction of my enemy, or exulted when evil overtook him—
I have not even permitted my mouth to sin by requesting his life under a curse—
if the men of my tent have not said, “Who has not been satisfied with his meat?”—
the stranger did not lodge outside; I opened my doors to the wayfarer—
if I have concealed my transgressions like Adam, hiding my iniquity in my bosom,
because I stood in great fear of the multitude, and the contempt of families terrified me, so that I remained silent and did not go out of the door—
Oh, that I had One to hear me! Here is my signature; let the Almighty answer me; and let my accuser compose an indictment.
Surely I would bear it upon my shoulder; I would bind it upon me like a crown.
I would recount to Him the number of my steps; like a prince I would draw near to Him.
If my land cries out against me, and its furrows weep in unison;
if I have consumed its produce without remuneration, and caused the life of its possessors to expire,
let thorns spring up instead of wheat, and weeds instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.
When these three men desisted from answering Job, because he was righteous in his own estimation.
Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the clan of Ram, became incandescent with rage; his wrath blazed against Job because he vindicated himself rather than God.
His anger also burned against his three friends, because they had found no answer, yet had condemned Job.
Now Elihu had waited to address Job, because they were older than he in days.
Yet when Elihu saw that these three men had no answer in their mouths, his anger burned again.
“I am young in days, and you are aged; therefore I held back and was afraid to declare my knowledge to you.
I said, ‘Days should speak, and a multitude of years should teach wisdom.’
But truly it is spirit in man, and the breath of the Almighty gives them understanding.
It is not the many who are wise, nor do elders understand justice.
Therefore I say: Hear me; I too will declare my knowledge.
“Behold, I waited for your words; I listened to your reasonings while you searched for words.
I paid close attention to you, and behold, none of you convicted Job; none of you answered his words.
Lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom; God, not man, will thrust him down.’
He has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your words.
“They are dismayed; they answer no more, for words have departed from them.
I have waited, because they do not speak, because they stand still and answer no more.
I too will answer my part; I too will declare my knowledge.
For I am full of words; the spirit within my belly constrains me.
Behold, my belly is like wine without a vent; like new wineskins, it is ready to burst.
I will speak, that I may be relieved; I will open my lips and answer.
I will not show partiality to any man, nor flatter any person.
For I do not know how to flatter; my Maker would soon take me away.”
But now, Job, please hear my words; listen to all my speech.
Behold, I have now opened my mouth, and my tongue speaks.
My words declare the uprightness of my heart, and my lips utter knowledge sincerely.
The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
If you can, answer me; take your stand before me; stand up.
Behold, I am, like you, a mortal before God; I too was formed from clay.
Behold, my terror shall not make you afraid, nor shall my hand be heavy upon you.
Surely you have spoken in my hearing, and I have heard the voice of your words:
“I am pure, without transgression; I am innocent, and there is no iniquity in me.
Behold, He finds pretexts against me; He counts me as His enemy.
He puts my feet in the stocks; He watches all my paths.”
Behold, in this you are not right; I will answer you, for God is greater than man.
Why do you contend against Him? For He need not answer for any of His words.
For God speaks once, and again, yet man does not perceive it.
In a dream, a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls upon men, in slumberings upon the bed,
then He opens the ears of men and seals His instruction upon them through their chastening,
to turn man from his deed and to hide pride from man.
He keeps back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.
He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and with unceasing contention in his bones,
so that his life loathes bread, and his soul dainty food.
His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; and his bones, which were not seen, stick out.
Yea, his soul draws near to the pit, and his life to the destroyers.
If there be with him an angel, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to declare to man what is right for him,
then He is gracious to him and says, “Deliver him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom.”
His flesh shall be fresher than a child’s; he shall return to the days of his youth.
He shall pray to God, and He will be favorable to him; and he shall see His face with joy, and He will render to man his righteousness.
He looks upon men, and if any say, “I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it availed me nothing,”
He will redeem his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light.
Behold, all these things God works twice, three times with a man,
to bring back his soul from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of life.
Pay attention, O Job, listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
If you have anything to say, answer me; speak, for I desire to justify you.
If not, listen to me; be silent, and I shall teach you wisdom.
Then Elihu resumed his discourse and said:
“Hear my words, you who are wise; attend to me, you who possess learning.
For the ear assays words even as the palate savors food.
Let us choose justice for ourselves and discern among ourselves what is good.
For Job has declared, ‘I am righteous, yet the LORD has deprived me of justice.
Should I lie concerning my right? My wound is incurable, though I am without transgression.’
What mortal is like Job, who drinks in derision as though it were water?
He keeps company with evildoers and walks in the way of the wicked.
For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight in God.’
“Therefore listen to me, you men of understanding: far be it from the LORD to do evil, and from the Almighty to do wrong.
For according to a man’s deeds He repays him, and according to his ways He lets it find him.
Indeed, the LORD does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert justice.
Who gave Him charge over the earth? Who appointed Him over the whole world?
If He were to set His heart upon it and gather to Himself His Spirit and breath,
all flesh would perish together, and man would return to dust.
If you have understanding, hear this; give ear to the sound of my words.
Can one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the just and mighty One?
Is it fitting to say to a king, ‘Worthless one!’ or to nobles, ‘Wicked men!’?
Yet He is not partial to princes, nor does He regard the rich more than the poor, for they are all the work of His hands.
In a moment they die, even at midnight; the people are shaken and pass away, and the mighty are removed without a hand.
“For His eyes are upon the ways of a man, and He sees all his steps.
There is no darkness nor shadow of death where the workers of iniquity may hide.
For He need not examine a man further, that he should go before the LORD in judgment.
He breaks the mighty without inquiry and sets others in their place.
Therefore He knows their deeds, and He overthrows them in the night, and they are crushed.
He strikes them as wicked men in the sight of others,
because they turned aside from following Him and had no regard for any of His ways,
so that they caused the cry of the poor to reach Him, and He heard the cry of the afflicted.
When He gives quietness, who then can condemn? And when He hides His face, who then can see Him? Whether a nation or a man alone,
He prevents the godless man from reigning, so that the people are not ensnared.
“Suppose someone says to the LORD, ‘I have endured chastening; I will offend no more.
Teach me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again.’
Should He repay you on your terms when you refuse to repent? You must decide, not I; so tell me what you know.
Men of understanding will say to me—indeed, a wise man who hears me—
‘Job speaks without knowledge; his words lack insight.’
If only Job were tried to the utmost, for his answers are those of wicked men.
For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against the LORD.”
“Do you reckon this to be just? You have declared, ‘My righteousness exceeds God’s.’
For you say, ‘What profit is there for me? What do I gain by not sinning?’
I shall answer you in words, and your friends along with you. “
Look up to the heavens and see; gaze upon the clouds, for they are higher than you.
If you sin, what do you accomplish against Him? If your transgressions abound, what do you do to Him?
If you are righteous, what do you give Him, or what does He receive from your hand?
Your wickedness affects only a fellow mortal like yourself, and your righteousness only a human being. “
Because of abundant oppression they cry out; they plead for relief from the arm of the mighty.
Yet no one says, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the air?’
There they cry out, but He does not answer, because of the pride of evil men.
Surely God does not listen to empty pleas, and the Almighty does not regard them.
How much less, then, when you say that you do not see Him, though your case is before Him and you must wait for Him. “
And now, because His anger does not punish and He does not take much notice of transgression,
Job opens his mouth in vain and multiplies words without knowledge.”
Elihu resumed his discourse and declared:
“Grant me a brief forbearance, and I shall disclose to you what remains to be said on God's behalf.
I shall fetch my understanding from afar and ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
For, in truth, my words are not mendacious; one consummate in knowledge stands with you.
“Behold, God is mighty, yet He does not despise anyone; He is mighty in the sagacity of His understanding.
He does not preserve the wicked in life, but accords justice to the afflicted.
He does not avert His eyes from the righteous; He enthrones them with kings and exalts them in perpetuity.
“If, moreover, they are bound in fetters and ensnared by cords of affliction,
then He discloses to them their deeds and their transgressions, inasmuch as they have acted with overweening pride.
He uncovers their ears to instruction and enjoins them to turn back from iniquity.
If they heed and serve Him, they shall consummate their days in prosperity and their years in delights.
But if they do not heed, they shall perish by the sword and expire without understanding.
“The godless in heart treasure up wrath; they do not cry out when He binds them.
They perish in their youth, and their life ends among the male shrine prostitutes.
Yet He delivers the afflicted through their affliction and uncovers their ears in oppression.
“Indeed, He drew you from the maw of distress into a spacious place devoid of constraint, with your table laden with rich fare.
Yet you are replete with the judgment due the wicked; judgment and justice have seized you.
Let not wrath entice you into scoffing, nor let the magnitude of the ransom turn you aside.
Will your cry for help avail you, or all your mighty endeavors?
Do not yearn for the night, when peoples are cut off in their place.
Beware; do not turn toward iniquity, for you have chosen this rather than affliction.
“Behold, God is exalted in His power; who is an instructor like Him?
Who has prescribed His way for Him, or who can say, ‘You have done wrong’?
Remember to magnify His work, which men have lauded,
that all humanity has beheld; man regards it from afar.
Behold, God is great, beyond our ken; the number of His years is unsearchable.
“For He draws up the drops of water; they distill as rain from His mist,
which the clouds pour down and shower abundantly upon mankind.
Can anyone comprehend the spreading of the clouds, the thunderings of His pavilion?
Behold, He spreads His lightning over it and covers the roots of the sea.
For by these He judges the peoples and gives food in abundance.
He fills His hands with lightning and commands it to strike its mark.
His thunder announces His presence; even the cattle regard the approaching storm.”
At this my heart likewise trembles and leaps from its place.
Listen attentively to the thunder of His voice and to the rumbling that issues from His mouth.
He sends it forth beneath the whole heaven, and His lightning to the very ends of the earth.
Afterward a voice roars; He thunders with the majesty of His voice, and He does not restrain the lightning when His voice is heard.
God thunders marvelously with His voice; He does great things that we do not know. "
For He commands the snow, 'Fall upon the earth,' and the rain shower, 'Be a mighty downpour.'
He seals the hand of every person, so that all mankind may recognize His work.
Then the beasts retreat into their lairs and remain in their dens.
From its chamber comes the tempest, and cold from the scattering winds.
By the breath of God ice is formed, and the broad waters are frozen. "
He also burdens the thick cloud with moisture and scatters His lightning through the clouds.
And it turns about at His direction, that they may do whatever He commands them upon the face of the inhabited earth.
Whether for correction, for His land, or for mercy, He brings it to pass. "
Hear this, O Job; stand still and consider the wondrous works of God.
Do you know how God ordains them, and causes the light of His cloud to shine?
Do you know the balancing of the clouds, the wondrous works of Him who is perfect in knowledge?
Your garments grow warm when the earth is stilled by the south wind. "
Can you, with Him, spread out the skies, strong as a cast metal mirror?
Teach us what we should say to Him; we cannot arrange our case because of darkness.
Shall it be reported to Him that I would speak? If a man speaks, surely he will be swallowed up. "
And now they do not see the light, though it is bright in the skies; but the wind passes and clears them.
From the north comes golden splendor; God is clothed with awesome majesty.
The Almighty is beyond our reach; He is exalted in power; and in justice and abundant righteousness He does not oppress.
Therefore men fear Him; He does not regard any who are wise of heart."
Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said: “
Who is this who darkens counsel with words devoid of knowledge?
Now brace your loins like a man; I will interrogate you, and you shall instruct Me. “
Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you possess understanding.
Who fixed its dimensions—surely you know!—or who stretched the measuring line across it?
Upon what were its pillars sunk, or who laid its cornerstone,
when the morning stars sang in concert and all the sons of God shouted for joy? “
Or who enclosed the sea behind doors when it burst forth from the womb,
when I made the cloud its garment and thick darkness its swaddling band,
and prescribed My boundary for it, and set bars and doors,
and said, ‘Thus far shall you come, and no farther, and here shall your proud waves be stayed’? “
Have you ever commanded the morning since your days began, and caused the dawn to know its place,
that it might seize the skirts of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
It is transformed like clay under a seal, and its features stand forth like a garment.
From the wicked their light is withheld, and the uplifted arm is broken. “
Have you entered the springs of the sea, or walked the recesses of the deep?
Have the gates of death been revealed to you, or have you seen the gates of deep darkness?
Have you comprehended the breadth of the earth? Declare, if you know it all. “
Where is the way to the dwelling of light, and where is the place of darkness,
that you may take it to its territory and discern the paths to its home?
You know, of course, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great! “
Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, or have you seen the storehouses of the hail,
which I have reserved for the time of trouble, for the day of battle and war?
What is the way to the place where the light is distributed, or where the east wind is scattered over the earth? “
Who has cleft a channel for the torrents, or a path for the thunderbolt,
to rain upon a land devoid of man, upon a wilderness where no human dwells,
to satisfy the desolate waste and make the ground sprout with grass?
Has the rain a father, or who has begotten the drops of dew? “
From whose womb did the ice come forth, and who has given birth to the frost of heaven?
The waters become hard like stone, and the face of the deep is frozen. “
Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades, or loose the cords of Orion?
Can you bring forth the Mazzaroth in their season, or guide the Bear with its children?
Do you know the ordinances of the heavens? Can you establish their dominion over the earth? “
Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, that a flood of waters may cover you?
Can you send forth lightnings, that they may go and say to you, ‘Here we are’? “
Who has put wisdom in the inward parts, or given understanding to the mind?
