Our God comes and does not keep silence; a devouring fire goes before Him, and a fierce tempest encircles Him.
He summons the heavens above and the earth, to judge His people.
“Gather to Me My faithful ones, who have solemnized My covenant by sacrifice.”
The heavens declare His righteousness, for God Himself is Judge. Selah.
“Hear, O My people, and I will speak; O Israel, I will testify against you: I am God, your God.
I do not rebuke you for your sacrifices, nor for your burnt offerings, which are ever before Me.
I will take no bull from your house, nor goats from your folds.
For every beast of the forest is Mine, and the cattle upon a thousand hills.
I know every bird of the mountains, and the creatures of the field are Mine.
If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is Mine, and all its fullness.
Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and pay your vows to the Most High.
Call upon Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you shall honor Me.”
But to the wicked God says, “What right have you to recite My statutes, or to take My covenant upon your lips?
For you hate discipline and cast My words behind you.
When you see a thief, you make common cause with him, and your portion is with adulterers.
You have unleashed your mouth for evil, and your tongue frames deceit.
You sit and speak against your brother; you slander your mother’s son.
These things you have done, and I kept silent; you thought that I was altogether like you. But now I rebuke you and set the case before your eyes.”
“Consider this, you who forget God, lest I tear you to pieces, with no one to deliver.
He who offers a sacrifice of thanksgiving honors Me, and to him who orders his way aright I will show the salvation of God.”
Be gracious to me, O God, according to Your steadfast love; according to the plenitude of Your compassions, efface my transgressions.
Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity, and purify me from my sin.
For I acknowledge my transgressions, and my sin remains perpetually before me.
Against You—You alone—have I sinned, and I have wrought that which is evil in Your sight, so that You may be vindicated in Your utterance and acquitted in Your judgment.
Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity, and in sin did my mother conceive me.
Behold, You delight in truth in the inward parts, and in the hidden place You cause me to know wisdom.
Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean; wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.
Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones that You have crushed rejoice.
Hide Your face from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities.
Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me.
Do not cast me away from Your presence, and do not take Your Holy Spirit from me.
Restore to me the joy of Your salvation, and uphold me with a willing spirit.
Then I will teach transgressors Your ways, and sinners shall return to You.
Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, the God of my salvation, and my tongue shall sing aloud of Your righteousness.
O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth shall declare Your praise.
For You do not delight in sacrifice, else would I bring it; You take no pleasure in burnt offerings.
The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.
In Your favor do good to Zion; build the walls of Jerusalem.
Then will You delight in righteous sacrifices, in burnt offerings and whole burnt offerings; then bulls will be offered upon Your altar.

For the choirmaster: a didactic psalm of David, occasioned by Doeg the Edomite’s arrival before Saul, wherein he reported, “David has come to the house of Ahimelech.” Why do you exult in wickedness, O mighty man? The steadfast love of God endures throughout the day.
Your tongue contrives devastation, sharpened like a razor, you architect of treachery.
You cleave to evil in preference to good, and to falsehood in preference to righteous discourse. Selah.
You delight in every devouring utterance, O tongue of guile.
Yet God will demolish you forever; He will seize you and rend you from your tent; He will extirpate you from the land of the living. Selah.
The righteous shall behold and be seized with reverent dread, and they shall mock him:
“Behold the man who did not make God his stronghold, but reposed his confidence in the abundance of his riches and fortified himself in his iniquity.”
As for me, I am like a verdant olive tree in the house of God; I have reposed my trust in the steadfast love of God forever and ever.
I will give You thanks in perpetuity, because You have brought it to pass; I will wait upon Your name, for it is good, in the presence of Your saints.
The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They have become corrupt, and they commit abominable iniquity; there is no one who does good.
God gazes down from heaven upon the children of men, to discern whether any are wise, any who seek God.
All have turned aside; together they have become depraved; there is none who does good, not even one.
Do the workers of iniquity possess no understanding, they who devour my people as readily as bread and do not call upon God?
There they were overwhelmed with dread, though no dread had been; for God has scattered the bones of your besiegers; you have put them to shame, for God has rejected them.
Oh, that salvation for Israel would come out of Zion! When God restores the fortunes of His people, Jacob shall rejoice and Israel shall be glad.

For the choirmaster, with stringed instruments—a Maskil of David—composed when the Ziphites approached Saul and declared, “Is David not concealed among us?” Deliver me, O God, by Your name, and vindicate me by Your might.
Hear my prayer, O God; attend to the utterances of my mouth.
For strangers have risen against me, and ruthless men seek my life, inasmuch as they have no regard for God. Selah.
Behold, God is my helper; the Lord is the sustainer of my soul.
He will repay my enemies with evil; in Your faithfulness, bring them to ruin.
I will freely sacrifice to You; I will praise Your name, O the LORD, for it is good.
For He has delivered me from every distress, and my eyes have looked in triumph upon my foes.
Hearken to my prayer, O God, and do not conceal Yourself from my supplication.
Give heed to me and answer me; I am distraught in my meditation and I groan.
Because of the voice of the enemy, because of the oppression of the wicked—for they cast iniquity upon me and in anger they bear a grudge against me.
My heart is in anguish within me, and the terrors of death have fallen upon me.
Fear and trembling come upon me, and horror has overwhelmed me.
And I said, "If only I had wings like a dove! I would fly away and find rest.
Behold, I would wander far away; I would lodge in the wilderness. Selah.
I would hasten to my refuge from the rushing wind and the storm."
O Lord, confound their speech, for I see violence and strife in the city.
Day and night they surround it upon its walls, and iniquity and toil are within it.
Destruction is in its midst; oppression and deceit do not depart from its streets.
For it is not an enemy who taunts me—then I could endure it; nor is it one who hates me who has risen up against me—then I could hide from him.
But it is you, a man my equal, my companion, my familiar friend—
we who shared sweet counsel together and walked in the house of God among the throng.
Let death seize them by surprise; let them go down alive to Sheol, for evil is in their midst, in their dwellings.
As for me, I call upon God, and the LORD delivers me.
Evening, morning, and noon I lament and moan, and He hears my voice.
He redeems my soul in peace from the battle waged against me, for many are arrayed against me.
God will hear and answer them—He who sits enthroned from of old—Selah—because they do not change and do not fear God.
He has stretched out his hands against his allies; he has profaned his covenant.
His speech was flattery itself, smoother than butter, yet war lurked in his heart; his words were softer than oil, but they were unsheathed blades.
Cast your burden upon the LORD, and He will sustain you; He will never permit the righteous to be shaken.
But You, O God, will bring them down to the pit of destruction; bloodthirsty and deceitful men will not live out half their days. But I will trust in You.

For the choirmaster, to the melody “The Dove on Distant Terebinths,” a Miktam of David, composed when the Philistines seized him in Gath. Be gracious to me, O God, for mortals trample me; all day long they assail and crush me.
My adversaries pursue me without respite; indeed, many in their arrogance contend against me.
On the day I am afraid, I will put my trust in You.
In God—whose word I extol—in God I have trusted; I shall not fear. What can mere flesh accomplish against me?
All day long they distort my words; every one of their schemes is bent upon my ruin.
They conspire, they lurk, they watch my steps, while they wait to take my life.
Shall they escape despite their iniquity? In Your wrath, O God, cast down the peoples.
You have reckoned my wanderings; place my tears in Your flask. Are they not recorded in Your ledger?
Then my foes will turn back on the day I call. This I know: God is on my side.
In God, whose word I praise, in the LORD, whose word I praise,
in God I have trusted; I will not be afraid. What can a human being do to me?
Your vows are upon me, O God; I will render thank offerings to You.
For You have delivered my soul from death, and my feet from stumbling, that I may walk before God in the light of life.
Be gracious to me, O God, be gracious to me, for in You my soul takes refuge; in the shadow of Your wings I shall seek shelter until the calamities pass by.
I shall call upon God Most High, unto God who fulfills His purpose for me.
He shall send from heaven and rescue me; He shall put to shame the one who tramples upon me. Selah. God shall send forth His lovingkindness and His truth.
My soul is in the midst of lions; I lie down among ravenous beasts—men whose teeth are spears and arrows, and whose tongues are sharp swords.
Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; let Your glory be over all the earth.
They have spread a net for my steps; my soul is bowed down. They have dug a pit before me, yet they themselves have fallen into it. Selah.
My heart is steadfast, O God; my heart is steadfast. I will sing and make melody.
Awake, my glory; awake, O harp and lyre! I shall rouse the dawn.
I will give thanks unto You, O Lord, among the peoples; I will sing praises unto You among the nations.
For Your steadfast love is great even unto the heavens, and Your faithfulness reaches unto the clouds.
Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; let Your glory be over all the earth.
Do you indeed speak righteousness, O mighty ones? Do you judge with equity, O sons of men?
No, in your hearts you devise injustice; your hands mete out violence upon the earth.
The wicked are estranged from the womb; they go astray from birth, speaking lies.
Their venom is like the venom of a snake, like a cobra that shuts its ears,
that it cannot hear the voice of the charmers who skillfully weave spells.
O God, shatter their teeth in their mouths; O the LORD, tear out the fangs of the lions.
May they vanish like water that runs off; when they draw the bow, may their arrows be blunted.
Like a snail that dissolves in its slime, like a stillborn child, may they never see the sun.
Before your pots can feel the heat of the thorns—whether green or dry—He will sweep them away.
The righteous will rejoice when they see vengeance; they will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.
Then men will say, “Surely there is a reward for the righteous; surely there is a God who judges in the earth.”
Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; lift me beyond the reach of those who rise against me.
Deliver me from evildoers and save me from bloodthirsty men.
For behold, they lie in wait for my life; fierce men conspire against me—not for any transgression or sin of mine, O LORD.
Though I am innocent, they rush to array themselves against me; rouse Yourself to meet me, and see.
You, O LORD God of Hosts, God of Israel, rouse Yourself to punish all the nations; show no mercy to any who treacherously practice iniquity. Selah.
They return at evening; they howl like dogs and prowl around the city.
See how they pour forth cutting words from their mouths; their lips are like drawn swords, for they say, “Who will hear?”
But You, O LORD, laugh at them; You hold all the nations in derision.
O my Strength, I will keep watch for You, for God is my fortress.
My God of loving devotion will go before me; God will let me gaze in triumph upon my enemies.
Do not kill them, lest my people forget; scatter them by Your power and bring them down, O Lord, our shield.
For the sin of their mouths and the words of their lips, let them be ensnared in their pride, on account of the cursing and lies they utter.
Consume them in wrath; consume them until they are no more, that the ends of the earth may know that God rules over Jacob. Selah.
They return at evening; they howl like dogs and prowl around the city.
They roam in search of food and growl if they remain unsatisfied.
But I will sing of Your strength and proclaim Your loving devotion in the morning, for You have been my fortress and my refuge in the day of my distress.
O my Strength, I will sing praises to You, for God is my fortress, my God of loving devotion.

For the choirmaster, to the melody “Lily of the Testimony”; a Miktam of David for instruction—when he fought Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and struck down twelve thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt. You have rejected us, O God; You have breached our defenses; You have been angry; restore us!
You have made the earth quake and split it asunder; heal its fissures, for it is tottering.
You have shown Your people harsh affliction; You have made us drink a wine that makes us reel.
You have raised a standard for those who revere You, to be unfurled in the cause of truth. Selah.
Answer us! Save with Your right hand, that Your beloved may be delivered.
God has spoken in His sanctuary: “I will exult; I will apportion Shechem and measure off the Valley of Succoth.
Gilead is Mine, Manasseh is Mine; Ephraim is My helmet, and Judah is My scepter.
Moab is My washbasin; upon Edom I fling My sandal; over Philistia I raise a shout of triumph.”
Who will conduct me to the fortified city? Who will guide me into Edom?
Have You not, O God, cast us off? And will You not go forth with our armies?
Grant us succor against the adversary, for human deliverance is futile.
In God we shall act with valor, and He will trample down our adversaries.
Hear my cry, O God; attend to my prayer.
From the farthest reaches of the earth I call to You when my heart is overwhelmed; lead me to the rock that rises above me.
For You have been my refuge, a fortified tower against the foe.
I shall dwell in Your tent forevermore; I shall take refuge beneath the shelter of Your wings. Selah.
For You, O God, have heard my vows; You have granted me the inheritance of those who fear Your name.
You shall add days to the king; his years shall extend through generation upon generation.
He shall sit in the presence of God forever; steadfast love and truth shall preserve him.
So I will sing praise to Your name forever, that I may discharge my vows day by day.
My soul waits in silence for God alone; from Him comes my salvation.
He alone is my Rock and my salvation, my stronghold; I shall not be greatly shaken.
How long will all of you assail a single man, intent on murdering him—like a wall that bulges outward or a fence that totters toward collapse?
They conspire only to thrust him down from his exalted station; they take delight in falsehood, blessing with their mouths while cursing in their hearts. Selah.
Rest in God alone, O my soul, for my hope is from Him.
He alone is my Rock and my salvation, my stronghold; I shall not be shaken.
My salvation and my honor rest upon God; my mighty Rock, my refuge, is in God.
Trust in Him at all times, O people; pour out your hearts before Him. God is our refuge. Selah.
Mere mortals are but a breath; even the highborn are a deception; placed upon the scales, they rise together, lighter than a mere vapor.
Do not trust in oppression, nor set vain hope upon plunder; though your riches increase, do not fix your heart upon them.
Once God has spoken—twice I have heard it—that power belongs to God,
and that steadfast love belongs to You, O Lord; for You repay each person according to his deeds.
O God, You are my God; I seek You with ardent devotion. My soul thirsts for You; my flesh languishes for You in a parched and exhausted land, devoid of water.
I have beheld You in the sanctuary, to gaze upon Your power and Your glory.
Because Your steadfast love is better than life itself, my lips will extol You.
Thus I will bless You throughout my days; in Your name I will lift up my hands.
My soul shall be sated as with the richest fare; my mouth will praise You with exultant lips.
When I remember You upon my bed, I meditate upon You through the watches of the night.
For You have been my help; and in the protective shadow of Your wings I will sing for joy.
My soul clings to You; Your right hand sustains me.
But those who seek my life in order to destroy it will descend into the lowest regions of the earth.
They will be delivered to the sword; they will become carrion for jackals.
Yet the king will rejoice in God; everyone who swears by Him will exult, for the mouths of those who speak falsehood will be stopped.
Hear my voice, O God, in my lamentation; preserve my life from the terror of the enemy.
Conceal me from the clandestine counsel of evildoers, from the tumult of those who practice iniquity,
who whet their tongues like swords and aim bitter words as arrows,
to shoot in secret at the blameless; suddenly they discharge them, and they do not fear.
They fortify one another in an evil purpose; they recount their scheme to hide snares, saying, “Who will see us?”
They search out iniquities and complete a diligent investigation, probing the inner thought and the deep heart of man.
But God will shoot at them with an arrow; suddenly they will be stricken.
Their own tongues will cause them to stumble; all who behold them will shake their heads in derision.
Then all mankind will fear and proclaim the work of God, and they will discern His deed.
The righteous will rejoice in the LORD and take refuge in Him; all the upright in heart will glory.
For the choirmaster—a psalm of David, a song. Praise is Your due in Zion, O God, and to You vows will be discharged.
O You who hear prayer, unto You all humanity shall come.
When iniquities prevail against me, You make atonement for them.
How blessed is the one You choose and bring near, that he may dwell in Your courts! We shall be sated with the beneficence of Your house, Your holy temple.
By awe-inspiring acts of righteousness You answer us, O God of our salvation, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of the farthest seas.
You establish the mountains by Your strength, being girded with might.
You quell the roaring of the seas, the roaring of their waves, and the tumult of the peoples.
Thus those who dwell at the ends of the earth stand in awe of Your signs; You make the dawn and the sunset shout for joy.
You attend to the earth and saturate it; You enrich it immeasurably; the river of God is brimful of water; You prepare their grain, for thus You prepare the earth.
You drench its furrows; You level its ridges; You soften it with gentle rains; You bless its burgeoning.
You crown the year with Your bounty, and Your paths overflow with abundance.
The wilderness pastures drip with plenty, and the hills gird themselves with rejoicing.
The meadows are clothed with flocks, and the valleys are mantled with grain; they shout for joy, they also sing.
Raise a jubilant shout to God, all the earth;
extol the splendor of His name; accord to Him glory befitting His majesty.
Declare to God, “How awe-inspiring are Your deeds! So great is Your power that Your adversaries cringe before You.”
All the earth bows in worship to You and makes music to You; they sing praise to Your name. Selah
Come and behold the works of God: He is awe-inspiring in His dealings with humankind.
He transformed the sea into dry ground; they crossed the river on foot. There we exulted in Him.
He governs the ages by His might; His eyes scrutinize the nations—let the rebellious not exalt themselves. Selah
Bless our God, O peoples, and make the voice of His praise resound,
for He has preserved our life and has not permitted our feet to slip.
For You, O God, have put us to the proof; You have refined us as silver is refined.
You led us into the snare; You imposed a crushing weight upon our loins.
You allowed men to ride over our heads; we traversed fire and water, yet You brought us forth into abundance.
I shall enter Your house with burnt offerings; I shall fulfill my vows to You,
the utterances my lips pronounced and my mouth spoke in my distress.
I shall offer You burnt offerings of fattened beasts, together with the smoke of rams; I shall sacrifice bulls and goats. Selah
Come and listen, all you who fear God, and I will recount what He has accomplished for my soul.
I cried to Him with my mouth, and exalted praise was upon my tongue.
Had I cherished iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
Yet God has indeed listened; He has given heed to the voice of my prayer.
Blessed be God, for He has not spurned my prayer nor withdrawn His steadfast love from me!
God be gracious to us and bless us; may His face shine upon us. Selah.
That Your way may be known on earth, Your salvation among all nations.
Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You.
Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for You judge the peoples with equity and guide the nations on earth. Selah.
Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You.
The earth has yielded its harvest; God, our God, will bless us.
God bless us, and let all the ends of the earth fear Him.
God shall arise, His enemies shall be scattered, and those who hate Him shall flee before Him.
As smoke is driven away, so You shall drive them away; as wax melts before the fire, so the wicked shall perish before God.
But the righteous shall be glad; they shall exult before God and be jubilant with joy.
Sing to God, sing praises to His name; lift up a song to Him who rides through the deserts; His name is the LORD; exult before Him.
Father of the fatherless and Judge of widows is God in His holy habitation.
God settles the solitary in a home; He leads out the prisoners into prosperity, but the rebellious dwell in a parched land.
O God, when You went out before Your people, when You marched through the wilderness—Selah.
The earth quaked, the heavens poured down rain, before God, the God of Sinai, before God, the God of Israel.
Rain in abundance, O God, You shed abroad; You restored Your inheritance as it languished.
Your flock found a dwelling in it; in Your goodness, O God, You provided for the needy.
The Lord gives the word; the women who announce the news are a great host.
The kings of the armies—they flee, they flee! The women at home divide the spoil.
Though you lie down among the sheepfolds, you are like the wings of a dove covered with silver, its pinions with shimmering gold.
When the Almighty scatters kings there, snow falls on Zalmon.
O mountain of God, mountain of Bashan; O many-peaked mountain, mountain of Bashan!
Why do you look with hatred, O peaked mountains, at the mount that God desired for His abode—yes, where the LORD will dwell forever?
The chariots of God are twice ten thousand, thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them; Sinai is in the sanctuary.
You ascended on high, leading a host of captives in Your train and receiving gifts among men, even among the rebellious, that the LORD God may dwell there.
Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears us up; God is our salvation. Selah.
Our God is a God of salvation, and to the LORD, the Lord, belong deliverances from death.
But God will strike the heads of His enemies, the hairy crown of him who walks in his guilty ways.
The Lord said, “I will bring them back from Bashan, I will bring them back from the depths of the sea,
that you may strike your feet in their blood, that the tongues of your dogs may have their portion from the foe.”
Your procession is seen, O God, the procession of my God, my King, into the sanctuary.
The singers in front, the musicians last, between them virgins playing tambourines.
Bless God in the great congregation, the LORD, O you who are of Israel's fountain.
There is Benjamin, the least, leading them, the princes of Judah in their throng, the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.
Summon Your power, O God, the power, O God, by which You have worked for us.
Because of Your temple at Jerusalem kings shall bring gifts to You.
Rebuke the beasts that dwell among the reeds, the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples. Trample underfoot those who lust after tribute; scatter the peoples who delight in war.
Nobles shall come from Egypt; Cush shall hasten to stretch out her hands to God.
O kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing praises to the Lord, Selah.
To Him who rides in the heavens, the ancient heavens; behold, He sends out His voice, His mighty voice.
Ascribe power to God, whose majesty is over Israel, and whose power is in the skies.
Awesome is God from His sanctuary; the God of Israel—He gives power and strength to His people. Blessed be God!
Deliver me, O God, for the waters have risen to my very throat.
I am sinking in the fathomless mire, where no footing may be found; I have plunged into the abyssal waters, and the torrent has swept over me.
I have worn myself out with crying; my throat is hoarse, and my eyes grow dim while I wait for my God.
My foes who hate me without cause are more than the hairs of my head; those who would destroy me have grown powerful, and they hate me with lies; though I stole nothing, I must now make restitution.
O God, You know my folly; my trespasses are not concealed from You.
May those who hope in You not be ashamed because of me, O Lord, the LORD of Hosts; may those who seek You not be dishonored because of me, O God of Israel.
For I have borne reproach on Your account; shame has veiled my face.
I have become a stranger to my brothers, an alien to my mother's sons.
For zeal for Your house has devoured me, and the insults of those who insult You have fallen upon me.
When I wept and afflicted my soul with fasting, my very devotion became a reproach to me.
I made sackcloth my garment, and I became a byword to them.
Those who sit in the gate mock me, and I am the song of the drunkards.
But as for me, my prayer is to You, O the LORD, at a time of favor; in the greatness of Your steadfast love, O God, answer me in the truth of Your salvation.
Rescue me from the mire, and do not let me sink; deliver me from my enemies and from the depths of the waters.
Let not the torrent of waters overwhelm me, nor the abyss swallow me, nor the pit close its mouth over me.
Answer me, O the LORD, for Your steadfast love is good; in the greatness of Your compassion, turn to me.
Do not hide Your face from Your servant, for I am in anguish; answer me speedily.
Draw near to my soul and redeem it; ransom me on account of my foes.
You know my reproach, my shame, and my disgrace; all my oppressors are before You.
Reproach has shattered my heart, and I am sick; I waited for pity, but there was none, and for comforters, but I found none.
They gave me gall for my food, and in my thirst they made me drink vinegar.
Let their table become a snare before them, and their well-being a trap.
Let their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see, and make their loins shake unceasingly.
Pour out Your wrath upon them, and let Your fierce anger pursue them.
Let their encampment be desolate; let no one inhabit their tents.
For they persecute the one You have struck, and they rehearse the anguish of those You have wounded.
Lay guilt upon their guilt, and let them not enter into Your righteousness.
Let them be erased from the book of life, and let them not be inscribed among the righteous.
But I am afflicted and in pain; may Your salvation, O God, exalt me.
I will praise the name of God with song, and I will magnify Him with thanksgiving.
This will please the the LORD more than an ox or a bull with horns and hooves.
The humble have seen it and rejoice; you who seek God, let your hearts live.
For the the LORD hears the poor, and does not despise His prisoners.
Let heaven and earth praise Him, the seas and everything that moves within them.
For God will save Zion and rebuild the cities of Judah, so that they may dwell there and inherit it.
The offspring of His servants shall inherit it, and those who love His name shall dwell therein.
Hasten, O God, to rescue me; make haste, O the LORD, to my aid.
May those who seek my life be shamed and confounded; may those who delight in my ruin turn back and be dishonored.
May those who cry, “Aha! Aha!” recoil in their own disgrace.
Let all who seek You rejoice and be glad in You; let those who love Your salvation say continually, “God is great!”
But I am poor and needy; hasten to me, O God. You are my help and my deliverer; O the LORD, do not delay.
In You, O the LORD, I have taken refuge; let me never be put to shame.
In Your righteousness deliver me and rescue me; incline Your ear to me and save me.
Be to me a rock of refuge to which I may continually resort; You have ordained salvation for me, for You are my rock and my fortress.
Deliver me, O my God, from the hand of the wicked, from the grasp of the unjust and cruel man.
For You, O Lord, the LORD, are my hope, my confidence from my youth.
From birth I have leaned upon You; You drew me forth from my mother's womb; my praise is ever of You.
I have become, as it were, a portent to multitudes, yet You remain my mighty refuge.
My mouth is filled with Your praise and with Your glory all the day long.
Do not cast me off in the time of old age; do not forsake me when my strength is exhausted.
For my enemies speak concerning me, and those who watch for my life take counsel together,
saying, "God has forsaken him; pursue and seize him, for there is no one to deliver."
O God, do not be far from me; O my God, make haste to help me.
Let those who accuse my soul be put to shame and brought to ruin; let those who seek my calamity be clothed with reproach and dishonor.
But I shall hope continually, and I shall praise You yet more and more.
My mouth shall recount Your righteousness and Your salvation all day long, for their number is beyond my reckoning.
I will come with the mighty acts of the Lord, the LORD; I will remember Your righteousness, Yours alone.
O God, You have taught me from my youth, and to this day I proclaim Your wondrous deeds.
And even to old age and gray hair, O God, do not forsake me, until I proclaim Your might to a generation, Your power to all who are to come.
Your righteousness, O God, reaches the heavens; You who have done great things, O God, who is like You?
You, who have made me see many and bitter troubles, will revive me again; from the depths of the earth You will bring me up again.
You will increase my honor and comfort me once more.
I will also praise You with the harp for Your faithfulness, O my God; I will sing to You with the lyre, O Holy One of Israel.
My lips shall shout for joy when I sing praises to You, and my soul, which You have redeemed.
My tongue also shall recount Your righteousness all day long, for those who seek my hurt are put to shame and confounded.
Of Solomon. Grant to the king Your judgments, O God, and Your righteousness to the king's son.
He shall judge Your people in righteousness and Your afflicted in justice.
Let the mountains bear peace to the people, and the hills, righteousness.
He shall vindicate the afflicted of the people; he shall save the children of the needy and crush the oppressor.
May reverence for You endure as long as the sun shines, and before the moon, throughout all generations.
He shall descend like rain upon freshly mown grass, like showers that irrigate the earth.
In his days the righteous shall flourish, and an abundance of peace, until the moon is no more.
He shall hold dominion from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.
Before him shall bow the denizens of the desert, and his enemies shall be reduced to abject humiliation.
The kings of Tarshish and of the coastlands shall render tribute; the kings of Sheba and Seba shall present offerings.
All kings shall bow down to him, and all nations shall serve him.
For he rescues the needy who cry for help, and the afflicted who has no helper.
He will show compassion to the poor and needy, and will save the lives of the needy.
He will redeem their lives from oppression and violence, and their blood shall be precious in his sight.
May he live long; may gold from Sheba be bestowed upon him; may prayer be offered on his behalf continually, and may he be blessed throughout the day.
Let grain abound in the land; may it sway upon the mountain peaks; its fruit shall be like Lebanon; and they shall flourish from the city like grass of the earth.
May his name endure in perpetuity; may it be continued as long as the sun shines. All nations shall be blessed in him, and they shall pronounce him blessed.
Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone performs wonders.
And blessed be His glorious name forever; let the whole earth be filled with His glory. Amen and Amen.
The prayers of David, the son of Jesse, are concluded.
A psalm of Asaph. Surely God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart.
But as for me, my feet had almost slipped; my steps had nearly given way.
For I envied the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
They have no pangs in their death, and their bodies remain well nourished.
They are free from the burdens common to mortals, nor are they afflicted as others are.
Therefore pride is their necklace, and violence envelops them like a garment.
Their eyes protrude from sheer abundance, while the conceits of their hearts overflow unchecked.
They scoff and utter evil; from their lofty station they threaten oppression.
They set their mouths against the heavens, and their tongues strut across the earth.
Therefore their people turn to them and drink in their overflowing words.
They say, “How can God know? Does the Most High have knowledge?”
Behold, these are the wicked—always at ease, they amass wealth.
Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure and washed my hands in innocence.
All day long I am afflicted, and every morning brings new chastening.
If I had said, “I will speak this way,” I would have betrayed the generation of Your children.
When I sought to comprehend this, it proved wearisome to my sight.
Until I entered the sanctuary of God, then I discerned their end.
Surely You set them on slippery ground; You cast them down to ruin.
How suddenly they are laid waste, utterly consumed by terrors!
Like a dream when one awakes, O Lord, when You arise, You despise their form.
When my heart was grieved and my inmost being was pierced,
I was senseless and ignorant; I was a brute beast before You.
Yet I am always with You; You have held my right hand.
You guide me with Your counsel, and afterward You will take me into glory.
Whom have I in heaven but You? And on earth I desire no one besides You.
My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
Those far from You will perish; You destroy all who are unfaithful to You.
But as for me, it is good to draw near to God. I have made the Lord the LORD my refuge, that I may declare all Your works.
Why have You cast us off in perpetuity, O God, so that Your wrath smolders against the sheep of Your pasture?
Remember Your congregation, which You acquired in antiquity, which You redeemed to be the tribe of Your inheritance—Mount Zion, wherein You have dwelt.
Lift Your steps toward the everlasting desolations, toward every atrocity the enemy has perpetrated in the sanctuary.
Your adversaries roar in the midst of Your meeting place; they have set up their ensigns as signs.
They are recognized as men who wield axes amid a thicket of trees.
And now, with hatchet and hammers, they batter down all its carved work alike.
They have committed Your sanctuary to the flames; they have profaned the dwelling place of Your name to the ground.
They said in their hearts, “Let us crush them all at once”; they have burned every meeting place of God in the land.
We no longer behold our signs; no prophet remains, and none among us knows how long.
How long, O God, will the adversary taunt? Will the enemy blaspheme Your name in perpetuity?
Why do You withdraw Your hand, even Your right hand? Withdraw it from Your bosom and consume them.
Yet God is my King from of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth.
You divided the sea by Your strength; You shattered the heads of the sea monsters upon the waters.
You crushed the heads of Leviathan; You consigned him as food to the peoples of the wilderness.
You split open fountain and torrent; You dried up ever-flowing rivers.
The day is Yours, and Yours also the night; You established the light and the sun.
You have set all the boundaries of the earth; You have ordained summer and winter.
Remember this: the enemy has reproached the LORD, and a foolish people has blasphemed Your name.
Do not deliver the soul of Your turtledove to the beasts; do not forget the life of Your afflicted in perpetuity.
Have regard to the covenant, for the dark places of the earth are full of habitations of violence.
Let not the oppressed return ashamed; let the poor and needy praise Your name.
Arise, O God, plead Your cause; remember how the foolish man reproaches You all day long.
Do not forget the voice of Your adversaries, the uproar of those who rise against You, which ascends continually.
We give thanks to You, O God; we give thanks, for Your name is near. The people declare Your wondrous works.
“When I choose the appointed time, I will judge with equity.
When the earth and all its inhabitants dissolve, it is I who uphold its pillars. Selah.
I said to the boastful, ‘Do not boast,’ and to the wicked, ‘Do not exalt your strength.’
Do not exalt your strength on high, nor speak with haughty insolence.”
For exaltation comes neither from the east nor from the west, nor from the mountainous wilderness;
rather, it is God who judges—He brings one down and exalts another.
For a cup is in the hand of the LORD, full of foaming wine mixed with spices; He pours it out, and all the wicked of the earth drink it down to the dregs.
But I will proclaim forever; I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.
I will cut off all the strength of the wicked, but the strength of the righteous will be exalted.
For the choirmaster, with stringed instruments. A Psalm of Asaph. A Song. God is known in Judah; His name is great in Israel.
His abode has been established in Salem, His dwelling place in Zion.
There He shattered the fiery arrows, the shield, the sword, and the weapons of war. Selah
Glorious are You, more majestic than the mountains of prey.
The stout-hearted were despoiled; they sank into slumber; none of the warriors could so much as raise a hand.
At Your rebuke, O God of Jacob, horse and rider alike were stunned.
You, You are to be feared! Who can stand before You when Your anger is roused?
From heaven You uttered judgment; the earth feared and was still,
when God arose to establish judgment, to save all the humble of the earth. Selah
Surely the wrath of man shall praise You; the remnant of wrath You shall gird about Yourself.
Make your vows to the LORD your God and perform them; let all who surround Him bring tribute to Him who is to be feared,
who breaks the spirit of princes and is feared by the kings of the earth.
I cried aloud to God for deliverance; I cried aloud to God, that He might hear me.
In the day of my distress I sought the Lord; throughout the night my outstretched hand did not grow weary, and my soul refused to be comforted.
I remembered God, and I groaned; I mused, and my spirit fainted. Selah
You have kept my eyes from closing; I was too distraught to speak.
I considered the days of old, the years of antiquity.
At night I remember my song; I meditate within my heart, and my spirit searches:
“Will the Lord cast off forever? Will He never again show favor?
Has His steadfast love ceased forever? Has His promise failed for all generations?
Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has He in anger withheld His compassion?” Selah
Then I said, “This is my anguish: the years of the right hand of the Most High.”
I will remember the deeds of Yah; indeed, I will remember Your wonders of old.
I will meditate on all Your work; I will ponder Your mighty deeds.
Your way, O God, is in holiness; what god is as great as our God?
You are the God who works wonders; You have made known Your strength among the peoples.
With Your mighty arm You redeemed Your people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah
The waters saw You, O God; the waters saw You and were convulsed; even the depths trembled.
The clouds poured down water; the skies thundered; Your arrows flashed back and forth.
The sound of Your thunder was in the whirlwind; Your lightnings illuminated the world; the earth trembled and quaked.
Your way was in the sea, and Your path through the mighty waters, yet Your footsteps were not known.
You led Your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
Attend, O my people, to my instruction, and incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
I will open my mouth in a parable; I will propound riddles whose origins lie in antiquity—
things we have heard and known, and which our fathers have recounted to us.
We shall not conceal them from their children, but shall recount to the latest generation the praises of the LORD, His might, and the wonders He has wrought.
For He established a testimony in Jacob and instituted a law in Israel, which He commanded our fathers to make known to their children,
so that the generation to come might know them—the children yet unborn—that they might arise and declare them to their own children,
and that they might set their confidence in God, neither forgetting His works nor forsaking His commandments.
Thus they would not be like their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation, a generation whose heart was not steadfast and whose spirit was not faithful to God.
The Ephraimites, though armed with bows, retreated on the day of battle.
They did not keep the covenant of God, and they refused to walk in His law.
They forgot His deeds and the wonders He had shown them.
In the sight of their fathers He performed wonders in the land of Egypt, in the fields of Zoan.
He split the sea and led them through, and He made the waters stand like a wall.
He guided them with a cloud by day, and all the night with a fiery light.
He split rocks in the wilderness and gave them drink as from the great deep.
He brought forth streams from the rock and made waters run down like rivers.
Yet they sinned still more against Him, rebelling against the Most High in the arid waste.
They tested God in their hearts by demanding food for their craving.
They spoke against God, saying, “Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?
Behold, He struck the rock, and waters gushed out, and streams overflowed. Can He give bread also? Can He provide meat for His people?”
Therefore the LORD heard and was enraged; a fire was kindled against Jacob, and anger ascended against Israel,
because they did not believe in God and did not trust in His salvation.
Yet He commanded the skies above and opened the doors of heaven,
and He rained down manna upon them to eat and gave them the grain of heaven.
Mortals ate the bread of angels; He sent them provision in abundance.
He made the east wind blow in the heavens, and by His power He drove the south wind.
He rained flesh upon them like dust, winged fowl like the sand of the seas.
He let it fall in the midst of their camp, round about their dwellings.
So they ate and were well filled, for He granted them their craving.
But before their craving was sated, while the food was still in their mouths,
the anger of God rose against them and slew their stoutest and struck down the chosen of Israel.
In spite of all this they sinned still and did not believe His wondrous works.
Therefore He consumed their days in futility and their years in terror.
When He slew them, they sought Him; they repented and sought God earnestly.
They remembered that God was their Rock, and that the Most High God was their Redeemer.
But they flattered Him with their mouth and lied to Him with their tongue.
Their heart was not steadfast toward Him, nor were they faithful to His covenant.
Yet He, being merciful, forgave their iniquity and did not destroy them; many times He turned His anger away and did not arouse all His wrath.
For He remembered that they were flesh, a passing breath that does not return.
How often they rebelled against Him in the wilderness and grieved Him in the desert!
They turned back and tested God, and they provoked the Holy One of Israel.
They did not remember His hand, nor the day when He redeemed them from the adversary,
when He displayed His signs in Egypt and His wonders in the fields of Zoan,
and turned their rivers into blood, so that their streams became undrinkable.
He sent among them swarms of flies that devoured them, and frogs that ruined them.
He gave their produce to the caterpillar and their labor to the locust.
He destroyed their vines with hail and their sycamore trees with frost.
He delivered their cattle to the hail and their flocks to bolts of lightning.
He let loose upon them the fierceness of His anger—wrath, indignation, and distress—a band of destroying angels.
He cleared a path for His anger; He did not spare their souls from death, but gave their lives over to the plague.
He struck down all the firstborn of Egypt, the firstfruits of their vigor in the tents of Ham.
But He led forth His people like sheep and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.
He led them safely, so that they feared not, while the sea overwhelmed their enemies.
He brought them to the border of His sanctuary, to this mountain that His right hand had acquired.
He drove out nations before them and apportioned them an inheritance by line, settling the tribes of Israel in their tents.
Yet they tested and rebelled against God the Most High, and did not keep His decrees.
They turned back and acted treacherously like their fathers; they proved as unreliable as a warped bow.
They provoked Him to anger with their high places and moved Him to jealousy with their graven images.
When God heard this, He was furious and utterly rejected Israel,
and He abandoned the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent He had pitched among mortals,
and delivered His strength into captivity and His splendor into the hand of the foe.
He gave His people over to the sword and was enraged at His inheritance.
Fire consumed His young men, and His maidens were not given in marriage.
Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows could not weep.
Then the Lord awoke as from sleep, like a warrior roused by wine.
He beat back His enemies; He put them to everlasting reproach.
He rejected the tent of Joseph and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim,
but chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which He loved.
He built His sanctuary like the high heavens, like the earth which He established forever.
He chose David His servant and took him from the sheepfolds;
from following the nursing ewes He brought him to shepherd Jacob His people and Israel His inheritance.
So he shepherded them with integrity of heart and guided them with skillful hands.
O God, the nations have invaded your inheritance; they have defiled your holy sanctuary and reduced Jerusalem to a heap of rubble.
They have consigned the corpses of your servants to the birds of the sky for food, and the flesh of your faithful to the beasts of the earth.
They have poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem, with no one to bury them.
We have become a reproach to our neighbors, an object of taunting and derision to those who surround us.
How long, O the LORD? Will you be indignant forever? Will your jealousy blaze like fire?
Pour out your wrath upon the nations that do not know you, and upon the kingdoms that never invoke your name.
For they have ravaged Jacob and desolated his homeland.
Do not charge us with the iniquities of former times; let your compassion hasten to meet us, for we have been brought to utter destitution.
Come to our aid, O God of our deliverance, for the glory of your name; rescue us and expiate our sins for the honor of your name.
Why should the nations taunt, "Where is their God?" May the retribution for your servants' shed blood be displayed among the nations before our eyes.
Let the groaning of the captive reach your presence; by the might of your arm, preserve those condemned to die.
Repay our neighbors sevenfold, letting their reproach recoil upon their own heads, O Lord.
But we, your people and the flock of your pasture, will render thanks to you in perpetuity; from generation to generation we shall proclaim your praise.
For the director of music, to the melody “Lilies”—a testimony of Asaph. Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, You who shepherd Joseph like a flock; You who are enthroned between the cherubim, shine forth.
Before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, stir up Your might and come to our salvation.
Restore us, O God; cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
the LORD God of Hosts, how long will You let Your wrath smolder against the prayers of Your people?
You have fed them with the bread of tears, and You have made them drink tears by the bowlful.
You have made us a cause of contention to our neighbors, and our enemies deride us.
Restore us, O God of Hosts; cause Your face to shine, that we may be saved.
You removed a vine from Egypt; You drove out the nations and planted it.
You cleared ground before it, and it took root and filled the land.
The mountains were mantled with its shade, and the cedars of God with its boughs.
It stretched its branches to the Sea and its shoots to the River.
Why have You torn down its walls, so that every passerby plucks its fruit?
The boar from the forest ravages it, and the beasts of the field feed upon it.
Return, O God of Hosts; look down from heaven and see; attend to this vine,
the root that Your right hand planted, and the son You have raised up for Yourself.
It is cut down and burned with fire; at the rebuke of Your countenance Your people perish.
Let Your hand be upon the man of Your right hand, upon the son of man whom You have made strong for Yourself.
Then we shall not turn away from You; revive us, and we shall invoke Your name.
Restore us, the LORD God of Hosts; cause Your face to shine, that we may be saved.
Sing exultantly to God, our strength; shout triumphantly to the God of Jacob.
Lift up a song and beat the tambourine, the melodious lyre together with the harp.
Blow the trumpet at the new moon, at the full moon, on the day of our festival.
For this is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob.
He established it as a testimony in Joseph when He marched out against the land of Egypt; I heard a tongue I had not known.
I relieved his shoulder of its burden; his hands were freed from the basket.
You called in distress, and I delivered you; I answered you in the secret place of thunder; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah.
Hear, O My people, and I will testify against you; O Israel, if you would but listen to Me!
There shall be no strange god among you, nor shall you bow down to a foreign god.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
My people did not listen to My voice, and Israel refused to obey Me.
So I gave them up to the stubbornness of their hearts; they walked in their own counsels.
If only My people would listen to Me, that Israel might walk in My ways!
I would soon subdue their enemies and turn My hand against their foes.
Those who hate the LORD would cringe before Him, and their doom would last forever.
He would feed you with the finest wheat; with honey from the rock I would satisfy you.
A Psalm of Asaph. God takes His stand in the divine council; in the midst of the gods He renders judgment.
“How long will you render unjust judgments and show partiality to the wicked?
Vindicate the powerless and the fatherless; uphold the rights of the afflicted and the oppressed.
Deliver the weak and the needy; rescue them from the hand of the wicked.” Selah.
They know nothing and understand nothing; they walk about in darkness, and all the foundations of the earth are destabilized.
“I said, ‘You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High.’
Yet you will perish like mortals; you will fall like any of the princes.”
Rise up, O God, and judge the earth, for all the nations are Your inheritance.
A song; a psalm of Asaph. O God, do not remain silent; do not be quiet, O God; do not be still.
For behold, Your enemies are in tumult, and those who hate You have grown arrogantly defiant.
They scheme with cunning against Your people, and they conspire against Your treasured ones.
They say, “Come, let us annihilate them as a nation, so that the name of Israel may be remembered no more.”
For they have conspired with one accord; they have made a covenant against You—
the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
Gebal and Ammon and Amalek, Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre.
Assyria also has joined them; they have become the arm of the children of Lot. Selah.
Do to them as to Midian, as to Sisera, as to Jabin at the River Kishon—
those who were destroyed at Endor, who became manure for the soil.
Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
who said, “Let us seize for ourselves the pastures of God.”
Make them like whirling dust, O my God, like chaff before the wind.
As fire consumes a forest, as a flame sets the mountains ablaze,
so pursue them with Your tempest and terrify them with Your storm.
Fill their faces with shame, that they may seek Your name, O the LORD.
Let them be put to shame and dismayed forever; let them perish in disgrace.
Let them know that You alone are the LORD, the Most High over all the earth.
How delectable are Your sanctuaries, O the LORD of Hosts!
My soul has languished with longing and is utterly spent for the courts of the the LORD; my heart and my flesh exult in jubilation toward the living God.
Even the sparrow has discovered a dwelling, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young—at Your altars, O the LORD of Hosts, my King and my God.
How blessed are those who inhabit Your house; they perpetually praise You. Selah.
How blessed is the man whose might is in You, in whose heart lie the highways to Zion.
As they traverse the Valley of Baca, they transform it into a spring; the early rain likewise mantles it with blessings.
They advance from strength to strength; each appears before God in Zion.
O the LORD God of Hosts, hear my prayer; attend, O God of Jacob. Selah.
Behold our shield, O God, and regard the face of Your Anointed.
For a single day in Your courts surpasses a thousand elsewhere; I would rather serve as a doorkeeper in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of wickedness.
For the the LORD God is a sun and shield; the the LORD bestows grace and glory; He withholds no good thing from those who walk in integrity.
O the LORD of Hosts, how blessed is the man who trusts in You!
To the choirmaster—a psalm of the sons of Korah: You were propitious toward Your land, O the LORD, and You restored Jacob’s fortunes;
You bore away the iniquity of Your people and veiled all their transgressions. Selah.
You gathered up all Your wrath and averted the fierceness of Your anger.
Restore us again, O God of our salvation, and put away Your indignation toward us.
Will You be indignant with us forever, and will You prolong Your wrath from generation to generation?
Will You not revive us again, so that Your people may exult in You?
Show us Your steadfast love, O the LORD, and grant us Your salvation.
I will listen to what God the the LORD speaks, for He will speak peace to His people and to His faithful ones, lest they relapse into folly.
Surely His salvation is near to those who fear Him, that glory may dwell in our land.
Steadfast love and faithfulness have met; righteousness and peace have kissed.
Faithfulness springs from the earth, while righteousness looks down from heaven.
Indeed, the the LORD will give what is good, and our land will yield its harvest.
Righteousness goes before Him and prepares a way for His steps.
Incline Your ear, O the LORD; answer me, for I am poor and needy.
Preserve my life, for I am godly; O my God, save Your servant who trusts in You.
Be gracious to me, O Lord, for to You I cry all day long.
Gladden the soul of Your servant, for to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul.
For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, abounding in steadfast love to all who call on You.
Give ear to my prayer, O the LORD, and attend to the voice of my supplications.
In the day of my distress I will call upon You, for You will answer me.
Among the gods there is none like You, O Lord, nor are there works like Yours.
All the nations You have made will come and bow down before You, O Lord, and they will glorify Your name.
For You are great and perform wonders; You alone are God.
Teach me Your way, O the LORD; I will walk in Your truth. Grant me an undivided heart, that I may fear Your name.
I will praise You, O Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will glorify Your name forever.
For great is Your steadfast love toward me; You have delivered my soul from the depths of Sheol.
O God, the arrogant have risen against me; a band of ruthless men seeks my life; they have no regard for You.
But You, O Lord, are a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness.
Turn to me and have mercy on me; grant Your strength to Your servant, and save the son of Your maidservant.
Show me a sign of Your favor, that my enemies may see it and be put to shame, because You, O the LORD, have helped me and comforted me.
His foundation is established upon the holy mountains.
The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
Glorious things are spoken of you, O city of God. Selah.
“I will recount Egypt and Babylon among those who acknowledge Me—along with Philistia, Tyre, and Cush—each one born there.”
And concerning Zion it shall be said, “This one and that one were born in her,” and the Most High Himself will establish her.
The LORD will record in the register of the nations, “This one was born there.” Selah.
Singers and dancers will declare, “All my springs are in you.”

A song, a psalm of the sons of Korah, for the director of music, according to Mahalath Leannoth; a Maskil of Heman the Ezrahite. The LORD, God of my salvation, day and night I have cried out before You.
May my prayer come before You; incline Your ear to my supplication.
For my soul is overwhelmed with troubles, and my life has drawn near to Sheol.
I am reckoned among those who descend into the pit; I have become as a man bereft of strength.
I am forsaken among the dead, like the slain who lie in the grave, whom You remember no longer, cut off from Your care.
You have laid me in the lowest pit, in dark places, in the depths.
Your wrath presses hard upon me, and You have afflicted me with all Your waves. Selah.
You have removed my companions far from me; You have made me an object of loathing to them; I am imprisoned and cannot go forth.
My eye wastes away from affliction; every day I call upon You, the LORD; I spread out my hands to You.
Will You work wonders for the dead? Will the shades arise to praise You? Selah.
Is Your steadfast love recounted in the grave, Your faithfulness in Abaddon?
Are Your wonders known in the darkness, Your righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?
But I cry out to You, the LORD; in the morning my prayer comes before You.
Why, the LORD, do You reject my soul? Why do You hide Your face from me?
From my youth I have been afflicted and near death; I bear Your terrors; I am overwhelmed.
Your burning anger has swept over me; Your terrors have destroyed me.
They surround me like water all day long; they encompass me on every side.
You have removed friend and companion far from me; darkness is my only companion.
I will sing of the LORD’s steadfast love forever; with my mouth I will make known Your faithfulness to every generation.
For I said, “Steadfast love will be built up forever; in the heavens You will establish Your faithfulness.”
You have said, “I have made a covenant with My chosen one; I have sworn to David My servant:
‘I will establish your offspring forever, and build your throne for all generations.’” Selah
The heavens praise Your wonders, O the LORD, Your faithfulness also in the assembly of the holy ones.
For who in the skies can be compared to the LORD? Who among the heavenly beings is like the LORD,
a God greatly feared in the council of the holy ones, and awesome beyond all who surround Him?
O the LORD God of Hosts, who is mighty like You, O the LORD? Your faithfulness surrounds You.
You rule the raging sea; when its waves surge, You still them.
You crushed Rahab as though it were a corpse; You scattered Your enemies with Your mighty arm.
The heavens are Yours, and the earth is Yours; the world and all that fills it—You founded them.
The north and the south You created; Tabor and Hermon rejoice in Your name.
You possess might; strong is Your hand, and high is Your right hand.
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne; steadfast love and faithfulness go before You.
Blessed are the people who know the festal shout; they walk, O the LORD, in the light of Your face,
they exult in Your name all day long, and in Your righteousness they are exalted.
For You are the glory of their strength; by Your favor our power is exalted.
For our shield belongs to the LORD, and our king to the Holy One of Israel.
Long ago You spoke in a vision to Your godly ones and said, “I have granted help to one who is mighty; I have exalted one chosen from the people.
I have found David My servant; with My holy oil I have anointed him,
so that My hand may be established with him, and My arm may strengthen him.
No enemy shall deceive him, nor shall a son of wickedness afflict him.
I will crush his foes before him and strike down those who hate him.
My faithfulness and My steadfast love shall be with him, and in My name his power shall be exalted.
I will set his hand on the sea and his right hand on the rivers. “
He will call to Me, ‘You are my Father, my God, and the Rock of my salvation.’
I will also make him My firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth.
My steadfast love I will keep for him forever, and My covenant with him shall remain firm.
I will establish his descendants forever, and his throne as long as the heavens endure.
If his children forsake My law and do not walk in My judgments,
if they violate My statutes and do not keep My commandments,
then I will punish their transgression with the rod and their iniquity with blows.
But I will not withdraw My steadfast love from him, nor will I prove false to My faithfulness.
I will not violate My covenant, nor alter the word that has gone forth from My lips.
Once for all I have sworn by My holiness; I will not lie to David.
His descendants shall endure forever, and his throne before Me like the sun.
Like the moon it shall be established forever, a faithful witness in the heavens.” Selah
But now You have cast off and rejected him; You are full of wrath against Your anointed.
You have renounced the covenant with Your servant; You have profaned his crown in the dust.
You have broken down all his walls; You have brought his strongholds to ruin.
All who pass by plunder him; he has become a scorn to his neighbors.
You have exalted the right hand of his foes; You have made all his enemies rejoice.
You have turned back the edge of his sword and have not upheld him in battle.
You have ended his splendor and cast his throne to the ground.
You have shortened the days of his youth; You have covered him with shame. Selah
How long, O the LORD? Will You hide Yourself forever? How long will Your wrath burn like fire?
Remember how brief my life is; for what futility have You created all the children of man?
What man can live and never see death? Who can deliver his soul from the power of Sheol? Selah
O Lord, where are Your former acts of steadfast love, which You swore to David in Your faithfulness?
Remember, O Lord, the reproach of Your servants; how I bear in my heart the insults of all the many peoples,
with which Your enemies mock, O the LORD, with which they mock the footsteps of Your anointed.
Blessed be the LORD forever! Amen and Amen.
Lord, You have been our dwelling place throughout all generations.
Before the mountains were born, before You brought forth the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting, You are God.
You consign mortals to dust, declaring, "Return, you children of Adam."
For in Your sight a thousand years are as yesterday when it passes, or as a watch in the night.
You sweep them away; they are like a sleep, like grass that flourishes.
In the morning it blossoms and withers; by evening it is cut down and dries.
For we are consumed by Your anger and dismayed by Your wrath.
You have set our iniquities before You, our hidden sins in the light of Your face.
All our days pass away beneath Your wrath; we bring our years to an end with a sigh.
The span of our years is seventy, or eighty if we are vigorous; yet their boast is but toil and sorrow, for they are soon cut off, and we fly away.
Who can fathom the might of Your anger, or Your wrath in proportion to the reverence due You?
So teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
Return, O the LORD; how long? Have compassion on Your servants.
Satisfy us in the morning with Your steadfast love, that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.
Make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us, for the years in which we have seen evil.
Let Your work be revealed to Your servants, and Your glory to their children.
May the favor of the Lord our God rest upon us; establish the work of our hands for us—yes, establish the work of our hands.
He who inhabits the covert of the Most High shall lodge in the shadow of the Almighty.
I will say of the LORD, "He is my refuge and my fortress, my God, in Whom I will trust."
Surely He will deliver you from the trapper's snare and from the deadly plague.
He will cover you with His feathers, and under His wings you shall take refuge; His truth shall be your shield and bulwark.
You shall not fear the terror of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day,
nor the pestilence that stalks in darkness, nor the destruction that lays waste at noon.
A thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand, but it shall not approach you.
You shall only look with your eyes and see the recompense of the wicked.
Because you have made the LORD—my refuge, the Most High—your dwelling place,
no evil shall befall you, nor shall any plague come near your tent.
For He will command His angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.
They will bear you up in their hands, lest you strike your foot against a stone.
You shall tread upon the lion and the cobra; you shall trample the young lion and the serpent.
"Because he has devoted himself to Me, I will deliver him; I will set him on high, because he has known My name.
He will call upon Me, and I will answer him; I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him and honor him.
With long life I will satisfy him, and I will show him My salvation."
It is fitting to give thanks to the LORD, and to sing praises to Your name, O Most High;
to declare Your steadfast love in the morning and Your faithfulness through the night,
with the ten-stringed harp and the melody of the lyre.
For You, O LORD, have made me glad by Your work; I will sing for joy at the works of Your hands.
How magnificent are Your works, O LORD! How unfathomably deep are Your thoughts!
A senseless man does not know, nor does a fool understand this.
When the wicked spring up like grass and all evildoers flourish, they will be destroyed forever.
But You, O LORD, are exalted forevermore.
For behold, Your enemies, O LORD—for behold, Your enemies will perish; all evildoers will be scattered.
But You have exalted my horn like that of a wild ox; I have been anointed with fresh oil.
My eyes have looked upon the downfall of my foes; my ears have heard the ruin of my wicked assailants.
The righteous will flourish like the palm tree and grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
Planted in the house of the LORD, they will flourish in the courts of our God.
In old age they will still bear fruit; they will remain vigorous and verdant,
to declare that the LORD is upright; He is my Rock, and in Him there is no unrighteousness.
The LORD reigns; He is robed in majesty. the LORD has girded Himself with strength, so that the world is firmly established and cannot be moved.
Your throne has been established from of old; You are from everlasting.
The rivers have lifted up, O the LORD; the rivers have lifted up their voice; the rivers lift up their roaring.
Above the roar of many waters, above the mighty breakers of the sea, the LORD on high is mighty.
Your testimonies are exceedingly sure; holiness adorns Your house, O the LORD, for length of days.
The LORD, God of vengeance; God of vengeance, shine forth.
Lift Yourself up, Judge of the earth; repay to the proud their recompense.
How long, O the LORD, will the wicked? How long will the wicked exult?
They pour forth insolent speech; all workers of iniquity speak; they boast.
They crush Your people, O the LORD; they afflict Your inheritance.
They slay the widow and the sojourner; they murder orphans.
And they say, "The LORD does not see; the God of Jacob does not regard."
Understand, you brutish among the people; and you fools, when will you be wise?
He who planted the ear, does He not hear? He who formed the eye, does He not see?
He who disciplines the nations, does He not rebuke? He who teaches man knowledge?
The LORD knows the thoughts of man, that they are vanity.
Blessed is the man whom You, the LORD, discipline, whom You teach from Your law,
to give him quiet from days of evil, until a pit is dug for the wicked.
For the LORD will not abandon His people; nor will He forsake His inheritance.
For judgment will return to righteousness; and all the upright in heart will follow.
Who will rise for me against evildoers? Who will stand with me against workers of iniquity?
If the LORD had not been my help, my soul would soon have dwelt in silence.
If I said, "My foot has slipped," Your mercy, O the LORD, supported me.
In the multitude of my thoughts within me, Your comforts delight my soul.
Can a throne of destruction be allied with You, one that frames mischief by statute?
They band together against the soul of the righteous; they condemn innocent blood.
But the LORD has been my stronghold; and my God the rock of my refuge.
And He will turn their iniquity upon them; and in their evil the LORD our God will cut them off.
Come, let us sing to the LORD; let us raise a joyful shout to the Rock of our salvation.
Let us advance into His presence with thanksgiving; let us acclaim Him with songs of praise.
For the LORD is a great God, and a great King above all gods.
In His hand lie the earth’s hidden depths, and the mountain summits are His.
The sea is His, for He made it, and His hands fashioned the dry land.
Come, let us worship and bow down; let us kneel before the LORD, our Maker.
For He is our God, and we are the people of His pasture, the sheep of His hand. Today, if you hear His voice,
“Do not harden your hearts, as in the rebellion, as on the day of testing in the wilderness,
when your fathers tested Me and put Me to the proof, though they had seen My work.
For forty years I was provoked by that generation, and I said, ‘They are a people whose hearts go astray, and they have not known My ways.’
Therefore I swore in My wrath, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’”
Sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth.
Sing to the LORD, bless His name; proclaim His salvation from day to day.
Declare His glory among the nations, His wonders among all peoples.
For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; He is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are but idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
Splendor and majesty are before Him; strength and beauty are in His sanctuary.
Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
Ascribe to the LORD the glory due His name; bring an offering and come into His courts.
Worship the LORD in the splendor of holiness; tremble before Him, all the earth.
Say among the nations, “The LORD reigns. The world is firmly established; it will not be moved. He will judge the peoples with equity.”
Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad; let the sea resound, and all that fills it.
Let the field exult, and all that is in it; then all the trees of the forest will sing for joy
before the LORD, for He comes, for He comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world in righteousness and the peoples in His faithfulness.
the LORD reigns; let the earth exult, and let the myriad isles rejoice.
Cloud and dense darkness enshroud Him, while righteousness and justice constitute the foundation of His throne.
Fire advances before Him and consumes His adversaries on every side.
His lightning illuminates the world; the earth beholds it and quakes.
The mountains melt like wax before the LORD, before the Lord of all the earth.
The heavens proclaim His righteousness, and all peoples behold His glory.
All who serve graven images are put to shame, those who boast in worthless idols; let all gods worship Him.
Zion has heard and is glad, and the daughters of Judah exult because of Your judgments, the LORD.
For You, the LORD, are Most High above all the earth; You are exalted far above all gods.
You who love the LORD, hate evil! He preserves the lives of His faithful ones and delivers them from the hand of the wicked.
Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart.
Rejoice in the LORD, you righteous, and give thanks to His holy name.
Sing to the LORD a new song, for He has wrought wonders; His right hand and holy arm have secured triumph for Him.
The LORD has made known His salvation, and He has unveiled His righteousness before the eyes of the nations.
He has remembered His loving devotion and faithfulness toward the house of Israel, and all the ends of the earth have beheld the salvation of our God.
Shout for joy to the LORD, all the earth; break forth into jubilant song and make music.
Make music to the LORD with the lyre, with the lyre and the resonance of song.
With trumpets and the blast of the ram’s horn, shout in triumph before the LORD, the King.
Let the sea roar, and all that fills it; let the world and its inhabitants resound.
Let the rivers clap their hands; let the mountains sing together for joy.
Let them do so before the LORD, for He comes to judge the earth; He will judge the world in righteousness and the peoples with equity.
The LORD reigns; let the peoples tremble. He is enthroned between the cherubim; let the earth quake.
Great is the LORD in Zion; He is exalted above all the peoples.
Let them praise Your great and awesome name—He is holy.
The King is mighty; He loves justice. You have established equity; You have executed justice and righteousness in Jacob.
Exalt the LORD our God and worship at His footstool; He is holy.
Moses and Aaron were among His priests, and Samuel among those who called upon His name. They called to the LORD, and He answered them.
He spoke to them in the pillar of cloud; they kept His testimonies and the statute He gave them.
O the LORD our God, You answered them. You were a forgiving God to them, yet You avenged their misdeeds.
Exalt the LORD our God and worship at His holy mountain, for the LORD our God is holy.
Shout joyfully unto the the LORD, all the earth.
Serve the the LORD with gladness; come into His presence with exultant song.
Know that the the LORD—He is God; it is He who fashioned us, and not we ourselves; we are His people, and the sheep of His pasture.
Enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise; give thanks unto Him, bless His Name.
For the the LORD is good; His steadfast love endures forever, and His faithfulness unto all generations.
I shall sing of steadfast love and justice; to You, the LORD, I shall sing.
I shall conduct myself with wisdom along the blameless way; when shall You come to me? I shall walk within my house in the integrity of my heart.
I shall set no base thing before my eyes; I hate the practice of those who turn aside, and it shall not cling to me.
A perverse heart shall turn away from me; I shall know nothing of evil.
Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret, him I will destroy; the proud of eye and haughty of heart, I cannot endure.
My eyes are upon the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me; he who walks in the blameless way, he shall minister to me.
No one who practices deceit shall dwell within my house; no one who speaks falsehood shall stand before my eyes.
Morning by morning I will destroy all the wicked of the land, to cut off from the city of the LORD every worker of iniquity.
Hear my prayer, O the LORD; let my cry for help come before You.
Do not conceal Your countenance from me in the day of my distress; incline Your ear toward me; answer me speedily on the day I call.
For my days are consumed like smoke, and my bones are scorched as though by fire.
My heart is blighted and withered like grass, because I have forgotten to eat my bread.
At the sound of my groaning, my bones cleave to my flesh.
I am likened to a pelican of the wilderness, like an owl dwelling among ruins.
I keep vigil and am like a solitary bird upon a rooftop.
All day long my enemies reproach me; those who rail against me invoke my name as a curse.
For I have eaten ashes as though they were bread, and mingled my drink with tears.
Because of Your indignation and wrath, for You have lifted me up and cast me down.
My days are like an evening shadow, and I wither like grass.
But You, O the LORD, sit enthroned forever, and Your renown endures throughout all generations.
You will arise and show compassion to Zion, for it is the season to be gracious to her; the appointed time has arrived.
For Your servants cherish her stones and take pity on her dust.
The nations will fear the name of the the LORD, and all the kings of the earth will revere Your glory.
For the the LORD will rebuild Zion and reveal Himself in His glory.
He will attend to the prayer of the destitute and will not despise their supplication.
Let this be written for the generation to come, that a people yet to be created may praise the the LORD.
For He has looked down from His holy height; from heaven the the LORD has beheld the earth,
to hear the groaning of the captive and to release those condemned to death.
that the name of the the LORD may be declared in Zion and His praise in Jerusalem,
when peoples and kingdoms assemble together to serve the the LORD.
