Throughout all his days he eats in darkness, amid much vexation, sickness, and resentment.

Behold, I have seen what is good and fitting: that a person eat and drink and find enjoyment in all his toil in this world during the number of days of his life that God has given him, for this is his portion.
Moreover, for every person to whom God grants wealth and possessions and empowers him to eat of them, to receive his portion, and to rejoice in his toil—this is the gift of God.
For such a person will not dwell much on the days of his life, since God keeps him occupied with the gladness of his heart.
I have discerned beneath the sun an evil that weighs heavily upon humankind, and its prevalence is grievous.

God bestows upon a man riches, possessions, and honor, so that he lacks nothing his soul might covet; yet God does not grant him sovereignty to consume what has been given, and a stranger devours it. This is vanity and a grievous malady.

If a man begets a hundred children and lives through many years, however numerous the days of his life may be, yet his soul is not sated by prosperity, and he receives no burial—I declare that the stillborn is better than he.
For that one comes in futility and departs into darkness, while his name is shrouded in obscurity.
He has neither seen the sun nor known anything; nevertheless, he enjoys tranquility beyond that man.
Even if he had lived twice a thousand years without beholding the good, would not all proceed to a single destination?
All human toil is for the mouth, yet the appetite remains insatiable.
What advantage, then, does the wise possess over the fool, or what does the impoverished man gain by knowing how to conduct himself among the living?
Better is the contentment of the eyes than the wandering of desire; this too is vanity and a chasing after wind.
Whatever has come to be has already been named, and it is known what humanity is; he cannot contend with the one who is mightier than he.
Since many words multiply futility, what benefit accrues to humanity?
For who knows what is good for a person during the brief span of his vain life, which passes like a shadow? And who will disclose to humanity what shall occur after him beneath the sun?
A good name is better than precious ointment, and the day of death better than the day of birth.
It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting, for that is the end of every human being, and the living should take it to heart.
Sorrow is better than laughter, for by the sadness of countenance the heart is made good.
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise than for a man to hear the song of fools.
For as the crackling of thorns beneath a pot, so is the laughter of fools; this too is vanity.
For oppression drives the wise to folly, and a bribe corrupts the heart.
Better is the end of a matter than its beginning; patience is better than pride.
Do not be quick to anger in your spirit, for anger lodges in the bosom of fools.
Do not say, "Why were the former days better than these?" for it is not from wisdom that you ask this.
Wisdom, alongside an inheritance, is good, and it is an even greater benefit to those who see the sun.
For wisdom is a shelter, as money is a shelter, but the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its possessors.
Consider the work of God: who can straighten what He has made crooked?
In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider that God has made the one as well as the other, so that no one may know what will come after him.
In my days of vanity I have seen everything: there is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness, and a wicked man who prolongs his life in his wickedness.
Do not be excessively righteous, nor be overly wise; why should you destroy yourself?
Do not be excessively wicked, nor be a fool; why should you die before your time?
It is good that you grasp this, and that you do not withdraw your hand from that; for the one who fears God will avoid every extreme.
Wisdom strengthens the wise more than ten rulers who are in a city.
Surely there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.
Moreover, do not take to heart every word that is spoken, lest you hear your servant cursing you.
For your own heart knows that many times you have cursed others.
All this I have tested by wisdom; I said, "I will be wise," but it was far from me.
That which is far off and exceedingly deep—who can find it out?
I turned my heart to know, to search out, and to seek wisdom and the sum of things, and to know the wickedness of folly and the madness of foolishness.
And I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and nets, whose hands are chains. The one who pleases God escapes from her, but the sinner is ensnared by her.
"See, this is what I found," says the Teacher, "adding one thing to another in order to discover the sum."
My soul is still seeking, and I have not found it: one man among a thousand I have found, but a woman among all these I have not found.
See, this alone I found: God made man upright, but they have sought out many schemes.
Who resembles the sage, and who apprehends the elucidation of a matter? Wisdom illumines a man's visage, and the severity of his countenance is transfigured.
Keep the king's injunction—I enjoin this on account of the oath sworn before God.
Be not precipitate in withdrawing from his presence, nor persist in an evil affair, for he executes whatsoever he desires.
For a king's word is sovereign; who may say to him, "What are you doing?"
The keeper of the commandment knows no evil thing; a wise heart discerns both season and judgment.
For every purpose has its season and its judgment, because the wretchedness of man is heavy upon him.
For he knows not what shall be, and who can declare to him how it shall transpire?
No one has dominion over the breath to restrain it, nor authority over the day of death, nor is there any discharge from war; and wickedness does not rescue those enthralled to it.
All this I have seen, and I applied my heart to every work wrought under the sun, in the time when one man tyrannized over another to his detriment.
Thus I saw the wicked interred—those who once frequented the holy place—and forgotten in the very city where they had acted so; this too is vanity.
Because sentence against an evil work is not executed with celerity, the heart of the sons of men is fully emboldened within them to do evil.
Although a sinner does evil a hundred times and prolongs his days, yet I know that it shall be well with those who fear God, who stand in awe before Him.
But it shall not be well with the wicked, nor shall he prolong his days, which are as a shadow, because he does not fear before God.

There is a vanity wrought upon the earth: righteous men to whom it happens according to the deeds of the wicked, and wicked men to whom it happens according to the deeds of the righteous. I declared that this too is vanity.

Therefore I commended joy, for there is no good for a man under the sun save to eat, drink, and rejoice; and this shall accompany him in his toil throughout the days of life that God has given him under the sun.
When I set my heart to know wisdom and to observe the business done on the earth—for neither by day nor by night does sleep visit his eyes—

then I saw all the work of God, that man cannot discover the work done under the sun; however much he labors in seeking, he shall not find it; and even if the wise man professes to know, he cannot find it.

For I have taken all this to heart and sought to apprehend its full import: the righteous and the wise, together with their deeds, lie in the hand of God, and no one can foreknow whether love or hatred awaits them.

A uniform fate befalls all alike—one destiny overtakes the righteous and the wicked, the good and the evil, the clean and the unclean, the one who sacrifices and the one who does not; as it is with the good, so with the sinner; as with the swearer, so with him who fears an oath.

This is the grievous evil pervading all that is wrought beneath the sun: one fate overtakes everyone, and the human heart is saturated with evil; madness resides in their hearts throughout their lives, and thereafter they join the dead.
Yet hope remains for anyone still reckoned among the living, since a living dog surpasses a dead lion.
For the living know that they must die, but the dead know nothing; they have no further reward, for their memory is forgotten.
Their love, their hatred, and their jealousy have already perished, and they no longer possess any share in anything done beneath the sun.
Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a glad heart, for God has already approved your works.
Let your garments be white at all times, and do not let oil be lacking upon your head.

Enjoy life with the wife whom you love throughout all the days of your ephemeral life, which He has granted you beneath the sun—all your days of futility—for this is your portion in life and in the labor you perform beneath the sun.
Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your might, for in Sheol, whither you are going, there is no work, nor reckoning, nor knowledge, nor wisdom.

I observed once more beneath the sun that the race belongs not to the swift, nor battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise, nor wealth to the discerning, nor favor to the knowing; instead, time and chance befall them all.
For no one knows his time. Like fish caught in a cruel net and like birds seized in a snare, so the sons of men are ensnared in an evil time when it suddenly falls upon them.
I have likewise seen this wisdom beneath the sun, and it appeared momentous to me:
there was a small city with few men in it; a great king came against it, surrounded it, and erected massive siegeworks against it.
Now a poor wise man was found in it, and he saved the city by his wisdom; yet no one remembered that poor man.
So I said, "Wisdom is better than strength, but the wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are not heeded."
The quiet words of the wise are better heard than the shouting of a ruler among fools.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.
Dead flies cause a perfumer’s ointment to reek; likewise, a modicum of folly outweighs wisdom and honor in its capacity to corrupt.
The heart of the wise inclines toward the right, whereas the heart of the fool inclines toward the left.
Even as the fool traverses the road, his heart remains deficient, and he proclaims to everyone, “He is a fool.”
Should a ruler’s wrath surge against you, do not abandon your post, for composure pacifies even grave transgressions.
I have observed an evil beneath the sun, akin to an inadvertent misjudgment emanating from a sovereign.
Folly is elevated to many exalted stations, while the affluent are relegated to humble positions.
I have seen slaves mounted on horses, and princes proceeding on foot like slaves.
He who excavates a pit falls into it, and he who breaches a wall is bitten by a serpent.
He who quarries stones is injured by them, and he who cleaves wood is endangered by them.
If an iron blade grows dull and its edge remains unsharpened, one must marshal greater force; yet wisdom confers advantage by directing one’s efforts.
If a serpent bites before it is charmed, then the charmer derives no advantage.
The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious, but the lips of a fool consume him.
The beginning of his mouth’s words is folly, and the conclusion of his speech is wicked madness.
The fool multiplies words, though no one knows what is coming; and who can declare to him what will transpire thereafter?
The toil of fools exhausts each of them, for he does not know the way to the city.
Woe to you, O land, when your king is a child and your princes feast in the morning.
Blessed are you, O land, when your king is a son of nobles and your princes feast at the proper time—for strength and not for drunkenness.
Through sloth the rafters sag, and through idleness of hands the house leaks.
Bread is made for laughter, wine gladdens the living, and money answers all things.
Even in your thoughts, do not curse the king, nor in your bedroom curse the rich, for a bird of the heavens will carry the voice, and a winged creature will report the matter.
Commit your resources to uncertain ventures, for after many days you will recover them.
Allot a share to seven, and even to eight, since you cannot know what calamity may befall the land.
If the clouds are saturated, they pour forth rain upon the earth; and if a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the very place where it falls, there it shall remain.
The one who waits for the wind to settle will never sow, and the one who fixes his gaze upon the clouds will never reap.
Just as you do not know the way of the wind, nor comprehend how bones coalesce within the womb of her who carries a child, so likewise you cannot know the work of God, who accomplishes all things.
Sow your seed in the morning, and do not withhold your hand in the evening, for you do not know which undertaking will prosper—this one or that—or whether both will prove equally fruitful.
Light is sweet, and it is a delight for the eyes to behold the sun.
If a man lives for many years, let him rejoice throughout them all, yet let him remember the days of darkness—for they will be numerous; all that comes to pass is futility.

Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart cheer you in the days of your young manhood; walk in the inclinations of your heart and in the desires of your eyes; yet know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
So remove vexation from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh, for childhood and youth are futility.

Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days arrive and the years draw near when you will say, “I have no pleasure in them”; and before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars are darkened and the clouds return after the rain;
in the day when the keepers of the house tremble, the men of strength are bent, the grinders cease because they are few, and those who look through the windows grow dim.
When the doors to the street are shut and the sound of grinding is low, when one rises at the sound of a bird, and all the daughters of song are brought low;

when men are afraid of heights and terrors are in the road; when the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper drags itself along, and desire fails—for man goes to his eternal home, and mourners walk about in the street;
before the silver cord is severed, or the golden bowl is crushed, or the pitcher is shattered at the spring, or the wheel is broken at the well;
and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
“Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher, “all is futility.”
Not only was the Teacher wise, but he also taught the people knowledge; he pondered, searched out, and arranged many proverbs.
The Teacher sought to find pleasing words, and he wrote words of truth with uprightness.
The words of the wise are like goads, and like nails firmly fixed are the collected sayings; they are given by one Shepherd.
My son, be warned by these: of making many books there is no end, and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
When all has been heard, the conclusion of the matter is this: Fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole duty of man.
For God will bring every deed into judgment, along with every hidden thing, whether good or evil.
The Song of Songs, which is Solomon's.
"Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, for your love is more delectable than wine.
Your ointments exhale a fragrance most exquisite; your name itself is as oil poured forth; therefore the maidens cherish you.
Draw me after you, and we shall run; the king has conducted me into his chambers. We shall exult and take delight in you; we shall extol your love above wine; with rectitude do they cherish you."
"I am dark, yet comely, O daughters of Jerusalem—like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.
Do not stare at me because I am swarthy, because the sun has scorched me. My mother's sons were incensed against me; they appointed me keeper of the vineyards, yet my own vineyard I have not kept."
"Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you pasture your flock, where you make it lie down at noon; for why should I be like one who veils herself beside the flocks of your companions?"
"If you do not know, O fairest among women, go forth, follow in the tracks of the flock, and pasture your young goats beside the shepherds' tents."
"I compare you, my love, to a mare among Pharaoh's chariots.
Your cheeks are comely with ornaments, your neck with strings of jewels."
"We will make you circlets of gold studded with silver."
"While the king was upon his couch, my nard diffused its fragrance.
My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh resting between my breasts.
My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of En-gedi."
"Behold, you are beautiful, my love; behold, you are beautiful; your eyes are doves."
"Behold, you are handsome, my beloved, truly delightful. Our couch is verdant.
The beams of our house are cedars; our rafters are firs."
I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.
As a lily among thorns, so is my beloved among the daughters.
As an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my beloved among the sons. I delighted to sit in his shade, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
He has brought me into the banqueting house, and his banner over me is love.
Sustain me with raisin cakes, refresh me with apples, for I am overcome with love.
His left hand is beneath my head, and his right hand embraces me.
"I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or by the does of the field, that you not stir up nor awaken love until it so desires."
The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes, leaping upon the mountains, bounding over the hills.
My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Behold, he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice.
My beloved answered and said to me, "Arise, my darling, and come away, my beautiful one.
For behold, the winter has passed; the rain is over and gone.
The flowers appear on the earth; the time of singing has arrived; and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
The fig tree ripens its early figs, and the blossoming vines give forth their fragrance. Arise, my darling, and come away, my beautiful one.
My dove, in the clefts of the rock, in the shelter of the cliff, let me see your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your countenance is lovely."
Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that ruin the vineyards, for our vineyards are in blossom.
My beloved is mine, and I am his; he shepherds among the lilies.
Until the day breathes and the shadows flee, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag upon the mountains of Bether.
Upon my bed by night I sought the beloved of my soul; I sought him, but did not find him.
I will now arise and go about the city, through the streets and squares; I will seek the beloved of my soul. I sought him, but did not find him.
The watchmen who patrol the city found me: “Have you seen the beloved of my soul?”
Scarcely had I passed them when I found the beloved of my soul. I seized him and would not let him go until I had brought him to my mother’s house, to the chamber of the one who bore me.
Daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles or by the does of the field: Do not stir up or awaken love until it pleases.
Who is this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with every powder of the merchant?
Behold, it is Solomon’s palanquin, escorted by sixty warriors from the mightiest of Israel,
all of them grasping swords and trained in war, each with his sword at his thigh, because of the terror of the nights.
King Solomon has made for himself a palanquin from the wood of Lebanon.
He has made its posts of silver, its base of gold, its seat of purple; its interior is inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.
“Come out, O daughters of Zion, and gaze upon King Solomon, wearing the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, the day of the gladness of his heart.”
“Behold, you are beautiful, my darling; behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are doves behind your veil. Your hair falls like a flock of goats descending from Mount Gilead.
Your teeth resemble a flock of newly shorn ewes ascending from the washing, each bearing twins, with none among them bereaved.
Your lips are like a scarlet ribbon, and your mouth is comely. Your brow is like a slice of pomegranate behind your veil.
“Your neck is like the tower of David, built in courses, upon which hang a thousand shields—all the shields of the mighty.
Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, grazing among the lilies.
“Until the day breathes and the shadows flee, I shall betake myself to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.
“You are altogether beautiful, my darling; there is no blemish in you.
“Come with me from Lebanon, my bride; come with me from Lebanon. Descend from the peak of Amana, from the peak of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of lions, from the mountains of leopards.
You have captivated my heart, my sister, my bride; you have captivated my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your necklace.
“How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much more delightful is your love than wine, and the fragrance of your perfume than all spices!
Your lips drip honey, my bride; honey and milk are beneath your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon.
“You are a garden locked, my sister, my bride, a spring enclosed, a fountain sealed.
Your branches are an orchard of pomegranates with the choicest fruits, with henna and nard.
Nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with all frankincense, myrrh and aloes, with all the finest spices.
You are a garden spring, a well of living water flowing down from Lebanon.”
“Awake, O north wind, and come, O south wind! Blow upon my garden, that its spices may flow out. Let my beloved come to his garden and eat its choicest fruits.”

I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O companions; drink, and be intoxicated, O lovers.
I slept, but my heart was awake. A sound! My beloved is knocking. "Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one, for my head is drenched with dew, my tresses with the drops of night."
I have removed my garment; how am I to don it anew? I have cleansed my feet; how am I to soil them?
My beloved thrust his hand through the latch-opening, and my inmost being was stirred for him.
I rose to open to my beloved, and my hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, upon the handles of the bolt.
I opened to my beloved, but my beloved had withdrawn and gone. My spirit faltered when he spoke. I sought him, but did not find him; I called him, but he gave no answer.
The watchmen who go about the city found me; they struck me, they wounded me; they took away my veil from me, those watchmen of the walls.
I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, what will you tell him?—that I am faint with love.
What is your beloved more than another beloved, O fairest among women? What is your beloved more than another beloved, that you so adjure us?
My beloved is radiant and ruddy, preeminent among ten thousand.
His head is finest gold; his locks are wavy, black as a raven.
His eyes are like doves beside channels of water, washed in milk, resting beside a brimming pool.
His cheeks are like beds of spices, towers of perfumes; his lips are lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.
His arms are rods of gold set with topaz; his torso is polished ivory inlaid with sapphires.
His legs are pillars of alabaster founded upon bases of gold; his aspect is like Lebanon, select as the cedars.
His palate is sweetness itself, and he is altogether desirable. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
"Where has your beloved departed, O fairest among women? Where has he turned aside, that we may seek him in company with you?"
"My beloved has descended to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture among the gardens and to gather lilies.
I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine; he feeds among the lilies."
"You are beautiful, my darling, as Tirzah, lovely as Jerusalem, majestic as an army with banners.
Turn your eyes away from me, for they overwhelm me. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down from Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of ewes ascending from the washing, each bearing its twin, with none among them bereaved.
Your temples are like a slice of pomegranate behind your veil."
"There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and maidens beyond numbering.

My dove, my perfect one, is unique; she is the only daughter of her mother, the cherished one of her who bore her. The daughters saw her and pronounced her blessed; the queens and concubines extolled her."
"Who is this that gazes forth like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, radiant as the sun, majestic as an army with banners?"
"I descended to the walnut garden to observe the blossoms of the valley, to ascertain whether the vine had budded and the pomegranates had bloomed.
Before I was aware, my longing had set me among the chariots of my noble people."
"Return, return, O Shulammite; return, return, that we may gaze upon you. Why should you gaze upon the Shulammite, as upon the dance of Mahanaim?"
How exquisite are your steps in sandals, O daughter of nobility! The sinuous contours of your thighs resemble precious gems, the masterpiece of an artisan's hands.
Your navel is a rounded goblet that never lacks blended wine; your belly is a mound of wheat, encircled by lilies.
Your breasts are like twin fawns, the offspring of a gazelle.
Your neck resembles an ivory tower; your eyes are pools in Heshbon, beside the gate of Bath-rabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, overlooking Damascus.
Your head crowns you like Carmel, and the flowing locks of your head are like royal purple; a king is held captive by your tresses.
How beautiful and pleasant you are, O love, amid your delights!
Your stature is like a palm tree, and your breasts are like its clusters.
I said, "I will climb the palm tree and seize its fruit." May your breasts be like clusters of the vine, and the fragrance of your breath like apples,
and your palate be like the finest wine, flowing smoothly to my beloved, gliding over the lips of sleepers.
I am my beloved's, and his desire is for me.
Come, my beloved, let us go out into the countryside; let us spend the night among the henna blossoms.
Let us go early to the vineyards, to see whether the vine has budded, whether the blossom has opened, and whether the pomegranates are in bloom; there I will give you my love.
The mandrakes give forth their fragrance, and at our door are all manner of delicacies, both new and old, which I have treasured up for you, my beloved.
“Were you but my brother, one who nursed at my mother's breast—then, finding you in the open, I could kiss you, and none would hold me in contempt.
I would lead you and bring you into my mother's house—there you would instruct me—and I would give you spiced wine to drink, the nectar of my pomegranate.
His left hand beneath my head, and his right hand embraces me.”
“Daughters of Jerusalem, I charge you: do not arouse or awaken love until it so desires.”
Who is this ascending from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I awakened you beneath the apple tree; there your mother conceived you, there she who bore you was in labor.
“Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm; for love is as strong as death, and jealousy is as unrelenting as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a blaze of unsurpassed intensity.
Many waters cannot quench love, nor can rivers sweep it away; and if a man were to offer all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly despised.”
“We have a little sister, and she has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister on the day she is betrothed?
If she is a wall, we will build upon her a battlement of silver; but if she is a door, we will enclose her with cedar boards.”
“I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers; then I became in his eyes as one who finds peace.”
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon; he leased the vineyard to keepers, and each was to bring a thousand pieces of silver for its fruit.
“My vineyard, my very own, is before me: you, Solomon, may have the thousand, and those who tend its fruit two hundred.”
“O you who dwell in the gardens, your companions are listening for your voice; let me hear it.”
“Flee, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag upon the mountains of spices.”
The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Hear, O heavens, and hearken, O earth, for the LORD has spoken: “I have reared children and brought them up, yet they have rebelled against Me.”
The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master’s manger, but Israel does not know; My people do not understand.

Woe to the sinful nation, a people heavy with iniquity, offspring of evildoers, children who deal corruptly! They have forsaken the LORD; they have despised the Holy One of Israel; they have turned their backs on Him.
Why should you be struck down again? You will only add to your rebellion. The whole head is sick, and the whole heart is faint.
From the sole of the foot to the head there is no soundness in it—only wounds and welts and festering sores; they have not been cleansed, nor bound up, nor soothed with oil.
Your land is desolate; your cities are burned with fire; before your eyes strangers devour your land, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.
The Daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a cucumber field, like a city under siege.
If the LORD of Hosts had not left us a remnant, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.
Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom; give ear to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah.

“What to Me is the multitude of your sacrifices?” says the LORD. “I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened beasts; I do not delight in the blood of bulls, or of lambs, or of goats.
When you come to appear before Me, who has required this trampling of My courts from your hand?
Bring no more worthless offerings; incense is an abomination to Me. New moon and Sabbath and the calling of assemblies—I cannot endure iniquity and the solemn assembly.
Your new moons and your appointed feasts My soul hates; they have become a burden to Me; I am weary of bearing them.
When you spread out your hands, I will hide My eyes from you; even though you multiply prayers, I will not listen; your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean; remove the evil of your deeds from before My eyes; cease to do evil.
Learn to do right; seek justice and correct the oppressor; defend the fatherless and plead the case of the widow.
Come now, let us reason together,” says the LORD. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool.
If you are willing and obedient, you shall eat the good of the land;
but if you refuse and rebel, you shall be devoured by the sword; for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.”
How the faithful city has become a harlot! She who was full of justice—righteousness once lodged in her—but now murderers.
Your silver has become dross; your wine is diluted with water.
Your princes are rebels and companions of thieves; everyone loves a bribe and runs after gifts; they do not judge the fatherless, and the widow’s plea does not reach them.
Therefore the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, declares: “Ah, I will be relieved of My adversaries and avenge Myself on My enemies.
I will turn My hand against you, and I will smelt away your dross as with lye, and remove all your tin.
And I will restore your judges as at the first, and your counselors as at the beginning. Afterward you shall be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful City.
Zion shall be redeemed with justice, and her penitent ones with righteousness.
But rebels and sinners shall be destroyed together, and those who forsake the LORD shall be consumed.
For you shall be ashamed of the oaks in which you delighted, and you shall blush for the gardens that you have chosen.
For you shall be like an oak whose leaf withers, and like a garden without water.
And the strong shall be as tinder, and his work as a spark; and both shall burn together, with none to quench them.”
The vision that Isaiah son of Amoz beheld concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
In the last days, the mountain of the house of the the LORD shall be established as the chief of the mountains and exalted above the hills, and all nations shall stream toward it.

Many peoples shall come and say, “Come, let us ascend to the mountain of the the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, that He may instruct us in His ways and that we may walk in His paths.” For from Zion shall issue forth instruction, and the word of the the LORD from Jerusalem.

He shall judge among the nations and arbitrate for many peoples; they shall beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks; nation shall not lift up sword against nation, nor shall they learn war any longer.
O house of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the the LORD.

For You have forsaken Your people, the house of Jacob, because they are replete with customs imported from the East and practice divination like the Philistines, and they enter into alliances with the children of foreigners.
Their land is glutted with silver and gold, and their treasuries know no limit; their land is filled with horses, and their chariots are beyond numbering.
Their land is likewise overrun with idols; they prostrate themselves before the work of their own hands, before that which their fingers have fashioned.
Thus humankind is humbled, and man is brought low; do not pardon them.
Enter the rock and hide in the dust from the terror of the the LORD and from the splendor of His majesty.
The haughty eyes of man shall be brought low, and the lofty pride of men shall be abased; the the LORD alone shall be exalted in that day.
For the day of the the LORD of Hosts shall come against all that is proud and lofty, against all that is exalted and abased;
against all the cedars of Lebanon, high and lifted up, and against all the oaks of Bashan;
against all the high mountains and all the lifted-up hills;
against every high tower and every fortified wall;
against all the ships of Tarshish and against all desirable things.
The haughtiness of man shall be brought low, and the pride of men shall be abased; the the LORD alone shall be exalted in that day.
They shall go into the caves of the rocks and into the holes of the dust from the terror of the the LORD and from the splendor of His majesty, when He arises to terrify the earth.
In that day a man shall cast away his silver idols and his gold idols, which they made for themselves to worship, to the moles and to the bats,
to enter the clefts of the rocks and the crevices of the cliffs from the terror of the the LORD and from the splendor of His majesty, when He arises to terrify the earth.
Cease from man, whose breath is in his nostrils, for of what account is he?
For behold, the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, is withdrawing from Jerusalem and from Judah both prop and stay—every prop of bread and every prop of water—
the warrior and the man of war, the judge and the prophet, the diviner and the elder,
the commander of fifty and the man of distinction, the counselor, the consummate craftsman, and the adept in incantations.
I will appoint callow youths as their princes, and petulant children shall rule over them.
The people will be oppressed, one by another and each by his neighbor; the youth will behave insolently toward the elder, and the despised toward the honorable.
A man will seize his brother in his father’s house, saying, “You have a garment; you shall be our leader, and this ruin shall be under your hand.”
In that day he will lift up his voice, saying, “I will not be a healer; in my house there is neither bread nor garment; you shall not make me leader of the people.”
For Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen, because their tongue and their deeds are against the LORD, defying the radiance of His glory.
The cast of their countenance testifies against them; they proclaim their sin as Sodom does and do not conceal it. Woe to them, for they have brought calamity upon themselves!
Say of the righteous that it shall be well with them, for they shall eat the fruit of their doings.
Woe to the wicked! It shall be ill with him, for the recompense of his hands shall be rendered to him.
As for My people, children are their taskmasters, and women rule over them. O My people, your guides lead you astray and have swallowed up the course of your paths.
The LORD arises to plead His cause and stands to judge the peoples.
The LORD will enter into judgment with the elders and princes of His people: “It is you who have devoured the vineyard; the plunder of the poor is in your houses.
What do you mean by crushing My people and grinding the faces of the poor?” says the Lord, the LORD of Hosts.
Moreover, the LORD says: “Because the daughters of Zion are haughty and walk with outstretched necks, glancing wantonly with their eyes, mincing along as they go, tinkling with their feet,
therefore the Lord will bring sores upon the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion, and the LORD will lay bare their secret parts.”
In that day the Lord will take away the finery of the anklets, the headbands, and the crescents;
the pendants, the bracelets, and the veils;
the headdresses, the armlets, the sashes, the perfume boxes, and the charms;
the rings and the nose rings;
the festal robes, the mantles, the cloaks, and the handbags;
the mirrors, the linen garments, the turbans, and the veils.
Instead of perfume there will be stench; instead of a belt, a rope; instead of well-set hair, baldness; instead of a rich robe, a girding of sackcloth; and branding instead of beauty.
Your men shall fall by the sword, and your mighty men in battle.
And her gates shall lament and mourn; and she, desolate, shall sit upon the ground.
On that day seven women will seize a single man, declaring, “We will consume our own bread and attire ourselves in our own garments; only let your name be invoked over us—remove our disgrace!”
On that day the Branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious, and the land’s fruit will be the pride and splendor of Israel’s remnant.
Then every survivor in Zion and every remnant in Jerusalem will be proclaimed holy—each one inscribed for life in Jerusalem—
when the Lord has washed away the filth of Zion’s daughters and purged the bloodshed from Jerusalem’s midst by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.

Then the the LORD will create over all the site of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud and smoke by day, and the radiance of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory there will be a canopy.
It will be a booth affording shade from the heat by day, and a refuge and hiding place from storm and rain.
Let me now sing to my beloved a song of my beloved concerning His vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a hill of exceptional fertility.

He fenced it, cleared it of stones, and planted it with the choicest vine; He built a watchtower in its midst and hewed a winepress in it. Then He expected it to yield grapes, but it yielded only sour grapes.
“Now then, O inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, judge between Me and My vineyard.
What more was there to do for My vineyard that I did not do? Why, when I looked for it to yield grapes, did it yield only sour grapes?
And now I will tell you what I am about to do to My vineyard: I will remove its hedge, and it shall be consumed; I will break down its wall, and it shall be trampled underfoot.
I will make it a waste; it shall not be pruned or hoed, and briers and thorns shall grow up. I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it.”
For the vineyard of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are His pleasant planting. He looked for justice, and behold, bloodshed; for righteousness, and behold, an outcry.
Woe to those who add house to house and join field to field, until there is no more room, and you are left to dwell alone in the midst of the land.
In my hearing the LORD of Hosts has sworn: “Surely many houses, great and fine, shall become desolate, without inhabitant.
For ten acres of vineyard shall yield but a bath, and a homer of seed shall yield but an ephah.”
Woe to those who rise early in the morning to pursue strong drink, who linger late into the evening as wine inflames them.
They have lyre and harp, tambourine and flute, and wine at their feasts, but they do not regard the work of the LORD, nor do they consider the work of His hands.
Therefore My people go into exile for lack of knowledge; their honored men are famished, and their multitude is parched with thirst.
Therefore Sheol has enlarged its appetite and opened its mouth beyond measure; down go their glory, their multitude, their pomp, and their revelers.
So man is humbled, and each one is brought low; the eyes of the haughty are brought low.
But the LORD of Hosts is exalted in justice, and the Holy God shows Himself holy in righteousness.
Then the lambs shall graze as in their pasture, and strangers shall feed among the ruins of the rich.
Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of falsehood and sin as with cart ropes,
who say, “Let Him make speed; let Him hasten His work, that we may see it; let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, that we may know it.”
Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness in place of light and light in place of darkness, who put bitter in place of sweet and sweet in place of bitter.
Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and shrewd in their own sight.
Woe to those who are heroes at drinking wine and valiant men at mixing strong drink,
who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deprive the innocent of justice.

Therefore, as a tongue of fire devours the stubble, and as dry grass sinks down in the flame, so their root shall be as rottenness, and their blossom shall go up like dust; because they have rejected the law of the LORD of Hosts and have despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

Therefore the anger of the LORD is kindled against His people, and He has stretched out His hand against them and struck them; the mountains quaked, and their corpses were as refuse in the midst of the streets. For all this His anger is not turned away, and His hand is stretched out still.
He will raise a signal for nations afar off, and whistle for them from the ends of the earth; and behold, they will come with speed, swiftly.
None is weary, none stumbles, none slumbers nor sleeps; not a waistband is loose, nor a sandal strap broken;
their arrows are sharp, and all their bows are bent; their horses’ hooves seem like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind.
Their roaring is like a lion, they roar like young lions; they growl and seize the prey, they carry it off, and there is none to rescue.
They will growl over it in that day like the growling of the sea. And if one looks to the land, behold, darkness and distress; and the light is darkened by its clouds.
In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and exalted, and the train of His robe filled the temple.
Above Him stood the seraphim; each had six wings: with two he covered his face, with two he covered his feet, and with two he flew.
And one called to another, saying, “Holy, Holy, Holy is the the LORD of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory.”
The foundations of the thresholds trembled at the voice of the caller, and the temple was filled with smoke.
And I said, “Woe to me, for I am ruined! For I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the the LORD of Hosts.”
Then one of the seraphim flew to me, carrying in his hand a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.
And he touched my mouth and said, “Behold, this has touched your lips; your iniquity is removed, and your sin is atoned for.”
And I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for Us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me.”
And He said, “Go and tell this people: ‘Hear indeed, but understand not; see indeed, but perceive not.’
Make the heart of this people callous, their ears heavy, and their eyes shut, lest they see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed.”
And I said, “How long, O Lord?” And He said, “Until cities are laid waste without inhabitant, houses without people, and the land is utterly desolate,
and the the LORD has carried the people far away, and great desolation reigns in the midst of the land.
And though a tenth remains in it, it will be burned again; like the terebinth and the oak, whose stump remains when they are felled, so the holy seed is its stump.”

In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram marched up to wage war against Jerusalem, yet neither he nor Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, could prevail against it.
When the house of David was told, “Aram has allied itself with Ephraim,” the hearts of Ahaz and his people trembled like forest trees before the wind.
Then the LORD said to Isaiah, “Go out now, you and your son Shear-jashub, to meet Ahaz at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, on the road to the Fuller’s Field,

and say to him, ‘Be careful, keep calm, do not be afraid, and do not let your heart grow faint because of these two smoldering stubs of firebrands—in the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram and the son of Remaliah.
For Aram, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah have plotted evil against you, saying,
“Let us march up against Judah, throw it into panic, divide it among ourselves, and install the son of Tabeel as king in its midst.”
Thus says the Lord the LORD: “It shall not stand, nor shall it come to pass.
For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered so that it is no longer a people.
The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not believe, you will not be established.”’”
The LORD spoke again to Ahaz, saying,
“Ask a sign for yourself from the LORD your God; make it as deep as Sheol or as high as the heavens above.”
But Ahaz said, “I will not ask, and I will not put the LORD to the test.”
Then Isaiah said, “Hear now, O house of David: Is it too little for you to weary people, that you should weary my God as well?
Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign: Behold, the virgin will conceive and bear a son, and she will call His name Immanuel.
He will eat curds and honey until He knows to refuse the evil and choose the good.
For before the boy knows to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land of the two kings you dread will be abandoned.”
The LORD will bring upon you and upon your people and upon your father’s house days that have not come since the day Ephraim departed from Judah—the king of Assyria.
In that day the LORD will whistle for the fly that is at the end of the rivers of Egypt and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
And they will all come and settle in the steep ravines, in the clefts of the rocks, and on all thorn bushes and in all pastures.
In that day the Lord will shave with a razor hired from beyond the River—with the king of Assyria—the head, the hair of the legs, and the beard.
In that day a man will keep alive a young cow and two sheep.
And because of the abundance of milk they give, he will eat curds; for all who remain in the land will eat curds and honey.
In that day every place where there were a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels of silver will become briers and thorns.
Men will go there with bow and arrow, because all the land will be briers and thorns.
And as for all the hills that were hoed with a hoe, you will not go there for fear of briers and thorns; but they will become a place where oxen are turned loose and sheep trample.
The LORD said to me, “Take a large scroll and write on it with an ordinary stylus, ‘Swift to the spoil, speedy to the plunder.’”
I had reliable witnesses attest for me—Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah.
Then I approached the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. The LORD said to me, “Name him Swift to the Spoil, Speedy to the Plunder.”
For before the boy can say “My father” or “My mother,” the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried off to the king of Assyria.
The LORD spoke to me again, saying:
“Because this people has rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah and exults in Rezin and the son of Remaliah,
therefore the Lord is about to bring against them the mighty floodwaters of the Euphrates—the king of Assyria with all his glory. It will overflow its channels and run over all its banks.
It will sweep through Judah, flooding and passing over until it reaches the neck; its outstretched wings will cover the full breadth of your land, O Immanuel.”
Be shattered, O peoples, and be dismayed; give ear, all you distant lands. Arm yourselves and be dismayed; arm yourselves and be dismayed.
Devise a plan, but it will be thwarted; propose a word, but it will not stand, for God is with us.
For the the LORD spoke to me with a strong hand and warned me not to follow the way of this people, saying,
“Do not say, ‘A conspiracy,’ concerning everything this people calls a conspiracy, and do not fear what they fear, nor be in dread of it.
The LORD of Hosts—Him you shall sanctify; He shall be your fear, and He shall be your dread.
He will be a sanctuary, but to both houses of Israel a stone to stumble over and a rock to trip upon, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem a trap and a snare.
Many will stumble over them; they will fall and be broken; they will be ensnared and captured.”
Bind up the testimony and seal the law among my disciples.
I will wait for the the LORD, who hides His face from the house of Jacob, and I will hope in Him.
Here I am, and the children the the LORD has given me, as signs and wonders in Israel from the the LORD of Hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.
When they say to you, “Inquire of the mediums and the spiritists who whisper and mutter,” should not a people inquire of their God? Should they consult the dead on behalf of the living?
To the law and to the testimony! If they do not speak in accordance with this word, there is no dawn for them.
They will pass through the land distressed and hungry; and when they are hungry, they will be enraged and will curse their king and their God and look upward.
Then they will look to the earth and see only distress and darkness, the gloom of anguish; and they will be thrust into thick darkness.

For there shall be no gloom for her who was in anguish: as in the former time He brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, so in the latter time He has glorified the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
The people who walk in darkness have seen a great light; upon those dwelling in the land of deep darkness, a light has dawned.
You have multiplied the nation, yet You have not magnified its joy; they rejoice before You as with the joy of harvest, as men exult when dividing plunder.
For, as in the day of Midian’s defeat, You have shattered the yoke that burdened them, the bar upon their shoulders, and the rod of their oppressor.
For every boot that tramples in the tumult of battle, and every garment rolled in blood, shall be consigned to the fire as fuel.
For to us a child is born, to us a son is given; and the government will be upon His shoulder, and His name shall be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

Of the increase of His government and of peace there shall be no end; upon the throne of David and over his kingdom He shall reign, to establish and uphold it with justice and with righteousness from this time forth and forevermore. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this.
The Lord has dispatched a word against Jacob, and it has fallen upon Israel.
All the people shall know it—Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria—who in pride and in the arrogance of heart say:
“The bricks have fallen, yet we shall rebuild with dressed stone; the sycamores have been felled, yet we shall replace them with cedars.”
Therefore the LORD has raised up the adversaries of Rezin against him and incited his enemies.
Arameans from the east and Philistines from the west have devoured Israel with open mouth. Yet for all this His anger is not turned away, and His hand is still upraised.
But the people did not turn back to Him who struck them, nor did they seek the LORD of Hosts.
Therefore the LORD will cut off from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed, in a single day.
The head is the elder and the honored man; the tail is the prophet who teaches falsehood.
For the leaders of this people lead them astray, and those who are led by them are swallowed up.

Therefore the Lord will take no delight in their young men, and will show no compassion to their fatherless and widows; for everyone is profane and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks folly. Yet for all this His anger is not turned away, and His hand is still upraised.
For wickedness burns like a fire consuming thorns and briers; it kindles the thickets of the forest, so that they roll upward in a column of smoke.
By the wrath of the LORD of Hosts the land is scorched, and the people become fuel for the fire; no one spares his brother.
They snatch on the right, yet are still hungry; they devour on the left, yet are not satisfied; each devours his own kindred.
Manasseh devours Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh; together they turn against Judah. Yet for all this His anger is not turned away, and His hand is still upraised.
Woe to those who legislate iniquity, and to the scribes who codify oppression—
who turn aside the needy from justice and despoil the poor of My people of their rightful claim, so that widows become their spoil and orphans are plundered.
What, then, will you do on the day of reckoning, when devastation arrives from afar? To whom will you flee for succor, and where will you abandon your glory?
Nothing remains but to crouch among the captives or fall among the slain. Yet for all this His anger is not turned away, and His hand remains outstretched.
Woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger; the staff in their hand is My indignation.
I send him against a godless nation; I commission him against a people destined for My wrath, to seize loot and snatch plunder, and to trample them like clay in the streets.
Yet this is not his purpose, nor does he so intend; rather, it is in his heart to annihilate and to cut off many nations.
“Are not my commanders all kings?” he says.
“Is not Calno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria like Damascus?
As my hand has seized the kingdoms of the idols—whose graven images surpassed those of Jerusalem and Samaria—
shall I not do to Jerusalem and its idols as I have done to Samaria and its idols?”
When the Lord has completed all His work against Mount Zion and Jerusalem, He will punish the king of Assyria for the fruit of his arrogant heart and the glory of his haughty eyes.

For he says: “By the strength of my hand I have accomplished this, and by my wisdom, for I am discerning. I have removed the boundaries of nations and plundered their treasures; and, like a mighty one, I have brought down their inhabitants.
My hand has found, as a nest, the wealth of the peoples; and as one gathers forsaken eggs, I have gathered all the earth. There was none that moved a wing, opened its mouth, or chirped.”
Does the axe boast against the one who cuts with it? Does the saw magnify itself against the one who wields it? As if a rod could wield him who lifts it! As if a staff could lift him who is not wood!
Therefore the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, will send a wasting disease among his stalwart warriors; and beneath his glory a fire will be kindled like a blazing flame.
And the Light of Israel will be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame; and it will burn and consume his thorns and briers in a single day.
The glory of his forest and his fruitful field—He will consume both soul and body; and it will be as when a sick man wastes away.
The rest of the trees of his forest will be so few that a child could write them down.
In that day the remnant of Israel and the survivors of the house of Jacob will no longer depend on the one who struck them, but will truly depend on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
A remnant will return, the remnant of Jacob, to the Mighty God.
For though your people, O Israel, be as the sand of the sea, only a remnant will return. Destruction is decreed, overflowing with righteousness.
For the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, will carry out the destruction decreed upon the whole earth.
Therefore thus says the Lord, the LORD of Hosts: “O My people who dwell in Zion, do not fear the Assyrian. He will strike you with a rod and lift up his staff against you, as Egypt did.”
For in a very little while My indignation will be spent, and My anger will be turned to their destruction.
And the LORD of Hosts will brandish a scourge against him, as in the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb; and He will raise His staff over the sea, as He did against Egypt.
In that day his burden will be lifted from your shoulder, and his yoke from your neck; the yoke will be broken because of the anointing oil.
He has come to Aiath; he has passed through Migron; at Michmash he stores his supplies.
They have crossed the pass; their lodging is at Geba. Ramah trembles; Gibeah of Saul has fled.
Cry aloud, O daughter of Gallim! Listen, O Laishah! O poor Anathoth!
Madmenah has fled; the inhabitants of Gebim have sought refuge.
This very day he will halt at Nob; he will shake his fist at the mountain of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
Behold, the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, will lop off the boughs with terror; and those tall in stature will be cut down, and the lofty will be humbled.
He will clear the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall by the Mighty One.
A shoot shall spring from the stump of Jesse, and a Branch from his roots shall bear fruit.
The Spirit of the LORD shall rest upon Him: the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and might, the Spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.
His delight shall be in the fear of the LORD; He shall not judge by the sight of His eyes, nor reprove by the hearing of His ears.

But with righteousness He shall judge the poor, and with equity He shall decide for the meek of the earth; He shall smite the earth with the rod of His mouth, and with the breath of His lips He shall slay the wicked.
Righteousness shall be the belt about His hips, and faithfulness the sash about His waist.
The wolf shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the young goat; the calf, the young lion, and the fatling shall be together, and a little child shall lead them.
The cow and the bear shall graze; their young shall lie down together; and the lion shall eat straw like the ox.
The nursing child shall play over the hole of the cobra, and the weaned child shall put his hand upon the adder’s den.
They shall not hurt nor destroy in all My holy mountain, for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.
In that day the Root of Jesse shall stand as a banner for the peoples; to Him the nations shall seek, and His resting place shall be glorious.

In that day the Lord shall extend His hand a second time to recover the remnant of His people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the coastlands of the sea.
He shall raise a banner for the nations, and shall gather the outcasts of Israel, and assemble the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
The jealousy of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off; Ephraim shall not be jealous of Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.

They shall swoop down upon the slopes of the Philistines in the west, and together they shall plunder the sons of the east; they shall lay their hand upon Edom and Moab, and the Ammonites shall obey them.
The LORD shall devote to destruction the gulf of the Egyptian Sea, and shall wave His hand over the River with His scorching wind, and strike it into seven streams, and make men traverse it dry-shod.
And there shall be a highway for the remnant of His people who remain from Assyria, as there was for Israel when he came up from the land of Egypt.
In that day you will say, “O the LORD, I will give thanks to You, for though You were angry with me, Your anger has turned away, and You comfort me.
Surely God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid, for Yah the LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation.”
With joy you will draw water from the springs of salvation.
In that day you will say, “Give thanks to the the LORD, call upon His name; make known His deeds among the nations; proclaim that His name is exalted.”
Sing to the the LORD, for He has done glorious things; let this be known in all the earth.
Cry out and shout, O inhabitant of Zion, for great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel.
An oracle concerning Babylon, which Isaiah son of Amoz beheld.
Raise a banner upon the barren height; call aloud to them; wave your hand, that they may enter the gates of the nobles.
I have commanded My consecrated ones; I have likewise summoned My warriors to execute My wrath—those who exult in My majesty.
A tumult resounds upon the mountains, like that of a great multitude; an uproar among the kingdoms, like nations assembled together. The LORD of Hosts is mustering a host for war.
They come from a distant land, from the ends of heaven—the the LORD and the instruments of His wrath—to devastate the whole earth.
Wail, for the day of the the LORD is near; it comes as devastation from the Almighty.
Therefore every hand will grow feeble, and every human heart will melt away.
They will be seized with terror; pangs and anguish will grip them. They will writhe like a woman in labor, staring at one another in astonishment, their faces aflame.
Behold, the day of the the LORD comes—cruel, with wrath and fierce anger—to render the earth a desolation and to exterminate its sinners from it.
For the stars of heaven and their constellations will not give their light; the sun will be darkened as it rises, and the moon will not shed its light.
I will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their iniquity; I will bring to an end the arrogance of the proud and abase the haughtiness of the ruthless.
I will make mortals rarer than pure gold, and humankind rarer than the gold of Ophir.
Therefore I will shake the heavens, and the earth will be displaced from its place, because of the wrath of the the LORD of Hosts and the day of His fierce anger.
And it will be as with a hunted gazelle, or as sheep without a shepherd: each will turn to his own people, and each will flee to his own land.
Everyone who is found will be pierced; everyone who is captured will fall by the sword.
Their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes; their houses will be plundered, and their wives will be ravished.
Behold, I am stirring up the Medes against them—men who have no regard for silver and no delight in gold.
Their bows will dash the young men to pieces; they will show no mercy to the fruit of the womb, and their eyes will not pity the children.
Babylon, the jewel of kingdoms, the glory and pride of the Chaldeans, will be overthrown by God like Sodom and Gomorrah.
It will never be inhabited or settled from generation to generation; no Arab will pitch his tent there, and no shepherd will make his flock lie down there.
But desert creatures will lie down there, and their houses will be full of owls; ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will frolic there.
Hyenas will howl in their citadels, and jackals in their luxurious palaces. Her time is near, and her days will not be prolonged.
For the LORD will have compassion on Jacob and will choose Israel again; He will settle them upon their own land, and the foreigner will join them and attach himself to the house of Jacob.

The nations will conduct them and restore them to their homeland, and the house of Israel will possess them as bondmen and bondwomen in the land of the LORD; they will take captive their former captors and exercise dominion over their oppressors.
On the day the LORD gives you rest from your pain and turmoil and from the hard service imposed upon you,
you will take up this taunt against the king of Babylon and say, "How the oppressor has ceased! How the golden city has ceased!"
The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of rulers,
who smote the peoples in fury with incessant blows and subjugated the nations in wrath without relenting.
The whole earth reposes in tranquility; it bursts into song.
Even the cypresses and the cedars of Lebanon exult over you, saying, "Since you were laid low, no woodcutter has ascended against us."
Sheol beneath is agog to receive you at your coming; it rouses the shades to welcome you, even all the chieftains of the earth, and makes all the kings of the nations rise from their thrones.
They all answer you: "You also have been enfeebled as we are; you have been made like us."
Your pomp is brought down to Sheol, together with the music of your lyres; maggots are spread beneath you, and worms envelop you.
How you have fallen from heaven, O Day Star, son of Dawn! How you have been hewn down to the earth, you who prostrated the nations!
You said in your heart, "I will ascend to heaven; I will exalt my throne above the stars of God; I will sit upon the mount of assembly in the uttermost north.
I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will make myself comparable to the Most High."
Yet you are brought down to Sheol, to the uttermost depths of the pit.
Those who behold you gaze upon you and scrutinize you: "Is this the man who made the earth tremble, who shook kingdoms,
who rendered the world a wasteland and demolished its cities, who would not release his captives to their homes?"
All the kings of the nations repose in glory, each in his own sepulcher.
But you are cast forth from your grave like a despised shoot, clothed with the slain, those pierced by the sword, who descend to the stones of the pit, like a trampled corpse.
You will not be united with them in burial, because you have laid waste your land and massacred your people. The seed of evildoers will never be named.
Prepare a place of slaughter for his sons on account of the iniquity of their fathers; they shall never arise and take possession of the land or populate the face of the world with cities.
"I will rise against them," declares the LORD of Hosts. "I will cut off from Babylon name and remnant, progeny and posterity," declares the LORD.
"I will make it an inheritance of hedgehogs and marshes of water, and I will sweep it with the broom of destruction," declares the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD of Hosts has sworn: "Surely, as I have devised, so shall it come to pass; and as I have purposed, so shall it stand.
I will shatter Assyria in My land; I will tread him underfoot upon My mountains. His yoke shall be removed from their shoulders, and his burden from their backs."
This is the counsel devised for the whole earth, and this is the hand stretched forth over all the nations.
For the LORD of Hosts has counseled, and who shall frustrate it? His hand is stretched out, and who shall turn it back?"
In the year of King Ahaz's demise, this oracle was delivered:
"Rejoice not, all you Philistia, that the rod which smote you is broken, for from the root of the serpent shall come forth a viper, and its offspring shall be a flying serpent.
The firstborn of the poor shall pasture, and the needy shall lie down in safety; but I will slay your root with famine, and your remnant I will put to death.
Wail, O gate; cry out, O city; dissolve in terror, all you Philistia; for smoke comes from the north, and there is no straggler in his ranks."
What answer, then, will be given to the messengers of the nation? "The LORD has founded Zion, and in her His afflicted people shall find refuge."
A prophetic oracle concerning Moab: in a single night Ar of Moab is devastated and brought to silence, and in a single night Kir of Moab is devastated and brought to silence.
Dibon ascends to its sanctuary, to the high places, to weep; Moab wails over Nebo and over Medeba; upon all its heads there is baldness, and every beard is shorn.
In its streets they gird themselves with sackcloth; upon its rooftops and in its broad plazas everyone wails, descending in tears.
Heshbon and Elealeh cry aloud; their voice is heard as far as Jahaz; therefore the armed men of Moab shout, and his soul quails within him.
My heart cries out for Moab; her fugitives flee to Zoar and to Eglath-shelishiyah. For along the ascent of Luhith they go up weeping, and along the road to Horonaim they raise a cry of ruin.
For the waters of Nimrim shall be turned to desolation; for the grass has withered, the verdure has perished, and no green thing remains.
Therefore they carry away the abundance they have gained, together with their hoarded stores, over the Brook of the Willows.
For the cry has encircled the border of Moab; its wailing reaches Eglaim, and its wailing reaches Beer-elim.
For the waters of Dimon are full of blood; for I will bring upon Dimon even more—a lion upon the remnant of Moab and upon the survivors of the land.
Dispatch a lamb to the sovereign of the land, from Sela in the wilderness, to the mountain of the daughter of Zion.
Like a fluttering bird driven from its nest, the daughters of Moab shall linger at the fords of the Arnon.
Bring counsel, execute judgment; let your shadow be as night at noonday; conceal the outcasts, and do not betray the fugitive.
Let My outcasts dwell with you; be a refuge for Moab from the destroyer, for the oppressor has ceased, devastation is ended, and the trampler has vanished from the land.
In steadfast love a throne shall be established, and one shall sit upon it in truth in the tent of David, judging and seeking justice, swift in righteousness.
We have heard of Moab’s pride—how exceedingly proud he is—of his haughtiness, his arrogance, and his wrath; yet his boasting is empty.
Therefore Moab shall wail, yea, all Moab shall wail; for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth they shall mourn, utterly stricken.

For the fields of Heshbon languish, and the vine of Sibmah; the rulers of the nations have struck down its choice vines, which reached as far as Jazer and strayed into the desert; its shoots spread abroad and passed over the sea.
Therefore I weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah; I water you with my tears, O Heshbon and Elealeh, for upon your summer fruits and your harvest the shout of joy has fallen.
Joy and gladness are taken from the fruitful field; in the vineyards there is no singing, no shouting; the treader treads out no wine in the presses, for I have caused the vintage shout to cease.
Therefore my inward parts sound like a harp for Moab, and my soul for Kir-hareseth.
And when Moab appears upon the high place, weary, and comes to his sanctuary to pray, he shall not prevail.
This is the word that the LORD spoke concerning Moab from of old.
But now the LORD says: Within three years, as the years of a hired worker, the glory of Moab shall be despised, together with all his great multitude; and the remnant shall be very small and feeble.
An oracle concerning Damascus: Behold, Damascus shall be divested of its civic standing and reduced to a heap of ruins.
The cities of Aroer shall be abandoned, becoming sheepfolds where flocks repose untroubled by any terror.
The fortress shall vanish from Ephraim, and sovereignty from Damascus, together with the remnant of Aram; they shall become like the glory of the children of Israel, declares the LORD of Hosts.
In that day the glory of Jacob shall be brought low, and the fatness of his flesh shall waste away.
It shall be as when a reaper gathers the standing grain and his arm harvests the ears; yes, as when one gleans ears in the Valley of Rephaim.

Yet gleanings shall remain in it, as when an olive tree is beaten—two or three berries upon the summit of the uppermost bough, four or five upon its fruitful branches—declares the LORD, the God of Israel.
In that day a person shall look to his Maker, and his eyes shall regard the Holy One of Israel.
He shall not look to the altars, the work of his hands, nor regard what his fingers have fashioned—neither the Asherah poles nor the incense altars.
In that day his fortified cities shall resemble the abandoned thickets and lofty summits that were forsaken before the children of Israel, and desolation shall prevail.
For you have forgotten the God of your salvation and have not remembered the Rock of your stronghold; therefore you plant pleasant plants and sow the shoot of a stranger.
On the day you plant it, it shall flourish, and in the morning your seed shall blossom; yet the harvest shall be a heap of ruin in the day of sickness and incurable pain.
Woe to the multitude of many peoples, who roar like the roaring of the seas, and to the rushing of nations, which rush like the rushing of mighty waters!

The nations shall rush like the rushing of many waters; but He shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far away, chased like chaff upon the mountains before the wind, and like a rolling thistle before a gale.
At evening, behold, sudden terror; before morning, they are no more. This is the portion of our plunderers and the lot of our robbers.
Woe to the land of whirring wings, which lies beyond the rivers of Cush.

It sends envoys by sea in vessels of papyrus upon the waters. Go, swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth-skinned, to a people feared from near and far, a nation mighty and trampling, whose land the rivers divide.
All you inhabitants of the world, you who dwell on the earth, when a banner is raised on the mountains, you will see it; when a trumpet sounds, you will hear it.
For thus the LORD said to me: "I will be still and watch from My dwelling place, like shimmering heat in the sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest."
For before the harvest, when the blossom is spent and the flower has become a ripening grape, He will cut off the shoots with pruning hooks and remove the spreading branches.
Together the mountains will be left to the birds of prey and to the beasts of the earth; the birds of prey will summer upon it, and all the beasts of the earth will winter upon it.

At that time a gift will be brought to the LORD of Hosts from a people tall and smooth-skinned, from a people feared from near and far, a nation mighty and trampling, whose land the rivers divide—to Mount Zion, the place of the Name of the LORD of Hosts.
An oracle concerning Egypt: Behold, the LORD rides upon a swift cloud and comes to Egypt; the idols of Egypt tremble before Him, and the heart of Egypt melts within it.
I will incite Egyptian against Egyptian—brother against brother, neighbor against neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
The spirit of the Egyptians will be drained from within them; I will confound their counsel, and they will consult idols, spirits of the dead, mediums, and spiritists.
I will deliver Egypt into the hand of a cruel master, and a fierce king will rule over them, declares the Lord, the LORD of Hosts.
The waters of the sea will dry up, and the river will be parched and desiccated.
The canals will grow fetid; the streams of Egypt will dwindle and run dry, and the reeds and rushes will wither.
The papyrus beside the Nile, at the mouth of the Nile, and every sown field along the Nile, will wither, be driven away, and cease to be.
The fishermen will mourn, and all who cast a hook into the Nile will lament; those who spread nets upon the waters will languish.
The workers in flax will be dismayed, and the weavers of fine linen will turn pale.
Her foundations will be crushed, and all who labor for wages will be grieved.
The princes of Zoan are fools, and Pharaoh's wise counselors proffer witless advice. How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am a son of the wise, a son of ancient kings"?
Where are your wise men now? Let them tell you and disclose what the LORD of Hosts has planned against Egypt.
The princes of Zoan have become fools; the princes of Memphis are deceived, and the leaders of her tribes have led Egypt astray.
The LORD has poured out upon her a spirit of confusion, so that they have made Egypt stagger in all her undertakings, as a drunkard staggers in his own vomit.
There will be nothing Egypt can accomplish—neither by its leaders nor by its common people, neither by the strong nor by the weak.
In that day the Egyptians will be overcome by fearful helplessness; they will tremble and be terrified before the uplifted hand of the LORD of Hosts, which He brandishes over them.
The land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt; everyone who mentions it will be afraid, because of the plan that the LORD of Hosts has devised against them.
In that day five cities in the land of Egypt will speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the LORD of Hosts; one will be called the City of Destruction.
In that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the heart of Egypt, and a monument to the LORD near its border.
It will be a sign and witness to the LORD of Hosts in the land of Egypt; when they cry out to the LORD because of their oppressors, He will send them a Savior and Defender, and He will rescue them.
The LORD will make Himself known to Egypt, and in that day the Egyptians will acknowledge the LORD. They will worship with sacrifices and offerings; they will make vows to the LORD and fulfill them.
The LORD will strike Egypt with a plague; He will strike and heal. They will turn to the LORD, and He will respond to their pleas and heal them.
In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria. The Assyrians will go to Egypt, and the Egyptians to Assyria, and the Egyptians and Assyrians will worship together.
In that day Israel will be the third, along with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the earth.
The LORD of Hosts will bless them, saying, "Blessed be Egypt My people, Assyria My handiwork, and Israel My inheritance."
In the year that the commander-in-chief, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, came to Ashdod, fought against it, and captured it,
at that time the LORD spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz, saying, “Go, remove the sackcloth from your waist and take your sandals off your feet.” So he did, walking about naked and barefoot.
