Then the LORD said, “Just as My servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and portent against Egypt and Cush,
so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Cush, young and old, naked and barefoot, with their buttocks bared—to Egypt’s shame.
Those who made Cush their hope and Egypt their boast will be dismayed and ashamed.”
And on that day the inhabitants of this coastland will say, “See, such is our hope, to which we fled for help to be delivered from the king of Assyria! And how can we escape?”
The oracle concerning the wilderness of the sea: as whirlwinds sweep through the Negev, so it advances from the wilderness, from a land of terror.
A stern vision has been declared to me: the traitor continues to betray, and the devastator continues to devastate. Ascend, O Elam; besiege, O Media; I have brought to an end all her sighing.
Therefore my loins are filled with anguish; pangs have seized me, like the pangs of a woman in travail. I am so bowed down that I cannot hear; I am so dismayed that I cannot see.
My heart reels; horror has appalled me; the twilight I longed for has been transformed for me into trembling.
They lay the table, they spread the carpets, they eat, they drink. Arise, you princes, anoint the shield!
For thus the Lord said to me: "Go, station a watchman; let him announce what he sees.
When he sees riders, horsemen in pairs, riders on donkeys, riders on camels, let him listen with the utmost vigilance."
Then the watchman cried out, "Upon a watchtower I stand, O Lord, continually by day, and at my post I am stationed throughout the nights.
And behold, here comes a chariot of men, horsemen in pairs!" And he answered, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon, and all the carved images of her gods He has shattered to the ground."
O my threshed and winnowed one, what I have heard from the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, I announce to you.
The oracle concerning Dumah: someone calls to me from Seir, "Watchman, what hour of the night? Watchman, what hour of the night?"
The watchman replies, "Morning comes, and yet night follows. If you will inquire, then inquire; return once more."
The oracle concerning Arabia: in the thickets of Arabia you will lodge, O caravans of the Dedanites.
To the thirsty bring water; meet the fugitive with bread, O inhabitants of the land of Tema.
For they have fled from the swords, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, and from the crush of battle.
For thus the Lord said to me, "Within a year, according to the years of a hired worker, all the glory of Kedar will come to an end.
And the remainder of the number of the archers, the mighty men of the sons of Kedar, will be few, for the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken."
An oracle concerning the Valley of Vision: What ails you now, that you have all gone up to the rooftops?
O city full of shouting, tumultuous city, exultant town! Your slain are not slain by the sword, nor did they die in battle.
All your leaders fled together; they were captured without a bow being drawn; all who were found in you were bound together, though they had fled from afar.
Therefore I said, "Turn away from me, that I may weep bitterly; do not press me to be comforted over the ruin of the daughter of my people."
For the Lord, the LORD of Hosts has a day of tumult and trampling and confusion in the Valley of Vision—a breaking down of walls and a crying out to the mountain.
Elam took up the quiver, with chariots of men and horsemen, and Kir laid bare the shield.
Your choicest valleys were filled with chariots, and the horsemen stationed themselves at the gate.
He uncovered the defenses of Judah; and you looked that day to the weapons of the House of the Forest.
You have seen the breaches of the City of David, that they are many; and you gathered the waters of the lower pool.
You counted the houses of Jerusalem and tore down houses to fortify the wall.
You made a reservoir between the two walls for the waters of the old pool, but you did not look to its Maker, nor did you regard Him who fashioned it long ago.
In that day the Lord, the LORD of Hosts called for weeping and mourning, for baldness and for putting on sackcloth.
But behold, joy and gladness, slaughtering cattle and killing sheep, eating meat and drinking wine: "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die."
And it was revealed in my ears by the LORD of Hosts: "Surely this iniquity will not be atoned for you until you die," says the Lord, the LORD of Hosts.
Thus says the Lord, the LORD of Hosts: "Go to this steward, to Shebna, who is in charge of the household, and say,
"What have you here, and whom have you here, that you have hewn out a tomb for yourself here, hewing your tomb on high and carving a dwelling for yourself in the rock?
"Behold, the LORD will hurl you away violently, and will surely cover you.
"He will surely roll you up like a ball and throw you into a vast land; there you shall die, and there shall be the chariots of your glory, the shame of your lord's house.
"I will thrust you from your post, and from your office he will pull you down.
"And it shall come to pass on that day that I will call My servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
"I will clothe him with your robe and bind him with your sash; I will commit your authority into his hand. He will be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
"I will place on his shoulder the key of the house of David; what he opens, no one will shut, and what he shuts, no one will open.
"I will fasten him like a peg in a secure place, and he will be a throne of honor to his father's house.
"They will hang on him all the glory of his father's house—offspring and issue, all the small vessels, from bowls to every kind of jar.
"On that day, declares the LORD of Hosts, the peg fastened in the secure place will be removed and cut down and fall, and the burden hanging on it will be cut off; for the LORD has spoken."
The oracle concerning Tyre: Lament, O ships of Tarshish, for Tyre is devastated, bereft of dwelling and haven; from the land of Cyprus this is disclosed to them.
Be silent, O inhabitants of the coastland; you merchants of Sidon, whose traders have traversed the sea and enriched you.
By mighty waters the grain of the Shihor, the harvest of the Nile, was her revenue, and she became the emporium of the nations.
Be put to shame, O Sidon, fortress of the sea, for the sea itself has declared: "I have not travailed, nor brought forth children; I have not reared young men, nor nurtured maidens."
When the tidings reach Egypt, they will be seized with anguish at the tidings of Tyre.
Pass over to Tarshish; howl, O inhabitants of the coastland.
Is this your exultant city, whose antiquity extends to the days of old, whose own feet bore her to sojourn afar?
Who has devised this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose merchants are princes, whose traders are the honored of the earth?
The LORD of Hosts has purposed it, to profane all prideful glory, to abase all the honored of the earth.
Overflow your land like the Nile, O Daughter of Tarshish; there is no longer any restraint.
He stretched out His hand over the sea; He agitated the kingdoms. The LORD has issued a decree concerning Canaan to demolish its strongholds.
And He said, "You shall exult no more, O oppressed Virgin Daughter of Sidon. Arise, pass over to Cyprus; even there you shall find no repose."
Behold the land of the Chaldeans—this people is no more; Assyria destined it for the beasts of the desert. They erected their siege towers; they dismantled its palaces; they reduced it to ruin.
Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for your stronghold is devastated.
In that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years—the lifetime of a single king. Then, at the end of seventy years, it will befall Tyre as in the song of the prostitute:
"Take a harp, go about the city, O forgotten prostitute; play skillfully, sing a multitude of songs, that you may be remembered."
And at the end of seventy years, the LORD will visit Tyre. Then she will return to her hire and will prostitute herself with all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth.

Yet her profits and her earnings will be consecrated to the LORD; they will not be treasured up or hoarded, but her profits will belong to those who dwell before the LORD, to provide abundant food and fine clothing.
Behold, the LORD desolates the earth and renders it a waste; He distorts its countenance and disperses its inhabitants.

It shall be as with the people, so with the priest; as with the servant, so with his master; as with the maidservant, so with her mistress; as with the purchaser, so with the vendor; as with the lender, so with the borrower; as with the creditor, so with the debtor.
The earth shall be utterly emptied and utterly despoiled, for the LORD has uttered this word.
The earth mourns and withers; the world languishes and fades; the exalted among the people of the earth languish.
The earth is defiled beneath its inhabitants, because they have transgressed the laws, violated the statute, and shattered the everlasting covenant.
Therefore a curse devours the earth, and its inhabitants are adjudged guilty; hence the inhabitants of the earth are scorched, and few mortals remain.
The new wine mourns, the vine languishes, and all the merry-hearted sigh.
The mirth of tambourines ceases, the clamor of the revelers is stilled, and the joy of the lyre ceases.
They drink no wine with song; strong drink is bitter to its drinkers.
The city of chaos is shattered; every house is shut up, so that none may enter.
There is an outcry in the streets over wine; all joy has grown dark; the gladness of the earth is exiled.
Desolation remains in the city, and the gate is smitten with ruin.
For thus it shall be in the midst of the earth among the peoples: as the shaking of an olive tree, as the gleanings when the vintage is ended.
They lift up their voices and sing; from the west they acclaim the majesty of the LORD.
Therefore glorify the LORD in the east; extol the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, in the islands of the sea.

From the end of the earth we have heard songs: “Glory to the Righteous One.” But I said, “I waste away, I waste away! Woe to me! The treacherous deal treacherously; indeed, the treacherous deal most treacherously.”
Terror and pit and snare are upon you, O inhabitant of the earth.

It shall be that he who flees from the sound of terror shall fall into the pit, and he who ascends from the pit shall be ensnared; for the windows of heaven are opened, and the foundations of the earth tremble.
The earth is utterly broken; the earth is split asunder; the earth is shaken violently.
The earth reels like a drunkard and sways like a hut; its transgression lies heavy upon it, and it falls, never to rise again.
It shall be in that day that the LORD will punish the host of heaven in heaven and the kings of the earth on the earth.
They shall be gathered together as prisoners are gathered in a pit and shut up in prison; and after many days they shall be punished.
Then the moon will be confounded and the sun ashamed, for the LORD of Hosts reigns on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before His elders is glory.
O the LORD, You are my God; I will exalt You, and I will praise Your name, for You have wrought wonders—designs ordained from of old in perfect faithfulness.
For You have consigned the city to a heap and the fortified city to ruin; the palace of aliens is a city no more, and it shall never be rebuilt.
Therefore a mighty people will glorify You, and the cities of ruthless nations will revere You.

For You have been a fortress to the poor, a fortress to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm and a shade from the heat; for the breath of the ruthless is like a storm driving against a wall.
Like heat in a desiccated land, You will subdue the tumult of foreigners; like heat stilled beneath a cloud, the song of the ruthless will be silenced.
On this mountain the LORD of Hosts will prepare for all peoples a feast of rich food, a banquet of aged wines—rich food full of marrow, aged wine well refined.
On this mountain He will destroy the shroud that is cast over all peoples and the veil that is spread over all nations.
He will swallow up death forever; and the Lord the LORD will wipe away tears from every face; He will remove the reproach of His people from all the earth, for the LORD has spoken.
In that day it will be said, "Behold, this is our God; we have waited for Him, and He will save us. This is the LORD; we have waited for Him. Let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation."
For the hand of the LORD will rest upon this mountain, while Moab is trampled in its place, as straw is trampled in the waters of a dunghill.
He will spread out his hands in its midst, as a swimmer spreads his hands to swim; yet his pride will be brought low together with the craftiness of his hands.
He will bring down the high fortifications of your walls, lay them low, and cast them to the ground, even to the dust.
In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: “We have a strong city; He sets up salvation as walls and ramparts.
Open the gates, that the righteous nation may enter—the one that keeps faith.
You will keep in perfect peace those whose minds are stayed on You, because they trust in You. “
Trust in the the LORD forever, for the the LORD, even the the LORD Himself, is the Rock of ages.
For He has brought low those who dwell on high; He lays the exalted city low, bringing it down to the ground and casting it into the dust.
Feet trample it—the feet of the poor, the steps of the needy. “
The path of the righteous is level; O Upright One, You make the way of the righteous smooth.
Indeed, in the path of Your judgments, O the LORD, we wait for You; Your name and renown are the desire of our souls.
My soul yearns for You in the night; my spirit within me seeks You earnestly. For when Your judgments are upon the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
Though favor is shown to the wicked, he does not learn righteousness; in a land of uprightness he deals perversely, and does not perceive the majesty of the the LORD.
O the LORD, Your hand is lifted high, yet they do not see it. Let them see Your zeal for Your people and be ashamed; let the fire reserved for Your enemies consume them. “
O the LORD, You will establish peace for us, for You have accomplished all our works for us.
O the LORD our God, other lords besides You have ruled over us, but Your name alone we honor.
The dead shall not live; the departed shall not arise. Therefore You have visited them with destruction and annihilated them, and You have blotted out all remembrance of them.
You have increased the nation, O the LORD; You have increased the nation. You are glorified; You have extended all the borders of the land.
O the LORD, in distress they sought You; they poured out a whispered prayer when Your chastening was upon them.
As a woman with child who draws near to her time of delivery writhes and cries out in her pangs, so were we before You, O the LORD.
We were with child; we writhed in pain, yet we brought forth only wind. We have wrought no deliverance in the earth, and the inhabitants of the world have not fallen.
Your dead shall live; their bodies shall rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust! For Your dew is as the dew of the dawn, and the earth shall cast forth her dead.
Go, My people, enter your chambers and shut your doors behind you; hide yourselves for a little moment until the indignation has passed.

For behold, the the LORD is coming forth from His place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity; the earth will disclose the blood shed upon her, and will no longer cover her slain.”

In that day the LORD will bring judgment upon Leviathan, the fleeing serpent, with His fierce, great, and mighty sword—upon Leviathan, the coiling serpent—and He will slay the dragon that is in the sea.
In that day: “Sing of a delightful vineyard.
I, the LORD, am its keeper; I water it continually. Lest anyone harm it, I guard it night and day.
I have no wrath. If only thorns and briers confronted Me! I would march against them in battle and set them all ablaze together.
Or let them seize My stronghold and make peace with Me—yes, let them make peace with Me.”
In the days to come, Jacob will take root; Israel will bud and blossom and fill the whole world with fruit.
Has He struck them as He struck their strikers? Or have they been slain as their slayers were slain?
By measured exile You contend with her; He drives her away with His fierce blast in the day of the east wind.

Therefore by this Jacob's iniquity will be atoned for, and this is all the fruit of removing his sin: when he makes all the altar stones like pulverized chalk, no Asherah poles or incense altars will remain standing.
For the fortified city is desolate—a forsaken dwelling, abandoned like the wilderness. There the calf grazes; there it lies down and strips its boughs.

When its boughs wither, they are broken; women come and use them for kindling. For this is a people devoid of understanding; therefore their Maker will not pity them, and their Creator will not show them grace.
In that day the LORD will thresh from the River Euphrates to the Brook of Egypt, and you shall be gathered one by one, O sons of Israel.
In that day a great trumpet shall be blown, and those perishing in Assyria and those banished in Egypt shall come and worship the LORD on the holy mountain at Jerusalem.
Alas for the proud diadem of Ephraim—the drunkards whose splendor is withering—and for the fading blossom of its glorious beauty, situated upon the head of the fertile valley, those smitten by wine.
Behold, the Lord has one who is mighty and strong: like a hailstorm of destruction, like a tempest, like a torrent of mighty waters overflowing, He will cast it down to the earth with His hand.
The proud diadem of Ephraim, even its drunkards, shall be trampled underfoot.

And the fading blossom of its glorious beauty, which crowns the head of the fertile valley, shall be like the first-ripe fig before summer: no sooner does one behold it than, while it is still in his hand, he devours it.
In that day the LORD of Hosts will be a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty to the remnant of His people.
and a spirit of justice to him who sits in judgment, and strength to those who repel the assault at the gate.

These also have gone astray through wine and have staggered from strong drink; priest and prophet alike have gone astray through strong drink, have been engulfed by wine, have staggered from strong drink; they have gone astray in vision, they have stumbled in judgment.
For every table is covered with vomit, with filth, so that there is no clean place.
To whom, then, will He impart knowledge, and to whom will He render the message intelligible? To those weaned from milk, to those drawn from the breast.
For it is precept upon precept, precept upon precept, line upon line, line upon line, a little here, a little there.
For by stammering lips and a foreign tongue He will speak to this people.
To whom He said, “This is the rest with which you may give rest to the weary, and this is the repose”—yet they would not listen.

Thus the word of the LORD became to them precept upon precept, precept upon precept, line upon line, line upon line, a little here, a little there, so that they might go and stumble backward, be broken, be snared, and be taken.
Therefore hear the word of the LORD, you scoffers who rule this people in Jerusalem.

For you have said, “We have made a covenant with death, and with Sheol we have made an agreement; when the overflowing scourge passes through, it will not reach us, for we have made lies our refuge, and in falsehood we have hidden ourselves.”
Therefore thus says the Lord, the LORD: “Behold, I am laying in Zion a stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation; he who believes will not be in haste.”
I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the plumb line; hail will sweep away the refuge of lies, and waters will overflow the hiding place.
Your covenant with death will be annulled, and your pact with Sheol will not stand; when the overflowing scourge passes through, you will be trampled underfoot.
As often as it passes through, it will seize you; for morning by morning, by day and by night, it will pass through, and it will be sheer terror to comprehend the message.
For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the covering too narrow to wrap oneself in.
For the LORD will rise up as at Mount Perazim; He will be enraged as in the Valley of Gibeon—to do His work, His strange work, and to perform His task, His alien task.
Now therefore do not mock, lest your bonds be tightened; for I have heard from the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, a decree of utter destruction upon the whole land.
Give ear and hear my voice; listen closely and hear my speech.
Does the plowman plow all day to sow? Does he continually break up and harrow his ground?
When he has leveled its surface, does he not scatter dill and sow cumin, and put wheat in rows, barley in its designated place, and spelt along its border?
For his God instructs him and teaches him the principles of justice.
For dill is not threshed with a threshing sledge, nor is a cartwheel rolled over cumin; rather, dill is beaten out with a stick, and cumin with a rod.
Bread grain is crushed, but not forever; though the wheel of his cart and his horses rumble over it, they do not pulverize it.
This too comes from the LORD of Hosts, who is wonderful in counsel and great in wisdom.
Woe unto Ariel—Ariel, the city of David! Pile year upon year; let the festivals complete their circuits.
Yet I will distress Ariel, and there shall be mourning and lamentation, and she shall be unto Me as an altar hearth.
I shall encamp about you in a ring; I shall besiege you with a siege mound and raise fortifications against you.

You shall be brought low; you shall speak from the earth, and your speech shall issue from the dust. Your voice shall be faint, and your speech shall be like a spirit’s muttering from the ground, chirping from the dust.
The throng of your enemies shall be reduced to fine dust, and the horde of the ruthless shall pass like chaff—suddenly, in an instant.
You shall be visited by the LORD of Hosts with thunder and earthquake and great noise, with whirlwind and tempest and the flame of devouring fire.
It shall be as a dream, a night vision: the whole horde of the nations warring against Ariel—all her besiegers, her stronghold, and her oppressors.

As when a hungry man dreams that he is eating, but awakens and his soul is empty; or as when a thirsty man dreams that he is drinking, but awakens and is faint, his soul still craving—so shall be the whole horde of the nations warring against Mount Zion.
Pause and be astonished; blind yourselves and be blind. They are drunk, but not with wine; they reel, but not with strong drink.
For the LORD has poured out upon you a spirit of deep sleep; He has shut your eyes—the prophets—and covered your heads—the seers.
The whole vision has become to you like the words of a sealed book. If it is given to one who can read, saying, “Please read this,” He says, “I cannot, for it is sealed.”
Or if the book is given to one who cannot read, saying, “Please read this,” He says, “I do not know how to read.”

Then the Lord said: “Because this people draws near to Me with its mouth and honors Me with its lips, while its heart is far from Me, and its reverence for Me is but a human commandment learned by rote—
therefore, behold, I shall once more work wonders among this people—wonder upon wonder—and the wisdom of their wise shall perish, and the discernment of their discerning shall be hidden.”
Woe to those who dig deep to hide their counsel from the LORD, whose works are in darkness, and who say, “Who sees us? Who knows us?”
You turn things upside down! Shall the potter be counted as clay, that the thing made should say of its maker, “He did not make me,” Or the thing formed say of its former, “He has no understanding”?
In but a very little while, shall not Lebanon be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field be counted as forest?
In that day the deaf shall hear the words of a book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity and out of darkness.
The humble shall increase their joy in the LORD, and the needy among mankind shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
For the ruthless shall cease, and the scorner shall be consumed, and all who watch for iniquity shall be cut off—
those who make a man guilty for a word, and snare him who rebukes in the gate, and turn aside the righteous with empty charges.
Therefore thus says the LORD, who redeemed Abraham, concerning the house of Jacob: “Jacob shall not now be ashamed, neither shall his face now grow pale.
For when he sees his children, the work of My hands, in his midst, they will sanctify My name; they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob and stand in awe of the God of Israel.
Those who err in spirit shall come to understanding, and those who murmur shall learn instruction.”
Woe to the rebellious children, says the the LORD, who execute a counsel not Mine, and who ratify an alliance not by My Spirit, so as to heap sin upon sin.
They descend to Egypt without consulting My mouth, to take refuge in Pharaoh’s stronghold and to shelter in Egypt’s shadow.
Therefore Pharaoh’s stronghold shall become your ignominy, and the shelter of Egypt’s shadow your disgrace.
For though his princes are at Zoan and his envoys reach Hanes,
all shall be shamed by a people that cannot profit them—bringing neither help nor profit, but shame and reproach.

An oracle concerning the beasts of the Negeb. Through a land of distress and anguish—whence issue the lioness and the lion, the viper and the flying serpent—they bear their wealth upon donkeys’ backs and their treasures upon camels’ humps, to a people that cannot profit them.
Egypt’s help is a vanity and an emptiness; therefore I have called her “Rahab the Do-Nothing.”
And now, go, write it before them on a tablet and inscribe it in a book, that it may stand as a witness for the last day, forevermore.
For they are a rebellious people, mendacious children, children who refuse to hear the instruction of the the LORD.
They say to the seers, “Do not see,” and to the prophets, “Do not prophesy to us what is right; speak to us smooth things, prophesy illusions.
Turn aside from the way, depart from the path; let us hear no more of the Holy One of Israel.”
Therefore thus says the Holy One of Israel: “Because you despise this word and trust in oppression and rely upon perversity,
this iniquity shall be to you like a breach in a high wall, bulging out and collapsing suddenly, in an instant.

Its shattering shall be like the shattering of a potter’s vessel, smashed so ruthlessly that among its fragments no shard is found wherewith to take fire from the hearth or to draw water from the cistern.”
For thus says the Lord, the the LORD, the Holy One of Israel: “In returning and rest you shall be saved; in quietness and in trust shall be your strength. But you refused.
You said, ‘No! We will flee upon horses’—therefore you shall flee! ‘We will ride upon swift steeds’—therefore your pursuers shall be swift.
A thousand shall flee at the rebuke of one; at the rebuke of five you shall flee, until you are left like a mast upon the summit of a mountain and like a signal upon a hill.”
Therefore the the LORD waits to be gracious to you; therefore He will arise to show mercy to you. For the the LORD is a God of justice; blessed are all who wait for Him.
O people in Zion, who dwell in Jerusalem, you will weep no more. He will surely be gracious to you at the sound of your cry; when He hears, He will answer you.
Though the Lord gives you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, your Teacher will no longer hide Himself, and your eyes will see your Teacher.
When you turn to the right and when you turn to the left, your ears will hear a word behind you, saying, “This is the way; walk in it.”
Then you will defile the plating of your silver and the carved images of your gold; you will scatter them like a menstrual cloth, and you will say to them, “Be gone!”
He will give rain for the seed you sow in the ground, and bread from the produce of the ground, and it shall be rich and fat. In that day your cattle will graze in broad pastures.
The oxen and the donkeys that work the soil will eat salted fodder, winnowed with shovel and fork.
On every high mountain and on every high hill there will be brooks and streams of water in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.

Moreover, the light of the moon will be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be sevenfold, like the light of seven days, on the day when the the LORD binds up the brokenness of His people and heals the wounds inflicted by His blow.
Behold, the name of the the LORD comes from afar, burning with His anger, and in thick smoke; His lips are full of indignation, and His tongue is like a devouring fire.
His breath is like an overflowing torrent that reaches to the neck—to sift the nations with the sieve of destruction, and to put a misleading bridle upon the jaws of the peoples.
You shall have a song as in the night when a holy feast is kept, and gladness of heart, as when one goes with a flute to come to the mountain of the the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
The LORD will cause His majestic voice to be heard and the descending blow of His arm to be seen, in furious anger and a flame of devouring fire, with a cloudburst and tempest and hailstones.
The Assyrians will be terrified at the voice of the the LORD, when He strikes with His rod.
And every stroke of the rod of punishment that the the LORD lays upon them will be accompanied by timbrels and lyres; with battles of brandishing He will fight against them.

For Topheth has long been prepared; indeed, for the king it is made ready, its pyre made deep and wide, with fire and wood in abundance; the breath of the the LORD, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it.

Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, who rely on horses, who trust in the abundance of chariots and in the multitude of horsemen. They do not look to the Holy One of Israel; they do not seek the LORD.
Yet He too is wise and brings disaster; He does not retract His words. He will rise up against the house of the wicked and against the helpers of evildoers.

But the Egyptians are mere mortals, not God; their horses are flesh, not spirit. When the LORD stretches out His hand, the helper will stumble, and the one helped will fall; both will perish together.

For thus the LORD has said to me: “As a lion growls, a great lion over its prey—and though a whole band of shepherds is called together against it, it is not terrified by their shouting or daunted by their clamor—so the LORD of Hosts will come down to do battle on Mount Zion and on its heights.”
Like birds hovering overhead, so the LORD of Hosts will protect Jerusalem. He will protect and deliver it; He will pass over and preserve it.
Return to Him from whom you have so deeply revolted, O children of Israel.
For on that day, every one of you will reject the idols of silver and gold that your own hands have sinfully made.
Then Assyria shall fall, but not by the sword of man; a sword not of mortals will devour him. He will flee from the sword, and his young men will be put to forced labor.
His rock will pass away in terror, and his officers will panic at the battle standard,” declares the LORD, “whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.”
Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall govern with justice.
Each shall be like a refuge from the wind and a shelter from the storm, like rivulets of water in an arid land, like the shadow of a massive rock in a land of weariness.
Then the eyes of those who see shall not be dimmed, and the ears of those who hear shall hearken.
The heart of the rash shall attain understanding, and the tongue of the stammerer shall be quick to utter clear speech.
No longer shall the fool be called noble, nor shall the knave be styled a magnate.
For the fool utters folly, and his heart contrives iniquity: to practice hypocrisy, to speak perversity against the the LORD, to empty the soul of the hungry, and to withhold drink from the thirsty.
His implements are malign; he devises stratagems to ruin the meek with false words, even when the needy plead for justice.
But the nobleman devises noble purposes, and he shall stand firm in them.
Rise up, you women who are at ease; hear my voice, you complacent daughters; give ear to my speech.
In little more than a year you complacent women shall tremble, for the vintage shall be consumed and the harvest shall not arrive.
Tremble, you women at ease; strip yourselves bare and gird sackcloth about your loins.
Beat your breasts over the pleasant fields, over the fruitful vine.
Upon the soil of my people shall spring up thorns and briars, even upon all the houses of rejoicing in the exultant city.
For the citadel shall be abandoned, the throng of the city deserted; the mound and the watchtower shall become caves forever, a delight for wild asses, a pasture for flocks.
Until the Spirit is poured upon us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a garden-land, and the garden-land is reckoned a forest.
Then justice shall dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness shall abide in the fertile field.
And the effect of righteousness shall be peace, and the labor of righteousness, quietness and trust forever.
My people shall dwell in a habitation of peace, and in dwellings of security, and in quiet resting places.
When hail descends upon the forest, the city shall be humbled in the lowland.
Blessed are you who sow beside all waters, sending forth the ox and the donkey to roam.

Woe to you, destroyer, though you have not been destroyed; and you, betrayer, though none has betrayed you! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; when you have ceased betraying, they will betray you.
O the LORD, be gracious to us; we have waited for You. Be our arm every morning, our salvation in time of distress.
At the sound of the tumult, peoples fled; at Your exaltation, nations were scattered.
Your spoil is gathered as the caterpillar gathers; as locusts swarm, so they swarm over it.
The LORD is exalted, for He dwells on high; He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
He will be the stability of your times, a wealth of salvation, wisdom and knowledge; the fear of the LORD is His treasure.
Behold, their valiant ones cry aloud in the streets; the envoys of peace weep bitterly.
The highways are desolate; travelers have ceased. The covenant is broken; cities are despised; no regard is shown for man.
The land mourns and languishes; Lebanon is ashamed and withers; Sharon has become like a wilderness; Bashan and Carmel shed their foliage.
“Now I will arise,” says the LORD; “now I will be exalted; now I will be lifted up.”
You conceive chaff; you give birth to stubble; your breath is a fire that consumes you.
Peoples will be burned to lime; thorns cut down will be set ablaze.
Hear, you who are far away, what I have done; and you who are near, acknowledge My might.
Sinners in Zion are terrified; trembling grips the godless: “Who among us can dwell with devouring fire? Who among us can dwell with everlasting burnings?”

He who walks righteously and speaks uprightly, who despises gain from extortion, who shakes his hands free of bribes, who stops his ears from hearing of bloodshed and closes his eyes so as not to see evil—
he will dwell on the heights; his refuge will be the fortresses of rocks; his bread will be given, his water assured.
Your eyes will see the King in His beauty; they will behold a land far away.
Your heart will meditate on terror: “Where is the scribe? Where is the weigher? Where is he who counted the towers?”
You will see no more the insolent people, a people of obscure speech that you cannot comprehend, of a stammering tongue that you cannot understand.

Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed feasts; your eyes will see Jerusalem, a quiet habitation, a tent that will not be removed, whose stakes will never be pulled up, nor will any of its cords be broken.
But there the majestic the LORD will be for us a place of broad rivers and streams, where no galley with oars will go, and no mighty ship will pass.
For the LORD is our Judge, the LORD is our Lawgiver, the LORD is our King; He will save us.
Your cords are slack; they cannot strengthen the mast; they cannot spread the sail. Then abundant spoil will be divided; even the lame will plunder.
And no inhabitant will say, “I am sick”; the people who dwell in it will be forgiven their iniquity.
Draw near, you nations, to hear, and give heed, you peoples! Let the earth hear, together with all that fills it, the world and all its offspring.
For the LORD has indignation against all the nations and fury against all their host; He has devoted them to destruction and delivered them to the slaughter.
Their slain shall be cast out, and the stench of their corpses shall ascend; the mountains shall be drenched with their blood.
All the host of heaven shall waste away, and the skies shall be rolled up like a scroll; all their host shall wither, as a leaf withers from the vine and as one withers from the fig tree.
For My sword has drunk its fill in the heavens; behold, it descends in judgment upon Edom, upon the people whom I have devoted to destruction.

The sword of the LORD is gorged with blood and fattened with fat—from the blood of lambs and goats, from the fat of the kidneys of rams—for the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
Wild oxen shall fall with them, and young bulls with the mighty; their land shall be saturated with blood, and their dust shall be made fat with fat.
For the LORD has a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.
Her streams shall be turned into pitch, and her dust into sulfur; her land shall become burning pitch.
It shall not be quenched night or day; its smoke shall ascend forever. From generation to generation she shall lie desolate; no traveler shall pass through her forever and ever.
The desert owl and the screech owl shall possess her, and the great owl and the raven shall dwell in her. He shall stretch over her the line of desolation and the plumb line of emptiness.
Her nobles—there is no one there to proclaim a kingdom; all her princes shall be nothing.
Thorns shall spring up in her palaces, nettles and thistles in her fortresses; she shall become a haunt for jackals, a courtyard for ostriches.
Desert creatures shall meet with hyenas, and wild goats shall cry out to one another; there too Lilith shall settle and find rest.
There the owl shall nest and lay eggs; she shall hatch them and gather them under her shadow. Indeed, the kites shall gather there, each with its mate.
Search the book of the LORD and read: not one of these shall be missing; none shall lack its mate. For His mouth has commanded it, and His Spirit has gathered them.
He has cast the lot for them, and His hand has divided it among them by line. They shall possess it forever; from generation to generation they shall dwell in it.
The wilderness and the parched land shall exult; the desert shall rejoice and burst into bloom like the crocus.

It shall blossom abundantly and rejoice with exultation and song; the glory of Lebanon shall be conferred upon it, together with the majesty of Carmel and Sharon. They shall behold the glory of the LORD, the majesty of our God.
Strengthen the enfeebled hands, and fortify the tottering knees.
Say to those whose hearts are dismayed, “Take courage; do not be afraid. Behold, your God is coming with vengeance, with divine recompense; He will come and save you.”
Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.
Then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute shall sing for joy. For waters shall burst forth in the wilderness, and streams in the desert.
The burning sand shall become a pool, and the thirsty ground, springs of water; in the haunt of jackals, where they recline, grass shall become reeds and rushes.
A highway shall be there, and it shall be called the Way of Holiness. The unclean shall not traverse it, and it shall be for those who walk the way; even fools shall not stray.
No lion shall be there, nor shall any ravenous beast ascend it; none shall be found there, but the redeemed shall walk there.
And the ransomed of the LORD shall return and come to Zion with singing; everlasting joy shall crown their heads. They shall obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah's reign, Sennacherib, king of Assyria, marched against every fortified city of Judah and captured them.

The Assyrian monarch dispatched the Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah in Jerusalem, accompanied by a formidable host; he took his station beside the conduit of the upper pool, on the road to the Fuller's Field.
Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, went out to meet him.
The Rabshakeh said to them, "Tell Hezekiah, 'Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria: What is this confidence in which you trust?
You say—though it is merely a word of the lips—'I have counsel and strength for war.' Now in whom do you trust, that you have rebelled against me?
Behold, you are relying upon Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff, which, if a man leans upon it, will pierce his hand. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who rely upon him.
But if you say to me, 'We trust in the LORD our God,' is it not He whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, "You shall worship before this altar"?
"Now therefore, strike a bargain with my master, the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to mount riders upon them.
How then could you repel even one captain among the least of my master's servants, when you rely upon Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
Moreover, have I ascended against this land to destroy it apart from the LORD? The LORD said to me, 'Go up against this land and destroy it.'"
Then Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, "Please address your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it; and do not speak to us in Hebrew within earshot of the people on the wall."

But the Rabshakeh replied, "Has my master sent me to speak these words to your master and to you, and not to the men sitting on the wall, who, together with you, will eat their own excrement and drink their own urine?"
Then the Rabshakeh stood and cried out in a loud voice in Hebrew, "Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
Thus says the king: 'Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he will not be able to deliver you;
nor let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD, saying, "The LORD will surely deliver us; this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria."'

"Do not listen to Hezekiah; for thus says the king of Assyria: 'Make peace with me and come out to me; then every one of you shall eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and every one shall drink the water of his own cistern,
until I come and take you away to a land like your own land—a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.'
Beware lest Hezekiah mislead you, saying, 'The LORD will deliver us.' Has any of the gods of the nations delivered his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Have they delivered Samaria from my hand?
Who among all the gods of these lands has delivered his country from my hand, that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem from my hand?"
But they remained silent and did not answer him a word, for the king's command was, "Do not answer him."

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their garments torn, and reported to him the words of the Rabshakeh.
When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his garments, clothed himself in sackcloth, and entered the house of the LORD.
He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, together with Shebna the scribe and the senior priests, all clothed in sackcloth, to Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet.
They said to him, “Thus says Hezekiah: ‘This day is a day of distress, rebuke, and disgrace; for the people have reached the throes of travail, yet possess no strength to bring forth deliverance.

Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of Rabshakeh, whom his master, the king of Assyria, sent to defy the living God, and will rebuke the words that the LORD your God has heard. Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant that remains.’”
So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
Isaiah said to them, “Thus you shall say to your master: “‘Thus says the LORD: Do not be afraid of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed Me.
Behold, I will put a spirit in him, so that he will hear a report and return to his own land; and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.’”
Now when Rabshakeh heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, he withdrew and found him waging war against Libnah.
Then the king heard concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, “He has come out to fight against you,” and, upon hearing it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying:
“Thus says the king of Assyria: Do not let your God in whom you trust deceive you by promising that Jerusalem will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.
Behold, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, devoting them to destruction. And shall you be delivered?
Did the gods of the nations that my fathers destroyed deliver them—Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?”
Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it; then he went up to the house of the LORD and spread it before the LORD.
And Hezekiah prayed to the LORD, saying: “
O the LORD of Hosts, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, You alone are God of all the kingdoms of the earth; You have made heaven and earth.
Incline Your ear, O the LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, O the LORD, and see; and hear all the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to defy the living God.
Truly, O the LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the countries and their lands,
and have cast their gods into the fire; for they were not gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, and so they destroyed them.
Now therefore, O the LORD our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone are the LORD.”
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: “‘Because you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria,
this is the word that the LORD has spoken concerning him: The virgin daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you; the daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind you.
Whom have you reproached and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted up your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel!

By your servants you have reproached the Lord, and you have said, “‘“With my many chariots I have ascended the heights of the mountains, the farthest recesses of Lebanon; I cut down its tallest cedars, its choicest cypresses; I reached its farthest height, its densest forest.
I dug wells and drank waters; with the sole of my feet I dried up all the streams of Egypt.” “‘
Have you not heard? Long ago I ordained it; from days of old I planned it. Now I have brought it to pass, that you should turn fortified cities into heaps of ruins.
Their inhabitants, shorn of strength, are dismayed and put to shame; they are like grass of the field and green herb, like grass on the rooftops and grain blasted before it grows.
But I know your sitting down and your going out and your coming in, and your raging against Me.
Because your raging against Me and your arrogance have come up into My ears, therefore I will put My hook in your nose and My bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way you came.

And this shall be the sign for you: This year you shall eat what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs from that; but in the third year you shall sow and reap, and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
And the surviving remnant of the house of Judah shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward.
For out of Jerusalem shall go a remnant, and out of Mount Zion a band of survivors. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this.
Therefore thus says the LORD concerning the king of Assyria: He shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with a shield, nor cast up a siege mound against it.
By the way that he came, by the same he shall return; and he shall not come into this city, declares the LORD.
For I will defend this city to save it, for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.’”
Then the angel of the LORD went out and struck down 185,000 in the camp of the Assyrians; and when the people arose early in the morning, behold, all of them were dead bodies.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed and returned home and lived at Nineveh.

And as he was worshiping in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer, his sons, struck him down with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.

In those days Hezekiah became sick to the point of death, and Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came to him and said to him, “Thus says the LORD: Set your house in order, for you are dying and will not live.”
Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD.
He said, “O the LORD, remember, I pray, how I have walked before You in truth and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in Your sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah, saying,
“Go and say to Hezekiah, ‘Thus says the LORD, the God of your father David: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add fifteen years to your days.
I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city.’
And this shall be the sign to you from the LORD, that the LORD will do this thing which He has spoken:
Behold, I will make the shadow that has descended on the steps of Ahaz retreat ten steps backward. So the sun’s shadow went back ten steps on the steps by which it had descended.”
A writing of Hezekiah, king of Judah, when he had been sick and recovered from his sickness:
“I said, ‘In the very prime of my days I must enter the gates of Sheol; I am robbed of the remainder of my years.’
I said, ‘I shall not see the LORD in the land of the living; I shall no longer look upon man among the inhabitants of the world.’
My dwelling has been pulled up and removed from me like a shepherd’s tent; I have rolled up my life like a weaver; He cuts me off from the loom; from day to night You make an end of me.
I composed myself until morning; like a lion He breaks all my bones; from day to night You make an end of me.
Like a swallow, like a crane, so I chirp; I moan like a dove; my eyes grow weak as I look to the heights. O Lord, I am oppressed; be my security.
What shall I say? He has spoken to me, and He Himself has done it. I shall walk softly all my years because of the bitterness of my soul.
O Lord, by these things men live, and in all these things is the life of my spirit; You will restore me and make me live.
Behold, for my peace I had great bitterness; but You have, in love for my soul, delivered it from the pit of destruction, for You have cast all my sins behind Your back.
For Sheol cannot thank You, death cannot praise You; those who go down to the pit cannot hope for Your faithfulness.
The living, the living—he praises You, as I do this day; a father makes known Your faithfulness to his children.
The LORD is ready to save me; therefore we will sing my songs with stringed instruments all the days of our life in the house of the LORD.”
Now Isaiah had said, “Let them take a cake of figs and apply it to the boil, and he will recover.”
And Hezekiah had said, “What is the sign that I shall go up to the house of the LORD?”

At that time, Merodach-baladan, son of Baladan and king of Babylon, dispatched envoys bearing letters and a tribute to Hezekiah, having learned that Hezekiah had been afflicted by illness and had subsequently convalesced.

Hezekiah rejoiced at their arrival and exhibited to them his treasury—the silver, the gold, the spices, the precious oil, his entire armory, and every treasure found within his storehouses—so that there was not a single article in his palace or throughout his dominion that Hezekiah did not disclose to them.
Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and inquired, “What did these men say, and whence have they come to you?” Hezekiah replied, “They have come to me from a distant land, from Babylon.”
Isaiah asked further, “What have they seen in your house?” Hezekiah answered, “They have seen everything that is in my house; there was nothing in my treasuries that I did not show them.”
Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the LORD of Hosts:
Behold, days are coming when all that is in your house, together with all that your fathers have stored up until this day, shall be carried away to Babylon; nothing shall be left, says the LORD.
And among your sons who shall issue from you, whom you shall beget, some shall be taken away and shall serve as eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”
Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good.” For he thought, “There will be peace and truth in my days.”
“Comfort, comfort My people,” says your God.
“Speak tenderly to Jerusalem, and cry out to her that her warfare is ended, that her iniquity is pardoned, and that she has received from the hand of the LORD double for all her sins.”
A voice cries out: “In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD; make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”
Every valley shall be lifted up, and every mountain and hill made low; the crooked shall become straight, and the rough places a plain.
Then the glory of the LORD shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together, for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
A voice says, “Cry!” And I asked, “What shall I cry?” “All flesh is grass, and all its splendor is like the flower of the field.
The grass withers, the flower fades when the breath of the LORD blows upon it; surely the people are grass.
The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God will stand forever.”

Go up on a high mountain, O Zion, herald of good tidings; lift up your voice with strength, O Jerusalem, herald of good tidings; lift it up, do not fear; say to the cities of Judah, “Behold, your God!”
Behold, the Lord the LORD comes with might, and His arm rules for Him; behold, His reward is with Him, and His recompense before Him.
He will tend His flock like a shepherd; He will gather the lambs in His arm; He will carry them in His bosom, and gently lead those that are with young.

Who has measured the waters in the hollow of His hand and marked off the heavens with a span, enclosed the dust of the earth in a measure and weighed the mountains in scales and the hills in a balance?
Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD, or as His counselor instructed Him?
Whom did He consult, and who made Him understand? Who taught Him the path of justice, and taught Him knowledge, and showed Him the way of understanding?
Behold, the nations are like a drop from a bucket, and are accounted as the dust on the scales; behold, He takes up the coastlands like fine dust.
Lebanon would not suffice for fuel, nor are its beasts enough for a burnt offering.
All the nations are as nothing before Him; they are accounted by Him as less than nothing and emptiness.
To whom then will you liken God, or what likeness compare with Him?
An idol! A craftsman casts it, and a goldsmith overlays it with gold and casts for it silver chains.
He who is too impoverished for an offering chooses wood that will not rot; he seeks out a skillful craftsman to set up an idol that will not move.
Do you not know? Do you not hear? Has it not been told you from the beginning? Have you not understood from the foundations of the earth?
It is He who sits above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; who stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them like a tent to dwell in;
who brings princes to nothing, and makes the rulers of the earth as emptiness.
Scarcely are they planted, scarcely sown, scarcely has their stem taken root in the earth, when He blows on them, and they wither, and the tempest carries them off like stubble.
“To whom then will you compare Me, that I should be like him?” says the Holy One.

Lift up your eyes on high and see: Who created these? He who brings out their host by number, calling them all by name, by the greatness of His might, and because He is strong in power not one is missing.
Why do you say, O Jacob, and speak, O Israel, “My way is hidden from the LORD, and my justice is disregarded by my God”?
Have you not known? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He does not faint or grow weary; His understanding is unsearchable.
He gives power to the faint, and to him who has no might He increases strength.
Even youths shall faint and be weary, and young men shall stumble and fall;
but those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles; they shall run and not be weary; they shall walk and not faint.
"Be silent before Me, O islands, and let the peoples renew their strength. Let them approach and speak; let us draw near together for judgment.

Who has roused from the east the one whom righteousness summons to His foot? He delivers nations into his hand and tramples kings beneath him; He makes them like dust before his sword, like driven stubble before his bow.
He pursues them and passes on unscathed, by a way his feet have never before trodden.
Who has wrought and accomplished this, summoning the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD—the First and the Last—I am He.
"The islands behold and fear; the ends of the earth tremble. They approach and draw near.
Each helps his neighbor and says to his brother, 'Be strong!'
The artisan encourages the goldsmith; he who smooths with the hammer spurs on him who strikes the anvil. He says of the solder, 'It is good,' and fastens it with nails that it may not be moved."
"But you, Israel, My servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, descendant of Abraham, My friend—
I brought you from the ends of the earth and called you from its remotest corners. I said to you, 'You are My servant.' I have chosen you and have not rejected you.
Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you; indeed, I will help you; indeed, I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.
"Behold, all who rage against you will be ashamed and disgraced; those who contend with you will be brought to nothing and will perish.
You will seek them but will not find them; those who war against you will be as nothing at all.
For I am the LORD your God, who takes hold of your right hand and says to you, 'Do not fear; I will help you.'
"Do not fear, O worm Jacob, O few men of Israel. I will help you," declares the LORD. "Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
"Behold, I will make you a threshing sledge, new and sharp, with many teeth. You will thresh the mountains and crush them, and reduce the hills to chaff.
You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away; the tempest will scatter them. But you will rejoice in the LORD; you will glory in the Holy One of Israel."
"The poor and needy seek water, but there is none; their tongues are parched with thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
I will open rivers on the barren heights, and springs in the midst of the valleys. I will turn the desert into a pool of water, and the arid land into flowing springs.
I will plant in the wilderness cedar, acacia, myrtle, and olive; I will set in the desert cypress, elm, and boxwood together,
so that people may see and know, may consider and understand, that the hand of the LORD has done this and the Holy One of Israel has created it."
"Present your case," says the LORD. "Submit your arguments," says the King of Jacob.
"Let them come and tell us what will happen. Tell us the former things, so that we may consider them and know their outcome. Or declare to us the things to come.
Tell us what the future holds, so that we may know that you are gods. Indeed, do good or evil, that we may be dismayed and filled with dread.
Behold, you are nothing and your works are naught. Whoever chooses you is an abomination.
"I have raised up one from the north, and he has come; from the rising of the sun, one who calls on My name. He will trample rulers as if they were mortar, as a potter treads the clay.
Who has declared this from the beginning, so that we may know, or beforehand, so that we may say, 'He is right'? No one announced it, no one foretold it, no one heard your words.
I was the first to tell Zion, 'Look, here they are!' And I gave to Jerusalem one who brings good news.
I look, but there is no one; among them there is no counselor who, when I ask, can give an answer.
See, they are all a delusion; their works are nothing; their images are but wind and confusion."
Behold My Servant, whom I uphold; My Chosen One, in whom My soul delights. I have placed My Spirit upon Him, and He shall promulgate justice among the nations.
He shall not cry out, nor lift up His voice, nor make Himself heard in the thoroughfares.
A bruised reed He shall not shatter, nor will He extinguish a dimly burning wick; He shall establish justice with fidelity.
He will neither falter nor be crushed until He has established justice upon the earth, and the remotest coastlands shall await His law.” “
Thus says God, the LORD, who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread forth the earth and its offspring, who gives breath to the people upon it and spirit to those who walk therein.
I, the LORD, have summoned You in righteousness; I will grasp Your hand, preserve You, and constitute You as a covenant for the people, a light unto the nations,
to open the eyes of the blind, to liberate captives from confinement, and to bring forth from the dungeon those who dwell in darkness.
I am the LORD; that is My name. My glory I will not yield to another, nor My praise to graven images.
Behold, the former things have come to pass; now I announce new things. Before they spring into being, I proclaim them to you.”
Sing to the LORD a new song; let His praise resound from the ends of the earth—you who descend to the sea and all its fullness, the coastlands and their dwellers.
Let the wilderness and its towns raise their voices; let the settlements of Kedar exult; let the inhabitants of Sela shout for joy; let them cry out from the mountain peaks.
Let them ascribe glory to the LORD and proclaim His praise throughout the coastlands.
The LORD marches forth like a mighty warrior; like a man of war He rouses His zeal. He shouts—indeed, He raises a war cry—and He triumphs over His adversaries. “
Long have I held My peace; I have been still and restrained Myself. But now I will cry out like a woman in travail; I will gasp and pant together.
I will devastate mountains and hills, and wither all their vegetation; I will transform rivers into islands and desiccate the pools.

I will lead the blind along a path they have not known; through unfamiliar paths I will guide them. I will turn darkness into light before them and make the crooked ways level. These things I will accomplish, and I will not abandon them.”
They shall be turned back and utterly put to shame—those who trust in carved images and say to molten idols, “You are our gods.” “
Hear, you deaf; behold, you blind, that you may see.
Who is blind but My Servant, or deaf as My messenger whom I send? Who is blind like the one consecrated to Me, blind like the Servant of the LORD?
You have seen many things, but you have not observed them; your ears are open, yet you do not hear.”
The LORD was pleased, for the sake of His righteousness, to magnify the law and make it glorious.
But this is a people plundered and despoiled; all of them are snared in holes and hidden in prisons. They have become plunder, with no one to rescue them, and spoil, with no one to say, “Restore!”
Who among you will give heed to this, who will attend and hear what is to come?
Who delivered Jacob to the spoiler and Israel to plunderers? Was it not the LORD, against whom we have sinned, in whose ways they refused to walk, and whose law they would not obey?
Therefore He poured out upon him the fury of His anger and the violence of war. It blazed all around him, yet he did not know it; it consumed him, yet he did not lay it to heart.
But now thus says the LORD, He who created you, O Jacob, and He who formed you, O Israel: “Do not be afraid, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by your name; you are Mine.
When you pass through the waters, I will be with you, and through the rivers they shall not overwhelm you; when you walk through fire, you shall not be scorched, and the flame shall not burn you.
For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior; I have given Egypt as your ransom, Cush and Seba in your place.
Because you are precious in My sight, and honored, and I love you, I will give people in your place and nations in exchange for your life.
“Do not be afraid, for I am with you; I will bring your offspring from the east and gather you from the west.
I will say to the north, ‘Give them up,’ and to the south, ‘Do not withhold them.’ Bring My sons from afar and My daughters from the ends of the earth—
everyone who is called by My name, whom I created for My glory, whom I formed and made.”
Bring out the people who are blind, yet have eyes, and the deaf, yet have ears.

Let all the nations be gathered together, and let the peoples be assembled. Who among them can declare this and show us the former things? Let them bring their witnesses to prove themselves right, and let them hear and say, “It is true.”

“You are My witnesses,” declares the LORD, “and My servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe Me and understand that I am He. Before Me no god was formed, nor will there be one after Me.
I, yes I, am the LORD, and apart from Me there is no Savior.
I have revealed and saved and proclaimed—I, and not some foreign god among you. You are My witnesses,” declares the LORD, “that I am God.
Even from eternity I am He, and none can deliver out of My hand. I act, and who can reverse it?”
Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: “For your sake I will send to Babylon and bring them all down as fugitives, even the Chaldeans, in the ships over which they rejoice.
I am the LORD, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King.”
Thus says the LORD, who makes a way in the sea and a path through the mighty waters,
who brings out chariot and horse, army and mighty man; they lie down together and do not rise; they are extinguished, quenched like a wick.
“Do not remember the former things, nor consider the things of old.
Behold, I am doing a new thing; now it springs up. Do you not perceive it? I will make a way in the wilderness and rivers in the wasteland.
The beasts of the field will honor Me, the jackals and the ostriches, because I give water in the wilderness and rivers in the wasteland, to give drink to My people, My chosen,
the people I formed for Myself, that they may declare My praise.”
“Yet you have not called upon Me, O Jacob; you have grown weary of Me, O Israel.
You have not brought Me sheep for your burnt offerings, nor honored Me with your sacrifices. I have not burdened you with grain offerings, nor wearied you with frankincense.
You have bought Me no sweet cane with money, nor satisfied Me with the fat of your sacrifices. Instead, you have burdened Me with your sins; you have wearied Me with your iniquities.
I, yes I, am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake, and I will not remember your sins.
Remind Me, let us argue the case together; state your case, that you may be proved right.
Your first father sinned, and your mediators transgressed against Me.
So I will profane the princes of the sanctuary, and I will devote Jacob to destruction and Israel to reproach.”
Now, therefore, attend, O Jacob, My servant, and Israel, whom I have elected.
Thus says the LORD, your Maker, and He who formed you from the womb, who will help you: “Fear not, O Jacob My servant, and Jeshurun, whom I have chosen.
For I will pour water upon the parched, and flowing streams upon the arid ground; I will pour out My Spirit upon your offspring, and My blessing upon your descendants.
They shall burgeon amid the grass, like poplars beside watercourses.”
One will declare, “I belong to the LORD,” another will invoke the name of Jacob, and another will inscribe upon his hand, “The LORD’s,” and adopt the name of Israel.
Thus says the LORD, the King of Israel and his Redeemer, the LORD of Hosts: “I am the First and I am the Last; apart from Me there is no God.
Who is like Me? Let him proclaim it. Let him declare and set it before Me, since I appointed an ancient people. Let them declare what is to come and what will happen.
Fear not, nor be afraid. Have I not told you from of old and declared it? You are My witnesses. Is there any God besides Me? There is no other Rock; I know none.”
All fashioners of idols are nothing, and their cherished things profit nothing. Their witnesses neither see nor know, to their own confusion.
Who fashions a god or casts an idol, to no profit?
Behold, all his associates shall be ashamed, and the craftsmen are but mortals. Let them all gather and stand together; they shall tremble and be put to shame.
The smith works with iron, laboring over the coals; he shapes it with hammers and exerts his strength with his arm. He grows hungry and his strength fails; he drinks no water and is weary.

The woodworker stretches a line; he outlines it with a stylus; he carves it with planes and traces it with a compass; he fashions it in the likeness of a man, with the comeliness of a man, to dwell in a house.
He fells cedars, or selects a cypress or an oak, and makes it strong among the trees of the forest; he plants a pine, and the rain makes it grow.
It serves a man for fuel: he takes some of it and warms himself; he kindles a fire and bakes bread; he also makes a god of it and worships it; he fashions an idol and bows down to it.
Half of it he burns in the fire; over that half he roasts meat, eats, and is satisfied; he also warms himself and says, “Ah, I am warm; I behold the blaze.”
The remainder he makes into a god, his idol; he bows to it and worships; he prays to it and says, “Rescue me, for you are my god.”
They know not and discern not, for He has blinded their eyes so that they cannot see, and their hearts so that they cannot understand.

No one takes it to heart, nor is there knowledge or understanding to say, “Half of it I burned in the fire; I also baked bread upon its coals; I roasted meat and ate. Shall I make the rest an abomination? Shall I bow down to a log of wood?”
He feeds on ashes; a deluded heart has led him astray, so that he cannot deliver his soul nor say, “Is there not a falsehood in my right hand?”
“Remember these things, O Jacob, and Israel, for you are My servant. I formed you; you are My servant, O Israel; you shall not be forgotten by Me.
I have blotted out your transgressions like a cloud, and your sins like a mist. Return to Me, for I have redeemed you.”

Sing, O heavens, for the LORD has wrought it; shout, O depths of the earth; burst into song, O mountains, O forest, and every tree therein! For the LORD has redeemed Jacob, and in Israel He will be glorified.
Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, and He who formed you from the womb: “I am the LORD, who made all things, who alone stretched out the heavens, who by Myself spread out the earth—
who frustrates the omens of false prophets and makes fools of diviners, who turns the wise backward and makes their knowledge foolish;

who confirms the word of His servant and fulfills the counsel of His messengers; who says of Jerusalem, ‘She shall be inhabited,’ and of the cities of Judah, ‘They shall be rebuilt, and I will raise up their ruins’;
who says to the deep, ‘Be dry, and I will dry up your rivers’;
who says of Cyrus, ‘He is My shepherd, and he shall fulfill all My purpose,’ and of Jerusalem, ‘She shall be built,’ and of the temple, ‘Your foundation shall be laid.’”

“Thus says the LORD to Cyrus, His anointed, whose right hand I have grasped, to subdue nations before him and to strip kings of their strength, to open doors before him so that gates will not be shut.
I will go before you and level the rugged places; I will break the doors of bronze and cut through the bars of iron.
I will give you the treasures of darkness and the hoards hidden in secret places, that you may know that I am the LORD, the God of Israel, who calls you by your name.
“For the sake of My servant Jacob, and Israel My chosen, I call you by your name; I have given you a title, though you do not know Me.
I am the LORD, and there is no other; besides Me there is no God. I equip you, though you do not know Me.
“That people may know from the rising of the sun and from the west that there is none besides Me. I am the LORD, and there is no other.
I form light and create darkness; I make well-being and create calamity; I am the LORD, who does all these things.”
Let the heavens shower from above, and let the clouds rain down righteousness; let the earth open, that salvation and righteousness may bear fruit together; I, the LORD, have created it.

Woe to the one who contends with his Maker—a mere shard among the shards of the earth! Shall the clay say to its fashioner, “What are you making?” or shall the work declare, “The artisan is devoid of skill”?
Woe to the one who says to a father, “What are you begetting?” or to a woman, “With what are you in labor?”
“Thus says the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, and its Maker: ‘Will you question Me about My children, or give Me commands concerning the work of My hands?’
I made the earth and created man upon it; it was My hands that stretched out the heavens, and I commanded all their host.
“I have stirred him up in righteousness, and I will make all his ways level; he shall build My city and set My exiles free, not for price nor reward,” says the LORD of Hosts.

“Thus says the LORD: ‘The labor of Egypt and the merchandise of Cush and of the Sabeans—men of stature—shall come over to you and be yours; they shall follow you; they shall come over in chains and bow down to you. They will plead with you, saying, “Surely God is in you, and there is no other, no god besides Him.”’”
Truly, You are a God who hides Himself, O God of Israel, the Savior.
All of them are put to shame and confounded; the makers of idols go away in confusion together.
But Israel is saved by the LORD with everlasting salvation; you shall not be put to shame or confounded to all eternity.

“For thus says the LORD, who created the heavens—He is God!—who formed the earth and made it—He established it; He did not create it a chaos, He formed it to be inhabited: ‘I am the LORD, and there is no other.’
I did not speak in secret, in a dark place of the earth; I did not say to the offspring of Jacob, ‘Seek Me in vain.’ I, the LORD, speak righteousness and declare what is right.
“Assemble yourselves and come; draw near together, you survivors of the nations! They have no knowledge who carry about their wooden idols and keep praying to a god that cannot save.

Declare and present your case; let them take counsel together! Who announced this from of old? Who declared it of old? Was it not I, the LORD? And there is no other god besides Me, a righteous God and a Savior; there is none besides Me.
“Turn to Me and be saved, all the ends of the earth! For I am God, and there is no other.
By Myself I have sworn; from My mouth has gone out in righteousness a word that shall not return: ‘To Me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear allegiance.’”
“Only in the LORD,” it shall be said of Me, “are righteousness and strength”; to Him shall come and be ashamed all who were incensed against Him.
In the LORD all the offspring of Israel shall be justified and shall glory.
Bel has bowed down, Nebo stoops; their idols are laid upon beasts and cattle. The burdens you bear are onerous, a load for the weary beast.
They stoop and bow down together; they are powerless to deliver the burden, and their very selves have gone into captivity.
“Listen to Me, O house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, you who have been borne from the belly and carried from the womb:
Even to your old age I am He, and even to your gray hairs I will bear you; I have made you, and I will bear you; I will carry you and deliver you.
“To whom, then, will you liken Me, or make Me equal, or compare Me, that we should be alike?
They lavish gold from the purse, weigh out silver on the scale, employ a goldsmith, who fashions it into a god; then they bow down and worship.
They lift it to the shoulder, carry it, set it in its place, and there it stands; it does not budge from its spot. One cries to it, yet it does not answer or save him from his distress.
“Remember this, and be resolute; lay it to heart, you transgressors.
Remember the former things of old; for I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is none like Me,
declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times things not yet done, saying, ‘My counsel shall stand, and all My pleasure I will accomplish,’
summoning a bird of prey from the east, the man of My counsel from a far country. Indeed, I have spoken, and I will bring it to pass; I have purposed, and I will do it.
“Listen to Me, you who are stout of heart, you who are far from righteousness:
I bring near My righteousness; it shall not be far off, and My salvation shall not delay; and I will put salvation in Zion for Israel, My glory.”

Descend and seat yourself upon the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon; settle upon the ground bereft of a throne, O daughter of the Chaldeans, for you shall no longer be acclaimed as tender and delicate.
Take up the millstones and grind flour; strip away your veil, bare your skirt, expose your thigh, and ford the rivers.
Your nakedness shall be uncovered, and your disgrace shall be exposed to view; I will exact retribution, sparing no mortal.
Our Redeemer—the LORD of Hosts is His name—the Holy One of Israel.
Sit in silence and enter the darkness, O daughter of the Chaldeans, for you shall no longer be called mistress of kingdoms.
I was angry with My people; I profaned My inheritance and delivered them into your hand. You showed them no mercy; upon the aged you made your yoke exceedingly heavy.
You said, "I shall be mistress forever," so that you did not lay these things to heart, nor remember their final outcome.
