Now, then, hear this, you who luxuriate in pleasures, who dwell in security, who say in your heart, 'I am, and there is no one besides me; I shall not sit as a widow, nor know the loss of children.'

These two things shall befall you in a moment, in a single day: bereavement and widowhood. They shall come upon you in all their fullness, notwithstanding your many sorceries and the great abundance of your enchantments.
You have trusted in your wickedness; you have said, 'No one sees me.' Your wisdom and your knowledge have led you astray, and you have said in your heart, 'I am, and there is no one besides me.'

But evil shall come upon you, which you shall not know how to charm away; and calamity shall fall upon you, which you cannot expiate; and desolation shall overtake you suddenly, beyond your foreknowledge.
Stand now among your enchantments and in the multitude of your sorceries, in which you have toiled since your youth; perhaps you can derive some profit, perhaps you can prevail.
You have wearied yourself with your many counsels; let them stand now and save you—those who divide the heavens, who gaze upon the stars, who announce by the months what shall befall you.
Behold, they are like stubble; fire consumes them; they cannot deliver themselves from the power of the flame; there is no ember to warm them, no fire to sit before.
Thus have they become to you—those with whom you have trafficked, your merchants from your youth—each strays to his own quarter; there is no one to save you.

Hear this, O house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel and have come forth from the waters of Judah, you who swear by the name of the LORD and invoke the God of Israel, yet not in truth or in righteousness.
For they are called after the holy city, and they lean upon the God of Israel—the the LORD of Hosts is His name.
I have declared the former things from of old; from My mouth they went forth, and I proclaimed them; suddenly I acted, and they came to pass.
Because I knew that you are obstinate, and your neck is an iron sinew, and your forehead is bronze.
And I declared to you from of old; before it came to pass I proclaimed it to you, lest you should say, 'My idol has done this, and my carved image and my molten image have commanded it.'
You have heard; behold all of it. And will you not declare it? From now I announce to you new things, hidden things, which you have not known.
Now they are created, and not from of old; and before today you have not heard of them, lest you should say, 'Behold, I knew them.'

Indeed, you have not heard; indeed, you have not known; indeed, from of old your ear has not been opened. For I knew that you would deal treacherously, and that you have been called a rebel from the womb.
For the sake of My name I will defer My anger, and for My praise I will restrain it for you, that I may not cut you off.
Behold, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.
For My own sake, for My own sake, I will do it; for how should My name be profaned? And My glory I will not give to another.
Hearken to Me, O Jacob, and Israel, whom I have called: I am He; I am the first, I also am the last.
My hand also has laid the foundation of the earth, and My right hand has spanned the heavens; when I call to them, they stand together.
Assemble, all of you, and hear: who among them has declared these things? The LORD loves him; He will perform His pleasure on Babylon, and His arm shall be upon the Chaldeans.
I, even I, have spoken; indeed, I have called him; I have brought him, and he will prosper in his way.
Draw near to Me, hear this: from the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time of its coming to be, there am I. And now the Lord the LORD has sent Me, and His Spirit.
Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am the LORD your God, who teaches you for your profit, who leads you in the way you should go.
If you had hearkened to My commandments, then your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
Your seed also would have been like the sand, and the offspring of your body like its grains; his name would not have been cut off or destroyed from before Me.
Go out from Babylon, flee from the Chaldeans, declare with a voice of rejoicing, proclaim this, send it forth to the end of the earth; say, 'The LORD has redeemed His servant Jacob.'
And they did not thirst when He led them through the deserts; He made water flow for them from the rock; He split the rock, and the waters gushed out.
There is no peace, says the LORD, for the wicked.
“Listen to me, O coastlands, and give ear, O distant peoples: the LORD called me from the womb; from my mother's body He made mention of my name.
He made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of His hand He concealed me; He made me a polished arrow; in His quiver He hid me.”
And He said to me, “You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified.”
But I said, “I have labored in vain; I have spent my strength for nothing and vanity; yet surely my right is with the LORD, and my recompense with my God.”

“And now the LORD says—He who formed me from the womb to be His servant, to bring Jacob back to Him and gather Israel to Himself—for I am honored in the eyes of the LORD, and my God has become my strength—”

He says, “It is too light a thing that you should be My servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob and to restore the survivors of Israel; I will make you a light for the nations, that My salvation may extend to the ends of the earth.”

Thus says the LORD, the Redeemer and Holy One of Israel, to the one deeply despised, abhorred by the nation, the servant of rulers: “Kings shall see and arise; princes shall prostrate themselves; because of the LORD, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you.”

Thus says the LORD: “In a time of favor I have answered you; in a day of salvation I have helped you; I will keep you and make you a covenant for the people, to restore the land and to allot the desolate inheritances,
saying to the prisoners, ‘Come out,’ and to those in darkness, ‘Show yourselves.’ They shall feed along the ways, and on all the bare heights shall be their pasture.”
“They shall not hunger or thirst, neither scorching heat nor sun shall strike them; for He who has compassion on them will guide them and lead them beside springs of water.
I will turn all My mountains into a road, and My highways shall be raised up.”
“Behold, these shall come from afar, and behold, these from the north and from the west, and these from the land of Sinim.”
Sing, O heavens, and exult, O earth; break forth into singing, O mountains! For the LORD has comforted His people and will have compassion on His afflicted.
But Zion said, “The LORD has forsaken me; the Lord has forgotten me.”
“Can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should have no compassion on the son of her womb? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you.
Behold, I have inscribed you on the palms of My hands; your walls are continually before Me.”
“Your children hasten; your destroyers and your devastators go forth from you.”
“Lift up your eyes and look around; all these gather and come to you. As I live, declares the LORD, you shall put them all on as an ornament; you shall bind them on as a bride.”
“Surely your waste and desolate places and your devastated land—surely now you will be too narrow for your inhabitants, and those who swallowed you up will be far away.”
“The children of your bereavement will yet say in your ears, ‘The place is too narrow for me; make room for me that I may dwell.’
Then you will say in your heart, ‘Who has borne me these? I was bereaved and barren, exiled and rejected; who has reared these? Behold, I was left alone; where then have these come from?’”

Thus says the Lord, the LORD: “Behold, I will lift up My hand to the nations and raise My signal to the peoples; and they shall bring your sons in their bosom, and your daughters shall be carried on their shoulders.

Kings shall be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. With their faces to the ground they shall bow down to you, and lick the dust of your feet. Then you will know that I am the LORD; those who wait for Me shall not be put to shame.
Can the prey be taken from the mighty, or the captives of a tyrant be rescued?
For the LORD says, ‘Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the prey of the tyrant be rescued; for I will contend with those who contend with you, and I will save your children.’

I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh, and they shall be drunk with their own blood as with sweet wine. Then all flesh shall know that I am the LORD your Savior, and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.”

Thus says the LORD: “Where is your mother’s certificate of divorce, with which I sent her away? Or which of My creditors is it to whom I sold you? Behold, you were sold for your iniquities, and for your transgressions your mother was sent away.”

“Why, when I came, was there no man? When I called, why was there no one to answer? Is My hand shortened, that it cannot redeem? Or have I no power to deliver? Behold, by My rebuke I dry up the sea; I make the rivers a wilderness; their fish stink for lack of water and die of thirst.
I clothe the heavens with blackness and make sackcloth their covering.”
The Lord the LORD has given Me the tongue of the learned, that I may know how to sustain the weary with a word. He awakens Me morning by morning; He awakens My ear to hear as the learned.
The Lord the LORD has opened My ear, and I was not rebellious; I did not turn backward.
I gave My back to those who strike, and My cheeks to those who pluck out the beard; I did not hide My face from shame and spitting.
Because the Lord the LORD helps Me, I have not been disgraced; therefore I have set My face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame.
He who vindicates Me is near. Who will contend with Me? Let us stand together. Who is My adversary? Let him draw near to Me.
Behold, the Lord the LORD helps Me; who will declare Me guilty? Behold, all of them will wear out like a garment; the moth will eat them.
“Who among you fears the the LORD and obeys the voice of His servant? Let him who walks in darkness and has no light trust in the name of the the LORD and rely on his God.

Behold, all of you who kindle a fire, who equip yourselves with burning torches, walk by the light of your fire and by the torches that you have kindled! This you shall have from My hand: you shall lie down in torment.”
"Listen to Me, you who pursue righteousness, you who seek the the LORD: look to the rock from which you were hewn, and to the quarry from which you were dug.
Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah who bore you; for when he was but one I called him, and I blessed him and multiplied him."

For the the LORD will comfort Zion; He will comfort all her waste places, and He will make her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of the the LORD; joy and gladness will be found in her, together with thanksgiving and the voice of song.
"Pay attention to Me, O My people, and give ear to Me, O My nation; for a law will go forth from Me, and I will establish My justice as a light for the peoples.
My righteousness is near; My salvation has gone forth; and My arms will judge the peoples; the coastlands will wait for Me, and for My arm they will hope.

Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look upon the earth beneath; for the heavens will vanish like smoke, and the earth will wear out like a garment, and its inhabitants will perish in like manner; but My salvation will be forever, and My righteousness will not be abolished.
Listen to Me, you who know righteousness, a people in whose heart is My law; do not fear the reproach of man, nor be dismayed at their revilings.
For the moth will devour them like a garment, and the worm will devour them like wool; but My righteousness will be forever, and My salvation to all generations."
Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the the LORD; awake as in the days of old, the generations of long ago. Was it not You who cut Rahab to pieces, who pierced the dragon?
Was it not You who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, who made the depths of the sea a path for the redeemed to cross?
So the redeemed of the the LORD will return and come with singing to Zion, and everlasting joy will be upon their heads; they will obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.
"I, even I, am He who comforts you. Who are you that you are afraid of man, who dies, and of the son of man, who is made like grass,

that you have forgotten the the LORD your Maker, who stretched out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth, and that you fear continually all the day because of the fury of the oppressor, as he prepares to destroy? And where is the fury of the oppressor?
The exile will soon be set free, and will not die in the dungeon, nor will his bread be lacking.
For I am the the LORD your God, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar—the the LORD of hosts is His name.
I have put My words in your mouth, and I have covered you with the shadow of My hand, to plant the heavens and to found the earth, and to say to Zion, 'You are My people.'"
"Rouse yourself! Rouse yourself! Arise, O Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the hand of the the LORD the cup of His wrath; you have drained the bowl of staggering.
There is none to guide her among all the sons she has borne, and none to take her by the hand among all the sons she has reared.
These two things have befallen you—who will grieve for you?—devastation and destruction, famine and sword. How shall I comfort you?
Your sons have fainted; they lie at the head of every street, like an antelope in a net, full of the wrath of the the LORD, the rebuke of your God.
Therefore hear this now, you afflicted one, who are drunk, but not with wine:
Thus says your Lord, the the LORD, even your God who contends for His people, 'Behold, I have taken from your hand the cup of staggering, the bowl of My wrath; you shall drink it no more.

I will put it into the hand of your tormentors, who have said to you, "Lie down, that we may pass over you." You have even made your back like the ground, and like the street, for them to pass over.'"
Awake, awake, put on your strength, O Zion; put on your garments of beauty, O Jerusalem, the holy city, for neither the uncircumcised nor the impure shall any longer intrude upon you.
Shake off the dust; arise, sit enthroned, O Jerusalem; loose the bonds from your neck, O captive daughter of Zion.
For thus says the LORD: “You were sold for nothing, and you shall be redeemed without money.”
For thus says the Lord the LORD: “At first My people went down to Egypt to sojourn there, and the Assyrian oppressed them without cause.”
And now what have I here? declares the LORD, for My people have been taken away for nothing; their rulers wail, declares the LORD, and My name is continually blasphemed all day long.
Therefore My people shall know My name; therefore on that day they shall know that I am He who speaks: ‘Here I am.’”
How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the herald who brings good news, who proclaims peace, who brings good tidings of salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
The voice of your watchmen—they raise their voices; together they shout for joy, for eye to eye they behold the LORD returning to Zion.
Break forth into singing together, O ruins of Jerusalem, for the LORD has comforted His people; He has redeemed Jerusalem.
The LORD has bared His holy arm in the sight of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth shall behold the salvation of our God.
Depart, depart, go out from there; touch no unclean thing; go out from her midst; purify yourselves, you who bear the vessels of the LORD.
For you shall not go out in haste, nor shall you flee in panic, for the LORD goes before you, and the God of Israel is your rear guard.
Behold, My Servant shall prosper; He shall be exalted and lifted up and shall be very high.
As many were appalled at You—His appearance was so disfigured, beyond that of any man, and His form beyond that of the sons of mankind—
so shall He sprinkle many nations. Kings shall shut their mouths because of Him; for what was not told them they shall see, and what they have not heard they shall understand.
Who has believed our report, and to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?
He shot up before Him like a tender shoot, and like a root from parched soil; He possessed no stately form or splendor, and when we beheld Him, there was no comeliness that we should covet Him.
He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows and acquainted with grief; and as one from whom men hide their faces, He was despised, and we esteemed Him not.
Surely He has borne our griefs and carried our sorrows; yet we esteemed Him stricken, smitten by God, and afflicted.
But He was pierced for our transgressions, He was crushed for our iniquities; the chastisement that brought us peace was upon Him, and by His wounds we are healed.
We all, like sheep, have gone astray; each of us has turned to his own way; and the LORD has laid upon Him the iniquity of us all.
He was oppressed and afflicted, yet He did not open His mouth; He was led like a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is silent, so He did not open His mouth.
By oppression and judgment He was taken away; and who among His generation considered that He was cut off from the land of the living for the transgression of My people, to whom the stroke was due?
He was assigned a grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in His death, although He had done no violence, nor was any deceit in His mouth.

Yet it was the LORD’s will to crush Him and to cause Him to suffer; when His soul is made a guilt offering, He will see His offspring, He will prolong His days, and the good pleasure of the LORD will prosper in His hand.
After the anguish of His soul, He will see and be satisfied; by His knowledge My righteous Servant will justify many, and He will bear their iniquities.

Therefore I will allot Him a portion with the great, and He will divide the spoils with the strong, because He poured out His life unto death and was numbered with the transgressors; yet He bore the sin of many and made intercession for the transgressors.

“Sing, O barren woman who has never borne a child; burst into song and cry aloud, you who have never travailed in labor; for more numerous are the children of the desolate woman than the children of the married woman,” says the LORD.
“Enlarge the place of your tent, and let them stretch out the curtains of your dwellings; do not hold back; lengthen your cords, and strengthen your stakes.
For you will spread out to the right and to the left, and your offspring will possess nations and inhabit desolate cities.

Do not fear, for you will not be put to shame; and do not be disgraced, for you will not be humiliated; for you will forget the shame of your youth, and you will remember no more the reproach of your widowhood.
For your Maker is your husband—the the LORD of Hosts is His name—and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel; He is called the God of all the earth.”
“For the LORD has called you back, like a wife deserted and wounded in spirit, like the wife of one’s youth when she is rejected,” says your God.
“For a brief moment I forsook you, but with great compassion I will gather you.
In a surge of anger I hid My face from you for a moment, but with everlasting kindness I will have compassion on you,” says the LORD, your Redeemer.
“For this is to Me as the days of Noah, when I swore that the waters of Noah would never again cover the earth; so I have sworn not to be angry with you or to rebuke you.
Though the mountains may be removed and the hills be shaken, My loving devotion will not depart from you, and My covenant of peace will not be shaken,” says the LORD, who has compassion on you.”
“O afflicted one, storm-tossed and not comforted, Behold, I will set your stones in antimony and lay your foundations with sapphires.
I will make your pinnacles of rubies, your gates of sparkling stones, and all your walls of precious stones.
All your children will be taught by the LORD, and great will be their peace.
In righteousness you will be established: you will be far from oppression, for you will not fear; and from terror, for it will not come near you.
If anyone stirs up strife, it is not from Me; whoever gathers against you will fall because of you.
Behold, I have created the smith who blows the coals in the fire and produces a weapon for his work; and I have created the destroyer to wreak havoc.

No weapon formed against you will prosper, and you will refute every tongue that accuses you in judgment. This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their vindication is from Me,” declares the LORD.”
Behold, all you who thirst—come to the waters; and you who possess no silver, come, buy and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without silver and without price.
Why do you expend silver upon that which is not bread, and your toil upon that which cannot satisfy? Listen attentively to me, and eat what is good, and let your soul delight in rich abundance.
Incline your ear and come to me; listen, that your soul may live. I will establish with you an everlasting covenant—the faithful lovingkindness promised to David.
See, I have appointed him a witness to the nations, a ruler and commander of peoples.
Behold, you will summon a nation you do not know, and nations that do not know you will hasten to you, because of the the LORD your God and the Holy One of Israel, for He has glorified you.
Seek the the LORD while He may be found; call upon Him while He is near.
Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts; let him return to the the LORD, and He will have mercy on him, and to our God, for He will abundantly pardon.
“For My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways My ways,” declares the the LORD.
For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are My ways higher than your ways and My thoughts than your thoughts.
For as the rain and snow descend from heaven and do not return thither, but water the earth and make it bring forth and bud, yielding seed to the sower and bread to the eater—
so shall My word be that proceeds from My mouth: it shall not return to Me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in that for which I sent it.
For you shall go forth with joy and be led forth in peace; the mountains and hills shall break forth into singing before you, and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands.
Instead of the thorn the cypress shall rise, and instead of the brier the myrtle shall rise; and it shall be to the the LORD for a name, for an everlasting sign that shall not be cut off.
Thus says the the LORD: “Uphold justice and execute righteousness, for My salvation is imminent, and My righteousness is on the verge of disclosure.”
Blessed is the man who performs this, and the son of man who cleaves to it—who safeguards the Sabbath from profanation and restrains his hand from perpetrating any evil.

Let not the foreigner who has affiliated himself with the the LORD say, “The the LORD will assuredly alienate me from His people”; nor let the eunuch say, “Behold, I am barren and bereft of posterity.”
For thus says the the LORD: “To the eunuchs who preserve My Sabbaths, who elect what pleases Me, and who tenaciously uphold My covenant—

I shall bestow upon them, within My house and within My walls, a memorial and a name surpassing sons and daughters; I shall confer upon them an everlasting name that shall never be excised. “And to the foreigners who cleave to the the LORD in order to minister to Him, to love the name of the the LORD, and to become His servants—everyone who guards the Sabbath from desecration and clings to My covenant—

I shall usher them into My holy mountain and gladden them in My house of prayer; their burnt offerings and sacrifices shall find acceptance upon My altar, for My house shall be denominated a house of prayer for all peoples.”
Declares the Lord GOD, who gathers the dispersed of Israel: “I shall yet gather to him others besides those already assembled.”
Come, all you beasts of the field; come, all you beasts of the forest, to devour.
Israel’s sentinels are blind; they are all devoid of knowledge. They are all mute hounds, incapable of barking; they are dreamers reclining, enamored of slumber.
Moreover, the hounds are ravenous; they know no satiety. They are shepherds devoid of discernment; they have all veered to their own course, each in pursuit of his own lucre.
They cry, “Come, let us procure wine; let us intoxicate ourselves with strong drink! Tomorrow will resemble today, only in far greater measure.”
The righteous perish, yet none takes it to heart; the godly are gathered away, while no one discerns that the righteous are gathered away from evil.
The upright one enters into peace and rests upon his bed.
“Draw near here, you sons of the sorceress, seed of the adulterer and the prostitute.
At whom do you make sport? At whom do you widen your mouth and lengthen your tongue? Are you not children of transgression, seed of falsehood?
You who inflame yourselves among the oaks, beneath every verdant tree, slaughtering children in the valleys, beneath the clefts of the rocks.

Your portion is among the smooth stones of the valley; they, they are your lot. You have poured out a drink offering to them; you have offered a grain offering. Shall I relent concerning these things?
On a high and lofty mountain you have set your bed; there too you went up to sacrifice.

Behind the door and the doorpost you set your memorial, for, apart from Me, you uncovered your bed and ascended; you widened it and cut off their bed for yourself from them; you loved; you gazed upon a hand.
You went to Molech with oil and multiplied your perfumes; you sent your envoys far away and debased yourself even to Sheol.
“You wearied yourself in the abundance of your way; you did not say, ‘It is hopeless’; you found strength in your own hand; therefore you were not sick.
And of whom have you been anxious and afraid, that you should lie? And Me you did not remember; you did not set Me upon your heart. Have I not been silent from of old, and yet you do not fear Me?
I will declare your righteousness and your works, and they will not profit you.

When you cry out, let your gathered ones save you; but the wind will carry them all away, and a breath will take them. But he who takes refuge in Me will inherit the land and possess My holy mountain.”
And He will say, “Build up, build up, prepare the way, remove the stumbling block from the way of My people.”

For thus says the High and Lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: “I dwell in the high and holy place, and with the contrite and lowly in spirit, to revive the spirit of the lowly and to revive the heart of the contrite.
For I will not contend forever, nor will I always be angry, for the spirit would grow faint before Me, and the breaths that I made.
Because of the iniquity of his covetous gain I was angry and struck him; I hid My face and was angry, yet he went on in the way of his heart.
I have seen his ways, and I will heal him; I will lead him and restore comforts to him and to his mourners.
I create the fruit of the lips: Peace, peace to the far and to the near,” says the the LORD, “and I will heal him.”
But the wicked are like the tossing sea, for it cannot be quiet, and its waters toss up mire and mud.
“There is no peace,” says My God, “for the wicked.”
“Cry aloud; do not hold back; lift up your voice like a trumpet, and declare to My people their transgression, and to the house of Jacob their sins.

Yet they seek Me day by day and delight in drawing near to God, as though they were a nation that had practiced righteousness and had not forsaken the justice of its God. They ask Me for righteous judgments; they delight in the nearness of God.”
“Why have we fasted, and You have not seen? Why have we afflicted our souls, and You have not noticed?” “Behold, on the day of your fast you find pleasure, and you exploit all your laborers.
Behold, you fast for strife and contention, to strike with a wicked fist. You cannot fast as you do today and expect your voice to be heard on high.
Is this the fast I have chosen—a day for a person to afflict his soul, to bow his head like a reed, and to spread sackcloth and ashes? Will you call this a fast, a day acceptable to the LORD?
Is not this the fast I choose: to loose the bonds of wickedness, to untie the cords of the yoke, to set the oppressed free, and to break every yoke?
Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, and to bring the homeless poor into your house; when you see the naked, to cover him, and not to hide yourself from your own kin?”
“Then your light will break forth like the dawn, and your healing will spring up speedily; your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of the LORD will be your rear guard.
Then you will call, and the LORD will answer; you will cry out, and He will say, ‘Here I am.’ If you remove the yoke from your midst, and abandon the pointing of the finger and malicious speech,
and if you pour out your soul for the hungry and satisfy the afflicted soul, then your light will rise in the darkness, and your gloom will be like the noonday.
The LORD will guide you continually; He will satisfy your soul in a sun-scorched land and strengthen your frame. You will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail.
Your people will rebuild the ancient ruins; you will restore the foundations of generations. You will be called a repairer of the breach, a restorer of streets for habitation.”

“If you turn your foot from the Sabbath, from pursuing your own pleasure on My holy day, and if you call the Sabbath a delight, the holy day of the LORD honorable, and honor it by not going your own way, not seeking your own pleasure, and not speaking idle words,
then you will delight in the LORD, and I will make you ride on the heights of the land and feed you with the heritage of your father Jacob; for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.”
Behold, the hand of the LORD is not so shortened that it cannot deliver, nor is His ear so dull that it cannot hear.
Rather, it is your iniquities that have severed you from your God, and your sins have concealed His face from you, so that He does not hear.
For your hands are stained with blood, and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken falsehood, and your tongue mutters injustice.
No one calls in righteousness, and none pleads in faithfulness; they trust in emptiness and speak vanity; they conceive trouble and beget iniquity.
They hatch viper's eggs and weave a spider's web; whoever consumes their eggs dies, and a crushed egg hatches forth a viper.
Their webs shall not become garments, nor shall they cover themselves with their works; their works are works of iniquity, and deeds of violence are in their hands.
Their feet run to evil, and they hasten to shed innocent blood; their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity; devastation and ruin lie along their paths.
The way of peace they do not know, and there is no justice in their tracks; they have made crooked paths for themselves, and no one who walks in them knows peace.
Therefore justice is far from us, and righteousness does not overtake us; we hope for light, but behold, darkness; for brightness, but we walk in gloom.
Like the blind we grope along a wall, and as though we had no eyes we grope; we stumble at noon as in twilight; among the vigorous we are as the dead.
We all growl like bears and moan bitterly like doves; we look for justice, but there is none, for salvation, but it is far from us.
For our transgressions are multiplied before You, and our sins testify against us; for our transgressions are with us, and our iniquities—we know them.
We have been rebelling and denying the LORD, turning away from our God, speaking oppression and apostasy, conceiving and uttering from the heart words of falsehood.
So justice is driven back, and righteousness stands at a distance; for truth has stumbled in the street, and uprightness cannot enter.
Truth is lacking, and whoever turns from evil is plundered. The LORD saw it, and it was evil in His eyes that there was no justice.
He saw that there was no man, and was appalled that there was no intercessor; so His own arm brought salvation to Him, and His righteousness upheld Him.
He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation on His head; He put on garments of vengeance for clothing, and wrapped Himself in zeal as in a cloak.
According to their deeds, so will He repay: wrath to His adversaries, recompense to His enemies; to the coastlands He will render recompense.
So they shall fear the name of the LORD from the west, and His glory from the rising of the sun; for He will come like a rushing torrent, driven by the breath of the LORD.
"The Redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from transgression," declares the LORD.

"And as for Me, this is My covenant with them," says the LORD: "My Spirit that is upon you, and My words that I have put in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your offspring, nor from the mouth of your offspring's offspring, from now and forever," says the LORD.
Arise and be illumined, for your light has arrived, and the glory of the the LORD has dawned upon you.
For behold, darkness shall enshroud the earth, and a dense gloom the peoples; yet the the LORD shall arise upon you, and His glory shall be manifested upon you.
Nations shall journey toward your light, and kings toward the radiance of your dawn.
Lift up your eyes and behold: all are gathered together; they come to you. Your sons shall arrive from afar, and your daughters shall be borne upon the hip.
Then you shall perceive and radiate; your heart shall tremble and dilate with joy, because the fullness of the sea shall be turned toward you, and the wealth of the nations shall come to you.

A profusion of camels shall overspread you—the young camels of Midian and Ephah; all of them from Sheba shall come. They shall bear gold and frankincense, and shall proclaim the praises of the the LORD.
All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered to you; the rams of Nebaioth shall serve you. They shall ascend upon My altar as an acceptable offering, and I will adorn the house of My glory.
Who are these that fly like a cloud, and like doves to their windows?

Surely the coastlands shall wait for Me, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring your sons from afar, together with their silver and gold, for the name of the the LORD your God, and for the Holy One of Israel, because He has glorified you.
Foreigners shall rebuild your walls, and their kings shall serve you; for in My wrath I struck you, yet in My favor I have shown you mercy.
Your gates shall remain open continually; they shall not be shut by day or by night, so that the wealth of the nations may be brought to you, with their kings led in procession.
For the nation and kingdom that will not serve you shall perish; indeed, those nations shall be utterly desolated.
The glory of Lebanon shall come to you—the cypress, the plane tree, and the pine—together to adorn the place of My sanctuary, and I will glorify the place of My feet.

The sons of your oppressors shall come bending low to you, and all who despised you shall bow down at the soles of your feet; and they shall call you the City of the the LORD, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
Whereas you were forsaken and hated, with no passerby, I will make you an everlasting majesty, a joy from generation to generation.
You shall suck the milk of nations; you shall nurse at the breast of kings; and you shall know that I am the the LORD, your Savior and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
Instead of bronze I will bring gold, and instead of iron, silver; instead of wood, bronze, and instead of stones, iron. I will make your overseers peace and your taskmasters righteousness.
Violence shall no longer be heard in your land, nor devastation and destruction within your borders; but you shall call your walls Salvation, and your gates Praise.
The sun shall no longer be your light by day, nor shall the moon give you light for brightness; but the the LORD shall be to you an everlasting light, and your God shall be your glory.
Your sun shall no more set, nor your moon withdraw; for the the LORD shall be to you an everlasting light, and the days of your mourning shall be completed.
All your people shall be righteous; they shall inherit the land forever—the branch of My planting, the work of My hands—that I may be glorified.
The least shall become a thousand, and the small one a mighty nation; I am the the LORD; in its appointed time I will hasten it.

The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me to bring glad tidings to the afflicted. He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim release to the captives and liberation to the imprisoned.
I am sent to proclaim the year of the LORD’s favor and the day of vengeance of our God, to comfort all who mourn—

to appoint for those who grieve in Zion, to give them a crown of beauty in place of ashes, the oil of joy in place of mourning, and a garment of praise in place of a spirit of faintness, so that they may be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified.
They will rebuild the ancient ruins; they will restore the places long devastated; they will renew the ruined cities that have been desolate for generations.
Foreigners will stand and shepherd your flocks, and the sons of strangers will be your plowmen and your vinedressers.
But you will be called priests of the LORD; they will speak of you as ministers of our God. You will feed on the wealth of the nations, and in their riches you will boast.

Instead of your shame, you will receive a double portion; instead of disgrace, they will rejoice in their inheritance. Therefore they will inherit a double portion in their land; everlasting joy will be theirs.
For I, the LORD, love justice; I hate robbery and iniquity; in My faithfulness I will give them their recompense and make an everlasting covenant with them.
Their offspring will be known among the nations, and their descendants among the peoples. All who see them will acknowledge that they are a people the LORD has blessed.

I will rejoice greatly in the LORD; my soul will exult in my God. For He has clothed me with garments of salvation and wrapped me in a robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom adorns his head like a priest, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
For as the earth brings forth its sprouts, and as a garden causes its seeds to spring up, so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations.
For Zion’s sake I will not remain silent, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not be still, until her righteousness radiates like the dawn and her salvation blazes like a torch.
The nations shall behold your righteousness, and all kings your glory; you shall be called by a new name that the mouth of the the LORD will designate.
You shall be a crown of splendor in the hand of the the LORD, a royal diadem in the hand of your God.

No longer shall you be called Forsaken, nor shall your land be called Desolate; rather, you shall be called “My Delight Is in Her,” and your land “Married,” because the the LORD delights in you, and your land shall be married.
For as a young man marries a virgin, so your sons shall marry you; and as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God shall rejoice over you.
Upon your walls, O Jerusalem, I have stationed sentinels; day and night they shall never fall silent. You who invoke the the LORD, grant yourselves no respite,
and give Him no rest until He establishes Jerusalem and makes her the praise of the earth.
The the LORD has sworn by His right hand and by His mighty arm: “Never again will I consign your grain to your enemies as food, nor shall foreigners drink the new wine for which you have labored.”
But those who reap it shall eat it and praise the the LORD, and those who gather it shall drink it in My sacred courts.
Pass through, pass through the gates; clear the way for the people. Raise up, raise up the highway; clear away the stones; lift high a standard for the peoples.
Behold, the the LORD has proclaimed to the ends of the earth: “Say to Daughter Zion, ‘See, your salvation is coming; His reward is with Him, and His recompense precedes Him.’”
They shall be called the Holy People, the Redeemed of the the LORD; and you shall be called Sought Out, a City Not Forsaken.

Who is this coming from Edom, from Bozrah, with garments stained crimson? This One, glorious in apparel, striding in the fullness of His strength? “It is I, speaking in righteousness, mighty to save.”
Why are Your garments red, and Your apparel like that of one treading the winepress?

I have trodden the winepress alone, and from the peoples no one was with Me. I trod them in My anger and trampled them in My wrath; their blood bespattered My garments, and I have defiled all My raiment.
For the day of vengeance was in My heart, and the year of My redemption had come.
I looked, but there was no one to help; I was astonished that none sustained Me. So My own arm brought Me salvation, and My wrath upheld Me.
I trampled the nations in My anger; in My wrath I made them drunk and poured out their lifeblood upon the earth.

I shall recount the steadfast love of the LORD, the praises of the LORD, according to all that the LORD has bestowed upon us, and the great goodness to the house of Israel that He has granted according to His compassion and the abundance of His steadfast love.
He said, “Surely they are My people, children who will not deal falsely.” So He became their Savior.
In all their affliction He was afflicted, and the Angel of His Presence saved them. In His love and in His compassion He redeemed them; He lifted them up and carried them all the days of old.
But they rebelled and grieved His Holy Spirit; so He turned and became their enemy, and He Himself fought against them.
Then His people remembered the days of old, the days of Moses: Where is He who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of His flock? Where is He who put His Holy Spirit in their midst—
the One who made His glorious arm go at the right hand of Moses, who divided the waters before them to make for Himself an everlasting name—
who led them through the depths like a steed in the desert, so that they did not stumble?
Like cattle descending into the vale, the Spirit of the LORD gave them rest. So You led Your people, to make for Yourself a glorious name.
Look down from the heavens and see, from Your holy and glorious habitation. Where are Your zeal and Your might? Your yearning and Your compassion are withheld from us.
For You are our Father, though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not acknowledge us; You, O LORD, are our Father, our Redeemer from antiquity is Your name.
Why, O LORD, do You cause us to wander from Your ways and harden our heart from fearing You? Return, for the sake of Your servants, the tribes of Your inheritance.
For a brief while Your people possessed Your holy place, but our adversaries have trampled Your sanctuary.
We have become like those over whom You have never ruled, like those not called by Your name.
If only You would rend the heavens and come down, so that the mountains might melt at Your presence—
as fire kindles brushwood, as fire causes water to boil—to make Your name known to Your adversaries, so that the nations might tremble at Your presence!
When You did awesome things that we did not expect, You came down, and the mountains melted at Your presence.
From of old no one has heard, no ear has perceived, no eye has seen any God besides You, who acts for those who wait for Him.

You meet the one who rejoices in doing righteousness, those who remember You in Your ways. Behold, You were angry, and we sinned; in these ways we have continued from of old—how then shall we be saved?
We have all become like one who is unclean, and all our righteous deeds are like a polluted garment; we all wither like a leaf, and our iniquities carry us away like the wind.
No one calls upon Your name, no one rouses himself to take hold of You; for You have hidden Your face from us and have caused us to melt away in the hand of our iniquity.
Yet now, O the LORD, You are our Father; we are the clay, and You are our potter; we are all the work of Your hand.
Do not be exceedingly angry, O the LORD, nor remember iniquity forever; behold, please look, for we are all Your people.
Your holy cities have become a wilderness; Zion has become a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.
Our holy and glorious temple, where our fathers praised You, has been burned with fire, and all our pleasant places have become a ruin.
After all this, O the LORD, will You restrain Yourself? Will You keep silent and afflict us beyond measure?
"I was sought by those who did not petition Me; I was found by those who did not quest after Me. To a nation that did not invoke My name, I said, 'Here am I, here am I.'"
"All day long I have extended My hands to an obdurate people, who pursue a path that is not good, walking after their own machinations."
"A people who perpetually provoke Me to My face, sacrificing in gardens and burning incense upon bricks;
who sit among tombs and lodge in secluded places; who consume swine's flesh, and whose vessels hold the putrid broth of abominations;
who say, 'Keep away from me; do not approach me, for I am too sacred for you.' Such people are a provocation that rankles in My nostrils, a fire that burns all the day.
Behold, it is inscribed before Me: I will not be silent, but I will requite, and I will requite into their bosom,

your iniquities and the iniquities of your fathers together, says the LORD, because they burned incense on the mountains and reviled Me on the hills; therefore I will measure their retribution into their bosom."
"Thus says the LORD: 'As fresh wine is found in a cluster, and one says, "Do not destroy it, for a blessing is in it," so will I act for the sake of My servants, that I may not destroy them all.
I will bring forth descendants from Jacob, and from Judah an heir of My mountains; My chosen shall inherit it, and My servants shall dwell there.
Sharon shall become a pasture for flocks, and the Valley of Achor a repose for herds, for My people who have sought Me.'"
"But you who forsake the LORD, who forget My holy mountain, who spread a table for Fortune and pour mixed wine for Destiny—

I will allot you to the sword, and all of you shall stoop to the slaughter, because when I called, you did not answer; when I spoke, you did not hearken; but you did what was evil in My sight and chose that in which I did not delight."

"Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: 'Behold, My servants shall eat, but you shall hunger; behold, My servants shall drink, but you shall thirst; behold, My servants shall rejoice, but you shall be put to shame.
Behold, My servants shall exult with gladness of heart, but you shall cry out in anguish of heart and wail for a crushed spirit.
You shall leave your name as an execration to My chosen, and the Lord the LORD will put you to death, but He will call His servants by another name,

so that whoever blesses himself in the land shall bless himself by the God of truth, and whoever swears in the land shall swear by the God of truth, because the former afflictions are forgotten and hidden from My eyes.'"
"For behold, I am creating new heavens and a new earth, and the former things shall not be remembered nor arise in the mind.
But be glad and rejoice forever in what I create; for behold, I create Jerusalem as a rejoicing and her people as a joy.
I will rejoice in Jerusalem and be glad in My people; no more shall the sound of weeping or the cry of distress be heard in it.

No more shall an infant there perish after a mere handful of days, nor an old man fail to complete his years; for one who dies at a hundred shall be reckoned a mere youth, and the sinner who attains a hundred shall be accursed.
They shall build houses and inhabit them; they shall plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
They shall not build and another inhabit; they shall not plant and another eat; for as the days of a tree, so shall be the days of My people, and My chosen shall long enjoy the work of their hands.
They shall not labor in vain, nor bear children for calamity; for they are the offspring of the blessed of the LORD, and their descendants with them.
Before they invoke Me, I will answer; while yet they are speaking, I will hear.
The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, the lion shall eat straw like the ox, and dust shall be the serpent's food. They shall not do harm nor destroy in all My holy mountain, says the LORD."
Thus says the LORD: “The heavens are My throne, and the earth is My footstool. What house could you build for Me, and what place would suffice as My resting place?”
“My hand has made all these things, and so they came into being,” declares the LORD. “Yet this is the one to whom I will look: the humble and contrite in spirit, who trembles at My word.”

He who slaughters an ox is as one who strikes down a man; he who sacrifices a lamb is as one who breaks a dog’s neck; he who presents a grain offering is as one who offers pig’s blood; he who burns incense is as one who blesses an idol. Indeed, they have chosen their own ways, and their soul delights in their abominations.

So I will choose harsh treatment for them and bring their fears upon them, because when I called, no one answered; when I spoke, they did not listen. They did evil in My sight and chose what displeased Me.

Hear the word of the LORD, you who tremble at His word: “Your brothers who hate you and exclude you for My name’s sake have said, ‘Let the LORD be glorified, that we may see your joy!’ But they will be put to shame.”
A voice of uproar from the city, a voice from the temple—the voice of the LORD repaying His enemies what they deserve.
Before she was in labor, she gave birth; before her pain came, she was delivered of a male child.

Who has heard such a thing? Who has seen such things? Can a land be born in a single day? Can a nation be brought forth in an instant? Yet as soon as Zion was in labor, she gave birth to her children.
“Shall I bring to the point of birth and not give delivery?” says the LORD. “Or shall I, who give birth, shut the womb?” says your God.
Rejoice with Jerusalem and be glad for her, all you who love her; rejoice greatly with her, all you who mourn over her,
that you may nurse and be satisfied from her comforting breast, that you may drink deeply and delight in her glorious abundance.
For thus says the LORD: “I will extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the nations like a flooding stream; you will nurse, you will be carried on her hip, and bounced upon her knees.
As a man whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you; you will be comforted in Jerusalem.
You will see, and your heart will rejoice, and your bones will flourish like grass; and the hand of the LORD will be made known to His servants, and He will show indignation toward His enemies.”
For behold, the LORD will come in fire, and His chariots like a whirlwind, to render His anger with fury, and His rebuke with flames of fire.
For by fire and by His sword the LORD will execute judgment on all flesh, and those slain by the LORD will be many.
Those who sanctify and purify themselves to go into the gardens, following one in their midst, eating pig’s flesh and the abomination and mice, shall come to an end together, says the LORD.
For I know their works and their thoughts; the time is coming to gather all nations and tongues, and they shall come and see My glory.

I will set a sign among them and send survivors from them to the nations—to Tarshish, Put, and Lud, those who draw the bow, to Tubal and Javan, and the distant coastlands that have not heard My fame nor seen My glory; and they shall declare My glory among the nations.

They shall bring all your brothers from all the nations as an offering to the LORD, on horses and in chariots and in litters and on mules and on dromedaries, to My holy mountain Jerusalem, says the LORD, just as the Israelites bring their grain offering in a clean vessel to the house of the LORD.
And I will also take some of them for priests and Levites, says the LORD.
For as the new heavens and the new earth that I make shall remain before Me, says the LORD, so shall your offspring and your name remain.
From new moon to new moon, and from Sabbath to Sabbath, all flesh shall come to worship before Me, says the LORD.

And they shall go out and look on the dead bodies of the men who have rebelled against Me; for their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched, and they shall be an abhorrence to all flesh.
The words of Jeremiah, son of Hilkiah, one of the priests at Anathoth in the land of Benjamin—
the word of the LORD came to him in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.
It came also in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the fifth month of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, when Jerusalem was carried into exile.
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
"Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you; before you came forth from the womb, I sanctified you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations."
Then I said, "Ah, Lord the LORD! Behold, I do not know how to speak, for I am only a youth."
But the LORD said to me, "Do not say, 'I am only a youth,' for you shall go to all to whom I send you, and whatever I command you, you shall speak.
Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you," declares the LORD.
Then the LORD stretched out His hand and touched my mouth, and the LORD said to me, "Behold, I have put My words in your mouth.
See, today I have appointed you over nations and over kingdoms, to uproot and to tear down, to destroy and to demolish, to build and to plant."
The word of the LORD came to me, saying, "Jeremiah, what do you see?" And I said, "I see a branch of an almond tree."
The LORD said to me, "You have seen well, for I am watching over My word to perform it."
The word of the LORD came to me a second time, saying, "What do you see?" And I said, "I see a boiling pot, tilting away from the north."
Then the LORD said to me, "Out of the north disaster will be poured out on all the inhabitants of the land.

For behold, I am calling all the families of the kingdoms of the north," declares the LORD. "They will come, and each will set his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem, and against all its surrounding walls, and against all the cities of Judah.
I will pronounce My judgments against them for all their wickedness, because they have forsaken Me and have burned incense to other gods and have worshiped the works of their own hands."
"But you, prepare yourself and arise and speak to them all that I command you. Do not be dismayed before them, lest I dismay you before them.

Now behold, today I have made you a fortified city, an iron pillar, and bronze walls against the whole land—against the kings of Judah, against its princes, against its priests, and against the people of the land.
They will fight against you, but they will not prevail against you, for I am with you to deliver you," declares the LORD.
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

“Go and proclaim in the hearing of Jerusalem: Thus says the LORD: I remember you—the devotion of your youth, the love of your betrothals, your following after Me in the wilderness, in a land not sown.
Israel is holy to the LORD, the firstfruits of His harvest; all who devour him shall be held guilty, and calamity shall come upon them, declares the LORD.”
Hear the word of the LORD, O house of Jacob, and all the families of the house of Israel.
Thus says the LORD: “What wrong did your fathers find in Me, that they went far from Me and walked after emptiness and became empty?

They did not say, ‘Where is the LORD who brought us up from the land of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness, through a land of deserts and pits, through a land of drought and of the shadow of death, through a land through which no one passed and in which no one dwelt?’
I brought you into a land of abundant yield to eat its fruit and its goodness; but you came and defiled My land, and made My heritage an abomination.

The priests did not say, ‘Where is the LORD?’ and those who handle the law did not know Me; the shepherds transgressed against Me; and the prophets prophesied by Baal and walked after what does not profit. “
Therefore I will still contend with you, declares the LORD; I will even contend with your children’s children.
Cross over to the coasts of Kittim and see; send to Kedar and consider carefully; see whether such a thing has ever happened.
Has a nation ever exchanged its gods, though they are no gods? But My people have exchanged their Glory for what does not profit.
Be appalled at this, O heavens, and shudder with great horror; be utterly desolate, declares the LORD.
For My people have committed two evils: they have forsaken Me, the fountain of living waters, and hewn out cisterns for themselves—broken cisterns that can hold no water. “
Is Israel a servant? Is he a home-born slave? Why has he become plunder?
Young lions have roared against him; they have raised their voices. They have made his land a waste; his cities are burned and without inhabitant.
Moreover, the men of Noph and Tahpanhes have ravaged the crown of your head.
Have you not brought this upon yourself by forsaking the LORD your God when He led you in the way?
And now what have you to do with the way of Egypt, to drink the waters of the Shihor? Or what have you to do with the way of Assyria, to drink the waters of the River?

Your own wickedness will discipline you, and your backslidings will rebuke you. Know then and see that it is an evil and bitter thing that you have forsaken the LORD your God and that you have no fear of Me, declares the Lord GOD of Hosts. “
For long ago I broke your yoke and tore off your bonds, but you said, ‘I will not serve!’ For upon every high hill and under every green tree you bowed down, prostituting yourself.
Yet I planted you as a choice vine, a seed of utmost integrity. How then have you turned degenerate before Me into a wild vine?
For though you wash yourself with lye and use much soap, yet your guilt is stained before Me, declares the Lord GOD.
How can you say, ‘I am not defiled; I have not gone after the Baals’? Look at your way in the valley; know what you have done. You are a swift young camel, restlessly tracing her paths.
A wild donkey accustomed to the wilderness, sniffing the wind in her craving—who can restrain her lust? All who seek her will not weary themselves; in her month they will find her.
Keep your feet from going bare and your throat from thirst. But you said, ‘It is hopeless! No, for I have loved strangers, and after them I will go.’
As a thief is ashamed when he is caught, so is the house of Israel ashamed—they, their kings, their officials, their priests, and their prophets—

saying to a tree, ‘You are my father,’ and to a stone, ‘You gave birth to me.’ For they have turned their back to Me and not their face; yet in the time of their trouble they say, ‘Arise and save us!’
But where are your gods that you made for yourself? Let them arise, if they can save you in your time of trouble; for according to the number of your cities are your gods, O Judah. “
Why will you contend with Me? You have all transgressed against Me, declares the LORD.
In vain I have struck your children; they accepted no discipline. Your own sword has devoured your prophets as a ravaging lion.
O generation, behold the word of the LORD: Have I been a wilderness to Israel, or a land of deep darkness? Why do My people say, ‘We are free; we will come to You no more’?
Can a virgin forget her ornaments, or a bride her wedding attire? Yet My people have forgotten Me for days without number.
How skillfully do you arrange your way to seek love! Therefore you have also taught the wicked women your ways.
Also on your skirts is found the blood of innocent lives; I did not find it by digging, but it is upon all these.
Yet you say, ‘I am innocent; surely His anger has turned from me.’ Behold, I will enter into judgment with you, because you say, ‘I have not sinned.’
Why do you wander so far to change your way? You shall be ashamed of Egypt as you were ashamed of Assyria.
From there also you will go out with your hands on your head, for the LORD has rejected those in whom you trusted, and you will not prosper through them.”

"If a man divorces his wife, and she departs from him and becomes another man’s, would he return to her again? Would not that land be utterly defiled? Yet you have prostituted yourself with many lovers; nevertheless, return to Me," declares the LORD.

"Lift up your eyes to the barren heights and see: is there any place where you have not been ravished? By the roadsides you sat waiting for lovers, like a nomad in the desert. You have defiled the land with your prostitution and wickedness.
Therefore the showers have been withheld, and no spring rains have fallen. Yet you have the brazen look of a prostitute; you refuse to be ashamed."
"Have you not just now cried to Me, 'My Father, You are the companion of my youth'?
Will He be angry forever? Will He maintain His indignation to the end? Behold, I have spoken, yet you have done evil things and prevailed."
In the days of King Josiah, the LORD said to me, "Have you seen what faithless Israel has done? She has gone up on every high hill and under every green tree and has prostituted herself there.
I thought that after she had done all these things she would return to Me, but she did not return; and her treacherous sister Judah saw it.
I saw that for all the adulteries of faithless Israel I had given her a certificate of divorce and sent her away. Yet her treacherous sister Judah was not afraid; she too went and played the harlot."
"Indifferent to her own defilement, she defiled the land and committed adultery with stone and wood.
Yet in spite of all this, her treacherous sister Judah did not return to Me with all her heart, but only in pretense," declares the LORD.
Then the LORD said to me, "Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.
Go and proclaim these words toward the north: 'Return, faithless Israel,' declares the LORD. 'I will not look on you in anger, for I am merciful,' declares the LORD. 'I will not be angry forever.
Only acknowledge your guilt, that you have transgressed against the LORD your God. You have scattered your ways to strangers under every green tree and have not obeyed My voice,'" declares the LORD.
"Return, O backsliding children," declares the LORD, "for I am your Master, and I will take you—one from a city and two from a clan—and bring you to Zion.
Then I will give you shepherds after My own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding."

"In those days, when you multiply and increase in the land," declares the LORD, "they will no longer say, 'The ark of the covenant of the LORD.' It will never come to mind, and they will not remember it or miss it, nor will another one be made.

At that time Jerusalem will be called The Throne of the LORD, and all the nations will be gathered to it, to the name of the LORD in Jerusalem. They will no longer follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts.
In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel, and they will come together from the land of the north to the land I gave your fathers as an inheritance."
"How I longed to make you My sons and give you a desirable land, the most beautiful inheritance of all the nations! I thought you would call Me 'My Father' and not turn away from Me.
But like a woman unfaithful to her husband, so you have been unfaithful to Me, O house of Israel," declares the LORD.
A voice is heard on the barren heights, the weeping and pleading of the children of Israel, because they have perverted their ways and forgotten the LORD their God.
"Return, O backsliding children; I will heal your backslidings," declares the LORD. "Here we are! We come to You, for You are the LORD our God.
Surely the idolatry of the hills and mountains is a delusion; surely in the LORD our God is the salvation of Israel.
From our youth, shame has consumed the fruit of our fathers' labor—their flocks and herds, their sons and daughters.

Let us lie down in our shame; let our disgrace cover us. For we have sinned against the LORD our God, both we and our fathers, from our youth even to this day. We have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God."
If you return, O Israel, declares the LORD, return to Me. If you remove your abominations from My presence, you will not be uprooted.
And you shall swear, “As the LORD lives,” in truth, in justice, and in righteousness; and the nations shall bless themselves by Him, and in Him they shall glory.
For thus says the LORD to the men of Judah and to Jerusalem: Break up your fallow ground, and do not sow among thorns.

Circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and remove the foreskins of your hearts, O men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, lest My wrath go forth like fire and burn with none to quench it, because of the evil of your deeds.
Declare in Judah and proclaim in Jerusalem, and say, “Blow the trumpet in the land!” Cry aloud and say, “Gather yourselves, and let us go into the fortified cities!”
Raise a standard toward Zion; flee for safety, do not delay, for I am bringing disaster from the north, and great destruction.
A lion has gone up from his thicket, and a destroyer of nations has set out; he has left his place to make your land a desolation; your cities will be laid waste, without inhabitant.
For this, gird yourselves with sackcloth, lament and wail, for the fierce anger of the LORD has not turned back from us.
And it shall come to pass in that day, declares the LORD, that the king and the princes shall lose heart, and the priests shall be appalled, and the prophets shall be astonished.
Then I said, “Ah, Lord the LORD! Surely You have utterly deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, ‘You will have peace,’ while the sword reaches to the soul.”
At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem: “A scorching wind from the bare heights in the wilderness toward the daughter of My people—not to winnow or to cleanse—”
a wind too strong for this will come for Me; now I will also pronounce judgments against them.
Behold, he ascends like clouds, and his chariots like the whirlwind; his horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, for we are ruined!
Wash your heart from evil, O Jerusalem, that you may be saved. How long shall your wicked thoughts remain within you?
For a voice declares from Dan, and announces disaster from Mount Ephraim.
Announce to the nations; behold, proclaim concerning Jerusalem: “Besiegers are coming from a far country, and they raise their voice against the cities of Judah.”
Like keepers of a field they are against her all around, because she has rebelled against Me, declares the LORD.
Your way and your deeds have brought these things upon you. This is your wickedness; how bitter it is, for it reaches to your heart!
My anguish, my anguish! I am in agony! Oh, the anguish of my heart! My heart pounds within me; I cannot keep silent, for I have heard the sound of the trumpet, the alarm of war.
Disaster upon disaster is proclaimed, for the whole land is devastated; suddenly my tents are destroyed, my curtains in a moment.
How long shall I see the standard and hear the sound of the trumpet?
For My people are foolish; they do not know Me. They are senseless children, without understanding. They are skilled in doing evil, but they do not know how to do good.
I looked on the earth, and behold, it was formless and void; and to the heavens, and they had no light.
I looked on the mountains, and behold, they were quaking, and all the hills were swaying.
I looked, and behold, there was no man, and all the birds of the heavens had fled.
I looked, and behold, the fruitful land was a desert, and all its cities were broken down before the LORD, before His fierce anger.
For thus says the LORD: “The whole land shall be a desolation, yet I will not make a full end.”
For this the earth shall mourn, and the heavens above shall be dark; because I have spoken, I have purposed, and I will not relent, nor will I turn back from it.
At the sound of the horseman and the archer every city flees; they go into the thickets and climb up among the rocks; every city is forsaken, and no one dwells in them.

And you, O devastated one, what will you do? Though you clothe yourself in scarlet, though you deck yourself with ornaments of gold, though you enlarge your eyes with paint, in vain you beautify yourself; your lovers despise you; they seek your life.

For I have heard a voice as of a woman in labor, the anguish as of one bearing her first child, the voice of the daughter of Zion gasping for breath, spreading her hands: “Woe is me, for my soul faints before the murderers!”

“Scrutinize the broad thoroughfares of Jerusalem; observe intently, take cognizance, and inquire in her open squares whether you can discover a single man—anyone who administers justice and seeks fidelity—and I will pardon the city.
Even when they protest, ‘As the LORD lives,’ they swear deceitfully.”

“O the LORD, do not Your eyes seek fidelity? You have struck them, yet they felt no anguish; You have consumed them, yet they refused correction; they have hardened their faces beyond stone and refused to return.”
“I said, ‘Surely these are only the poor; they have acted foolishly, for they do not know the way of the LORD, the justice of their God.’
I will go to the great and address them, for they know the way of the LORD, the justice of their God. Yet they, all together, have shattered the yoke and torn away the bonds.”

“Therefore a lion from the forest has struck them down, a wolf of the steppes will ravage them, a leopard keeps vigil over their cities: everyone who departs from them will be torn apart, because their transgressions are manifold and their backslidings have multiplied.
How can I pardon you? Your children have forsaken Me and sworn by what is no god; though I satiated them, they committed adultery and thronged to a prostitute’s house.
They are well-fed, lustful stallions, each neighing after his neighbor’s wife.
Shall I not call them to account for these things? declares the LORD. Shall not My soul take vengeance on a nation such as this?
“Ascend her walls and destroy, yet do not make a full end; remove her branches, for they do not belong to the LORD.
For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt treacherously with Me, declares the LORD.
They have denied the LORD and said, ‘He is not; no evil will come upon us; we will not see sword or famine.’
The prophets will be mere wind, and the word is not in them; thus shall it be done to them.
Therefore thus says the LORD God of Hosts: Because you speak this word, behold, I am making My words in your mouth a fire, and this people the wood, and it will consume them.

“Behold, I am bringing from afar a nation against you, O house of Israel, declares the LORD; it is an enduring nation, an ancient nation, a nation whose language you will not know, and whose words you will not hear.
Their quiver is an open grave; they are all mighty men.

They will devour your harvest and your bread; they will devour your sons and your daughters; they will devour your flocks and your herds; they will devour your vines and your fig trees; they will shatter with the sword your fortified cities in which you trust.
Yet even in those days, declares the LORD, I will not make a full end of you.

“When you ask, ‘Why has the LORD our God done all these things to us?’ you shall say to them, ‘As you have forsaken Me and served foreign gods in your land, so you shall serve strangers in a land that is not yours.’
“Declare this in the house of Jacob and proclaim it in Judah:
Hear this now, O foolish people without understanding, who have eyes but do not see and ears but do not hear.

Do you not fear Me? declares the LORD. Do you not tremble before Me, who set the sand as the boundary of the sea, an everlasting statute that it cannot pass? Though its waves toss, they cannot prevail; though they roar, they cannot pass over it.
But this people has a stubborn and rebellious heart; they have turned aside and gone away.
They have not said in their hearts, ‘Let us fear the LORD our God, who gives the rain, both the early and the latter, in its season, and keeps for us the appointed weeks of harvest.’
Your iniquities have turned these things away, and your sins have withheld good from you.
“For wicked men are found among My people; they lie in wait like fowlers who crouch; they set a trap and catch men.
Like a cage full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit; therefore they have grown great and rich.
They are fat and sleek; they have also excelled in deeds of evil; they do not plead the cause of the orphan, nor do they secure justice for the needy, yet they prosper.
Shall I not punish them for these things? declares the LORD. Shall not My soul take vengeance on a nation such as this?
“An appalling and horrible thing has happened in the land:
the prophets prophesy falsely, the priests rule by their own authority, and My people love it so. But what will you do when the end comes?”
Flee, sons of Benjamin, from the midst of Jerusalem! Blow the trumpet in Tekoa; raise a signal over Beth-haccerem, for evil looks down from the north, even great destruction.
Though she is beautiful and delicate, I will destroy the Daughter of Zion.
Shepherds and their flocks will come against her; they will pitch their tents all around her, and each will claim his own portion.
Consecrate war against her! Arise, let us go up at noon. Woe to us, for the day turns, and the shadows of evening lengthen.
Arise, let us go up by night and destroy her palaces.
For thus says the LORD of hosts: Cut down trees and cast up a siege ramp against Jerusalem. This is the city to be punished; she is full of oppression within her.
As a well keeps its water cold, so she keeps her wickedness cold; violence and destruction are heard in her; sickness and wounds are continually before Me.
Be corrected, O Jerusalem, lest My soul be estranged from you; lest I make you a desolation, a land uninhabited.
Thus says the LORD of hosts: They shall thoroughly glean the remnant of Israel like a vine; pass your hand again over the branches like a grape gatherer.

To whom shall I speak and give warning, that they may hear? Behold, their ears are closed, and they cannot listen. Behold, the word of the LORD has become a reproach to them; they have no delight in it.

I am full of the wrath of the LORD; I am weary of holding it in. Pour it out upon the children in the street and upon the young men gathered together, for both husband and wife shall be taken, the old with those full of days.
Their houses shall be turned over to others, their fields and wives together, for I will stretch out My hand against the inhabitants of the land, declares the LORD.
For from the least to the greatest, everyone is greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, everyone deals falsely.
They have healed the wound of My people lightly, saying, “Peace, peace,” when there is no peace.

Were they ashamed when they committed abomination? No, they were not at all ashamed; they did not know how to blush. Therefore they shall fall among those who fall; at the time I punish them, they shall stumble, says the LORD.
Thus says the LORD: Stand by the roads and look, and ask for the ancient paths, where the good way is, and walk in it, and find rest for your souls. But they said, “We will not walk in it.”
I set watchmen over you, saying, “Pay attention to the sound of the trumpet.” But they said, “We will not pay attention.”
Therefore hear, O nations, and know, O congregation, what shall befall them.
Hear, O earth: behold, I am bringing disaster upon this people, the fruit of their devices, because they have not paid attention to My words; and as for My law, they have rejected it.
What is this to Me, frankincense from Sheba, and sweet cane from a distant land? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices do not please Me.
Therefore thus says the LORD: Behold, I will lay stumbling blocks before this people, and fathers and sons together shall stumble over them; neighbor and friend shall perish.
Thus says the LORD: Behold, a people is coming from the north country, a great nation is stirring from the farthest parts of the earth.
They lay hold of bow and spear; they are cruel and have no mercy; their voice roars like the sea; they ride on horses, set in array as a man for war, against you, O Daughter of Zion.
We have heard the report of it; our hands drop down; anguish has seized us, pain as of a woman in labor.
Go not out into the field, nor walk on the road, for the sword of the enemy and terror are on every side.
O Daughter of My people, put on sackcloth and roll in ashes; make mourning as for an only son, most bitter lamentation, for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us.
I have made you a tester of metals among My people, a fortress, that you may know and test their ways.
They are all stubborn rebels, going about with slanders; they are bronze and iron, all of them corrupt.
The bellows are scorched; the lead is consumed in the fire; the refining is in vain, and the wicked are not separated.
They are called rejected silver, for the LORD has rejected them.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the the LORD was this:

the LORD said to Jeremiah, “Stand at the gate of the house of the the LORD and proclaim this word there, saying, ‘Hear the word of the the LORD, all you people of Judah who enter these gates to worship the the LORD.’
Thus says the the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: Amend your ways and your deeds, and I will let you dwell in this place.
Do not trust in deceptive words that say, ‘The temple of the the LORD, the temple of the the LORD, the temple of the the LORD—these are our refuge.’
For if you truly amend your ways and your deeds, if you truly execute justice between one person and another,
if you do not oppress the sojourner, the fatherless, or the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not walk after other gods to your own detriment,
then I will let you dwell in this place, in the land I gave to your fathers, forever and ever.”
“Behold, you are trusting in deceptive words to no avail.
Do you suppose you may steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, burn incense to Baal, and walk after other gods you do not know,
and then come and stand before Me in this house that bears My name, saying, ‘We are delivered!’—all so that you may continue in these abominations?
Has this house, which is called by My name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, even I have seen it, declares the the LORD.”
“But go now to the place I formerly established in Shiloh, where I first caused My name to dwell, and observe what I did to it on account of the wickedness of My people Israel.
