And now, because you persist in all these practices, declares the the LORD, and because I spoke to you earnestly and repeatedly, yet you did not listen, and I called to you, but you did not answer,
I will therefore deal with this house that bears My name—the very house in which you place your trust—and with the place I gave to you and to your fathers, just as I dealt with Shiloh.
I will cast you out of My presence, just as I cast out all your kindred, the entire seed of Ephraim.
As for you, do not pray on behalf of this people, nor raise a cry or petition for them, nor intercede with Me, because I will not hear you.
Do you not perceive what they are doing in the towns of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?

The children collect the wood, the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead dough, in order to make cakes for the queen of heaven and to pour out libations to other gods, thereby provoking Me to anger.
Is it I whom they provoke to anger? declares the the LORD. Is it not themselves, to their own disgrace?”

“Therefore, thus says the Lord, the the LORD: Behold, My anger and My wrath shall be poured out upon this place—upon human beings and animals, upon the trees of the field and the fruit of the ground—and it shall burn without being quenched.
Thus says the the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: Heap your burnt offerings upon your sacrifices and eat the flesh.
For when I brought your ancestors out of the land of Egypt, I did not speak to them or command them about burnt offerings or sacrifices.
But this is the word I commanded them: ‘Obey My voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be My people. Walk in all the way I command you, so that it may go well with you.’
Yet they did not listen or incline their ear; instead, they walked in the counsels and in the stubbornness of their evil heart, moving backward rather than forward.
From the day your ancestors left the land of Egypt until this day, I have sent to you all My servants the prophets, rising early each day and sending them.
Yet they did not listen to Me or incline their ear; rather, they stiffened their necks and acted more wickedly than their fathers.
Therefore you are to speak all these words to them, but they will not listen to you; you are to call to them, but they will not answer you.
And you are to tell them, ‘This is the nation that has not obeyed the voice of the the LORD its God or accepted discipline. Truth has vanished; it has been cut off from their mouths.’
Cut off your hair and cast it away; raise a lamentation on the barren heights, for the the LORD has rejected and abandoned the generation of His wrath.
For the people of Judah have done what is evil in My sight, declares the the LORD. They have set their abominations in the house that bears My name, thereby defiling it.
They have built the high places of Topheth in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and daughters in the fire—something I never commanded, nor did it ever enter My mind.

Therefore, behold, days are coming, declares the the LORD, when it will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter; for they shall bury in Topheth until no space remains.
The corpses of this people shall become food for the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the earth, and no one shall drive them away.

I will bring to an end in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, for the land shall become a desolation.”

At that time, declares the LORD, they shall exhume the bones of the kings of Judah, the bones of its princes, the bones of the priests, the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem from their sepulchers.

They shall spread them before the sun, the moon, and all the host of heaven, which they loved and served, after which they walked, which they sought, and before which they bowed down. They shall not be gathered or buried; they shall be left as dung upon the face of the earth.
And in every place where the survivors remain, wherever I have driven them, death shall be chosen rather than life by all the remnant of this wicked family, declares the LORD of Hosts.
You shall say to them, "Thus says the LORD: Do men fall and not rise again? If one turns away, does he not return?"
Why then has this people—Jerusalem itself—turned away in perpetual backsliding? They cling to deceit and refuse to return.
I have listened and heard, yet they do not speak aright; no one repents of his wickedness, saying, 'What have I done?' Each one rushes headlong in his own course, like a horse charging into battle.
Even the stork in the heavens knows her appointed seasons, and the turtledove, the swift, and the crane observe the time of their coming; but My people do not know the judgment of the LORD.
How can you say, "We are wise, and the law of the LORD is with us"? Behold, the lying pen of the scribes has made it a lie.
The wise are put to shame; they are dismayed and taken. Behold, they have rejected the word of the LORD; what wisdom, then, is in them?

Therefore I will give their wives to others and their fields to those who shall inherit them, because from the least to the greatest everyone is greedy for gain; from prophet to priest everyone practices deceit.
They have healed the brokenness of My people superficially, saying, "Peace, peace," when there is no peace.

Were they ashamed when they committed abomination? No, they were not at all ashamed; they did not even know how to blush. Therefore they shall fall among the fallen; at the time of their visitation they shall stumble, says the LORD.
I will surely gather them, declares the LORD. There are no grapes on the vine, no figs on the fig tree, and even the leaf has withered; and whatever I have given them shall be taken from them.

"Why are we sitting here? Assemble, and let us flee to the fortified cities and perish there, for the LORD our God has doomed us. He has given us poisoned water to drink, because we have sinned against the LORD.
We hoped for peace, but no good has come; for a time of healing, but behold, terror."
From Dan is heard the snorting of his horses; at the sound of the neighing of his stallions the whole land trembles. They come and devour the land and all that fills it, the city and its inhabitants.
"For behold, I am sending among you serpents, adders that cannot be charmed, and they shall bite you," declares the LORD.
My sorrow is beyond healing; my heart is faint within me.

Behold, the cry of the daughter of My people from a distant land: "Is the LORD not in Zion? Is her King not in her?" Why have they provoked Me with their carved images, with their worthless foreign idols?
The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved.
For the shattering of the daughter of My people I am shattered; I mourn, and horror has seized Me.
Is there no balm in Gilead, no physician there? Why then has the healing of My people not come?
Oh, that my head were a spring of water and my eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night over the slain of the daughter of my people!
If only I had in the wilderness a traveler’s lodge, I would abandon my people and withdraw from them, for they are all adulterers, an assembly of traitors.
“They bend their tongue like a bow; falsehood prevails over truth in the land. For they proceed from one evil to another, and they do not know Me,” declares the LORD.
“Let everyone beware of his neighbor, and put no trust in any brother, for every brother is a deceiver and every friend is a slanderer.
They deceive one another and do not speak the truth; they have trained their tongues to lie and wear themselves out in iniquity.
You dwell in the midst of deception; in their deceit they refuse to know Me,” declares the LORD.
Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Behold, I will refine and test them, for what else can I do because of the daughter of My people?
Their tongue is a deadly arrow; it speaks deceit. With his mouth a man speaks peace to his neighbor, but in his heart he sets an ambush.
Should I not punish them for these things?” declares the LORD. “Should I not avenge Myself on a nation such as this?”

“I will take up a weeping and wailing for the mountains, and a lamentation for the pastures of the wilderness, because they are desolate, with no one passing through; the sound of cattle is not heard; both the birds of the air and the beasts have fled and are gone.
I will make Jerusalem a heap of ruins, a haunt of jackals, and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant.”

Who is the man wise enough to understand this? To whom has the mouth of the LORD spoken, that he may declare it? Why has the land been ruined and laid waste like a desert, so that no one passes through?
The LORD said, “It is because they have forsaken My law, which I set before them; they have not obeyed My voice or walked according to it,
but have followed the stubbornness of their own hearts and gone after the Baals, as their fathers taught them.”
Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Behold, I will feed this people wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink.
I will scatter them among the nations that neither they nor their fathers have known, and I will send the sword after them until I have finished them off.”
This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Consider, and call for the mourning women; send for the skilled women.
Let them come quickly and raise a wail for us, that our eyes may overflow with tears and our eyelids gush with water.
For the sound of wailing is heard from Zion: ‘How we are ruined! We are greatly ashamed, for we have left the land, because they have thrown down our dwellings.’”
Now hear the word of the LORD, O women, and let your ears receive the word of His mouth. Teach your daughters to wail, and let each woman teach her neighbor a lament.
For death has climbed through our windows and entered our palaces, to cut off the children from the streets and the young men from the squares.
Speak: “This is what the LORD declares: ‘The corpses of men will fall like dung in the open field, and like sheaves behind the reaper, with no one to gather them.’”
This is what the LORD says: “Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom, nor the strong man in his strength, nor the rich man in his riches.

But let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows Me, that I am the LORD, who exercises loving devotion, justice, and righteousness on the earth. For in these things I delight,” declares the LORD.
“Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will punish all who are circumcised yet uncircumcised:

Egypt, Judah, Edom, the Ammonites, the Moabites, and all the inhabitants of the desert who clip the corners of their hair. For all these nations are uncircumcised, and the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.”
Hear the word that the LORD has spoken to you, O house of Israel.
Thus says the LORD: “Do not learn the way of the nations, nor be dismayed by the signs of the heavens, for the nations are dismayed by them.
For the customs of the peoples are vanity: one cuts a tree from the forest, the work of a craftsman's hands with an axe.
They embellish it with silver and gold; they secure it with nails and hammers, lest it topple.
They are like a scarecrow in a cucumber patch: they cannot speak, and they must be borne, for they cannot walk. Do not fear them, for they can do no harm, nor are they capable of any good.”
There is none like You, O the LORD; You are great, and Your name is great in might.
Who would not fear You, O King of the nations? For it is Your due; for among all the wise men of the nations, and in all their kingdoms, there is none like You.
Yet in one respect they are uniformly brutish and foolish: the instruction drawn from these vanities is mere timber.
Silver, beaten into plates, is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz—the work of a craftsman and the hands of a goldsmith. Their vestments are blue and purple; all are the work of skilled men.
But the LORD is the true God; He is the living God and eternal King. The earth trembles at His wrath, and the nations cannot endure His indignation.
Thus you shall say to them: “The gods that did not make heaven and earth shall perish from the earth and from under these heavens.”
He made the earth by His power; He established the world by His wisdom, and by His understanding He stretched out the heavens.
When He thunders, the waters in the heavens roar; He causes vapors to rise from the ends of the earth. He makes lightning for the rain and brings forth the wind from His storehouses.
Every man is brutish in his knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his idol, for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.
They are vanity, a work of delusion; in the time of their punishment they shall perish.
The Portion of Jacob is not like them; for He is the Maker of all things, and Israel is the tribe of His inheritance—the LORD of Hosts is His name.
Gather up your belongings from the land, you who dwell under siege.
For thus says the LORD: “Behold, I am about to hurl the inhabitants of the land away; I will distress them, that they may be captured.”
Woe is me for my hurt! My wound is grievous; yet I said, “This is my sickness, and I must bear it.”
My tent is destroyed, and all its cords are snapped; my children have departed from me, and are no more. There is no one left to pitch my tent or to raise its curtains.
For the shepherds are brutish and have not sought the LORD; therefore they have not prospered, and all their flock is scattered.
Behold, a report is coming—a great commotion from the north country—to make the cities of Judah a desolation, a lair of jackals.
O the LORD, I know that a person's course is not in his own power; it is not for a man who walks to direct his own steps.
Correct me, O the LORD, but with justice; not in Your anger, lest You reduce me to nothing.
Pour out Your wrath upon the nations that do not know You, and upon the families that do not call on Your name; for they have devoured Jacob, consumed him, and laid waste his homeland.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying:
“Hear the words of this covenant, and speak them to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
Say to them, ‘Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: “Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant—

the covenant that I commanded your fathers on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron furnace, saying, ‘Obey My voice, and do them, according to all that I command you; so you shall be My people, and I will be your God,’
that I may establish the oath that I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is this day.”’” Then I answered and said, “Amen, O the LORD.”
And the LORD said to me, “Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, saying, ‘Hear the words of this covenant and do them.
For I solemnly warned your fathers from the day I brought them up out of the land of Egypt until this day, rising early and warning them, saying, “Obey My voice.”

Yet they did not obey or incline their ear; instead, each one walked in the stubbornness of his evil heart. Therefore I have brought upon them all the words of this covenant, which I commanded them to do, but they did not do them.’”
And the LORD said to me, “A conspiracy has been found among the men of Judah and among the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

They have turned back to the iniquities of their forefathers, who refused to hear My words; they have gone after other gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken My covenant, which I made with their fathers.”
“Therefore thus says the LORD: ‘Behold, I am bringing disaster upon them that they cannot escape; though they cry to Me, I will not listen to them.
Then the cities of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem will go and cry to the gods to whom they burn incense, but those gods will not save them at all in the time of their trouble.’

For according to the number of your cities are your gods, O Judah; and according to the number of the streets of Jerusalem you have set up altars to that shameful thing, altars to burn incense to Baal.”
“So do not pray for this people, nor lift up a cry or prayer for them; for I will not hear them in the time that they cry to Me because of their trouble.”
“What right has My beloved in My house, when she has wrought so many wicked things? Can consecrated flesh pass from you to avert your calamity? For when you do evil, you rejoice.”
The LORD called your name, “A green olive tree, beautiful in form, bearing goodly fruit.” With the noise of a great tumult He has kindled fire upon it, and its branches are broken.

For the LORD of Hosts, who planted you, has pronounced disaster against you, because of the evil of the house of Israel and the house of Judah, which they have wrought against themselves, to provoke Me to anger by offering incense to Baal.
And the LORD made known to me, and I knew it; then You showed me their deeds.

But I was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter; I did not know that they had devised plots against me, saying, “Let us destroy the tree with its fruit, and let us cut him off from the land of the living, that his name be remembered no more.”
But, O the LORD of Hosts, who judges righteously, who tests the heart and mind, let me see Your vengeance upon them; for to You I have committed my cause.
Therefore thus says the LORD concerning the men of Anathoth, who seek your life, saying, “You shall not prophesy in the name of the LORD, lest you die by our hand”—
“Therefore thus says the LORD of Hosts: ‘Behold, I will punish them. The young men shall die by the sword; their sons and their daughters shall die by famine.
And there shall be no remnant of them, for I will bring disaster upon the men of Anathoth in the year of their punishment.’”
Righteous are You, O the LORD, when I plead my cause before You; yet I would reason with You concerning justice: why does the way of the wicked prosper, and why do all the treacherous live at ease?
You have planted them, and they have struck root; they have grown and even borne fruit. You are ever upon their lips, yet remote from their inmost being.
But You know me, O the LORD; You see me and test my heart toward You. Drag them away like sheep to the slaughter, and set them apart for the day of slaughter.
How long must the land mourn and the grass of every field wither? Because of the wickedness of those who dwell in it, beasts and birds are swept away; for they say, “He will not see our final end.”
If you have run with footmen and they have wearied you, how then will you compete with horses? If you have stumbled in a land of peace, what will you do in the thickets of the Jordan?
For even your brothers and your father’s house—even they have betrayed you; even they have cried out after you. Do not trust them, though they speak kindly to you. “
I have forsaken My house; I have abandoned My inheritance. I have given the beloved of My soul into the hands of her enemies.
My inheritance has become to Me like a lion in the forest; she has raised her voice against Me; therefore I have hated her. “
Is not My inheritance to Me like a speckled bird of prey, with other birds of prey circling against her? Go, gather all the beasts of the field; bring them to devour her.
Many shepherds have destroyed My vineyard; they have trampled My plot of land. They have turned My pleasant field into a desolate wasteland.
They have made it a desolation; desolate, it mourns to Me. The whole land is laid waste, because no one takes it to heart. “
On all the barren heights in the wilderness destroyers have come, for the sword of the the LORD devours from one end of the earth to the other. No one has peace.
They sowed wheat but harvested thorns; they exhausted themselves to no avail. Be ashamed of your harvests because of the fierce anger of the the LORD.” “

Thus says the the LORD concerning all My wicked neighbors who touch the inheritance that I gave My people Israel: Behold, I will uproot them from their land, and I will uproot the house of Judah from among them.
And after I have uprooted them, I will again have compassion on them and bring them back, each to his inheritance and each to his land. “
And if they will diligently learn the ways of My people—to swear by My name, ‘As the the LORD lives,’ just as they taught My people to swear by Baal—then they will be established among My people.
But if they will not obey, then I will uproot that nation and destroy it, declares the the LORD.”
This is what the LORD said to me: “Go and procure for yourself a linen loincloth, and place it about your waist, but do not let it touch water.”
So I bought a loincloth in accordance with the word of the LORD, and I placed it about my waist.
Then the word of the LORD came to me a second time:
“Take the loincloth that you bought and are wearing, and go at once to Perath and hide it there in a crevice of the rocks.”
So I went and hid it at Perath, exactly as the LORD had commanded me.
Many days later the LORD said to me, “Arise, go to Perath, and take the loincloth that I commanded you to hide there.”
So I went to Perath and dug, and I took the loincloth from the place where I had hidden it; and, behold, it was ruined—it had become altogether worthless.
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
“This is what the LORD says: In the same way I will ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.

These evil people, who refuse to listen to My words, who follow the stubbornness of their own hearts, and who go after other gods to serve and worship them, shall be like this loincloth—utterly useless.

For just as a loincloth clings to a man’s waist, so I have made the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to Me, declares the LORD, so that they might be My people for My renown, praise, and glory. But they would not listen.”

“Therefore you are to tell them that this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Every wineskin should be filled with wine.’” And when they reply, “Do we not surely know that every wineskin will be filled with wine?”

“Then you are to tell them that this is what the LORD says: ‘Behold, I will fill all the inhabitants of this land—the kings who sit on David’s throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem—with drunkenness.
I will smash them against one another, fathers and sons alike, declares the LORD. I will allow no pity, nor mercy, nor compassion to keep Me from destroying them.’”
Listen and give heed. Do not be proud, for the LORD has spoken.

Give glory to the LORD your God before He brings darkness, and before your feet stumble upon the twilight hills; while you wait for light, He turns it into the shadow of death and makes it deep gloom.
But if you do not listen, I will weep in secret because of your pride; my eyes will overflow with tears, because the LORD’s flock has been taken captive.
Say to the king and to the queen mother: “Take a lowly seat, for your glorious crowns have fallen from your heads.”
The cities of the Negev have been shut up, and there is no one to open them. All Judah has been carried into exile—wholly carried into exile.
Raise your eyes and see those coming from the north. Where is the flock entrusted to you, the sheep that were your pride?
What will you say when He sets over you those you have trained to be your allies? Will not pangs seize you like a woman in labor?
And if you say in your heart, “Why has this happened to me?”—it is because of the greatness of your iniquity that your skirts have been stripped off and your bare feet exposed.
Can the Cushite change his skin, or the leopard its spots? Then neither can you do good, you who are accustomed to doing evil.
“I will scatter you like chaff driven by the wind from the desert.
This is your lot, the portion I have measured out to you,” declares the LORD, “because you have forgotten Me and trusted in falsehood.
I will also pull up your skirts over your face, that your shame may be seen.
I have seen your abominations on the hills and in the fields. Woe to you, O Jerusalem! How long will you remain unclean?”
The word of the the LORD that came to Jeremiah concerning the drought.
Judah mourns, and her gates languish; they are bowed down to the ground in mourning, and the cry of Jerusalem ascends.

Her magnates have dispatched their servants to draw water; they have reached the cisterns and found them dry; they have returned with their vessels unfilled; they have been put to shame and confounded, and have veiled their heads.
Because the soil is fractured—for no rain has fallen upon the land—the tillers of the soil have been disgraced; they have covered their heads.
Even the doe in the field has calved and forsaken her offspring, because no herbage remains.
The wild asses have taken their stand upon the bare heights; they have snuffed the wind like jackals; their eyes have been consumed, because no verdure is to be found.
Although our iniquities bear witness against us, O the LORD, act for the sake of Your name; for our apostasies are numerous, and we have sinned against You.
O Hope of Israel, its Deliverer in the time of distress, why should You be as a sojourner in the land, as a wayfarer who turns aside to lodge for a night?
Why should You be like one bewildered, like a warrior unable to deliver? Yet You are in our midst, O the LORD, and we are called by Your name; do not forsake us.

Thus says the the LORD concerning this people: "They have loved to wander; they have not withheld their feet. Therefore the the LORD does not accept them; now He will remember their iniquity and visit their sins upon them."
The LORD said to me, "Do not intercede for the well-being of this people.

When they fast, I will not hearken to their cry; and when they present burnt offering and grain offering, I will not receive them with favor. Rather, I am bringing them to an end by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence."
Then I said, "Ah, Lord the LORD! Behold, the prophets are declaring to them, 'You shall not see the sword, nor shall you have famine, but I will give you enduring peace in this place.'"

The LORD said to me, "The prophets are prophesying a lie in My name. I have not sent them, neither have I commanded them, nor have I spoken to them. They are prophesying to you a false vision, divination, vanity, and the delusion of their own hearts.

Therefore thus says the the LORD concerning the prophets who prophesy in My name, although I did not send them, and who say, 'Neither sword nor famine shall befall this land'—by sword and famine those prophets shall be consumed.

And the people to whom they prophesy shall be cast out into the streets of Jerusalem because of famine and sword, and none shall bury them—neither them, nor their wives, nor their sons, nor their daughters—for I will pour out their own evil upon them."

You shall say this word to them: "Let my eyes stream with tears night and day, and let them not be still; for the virgin daughter of my people has been shattered with a great fracture, with an exceedingly grievous stroke."
If I go forth into the field, behold, those slain by the sword; and if I enter the city, behold, those languishing with famine. For both prophet and priest have roamed into a land they do not know.

Have You utterly rejected Judah? Has Your soul abhorred Zion? Why have You smitten us so that there is no healing? We looked for peace, but no good came; and for a time of healing, but behold, terror.
We acknowledge our wickedness, O the LORD, and the iniquity of our fathers; for we have sinned against You.
For Your name's sake, do not despise us; do not dishonor the throne of Your glory; remember Your covenant, and do not annul it with us.

Are there any among the futile idols of the nations that can cause rain? Or can the heavens themselves give showers? Are You not He, O the LORD our God? Therefore we place our hope in You, for You have made all these things.
The LORD said to me, “Even if Moses and Samuel were to stand before Me, My soul would not be inclined toward this people. Banish them from My presence, and let them depart.”

“When they say to you, ‘Where shall we go?’ you shall answer, ‘Thus says the LORD: Those destined for death, to death; those for the sword, to the sword; those for famine, to famine; and those for captivity, to captivity.’”

“I will summon four agents of ruin against them,” declares the LORD, “the sword to slay, dogs to drag them away, and the birds of the sky together with the beasts of the earth to consume and to ravage.”
“I will make them an object of horror to every kingdom of the earth, because of the atrocities Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, perpetrated in Jerusalem.”
“For who will pity you, O Jerusalem? Who will grieve for you? Who will turn aside to inquire after your welfare?”
“you have forsaken Me,” declares the LORD, “you have turned your back upon Me. Therefore I have stretched out My hand against you and brought you to ruin, and I am weary of relenting.”
“I will winnow them with a winnowing fork at the gates of the land; I will bereave them and destroy My people, because they have not turned from their ways.”
“Their widows shall outnumber the sand of the seas; I will send a ravager against the mothers of youths at noonday, and I will make anguish and dread descend upon them of a sudden.”

“The mother of seven shall pine away and yield up her spirit; her sun shall go down while it is yet daytime; she shall be disgraced and humiliated. As for their remnant, I will give them to the sword before their foes,” declares the LORD.
“Woe is me, my mother, that you brought me forth—a man of strife and discord to the entire earth! Though I have neither lent nor borrowed, all men revile me.”
The LORD said, “Surely I will set you free for your welfare; surely I will cause your enemies to supplicate you in the hour of disaster and in the hour of tribulation.
Can iron shatter iron that comes from the north, or bronze?
Your substance and your treasures I will surrender to plunder, without price, for all your sins, throughout all your territory.
I will cause your enemies to carry you into a land you have not known, for a fire is kindled in My anger; it will burn against you.”
“O the LORD, You know; remember me and take note of me, and avenge me upon my persecutors. In Your forbearance do not remove me; know that I suffer reproach for Your sake.
Your words were found, and I devoured them; they became my rejoicing and the gladness of my heart, for Your name is called upon me, O the LORD God of Hosts.
I did not sit in the council of revelers, nor did I make merry; under the pressure of Your hand I sat solitary, for You had filled me with wrath.
Why has my anguish become perpetual, and my wound incurable, declining to be healed? Will You be to me as a deceitful torrent, as waters that run dry?”

Therefore thus says the LORD, “If you return, I will restore you, and you shall stand in My presence. If you extract the precious from the worthless, you shall be as My mouth. They shall turn to you, but you shall not turn to them.
I will make you to this people a fortified wall of bronze; they will fight against you, but they shall not prevail over you, for I am with you to save you and to deliver you,” declares the LORD.
“I will deliver you from the hand of the wicked, and I will redeem you from the grasp of the ruthless.”
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying:
“You shall not take a wife for yourself, nor shall you have sons or daughters in this place.”
For thus says the the LORD concerning the sons and daughters born in this place, and concerning their mothers who bear them and their fathers who beget them in this land:

They shall die of deadly diseases. They shall not be lamented or buried; they shall be as dung upon the face of the earth. They shall perish by sword and famine, and their corpses shall become food for the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the earth.

For thus says the the LORD: “Do not enter the house of mourning, nor go to lament, nor bemoan them; for I have withdrawn My peace from this people,” declares the the LORD, “even lovingkindness and compassion.”
Both great and small shall die in this land. They shall not be buried, nor shall they be lamented; nor shall anyone gash himself or make himself bald for them.
Nor shall men break bread for them in mourning, to comfort them concerning the dead, nor give them the cup of consolation to drink on account of father or mother.
You shall not enter the house of feasting, to sit with them, to eat and to drink.

For thus says the the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: “Behold, I am about to remove from this place, before your eyes and in your days, the voice of mirth, the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride.”

And when you tell this people all these words, and they say to you, “Why has the the LORD pronounced all this great evil against us? What is our iniquity, and what is our sin that we have committed against the the LORD our God?”

Then say to them, “Because your fathers have forsaken Me,” declares the the LORD, “and have walked after other gods and served them and bowed down to them, and have forsaken Me and have not kept My law.
And you have done worse than your fathers; for behold, every one of you walks after the stubbornness of his evil heart, so as not to listen to Me.
Therefore I will hurl you out of this land into a land that you and your fathers have not known; and there you shall serve other gods day and night, where I will not show you favor.”
“Therefore behold, days are coming,” declares the the LORD, “when it shall no longer be said, ‘As the the LORD lives who brought up the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt,’

but, ‘As the the LORD lives who brought up the sons of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands where He had driven them.’ And I will bring them back to their land that I gave to their fathers.”

“Behold, I am sending many fishermen,” declares the the LORD, “and they shall fish for them; and afterward I will send many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every mountain, from every hill, and from the clefts of the rocks.
For My eyes are upon all their ways; they are not hidden from My face, nor is their iniquity concealed from My eyes.
And first I will doubly repay their iniquity and their sin, because they have polluted My land with the carcasses of their detestable things, and have filled My inheritance with their abominations.”

“O the LORD, my strength and my stronghold, and my refuge in the day of distress! To You the nations shall come from the ends of the earth and say, ‘Our fathers have inherited only lies, vanity, and things in which there is no profit.’
Can a man make gods for himself? Yet they are not gods.”
“Therefore behold, I will make them know—this once I will make them know My hand and My might, and they shall know that My name is the the LORD.”
The sin of Judah is written with an iron pen; with a diamond point it is engraved upon the tablet of their heart, and upon the horns of your altars.
Even their children remember their altars and their Asherah poles beside the verdant trees on the high hills.
O My mountain in the field, I will give your wealth and all your treasures for plunder, and your high places because of sin throughout your territory.
You will relinquish your inheritance, which I gave you; I will enslave you to your enemies in a land you do not know, for you have kindled a fire in My anger, and it will burn forever.
Thus says the LORD: "Cursed is the man who trusts in man and makes flesh his strength, whose heart turns away from the LORD.
He will be like a shrub in the desert; he will not see when prosperity comes. He will dwell in the parched places of the wilderness, in a salt land where no one lives.
Blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD, whose confidence is the LORD.

He will be like a tree planted by the water, sending out its roots by the stream. It does not fear when heat comes; its leaves remain green. It does not worry in a year of drought, nor does it cease from bearing fruit."
The heart is deceitful above all things and desperately sick; who can know it?
I, the LORD, search the heart and examine the mind, to reward each man according to his conduct, according to the fruit of his deeds.
Like a partridge that hatches eggs it did not lay is the man who amasses wealth unjustly; in the middle of his days his riches will forsake him, and in the end he will be a fool.
A glorious throne, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary.
O LORD, the hope of Israel, all who forsake You will be put to shame; those who turn away from me will be written in the dust, because they have forsaken the LORD, the fountain of living waters.
Heal me, O LORD, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved, for You are my praise.
Behold, they say to me, "Where is the word of the LORD? Let it come now!"
As for me, I have not shrunk from shepherding in Your service, nor have I coveted the day of calamity; You know that what proceeded from my lips was uttered before Your face.
Do not become a terror to me; You are my refuge in the day of disaster.
Let my persecutors be put to shame, but let me not be put to shame; let them be dismayed, but let me not be dismayed. Bring upon them the day of calamity; shatter them with a double destruction.
This is what the LORD said to me: "Go and stand at the gate of the people, through which the kings of Judah enter and go out, and at all the gates of Jerusalem.
And say to them, 'Hear the word of the LORD, you kings of Judah, and all Judah, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem who enter by these gates.'"
This is what the LORD says: "Guard your lives, and do not carry a burden on the Sabbath day or bring it in through the gates of Jerusalem.
Do not carry a load out of your houses on the Sabbath day, nor do any work, but consecrate the Sabbath day, as I commanded your fathers.
Yet they did not listen or incline their ear; they stiffened their necks and would not hear or accept discipline.
But if you diligently listen to Me, declares the LORD, and bring no load through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, and sanctify the Sabbath day by doing no work in it,

then kings and princes sitting on the throne of David will enter the gates of this city, riding in chariots and on horses—they and their officials, the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem—and this city will be inhabited forever.

People will come from the cities of Judah and the places around Jerusalem, from the land of Benjamin, from the foothills, from the hill country, and from the Negev, bringing burnt offerings and sacrifices, grain offerings and incense, and thank offerings to the house of the LORD.

But if you do not listen to Me to sanctify the Sabbath day, and to refrain from bearing a load and entering the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, then I will kindle a fire in its gates that will not be quenched, and it will consume the palaces of Jerusalem."
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying:
“Arise, and go down to the potter’s house, and there I will cause you to hear My words.”
So I went down to the potter’s house, and behold, he was working at the wheel.
And the vessel that he was making of clay was marred in the potter’s hand; so he made it again into another vessel, as it seemed good to the potter to make.
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying:
“O house of Israel, can I not do with you as this potter?” says the LORD. “Look, as the clay is in the potter’s hand, so are you in My hand, O house of Israel.
At one moment I might speak concerning a nation and concerning a kingdom, to pluck up, to pull down, and to destroy it.
But if that nation against whom I have spoken turns from its evil, then I will relent of the evil that I thought to do to it.
And at another moment I might speak concerning a nation and concerning a kingdom, to build and to plant it.
But if it does evil in My sight, not obeying My voice, then I will relent concerning the good with which I said I would benefit it.

“Now therefore, speak to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD: “Behold, I am fashioning evil against you and devising a plan against you. Return now, each one, from his evil way, and make your ways and your doings good.” ’”
But they say, “It is hopeless! For we will walk after our own plans, and each of us will do the stubbornness of his evil heart.”
Therefore thus says the LORD: “Ask now among the nations, who has heard such things? The virgin of Israel has committed a deed of shocking depravity.
Would the snow of Lebanon abandon the rocky heights of the field? Would the cold waters flowing from afar ever be cut off?
But My people have forgotten Me; they burn incense to vanity, and they have caused themselves to stumble in their ways, in the ancient paths, to walk in bypaths, not on a highway,
to make their land a desolation, a perpetual hissing; everyone who passes by it will be astonished and shake his head.
Like the east wind I will scatter them before the enemy; I will turn My back upon them, and not My face, in the day of their calamity.”

Then they said, “Come, and let us devise plots against Jeremiah; for the law shall not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come, and let us attack him with the tongue, and let us not give heed to any of his words.”
Give heed to me, O the LORD, and listen to the voice of those who contend with me.
Shall evil be repaid for good? For they have dug a pit for my soul. Remember that I stood before You to speak good concerning them, to turn away Your wrath from them.

Therefore give their children to famine, and pour them out by the power of the sword; and let their wives be bereaved and widows; and let their men be slain unto death, their young men struck by the sword in battle.
Let a cry be heard from their houses, when You suddenly bring a troop upon them; for they have dug a pit to take me, and hidden snares for my feet.

Yet You, O the LORD, know all their counsel against me unto death. Do not forgive their iniquity, nor blot out their sin from Your sight; but let them be overthrown before You; deal with them in the time of Your anger.
Thus says the LORD: "Go and buy a potter's earthen flask, and take some of the elders of the people and some of the elders of the priests.
And you shall go out to the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, at the entrance of the Potsherd Gate, and proclaim there the words that I will tell you."

And you shall say, "Hear the word of the LORD, O kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem. Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I am bringing calamity upon this place, so that the ears of everyone who hears of it will tingle.

Because they have forsaken Me and profaned this place, burning incense in it to other gods whom neither they nor their fathers nor the kings of Judah have known, and have filled this place with the blood of the innocent.
They have built the high places of Baal, to burn their sons in the fire as burnt offerings to Baal, which I did not command or speak, nor did it enter My mind."
"Therefore, behold, days are coming, declares the LORD, when this place shall no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter.

And in this place I will make void the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem, and I will cause them to fall by the sword before their enemies and by the hand of those who seek their lives; and I will give their carcasses as food to the birds of the heavens and to the beasts of the earth.
I will make this city a desolation and an object of scorn, so that every passerby will be appalled and hiss at all its wounds.

I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters, and they shall eat, each the flesh of his neighbor, in the siege and in the distress with which their enemies and those who seek their lives shall distress them."
And you shall break the flask in the sight of the men who go with you.

And you shall say to them, "Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Even so will I break this people and this city, as one breaks a potter's vessel that cannot be repaired; and men shall bury them in Topheth, for there will be no place to bury them.
Thus will I do to this place, declares the LORD, and to its inhabitants, making this city like Topheth.

The houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah shall be defiled, like the place of Topheth, even all the houses upon whose roofs they burned incense to all the host of heaven and poured out drink offerings to other gods."
Then Jeremiah came from Topheth, whither the LORD had sent him to prophesy, and he stood in the court of the LORD's house and said to all the people,

"Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I am bringing upon this city and upon all its towns all the calamity that I have spoken against it, because they have stiffened their necks, so as not to heed My words."
Pashhur the priest—son of Immer and chief officer in the house of the LORD—heard Jeremiah prophesying these words.
So Pashhur struck Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks in the upper gate of Benjamin at the house of the LORD.
The next day, when Pashhur released Jeremiah from the stocks, Jeremiah said to him, “The LORD has not called your name Pashhur, but Magor-missabib—‘Terror on Every Side.’

For thus says the LORD: ‘Behold, I am making you a terror to yourself and to all your friends; they shall fall by the sword of their enemies while your eyes behold it. I will also give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon; he shall carry them captive to Babylon and strike them down with the sword.

I will give all the wealth of this city—all its labor and all its precious things—and all the treasures of the kings of Judah into the hand of their enemies; they shall plunder them, seize them, and carry them off to Babylon.

And you, Pashhur, and all who dwell in your house, shall go into captivity; to Babylon you shall come, and there you shall die and be buried—you and all your friends to whom you have prophesied falsely.’”
You have deceived me, O the LORD, and I was deceived; You are stronger than I, and You have prevailed. I have become a laughingstock all day long; everyone mocks me.
For whenever I speak, I cry out and proclaim violence and destruction, because the word of the LORD has become for me a reproach and a derision all day long.
If I say, “I will not mention Him, nor will I speak anymore in His name,” then His word becomes like a burning fire shut up in my bones; I grow weary of holding it in, and I cannot.

For I have heard the whispering of many: “Terror on every side! Report him, and we will report him.” All my trusted friends watch for my stumbling, saying, “Perhaps he will be enticed, so that we may prevail against him and take vengeance upon him.”

But the LORD is with me like a mighty, awesome warrior; therefore my persecutors will stumble and not prevail. They will be utterly ashamed, because they have not prospered; their everlasting disgrace will never be forgotten.
O the LORD of Hosts, You who test the righteous and see the kidneys and the heart, let me see Your vengeance upon them, for to You I have committed my cause.
Sing to the LORD! Praise the LORD, for He has delivered the soul of the needy from the hand of evildoers.
Cursed be the day on which I was born; the day my mother bore me, let it not be blessed.
Cursed be the man who brought news to my father, saying, “A son is born to you,” and made him exceedingly glad.
Let that man be like the cities that the LORD overthrew without relenting; let him hear an outcry in the morning and a war cry at noon.
Because He did not kill me in the womb, so that my mother would have been my grave and her womb forever great with child.
Why did I come forth from the womb to see toil and sorrow and to spend my days in shame?
The word that came to Jeremiah from the the LORD when King Zedekiah sent Pashhur son of Malchiah and Zephaniah the priest, son of Maaseiah, to him with this message:

“Please inquire of the the LORD on our behalf, for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon is waging war against us. Perhaps the the LORD will deal with us according to all His wonders and cause him to withdraw from us.”
Jeremiah said to them, “You shall say to Zedekiah, ‘

Thus says the the LORD, the God of Israel: Behold, I am turning back the weapons of war that are in your hand—the very weapons with which you fight against the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who besiege you outside the wall—and I will gather them into the midst of this city.
I Myself will fight against you with manifest power and irresistible might, in anger, in fury, and in great wrath.
I will strike down the inhabitants of this city, both people and animals, and they will die of a great pestilence.

Afterward, declares the the LORD, I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah, his servants, the people, and those who survive in this city from the pestilence, the sword, and the famine, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of those who seek their lives. He will put them to the sword without pity, without compassion, and without mercy.’”
And to this people you shall say, “Thus says the the LORD: Behold, I set before you the way of life and the way of death.
Whoever remains in this city will die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence; but whoever goes out and surrenders to the Chaldeans who besiege you will live, and his life will be his prize.
For I have set Myself against this city for disaster and not for prosperity, declares the the LORD; it will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.”
And to the house of the king of Judah: Hear the word of the the LORD.

“O house of David, thus says the the LORD: Render just judgment each morning, and rescue the plundered from the hand of the oppressor, lest My wrath go forth like fire and burn with none to quench it, because of the evil of your deeds.
Behold, I am against you, O inhabitant of the valley, O rocky height of the plain, declares the the LORD—those who say, ‘Who shall come down against us, or who shall enter our dwellings?’
I will punish you according to the consequences of your deeds, declares the the LORD; I will kindle a fire in her forest, and it will consume all that surrounds her.”
Thus says the LORD: “Go down to the house of the king of Judah and speak this word there,
saying, ‘Hear the word of the LORD, O king of Judah, you who sit on the throne of David—you and your servants and your people who enter these gates.

Thus says the LORD: Execute judgment and righteousness, and deliver the plundered from the hand of the oppressor. Do not mistreat or do violence to the sojourner, the fatherless, or the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place.
For if you indeed do this, kings sitting on David’s throne will enter through the gates of this house, riding in chariots and on horses—he, his servants, and his people.
But if you will not hear these words, I swear by Myself, declares the LORD, that this house shall become a desolation.’”
For thus says the LORD concerning the house of the king of Judah: “You are Gilead to Me, the summit of Lebanon; yet I will surely make you a wilderness, cities uninhabited.
I will consecrate destroyers against you, each with his weapons; and they shall cut down your choice cedars and cast them into the fire.
Many nations will pass by this city, and each will say to his neighbor, ‘Why has the LORD done so to this great city?’
And they will answer, ‘Because they have forsaken the covenant of the LORD their God and bowed down to other gods and served them.’”
“Do not weep for the dead, nor mourn for him; weep bitterly for him who goes away, for he shall return no more, nor see his native land.
For thus says the LORD concerning Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah, who reigned in place of his father Josiah, who went out from this place: ‘He shall not return here anymore,
but he shall die in the place to which they have carried him captive, and he shall see this land no more.’”
“Woe to him who builds his house by unrighteousness and his upper rooms by injustice, who makes his neighbor serve for nothing and does not give him his wages,
who says, ‘I will build for myself a spacious house with roomy upper chambers, and cut out windows for it, paneling it with cedar and painting it with vermilion.’
Shall you reign because you boast in cedar? Did not your father eat and drink and do justice and righteousness? Then it was well with him.
He judged the cause of the poor and needy; then it was well. Is this not what it is to know Me?” declares the LORD.
“Yet your eyes and your heart are set on nothing but your gain, on shedding innocent blood, and on practicing oppression and violence.”

“Therefore thus says the LORD concerning Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: ‘They shall not lament for him, saying, “Alas, my brother!” or “Alas, my sister!” They shall not lament for him, saying, “Alas, my lord!” or “Alas, his glory!”’
He shall be buried with the burial of a donkey—dragged and cast out beyond the gates of Jerusalem.”
“Go up to Lebanon and cry out; lift up your voice in Bashan; cry out from Abarim, for all your allies are shattered.
I spoke to you in your time of security, but you said, ‘I will not listen.’ This has been your way from your youth, for you have not obeyed My voice.
The wind will drive away all your shepherds, and your allies shall go into captivity; then you shall be ashamed and confounded because of all your wickedness.
O inhabitant of Lebanon, you who nest in the cedars, how you will wail when pangs come upon you, pain like that of a woman in labor!”
“As I live,” declares the LORD, “though Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were the signet ring on My right hand, yet I would pluck you from there.
I will give you into the hand of those who seek your life and into the hand of those whom you dread—even into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and into the hand of the Chaldeans.
I will cast you out, and your mother who bore you, into another land where you were not born, and there you shall die.
But to the land to which they long to return, there they shall not return.”
“Is this man Coniah a despised, broken vessel, an object in which no one takes pleasure? Why are he and his offspring cast out and thrown into a land that they do not know?
O earth, earth, earth, hear the word of the LORD!
Thus says the LORD: ‘Write this man down as childless, a man who shall not prosper in his days; for none of his offspring shall prosper, sitting on the throne of David and ruling anymore in Judah.’”
“Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of My pasture!” declares the the LORD.

Therefore thus says the the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning the shepherds who shepherd My people: “You have scattered My flock and driven them away, and you have not attended to them. Behold, I will attend to you for the evil of your deeds,” declares the the LORD.
“Then I will gather the remnant of My flock from all the lands to which I have driven them, and I will bring them back to their fold, and they shall be fruitful and multiply.
I will raise up shepherds over them who will shepherd them, and they shall fear no more, nor be dismayed, nor shall any be missing,” declares the the LORD.

“Behold, the days are coming,” declares the the LORD, “when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, and He shall reign as King and act wisely, and He shall execute justice and righteousness in the land.
In His days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell securely; and this is the name by which He will be called: ‘The LORD is our righteousness.’”
“Therefore, behold, the days are coming,” declares the the LORD, “when they shall no longer say, ‘As the the LORD lives who brought up the people of Israel out of the land of Egypt,’

but, ‘As the the LORD lives who brought up and led the descendants of the house of Israel out of the north country and out of all the lands where I had driven them.’ Then they shall dwell in their own land.”
Concerning the prophets: my heart is broken within me; all my bones shake; I am like a drunken man, like a man overcome by wine, because of the the LORD and because of His holy words.
For the land is full of adulterers; because of the curse the land mourns, and the pastures of the wilderness are dried up. Their course is evil, and their might is not right.
“Both prophet and priest are profane; even in My house I have found their wickedness,” declares the the LORD.

“Therefore their way shall be to them like slippery paths in the darkness; they shall be driven and fall in it, for I will bring disaster upon them in the year of their punishment,” declares the the LORD.
“In the prophets of Samaria I saw an offensive thing: they prophesied by Baal and led My people Israel astray.

But in the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen a horrible thing: they commit adultery and walk in falsehood; they strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns from his evil; all of them have become like Sodom to Me, and its inhabitants like Gomorrah.

Therefore thus says the the LORD of Hosts concerning the prophets: Behold, I will feed them with wormwood and give them poisonous water to drink, for from the prophets of Jerusalem ungodliness has gone out into all the land,” declares the the LORD of Hosts.
Thus says the the LORD of Hosts: “Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you; they delude you. They speak a vision of their own heart, not from the mouth of the the LORD.
They say continually to those who despise Me, ‘The the LORD has said, “You shall have peace,”’ and to everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his own heart, ‘No disaster shall come upon you.’
For who among them has stood in the council of the the LORD to see and to hear His word, or who has paid attention to His word and listened?
Behold, the storm of the the LORD! Wrath has gone forth, a whirling tempest; it will burst upon the head of the wicked.
The anger of the the LORD will not turn back until He has executed and accomplished the designs of His heart. In the latter days you will understand it clearly.”
“I did not send the prophets, yet they ran; I did not speak to them, yet they prophesied.
But if they had stood in My council, then they would have proclaimed My words to My people, and they would have turned them from their evil way and from the evil of their deeds.
Am I a God at hand,” declares the the LORD, “and not a God far away?
Can a man hide himself in secret places so that I cannot see him?” declares the the LORD. “Do I not fill heaven and earth?” declares the the LORD.
“I have heard what the prophets say who prophesy lies in My name, saying, ‘I have dreamed, I have dreamed!’
How long shall there be lies in the heart of the prophets who prophesy lies, and who prophesy the deceit of their own heart,
who think to make My people forget My name by their dreams that they tell one another, even as their fathers forgot My name for Baal?
Let the prophet who has a dream tell the dream, but let him who has My word speak My word faithfully. What has straw in common with wheat?” declares the the LORD.
“Is not My word like fire,” declares the the LORD, “and like a hammer that breaks the rock in pieces?”
“Therefore, behold, I am against the prophets,” declares the the LORD, “who steal My words from one another.
Behold, I am against the prophets,” declares the the LORD, “who use their tongues and declare, ‘Declares the the LORD.’

Behold, I am against those who prophesy lying dreams,” declares the the LORD, “and who tell them and lead My people astray by their lies and their rashness, when I did not send them or command them, so they do not profit this people at all,” declares the the LORD.
“When this people or a prophet or a priest asks you, ‘What is the burden of the the LORD?’ you shall say to them, ‘You are the burden, and I will cast you off,’ declares the the LORD.
And as for the prophet or priest or any of the people who says, ‘The burden of the the LORD,’ I will punish that man and his house.”
“Thus you shall say every one to his neighbor and every one to his brother, ‘What has the the LORD answered?’ or ‘What has the the LORD spoken?’
But the burden of the the LORD you shall mention no more, for the burden is every man’s own word, and you pervert the words of the living God, the the LORD of Hosts, our God.
Thus you shall say to the prophet, ‘What has the the LORD answered you?’ or ‘What has the the LORD spoken?’

But if you say, ‘The burden of the the LORD,’ thus says the the LORD, ‘Because you have said this word, “The burden of the the LORD,” when I sent to you, saying, “You shall not say, ‘The burden of the the LORD,’”
therefore, behold, I will surely lift you up and cast you away from My presence, and the city that I gave to you and your fathers.
And I will bring upon you everlasting reproach and perpetual shame, which shall not be forgotten.’”

After Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had exiled Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, together with the officials of Judah, the artisans, and the metalworkers from Jerusalem, and had transported them to Babylon, the LORD showed me two baskets of figs placed before the temple of the LORD.
One basket held figs of exceptional quality, comparable to the first ripe figs; the other held figs so thoroughly spoiled that they were inedible.
Then the LORD said to me, “What do you see, Jeremiah?” I answered, “Figs: the very good ones are exceptionally fine, and the very bad ones are so thoroughly spoiled that they cannot be eaten.”
And the word of the LORD came to me:
“Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Like these good figs, so I will regard with favor the exiles of Judah whom I have sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans.
I will set My eyes upon them for good, and I will restore them to this land; I will build them up and not tear them down, and I will plant them and not uproot them.
I will give them a heart to know Me, that I am the LORD. They shall be My people, and I will be their God, because they will return to Me with all their heart.”

“But like the bad figs, which are so rotten that they cannot be eaten—thus says the LORD—so I will deal with Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, and the remnant of Jerusalem who remain in this land, together with those who dwell in the land of Egypt.
I will make them an object of horror and calamity to all the kingdoms of the earth, a reproach, a proverb, a taunt, and a curse in all the places to which I banish them.
I will send upon them sword, famine, and pestilence, until they are consumed from the land that I gave to them and to their fathers.”
The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah—that year being the first of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon—
which Jeremiah the prophet spoke to all the people of Judah and to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying:

From the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, even to this day—twenty-three years—the word of the LORD has come to me, and I have spoken to you again and again, but you have not listened.
And the LORD has sent to you all His servants the prophets, sending them early and often; yet you have neither listened nor inclined your ear to hear.
“Return, every one, from his evil way and from the evil of your deeds, and dwell in the land that the LORD has given to you and to your fathers forever and ever.
Do not walk after other gods to serve them or bow down to them, and do not provoke Me with the work of your hands; then I will do you no harm.”
“Yet you did not listen to Me,” declares the LORD, “so as to provoke Me to anger with the work of your hands to your own hurt.”

Therefore thus says the LORD of hosts: “Because you have not heard My words, behold, I will send for and take all the families of the north,” declares the LORD, “and Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, My servant, and I will bring them against this land and its inhabitants and against all these surrounding nations. I will devote them to destruction and make them a desolation and a hissing and perpetual ruins.
I will banish from them the voice of mirth and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the bride, the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp.
This whole land shall become a ruin and a waste, and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.”
“Then, when seventy years are completed, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation, the land of the Chaldeans, for their iniquity,” declares the LORD, “and I will make it desolate forever.
I will bring upon that land all My words that I have spoken against it, all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah has prophesied against all the nations.
For many nations and great kings shall themselves reduce them to servitude; I will requite them according to their deeds and the work of their hands.”
For thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, to me: “Take from My hand this cup of the wine of wrath, and make all the nations to whom I send you drink it.
They shall drink and stagger and go mad because of the sword that I am sending among them.”
So I took the cup from the LORD’s hand and made all the nations drink to whom the LORD sent me:
Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, its kings and officials, to make them a desolation, a hissing, a curse, and a ruin, as it is this day;
Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his princes, and all his people;
all the mixed multitude; all the kings of the land of Uz; all the kings of the land of the Philistines—Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod;
Edom, Moab, and the sons of Ammon;
all the kings of Tyre, all the kings of Sidon, and the kings of the coastland across the sea;
Dedan, Tema, Buz, and all who clip the hair at their temples;
all the kings of Arabia and all the kings of the mixed peoples who dwell in the wilderness;
all the kings of Zimri, all the kings of Elam, and all the kings of Media;
all the kings of the north, far and near, one with another, and all the kingdoms of the world that are on the face of the earth. After them the king of Sheshach shall drink.
Then you shall say to them, “Thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: Drink, be drunk, vomit, fall, and rise no more, because of the sword that I am sending among you.
And if they refuse to take the cup from your hand to drink, then you shall say to them, ‘Thus says the LORD of hosts: You shall drink!’”

“For behold, I begin to bring disaster upon the city that is called by My name, and shall you go unpunished? You shall not go unpunished, for I am summoning a sword against all the inhabitants of the earth,” declares the LORD of hosts.

“Therefore prophesy against them all these words, and say to them: ‘The LORD roars from on high and utters His voice from His holy habitation; He roars mightily against His fold. He shouts like those who tread grapes against all the inhabitants of the earth.
A tumult reaches to the end of the earth, for the LORD has a controversy with the nations; He enters into judgment with all flesh; He gives the wicked to the sword.’” declares the LORD.
“Thus says the LORD of hosts: ‘Behold, evil is going forth from nation to nation, and a great tempest is stirring from the farthest parts of the earth.
And those slain by the LORD on that day shall extend from one end of the earth to the other. They shall not be lamented or gathered or buried; they shall be dung upon the face of the ground.’”
“Wail, you shepherds, and cry out; roll in ashes, you leaders of the flock, for the days of your slaughter have come, and I will shatter you, and you shall fall like a precious vessel.
Flight shall perish from the shepherds, and escape from the leaders of the flock.
A voice—the cry of the shepherds and the wailing of the leaders of the flock! For the LORD is despoiling their pasture.
The peaceful folds are silenced because of the fierce anger of the LORD.
He has left His lair like a lion, for their land has become a waste because of the fierce anger of the oppressor and because of His fierce anger.”
At the commencement of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this oracle issued from the LORD:

“Thus says the LORD: Stand in the courtyard of the LORD’s house and speak to all the cities of Judah that come to worship there all the words that I have commanded you to speak; do not abridge a single word.
Perhaps they will listen and turn—each from his evil way—so that I may relent of the calamity I intend to inflict upon them because of the wickedness of their deeds.
And you shall declare to them, ‘Thus says the LORD: If you do not listen to Me and walk in My law, which I have set before you,
and if you do not heed the words of My servants the prophets, whom I send to you again and again—though you have not listened—
then I will make this house like Shiloh and this city a byword of execration among all the nations of the earth.’”
Now the priests, prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah uttering these words in the house of the LORD.
And as soon as Jeremiah had finished speaking all that the LORD had commanded him to speak to all the people, the priests, prophets, and all the people seized him, crying out, “You must surely die!”

“Why have you prophesied in the name of the LORD, saying, ‘This house will become like Shiloh, and this city will be desolate, without inhabitant’?” And all the people thronged about Jeremiah in the house of the LORD.
When the officials of Judah heard of these things, they ascended from the royal palace to the house of the LORD and took their seats at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD’s house.
Then the priests and prophets addressed the officials and all the people: “This man deserves death, for he has prophesied against this city, as you yourselves have heard with your own ears!”
Then Jeremiah said to all the officials and all the people, “The LORD sent me to prophesy against this house and against this city all the words you have heard.
Therefore, amend your ways and your deeds, and obey the voice of the LORD your God, so that He may relent of the disaster He has pronounced against you.
As for me, behold, I am in your hands; deal with me as seems good and right to you.

But be assured that if you put me to death, you will bring innocent blood upon yourselves, upon this city, and upon its inhabitants; for in truth the LORD has sent me to speak all these words in your hearing.”
Then the officials and all the people said to the priests and prophets, “This man is not deserving of death, for he has spoken to us in the name of the LORD our God!”
Then certain of the elders of the land rose and addressed the entire assembly:

“Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah and declared to all the people of Judah, ‘This is what the LORD of Hosts says: Zion shall be plowed like a field, Jerusalem shall become a heap of ruins, and the temple mount a forested ridge.’

Did Hezekiah king of Judah, or anyone in Judah, put him to death? Did not Hezekiah fear the LORD and entreat His favor, so that the LORD relented of the disaster He had pronounced against them? Yet we are on the verge of committing a great evil against our own lives!”
There was also a man, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim, who prophesied in the name of the LORD and prophesied against this city and this land in terms identical to all the words of Jeremiah.
When King Jehoiakim, together with all his warriors and officials, heard his words, the king sought to put him to death; but Uriah, upon hearing of it, was seized with fear and fled to Egypt.
Then King Jehoiakim dispatched men to Egypt—Elnathan son of Achbor, along with certain other men—
and they brought Uriah back from Egypt and delivered him to King Jehoiakim, who had him executed by the sword and cast his corpse into the burial ground of the common people.
Nevertheless, Ahikam son of Shaphan supported Jeremiah, so that he was not surrendered to the people to be put to death.
In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
The LORD said to me: Make for yourself straps and yoke-bars, and put them on your neck.

Then send them to the king of Edom, to the king of Moab, to the king of the Ammonites, to the king of Tyre, and to the king of Sidon, by the hand of the envoys who have come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah.
Give them this charge to deliver to their masters: ‘Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Thus you shall say to your masters:
‘“I made the earth—the human being and the beast that are upon the face of the earth—by My great power and by My outstretched arm, and I give it to whomever seems right in My eyes.
And now I have given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, My servant; I have likewise given him the beasts of the field to serve him.
All nations shall serve him, and his son, and his grandson, until the time appointed for his own land arrives; then many nations and great kings shall enslave him.

And the nation or kingdom that does not serve him—Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon—and does not put its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, I will punish that nation with sword, famine, and pestilence, declares the LORD, until I have consumed it by his hand.”’
And as for you, do not listen to your prophets, your diviners, your dreamers, your soothsayers, or your sorcerers, who say to you, ‘You shall not serve the king of Babylon.’
For they prophesy to you a lie, in order to remove you far from your land; I will drive you out, and you will perish.
But the nation that brings its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him, I will leave it in its own land, declares the LORD, and it shall till the soil and dwell in it.
And to Zedekiah king of Judah I spoke in accordance with all these words, saying, ‘Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live.’
Why should you and your people die by sword, famine, and pestilence, as the LORD has spoken concerning the nation that will not serve the king of Babylon?
Do not listen to the words of the prophets who say to you, ‘You shall not serve the king of Babylon,’ for they prophesy to you a lie.
For I have not sent them, declares the LORD, and they prophesy falsely in My name, to drive you out, so that you will perish—you and the prophets who prophesy to you.

And to the priests and to all this people I spoke, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD: Do not listen to the words of your prophets who prophesy to you, saying, “Behold, the vessels of the house of the LORD are being brought back from Babylon soon,” for they prophesy a lie to you.’
Do not listen to them; serve the king of Babylon, and live. Why should this city become a ruin?

And if they are prophets, and if the word of the LORD is with them, let them now intercede with the LORD of Hosts, that the vessels left in the house of the LORD, in the house of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem may not be carried away to Babylon.
For thus says the LORD of Hosts concerning the pillars, the sea, the stands, and the rest of the vessels that remain in this city,
which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon did not take when he carried Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon, together with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem.
For thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, concerning the vessels that remain in the house of the LORD, in the house of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem:
They shall be carried to Babylon, and there they shall remain until the day I attend to them, declares the LORD; then I will bring them up and restore them to this place.

In the fifth month of the fourth year, early in the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, Hananiah son of Azzur, the prophet from Gibeon, spoke to me in the house of the the LORD before the priests and all the people, saying:
“Thus says the the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: I have shattered the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Within two years I shall restore to this place all the vessels of the house of the the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon removed from here and carried off to Babylon.

I shall likewise restore to this place Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, together with all the exiles of Judah who were carried to Babylon, declares the the LORD, for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.”
Then the prophet Jeremiah spoke to the prophet Hananiah in the presence of the priests and all the people who were standing in the house of the the LORD:
“Amen! May the the LORD do so; may the the LORD establish the words you have prophesied, bringing back the vessels of the house of the the LORD and all the exiles from Babylon to this place.
Nevertheless, hear now this word that I speak in your ears and in the ears of all the people:
The prophets who preceded me and you from ancient times prophesied against many lands and great kingdoms—war, calamity, and pestilence.
As for the prophet who prophesies peace, only when his word comes to pass shall that prophet be recognized as one whom the the LORD has truly sent.”
Then Hananiah the prophet took the yoke from the neck of Jeremiah the prophet and broke it.

And Hananiah spoke in the sight of all the people, saying, “Thus says the the LORD: In this very manner, within two years, I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of all the nations.” And Jeremiah the prophet went his way.
After Hananiah the prophet had broken the yoke from the neck of Jeremiah the prophet, the word of the the LORD came to Jeremiah:
“Go and speak to Hananiah, saying, ‘Thus says the the LORD: You have broken wooden yokes, but in their place you have fashioned yokes of iron.

For thus says the the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: I have placed an iron yoke upon the neck of all these nations, that they may serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; and they shall serve him. I have given him even the beasts of the field.
Listen, Hananiah: The the LORD has not sent you, and you have led this people to trust in a lie.
Therefore thus says the the LORD: Behold, I will remove you from the face of the earth. This year you shall die, because you have spoken rebellion against the the LORD.’”
In the seventh month of that same year, the prophet Hananiah died.

These are the words of the epistle that Jeremiah the prophet dispatched from Jerusalem to the surviving elders among the exiles, together with the priests, the prophets, and all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had deported from Jerusalem into Babylon.
This dispatch followed the departure from Jerusalem of King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the court officials, the princes of Judah and Jerusalem, and the artisans and smiths.

The letter was entrusted to Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom King Zedekiah of Judah had commissioned as envoys to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, in Babylon, with this message:
“Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, to the whole company of exiles whom I have caused to be carried away from Jerusalem into Babylon:
Erect dwellings and inhabit them; cultivate gardens and consume their produce.
