Take spouses and beget sons and daughters; take spouses for your sons and give your daughters to husbands, so that they may bear sons and daughters; proliferate there, and do not let your numbers dwindle.
Moreover, pursue the welfare of the city into which I have exiled you, and intercede with the LORD on its behalf, for in its prosperity your own tranquility shall be found.
“For thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Let neither your prophets nor your diviners in your midst beguile you, and give no heed to the dreams you yourselves dream.
For they prophesy deceitfully to you in My name; I have not commissioned them, declares the LORD.”
“For thus says the LORD: When Babylon’s seventy years have run their course, I shall attend to you and fulfill My gracious promise by restoring you to this place.
For I know the designs I entertain concerning you, declares the LORD—designs of welfare and not of calamity, intended to bestow upon you a future and a hope.
Then you shall invoke Me, and you shall approach Me in prayer, and I shall heed you.
And you shall seek Me and find Me, provided you search for Me with your whole heart.

And I shall be found by you, declares the LORD, and I shall restore your fortunes, and I shall gather you from all the nations and from every region to which I have banished you, declares the LORD, and I shall return you to the place whence I exiled you.”
“Because you have asserted that the LORD has raised up prophets for you in Babylon.
Thus says the LORD concerning the king who occupies David’s throne, and concerning all the inhabitants of this city—your kinsmen who did not accompany you into exile:
Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Behold, I am unleashing upon them sword, famine, and plague, and I shall render them like vile figs, so putrid as to be inedible.

I shall hound them with sword, famine, and plague; I shall make them an object of terror to all the kingdoms of the earth, a curse, a spectacle of horror, a byword of derision, and a reproach among all the nations to which I have banished them.
Because they did not heed My words, declares the LORD, which I dispatched to them through My servants the prophets, assiduously and repeatedly; yet you refused to listen, declares the LORD.”
“Therefore, hear the word of the LORD, all you exiles whom I have dispatched from Jerusalem to Babylon.

Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, concerning Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who utter falsehood to you in My name: Behold, I shall deliver them into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar, king of Babylon, and he shall put them to death before your eyes.

And from them a byword of cursing shall be taken up by all the exiles of Judah in Babylon, praying that the LORD make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon consigned to the flames.

Because they perpetrated outrage in Israel, committing adultery with their neighbors’ wives and uttering falsehood in My name—something I never commanded—and I Myself know it and bear witness, declares the LORD.”
“You shall likewise declare to Shemaiah the Nehelamite:
‘Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Because you dispatched letters in your own name to all the people in Jerusalem, to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests,

claiming that the LORD has made Zephaniah priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to serve as an officer in the house of the LORD over every madman who prophesies, so that you might confine him in the stocks and in the collar.
Why, then, have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who prophesies to you?
For he has written to us in Babylon that the captivity is long and that we should build houses, dwell in them, plant gardens, and eat their fruit.’”
And Zephaniah the priest read this epistle in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.
“Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,
Send to all the exiles, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you, though I did not send him, and has caused you to trust in a lie,

therefore thus says the LORD: Behold, I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his offspring; he shall not have a man to dwell among this people, neither shall he behold the good that I will do for My people, declares the LORD, because he has spoken rebellion against the LORD.’”
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,
“Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: ‘Write for yourself in a book all the words that I have spoken to you.’

For behold, days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will restore the fortunes of My people Israel and Judah, says the LORD, and I will bring them back to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.”
These are the words that the LORD spoke concerning Israel and Judah.
For thus says the LORD: “We have heard a voice of trembling, of dread, and there is no peace.
Ask now, and see: can a male give birth? Why then do I see every man with his hands upon his loins like a woman in labor, and every face turned ashen?
Alas, for that day is great, without equal; it is a time of distress for Jacob, yet he shall be saved out of it.”
“And it shall come to pass in that day, declares the LORD of Hosts, that I will break his yoke from off your neck, and I will burst your bonds, and strangers shall no longer subject him to servitude.
They shall serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.”

“Therefore do not fear, O Jacob My servant, declares the LORD, nor be dismayed, O Israel; for behold, I will save you from afar, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob shall return, dwell in quiet, and be at ease, with none to terrify him.

For I am with you to save you, declares the LORD; for I will bring to a full end all the nations among whom I have scattered you, but I will not bring you to a full end; yet I will chastise you with justice, and I will not leave you unpunished.”
“For thus says the LORD: ‘Your wound is incurable, and your bruise is grievous.
There is no one to plead your cause, no remedy for your wound, no healing for you.

All your lovers have forgotten you; they do not seek you. For I have struck you with the stroke of an enemy, with the chastisement of a ruthless one, because of the multitude of your iniquity, because your sins have multiplied.
Why do you cry out over your wound? Your pain is incurable. Because of the multitude of your iniquity, because your sins have multiplied, I have done these things to you.’”
“Therefore all who devour you shall be devoured, and all your adversaries shall go into captivity; those who plunder you shall be plundered, and all who prey upon you I will make a prey.
For I will restore health to you, and I will heal you of your wounds, declares the LORD, because they have called you an outcast: ‘Zion, for whom no one inquires.’”

Thus says the LORD: “Behold, I will restore the fortunes of Jacob’s tents, and I will have compassion on his dwellings; and the city shall be rebuilt upon its mound, and the palace shall stand in its proper place.
Out of them shall come thanksgiving and the voice of merrymakers; and I will multiply them, and they shall not be diminished; and I will glorify them, and they shall not be small.
His children shall be as in former days, and his assembly shall be established before Me; and I will punish all who oppress him.”

“And his leader shall be one of them, and his ruler shall come forth from their midst; and I will bring him near, and he shall approach Me; for who is he who would dare devote his heart to approach Me? declares the LORD.
And you shall be My people, and I will be your God.”
“Behold, the whirlwind of the LORD has gone forth in fury, a sweeping tempest; it will burst upon the head of the wicked.
The fierce anger of the LORD will not turn back until He has fully accomplished the intents of His heart. In the latter days you will understand this.”
At that time, declares the LORD, I will be God to all the families of Israel, and they shall be My people.
Thus says the LORD: "The people who survived the sword found grace in the wilderness—Israel, when I went to give him rest."
The LORD has appeared to me from afar, saying, "I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore with loving devotion I have drawn you."
Again I will build you, and you shall be built, O virgin Israel. Again you shall take up your tambourines and go forth in the dances of the merrymakers.
Again you shall plant vineyards on the mountains of Samaria; the planters shall plant and enjoy the fruit.
For there is a day when watchmen will call in the hill country of Ephraim: "Arise, and let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God."
For thus says the LORD: "Sing aloud with gladness for Jacob, and shout among the chief of the nations; proclaim, give praise, and say, 'O the LORD, save Your people, the remnant of Israel.'"

Behold, I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the ends of the earth. Among them shall be the blind and the lame, the woman with child and she who is in labor; a great company shall return here.

They shall come with weeping, and with supplications I will lead them. I will guide them to streams of water by a straight path, wherein they shall not stumble; for I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is My firstborn.
Hear the word of the LORD, O nations, and declare it in the distant coastlands, and say, "He who scattered Israel will gather him, and will keep him as a shepherd keeps his flock."
For the LORD has ransomed Jacob, and redeemed him from the hand of one stronger than he.

They shall come and sing on the heights of Zion, and they shall flow unto the goodness of the LORD—for grain, and for new wine, and for oil, and for the young of the flock and of the herd. Their soul shall be like a watered garden, and they shall not languish anymore.
Then shall the virgin rejoice in the dance, and the young men and the old together; for I will turn their mourning into joy, and will comfort them, and make them rejoice from their sorrow.
And I will satiate the soul of the priests with fatness, and My people shall be satisfied with My goodness, declares the LORD.
Thus says the LORD: "A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping; Rachel weeps for her children and refuses to be comforted for her children, because they are no more."
Thus says the LORD: "Refrain your voice from weeping, and your eyes from tears; for your work shall be rewarded, declares the LORD, and they shall return from the land of the enemy."
And there is hope for your future, declares the LORD, that your children shall return to their own border.
I have surely heard Ephraim moaning: "You have chastised me, and I was chastised, as a calf unaccustomed to the yoke; turn me, and I shall be turned; for You are the LORD my God.
Surely after I was turned, I repented; and after I was instructed, I struck my thigh. I was ashamed, and even confounded, because I bore the reproach of my youth."
Is Ephraim My dear son? Is he a pleasant child? For as often as I speak against him, I still remember him. Therefore My heart yearns for him; I will surely have mercy on him, declares the LORD.
Set up signposts, make landmarks; set your heart toward the highway, the way by which you went. Return, O virgin of Israel, return to these your cities.
How long will you wander, O faithless daughter? For the LORD has created a new thing in the earth: a woman shall encompass a man.

Thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: "Again they shall speak this word in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I restore their fortunes: 'The LORD bless you, O habitation of righteousness, mountain of holiness.'"
And Judah and all its cities shall dwell therein together—farmers and those who wander with flocks.
For I have satiated the weary soul, and I have replenished every sorrowful soul.
At this I awoke and looked, and my sleep was sweet to me.
Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man and with the seed of beast.

And it shall come to pass that, as I have watched over them to pluck up, and to break down, and to throw down, and to destroy, and to afflict, so will I watch over them to build and to plant, declares the LORD.
In those days they shall no longer say that the children suffer for their fathers' sins.
But each shall die for his own iniquity; every man who does wrong shall bear his own punishment.
Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.

Not like the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt—a covenant which they broke, though I was a husband to them, declares the LORD.

But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the LORD: I will put My law within them, and write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be My people.

And no longer shall each teach his neighbor and each his brother, saying, "Know the LORD," for they shall all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest, declares the LORD; for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.
Thus says the LORD, who gives the sun for light by day and the fixed order of the moon and the stars for light by night, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar—the the LORD of hosts is His name.
If this fixed order departs from before Me, declares the LORD, then the offspring of Israel shall cease to be a nation before Me forever.

Thus says the LORD: "If the heavens above can be measured and the foundations of the earth below can be searched out, then I will cast off all the offspring of Israel for all that they have done," declares the LORD.
Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when the city shall be built for the LORD, from the tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
And the measuring line shall go out straight ahead to the hill Gareb, and shall turn about to Goah.

And the whole valley of the dead bodies and of the ashes, and all the fields as far as the brook Kidron, to the corner of the Horse Gate toward the east, shall be holy to the LORD. It shall not be plucked up or overthrown anymore forever.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah, king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
At that time the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was confined in the courtyard of the guard in the royal palace of Judah.

For Zedekiah, king of Judah, had imprisoned him, saying, “Why do you prophesy as you do, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD: Behold, I am giving this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it’?”

Zedekiah, king of Judah, will not escape from the hand of the Chaldeans, but will surely be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon; he will speak with him mouth to mouth and see him eye to eye.
He will take Zedekiah to Babylon, and there he will remain until I attend to him, declares the LORD. Though you fight against the Chaldeans, you will not succeed.
Jeremiah said, “The word of the LORD came to me:”
“Behold, Hanamel, the son of Shallum your uncle, is coming to you, saying, ‘Buy for yourself my field that is in Anathoth, for the right of redemption is yours to buy it.’”

Then, just as the LORD had said, my cousin Hanamel came to me in the courtyard of the guard and said, “Buy my field that is in Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin, for the right of inheritance and redemption is yours; buy it for yourself.” Then I knew that this was the word of the LORD.
So I bought the field in Anathoth from my cousin Hanamel, and I weighed out to him seventeen shekels of silver.
I signed and sealed the deed, called witnesses, and weighed the silver on the scales.
Then I took the sealed deed of purchase, containing the terms and conditions, together with the unsealed copy,

and I gave the deed to Baruch son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, in the presence of my cousin Hanamel, in the presence of the witnesses who signed the deed of purchase, and in the presence of all the Judeans who were sitting in the courtyard of the guard.
In their presence I gave Baruch these instructions:
“Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Take these documents, both the sealed deed of purchase and this unsealed copy, and put them in an earthen vessel, that they may endure for many days.
For thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Houses and fields and vineyards shall again be bought in this land.”
After I had given the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the LORD:
“Ah, Lord the LORD, You have made the heavens and the earth by Your great power and outstretched arm; nothing is too hard for You.
You show steadfast love to thousands, yet bring the iniquity of the fathers into the bosom of their children after them. O great and mighty God, whose name is the LORD of Hosts,
great in counsel and mighty in deed, whose eyes are open to all the ways of humankind, to give to each according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds.
“You performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, as You do to this day, both in Israel and among humankind, and You have made a name for Yourself, as it is this day.
You brought Your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with great terror.
You gave them this land, which You had sworn to give to their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.

“They came in and took possession of it, but they did not obey Your voice or walk in Your law; they did not do all that You commanded them to do. Therefore You have brought all this calamity upon them.

Behold, the siege ramps have come up to the city to capture it, and the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans who fight against it, because of the sword, famine, and plague; and what You have spoken has come to pass, and behold, You see it.
Yet You have said to me, ‘Buy the field for silver and call witnesses,’ although the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.”
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
“I am the LORD, the God of all flesh. Is anything too hard for Me?
Therefore thus says the LORD: Behold, I am giving this city into the hand of the Chaldeans and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

The Chaldeans who are fighting against this city will come in and set it on fire, and they will burn it down, along with the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to Baal and poured out drink offerings to other gods, to provoke Me to anger.

For the children of Israel and the children of Judah have done nothing but evil in My sight from their youth; indeed, the children of Israel have done nothing but provoke Me to anger by the work of their hands, declares the LORD.
For this city has been to Me a cause of My anger and My wrath from the day they built it until this day, so that I must remove it from My sight, “

because of all the evil of the children of Israel and the children of Judah, which they have done to provoke Me to anger—they, their kings, their officials, their priests, their prophets, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
They turned their backs to Me and not their faces; though I taught them again and again, they would not listen to receive instruction.
They set their abominations in the house that is called by My name, to defile it.

They built the high places of Baal in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, to make their sons and daughters pass through the fire to Molech, which I did not command them, nor did it enter My mind that they should do this abomination, to make Judah sin. “
You are saying about this city, ‘By sword, famine, and plague it will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon’; but thus says the LORD, the God of Israel:

Behold, I will gather them from all the lands to which I have driven them in My anger, in My great wrath, and in My fury, and I will bring them back to this place, and I will make them dwell in safety.
They shall be My people, and I will be their God.
I will give them one heart and one way, that they may fear Me always, for their good and for the good of their children after them.
I will make with them an everlasting covenant, that I will not turn away from doing good to them; and I will put My fear in their hearts, so that they will not depart from Me.
I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land in truth, with all My heart and with all My soul. “
For thus says the LORD: Just as I have brought all this great calamity upon this people, so I will bring upon them all the good that I have promised them.
Fields shall be bought in this land of which you say, ‘It is a desolate waste, without man or beast; it has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans.’

They shall buy fields for silver, and sign and seal deeds, and call witnesses, in the land of Benjamin, in the outskirts of Jerusalem, in the cities of Judah, in the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the lowland, and in the cities of the Negev; for I will restore their fortunes, declares the LORD.”
While Jeremiah was still confined in the courtyard of the guard, the word of the LORD came to him a second time, saying,
“Thus says the LORD, who brings it into being, who fashions it and establishes it—the LORD is His name:
‘Call to Me, and I will answer you, and I will declare to you great and inscrutable things that you have not known.’”
“For thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning the houses of this city and the palaces of the kings of Judah that have been torn down for the siege ramps and for the sword:
the Chaldeans are coming in to fight and to fill them with the corpses of the men whom I struck down in My anger and wrath, and because of all their wickedness I hid My face from this city.”
“Behold, I am bringing to it healing and cure, and I will heal them, and I will reveal to them an abundance of peace and truth.
I will restore the fortunes of Judah and Israel, and I will rebuild them as in former times.
I will cleanse them from all their iniquity by which they sinned against Me, and I will pardon all their iniquities by which they sinned against Me and rebelled against Me.

And it shall be to Me a name of joy, a praise, and a glory before all the nations of the earth who hear of all the good that I do for them; and they shall fear and tremble because of all the goodness and because of all the peace that I procure for it.”

“Thus says the LORD: In this place of which you say, ‘It is desolate, without man and without beast,’ in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem that are desolate, without inhabitant and without man and without beast,

there shall again be heard the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voice of those who bring offerings of thanksgiving to the house of the LORD, saying, ‘Give thanks to the LORD of hosts, for the LORD is good, for His steadfast love endures forever,’ for I will restore the fortunes of the land as in former times, says the LORD.”
“Thus says the LORD of hosts: In this place that is waste, without man and without beast, and in all its cities, there shall yet be pastures for shepherds causing their flocks to lie down.

In the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the Shephelah, in the cities of the Negeb, in the land of Benjamin, in the environs of Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, flocks shall again pass under the hand of the one who counts them, says the LORD.”
“Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will fulfill the good word that I have spoken concerning the house of Israel and concerning the house of Judah.
In those days and at that time I will cause a righteous Branch to spring up for David, and He shall execute justice and righteousness in the land.
In those days Judah will be saved, and Jerusalem will dwell securely; and this is the name by which she will be called: ‘The LORD Our Righteousness.’”
“For thus says the LORD: David shall never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel,
and the Levitical priests shall never lack a man in My presence to offer burnt offerings, to burn grain offerings, and to make sacrifices.”
And the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,
“Thus says the LORD: If you can break My covenant with the day and My covenant with the night, so that day and night will not come at their appointed time,
then also My covenant with David My servant may be broken, so that he shall not have a son to reign on his throne, and My covenant with the Levitical priests My ministers.
As the host of heaven cannot be numbered and the sand of the sea cannot be measured, so I will multiply the offspring of David My servant, and the Levites who minister to Me.”
The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,

“Have you not observed what this people have spoken, saying, ‘The two families that the LORD chose He has rejected’? Thus they have despised My people so that they are no longer a nation in their sight.
Thus says the LORD: If I have not established My covenant with day and night and the ordinances of heaven and earth,

then I will also reject the offspring of Jacob and David My servant and will not choose one of his offspring to rule over the offspring of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. For I will restore their fortunes and have compassion on them.”

The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, when Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, together with all his army, all the kingdoms of the earth under his dominion, and all the peoples, were waging war against Jerusalem and against all its cities, was this:

“Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah, and say to him, ‘Thus says the LORD: Behold, I am delivering this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall burn it with fire.

And you shall not escape from his hand, but you shall surely be captured and delivered into his hand; your eyes shall see the eyes of the king of Babylon, and his mouth shall speak to your mouth, and you shall go to Babylon.
Yet hear the word of the LORD, O Zedekiah king of Judah: Thus says the LORD concerning you: You shall not die by the sword.

You shall die in peace; and as spices were burned for your fathers, the former kings who were before you, so they shall burn spices for you and lament for you, saying, “Alas, my lord!” For I have spoken the word, declares the LORD.’”
Then Jeremiah the prophet spoke all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem,

while the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and against all the remaining cities of Judah—Lachish and Azekah—for among the cities of Judah only these fortified cities still remained.
The word came to Jeremiah from the LORD after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem to proclaim liberty to them,
so that every man would set free his Hebrew slave, male and female, and no one would any longer hold a fellow Jew in bondage.

All the officials and all the people who had entered into the covenant heard and set free, each his male servant and each his female servant, so that they would no longer enslave them; they heard and released them.
But afterward they turned back and brought back the male and female servants whom they had set free, and subjected them once more to servitude.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,
“Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I made a covenant with your fathers on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, saying,

‘At the end of seven years each of you shall set free his Hebrew brother who has been sold to you and has served you six years; you shall send him away free from you.’ But your fathers did not listen to Me or incline their ear.
You recently turned and did what was right in My eyes by proclaiming liberty, each to his neighbor, and you made a covenant before Me in the house that is called by My name.

But then you turned back and profaned My name when each of you took back his male servant and each his female servant, whom you had set free to go wherever they wished, and you subjected them to be your male and female servants.

Therefore thus says the LORD: You have not obeyed Me by proclaiming liberty, each to his brother and each to his neighbor; behold, I proclaim liberty for you, declares the LORD, to the sword, to pestilence, and to famine, and I will make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
“And I will make the men who transgressed My covenant, who did not establish the words of the covenant that they made before Me, when they cut the calf in two and passed between its parts—
the officials of Judah, the officials of Jerusalem, the eunuchs, the priests, and all the people of the land who passed between the parts of the calf—
I will give them into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their lives. Their dead bodies shall be food for the birds of the heavens and for the beasts of the earth.

And Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials I will give into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their lives, and into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, which has withdrawn from you.

Behold, I will issue a command, declares the LORD, and I will bring them back to this city. They will fight against it and capture it and burn it with fire. I will make the cities of Judah a desolation without inhabitant.”
The oracle that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying:
"Go to the house of the Rechabites, speak to them, bring them into one of the chambers of the house of the LORD, and give them wine to drink."
So Jeremiah took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah son of Habaziniah, his brothers, all his sons, and the entire house of the Rechabites.

He brought them into the house of the LORD, into the chamber of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God, which lay beside the chamber of the officials, above the chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum, keeper of the threshold.
Then he set before the Rechabites goblets full of wine and cups, and said to them, "Drink wine."
They replied, "We will not drink wine, for our father Jonadab son of Rechab commanded us that we and our sons should never drink wine.

He also commanded that we should not build houses, sow seed, or plant vineyards for ourselves, that no vineyard should belong to us, and that we should dwell in tents all our days, so that we might live many days upon the face of the land where we sojourn.
So we have obeyed the voice of our father Jonadab son of Rechab in all that he commanded us: we, our wives, our sons, and our daughters have never drunk wine.
We have not built houses in which to dwell, and we have possessed no vineyard, field, or seed.
We have dwelt in tents and have done everything our father Jonadab commanded us.
But when Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came up against the land, we determined to go to Jerusalem, away from the armies of the Chaldeans and the Arameans, and so we have dwelt in Jerusalem."
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,
"Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Go and say to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, 'Will you not receive instruction and listen to My words?' declares the LORD.

The words of Jonadab son of Rechab, which he commanded his sons not to drink wine, have been upheld; they have not drunk wine to this day, because they obeyed their father's command. But I have spoken to you repeatedly and earnestly, and you have not listened to Me.

I have sent to you all My servants the prophets, repeatedly and earnestly, saying, 'Turn now, each of you, from his evil way, amend your conduct, and do not go after other gods to serve them; then you shall dwell in the land that I gave to you and to your fathers.' Yet you have not inclined your ear or listened to Me.
Because the sons of Jonadab son of Rechab have kept the commandment of their father that he commanded them, while this people has not listened to Me.

Therefore thus says the LORD, the God of Hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I am bringing upon Judah and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the calamity that I have spoken against them, because I spoke to them and they did not listen, and I called to them and they did not answer."

And to the house of the Rechabites Jeremiah said, "Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Because you obeyed the commandment of your father Jonadab and kept all his commandments and did everything he commanded you,
therefore thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Jonadab son of Rechab shall never lack a man to stand before Me all the days."
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:

“Take for yourself a scroll of a book, and write on it all the words that I have spoken to you concerning Israel, concerning Judah, and concerning all the nations, from the day I first spoke to you in the days of Josiah until this day.
Perhaps the house of Judah will hear of all the disaster that I intend to bring upon them, so that each one may turn from his evil way, and I may forgive their iniquity and their sin.”
Then Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote on a scroll of a book, from the mouth of Jeremiah, all the words of the LORD that He had spoken to him.
Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, “I am confined; I cannot go into the house of the LORD.

So you go, and on the day of the fast read in the hearing of the people the words of the LORD from the scroll that you have written at My dictation; you shall also read them in the hearing of all Judah who come from their cities.
Perhaps the LORD will accept their supplication, and each will turn from his evil way, for great is the anger and the wrath that the LORD has pronounced against this people.”
Baruch son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading in the house of the LORD from the book the words of the LORD.

In the ninth month of the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, a fast was proclaimed before the LORD for all the people in Jerusalem and for all the people who came to Jerusalem from the cities of Judah.

Then Baruch read from the book the words of Jeremiah in the hearing of all the people, in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court, at the entry of the New Gate of the house of the LORD.
When Micaiah son of Gemariah, son of Shaphan, heard all the words of the LORD from the book,

he went down to the king’s house, into the scribe’s chamber, where all the officials were sitting—Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the officials.
Micaiah declared to them all the words he had heard when Baruch read the book in the hearing of the people.

Then all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi, to Baruch, saying, “Take in your hand the scroll that you have read in the hearing of the people, and come.” So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
They said to him, “Sit down, please, and read it in our ears.” So Baruch read it in their ears.
When they heard all the words, they regarded one another with alarm and said to Baruch, “We will surely tell the king all these words.”
They asked Baruch, “Tell us, please, how did you write all these words from his mouth?”
Baruch answered them, “He proclaimed all these words to me, and I wrote them with ink on the book.”
Then the officials said to Baruch, “Go, hide, you and Jeremiah, and let no man know where you are.”
They went to the king in the court, but they had deposited the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and they told the king all the words.

Then the king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and he took it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe. Jehudi read it in the hearing of the king and in the hearing of all the officials who stood beside the king.
Now the king was sitting in the winter house in the ninth month, with a fire burning in the brazier before him.

When Jehudi had read three or four columns, the king cut it with the scribe’s knife and threw it into the fire that was in the brazier, until the whole scroll was consumed in the fire that was in the brazier.
Yet neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words was afraid, nor did they tear their garments.
Even Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, but he would not listen to them.
Then the king commanded Jerahmeel the king’s son, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet, but the LORD hid them.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, after the king had burned the scroll and the words that Baruch had written at Jeremiah’s dictation, saying,
“Take for yourself another scroll, and write on it all the former words that were on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

Concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say, ‘Thus says the LORD: “You have burned this scroll, saying, ‘Why have you written in it, saying, “The king of Babylon will certainly come and destroy this land, and will cause to cease from it man and beast”’?
Therefore thus says the LORD concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: He shall have no one to sit on the throne of David, and his corpse shall be cast out to the heat by day and to the frost by night.

I will punish him, his offspring, and his servants for their iniquity; I will bring upon them and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem and upon the men of Judah all the disaster that I have pronounced against them, but they did not listen.”’”

Then Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch the scribe, son of Neriah, and he wrote on it from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the book that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire; and many similar words were added to them.
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, made Zedekiah son of Josiah king over Judah in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim.
Yet neither he, nor his servants, nor the people of the land, heeded the words that the the LORD had spoken through Jeremiah the prophet.
Nevertheless, King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah the prophet, saying, “Please pray to the the LORD our God on our behalf.”
Now Jeremiah moved freely among the people, for they had not yet cast him into prison.
Pharaoh’s army had marched out of Egypt, and when the Chaldeans besieging Jerusalem heard the report, they withdrew from the city.
Then the word of the the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet:
“Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Tell the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of Me, ‘Behold, Pharaoh’s army, which has come out to help you, is returning to its own land, to Egypt.
The Chaldeans will return and fight against this city; they will capture it and burn it with fire.’”
“Thus says the LORD: Do not deceive yourselves by saying, ‘The Chaldeans will surely depart from us,’ for they will not depart.
For even if you defeated the whole army of the Chaldeans now fighting against you, and only wounded men remained in their tents, they would rise up and burn this city with fire.”
When the Chaldean army withdrew from Jerusalem on account of Pharaoh’s army,
Jeremiah set out from Jerusalem for the land of Benjamin, to claim his allotted portion there among the people.
When he reached the Benjamin Gate, Irijah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah, an officer of the guard, was there; he seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying, “You are deserting to the Chaldeans!”
“That is false,” Jeremiah replied. “I am not deserting to the Chaldeans.” But Irijah would not listen; he seized Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
The officials were enraged at Jeremiah; they beat him and imprisoned him in the house of Jonathan the scribe, which they had converted into a prison.
Jeremiah entered a vaulted cell in a dungeon and remained there many days.

Then King Zedekiah sent for him and had him brought to the palace, where he questioned him privately: “Is there a word from the the LORD?” “There is,” Jeremiah answered. “You will be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon.”
Then Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, “What crime have I committed against you, your servants, or this people, that you have imprisoned me?”
Jeremiah asked, “Where are your prophets, who prophesied to you, ‘The king of Babylon will not come against you or this land’?”
“But now, please listen, my lord the king: may my plea come before you, and do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe, lest I die there.”

So King Zedekiah gave orders, and they committed Jeremiah to the courtyard of the guard, giving him a loaf of bread each day from the bakers’ street, until all the bread in the city was gone. Thus Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.
Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchijah hearkened to the words Jeremiah was proclaiming to the entire populace:

"Thus says the LORD: Whoever persists in dwelling within this city shall meet death by sword, famine, and pestilence; whereas whoever surrenders to the Chaldeans shall live, and his life shall be secured to him as spoil, so that he may continue to live.
Thus says the LORD: This city shall assuredly be delivered into the hand of the Babylonian king's martial host, and he shall subjugate it."

Then the officials said to the king, "This man merits execution, for he is enervating the resolve of the soldiers who remain in this city, as well as of the entire populace, by promulgating such words to them; indeed, this man does not seek the welfare of this people but their ruin."
King Zedekiah answered, "Behold, he is in your hands; for the king is powerless to resist you."

So they seized Jeremiah and hurled him into the cistern of Malchiah, the king's son, situated in the courtyard of the guard; and they lowered Jeremiah with ropes. Now the cistern contained no water, only mire, and Jeremiah sank into the mire.
Now Ebed-melech the Cushite, a eunuch in the royal palace, heard that they had consigned Jeremiah to the cistern. While the king was seated at the Gate of Benjamin,
Ebed-melech emerged from the palace and addressed the king, saying,

"My lord the king, these men have perpetrated wickedness in all they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, inasmuch as they have cast him into the cistern; and he will perish there of hunger, for there is no longer any bread in the city."
Thereupon the king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushite, "Take thirty men from here and extricate Jeremiah the prophet from the cistern before he expires."

So Ebed-melech took the men with him and went to the royal palace, to a place beneath the treasury; and from there he took tattered rags and worn-out garments and lowered them by ropes into the cistern to Jeremiah.
Then Ebed-melech the Cushite cried out to Jeremiah, "Place these worn-out rags and garments beneath your armpits, under the ropes." And Jeremiah complied.
So they hoisted Jeremiah by the ropes and lifted him out of the cistern; and Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.

Then King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah the prophet and had him brought to the third entrance of the house of the LORD. And the king said to Jeremiah, "I am about to interrogate you concerning a matter; do not withhold anything from me."
Jeremiah replied, "If I tell you, will you not assuredly put me to death? And if I proffer counsel to you, you will not heed me."

But King Zedekiah swore secretly to Jeremiah, "As surely as the LORD lives, who granted us this life, I will not put you to death, nor will I surrender you into the hand of these men who seek your life."

Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Hosts, the God of Israel: If you will indeed surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, your life shall be spared, this city shall not be consumed by fire, and you and your household shall live.

But if you do not surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, this city shall be delivered into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they shall burn it with fire, and you yourself shall not escape from their grasp."
King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "I am apprehensive of the Jews who have defected to the Chaldeans, lest they deliver me into their hand and abuse me."
Jeremiah replied, "They will not deliver you over. Obey the voice of the LORD in what I speak to you, that it may be well with you and your life be spared.
But if you refuse to go forth, this is the word that the LORD has revealed to me: "

All the women who remain in the house of the king of Judah shall be brought out to the officers of the king of Babylon, and they shall say, 'They beguiled you and prevailed over you, those confidants of yours. Your feet sank in the mire, and they recoiled.'

All your wives and children shall be brought out to the Chaldeans, and you yourself shall not escape from their hand, but shall be seized by the king of Babylon, and this city shall be burned with fire."
Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Let no one know of this colloquy, or you will die.

And if the officials hear that I have conversed with you and come to you and say, 'What did you say to the king, and what did the king say to you? Do not withhold it from us, or we will put you to death,'
then you shall say to them, 'I was presenting my petition before the king, that he would not return me to the house of Jonathan to die there.'"

When all the officials came to Jeremiah and interrogated him, he reported to them in accordance with all these words that the king had commanded; and they fell silent, because the matter had not been overheard.
And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured.
In the ninth year of Zedekiah, king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, advanced against Jerusalem with his entire army and besieged it.
On the ninth day of the fourth month of Zedekiah’s eleventh year, the city was breached.

Then all the officers of the king of Babylon entered and took their seats in the Middle Gate—Nergal-sharezer of Samgar, Nebo-sarsechim the chief eunuch, Nergal-sharezer the chief magus, and all the remaining officials of the king of Babylon.
When Zedekiah, king of Judah, and all the men of war saw them, they fled and departed from the city by night through the king’s garden gate, between the walls, and took the road toward the Arabah.

But the Chaldean army pursued them, overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, seized him, and escorted him to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced judgment upon him.
At Riblah, the king of Babylon executed Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes; he also executed all the nobles of Judah.
Then he put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him in bronze fetters, and carried him off to Babylon.
The Chaldeans burned the royal palace and the houses of the people with fire, and they tore down the walls of Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, carried into exile to Babylon the remnant left in the city, the deserters who had gone over to him, and the rest of the populace.
But Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, left in the land of Judah some of the poorest people, who had nothing, and on that day he gave them vineyards and fields.
Now Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had given orders concerning Jeremiah through Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, saying,
“Take him and set your eyes upon him, and do him no harm; rather, deal with him exactly as he asks of you.”

So Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, Nebushazban the chief eunuch, Nergal-sharezer the chief magus, and all the chief officers of the king of Babylon sent and took Jeremiah from the court of the guard.
They committed him to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, to escort him to his residence, and so he remained among the people.
While Jeremiah had been confined in the court of the guard, the word of the LORD came to him:

“Go and say to Ebed-melech the Cushite, ‘Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I am about to bring My words upon this city for disaster and not for prosperity, and they shall be fulfilled before you on that day.
But I will deliver you on that day, declares the LORD, and you shall not be given into the hand of the men whom you dread.
For I will surely save you, and you shall not fall by the sword; your life will be spared as plunder, because you have trusted in Me, declares the LORD.’”

The following oracle came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan, commander of the imperial guard, released him at Ramah, where he had discovered him fettered among the entire company of exiles from Jerusalem and Judah being deported to Babylon.
The captain of the guard found Jeremiah and said to him, “The LORD your God decreed this calamity upon this place,
and now the LORD has brought it to pass and fulfilled what He threatened; because you people sinned against the LORD and refused to heed His voice, this catastrophe has befallen you.

But now, behold, I release you this day from the chains upon your wrists. If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will watch over you; but if it seems wrong to you to come with me to Babylon, then stay. See, the whole land lies before you: wherever it seems good and right to you to go, go there.”

But before Jeremiah turned to depart, Nebuzaradan added, “Return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah, and dwell with him among the people, or go wherever it seems right to you.” Then the captain of the guard gave him provisions and a gift and sent him away.
So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and dwelt with him among the people who remained in the land.

When all the commanders of the armies in the field, together with their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land and had entrusted to him men, women, children, and the poorest of the land—those who had not been exiled to Babylon—

they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite, together with their men.

Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, swore an oath to them and to their men, saying, “Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Remain in the land, serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you.

As for me, I will remain in Mizpah to represent you before the Chaldeans when they come to us. But you, gather wine, summer fruit, and oil, store them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that you have occupied.”
When all the Jews in Moab, Ammon, Edom, and in all the other lands heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judah and had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, over them,
they returned from all the places to which they had been scattered and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and gathered a very great abundance of wine and summer fruit.
Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies in the field came to Gedaliah at Mizpah
and said to him, “Do you not know that Baalis, king of the Ammonites, has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to take your life?” But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke privately to Gedaliah at Mizpah, “Let me go and slay Ishmael son of Nethaniah; no one will know. Why should he take your life and scatter all the Jews gathered to you, so that the remnant of Judah would perish?”
But Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, “Do not do this thing! What you are saying about Ishmael is false.”

In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah—of royal stock and one of the king's chief officers, himself the son of Elishama—arrived at Mizpah with ten companions to visit Gedaliah son of Ahikam, and there they shared a meal.

Then Ishmael son of Nethaniah, together with those ten men, rose and struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, with the sword, murdering the man whom the king of Babylon had appointed governor over the land.
Ishmael also slew all the Jews who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, together with the Chaldean warriors found there.
On the day after Gedaliah's assassination, before the crime had become known,
eighty men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria, their beards shaved, their garments torn, and their bodies lacerated, bearing grain offerings and incense to present at the house of the the LORD.
Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he advanced; and as he encountered them, he said, "Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam."
When they had entered the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah and his associates slaughtered them and cast their bodies into a cistern.

Yet ten of them pleaded with Ishmael, "Do not put us to death, for we have concealed treasures in the field—wheat, barley, oil, and honey." So he desisted and did not slay them along with their companions.

The cistern into which Ishmael had cast all the corpses of the men he had struck down, along with Gedaliah, was the great reservoir that King Asa had excavated for defense against Baasha king of Israel; Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with the slain.

Ishmael then carried off captive the entire remnant of the people at Mizpah—the king's daughters and all who remained there, whom Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, had entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam—and set out to cross over to the Ammonites.
When Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces with him heard of the atrocities Ishmael son of Nethaniah had committed,
they mobilized their entire company and marched to confront Ishmael; they found him beside the great pool at Gibeon.
All the people who were with Ishmael rejoiced when they saw Johanan son of Kareah and the commanders accompanying him.
Consequently, the whole company whom Ishmael had seized at Mizpah turned about and went over to Johanan son of Kareah.
Ishmael son of Nethaniah, however, escaped from Johanan with eight men and fled to the Ammonites.

Then Johanan son of Kareah and all his commanders took the entire remnant they had recovered from Ishmael son of Nethaniah at Mizpah after the murder of Gedaliah son of Ahikam—the warriors, the women, the children, and the eunuchs whom he had brought back from Gibeon.
They journeyed onward and settled at Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem, intending to proceed into Egypt,
for they feared the Chaldeans, because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had slain Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
Then all the commanders of the forces, together with Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people—from the least to the greatest—approached
Jeremiah the prophet and said, “Please let our petition come before you; pray to the LORD your God for this entire remnant, for few of us remain of the many, as you can see.
May the LORD your God show us the way we should go and the thing we should do.”

“I have heard you,” replied Jeremiah the prophet. “I will certainly pray to the LORD your God as you have requested, and I will tell you everything the LORD answers; I will not withhold a word from you.”
Then they said to Jeremiah, “May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not act according to every word the LORD your God sends you to tell us.
Whether it is good or bad, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may go well with us, for we will obey the voice of the LORD our God.”
After ten days the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah,
and he summoned Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces with him, together with all the people—from the least to the greatest.
He said to them, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to bring your petition before Him, says:
‘If you will indeed stay in this land, then I will build you up and not tear you down; I will plant you and not uproot you, for I have relented of the disaster I brought upon you.
Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you now fear; do not be afraid of him, declares the LORD, for I am with you to save you and deliver you from his hand.
And I will show you compassion, so that he will have compassion on you and restore you to your own land.’
“But if you say, ‘We will not stay in this land,’ and so disobey the voice of the LORD your God,
saying, ‘No, we will go to the land of Egypt, where we will not see war or hear the sound of the trumpet or hunger for bread, and there we will live,’
“then hear the word of the LORD, O remnant of Judah! This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: ‘If you are determined to go to Egypt and reside there,
then the sword you fear will overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine you dread will follow hard upon your heels into Egypt, and there you will die.
All the men who set their faces to go to Egypt to reside there will die by sword and famine and pestilence; none of them will survive or escape the disaster I am bringing upon them.’

For this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: ‘Just as My anger and wrath were poured out upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so My wrath will be poured out on you if you go to Egypt; you will become an execration, an astonishment, a curse, and a reproach, and you will never see this place again.’
“The LORD has spoken to you, O remnant of Judah: Do not go to Egypt! Know for certain that I have warned you this day.
For you have deceived yourselves by sending me to the LORD your God, saying, ‘Pray to the LORD our God for us; as the LORD our God says, so tell us, and we will do it.’
For I have told you today, but you have not obeyed the voice of the LORD your God in all that He has sent me to tell you.
Now therefore, know for certain that you will die by sword and famine and pestilence in the place where you desire to go and reside.”
When Jeremiah had finished speaking to all the people all the words of the LORD their God, which the LORD their God had sent him to them—all these words.

Then Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the insolent men said to Jeremiah, "You are speaking falsely; the LORD our God did not send you to say, 'Do not go to Egypt to sojourn there.'
Rather, Baruch son of Neriah is inciting you against us, so that he may hand us over to the Chaldeans to be put to death and exiled to Babylon."
Yet Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces, together with all the people, refused to obey the voice of the LORD and to remain in the land of Judah.

Instead, Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces took all the remnant of Judah—those who had returned from all the nations to which they had been driven, in order to sojourn in the land of Judah—

the men, the women, the children, the king's daughters, every person whom Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, along with Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
They entered the land of Egypt, because they had not obeyed the voice of the LORD, and they went as far as Tahpanhes.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,
"Take large stones in your hand and hide them in mortar in the brickwork that is at the entrance of Pharaoh's house in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah,

and say to them, 'Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I am about to send for and take Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, My servant, and I will set his throne above these stones that I have hidden, and he will spread his royal pavilion over them.
He shall come and strike the land of Egypt: those destined for death to death, those for captivity to captivity, and those for the sword to the sword.

I will kindle fire in the temples of the gods of Egypt, and he shall burn them and carry them away captive; he shall envelop the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his mantle, and he shall go forth from there in peace.
He shall also break the pillars of Beth-shemesh in the land of Egypt, and the temples of the gods of Egypt he shall burn with fire.'"
The message that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Judeans dwelling in the land of Egypt—those in Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and the land of Pathros—ran as follows:

“Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: You have witnessed the entire calamity that I brought upon Jerusalem and upon all the cities of Judah; behold, this day they lie waste, bereft of inhabitants,
because of the wickedness they committed, provoking Me to anger by going to burn incense and serve other gods—gods that neither they, nor you, nor your fathers ever knew.
Yet I sent to you all My servants the prophets, early and persistently, saying, ‘Do not perpetrate this abominable thing that I abhor.’
But they would not listen or incline their ear; they did not repent of their wickedness or cease burning incense to other gods.
Therefore My wrath and indignation were poured out and kindled in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, so that they became a desolate waste, as they are this day.”

“Now therefore, thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Why do you inflict so great an evil upon your own souls, cutting off from the midst of Judah man and woman, infant and nursing child, so that no remnant is left to you?

You provoke Me to anger by the work of your hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt, to which you have gone to sojourn, thereby ensuring your own extermination and making yourselves a curse and a byword among all the nations of the earth.

Have you forgotten the wickedness of your fathers, the wickedness of the kings of Judah, the wickedness of their wives, your own wickedness, and the wickedness of your wives—all that was perpetrated in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
To this very day they have not been humbled, nor have they feared, nor have they walked in My law or in My statutes, which I set before you and before your fathers.
Therefore, thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I am setting My face against you for calamity, to destroy all Judah.

I will take the remnant of Judah—those who have resolved to enter Egypt to sojourn there—and they shall be utterly consumed; in the land of Egypt they shall fall, and by sword and famine they shall be consumed; from the least to the greatest, they shall die by sword and famine; and they shall become a horror, a desolation, a curse, and a reproach.
I will punish those dwelling in the land of Egypt just as I punished Jerusalem—by sword, famine, and plague.

Thus none of the remnant of Judah who have gone to sojourn in Egypt shall escape or survive to return to the land of Judah, for which they long to return and dwell; none shall return except a handful of fugitives.”

Then all the men who knew that their wives had been burning incense to other gods, together with all the women standing there—a great assembly—and all the people dwelling in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying:
“As for the word you have spoken to us in the name of the LORD, we will not listen to you!

Rather, we will surely do everything that has proceeded from our own mouths: we will burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out libations to her, just as we, our fathers, our kings, and our officials did in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. For then we had abundance of food, we prospered, and saw no calamity.
But ever since we ceased burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out libations to her, we have lacked everything and have been consumed by sword and famine.”
And the women added, “When we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out libations to her, did we make cakes bearing her image and pour out libations to her without our husbands' consent?”
Then Jeremiah addressed all the people—men and women alike—and all those who had given him that answer, saying:

“The incense that you, your fathers, your kings, your officials, and the people of the land burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem—did not the LORD remember it, and did it not come into His mind?

So the LORD could no longer endure the evil of your deeds and the abominations you committed; therefore your land has become a desolation, a horror, and a curse, without inhabitant, as it is this day.

Because you burned incense and sinned against the LORD, and did not obey the voice of the LORD or walk in His law, His statutes, or His testimonies, this calamity has befallen you, as it is this day.”
Jeremiah further said to all the people, and to all the women, “Hear the word of the LORD, all you people of Judah who are in the land of Egypt.

Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: ‘You and your wives have declared with your own mouths, “We will surely perform our vows that we have made to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and to pour out libations to her.” So keep your vows and carry them out!’

But hear the word of the LORD, all you people of Judah dwelling in the land of Egypt: ‘Behold, I have sworn by My great name, says the LORD, that My name shall no longer be invoked by any man of Judah throughout the land of Egypt, saying, “As the Lord the LORD lives.”’
‘Behold, I am watching over them for harm and not for good; all the men of Judah in the land of Egypt shall be consumed by sword and famine until they are gone.

Yet a small number who escape the sword shall return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah; and then the whole remnant of Judah that went to sojourn in Egypt shall know whose word stands—Mine or theirs.
And this shall be a sign to you, declares the LORD, that I will punish you in this place, so that you may know that My words will surely stand against you for harm.’

Thus says the LORD: ‘Behold, I will deliver Pharaoh Hophra, king of Egypt, into the hand of his enemies and into the hand of those who seek his life, just as I delivered Zedekiah, king of Judah, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.’”

The oracle that Jeremiah the prophet delivered to Baruch son of Neriah, when Baruch committed these words to a scroll from Jeremiah’s dictation, during the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying:
“Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning you, Baruch:
“You have said, ‘Alas for me now! For the LORD has compounded grief upon my affliction; I am exhausted by my groaning, and I have found no respite.’
“Thus you shall say to him, ‘Thus says the LORD: Behold, what I have erected I am dismantling, and what I have planted I am uprooting—even this entire land.

“‘And do you seek exalted things for yourself? Do not seek them; for behold, I am bringing calamity upon all flesh, says the LORD. Yet I will grant you your life as spoil in every place to which you go.’”
The word of the LORD concerning the nations, which came to Jeremiah the prophet—

concerning Egypt, the army of Pharaoh Necho, king of Egypt, which was at Carchemish on the Euphrates, and which Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, struck in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
Arrange the shield and buckler, and draw near to the battle.
Harness the horses and mount, O horsemen; take your positions in helmets; furbish the spears; put on the coats of mail.
Why have I seen them dismayed and turned backward? Their warriors are beaten down; they have fled in haste without looking back, and terror is on every side, declares the LORD.
Let not the swift flee, nor let the mighty escape; northward, by the river Euphrates, they stumble and fall.
Who is this rising like the Nile, like rivers whose waters toss themselves?
Egypt rises like the Nile, and its waters churn like rivers; and it says, “I will ascend, I will cover the earth; I will destroy the city and its inhabitants.”
Advance, O horses; rage, O chariots; go forth, O mighty men: Cush and Put, who bear the shield, and the Ludim, who draw the bow.

For that day belongs to the Lord, the the LORD of Hosts—a day of vengeance, to avenge Himself upon His adversaries. The sword shall devour and be satiated and be drunk with their blood, for the Lord, the the LORD of Hosts, has a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates.
Go up to Gilead and take balm, O Virgin Daughter of Egypt; in vain you have multiplied remedies for yourself; there is no healing for you.
The nations have heard your disgrace, and your outcry has filled the earth; for warrior has stumbled upon warrior, and both have fallen together.
The word that the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet, that Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, would come to strike the land of Egypt.
Declare in Egypt, and proclaim in Migdol; proclaim also in Noph and in Tahpanhes. Say, “Stand fast and prepare yourself, for the sword devours all around you.”
Why have your mighty ones been swept away? They did not stand, because the LORD thrust them down.
He has multiplied the stumbling; indeed, one has fallen against another, and they said, “Arise, and let us return to our people and to the land of our birth, away from the sword of the oppressor.”
There they cried out, “Pharaoh, king of Egypt, is but a noise; he has let the appointed time pass by.”
“As I live,” declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts, “surely, as Tabor stands among the mountains and as Carmel by the sea, so shall he come.”
Pack your bags for exile, O daughter dwelling in Egypt; for Noph shall become a desolation and be burned, without inhabitant.
Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a gadfly from the north is coming—it is coming!

Even her mercenaries in her midst are like fattened calves; they too will turn back, and together they will flee; they will not stand their ground, for the day of their calamity is upon them—the time of their punishment.
Egypt will hiss like a serpent, for they march with an army and come against her with axes, as woodcutters.
They shall cut down her forest, declares the LORD, though it be impenetrable; for they are more than locusts and without number.
The Daughter of Egypt shall be put to shame; she shall be delivered into the hand of the people of the north.
The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Behold, I will punish Amon of No, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, and her gods and her kings, and those who trust in Pharaoh.

And I will deliver them into the hand of those who seek their lives, and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and into the hand of his servants; and afterward she shall be inhabited, as in the days of old,” declares the LORD.

“But you, O Jacob My servant, do not fear, and do not be dismayed, O Israel; for behold, I will save you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and be quiet and at ease, and none shall make him afraid.

Fear not, O Jacob My servant,” declares the LORD, “for I am with you; for I will make a full end of all the nations to which I have driven you, but I will not make a full end of you; but I will discipline you justly, and will not leave you unpunished.”
The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza.

Thus says the LORD: “Behold, waters are rising from the north and shall become an overflowing torrent; they shall inundate the land and all its fullness, the city and those who dwell in it. Humanity will cry out, and every inhabitant of the land will wail.

At the sound of the stamping of the hoofs of his stallions, at the thunder of his chariots and the rumble of his wheels, fathers will not turn back for their children, for their hands have become utterly feeble.
This is the day that comes to destroy all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every surviving helper; for the LORD is destroying the Philistines, the remnant of the coastland of Caphtor.”
“Baldness has come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is silenced. O remnant of their valley, how long will you gash yourself?”
“Alas, sword of the LORD! How long until you are quiet? Sheathe yourself in your scabbard; be tranquil and silent.
How can it be quiet when the LORD has commanded it? Against Ashkelon and against the seacoast, there He has appointed it.”
Concerning Moab, thus declares the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Woe to Nebo, for it is laid waste; Kiriathaim is seized; Misgab is humiliated and confounded.
Moab's renown is no more; in Heshbon they plot calamity against her, saying, “Come, let us eradicate her as a nation.” You likewise, Madmen, shall be hushed; the sword shall pursue you.
A cry of lamentation rises from Horonaim: devastation and immense destruction.
Moab is shattered; her little ones raise a wail.
For the ascent of Luhith is accompanied by weeping upon weeping; for at the descent of Horonaim the adversaries have heard the cry of ruin.
Flee, preserve your lives, and resemble a desolate shrub in the wilderness.
For because you reposed trust in your works and in your treasures, you too shall be seized; Chemosh shall go into exile together with his priests and his princes.
The devastator shall assail every city, and no city shall elude him; the valley shall perish, and the plain shall be laid waste, as the LORD has spoken.
Bestow wings upon Moab, for she shall surely take flight; her cities shall become a desolation, devoid of inhabitants.
Cursed is he who executes the work of the LORD with negligence, and cursed is he who restrains his sword from blood.

Moab has been tranquil from his youth and has settled upon his lees; he has not been poured from vessel to vessel, nor has he gone into exile; therefore his savor remains in him, and his scent is unaltered.
Therefore, behold, days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will send to him pourers, and they shall pour him out; they shall empty his vessels and shatter his jars.
Then Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, their confidence.
How can you assert, “We are mighty men, valiant men of war”?
Moab is devastated, and her cities have been invaded; her chosen young men have descended to the slaughter, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.
Moab's calamity is imminent, and his disaster hastens exceedingly.
Lament for him, all you who dwell around him; all you who know his name. Say, “How broken is the mighty staff, the glorious rod!”
Descend from your glory, and sit in thirst, O inhabitant of Daughter Dibon; for the destroyer of Moab has come against you; he has destroyed your fortresses.
Stand by the way and keep watch, O inhabitant of Aroer; inquire of him who flees and of her who escapes; say, “What has happened?”
Moab is humiliated, for it is broken; wail and cry out! Proclaim in Arnon that Moab is devastated.
And judgment has come upon the land of the plain, upon Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath;
and upon Kerioth, Bozrah, and all the cities of the land of Moab, far and near.
The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken, declares the LORD.
Intoxicate him, for he magnified himself against the LORD; Moab shall wallow in his vomit, and he too shall become a laughingstock.
For was not Israel a derision to you? Was he found among thieves? For whenever you speak concerning him, you shake your head.
Abandon the cities, and dwell in the rock, O inhabitants of Moab, and be like the dove that nests in the clefts of a gorge.
We have heard of the pride of Moab—he is exceedingly proud—of his haughtiness, his pride, his arrogance, and the insolence of his heart.
I know his insolence, declares the LORD, but it is not right; his boasts have not availed.
Therefore I will wail for Moab; I will cry out for all Moab; for the men of Kir-heres I will mourn.
I will weep for you, O vine of Sibmah, with the weeping of Jazer; your tendrils crossed the sea, they reached to the sea of Jazer; upon your summer fruit and your vintage the destroyer has fallen.

Gladness and joy have been removed from the fruitful field and from the land of Moab; I have caused the wine to cease from the winepresses; no one treads with shouts of joy; the shout is not a shout of joy.
From the outcry of Heshbon to Elealeh, to Jahaz they lift their voice; from Zoar to Horonaim, to Eglath-shelishiyah; for the waters of Nimrim also shall become desolations.
And I will cause to cease in Moab, declares the LORD, him who ascends the high place and him who burns incense to his god.
Therefore My heart moans like flutes for Moab, and My heart moans like flutes for the men of Kir-heres; therefore the abundance he made has perished.
For every head is bald, and every beard is clipped; upon all hands are gashes, and upon the loins sackcloth.
On all the rooftops of Moab and in her streets there is lamentation everywhere; for I have broken Moab like a vessel in which there is no delight, declares the LORD.
How it is shattered! They wail. How Moab has turned his back in shame! So Moab shall be a derision and a terror to all who are around him.
For thus says the LORD: Behold, he shall fly like an eagle, and shall spread his wings over Moab.
Kerioth is taken, and the strongholds are seized; and the heart of the mighty men of Moab in that day shall be as the heart of a woman in travail.
And Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he magnified himself against the LORD.
Terror, and the pit, and the snare are upon you, O inhabitant of Moab, declares the LORD.

He who flees from the terror shall fall into the pit, and he who climbs out of the pit shall be caught in the snare; for I will bring upon her, upon Moab, the year of their visitation, declares the LORD.

In the shadow of Heshbon the fugitives stand powerless; for fire has gone out from Heshbon, and a flame from the midst of Sihon, and it has devoured the corner of Moab, and the crown of the sons of tumult.
Woe to you, Moab! The people of Chemosh has perished; for your sons are taken captive, and your daughters into captivity.
Yet I will restore the fortunes of Moab in the latter days, declares the LORD. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.
Concerning the Ammonites, thus says the LORD: "Does Israel have no sons? Has he no heir? Why then has Milcom taken possession of Gad, and his people settled in its cities?

Therefore, behold, days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will cause a battle cry to be heard against Rabbah of the Ammonites; and it shall become a desolate heap, and its surrounding towns shall be burned with fire. Then Israel shall dispossess those who dispossessed him, says the LORD."

Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is devastated! Cry out, daughters of Rabbah! Gird yourselves with sackcloth, mourn, and run back and forth along the walls, for Milcom shall go into exile, together with his priests and his officials.
"Why do you boast in your valleys, your valleys that flow with water, O faithless daughter? You trust in your treasures and ask who can come against you."
"Behold, I am bringing terror upon you, declares the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, from all around you; and you shall be driven out, each straight ahead, and there will be no one to gather the fugitives.
But afterward I will restore the fortunes of the Ammonites, declares the LORD."
