Concerning Edom, thus says the LORD of Hosts: "Is wisdom no longer found in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has their wisdom decayed?
Flee, turn back, dwell in the depths, inhabitants of Dedan! For I bring the calamity of Esau upon him, the time when I punish him.
If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave gleanings? If thieves came by night, would they not steal only as much as they needed?
But I have stripped Esau bare; I have uncovered his hiding places, so that he cannot hide. His offspring are devastated, along with his brothers and neighbors, and he is no more."
"Leave your orphans; I will keep them alive; and let your widows trust in Me."
For thus says the LORD: "Behold, those who were not destined to drink the
The word that the LORD spoke by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, was this:

“Declare among the nations and make it heard; lift up a standard and proclaim it without concealment: say, ‘Babylon is captured, Bel is put to shame, Merodach is dismayed; her idols are dismayed, her images are shamed.’
For a nation from the north has come up against her; it shall reduce her land to desolation, so that no one dwells in it; from man to beast they have fled away.”
“In those days and at that time,” declares the LORD, “the children of Israel and the children of Judah shall come together, weeping as they go, and seeking the LORD their God.
They shall ask the way to Zion, with their faces turned thitherward, saying, ‘Come, let us join ourselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant that shall not be forgotten.’”
“My people were lost sheep; their shepherds led them astray, turning them away upon the mountains; from mountain to hill they wandered, and they forgot their resting place.
All who found them devoured them, and their adversaries said, ‘We are not guilty, for they have sinned against the LORD—the righteous habitation, the hope of their fathers.’”
“Flee from the midst of Babylon, and go forth out of the land of the Chaldeans, and take the lead, like he-goats before the flock.

For behold, I am raising up and bringing against Babylon a great assembly of nations from the north country; they shall array themselves against her, and from there she shall be taken. Their arrows shall be like those of a skilled warrior, and none shall return empty.
Chaldea shall be plundered, and all who plunder her shall be sated,” declares the LORD.
“Because you rejoiced, because you exulted, you plunderers of My heritage, because you frisked like a heifer treading grain and neighed like stallions,
your mother shall be greatly ashamed; she who bore you shall be confounded. Behold, the last of the nations shall she be—a wilderness, a parched land, and a desert.
Because of the wrath of the LORD she shall not be inhabited, but she shall be wholly desolate; everyone who passes by Babylon shall be appalled and hiss at all her wounds.”
“Array yourselves against Babylon round about, all you who bend the bow; shoot at her, and spare no arrows, for she has sinned against the LORD.
Shout against her round about; she has surrendered; her bulwarks have fallen, her walls are demolished; for it is the vengeance of the LORD. Take vengeance on her; as she has done, do to her.
Cut off the sower from Babylon, and the handler of the sickle at harvest time; because of the sword of the oppressor, each shall turn to his own people, and each shall flee to his own land.”
“Israel is a scattered flock; the lions have driven him away. First the king of Assyria devoured him, and this last—Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon—has broken his bones.
Therefore thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will punish the king of Babylon and his land, as I punished the king of Assyria.
I will restore Israel to his pasture; he shall graze on Carmel and Bashan, and on Mount Ephraim and Gilead his soul shall be satisfied.

In those days and at that time, declares the LORD, the iniquity of Israel shall be sought and shall not be found, and the sins of Judah shall not be discovered; for I will pardon those whom I leave as a remnant.”
“Go up against the land of Merathaim, and against the inhabitants of Pekod; waste and utterly destroy them, says the LORD, and do according to all that I have commanded you.
A sound of battle is in the land, and great destruction.
How the hammer of the whole earth is cut down and broken! How Babylon has become a desolation among the nations!
I have laid a snare for you, O Babylon, and you are taken, though you did not know it; you are found and seized, because you have contended with the LORD.”
The LORD has opened His armory and brought forth the weapons of His indignation; for the Lord GOD of Hosts has a work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.
“Come against her from the farthest border; open her granaries; pile her up like heaps, and devote her to destruction; let no remnant remain.
Slay all her bulls; let them go down to slaughter. Woe to them! for their day has come, the time of their punishment.”
A voice of fugitives and refugees from the land of Babylon declares in Zion the vengeance of the LORD our God, the vengeance for His temple.

“Summon many against Babylon, all who bend the bow; encamp against her round about; let there be no escape; repay her according to her work; do to her according to all that she has done; for she has acted arrogantly against the LORD, against the Holy One of Israel.
Therefore her young men shall fall in her streets, and all her warriors shall be silenced in that day,” declares the LORD.
“Behold, I am against you, O arrogant one,” declares the Lord GOD of Hosts, “for your day has come, the time of your reckoning.
The arrogant one shall stumble and fall, and none shall raise him; I will kindle fire in his cities, and it shall consume all around him.”
Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “The children of Israel and the children of Judah are oppressed together; all their captors hold them fast; they refuse to release them.
Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of Hosts is His name. He will surely contend for their cause, to bring rest to the land and to agitate the inhabitants of Babylon.”
“A sword is upon the Chaldeans,” declares the LORD, “and upon the inhabitants of Babylon, and upon her princes, and upon her wise men.
A sword is upon the boasters, and they shall become fools; a sword is upon her mighty men, and they shall be dismayed.
A sword is upon their horses, and upon their chariots, and upon all the foreign folk in her midst, and they shall lose all courage; a sword is upon her treasures, and they shall be robbed.
A drought is upon her waters, and they shall dry up; for it is a land of graven images, and they are maddened by their idols.”
“Therefore the desert creatures and jackals shall dwell there, and ostriches shall inhabit it; it shall never again be inhabited, nor dwelt in from generation to generation.
As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, declares the LORD, no man shall dwell there, nor shall any son of man sojourn in it.”
“Behold, a people comes from the north, a great nation and many kings stirred up from the ends of the earth.
They shall lay hold on bow and spear; they are cruel and will show no mercy; their voice roars like the sea; they ride on horses, arrayed like a man for war, against you, O daughter of Babylon.
The king of Babylon has heard the report concerning them, and his hands have grown feeble; distress has seized him, pangs as of a woman in labor.”

“Behold, like a lion coming up from the thickets of the Jordan against the strong fold, for I will suddenly make them run away from her; and who is the chosen one whom I may appoint over her? For who is like Me? and who will summon Me? and who is this shepherd that shall stand before Me?

Therefore hear the counsel that the LORD has devised against Babylon, and His thoughts that He has thought against the land of the Chaldeans: Surely the little ones of the flock shall drag them away; surely He shall make their dwelling desolate over them.
At the sound of the capture of Babylon the earth shall tremble, and a cry shall be heard among the nations.”
Thus says the LORD: “Behold, I am stirring up against Babylon and against the inhabitants of Leb-kamai a destroying wind.
And I will send foreigners to Babylon, and they shall winnow her and empty her land, for they shall be against her on every side in the day of disaster.
Let not the archer bend his bow, and let him not lift himself up in his armor; and do not spare her young men; devote to destruction all her host.
And the slain shall fall in the land of the Chaldeans, and the pierced in her streets.”
For Israel and Judah are not forsaken by their God, by the LORD of Hosts, though their land is full of guilt against the Holy One of Israel.
Flee from the midst of Babylon, and save each his life; do not be cut off in her iniquity, for it is the time of the LORD’s vengeance; He is rendering to her a recompense.
Babylon was a golden cup in the hand of the LORD, making all the earth drunk; the nations drank of her wine; therefore the nations went mad.
Suddenly Babylon has fallen and is shattered; wail for her! Take balm for her pain; perhaps she may be healed.
We tried to heal Babylon, but she was not healed. Forsake her, and let us each go to his own country, for her judgment has reached to heaven and has been lifted up to the skies.
The LORD has brought forth our vindication; come, let us declare in Zion the work of the LORD our God.

Sharpen the arrows! Fill the quivers! The LORD has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, for His purpose is against Babylon to destroy it, because it is the vengeance of the LORD, the vengeance for His temple.
Raise a banner against the walls of Babylon; strengthen the guard; set up the watchmen; prepare the ambushes; for the LORD has both planned and done what He spoke against the inhabitants of Babylon.
O you who dwell by many waters, abundant in treasures, your end has come, the measure of your unjust gain.
The LORD of Hosts has sworn by Himself: “Surely I will fill you with men as with locusts, and they shall raise a shout against you.”
He who made the earth by His power, who established the world by His wisdom, and by His understanding stretched out the heavens.

When He utters His voice, there is a tumult of waters in the heavens, and He makes the clouds rise from the ends of the earth; He makes lightning for the rain, and brings forth the wind from His storehouses.
Every man is brutish and destitute of knowledge; every goldsmith is shamed by his idol, for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.
They are worthless, a work of delusion; in the time of their punishment they shall perish.
The Portion of Jacob is not like these, for He is the Maker of all things, and Israel is the tribe of His inheritance; the LORD of Hosts is His name.
“You are My hammer and weapon of war; with you I shatter nations, and with you I destroy kingdoms.
With you I shatter horse and rider; with you I shatter chariot and driver.
With you I shatter man and woman; with you I shatter old and young; with you I shatter young man and maiden.
With you I shatter shepherd and flock; with you I shatter farmer and yoke of oxen; with you I shatter governors and deputies.
Before your eyes I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Chaldea for all the evil they have done in Zion, declares the LORD.”

“Behold, I am against you, O destroying mountain, which destroys the whole earth, declares the LORD; and I will stretch out My hand against you, and roll you down from the rocks, and make you a burnt mountain.
And they shall not take from you a stone for a corner or a stone for foundations, but you shall be desolate forever, declares the LORD.”

Lift up a banner in the land; blow the trumpet among the nations; consecrate the nations against her; summon against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz; appoint a marshal against her; bring up horses like bristling locusts.
Consecrate the nations against her—the kings of the Medes, her governors and all her deputies, and all the land of their dominion.
The land trembles and writhes in pain, for the LORD’s purposes against Babylon stand, to make the land of Babylon a desolation, without inhabitant.
The mighty men of Babylon have ceased fighting; they remain in their strongholds; their strength has failed; they have become like women; her dwellings are set on fire; her bars are broken.
One runner runs to meet another, and one messenger to meet another, to tell the king of Babylon that his city is taken from end to end.
And the fords are seized, and the marshes are burned with fire, and the men of war are terrified.
For thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: “The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trodden; yet a little while, and the time of her harvest will come.”

“Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured us, he has crushed us, he has made us an empty vessel; he has swallowed us like a dragon; he has filled his belly with our delicacies; he has driven us away.”
“May the violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon,” says the inhabitant of Zion. “And may my blood be upon the inhabitants of Chaldea,” says Jerusalem.
Therefore thus says the LORD: “Behold, I will plead your cause and take vengeance for you; I will dry up her sea and make dry her spring.
Babylon shall become a heap of ruins, a haunt of jackals, a horror and a hissing, without inhabitant.
They shall roar together like young lions; they shall growl like lions’ cubs.”
“In their heat I will make their feasts, and I will make them drunk, that they may rejoice, and sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake, declares the LORD.
I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with goats.”
How Sheshach is taken! How the praise of the whole earth is seized! How Babylon has become a desolation among the nations!
The sea has come up over Babylon; she is covered with the multitude of its waves.
Her cities have become a desolation, a dry land and a desert, a land wherein no man dwells, neither does any son of man pass thereby.
And I will punish Bel in Babylon, and I will bring forth out of his mouth what he has swallowed; the nations shall not flow together to him any more; yea, the wall of Babylon shall fall.
Go out of the midst of her, My people, and save each his life from the fierce anger of the LORD.
And lest your heart faint and you fear at the report that is heard in the land—a report shall come in one year, and after that in another year a report, and violence in the land, ruler against ruler.
“Therefore behold, the days are coming when I will punish the graven images of Babylon, and her whole land shall be put to shame, and all her slain shall fall in the midst of her.
Then the heavens and the earth and all that is in them shall sing for joy over Babylon, because the destroyers shall come to her from the north, declares the LORD.”
As Babylon caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the earth.
You who have escaped the sword, go, do not stand still; remember the LORD from afar, and let Jerusalem come into your mind.
We are ashamed, because we have heard reproach; confusion has covered our faces, because strangers have come into the sanctuaries of the LORD’s house.
“Therefore behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will punish her graven images, and throughout all her land the wounded shall groan.
Though Babylon should mount up to heaven, and though she should fortify the height of her strength, yet from Me destroyers shall come to her, declares the LORD.”
A sound of a cry from Babylon, and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans!
For the LORD is plundering Babylon, and He has silenced her great voice; and their waves roar like many waters, the noise of their voice is uttered.
For the destroyer is come upon her, even upon Babylon, and her mighty men are taken, their bows are broken in pieces; for the LORD is a God of recompenses, He shall surely requite.

“And I will make drunk her princes and her wise men, her governors and her deputies and her mighty men; and they shall sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake, declares the LORD, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.”

Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “The broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly broken down, and her high gates shall be burned with fire; and the peoples shall labor in vain, and the nations for the fire, and they shall be weary.”

The word which Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah the king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Now Seraiah was the chief quartermaster.
And Jeremiah wrote in a book all the evil that should come upon Babylon, even all these words that are written against Babylon.
And Jeremiah said to Seraiah, “When you come to Babylon, then see that you read all these words.
And say, ‘O the LORD, You have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off, so that none shall dwell in it, neither man nor beast, but that it shall be desolate forever.’
And it shall be, when you have made an end of reading this book, that you shall bind a stone to it, and cast it into the midst of the Euphrates.
And say, ‘Thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise again from the evil that I will bring upon her; and they shall be weary.’ Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years of age when he assumed the throne, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; his mother was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, reproducing in every respect the conduct of Jehoiakim.
For it was on account of the LORD’s anger against Jerusalem and Judah—anger so inexorable that He ultimately cast them from His presence—that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

In the ninth year of his reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, advanced against Jerusalem with his entire host; they encamped around it and constructed siege works against it.
The city remained under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
By the ninth day of the fourth month, famine had become so severe in the city that the populace had no bread.
Then the city wall was breached; the Chaldeans, who encircled the city, prompted the warriors to flee by night through the gate between the two walls beside the king’s garden, making for the Arabah.
The Chaldean forces pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah on the plains of Jericho, for his entire army had been scattered from him.
They seized him and conducted him to Riblah in the land of Hamath, before the king of Babylon, who pronounced judgment upon him.
At Riblah, the king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes; he also slaughtered all the princes of Judah.
He then blinded Zedekiah, bound him in bronze fetters, and brought him to Babylon, where he confined him in a prison house until the day of his death.

On the tenth day of the fifth month in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, commander of the guard, who stood in attendance before the king of Babylon, entered Jerusalem.
He burned the house of the LORD, the king’s palace, and all the great houses of Jerusalem; every significant dwelling he consigned to the flames.
The entire Chaldean army under Nebuzaradan demolished the walls surrounding Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan, commander of the guard, deported the rest of the people who remained in the city, the deserters who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the remainder of the populace.
Only the poorest of the land did he leave behind, to serve as vinedressers and plowmen.
The Chaldeans shattered the bronze pillars, the stands, and the bronze sea that were in the house of the LORD, and they carried all the bronze to Babylon.
They also took the pots, shovels, snuffers, basins, and all the bronze vessels employed in the temple service.
The commander of the guard took the basins, firepans, bowls, pots, lampstands, pans, and libation bowls—whatever was of gold or silver.
As for the two pillars, the single sea, and the twelve bronze bulls beneath the stands that King Solomon had fashioned for the house of the LORD, their bronze was too great to be weighed.
Each pillar stood eighteen cubits high, with a circumference of twelve cubits and a thickness of four fingers, being hollow.
The bronze capital atop one pillar was five cubits high, and it was crowned with a network and pomegranates of bronze all around; the second pillar was furnished identically.
There were ninety-six pomegranates on the outer face, while the network bore one hundred pomegranates in total.
The commander of the guard seized Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three doorkeepers.

From the city he also seized the eunuch who had been in charge of the men of war, seven of the king’s close counselors who were found in the city, the secretary of the army commander who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the land who were found within the city.
Nebuzaradan, commander of the guard, took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
The king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was carried away captive from its own soil.
These are the people whom Nebuchadnezzar carried into exile: in the seventh year, three thousand twenty-three Judeans;
in the eighteenth year, eight hundred thirty-two persons from Jerusalem;
and in the twenty-third year, Nebuzaradan, commander of the guard, deported seven hundred forty-five Judeans. The total number of exiles was four thousand six hundred.

In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, restored Jehoiachin king of Judah to favor and released him from prison.
He spoke graciously to him and assigned him a seat above the seats of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
Jehoiachin put off his prison garments and ate at the king’s table for the remainder of his days.
A regular allowance was provided for him by the king of Babylon, a daily portion, every day of his life, until the day of his death.
How desolately sits the city that was once populous! She who was eminent among the nations has become like a widow; the princess among provinces has been reduced to vassalage.

She weeps bitterly in the night, and her tears stain her cheeks; among all her lovers there is none to console her. All her companions have dealt treacherously with her and have become her adversaries.
Judah has gone into exile under affliction and grievous servitude; though she dwells among the nations, she finds no repose, and all her persecutors overtook her in the straits.
The roads to Zion mourn, for none come to the appointed feasts; all her gates are desolate; her priests groan; her maidens are grieved, and she herself is in bitterness.

Her adversaries have become her masters; her enemies are at ease, because the LORD has afflicted her for the abundance of her transgressions. Her little ones have gone into captivity before the adversary.
All her splendor has departed from the daughter of Zion. Her princes have become like stags that find no pasture; they have gone forth without strength before the pursuer.

In the days of her affliction and wandering, Jerusalem remembers all her treasures from the days of old, when her people fell into the enemy's hand and no one helped her. The adversaries saw her and mocked at her ruin.
Jerusalem has sinned grievously; therefore she has become an object of revulsion. All who honored her despise her, for they have seen her nakedness; she herself groans and turns away.

Her uncleanness clings to her skirts; she did not consider her end. She has come down astonishingly, and there is no comforter for her. See, the LORD, my affliction, for the enemy has magnified himself.
The adversary has stretched out his hand over all her pleasant things, for she has seen the nations enter her sanctuary—those whom You commanded should not enter Your assembly.
All her people groan as they seek bread; they have given their treasures for food to revive their souls. See, the LORD, and consider, for I have become despised.
Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by? Look and see whether there is any sorrow like my sorrow, which was brought upon me, which the LORD inflicted in the day of His fierce anger.
From on high He sent fire into my bones and subdued them; He spread a net for my feet and turned me back; He has made me desolate and faint all the day.
The yoke of my transgressions is bound by His hand; they are knit together and placed upon my neck. He has made my strength fail; the Lord has delivered me into hands from which I cannot rise.
The Lord has trampled all my mighty men in my midst; He has summoned an assembly against me to crush my young men. The Lord has trodden the virgin daughter of Judah as in a winepress.
For these things I weep; my eyes, my eyes overflow with tears, because the comforter who should restore my soul is far from me. My children are desolate because the enemy has prevailed.

Zion stretches out her hands, yet there is no one to comfort her. The LORD has commanded concerning Jacob that his adversaries should be round about him. Jerusalem has become an unclean thing among them.
The LORD is righteous, for I have rebelled against His command. Hear, I pray, all peoples, and see my sorrow; my maidens and my young men have gone into captivity.
I called to my lovers, but they deceived me. My priests and my elders perished in the city while they sought food to revive their souls.
See, the LORD, for I am in distress; my inmost being is in turmoil; my heart is overturned within me, for I have been very rebellious. Outside, the sword bereaves; at home, it is like death.

They have heard that I groan, and there is no comforter for me. All my enemies have heard of my trouble and rejoice that You have done it. You have brought the day You proclaimed, and they shall become like me.
Let all their wickedness come before You, and do to them as You have done to me for all my transgressions. For my groans are many, and my heart is faint.
How the Lord has enshrouded Daughter Zion in the cloud of His indignation! He has hurled from heaven to earth the splendor of Israel, and He has not remembered His footstool in the day of His wrath.

Without mercy the Lord has engulfed all the habitations of Jacob; in His fury He has razed the fortresses of Daughter Judah; He has brought her sovereignty and her princes down to the dust, humiliating them.
In the heat of His anger He has cut off every horn of Israel; He has withdrawn His right hand before the enemy; He has kindled in Jacob a conflagration that devours on every side.
He has bent His bow like an enemy; His right hand stands poised like an adversary; He has slain all who were pleasing to the eye; in the tent of Daughter Zion He has poured out His wrath like fire.
The Lord has become like an enemy; He has swallowed up Israel; He has swallowed up all her palaces; He has destroyed her strongholds; and He has multiplied mourning and lamentation in Daughter Judah.

He has ravaged His tabernacle as though it were a garden; He has ruined His appointed meeting place; the LORD has caused Zion to forget her sacred seasons and her Sabbaths; in the fury of His anger He has rejected both king and priest.

The Lord has spurned His altar; He has profaned His sanctuary; He has delivered the walls of her citadels into the hand of the foe; they have shouted in the house of the LORD as though it were a day of festival.
The LORD resolved to lay waste the wall of Daughter Zion; He stretched out the measuring line; He did not withdraw His hand from devouring; rampart and wall alike lamented; together they wasted away.

Her gates have sunk into the earth; He has destroyed and shattered her bars; her king and her princes are exiled among the nations; instruction is no more; even her prophets obtain no vision from the LORD.

The elders of Daughter Zion sit on the ground in silence; they have cast dust upon their heads; they have girded themselves with sackcloth; the virgins of Jerusalem have bowed their heads to the ground.
My eyes are consumed with weeping; my inmost being churns within me; my heart is poured out upon the earth over the shattering of my people, as little ones and infants languish in the city’s streets.
They cry to their mothers, “Where is grain and wine?” as they swoon like the mortally wounded in the city’s streets, their lives ebbing away in their mothers’ arms.

What testimony can I offer on your behalf? To what shall I liken you, O Daughter Jerusalem? To what shall I compare you, that I might console you, O Virgin Daughter Zion? For your breach is as wide as the sea; who can heal you?

Your prophets have envisioned for you vanity and whitewash; they have not laid bare your guilt so as to restore your fortunes; instead, they have proclaimed for you oracles that are false and deluding.
All who pass by clap their hands at you; they hiss and shake their heads at Daughter Jerusalem: “Is this the city that was called the perfection of beauty, the joy of the whole earth?”
All your enemies open their mouths against you; they hiss and gnash their teeth; they say, “We have swallowed her up! Surely this is the day we have longed for; we have found it; we have seen it.”

The LORD has done what He purposed; He has fulfilled His word, which He decreed in days of old; He has overthrown without pity; He has made the enemy rejoice over you; He has exalted the horn of your adversaries.
Their hearts cried out to the Lord. O wall of Daughter Zion, let your tears stream down like a river day and night; grant yourself no relief; do not let your eyes cease.

Arise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the watches; pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord; lift up your hands to Him for the lives of your little ones, who faint from hunger at the head of every street.

Behold the LORD, and consider: to whom have You ever done this? Should women devour their offspring, the children of their tender care? Should priest and prophet be slain in the sanctuary of the Lord?
Young and old lie together in the dust of the streets; my young men and my virgins have fallen by the sword; You have slain them in the day of Your wrath; You have slaughtered without mercy.
You have summoned terrors on every side, as on a day of festival; in the day of the LORD’s anger no one escaped or survived; those whom I dandled and reared, my enemy has consumed.
I am the man who has seen affliction beneath the rod of His wrath.
He has led me and brought me into darkness, and not into light.
Surely He turns His hand against me again and again, all day long.
He has worn away my flesh and my skin; He has shattered my bones.
He has besieged me and encircled me with bitterness and tribulation.
He has made me dwell in darkness, like those long dead.
He has walled me in so that I cannot escape; He has made my fetters heavy.
Even when I cry out and plead for help, He shuts out my prayer.
He has barred my ways with hewn stone and made my paths crooked.
He is to me like a bear lying in wait, like a lion in secret places.
He has turned me aside from my path and torn me to pieces; He has made me desolate.
He has bent His bow and set me as a mark for His arrow.
He has driven the arrows of His quiver into my inmost parts.
I have become a derision to all my people, the subject of their song all day long.
He has filled me with bitterness and made me drunk with wormwood.
He has ground my teeth with gravel and made me wallow in ashes.
My soul has been banished from peace; I have forgotten prosperity.
Then I said, 'My strength has perished, together with my hope in the LORD.'
Remember my affliction and my wandering, the wormwood and the gall.
My soul remembers and is bowed down within me.
Yet this I bring to mind, and therefore I have hope:
Because of the LORD’s loving devotion we are not consumed, for His compassions never fail.
They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness!
'The LORD is my portion,' says my soul, 'therefore I will hope in Him.'
The LORD is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul who seeks Him.
It is good to wait quietly for the salvation of the LORD.
It is good for a man to bear the yoke in his youth.
Let him sit alone and keep silence, because He has laid it upon him.
Let him bury his face in the dust—there may yet be hope.
Let him offer his cheek to the one who strikes him; let him be filled with reproach.
For the Lord will not cast us off forever.
Though He brings grief, He will show compassion according to His abundant loving devotion.
For He does not willingly afflict or grieve the children of men.
To crush under His feet all the prisoners of the earth,
to deny a man justice before the Most High,
to subvert a man in his cause—the Lord does not approve.
Who is it that speaks, and it comes to pass, unless the Lord has commanded it?
Do not both calamity and good come from the mouth of the Most High?
Why should a living man complain, a man in view of the punishment for his sins?
Let us examine and test our ways, and turn back to the LORD.
Let us lift up our hearts and hands to God in heaven.
We have sinned and rebelled; You have not forgiven.
You have covered Yourself with anger and pursued us; You have slain without pity.
You have covered Yourself with a cloud so that no prayer can pass through.
You have made us scum and refuse among the nations.
All our enemies open their mouths against us.
Panic and pitfall have come upon us, devastation and destruction.
Streams of tears flow from my eyes because of the destruction of the daughter of my people.
My eyes will flow unceasingly, without relief,
until the LORD looks down from heaven and sees.
My eyes bring grief to my soul because of all the daughters of my city.
Those who were my enemies without cause hunted me like a bird.
They silenced my life in the pit and cast stones upon me.
Waters flowed over my head, and I said, 'I am cut off!'
I called on Your name, O the LORD, from the depths of the pit.
You heard my voice; do not hide Your ear from my cry for relief.
You came near when I called on You; You said, 'Do not be afraid.'
You redeemed my life, O Lord; You have pleaded my cause.
You have seen, O the LORD, the wrong done to me; judge my cause.
You have seen all their vengeance, all their plots against me.
You have heard their reproach, O the LORD, all their plots against me—
the lips and muttered schemes of those who rise against me all day long.
Whether they sit or rise, behold, I am their song.
Repay them, O the LORD, according to the work of their hands.
Give them anguish of heart; may Your curse be upon them.
Pursue them in anger and destroy them from under the heavens of the LORD.
How the gold has dimmed, and the finest ore grown tarnished; the hallowed stones lie strewn across every thoroughfare.
How the prized sons of Zion, once weighed against pure gold, are reckoned mere earthenware, the handiwork of a potter.
Even jackals bare the breast and suckle their whelps, yet the daughter of my people has grown merciless, akin to ostriches of the wasteland.
The suckling's tongue adheres to its palate in thirst, while children implore bread and find none to bestow.
Those who once feasted on delicacies are destitute in the streets; those reared in purple now embrace ash heaps.
For the guilt of my people's daughter exceeds Sodom's sin, overthrown in an instant without a hand laid upon her.
Her Nazirites were purer than snow, whiter than milk; their limbs glowed redder than coral, their visage like sapphire.
Their form is darker than soot; they are unrecognized in the streets; their skin has shriveled upon their bones and become dry as wood.
Those slain by the sword are better off than those slain by famine, who waste away, pierced by the lack of the field's produce.
Compassionate women have boiled their own children, making them sustenance amid the shattering of my people's daughter.
The LORD has accomplished His fury; He has poured out His fierce anger. He kindled a fire in Zion, and it consumed her foundations.
The kings of the earth and all the world's inhabitants never believed that adversary and foe could enter Jerusalem's gates.
It was because of the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests, who shed the blood of the righteous within her.
They stagger like blind men through the streets, defiled with blood, so that none may touch their garments.
People shouted for them to turn away and remain untouched, since they were unclean; so they fled and wandered, and among the nations it was said that they would no longer sojourn.
The LORD's countenance has scattered them; He will regard them no more, for they showed no honor to priests and no favor to elders.
Our eyes still fail, watching in vain for help; in our watch we looked for a nation that could not save.
They stalked our every step, so that we could not walk our streets; our end drew near, our days were fulfilled, for our doom had arrived.
Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of heaven; they pursued us over the mountains and ambushed us in the wilderness.
The breath of our nostrils, the LORD's Anointed, was caught in their traps; we had said that under his shadow we should live among the nations.
Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, you who dwell in the land of Uz! The cup will pass to you as well; you will become drunk and expose yourself.
O daughter of Zion, your guilt is at an end; He will not exile you again. O daughter of Edom, He will punish your guilt and expose your sins.
Remember, the LORD, what has befallen us; look upon us and behold our humiliation.
Our inheritance has passed into the hands of strangers, and our dwellings to foreigners.
We have been reduced to fatherless orphans, and our mothers are as widows.
We are compelled to purchase water for our drink, and our timber is furnished only at a price.
Our persecutors are at our throats; we labor and are afforded no repose.
We have pledged ourselves to Egypt and to Assyria merely to secure bread.
Our ancestors sinned and are gone, yet we suffer the penalty of their iniquities.
Bondsmen dominate us, and none rescues us from their grasp.
We obtain our bread at the hazard of our lives, exposed to the sword of the desert.
Our skin is scorched like an oven by the searing blasts of famine.
Women are ravished in Zion, and virgins in the cities of Judah.
Princes have been hanged by the hand, and the countenances of the aged have not been revered.
Young men are yoked to the millstone, and youths stagger under burdens of timber.
The aged have withdrawn from the gate, and the young have abandoned their songs.
Joy has departed from our hearts; our dancing has been turned into mourning.
Our crown has fallen from our head; woe unto us, for we have sinned.
For this cause our heart is sick; for these reasons our eyes have grown dim.
Mount Zion lies desolate, and foxes roam across it.
Yet You, the LORD, abide forever; Your throne is established from generation to generation.
Why do You forget us in perpetuity, and forsake us for days unnumbered?
Turn us back to Yourself, the LORD, and we shall return; renew our days as of old.
Unless You have indeed rejected us utterly and are enraged with us beyond measure.
In the thirtieth year, on the fifth day of the fourth month, while I was dwelling among the exiles by the Kebar River, the heavens were opened and I beheld visions of God.
On the fifth day of the month—it was the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin—
the word of the the LORD came to Ezekiel the priest, son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the Kebar River, and there the hand of the the LORD was upon him.

As I looked, behold, a storm wind came from the north: a great cloud, with flashing fire and a radiance encircling it; and from its midst there issued something like the gleam of burnished metal from the heart of the fire.
Out of its midst came the likeness of four living creatures, and this was their form: they had a human likeness.
Each had four faces and four wings.
Their legs were straight, and the soles of their feet were like the soles of a calf's foot; they sparkled like burnished bronze.
Beneath their wings, on their four sides, they had human hands; and all four possessed faces and wings.
Their wings touched one another; they did not turn as they went, but each moved straight ahead.
As for the likeness of their faces, each had a human face; the four had a lion's face on the right, an ox's face on the left, and an eagle's face.
Their wings were spread upward; two of each were joined to one another, and two covered their bodies.
Each moved straight ahead; wherever the spirit was to go, they went, without turning in their course.

As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like torches moving to and fro among the living creatures; the fire was bright, and lightning flashed out from the fire.
The living creatures darted to and fro like flashes of lightning.
As I looked upon the living creatures, behold, a wheel rested on the earth beside each one, corresponding to its four faces.
The appearance of the wheels and their workmanship was like the gleam of beryl; the four had one likeness; their appearance and workmanship were as though a wheel were within a wheel.
When they went, they went on their four sides; they did not turn as they went.
As for their rims, they were high and awesome, and their rims were full of eyes all around the four of them.
When the living creatures went, the wheels went beside them; and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up.
Wherever the spirit was to go, they went; there the spirit went; and the wheels were lifted up alongside them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.

When those went, these went; when those stood still, these stood still; and when those were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up alongside them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
Over the heads of the living creatures there was the likeness of an expanse, like the awesome gleam of crystal, stretched out above their heads.
Under the expanse their wings were straight, one toward another; each had two wings covering its body, and two covering the other side.

When they went, I heard the sound of their wings like the sound of many waters, like the voice of the Almighty, a tumultuous sound like the sound of an army; when they stood still, they let down their wings.
And there was a voice from above the expanse that was over their heads; when they stood still, they let down their wings.
Above the expanse over their heads was the likeness of a throne, in appearance like a sapphire stone; and upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness with the appearance of a man above it.

From the appearance of His waist upward I saw something like gleaming metal, like the appearance of fire enclosed all around; and from the appearance of His waist downward I saw something like the appearance of fire, and there was brightness around Him.

Like the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud on the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness all around. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the the LORD. And when I saw it, I fell upon my face, and I heard a voice speaking.
He said to me, “Son of man, stand upon your feet, and I will speak with you.”
As He spoke to me, the Spirit entered me and set me upon my feet, and I heard Him who spoke to me.
“Son of man, I am sending you to the Israelites, to a rebellious nation that has rebelled against Me; they and their fathers have transgressed against Me to this very day.
They are obstinate and hard-hearted. I am sending you to them, and you shall say to them, ‘This is what the Lord, the LORD, says.’
Whether they listen or refuse—for they are a rebellious house—they will know that a prophet has been among them.”

“And you, son of man, do not be afraid of them or of their words. Though briers and thorns surround you and you dwell among scorpions, do not be afraid of their words, nor be dismayed by their faces, for they are a rebellious house.
You shall speak My words to them, whether they listen or refuse, for they are utterly rebellious.
But you, son of man, hear what I say to you: do not be rebellious like that rebellious house. Open your mouth and eat what I give you.”
Then I looked, and behold, a hand was stretched out to me, and in it was a scroll of a book.
He unrolled it before me, and it was written on both sides; and written on it were lamentations, mourning, and woe.
He said to me, “Son of man, eat whatever you find; eat this scroll, and go speak to the house of Israel.”
I opened my mouth, and He made me eat this scroll.
He said to me, “Son of man, your stomach must eat, and your intestines must be filled with this scroll that I am giving you.” I ate it, and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth.
He said to me, “Son of man, go to the house of Israel and speak My words to them.
For you are not sent to a people of obscure speech and a heavy tongue, but to the house of Israel;
not to many peoples of obscure speech and heavy tongue, whose words you cannot understand. If I had sent you to them, they would have listened to you.
Yet the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, because they are not willing to listen to Me; for the whole house of Israel is obstinate of brow and hard of heart.
Behold, I have made your face strong against their faces, and your forehead strong against their foreheads.
I have made your forehead like adamant, harder than flint; do not fear them, nor be dismayed at their faces, for they are a rebellious house.”
He said to me, “Son of man, take all My words that I speak to you into your heart, and hear them with your ears.
Go and enter among the exiles, to the children of your people, and speak to them, and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord the LORD: Whether they hear or whether they refrain.’”
Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me a great rumbling sound: “Blessed be the glory of the LORD from His place.”
It was the sound of the wings of the living creatures touching one another, and the sound of the wheels beside them, and the sound of a great rumbling.
The Spirit lifted me and took me; I went in bitterness in the heat of my spirit, and the hand of the LORD was strong upon me.
I came to the exiles at Tel Abib, who dwelt by the river Chebar, and I sat there among them seven days, overwhelmed.
At the end of seven days, the word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel; hear a word from My mouth and warn them for Me.

When I say to the wicked, ‘You shall surely die,’ and you do not warn him, nor speak to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood I will require at your hand.
But if you warn the wicked, and he does not turn from his wickedness or from his wicked way, he shall die in his iniquity; but you have delivered your soul.

Again, when a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, and I lay a stumbling block before him, he shall die; because you have not warned him, he shall die in his sin, and his righteous deeds which he has done shall not be remembered; but his blood I will require at your hand.
Nevertheless, if you warn the righteous man not to sin, and he does not sin, he shall surely live because he took warning; and you have delivered your soul.”
The hand of the LORD was there upon me, and He said to me, “Arise, go out to the valley, and there I will speak with you.”
I arose and went out to the valley; and behold, the glory of the LORD stood there, like the glory which I had seen by the river Chebar; and I fell on my face.
Then the Spirit entered into me and set me on my feet, and He spoke with me and said to me, “Go, shut yourself inside your house.
As for you, son of man, behold, they will put ropes on you and bind you with them, so that you cannot go out among them.
I will make your tongue cling to the roof of your mouth, so that you will be mute and not be a reprover to them, for they are a rebellious house.

But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you shall say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord the LORD.’ He who hears, let him hear; and he who refrains, let him refrain; for they are a rebellious house.”
You, Son of man, procure a brick for yourself and set it before you, then incise upon its surface a representation of the city—that is, Jerusalem.
Lay siege against it; erect a siege rampart against it; pour out an earthen ramp against it; pitch camps against it; and station battering rams around it.

Take an iron plate for yourself and place it as an iron wall between you and the city; fix your gaze upon it, and let it be besieged while you besiege it. It shall serve as a sign to the house of Israel.
You shall recline upon your left side and place upon it the iniquity of the house of Israel; you shall bear their iniquity for the number of days that you recline upon it.
For I have allotted you three hundred ninety days, corresponding to the number of years of their iniquity, and you shall bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.

When you have completed these, you shall recline a second time, upon your right side, and bear the iniquity of the house of Judah; I have assigned it to you: forty days, a day for a year, a day for a year.
You shall direct your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, with your arm bared, and prophesy against it.
Behold, I am placing fetters upon you, so that you cannot turn from one side to the other until you have completed the days of your siege.

Take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt for yourself, put them into a single vessel, and make bread for yourself from them; you shall eat it during the three hundred ninety days that you recline upon your side.
Your food, which you eat, shall be by weight—twenty shekels a day—and you shall eat it at appointed times.
Water you shall drink by measure—the sixth part of a hin—and you shall drink it at appointed times.
You shall eat it in the form of barley cakes, baking it before their eyes over cakes of human excrement.
Then the LORD said, “Thus shall the children of Israel eat their bread unclean among the nations to which I will drive them.”

Then I said, “Ah, Lord the LORD! Behold, my soul has never been defiled; from my youth until now I have not eaten what died of itself or was torn by beasts, nor has any abominable flesh entered my mouth.”
And He said to me, “See, I have given you cow dung in place of human dung, and you shall prepare your bread upon it.”
And He said to me, “Son of man, behold, I am breaking the supply of bread in Jerusalem, so that they shall eat bread by weight and in anxious distress, and drink water by measure and in desolation.”
Thus they shall lack bread and water, and each man shall waste away with his brother, and they shall rot away in their iniquity.
“And you, son of man, take unto yourself a keen sword; use it as a barber’s razor, and pass it over your head and over your beard; then take scales for weighing, and apportion the hair.

During the days of the siege, when their term is fulfilled, you shall consign a third to the flames in the midst of the city; you shall take a third and smite it with the sword round about the city; and a third you shall disperse to the wind, while I unsheathe a sword in pursuit of them.
“But take a few strands from there, and bind them in the folds of your garment.
Again, take some of these and cast them into the midst of the fire, and burn them in the fire; from thence fire shall issue forth to the whole house of Israel.”
“Thus says the Lord the LORD: ‘This is Jerusalem. I have set her in the midst of the nations, with lands encircling her.

Yet she has perverted My judgments into wickedness beyond the nations, and My statutes beyond the lands that surround her; for they have rejected My judgments and have not walked in them, nor in My statutes.’

Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: ‘Because you have been more turbulent than the nations round about you, and you have not walked in My statutes nor kept My ordinances, but you have conformed to the ordinances of the nations round about you—’”
“Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: ‘Behold, I Myself am against you, Jerusalem, and I will execute judgments within you in the sight of the nations.
Because of all your abominations, I will do to you what I have not done before, nor will I ever do the like again.
Therefore fathers among you shall devour their sons, and sons shall devour their fathers; I will execute judgments against you, and I will disperse all your remnant to every wind.’

“Therefore, as surely as I live, declares the Lord the LORD, because you have profaned My sanctuary with all your detestable idols and abominations, I will withdraw My favor; I will not spare you, and I will have no pity.

A third of your people shall perish by pestilence or be consumed by famine in your midst, a third shall fall by the sword round about you, and a third I will scatter to every wind and send a sword after them.”
“And when My fury is spent and I have satisfied My wrath against them, I will be appeased. Then they shall know that I, the the LORD, have spoken in My zeal.
I will make you a desolation and a reproach among the nations round about you, in the sight of all who pass by.
So you shall be a reproach and a taunt, a warning and a horror to the nations round about you, when I execute judgments against you in anger, wrath, and raging rebuke. I, the the LORD, have spoken.
“When I shower upon them the deadly arrows of famine to destroy them—for I will intensify the famine against you and cut off your supply of bread—

I will send famine and wild beasts against you, and they shall bereave you of your children; pestilence and bloodshed shall sweep through you, and I will bring a sword against you. I, the the LORD, have spoken.”
The word of the LORD came to me, saying, “
Son of man, fix your gaze upon the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them.

And say, ‘Hear the word of the Lord, the LORD! Thus says the Lord, the LORD, to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys: Behold, I am bringing the sword against you, and I shall annihilate your high places.’” “
Your altars shall be rendered desolate, your incense altars shattered, and I will cast down your slain before your idols.
I will lay the corpses of the Israelites before their idols, and I will scatter your bones around your altars.

In all your dwelling places the cities shall be laid waste, and the high places shall be desolated, so that your altars may be laid waste and made desolate, your idols broken and destroyed, your incense altars cut down, and your works blotted out.
The slain shall fall in your midst, and you shall know that I am the LORD.” “
Yet I will leave a remnant, so that you may have some who escape the sword among the nations when you are dispersed throughout the lands.

Those of you who escape will remember Me among the nations to which they are carried captive—how I was crushed by their adulterous heart that turned away from Me and by their eyes that lusted after their idols. They will loathe themselves for the evils they have committed and for all their abominations.
And they shall know that I am the LORD; I did not speak in vain when I declared that I would bring this calamity upon them.” “

Thus says the Lord, the LORD: Clap your hand and stamp your foot, and say, ‘Alas!’ because of all the vile abominations of the house of Israel, for they shall fall by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence.
The one who is far off shall perish by pestilence, the one who is near shall fall by the sword, and the one who remains besieged shall die of famine. Thus I will expend My fury upon them.

And you shall know that I am the LORD when their slain lie among their idols around their altars—on every high hill, on all the mountaintops, under every green tree, and under every leafy oak—wherever they offered a pleasing aroma to all their idols.
I will stretch out My hand against them and render the land desolate and waste, from the wilderness to Diblah, throughout all their habitations. And they shall know that I am the LORD.”
The word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, this is what the Lord the LORD says to the land of Israel: ‘The end! The end has come upon the four corners of the earth.’
The end is now upon you, and I will send My anger against you; I will judge you according to your ways and bring upon you all your abominations.
My eye will not spare you, nor will I have pity; for I will bring your ways upon you, and your abominations will be in your midst. Then you will know that I am the the LORD.’”
“Thus says the Lord the LORD: ‘Disaster upon disaster! Behold, it is coming.
The end has come! The end has come! It has awakened against you. Behold, it is coming.
Doom has come upon you, O inhabitant of the land. The time has come; the day is near—panic in the mountains, not a joyful shout.
Now, very soon, I will pour out My wrath upon you and spend My anger against you; I will judge you according to your ways and bring upon you all your abominations.
My eye will not spare, nor will I have pity. I will repay you according to your ways, and your abominations will be in your midst. Then you will know that I am the the LORD who strikes.’”
Behold, the day! Behold, it is coming! The dawn has broken; the rod has budded; arrogance has blossomed.
Violence has grown into a rod of wickedness. None of them, none of their multitude, none of their wealth, nor anything eminent among them will remain.
The time has come; the day has arrived. Let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn, for wrath is upon all their multitude.

For the seller will not return to what he sold, even though they are still alive; for the vision concerning all their multitude will not be revoked, and because of their iniquity, no one will preserve his life.
They have blown the trumpet and made everything ready, but no one goes to battle, for My wrath is upon all their multitude.
The sword is outside, and plague and famine are within. Whoever is in the field will die by the sword, and famine and plague will devour those in the city.
Their fugitives who escape will be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, each for his own iniquity.
Every hand will go limp, and every knee will turn to water.
They will put on sackcloth; horror will cover them; shame will be on every face, and baldness on every head.

They will throw their silver into the streets, and their gold will be treated as unclean. Their silver and gold will not be able to save them in the day of the the LORD's wrath. They will not satisfy their souls or fill their stomachs, for their wealth was the stumbling block of their iniquity.
They transformed the beauty of His ornaments into pride and made images of their abominations and detestable things with it; therefore I will make it an unclean thing to them.
I will give it into the hands of foreigners as plunder, and to the wicked of the earth as spoil, and they will profane it.
I will turn My face away from them, and they will profane My hidden place; robbers will enter it and profane it.
Forge the chain, for the land is full of bloodshed, and the city is full of violence.
So I will bring the worst of the nations, and they will possess their houses; I will put an end to the pride of the strong, and their holy places will be profaned.
Anguish is coming; they will seek peace, but there will be none.
Disaster upon disaster will come, and rumor upon rumor. They will seek a vision from a prophet, but the law will perish from the priest and counsel from the elders.

The king will mourn, the prince will be clothed with desolation, and the hands of the people of the land will tremble. I will deal with them according to their conduct, and I will judge them by their own standards; then they will know that I am the the LORD.
In the sixth year, on the fifth day of the sixth month, I was sitting in my house, and the elders of Judah were sitting before me, when the power of the Lord GOD fell upon me there.
I looked, and behold, a figure like that of a man: from His waist downward He was like fire, and from His waist upward His appearance was like the gleam of glowing metal.

He stretched out the form of a hand and seized me by a lock of my head; the Spirit lifted me up between earth and heaven and brought me, in visions of God, to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the inner gate that faces north, where the idol of jealousy had its seat.
And there I saw the glory of the God of Israel, just as in the vision I had seen in the valley.
Then He said to me, “Son of man, look northward.” So I looked northward, and there, north of the altar gate, stood this idol of jealousy.

He said to me, “Son of man, do you see what they are doing—the great abominations that the house of Israel is committing here, to drive Me far from My sanctuary? Yet you will turn and see even greater abominations.”
Then He brought me to the entrance of the courtyard, and I looked, and behold, a hole in the wall.
He said to me, “Son of man, dig through the wall.” So I dug through the wall, and behold, an entrance.
He said, “Go in and see the wicked abominations they are committing here.”
So I went in and looked, and behold, every form of creeping thing and detestable beast and all the idols of the house of Israel were carved all around on the wall.
Before them stood seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them; each had a censer in his hand, and a dense cloud of incense was rising.

He said to me, “Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the dark, each in his chamber of carved images? For they say, ‘The LORD does not see us; the LORD has forsaken the land.’
Again, you will see them committing even greater abominations.”
Then He brought me to the entrance of the north gate of the house of the LORD, and there sat women weeping for Tammuz.
He said to me, “Son of man, have you seen this? You will see even greater abominations than these.”

He brought me into the inner court of the house of the LORD, and there, at the entrance to the temple of the LORD, between the portico and the altar, were about twenty-five men with their backs to the temple of the LORD and their faces toward the east; they were bowing down to the sun in the east.

He said to me, “Son of man, have you seen this? Is it a trivial thing for the house of Judah to commit the abominations they are committing here? For they have filled the land with violence and have provoked Me to anger again and again. Look, they are thumbing their noses at Me.
Therefore I will act in wrath: I will not look on them with pity, nor will I show compassion. Though they cry out with a loud voice in My ears, I will not hear them.”
Then He cried in my ears with a loud voice, saying, "Draw near, O executioners of the city, each with his weapon of destruction in his hand."

And behold, six men came from the direction of the upper gate, which faces north, each with his shattering weapon in his hand; and among them was one man clothed in linen, with a scribe's inkhorn at his waist. They entered and stood beside the bronze altar.
The glory of the God of Israel rose from above the cherub where it had been to the threshold of the temple, and He called to the man clothed in linen who had the scribe's inkhorn at his waist.

And the LORD said to him, "Pass through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and put a mark upon the foreheads of the men who sigh and groan over all the abominations committed within it."
To the others He said in my hearing, "Pass through the city after him and strike; let your eye not spare, and you shall show no pity."

"Slay outright the old man, the young man, the virgin, the woman, and the little child, but do not touch any man upon whom is the mark; and begin at My sanctuary." So they began with the elders who were before the temple.
And He said to them, "Defile the temple and fill the courts with the slain. Go out!" So they went out and struck throughout the city.
As they struck, I was left alone. I fell upon my face and cried out, "Ah, Lord the LORD, will You destroy the whole remnant of Israel by pouring out Your wrath upon Jerusalem?"

He said to me, "The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great; the land is full of bloodshed, and the city is full of perversity, for they say, 'The LORD has forsaken the land; the LORD does not see.'
So I will not look with pity or spare them, but I will bring their ways upon their own heads."
Then the man clothed in linen, who had the inkhorn at his waist, reported, "I have done as You commanded."
Then I looked, and behold, above the expanse over the heads of the cherubim there appeared something like a sapphire stone, in appearance resembling a throne above them.

And He said to the man clothed in linen, “Go in among the wheels beneath the cherub, and fill your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim, and scatter them over the city.” And he went in as I watched.
Now the cherubim were standing on the south side of the temple when the man entered, and a cloud filled the inner court.

Then the glory of the the LORD rose from above the cherub to the threshold of the temple. The temple was filled with the cloud, and the court was filled with the radiance of the glory of the the LORD.
The sound of the cherubim’s wings could be heard as far as the outer court, like the voice of God Almighty when He speaks.
When He commanded the man clothed in linen, saying, “Take fire from between the wheels, from between the cherubim,” the man went in and stood beside a wheel.
Then the cherub stretched out his hand from among the cherubim to the fire that was among them. He took some and placed it in the hands of the man clothed in linen, who took it and went out.
The cherubim appeared to have the form of a human hand beneath their wings.
Then I looked and saw four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside each cherub, and the wheels gleamed like beryl.
In appearance, all four were alike, as though a wheel were within a wheel.
As they moved, they traveled in any of the four directions without pivoting; they followed the direction in which the heads faced, without turning as they moved.
Their entire bodies—their backs, hands, and wings—were full of eyes all around, as were their four wheels.
I heard the wheels being called “the whirling wheels.”
Each of the cherubim had four faces: one face was that of a cherub, the second that of a man, the third that of a lion, and the fourth that of an eagle.
Then the cherubim rose upward. These were the living creatures I had seen by the Kebar River.
When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved beside them; and when the cherubim raised their wings to rise from the earth, the wheels did not leave their side.
When the cherubim stood still, the wheels stood still; when they rose, the wheels rose with them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in them.
Then the glory of the the LORD departed from the threshold of the temple and stood above the cherubim.

As I watched, the cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the earth, and the wheels accompanied them. They stopped at the entrance of the east gate of the house of the the LORD, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
These were the living creatures I had seen beneath the God of Israel by the Kebar River, and I knew that they were cherubim.
Each had four faces and four wings, and beneath their wings was the form of human hands.
Their faces were like the faces I had seen by the Kebar River. Each moved straight ahead.

The Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the east gate of the house of the LORD, the gate that faces east; and behold, at the entrance of the gate there were twenty-five men, and among them I saw Jaazaniah the son of Azur and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people.
And He said to me, “Son of man, these are the men who devise iniquity and give wicked counsel in this city, who say,
‘The day of reckoning is not at hand, so there is no need to build houses; this city is the cauldron, and we are the meat it shelters.’”
Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, Son of man.
And the Spirit of the LORD fell upon me, and He said to me, “Say, Thus says the LORD: So you have said, O house of Israel, for I know the things that come into your mind.
You have multiplied your slain in this city and filled its streets with the slain.
Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: Your slain whom you have laid in its midst, they are the meat, and this city is the pot; but I will bring you out of it.
“You have feared the sword, and I will bring the sword upon you, declares the Lord the LORD.
And I will bring you out of its midst and deliver you into the hand of strangers, and execute judgments upon you.
You shall fall by the sword; I will judge you at the border of Israel, and you shall know that I am the LORD.
This city shall not be your pot, nor shall you be the flesh in its midst; I will judge you at the border of Israel.
And you shall know that I am the LORD, for you have not walked in My statutes, nor executed My judgments, but have done according to the judgments of the nations that are around you.”
And as I prophesied, Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died. Then I fell upon my face and cried out with a loud voice, and said, “Alas, O Lord the LORD! Will You make a full end of the remnant of Israel?”
And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

“Son of man, your brothers, your brothers, the men of your redemption, and all the house of Israel, all of them, are those of whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said, “‘Go far from the LORD; this land has been given to us for a possession.’

“Therefore say, Thus says the Lord the LORD: Though I have removed them far off among the nations, and though I have scattered them among the countries, yet I have been a sanctuary to them for a little while in the countries where they have gone.
Therefore say, Thus says the Lord the LORD: I will gather you from the peoples and assemble you from the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.
And they shall come there, and they shall remove from it all its detestable things and all its abominations.
And I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take away the heart of stone from your flesh and give them a heart of flesh.
that they may walk in My statutes and keep My ordinances and do them; and they shall be My people, and I will be their God.
But as for those whose heart goes after their detestable things and their abominations, I will bring their way upon their own heads, declares the Lord the LORD.”
Then the cherubim lifted up their wings, and the wheels were beside them; and the glory of the God of Israel was over them above.
And the glory of the LORD went up from the midst of the city and stood upon the mountain that is on the east side of the city.
And the Spirit lifted me up and brought me in a vision by the Spirit of God into Chaldea, to the exiles. Then the vision that I had seen went up from me.
And I spoke to the exiles all the words of the LORD that He had shown me.
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, you dwell in the midst of a rebellious house; they have eyes to see, yet they do not see, and ears to hear, yet they do not hear, for they are a rebellious house.

“And you, son of man, prepare an exile’s baggage for yourself, and go into exile by day before their eyes; from your place you shall remove to another place before their eyes. Perhaps they will perceive, though they are a rebellious house.
Before their eyes you shall bring out your baggage by day, as baggage for exile, and in the evening you shall go out before their eyes, as those who go out into exile.
Before their eyes, dig through the wall for yourself, and carry your baggage out through it.

Before their eyes you shall lift it upon your shoulder and carry it out in the dark; you shall veil your face so that you do not see the land, for I have appointed you a portent to the house of Israel.”

So I did as I was commanded: I brought out my baggage by day, as baggage for exile, and in the evening I dug through the wall with my hand; I brought it out in the dark, and I bore it upon my shoulder before their eyes.
In the morning the word of the the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, has not the rebellious house, the house of Israel, said to you, ‘What are you doing?’”
“Say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord the LORD: This oracle concerns the prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel who are in it.’
Say, ‘I am a sign for you: as I have done, so shall it be done to them; they shall go into exile, into captivity.’

And the prince who is among them shall bear his baggage upon his shoulder in the dark and go out; they shall dig through the wall to bring him out through it; he shall cover his face, so that he may not see the land with his eyes.
I will spread My net over him, and he shall be caught in My snare; I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, yet he shall not see it, and there he shall die.
I will scatter to every wind all who are around him, his helpers and all his bands, and I will draw the sword after them.
Then they shall know that I am the the LORD, when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them through the countries.
But I will spare a few of them from the sword, from famine, and from pestilence, so that they may recount all their abominations among the nations to which they go, and know that I am the the LORD.”
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, eat your bread with trembling, and drink your water with quaking and anxiety.

Say to the people of the land, ‘Thus says the Lord the LORD concerning the inhabitants of Jerusalem in the land of Israel: They shall eat their bread with anxiety and drink their water in dismay, because the land shall be stripped of its fullness on account of the violence of all who dwell in it.
The inhabited cities shall be laid waste, and the land shall become a desolation; then you shall know that I am the the LORD.’”
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, what is this proverb that you have in the land of Israel, saying, ‘The days are prolonged, and every vision fails’?

Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord the LORD: I will put an end to this proverb, and they shall no longer use it as a proverb in Israel. But say to them, “The days are at hand, and every vision will be fulfilled.”’
For there shall no longer be any false vision or flattering divination among the house of Israel.

For I am the the LORD; I will speak the word that I will speak, and it will come to pass; it will no longer be delayed. For in your days, O rebellious house, I will speak the word and fulfill it, declares the Lord the LORD.”
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, behold, the house of Israel says, ‘The vision that he sees is for many days ahead, and he prophesies of distant times.’
Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord the LORD: None of My words will be delayed any longer, but the word that I speak will be performed, declares the Lord the LORD.’”
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
"Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who prophesy, and say to those who prophesy from their own heart, 'Hear the word of the LORD:'"
Thus says the Lord the LORD: "Woe to the fatuous prophets who follow their own spirit, though they have seen nothing.
O Israel, your prophets have been like foxes among ruins.
You have not ascended into the breaches, nor erected a wall for the house of Israel, that it might stand in battle on the day of the LORD."
"They have envisioned vanity and deceit, and say, 'The The LORD declares,' though the LORD has not sent them, and they have caused the people to hope that the word will be confirmed.
Did you not see a vain vision and utter a deceitful divination, saying, 'The The LORD declares,' although I have not spoken?"
Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: "Because you have spoken vanity and seen deceit, therefore I am against you," declares the Lord the LORD.

"My hand will be against the prophets who envision vanity and deceit; they shall not be in the council of My people, nor be inscribed in the register of the house of Israel, nor shall they enter the land of Israel; and you shall know that I am the Lord the LORD."
"Because, indeed because they have led My people astray, saying, 'Peace,' when there is no peace; and when one builds a wall, they plaster it with whitewash.
Say to those who plaster it with whitewash that it will collapse: a deluging rain will come, and you, O hailstones, will fall, and a tempestuous wind will rend it apart.
Behold, when the wall collapses, will it not be said to you, 'Where is the plaster with which you plastered it?'"
Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: "In My wrath I will let loose a tempestuous wind; in My anger a deluging rain and hailstones will come to destroy.

I will demolish the wall that you plastered with whitewash and bring it down to the ground, to its foundation, so that it is laid bare; it will collapse, and you will be consumed in its midst; and you will know that I am the LORD.
I will expend My wrath upon the wall and upon those who plastered it with whitewash, and I will say to you, 'The wall is no more, and those who plastered it are no more'—
namely, the prophets of Israel who prophesy concerning Jerusalem and envision peace for her, but there is no peace," declares the Lord the LORD.
"And you, Son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy out of their own heart, and prophesy against them,

and say, 'Thus says the Lord the LORD: Woe to the women who sew magic bands upon all wrists and fashion veils for heads of every stature, to ensnare souls! Will you ensnare the souls of My people and preserve your own souls alive?

You have profaned Me among My people for handfuls of barley and pieces of bread, by your lying to My people who give heed to lies, to put to death souls that should not die and to keep alive souls that should not live.'"

Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: "Behold, I am against your magic bands with which you ensnare souls there like birds, and I will tear them from your arms, and I will release the souls that you ensnare like birds.
I will tear away your veils and deliver My people from your hand, and they will no longer be prey in your hand; and you will know that I am the LORD.

Because you have grieved the heart of the righteous with falsehood, although I did not grieve him, and you have strengthened the hands of the wicked so that he does not turn from his wicked way to save his life,
therefore you will no longer see vain visions nor practice divination; and I will deliver My people from your hand, and you will know that I am the LORD."
The word of the LORD came to me, saying:
“Son of man, how does the wood of the vine surpass all other wood—the branch that grew among the trees of the forest?
Can any useful article be fashioned from its timber? Could one even extract from it a peg upon which to suspend some vessel?
