Behold, it has been consigned to the fire as fuel: the flames have consumed both its extremities, and its core is charred. Could it still be of service for any work?
Even when it was intact, it was not fashioned for any task; how much less, then, once fire has consumed and charred it, can it be turned to any useful purpose?”

“Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Just as I have consigned the vine’s timber—standing among the trees of the forest—to the fire as fuel, so have I consigned the inhabitants of Jerusalem to the flames.
I will set My face against them; though they come forth from the fire, the fire shall nonetheless devour them; and you shall know that I am the LORD when I set My face against them.
I will lay the land waste, because they have acted treacherously, declares the Lord GOD.”
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, make known to Jerusalem her abominations,
and say, Thus says the Lord the LORD to Jerusalem: Your origin and your birth are from the land of the Canaanites; your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite.
“On the day you were born, your umbilical cord was not cut, you were not bathed in water to cleanse you, you were not rubbed with salt, nor were you wrapped in swaddling cloths.
No eye looked upon you with pity to do any of these things for you out of compassion; rather, you were cast out into the open field, abhorred on the day of your birth.
When I passed by you and saw you wallowing in your blood, I said to you, ‘Live!’—yes, I said to you in your blood, ‘Live!’
I made you flourish like a plant of the field; you grew and became tall, and you attained full adornment. Your breasts were formed and your hair grew, yet you remained naked and bare.

“When I passed by you again and saw you, your time was the time of love. I took you to Myself in marriage and covered your nakedness; I swore to you and entered into a covenant with you, declares the Lord the LORD, and you became Mine.
Then I bathed you with water, washed your blood from you, and anointed you with oil.
I clothed you in embroidered cloth, shod you with fine leather, bound a linen turban about your head, and covered you with silk.
I adorned you with ornaments, placed bracelets upon your wrists, and hung a chain about your neck.
I put a ring in your nose, earrings in your ears, and a splendid crown upon your head.

Thus you were adorned with gold and silver, and your clothing was of fine linen, silk, and embroidered cloth. You ate fine flour, honey, and oil, and you grew exceedingly beautiful, advancing to royalty.
Your renown went out among the nations because of your beauty, for it was perfect through the splendor I had bestowed upon you, declares the Lord the LORD.
“But you trusted in your beauty and prostituted yourself because of your renown, lavishing your harlotries upon every passerby; your beauty became theirs.
You took some of your garments and made for yourself colorful shrines, and upon them you prostituted yourself—such a thing had never occurred and never shall again.
You also took your beautiful jewels, My gold and My silver that I had given you, and made for yourself male images, and with them you prostituted yourself.
You took your embroidered garments and covered them, and you set My oil and My incense before them.
My bread too—the fine flour, oil, and honey with which I fed you—you set before them as a pleasing aroma, declares the Lord the LORD.
“You took your sons and your daughters, whom you had borne to Me, and sacrificed them to be devoured. Were your acts of prostitution so insignificant
that you slaughtered My children and delivered them as burnt offerings to these idols?
In all your abominations and harlotries, you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, wallowing in your blood.
“After all your wickedness—woe, woe to you, declares the Lord the LORD—
you built yourself a vaulted chamber and erected a lofty shrine in every square.
At the head of every street you built your lofty shrine, rendered your beauty an abomination, and offered yourself to every passerby, multiplying your prostitution.
“You prostituted yourself to the Egyptians, your lustful neighbors, multiplying your prostitution to provoke Me to anger.
Therefore I stretched out My hand against you, diminished your allotment, and delivered you to the desire of your enemies, the daughters of the Philistines, who were ashamed of your lewd conduct.
You also prostituted yourself to the Assyrians, because you were not satisfied; you prostituted yourself to them and still were not satisfied.
You multiplied your prostitution with Chaldea, the land of commerce, and even then you were not satisfied.
“How sick is your heart, declares the Lord the LORD, for doing all these things, the deeds of a shameless prostitute!
When you built your vaulted chamber at the head of every street and your lofty shrine in every square, you were unlike a prostitute, because you scorned payment.
O adulterous wife, who takes strangers instead of her husband!
Men give gifts to all prostitutes, but you gave your gifts to all your lovers, bribing them to come to you from every side in your prostitution.
Thus you differed from other women in your prostitution: no one solicited you to prostitute yourself, and you gave payment, whereas they receive payment from you. So you were different.
“Therefore, O prostitute, hear the word of the LORD:

Thus says the Lord the LORD, Because your lust was poured out and your nakedness uncovered in your prostitution with your lovers and with all your abominable idols, and because of the blood of your children that you gave to them,

therefore I will gather all your lovers with whom you took pleasure, together with all those you loved and all those you hated. I will gather them against you from every side and uncover your nakedness to them, so that they may see all your nakedness.
“I will judge you with the judgments of adulteresses and of those who shed blood, and I will bring upon you the blood of wrath and jealousy.
I will deliver you into their hands, and they will demolish your vaulted chamber, tear down your lofty shrines, strip off your clothes, take your beautiful jewels, and leave you naked and bare.
They will bring a crowd against you, stone you, and cut you to pieces with their swords.
They will burn your houses with fire and execute judgments against you in the sight of many women. I will make you cease from prostitution, and you shall no longer give payment.
Thus I will satisfy My wrath against you, and My jealousy will depart from you; I will be calm and will be angry no more.

Because you did not remember the days of your youth but enraged Me in all these things, I have brought your conduct upon your own head, declares the Lord the LORD. Have you not committed lewdness in addition to all your abominations?
“Behold, everyone who uses proverbs will apply this proverb to you: ‘Like mother, like daughter.’

You are your mother’s daughter, who despised her husband and her children; and you are the sister of your sisters, who despised their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.
Your elder sister is Samaria, who lived with her daughters to the north of you; your younger sister is Sodom, who lived with her daughters to the south of you.
Yet you did not merely walk in their ways or commit their abominations; within a very little time you became more corrupt than they in all your ways.
“As I live, declares the Lord the LORD, your sister Sodom and her daughters have not done as you and your daughters have done.
Behold, this was the guilt of your sister Sodom: she and her daughters had pride, an abundance of food, and prosperous ease, but they did not aid the poor and needy.
They were haughty and committed an abomination before Me, so I removed them when I saw it.
Samaria has not committed even half of your sins; you have committed more abominations than they, and by all your abominations you have made your sisters appear righteous.

You too must bear your disgrace, because you have intervened on behalf of your sisters. Because of your sins, in which you acted more abominably than they, they are more righteous than you. So be ashamed and bear your disgrace, because you have made your sisters appear righteous.
“I will restore the fortunes of Sodom and her daughters and the fortunes of Samaria and her daughters, and I will restore your fortunes among them,
so that you may bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all that you have done, becoming a consolation to them.

As for your sisters, Sodom and her daughters shall return to their former state, Samaria and her daughters shall return to their former state, and you and your daughters shall return to your former state.
Was not your sister Sodom a byword in your mouth in the day of your pride,

before your wickedness was uncovered? Now you have become an object of reproach for the daughters of Edom and all her neighbors, and for the daughters of the Philistines, all around you who despise you.
You bear the penalty of your lewdness and your abominations, declares the LORD.
“For thus says the Lord the LORD: I will deal with you as you have done, you who despised the oath by breaking the covenant.
Yet I will remember My covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish for you an everlasting covenant.
Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you receive your sisters, both your elder and your younger, and I give them to you as daughters, but not on account of your covenant.
I will establish My covenant with you, and you shall know that I am the LORD,
so that you may remember and be confounded, and never open your mouth again because of your shame, when I make atonement for you for all that you have done, declares the Lord the LORD.”
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
"Son of man, propound a riddle and speak a parable to the house of Israel.
And you shall say, Thus says the Lord the LORD: A great eagle with great wings, long pinions, and full plumage of variegated feathers came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar.
He cropped off the topmost of its young twigs and carried it to a land of Canaan; in a city of merchants he set it.
He also took some of the seed of the land and planted it in a fertile field; he placed it beside abundant waters; he set it like a willow.
It sprouted and became a spreading vine of low stature, its branches turning toward him, while its roots remained beneath him; so it became a vine and produced branches and sent out boughs.

There was another great eagle with great wings and much plumage; and behold, this vine bent its roots toward him and sent out its branches toward him from the bed where it was planted, that he might water it.
It was planted in good soil beside abundant waters, that it might produce branches and bear fruit and become a splendid vine.

Say, Thus says the Lord the LORD: Will it thrive? Will he not pull up its roots and cut off its fruit, so that it withers—all its fresh sprouting leaves withering? It will not take a mighty arm or a multitude of people to pluck it up by its roots.
Behold, though planted, will it thrive? When the east wind strikes it, will it not wither? On the beds where it grew it will wither."
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

"Son of man, say now to the rebellious house, 'Do you not know what these things mean?' Say, 'Behold, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and took its king and its princes and brought them to him in Babylon.'
He took one of the royal seed and made a covenant with him, binding him by oath; he also took away the chief men of the land,
that the kingdom might be humble, not exalting itself, but keeping his covenant, that it might stand.
But he rebelled against him by sending his envoys to Egypt to obtain horses and many people. Will he prosper? Will he escape who does such things? Can he break the covenant and still escape?
As I live, declares the Lord the LORD, surely in the place of the king who made him king—whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke—there in Babylon he shall die.
Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company will not avail for him in war, when siege ramps are thrown up and siege walls built to cut off many lives.
He despised the oath by breaking the covenant; though he gave his hand, having done all these things, he shall not escape.
Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: As I live, surely My oath, which he despised, and My covenant, which he broke, I will bring upon his own head.
I will spread My net over him, and he shall be caught in My snare; I will bring him to Babylon and enter into judgment with him there for his trespass committed against Me.
All his fugitives in all his bands shall fall by the sword, and the survivors shall be scattered to every wind; and you shall know that I am the LORD; I have spoken."
"Thus says the Lord the LORD: I will also take from the top of the tall cedar a tender sprig from the topmost of its young twigs, and I will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.

On the mountain height of Israel I will plant it; it shall bear branches and produce fruit and become a noble cedar. Birds of every kind will nest under it; in the shade of its branches they will dwell.
All the trees of the field shall know that I am the LORD; I bring low the high tree, exalt the low tree, dry up the green tree, and make the dry tree flourish. I, the LORD, have spoken and done it."
The word of the LORD came to me, saying:
“What do you mean by repeating this proverb in the land of Israel: ‘The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge’?
As I live, declares the Lord the LORD, you shall no longer have occasion to employ this proverb in Israel.
Behold, every soul is Mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is Mine. The soul that sins, it shall die. “
If a man is righteous and practices justice and righteousness,

if he has not eaten upon the mountains, has not lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, has not defiled his neighbor’s wife, and has not approached a woman during her menstrual uncleanness;
if he has not oppressed anyone, but has restored the pledge to his debtor, has not committed robbery, has given his bread to the hungry, and has covered the naked with a garment;
if he has not lent at interest nor taken usury, has withdrawn his hand from iniquity, and has executed true justice between man and man;
if he walks in My statutes and keeps My ordinances, acting faithfully—he is righteous; he shall surely live, declares the Lord the LORD. “
Suppose he begets a son who is violent, a shedder of blood, and who does any of these things—
though his father has done none of them: a son who eats upon the mountains, defiles his neighbor’s wife,
oppresses the poor and needy, commits robbery, does not restore a pledge, lifts up his eyes to idols, commits an abomination,
lends at interest and takes usury. Shall he live? He shall not live. He has done all these abominations; he shall surely die, and his blood shall be upon him. “
Now suppose that man begets a son who sees all the sins his father has committed, and though he sees them, does not do likewise:
he does not eat upon the mountains, does not lift up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, does not defile his neighbor’s wife,
does not oppress anyone, does not withhold a pledge, does not commit robbery, gives his bread to the hungry, covers the naked with a garment,
withdraws his hand from harming the poor, takes no interest or usury, walks in My ordinances and keeps My statutes—he shall not die for his father’s iniquity; he shall surely live.
As for his father, because he practiced extortion, robbed his brother, and did what was not good among his people, behold, he shall die for his iniquity.“
Yet you say, ‘Why does the son not bear the iniquity of the father?’ When the son has done justice and righteousness, and has kept all My statutes and done them, he shall surely live.

The soul that sins, it shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, nor shall the father bear the iniquity of the son; the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him.“
But if the wicked man turns from all his sins that he has committed, and keeps all My statutes, and does justice and righteousness, he shall surely live; he shall not die.
None of the transgressions he has committed shall be remembered against him; in the righteousness he has done he shall live.
Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked? declares the Lord the LORD. Is it not rather that he should turn from his ways and live?

But when a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, doing according to all the abominations that the wicked man does, shall he live? All the righteousness he has done shall not be remembered; in his treachery and in his sin that he has committed, he shall die.“
Yet you say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ Hear now, house of Israel: Is My way not just? Is it not your ways that are not just?
When a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, he shall die for it; in the iniquity that he has committed, he shall die.
And when a wicked man turns from his wickedness that he has committed, and does justice and righteousness, he shall preserve his life.
Because he considered and turned from all his transgressions that he had committed, he shall surely live; he shall not die.
But the house of Israel says, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ Are My ways not just, O house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are not just?“
Therefore I will judge you, house of Israel, each according to his ways, declares the Lord the LORD. Repent and turn from all your transgressions, lest iniquity become your ruin.
Cast away from yourselves all the transgressions you have committed, and make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit! Why will you die, house of Israel?
For I have no pleasure in the death of anyone, declares the Lord the LORD; therefore turn back, and live.”
You are to intone a dirge over the princes of Israel.
And declare, “What was your mother? A lioness who crouched among lions and reared her cubs amid young lions.”
She nurtured one of her cubs until he became a young lion; he learned to rend prey and devoured human beings.
The nations heard of him; he was ensnared in their pit and dragged with hooks to the land of Egypt.
When she perceived that her hope had vanished, she took another cub and raised him to be a young lion.
He prowled among lions; he became a young lion; he learned to rend prey and devoured human beings.
He ravaged their widows and devastated their cities; the land and all its fullness were aghast at the sound of his roaring.
Nations from the provinces round about arrayed themselves against him; they spread their net over him, and he was taken in their pit.
They confined him in a cage with hooks and conveyed him to the king of Babylon; they incarcerated him in strongholds, so that his voice would no longer resound upon the mountains of Israel.
Your mother was like a vine of your own bloodline, planted beside the waters; it was fruitful and luxuriantly branched because of abundant water.
She had stalwart boughs, fit to be scepters of rulers; her stature towered above the dense foliage, and she was conspicuous in her height amid the profusion of her branches.
Yet she was uprooted in fury and cast to the ground; the east wind withered her fruit; her stout boughs were shattered and dried, and fire consumed them.
Now she is planted in the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty land.
Fire has issued from the rod of her branches and consumed her fruit, so that no sturdy bough remains in her to serve as a scepter for ruling. This is a dirge, and it shall remain a dirge.
On the tenth day of the fifth month in the seventh year, certain men from among the elders of Israel came to inquire of the the LORD, and they sat down before me.
Then the word of the the LORD came to me, saying:
“Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord the LORD: Have you come to inquire of Me? As I live, declares the Lord the LORD, I will not be inquired of by you.
Will you judge them, son of man? Will you judge them? Then confront them with the abominations of their fathers.’”

“And say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord the LORD: On the day I chose Israel, I raised My hand in oath to the descendants of the house of Jacob, and I made Myself known to them in the land of Egypt; I raised My hand to them, saying, “I am the the LORD your God.”
On that day I raised My hand to them to bring them out of the land of Egypt into a land that I had searched out for them, flowing with milk and honey, the most glorious of all lands.
And I said to them, “Each of you must throw away the detestable things before your eyes, and do not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt; I am the the LORD your God.”

But they rebelled against Me and were unwilling to listen to Me; they did not each throw away the detestable things before their eyes, nor did they forsake the idols of Egypt. So I said I would pour out My wrath upon them, to spend My anger on them in the midst of the land of Egypt.

But I acted for the sake of My Name, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations among whom they dwelt, in whose sight I had made Myself known to them by bringing them out of the land of Egypt.’”
“So I brought them out of the land of Egypt and led them into the wilderness.
I gave them My statutes and made known to them My judgments, by which, if a person does them, he shall live.
Moreover, I gave them My Sabbaths, to be a sign between Me and them, that they might know that I am the the LORD who sanctifies them.

But the house of Israel rebelled against Me in the wilderness; they did not walk in My statutes, and they rejected My judgments, which, if a person does them, he shall live by them; and they greatly profaned My Sabbaths. So I said I would pour out My wrath upon them in the wilderness to destroy them.”
“But I acted for the sake of My Name, lest it be profaned in the sight of the nations, in whose sight I had brought them out.
Moreover, I raised My hand to them in the wilderness that I would not bring them into the land that I had given them, flowing with milk and honey, the most glorious of all lands,
because they rejected My judgments and did not walk in My statutes, and profaned My Sabbaths; for their heart went after their idols.
Nevertheless, My eye spared them from destruction, and I did not make an end of them in the wilderness.”
“And I said to their children in the wilderness, ‘Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers, nor keep their judgments, nor defile yourselves with their idols.
I am the the LORD your God; walk in My statutes, keep My judgments, and do them.
And sanctify My Sabbaths, and they shall be a sign between Me and you, that you may know that I am the the LORD your God.’”

“But the children rebelled against Me; they did not walk in My statutes, nor keep My judgments to do them, which, if a person does them, he shall live by them; and they profaned My Sabbaths. So I said I would pour out My wrath upon them, to spend My anger on them in the wilderness.
Nevertheless, I withdrew My hand and acted for the sake of My Name, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations, in whose sight I had brought them out.
Moreover, I raised My hand to them in the wilderness, to scatter them among the nations and to disperse them through the lands,
because they had not executed My judgments, but had rejected My statutes and profaned My Sabbaths, and their eyes were set on their fathers’ idols.”
“Moreover, I gave them statutes that were not good and judgments by which they could not live.
And I defiled them through their gifts, in that they caused all that opens the womb to pass through the fire, that I might devastate them, so that they would know that I am the the LORD.”
“Therefore, son of man, speak to the house of Israel and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord the LORD: In this too your fathers have blasphemed Me by acting treacherously against Me.

For when I brought them into the land that I had sworn to give them, then they saw every high hill and every leafy tree, and there they offered their sacrifices and presented their provocative offerings; there they made their soothing aroma and poured out their drink offerings.
Then I said to them, “What is the high place to which you go?” So its name is called Bamah to this day.’”
“Therefore say to the house of Israel, ‘Thus says the Lord the LORD: Are you defiling yourselves in the way of your fathers, and prostituting yourselves with their detestable things?

And when you offer your gifts, when you make your sons pass through the fire, you defile yourselves with all your idols to this day. And shall I be inquired of by you, O house of Israel? As I live, declares the Lord the LORD, I will not be inquired of by you.
And what comes into your mind shall not be at all—what you say, “Let us be like the nations, like the families of the lands, serving wood and stone.”’”
“As I live, declares the Lord the LORD, surely with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm and with wrath poured out I will rule over you.
I will bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the lands where you have been scattered, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm and with wrath poured out.
And I will bring you into the wilderness of the peoples, and there I will enter into judgment with you face to face.
As I entered into judgment with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so I will enter into judgment with you, declares the Lord the LORD.
I will make you pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant.

I will purge from among you the rebels and those who transgress against Me; I will bring them out of the land where they sojourn, but they shall not enter the land of Israel. Then you shall know that I am the the LORD.”

“As for you, O house of Israel, thus says the Lord the LORD: Go, serve every one his idols, but afterward you will surely listen to Me, and you shall no longer profane My holy Name with your gifts and your idols.

For on My holy mountain, on the mountain height of Israel, declares the Lord the LORD, there all the house of Israel, all of them, shall serve Me in the land; there I will accept them, and there I will require your contributions and the choicest of your offerings, with all your holy things.

As a pleasing aroma I will accept you, when I bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the lands where you have been scattered; and I will be sanctified through you in the sight of the nations.
And you shall know that I am the the LORD, when I bring you into the land of Israel, into the land that I swore to give to your fathers.
And there you shall remember your ways and all your deeds by which you have been defiled; and you shall loathe yourselves in your own sight for all the evils that you have committed.

And you shall know that I am the the LORD, when I deal with you for My Name's sake, not according to your evil ways nor according to your corrupt deeds, O house of Israel, declares the Lord the LORD.”
And the word of the the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, set your face toward the south, and speak prophetically toward the south, and prophesy against the forest of the field in the Negev.

And say to the forest of the Negev, ‘Hear the word of the the LORD: Thus says the Lord the LORD: Behold, I will kindle a fire in you, and it shall devour every green tree in you and every dry tree; the blazing flame shall not be quenched, and every face from south to north shall be scorched by it.’”
“And all flesh shall see that I, the the LORD, have kindled it; it shall not be quenched.”
Then I said, “Alas, Lord the LORD! They are saying of me, ‘He is speaking in parables.’”
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, turn your gaze toward Jerusalem, speak prophetically against the sanctuaries, and prophesy against the land of Israel.
Say to the land of Israel, ‘Thus says the the LORD: Behold, I am against you, and I will draw My sword from its sheath and cut off from you both the righteous and the wicked.
Because I cut off from you both the righteous and the wicked, My sword will go out from its sheath against all flesh from south to north.
Then all flesh will know that I, the the LORD, have drawn My sword from its sheath; it shall not return again.’”
And as for you, son of man, groan in their sight with a breaking of your loins and with bitterness.

When they ask you, “Why are you groaning?” say, “At the report that is coming, every heart will melt, all hands will grow feeble, every spirit will faint, and all knees will become as water. Behold, it is coming, and it shall be, declares the Lord, the the LORD.”
Again the word of the the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, prophesy and say, ‘Thus says the Lord, the the LORD: A sword, a sword is sharpened and also polished.
It is sharpened for slaughter, polished to flash like lightning. Should we then rejoice in the scepter of My son? The blade treats every staff with contempt.
It has been given to be polished, to be seized in the hand; it is sharpened and polished to be placed in the hand of the slayer.
Cry out and wail, son of man, for it is against My people; it is against all the princes of Israel. They are delivered to the sword along with My people; therefore strike your thigh.
For it is a test; and what if even the scepter that holds all in contempt should be no more? declares the Lord, the the LORD.’”
“And you, son of man, prophesy and clap your hands; let the sword strike twice, even three times—the sword of the slain, the sword of the great one to be slain, penetrating them.
I have set the point of the sword against all their gates, to melt the heart and multiply their stumbling blocks. Ah, it is fashioned like lightning, honed for slaughter.
Slash to the right; set your blade to the left—wherever your face is turned.
I too will clap My hands, and I will satisfy My wrath. I, the the LORD, have spoken.”
The word of the the LORD came to me again:
“And you, son of man, set before yourself two roads for the sword of the king of Babylon to travel; both shall come from a single land. Make a signpost; make it at the head of the road to the city.
Appoint a road for the sword to come to Rabbah of the Ammonites, and to Judah, into fortified Jerusalem.
“For the king of Babylon stands at the parting of the ways, at the head of the two roads, to practice divination: he shakes arrows, inquires of household idols, and examines the liver.

In his right hand is the divination for Jerusalem—to set battering rams, to open the mouth in slaughter, to lift up a shout, to set battering rams against the gates, to cast up a siege ramp, and to build a siege wall.
To them it will seem like a vain divination, for sworn oaths are theirs; but he brings their iniquity to remembrance, that they may be seized.”

“Therefore thus says the Lord, the the LORD: Because you have made your iniquity to be remembered, in that your transgressions are uncovered and your sins revealed in all your deeds—because you have been remembered, you shall be seized by the hand.
And you, O profane, wicked prince of Israel, whose day has come in the time of final punishment,
thus says the Lord, the the LORD: Remove the turban and take off the crown; things shall not remain as they are. Exalt the lowly and abase the lofty.
A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it; this also shall not stand until the one whose right it is comes, and I will give it to Him.”

“And you, son of man, prophesy and say, ‘Thus says the Lord, the the LORD concerning the Ammonites and concerning their reproach: A sword, a sword is drawn for slaughter, polished to consume, to flash like lightning—
while they see false visions for you and divine lies for you, to lay you upon the necks of the wicked slain, whose day has come in the time of final punishment.
Return the sword to its sheath. In the place where you were created, in the land of your origin, I will judge you.
I will pour out My indignation upon you; I will blow upon you with the fire of My wrath, and I will deliver you into the hands of brutal men, craftsmen of destruction.
You shall be fuel for the fire; your blood shall be in the midst of the land. You shall not be remembered, for I, the the LORD, have spoken.’”
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying:
“You, son of man, will you judge—will you judge the city of bloodshed? Then declare to her all her abominations.
And say: Thus says the Lord the the LORD: O city that sheds blood in her midst, so that her day of reckoning may come, and that fashions idols for herself to defile herself!

You have become guilty by the blood you have shed, and you have been defiled by the idols you have made; you have hastened your days and brought on your years. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations and a mockery to all the lands.
Those near and those far from you will mock you—you whose name is defiled and whose turmoil is great.
Behold, the princes of Israel within you have each turned his strength to the shedding of blood.
Father and mother they have treated with contempt in you; they have oppressed the sojourner in your midst; orphan and widow they have wronged in you.
“My holy things you have despised, and My Sabbaths you have profaned.
In you are slanderers who shed blood; in you they feast upon the mountains; in your midst they commit lewdness.
In you they have uncovered a father’s nakedness; in you they have violated a woman during her menstrual impurity.
One man commits an abomination with his neighbor’s wife; another lewdly defiles his daughter-in-law; another humbles his sister, his father’s daughter, in you.
In you they take bribes to shed blood; you take interest and usury, and you extort your neighbors; and you have forgotten Me, declares the Lord the the LORD.
“And behold, I have struck My hand at your dishonest gain that you have made, and at the blood that has been in your midst.
Can your heart endure, or can your hands remain strong, in the days when I deal with you? I the the LORD have spoken, and I will do it.
I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you through the countries, and I will purge your filthiness from you.
You will be profaned in your own sight before the nations, and you will know that I am the the LORD.”
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying:
“Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross to Me; all of them are bronze, tin, iron, and lead in the furnace; they are the dross of silver.
Therefore thus says the Lord the the LORD: Because you all have become dross, behold, I will gather you into the midst of Jerusalem.
As one gathers silver, bronze, iron, lead, and tin into the furnace to blow fire upon it and melt it, so I will gather you in My anger and My wrath, and I will put you in and melt you.
I will collect you and blow upon you with the fire of My wrath, and you shall be melted in its midst.
As silver is melted in the furnace, so you shall be melted in its midst; and you shall know that I the the LORD have poured out My wrath upon you.”
The word of the the LORD came to me, saying:
“Son of man, say to her: You are a land not cleansed, not rained upon in the day of indignation.
A conspiracy of her prophets is in her midst, like a roaring lion tearing prey; they have devoured lives; they have taken treasure and precious things; they have multiplied her widows in her midst.

Her priests have done violence to My law and profaned My holy things; they have made no distinction between the holy and the common, nor have they taught the difference between the unclean and the clean; they have hidden their eyes from My Sabbaths, and I am profaned among them.
Her princes in her midst are like wolves tearing prey, shedding blood and destroying lives for dishonest gain.
Her prophets have smeared them with whitewash, seeing false visions and divining lies for them, saying, ‘Thus says the Lord the the LORD,’ when the the LORD has not spoken.
The people of the land have practiced extortion and committed robbery; they have oppressed the poor and needy; and they have mistreated the sojourner without justice.
I sought a man among them who would build up a wall and stand in the breach before Me for the land, that I might not destroy it, but I found none.
So I poured out My indignation upon them; I consumed them with the fire of My wrath; I brought their way upon their heads, declares the Lord the the LORD.”
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
"Son of man, there were two women, daughters of one mother,
and they prostituted themselves in Egypt. They engaged in prostitution from their youth; their breasts were fondled there, and their virgin bosoms were caressed.
The older was named Oholah, and her sister Oholibah. They became Mine and bore sons and daughters. As for their names, Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem.
"Oholah prostituted herself while she was Mine. She lusted after her lovers, the Assyrians, who were near at hand—
warriors clothed in blue, governors and commanders, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding upon horses.
She lavished her harlotry upon all the choice men of Assyria and defiled herself with every idol of those she coveted.
She did not abandon the prostitution she had begun in Egypt, when men lay with her in her youth, caressed her virgin bosom, and poured out their lust upon her.
Therefore I delivered her into the hands of her lovers, the Assyrians, after whom she lusted.
They exposed her nakedness, seized her sons and daughters, and put her to the sword. She became a byword among women, and they executed judgment upon her.
"Her sister Oholibah saw this, yet she was even more depraved in her lust than Oholah, and she surpassed her sister in promiscuity.
She lusted after the Assyrians—governors and commanders, warriors arrayed in full armor, horsemen riding upon horses—all of them desirable young men.
I saw that both of them were defiled; they had taken the same path.
But Oholibah carried her prostitution even further. She saw men portrayed upon the wall—images of the Chaldeans, incised in red,
with belts around their waists and flowing turbans upon their heads, all of them resembling officers, the very image of Babylonians of Chaldea, their native land.
At the sight of them she lusted after them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.
Then the Babylonians came to her, to the bed of love, and defiled her with their lust. After she had been defiled by them, she turned away from them in disgust.
When she uncovered her prostitution and exposed her nakedness, I turned away from her in disgust, just as I had turned away from her sister.
Yet she multiplied her prostitution, remembering the days of her youth, when she had prostituted herself in the land of Egypt.
She lusted after their paramours, whose flesh is like the flesh of donkeys and whose issue is like the issue of horses.
So you revisited the lewdness of your youth, when the Egyptians caressed your bosom and fondled your young breasts.
"Therefore, Oholibah, thus says the Lord, the LORD: I will incite your lovers against you—those from whom you turned away in disgust—and I will bring them upon you from every side—
the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, Pekod, Shoa, and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them—desirable young men, governors and commanders, officers and men of renown, all of them riding upon horses.

They will come against you with a host of peoples, with weapons, chariots, and wagons. They will array themselves against you on every side with buckler, shield, and helmet. I will commit judgment to them, and they will judge you according to their own standards.

I will vent My jealous rage against you, and they will deal with you in fury. They will cut off your nose and your ears, and your survivors will fall by the sword. They will seize your sons and your daughters, and your remnant will be consumed by fire.
They will strip you of your clothes and take your fine jewelry.
So I will put an end to your lewdness and your prostitution, which began in the land of Egypt, so that you will no longer lift your eyes to them or remember Egypt.
"For this is what the Lord, the LORD says: I am about to deliver you into the hands of those you hate, into the hands of those from whom you turned away in disgust.

They will deal with you in hatred and take all you have worked for; they will leave you naked and bare, and the nakedness of your prostitution will be exposed. Your lewdness and your prostitution will be brought to light.
I will do these things to you because you have prostituted yourself with the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.
You have followed the path of your sister, so I will put her cup into your hand.
This is what the Lord, the LORD says: You will drink your sister's cup, a cup deep and wide. It will bring you scorn and derision, for it holds so much.
You will be filled with drunkenness and grief, with a cup of devastation and desolation, the cup of your sister Samaria.
You will drink it and drain it; you will shatter it and tear your breasts. For I have spoken, declares the Lord, the LORD.
Therefore this is what the Lord, the LORD says: Because you have forgotten Me and cast Me behind your back, you must bear the consequences of your lewdness and your prostitution.
The LORD said to me: "Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Then confront them with their abominations.

"For they have committed adultery; blood is on their hands. They have committed adultery with their idols, and they have even sacrificed their children, whom they bore to Me, in the fire as food for them.
And they have done this to Me as well: On the same day they defiled My sanctuary and profaned My Sabbaths.
On the very day they sacrificed their children to their idols, they entered My sanctuary to profane it. Yes, this is what they did inside My house.
Furthermore, they sent for men who came from afar. When the messengers were sent, you bathed yourself, painted your eyes, and adorned yourself with jewelry.
You sat on a stately couch with a table spread before it, on which you had placed My incense and My oil.
The sound of a carefree crowd accompanied them; Sabeans were brought in from the desert along with men from the rabble, and they put bracelets on your wrists and beautiful crowns on your head.
Then I said of her who was worn out by adulteries, 'Now they will commit adultery with her, and she with them.'
"Yet men went to her as men go to a prostitute; so they went to Oholah and Oholibah, the lewd women.
But righteous men will judge them and sentence them as adulteresses and murderers, because they are adulteresses and blood is on their hands.
For this is what the Lord, the LORD says: I will bring a mob against them and give them over to terror and plunder.
The mob will stone them and cut them down with their swords. They will kill their sons and daughters and burn down their houses.
So I will put an end to lewdness in the land, that all women may be warned and not imitate your lewdness.
They will repay you for your lewdness, and you will bear the penalty of your idolatry. Then you will know that I am the Lord, the LORD."
In the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
"Son of man, inscribe for yourself the name of this day, this very day; for on this day the king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem.
And set forth a parable for the rebellious house, and say to them, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: Set the pot on the fire; set it on, and pour water into it.
Gather its pieces into it, every choice piece—the thigh and the shoulder; fill it with the select bones.
Take the choicest of the flock, and also heap the bones beneath it; boil its pieces thoroughly, and cook its bones in the midst of it.
"'Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Woe to the city of bloodshed, to the pot whose corrosion is in it, and whose corrosion has not gone out of it! Empty it piece by piece; no lot has fallen upon it.
For her blood was in the midst of her; she set it on the bare rock; she did not pour it out on the ground to cover it with dust.
To rouse wrath, to exact vengeance, I have set her blood on the bare rock, that it may not be covered.
Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Woe to the city of bloodshed! I too will make the pyre great.
Heap on the logs and kindle the fire; cook the meat thoroughly and mix in the spices; let the bones be scorched.
Then set the empty pot on its coals, that it may be heated and its bronze may glow, and its uncleanness may be melted in it, and its corrosion consumed.
She has wearied herself with toil, yet her thick corrosion has not gone out of her; her corrosion shall not go out by fire.
In your uncleanness lies indecency. Because I cleansed you, and you were not cleansed, you shall not be cleansed from your uncleanness anymore until I have satisfied My wrath upon you.

I, the LORD, have spoken; it shall come to pass, and I will do it. I will not recede, nor will I spare, nor will I relent; according to your ways and according to your deeds they will judge you, declares the Lord GOD.'
The word of The LORD came to me, saying,
"Son of man, behold, I am about to take away the desire of your eyes with a single blow. Yet you shall not mourn nor weep, nor shall your tears run down.
Groan quietly; make no mourning for the dead. Bind your turban on your head, and put your sandals on your feet; do not cover your mustache, and do not eat the bread of mourners."
So I spoke to the people in the morning, and in the evening my wife died. And in the morning I did as I was commanded.
And the people said to me, "Will you not tell us what these things you are doing mean for us?"
Then I said to them, "The word of the LORD came to me, saying: '

Say to the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am about to desecrate My sanctuary, the pride of your power, the desire of your eyes, and the yearning of your soul; and your sons and your daughters whom you left behind shall fall by the sword.
And you shall do as I have done. You shall not cover your mustache, nor eat the bread of mourners.
Your turbans shall be on your heads and your sandals on your feet; you shall not mourn nor weep, but you shall rot away in your iniquities and groan to one another.
Thus Ezekiel shall be a sign to you; according to all that he has done you shall do. When this comes, then you will know that I am the Lord GOD.'
"And you, son of man, on the day when I take from them their stronghold, the joy of their glory, the desire of their eyes, and the yearning of their soul—their sons and their daughters—
on that day a fugitive will come to you to report it to you.
On that day your mouth will be opened to the fugitive, and you shall speak and be mute no longer. So you will be a sign to them, and they shall know that I am the LORD."
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, direct your attention against the Ammonites and prophesy against them.

“And say to the Ammonites, ‘Hear the word of the Lord GOD: Thus says the Lord GOD: Because you said, “Aha!” concerning My sanctuary, that it was profaned, and concerning the land of Israel, that it was desolate, and concerning the house of Judah, that they went into exile,

“‘therefore I am consigning you to the eastern peoples as a possession. They shall pitch their camps in your midst and erect their dwellings within you; they shall consume your produce and drink your milk.
I will make Rabbah a pasture for camels and the Ammonites a resting place for flocks, and you shall know that I am the LORD.’
“For thus says the Lord GOD: Because you clapped your hands, stamped your feet, and rejoiced with all the contempt of your soul against the land of Israel,

therefore, behold, I have stretched out My hand against you and will give you as plunder to the nations. I will cut you off from the peoples and make you perish from the countries; I will destroy you, and you shall know that I am the LORD.”
“Thus says the Lord GOD: Because Moab and Seir said that the house of Judah was like all the nations,
therefore, behold, I am laying open the flank of Moab, from its cities to its frontier cities, the splendor of the land—Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim,
“and I will give it to the Ammonites as a possession, together with the sons of the East, so that the Ammonites may not be remembered among the nations.
I will execute judgments upon Moab, and they shall know that I am the LORD.”
“Thus says the Lord GOD: Because Edom acted vengefully against the house of Judah and incurred grave guilt by avenging itself upon them,
therefore thus says the Lord GOD: I will stretch out My hand against Edom and cut off from it both man and beast; I will make it desolate from Teman, and those of Dedan shall fall by the sword.
“I will take vengeance on Edom by the hand of My people Israel, and they shall deal with Edom according to My anger and My wrath; and they shall know My vengeance, declares the Lord GOD.”
“Thus says the Lord GOD: Because the Philistines acted vengefully and took revenge with malice in their souls, seeking to destroy with everlasting enmity,
therefore, behold, I am stretching out My hand against the Philistines; I will cut off the Cherethites and destroy the remnant of the seacoast,
“and I will execute great vengeance upon them in wrathful rebukes; and they shall know that I am the LORD, when I lay My vengeance upon them.”
In the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, because Tyre has said concerning Jerusalem, ‘Aha! The gates of the peoples are shattered; she has turned to me; I shall be filled, now that she is laid waste.’
Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: Behold, I am against you, O Tyre, and I will bring up against you many nations, as the sea brings up its waves.
They will destroy the walls of Tyre and demolish her towers; I will scrape her soil from her and make her a bare rock.
She shall be in the midst of the sea a place for spreading nets, for I have spoken, declares the Lord the LORD; and she shall become plunder for the nations.
Her villages in the countryside shall be slain by the sword, and they shall know that I am the LORD.”
“For thus says the Lord the LORD: Behold, I will bring against Tyre from the north Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, king of kings, with horses, chariots, horsemen, and a great company of people.
He will slay your villages in the countryside with the sword; he will set up a siege wall against you, pour out a siege ramp against you, and raise his shields against you.
He will direct the blow of his battering rams against your walls, and with his axes he will break down your towers.

Because of the multitude of his horses, their dust will cover you; your walls will tremble at the noise of horsemen, wheels, and chariots when he enters your gates as men enter a city already breached.
With the hooves of his horses he will trample all your streets; he will slay your people with the sword, and your mighty pillars will fall to the ground.

They will plunder your wealth and loot your merchandise; they will break down your walls and destroy your pleasant houses; and they will cast your stones, your timber, and your dust into the midst of the water.
I will put an end to the sound of your songs, and the sound of your harps will be heard no more.
I will make you a bare rock; you shall be a place for spreading nets; you shall never be rebuilt, for I the LORD have spoken, declares the Lord the LORD.”
“Thus says the Lord the LORD to Tyre: ‘Will not the coastlands tremble at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan and slaughter is made in your midst?’

Then all the princes of the sea will step down from their thrones, remove their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments; they will clothe themselves with trembling, sit on the ground, tremble every moment, and be appalled at you.

They will raise a lamentation over you and say to you, ‘How you have perished, O renowned city, inhabited by seafarers! She was mighty on the sea, she and her inhabitants, who spread their terror to all who dwelt around them.’
Now the coastlands tremble on the day of your fall; the coastlands that are in the sea are dismayed at your departure.”
“For thus says the Lord the LORD: When I make you a desolate city, like the cities that are not inhabited, when I bring up the deep over you and the great waters cover you,

then I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit, to the people of old, and I will make you dwell in the lowest parts of the earth, like the ancient ruins, with those who go down to the pit, so that you will not be inhabited; and I will bestow glory upon the land of the living.
I will make you a horror, and you shall be no more; though you are sought, you will never be found again, declares the Lord the LORD.”
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, raise a lamentation over Tyre,
and say to Tyre, who dwells at the entrances of the sea and traffics as a merchant among the peoples to many coastlands: Thus says the Lord, the LORD: You, Tyre, have said, ‘I am perfect in beauty.’”
Your borders are in the heart of the seas; your builders have perfected your beauty.
They built all your planks of fir from Senir; they took cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you.
They made your oars of oaks from Bashan; your deck they fashioned of ivory inlaid with boxwood from the isles of the Kittim.
Fine embroidered linen from Egypt was your sail, to be your banner; blue and purple from the isles of Elishah was your awning.
The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers; your wise men, Tyre, were within you; they were your pilots.
The elders of Gebal and its wise men were in you, repairing your seams; all the ships of the sea and their sailors were in you, to barter for your merchandise.
Men of Persia, Lud, and Put were in your army, your men of war; they hung shield and helmet in you; they gave you splendor.
Men of Arvad and your army were upon your walls all around, and the Gammadim were in your towers; they hung their shields all around your walls; they perfected your beauty.
Tarshish was your merchant because of the abundance of all wealth; they gave silver, iron, tin, and lead for your wares.
Javan, Tubal, and Meshech were your traders; they gave human beings and bronze vessels for your merchandise.
From Beth-togarmah they gave horses, war horses, and mules for your wares.
The sons of Dedan were your traders; many coastlands were the market of your hand; they brought back your payment in ivory tusks and ebony.
Aram was your merchant because of the abundance of your works; they gave turquoise, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies in your wares.
Judah and the land of Israel were your traders; they gave wheat of Minnith, millet, honey, oil, and balm for your merchandise.
Damascus was your merchant because of the abundance of your works, because of the abundance of all wealth, with wine of Helbon and wool of Zahar.
Dan and Javan from Uzal traded in your wares; wrought iron, cassia, and calamus were given in your merchandise.
Dedan traded with you in saddlecloths for riding.
Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were merchants of your hand; in lambs, rams, and goats they traded with you.
The traders of Sheba and Raamah were your traders; they gave for your wares the best of all spices, all precious stones, and gold.
Haran, Canneh, and Eden, the traders of Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad traded with you.
These traded with you in choice garments, in blue garments and embroidered work, and in carpets of colored stuff bound with cords and made secure, in your marketplace.
The ships of Tarshish were the carriers of your merchandise. You were filled and heavily laden in the heart of the seas.
Your rowers have brought you into great waters; the east wind has shattered you in the heart of the seas.

Your wealth, your wares, your merchandise, your mariners, your pilots, your caulkers, your traders, all your men of war, and your whole assembly within you will sink into the heart of the sea on the day of your ruin.
The surrounding countryside will quake at the sound of the cry of your pilots.
All who handle the oar, the mariners, and all the pilots of the sea will come down from their ships; they will stand on the land.
They will raise their voices over you and cry out bitterly; they will cast dust on their heads and roll in ashes.
They will make themselves bald for you and gird on sackcloth; they will weep over you in bitterness of soul, with bitter lamentation.
In their wailing they will take up a lamentation for you and lament over you: “Who is like Tyre, like one destroyed in the midst of the sea?”
When your wares went out from the seas, you satisfied many peoples; with the abundance of your wealth and your merchandise you enriched the kings of the earth.
Now you are shattered by the seas in the depths of the waters; your merchandise and all your company have fallen in your midst.
All the inhabitants of the coastlands are appalled at you; their kings shudder with horror; their faces are convulsed.
The merchants among the peoples hiss at you; you have become a horror, and you shall be no more forever.
The word of the LORD came to me, saying:

“Son of man, say to the prince of Tyre, ‘Thus says the Lord the LORD: Because your heart has been exalted, and you have said that you are a god dwelling in the seat of the gods in the heart of the seas, though you are only a man and not a god, and you have set your heart as though it were the heart of a god— ‘
Behold, you are wiser than Daniel; no secret is hidden from you.
By your wisdom and understanding you have amassed wealth for yourself and gathered gold and silver into your treasuries.
By the greatness of your wisdom in trade you have multiplied your wealth, and your heart has been lifted up because of your wealth. ‘
Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: Because you have set your heart like the heart of a god,
behold, I am bringing foreigners upon you, the most ruthless of nations; they will draw their swords against the beauty born of your wisdom and profane your splendor.
They will bring you down to the pit, and you will die the death of the slain in the heart of the seas.
Will you still say, “I am a god,” before those who kill you? You are a man, not a god, in the hands of those who profane you.
You will die the death of the uncircumcised at the hands of foreigners, for I have spoken, declares the Lord the LORD.’”
The word of the LORD came to me, saying:
“Son of man, raise a lamentation over the king of Tyre and say to him, ‘Thus says the Lord the LORD: You were the very epitome of perfection, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty. ‘

You were in Eden, the garden of God; every precious stone was your covering: ruby, topaz, and diamond, beryl, onyx, and jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and emerald; and your settings and mountings were fashioned in gold. On the day you were created they were prepared. ‘
You were the anointed cherub who covers; I placed you. You were on the holy mountain of God; you walked among the stones of fire.
You were blameless in your ways from the day you were created until iniquity was found in you. ‘

In the abundance of your trade your inner being was filled with violence, and you sinned; therefore I profaned you and expelled you from the mountain of God, and I destroyed you, O covering cherub, from the midst of the stones of fire.
Your heart was lifted up because of your beauty; you corrupted your wisdom for the sake of your splendor. I cast you to the ground and made you a spectacle before kings. ‘

By the multitude of your iniquities and by the unrighteousness of your trade you profaned your sanctuaries; so I brought fire out from your midst, and it consumed you, and I reduced you to ashes on the earth in the sight of all who saw you.
All who knew you among the peoples are appalled at you; you have become a horror, and you will be no more forever.’”
The word of the LORD came to me, saying:
“Son of man, set your face toward Sidon and prophesy against her.

Say, ‘Thus says the Lord the LORD: Behold, I am against you, O Sidon, and I will be glorified in your midst; and they will know that I am the LORD when I execute judgments in her and manifest My holiness in her. ‘
For I will send pestilence into her and blood into her streets; the slain will fall in her midst by the sword against her from all around; and they will know that I am the LORD.
For the house of Israel there will no longer be a pricking brier or a painful thorn from all around those who scorn them; and they will know that I am the Lord the LORD. ‘

Thus says the Lord the LORD: When I gather the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they are scattered, I will manifest My holiness among them in the sight of the nations; and they will dwell in their own land, which I gave to My servant Jacob.

They will dwell in it securely, build houses, and plant vineyards; they will dwell securely when I execute judgments upon all around them who despise them. Then they will know that I am the LORD their God.’”
In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the twelfth day of the month, the word of the the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against all Egypt.
Speak, and say: Thus says the Lord the LORD: Behold, I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great monster reclining among his rivers, who has said, ‘My Nile is mine; I made it for Myself.’ “

I will put hooks in your jaws, and make the fish of your rivers adhere to your scales, and I will draw you up out of the midst of your rivers, together with all the fish of your rivers that cling to your scales.

I will abandon you in the wilderness, you and all the fish of your rivers; you shall fall upon the open field, and not be gathered or buried. I have given you as food to the beasts of the earth and to the birds of the heavens. “
All the inhabitants of Egypt shall know that I am the the LORD, because they proved a fragile reed staff to the house of Israel.
When they grasped you with the hand, you broke and tore all their shoulders; and when they leaned on you, you broke and made all their loins quake. “
Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: Behold, I will bring a sword against you, and cut off from you both man and beast.
The land of Egypt shall become a desolation and a waste, and they shall know that I am the the LORD, because he said, ‘The Nile is mine, and I made it.’
Behold, I am against you and against your rivers, and I will reduce the land of Egypt to utter waste and desolation, from Migdol to Syene, as far as the border of Cush. “
No human foot shall pass through it, nor shall the foot of beast pass through it; it shall remain uninhabited for forty years.

I will make the land of Egypt a desolation among desolated lands, and her cities shall be a desolation for forty years among ruined cities; and I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them throughout the countries. “
For thus says the Lord the LORD: At the end of forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the peoples among whom they were scattered.
I will restore the fortunes of Egypt and bring them back to the land of Pathros, their native land, and there they shall constitute a lowly kingdom.
It shall be the lowliest of kingdoms, never again exalting itself above the nations; I will diminish them so that they never again rule over the nations. “
It shall never again serve as a source of confidence for the house of Israel, but will remind them of their iniquity whenever they turn toward Egypt. Then they will know that I am the Lord the LORD.”
In the twenty-seventh year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the word of the the LORD came to me, saying,

“Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made his army perform arduous labor against Tyre; every head was made bald and every shoulder rubbed bare, yet neither he nor his army received any wages from Tyre for the labor they expended against it. “

Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: Behold, I am giving the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he shall carry off its wealth, seize its spoil, and plunder its goods; and it shall serve as wages for his army.
I have given him the land of Egypt as recompense for the labor he performed, because they worked for Me, declares the Lord the LORD. “
On that day I will cause a horn to spring up for the house of Israel, and I will open your mouth in their midst; and they shall know that I am the the LORD.”
The word of the the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord the the LORD: Wail—alas for the day!
For the day is near, the day of the the LORD is near; it will be a day of clouds, a time of doom for the nations.
A sword will come upon Egypt, and anguish will seize Cush when the slain fall in Egypt, when her wealth is carried away and her foundations are torn down.
Cush and Put and Lud, all Arabia and Kub, together with the people of the land that is in league with Egypt, will fall by the sword alongside them.”
“Thus says the the LORD: Those who uphold Egypt will fall, and her proud might will descend; from Migdol to Syene they will fall within her by the sword, declares the Lord the the LORD.
They will be desolated among desolated lands, and their cities will lie among cities laid waste.
Then they will know that I am the the LORD, when I set fire in Egypt and all her helpers are broken.
On that day messengers will go out from Me in ships to terrify unsuspecting Cush, and anguish will seize them on the day of Egypt’s doom, for behold, it is coming.”
“Thus says the Lord the the LORD: I will put an end to the multitude of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
He and his people with him—the most ruthless of nations—will be brought in to destroy the land; they will draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain.

I will dry up the rivers, and I will sell the land into the hand of evildoers; by the hand of foreigners I will make the land desolate, together with all that fills it. I am the the LORD; I have spoken.”
“Thus says the Lord the the LORD: I will destroy the idols and make the images cease from Memphis; no longer will a prince arise from the land of Egypt, and I will put fear in the land of Egypt.
I will make Pathros a desolation, set fire in Zoan, and execute judgments in Thebes.
I will pour out My wrath upon Sin, the stronghold of Egypt, and cut off the multitude of Thebes.
I will set fire in Egypt; Sin will writhe in anguish; Thebes will be breached; and Memphis will face adversaries day by day.”
“The young men of On and Pi-beseth will fall by the sword, and their women will go into captivity.
At Tehaphnehes the day will be darkened when I break there the yoke-bars of Egypt; her proud might will cease within her; a cloud will cover her, and her daughters will go into captivity.
Thus I will execute judgments on Egypt, and they will know that I am the the LORD.”
In the eleventh year, in the seventh month, on the first day of the month, the word of the the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and behold, it has not been bound up to heal it, nor has a bandage been applied to strengthen it so that it might grasp the sword.

Therefore thus says the Lord the the LORD: Behold, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and I will break his arms—both the strong and the one already broken—and I will make the sword fall from his hand.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the countries.
“I will strengthen the arm of the king of Babylon and put My sword in his hand, and I will break the arms of Pharaoh, so that he will groan before him with the groanings of a mortally wounded man.

I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, but the arms of Pharaoh will fall; and they will know that I am the the LORD when I put My sword into the hand of the king of Babylon and he stretches it out against the land of Egypt.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the countries, and they will know that I am the the LORD.”
In the eleventh year, on the first day of the third month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying:
“Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his multitude: To whom are you like in your greatness?
Behold, Assyria was a cedar in Lebanon, beautiful of branch, shading and forested, and lofty in stature; its top was among the thick boughs. “
The waters made him grow; the deep exalted him; its rivers ran round about his planting, and it sent its channels to all the trees of the field.
Therefore his height was raised above all the trees of the field; his boughs multiplied, and his branches grew long as they spread, because of abundant water.
All the birds of heaven nested in its boughs; all the beasts of the field brought forth beneath its branches; and in its shade all the great nations dwelt. “
Thus it was beautiful in its greatness, in the length of its branches, for its root reached to abundant waters.
The cedars in the garden of God could not overshadow it; the cypresses were not like its boughs, and the plane trees were not like its branches; no tree in the garden of God resembled it in beauty.
I made it beautiful in the abundance of its branches, so that all the trees of Eden in the garden of God envied it.”
“Therefore thus says the Lord the LORD: Because you were exalted in stature, and it set its top among the thick boughs, and its heart was lifted up in its height,
I will deliver it into the hand of the ruler of the nations, who shall deal with it according to its wickedness; I have banished it. “

Foreigners, the most ruthless of the nations, cut it down and abandoned it; its branches fell upon the mountains and in all the valleys; its boughs were broken in all the ravines of the land; and all the peoples of the earth departed from its shadow and left it.
Upon its ruin all the birds of heaven dwell, and all the beasts of the field are among its branches. “

So that none of the trees by the waters may exalt themselves in their height, nor set their tops among the thick boughs, nor any that drink water stand in their height; for all are consigned to death, to the lower parts of the earth, among the sons of men, to those who descend into the pit.”

“Thus says the Lord the LORD: On the day of its descent to Sheol, I caused mourning; I covered the deep over it; I restrained its rivers, and the abundant waters were held back; I darkened Lebanon over it, and all the trees of the field fainted for it. “

I made the nations tremble at the sound of its fall, when I cast it down to Sheol with those who descend to the pit; and all the trees of Eden, the choicest and best of Lebanon, all that drink water, were comforted in the lower earth.
They too descended with it to Sheol, to those slain by the sword, and those who were its arm dwelt in its shadow among the nations.

“To whom are you like in glory and greatness among the trees of Eden? You shall be brought down with the trees of Eden to the lower parts of the earth; you shall lie among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his multitude,” declares the Lord the LORD.
In the twelfth year, on the first day of the twelfth month, the word of the LORD came to me:

“Son of man, raise a lamentation over Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and say to him: You are likened to a lion among the nations, yet you are like a monster in the seas; you thrashed in your rivers, churning the waters with your feet and fouling their streams.”
Thus says the Lord the LORD: “I will spread My net over you with a great assembly of peoples, and they shall haul you up in My dragnet.”
“I will leave you on the ground and cast you upon the open field; I will cause all the birds of heaven to settle upon you, and all the beasts of the earth to gorge themselves on you.”
“I will lay your flesh upon the mountains and fill the valleys with your remains.”
“I will drench the land with your flowing blood, as far as the mountains, and the ravines shall be filled from you.”
“When I extinguish you, I will cover the heavens and darken their stars; I will veil the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give its light.”
“All the bright luminaries of heaven I will darken over you, and I will set darkness upon your land, declares the Lord the LORD.”
“I will agitate the hearts of many peoples when I bring your ruin among the nations, into lands you have not known.”

“Many peoples shall be appalled at you; their kings shall shudder in horror at you when I brandish My sword before them, and on the day of your fall each man shall tremble for his life, moment by moment.”
“For thus says the Lord the LORD: The sword of the king of Babylon shall come upon you.”
“By the swords of the mighty, all of them the most ruthless of nations, I will bring down your hordes; they shall ravage the pride of Egypt, and all her multitudes shall be destroyed.”
“I will destroy all her livestock beside the abundant waters; no human foot shall muddy them again, nor shall the hoof of any beast muddy them.”
“Then I will let her waters settle and make her rivers flow like oil, declares the Lord the LORD.”
“When I make the land of Egypt a desolation, empty of all that filled it, when I strike down all who dwell in it, then they shall know that I am the LORD.”
“This is the lamentation they shall chant over her; the daughters of the nations shall chant it; over Egypt and all her multitudes they shall chant it, declares the Lord the LORD.”
In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
“Son of man, wail over the multitude of Egypt, and bring her down—her and the daughters of mighty nations—to the underworld, to those who descend to the Pit.”
“Whom do you surpass in beauty? Go down and be laid to rest with the uncircumcised.”
“They shall fall among those slain by the sword; the sword is drawn; let them drag her off with all her multitudes.”
“The mighty chiefs shall speak to him from the midst of Sheol with his allies: ‘They have gone down; they lie with the uncircumcised, slain by the sword.’”
“Assyria is there with all her company; her graves are all around her; all of them are slain, fallen by the sword.”
“Her graves are set in the recesses of the Pit; her company is all around her grave; all of them are slain, fallen by the sword—those who spread terror in the land of the living.”

“Elam is there with all her multitudes around her grave; all of them are slain, fallen by the sword—those who went down uncircumcised to the earth below, who spread their terror in the land of the living; they bear their shame with those who descend to the Pit.”

“Among the slain they prepare a resting place for her with all her multitudes; her graves are all around her; all of them are uncircumcised, slain by the sword, though their terror was once spread in the land of the living; they bear their shame with those who descend to the Pit; she is put among the slain.”

“Meshech and Tubal are there with all their multitudes, with their graves all around them; all of them are uncircumcised, slain by the sword, because they spread their terror in the land of the living.”

“They do not lie with the fallen warriors of old, who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, their swords placed beneath their heads and their shields resting upon their bones, although the terror of the mighty was once in the land of the living.”
“But you too shall be shattered and lie down among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword.”
“Edom is there, and all her kings and princes, who despite their might are laid among those slain by the sword; they lie with the uncircumcised, with those who descend to the Pit.”

“All the leaders of the north and all the Sidonians are there; they went down in disgrace with the slain, despite the terror of their might; they lie uncircumcised with those slain by the sword, and bear their shame with those who descend to the Pit.”
“Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all his multitudes—Pharaoh and all his army, slain by the sword, declares the Lord the LORD.”
“For I have put his terror in the land of the living, yet he shall be laid to rest among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword—Pharaoh and all his multitudes, declares the Lord the LORD.”
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, speak to the children of your people, and say to them, ‘When I bring the sword upon a land, and the people of the land take one man from among them and appoint him as their watchman,
and he sees the sword coming upon the land and blows the trumpet and warns the people,
then whoever hears the sound of the trumpet and does not take warning, and the sword comes and takes him away, his blood shall be upon his own head.
He heard the sound of the trumpet but did not take warning; his blood shall be upon himself, yet he who took warning would have saved his own life.

But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the trumpet, so that the people are not warned, and the sword comes and takes any one of them, that person is taken away in his iniquity, but his blood I will require at the watchman’s hand.’”
“As for you, son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel; so you shall hear a word from My mouth and warn them on My behalf.

When I say to the wicked, ‘Wicked one, you shall surely die,’ and you do not speak to warn the wicked from his way, that wicked person shall die in his iniquity, but his blood I will require at your hand.
But if you warn the wicked to turn from his way, and he does not turn from his way, he shall die in his iniquity, but you have delivered your own life.”
“And you, son of man, say to the house of Israel: ‘Thus you have said, “Our transgressions and our sins are upon us, and we are wasting away in them; how then can we live?”’

Say to them: ‘As I live, declares the Lord GOD, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that the wicked turn from his way and live. Turn back, turn back from your evil ways! For why should you die, O house of Israel?’”

“And you, son of man, say to the children of your people: ‘The righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him in the day of his transgression, nor shall the wickedness of the wicked make him stumble on the day that he turns from his wickedness; nor shall the righteous be able to live by his righteousness on the day that he sins.’

When I say to the righteous that he shall surely live, and he trusts in his righteousness and commits iniquity, none of his righteous deeds shall be remembered; but in the iniquity that he has committed he shall die.”
“Again, when I say to the wicked, ‘You shall surely die,’ and he turns from his sin and does justice and righteousness,
if the wicked restores the pledge, gives back what he has taken by robbery, walks in the statutes of life, committing no iniquity, he shall surely live; he shall not die.
None of the sins that he has committed shall be remembered against him; he has done justice and righteousness; he shall surely live.”
“Yet the children of your people say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just,’ when it is their own way that is not just.”
“When the righteous turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, he shall die in it.
And when the wicked turns from his wickedness and does justice and righteousness, he shall live by them.”
