“Yet you say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ I will judge each of you according to his ways, O house of Israel.”
In the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth month, on the fifth day of the month, a fugitive from Jerusalem came to me, saying, ‘The city has been struck down.’
Now the hand of the LORD had been upon me in the evening before the fugitive came, and He had opened my mouth before he reached me in the morning; thus my mouth was opened, and I was no longer mute.
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

“Son of man, the inhabitants of these waste places in the land of Israel are saying, ‘Abraham was only one man, yet he possessed the land; but we are many; the land has been given to us as a possession.’”
“Therefore say to them: ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: You eat flesh with the blood, and lift up your eyes to your idols, and shed blood; shall you then possess the land?
You have relied on your sword, you have committed abominations, and each of you has defiled his neighbor’s wife; shall you then possess the land?’”

“Say thus to them: ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: As I live, surely those who are in the waste places shall fall by the sword, and whoever is in the open field I have given to the beasts to be devoured, and those who are in the strongholds and in the caves shall die by pestilence.’
And I will make the land a desolation and a waste, and the pride of her power shall cease; and the mountains of Israel shall be desolate, so that no one passes through.
And they shall know that I am the LORD, when I make the land a desolation and a waste because of all their abominations which they have committed.”

“As for you, son of man, the children of your people are talking about you beside the walls and in the doorways of the houses; and they say to one another, each to his brother, ‘Come, please, and hear what word comes from the LORD.’
And they come to you as people come, and they sit before you as My people, and they hear your words, but they do not do them; for with their mouths they profess love, yet their hearts pursue gain.”
“And behold, you are to them like a very lovely song of one who has a pleasant voice and plays well on an instrument; for they hear your words, but they do not do them.
And when this comes to pass—behold, it is coming—then they will know that a prophet has been among them.”
The word of the LORD came to me, saying:

"Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel; prophesy, and say to them—to the shepherds themselves—Thus says the Lord, the LORD: Woe to the shepherds of Israel who have been feeding themselves! Should not shepherds feed the sheep?
"You consume the fat, you clothe yourselves with wool, you slaughter the well-fed, yet you do not pasture the sheep.

"The weak you have not strengthened; the sick you have not healed; the injured you have not bound up; the strayed you have not restored; the lost you have not sought; and with force and harshness you have dominated them.
"So they were scattered for want of a shepherd, and they became prey for every beast of the field.
"My sheep wandered through all the mountains and upon every high hill; My sheep were dispersed over the whole face of the earth, with no one to seek or search for them."
"Therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD:

"As I live—this is the declaration of the Lord, the LORD—because My sheep became prey, and My sheep became food for every beast of the field, for want of a shepherd, and because My shepherds did not seek My sheep, but the shepherds fed themselves and did not feed My sheep,
"therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD:

"Thus says the Lord, the LORD: Behold, I am against the shepherds, and I will require My sheep from their hand and put an end to their shepherding; the shepherds shall no longer feed themselves. I will rescue My sheep from their mouths, so that they may no longer be devoured by them."
"For thus says the Lord, the LORD: Behold, I Myself will search for My sheep and seek them out.

As a shepherd seeks out his flock on the day he is among his scattered sheep, so I will seek out My sheep and deliver them from all the places to which they were scattered on a day of cloud and thick darkness.

"I will bring them out from the peoples and gather them from the countries, and I will bring them into their own land; I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, by the ravines, and in all the inhabited places of the land.

I will feed them with good pasture, and their grazing ground shall be on the mountain heights of Israel; there they shall lie down in good grazing land, and on rich pasture they shall feed upon the mountains of Israel.
"I Myself will be the shepherd of My sheep, and I Myself will make them lie down, declares the Lord, the LORD.
I will seek the lost, bring back the strayed, bind up the injured, strengthen the weak; but the fat and the strong I will destroy. I will feed them with justice."
"As for you, My flock, thus says the Lord, the LORD: Behold, I will judge between sheep and sheep, between rams and male goats.
Is it not enough for you to feed on the good pasture, that you must trample the rest of your pasture with your feet, and to drink clear water, that you must muddy the remainder with your feet?
Must My sheep then feed on what your feet have trampled, and drink what your feet have muddied?
"Therefore, thus says the Lord, the LORD to them: Behold, I Myself will judge between the fat sheep and the lean sheep.
Because you push with side and shoulder, and gore all the weak with your horns until you have scattered them abroad,
I will rescue My sheep, and they shall no longer be prey; and I will judge between sheep and sheep."
"I will raise up over them one shepherd, My servant David, and he shall feed them; he shall feed them and be their shepherd.
I, the LORD, will be their God, and My servant David shall be prince among them. I am the LORD; I have spoken.
"I will make with them a covenant of peace and rid the land of wild beasts, so that they may dwell securely in the wilderness and sleep in the woods.
I will make them and the places around My hill a blessing, and I will send down the showers in their season; they shall be showers of blessing.

"The trees of the field shall yield their fruit, and the earth shall yield its increase, and they shall be secure in their land; and they shall know that I am the LORD, when I break the bars of their yoke and deliver them from the hand of those who enslaved them.
They shall no longer be prey to the nations, nor shall the beasts of the field devour them; they shall dwell securely, with no one to make them afraid.
I will establish for them a renowned plantation, so that they shall no longer be swept away by famine in the land, nor bear again the reproach of the nations.
"They shall know that I am the LORD their God with them, and that they—the house of Israel—are My people, declares the Lord, the LORD.
You are My sheep, the flock I pasture; you are humankind, and I am your God, declares the Lord, the LORD."
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, direct your hostility against Mount Seir, and prophesy against it.
And say to it: Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am set against you, Mount Seir, and I will reach out against you in judgment and reduce you to utter desolation and ruin.
I will reduce your cities to rubble, and you yourself shall become a desolation, and you shall know that I am the LORD.
“Because you have nursed an age-old enmity and have surrendered the people of Israel to the sword in the hour of their calamity, at the time of their final reckoning,
therefore, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will consign you to bloodshed, and bloodshed shall hound you; because you did not abhor bloodshed, bloodshed shall hound you.
I will make Mount Seir a desolation and a waste, and I will extirpate from it all who pass through and all who return.
I will glut its mountains with its slain; upon your hills, in your valleys, and in all your ravines, those felled by the sword shall lie.
I will make you an everlasting desolation, and your cities shall remain uninhabited; then you shall know that I am the LORD.
“Because you said, ‘These two nations and these two lands shall be mine, and we will possess them’—although the LORD was there—
therefore, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will requite you according to the wrath and jealousy you manifested in your hatred of them, and I will disclose Myself among them when I judge you.
Then you shall know that I, the LORD, have heard all the blasphemies that you have uttered against the mountains of Israel, saying, ‘They are laid waste; they are delivered to us to be devoured.’
You have magnified yourselves against Me with your mouths and have multiplied your words against Me; I have heard it.
“Thus says the Lord GOD: When the whole earth rejoices, I will make you desolate.

As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel because it lay desolate, so I will requite you; you shall be a desolation, Mount Seir, and all Edom, all of it. Then they shall know that I am the LORD.”
And you, son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel and say: “Hear the word of the LORD, O mountains of Israel.
Thus says the Lord GOD: Because the enemy has said of you, ‘Aha! The ancient heights have become our possession’—

therefore prophesy, and say: Thus says the Lord GOD: Because, even because they have laid you waste and snapped at you from every side, so that you might become a possession for the remnant of the nations, and you have been taken up on the lips of talkers and made an object of the people’s slander—

“therefore, O mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD: Thus says the Lord GOD to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys, to the desolate wastes and the forsaken cities, which have become a prey and a derision to the remnant of the nations round about—

therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Surely in the fire of My jealousy have I spoken against the remnant of the nations and against all Edom, who gave My land to themselves as a possession with wholehearted joy and with utter contempt of soul, that its pastureland might be plundered.

Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel, and say to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys: Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I have spoken in My wrath and in My jealousy, because you have borne the shame of the nations.
Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: I have sworn an oath; surely the nations that are around you shall themselves bear their shame.
“But you, O mountains of Israel, shall put forth your branches and bear your fruit for My people Israel, for they are near at hand to come home.
For behold, I am for you, and I will turn toward you, and you shall be tilled and sown.
I will multiply people upon you, all the house of Israel, even all of it; the cities shall be inhabited, and the waste places shall be rebuilt.

I will multiply upon you man and beast, and they shall increase and be fruitful; and I will cause you to be inhabited as in your former times, and I will do more good to you than at your beginnings; and you shall know that I am the LORD.
Yes, I will cause men to walk upon you, even My people Israel; and they shall possess you, and you shall be their inheritance, and you shall no more make them childless.
“Thus says the Lord GOD: Because they say to you, ‘You are a devourer of men and have bereaved your nation,’
therefore you shall devour men no more, neither shall you bereave your nation any more, says the Lord GOD.
Neither will I let you hear the taunts of the nations any more, nor shall you bear the reproach of the peoples any more, nor shall you cause your nation to stumble any more, says the Lord GOD.”
Moreover, the word of the LORD came to me, saying:
“Son of man, when the house of Israel dwelt in their own land, they defiled it by their way and by their deeds; their way before Me was like the uncleanness of a woman in her menstrual impurity.
So I poured out My wrath upon them for the blood which they had shed upon the land, and because they had defiled it with their idols.
And I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed through the countries; according to their way and according to their deeds I judged them.
And when they came to the nations, wherever they came, they profaned My holy name, in that men said of them, ‘These are the people of the LORD, and yet they have gone out of His land.’
But I had regard for My holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the nations to which they came.

“Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord GOD: I do not do this for your sake, O house of Israel, but for My holy name’s sake, which you have profaned among the nations to which you came.

I will sanctify My great name, which has been profaned among the nations, which you have profaned in their midst; and the nations shall know that I am the LORD, says the Lord GOD, when I am sanctified in you before their eyes.
“For I will take you from the nations, and gather you from all countries, and will bring you into your own land.
Then I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean; from all your filthiness and from all your idols will I cleanse you.
A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you; and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh.
And I will put My Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in My statutes, and you shall keep My judgments and do them.
And you shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers; and you shall be My people, and I will be your God.
I will also save you from all your uncleannesses; and I will call for the grain, and will increase it, and lay no famine upon you.
I will multiply the fruit of the tree and the increase of the field, so that you shall receive no more the reproach of famine among the nations.
Then you shall remember your evil ways and your doings that were not good, and you shall loathe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations.
Not for your sake do I do this, says the Lord GOD; be ashamed and confounded for your ways, O house of Israel.”
“Thus says the Lord GOD: In the day that I cleanse you from all your iniquities, I will cause the cities to be inhabited, and the waste places shall be rebuilt.
And the desolate land shall be tilled, whereas it lay desolate in the sight of all that passed by.
And they shall say, ‘This land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden; and the wasted and desolate and ruined cities are inhabited and fortified.’
Then the nations that are left round about you shall know that I, the LORD, have rebuilt the ruined places and planted that which was desolate; I, the LORD, have spoken it, and I will do it.
Thus says the Lord GOD: I will yet be inquired of by the house of Israel to do this for them: I will increase them with men like a flock.
As the holy flock, as the flock of Jerusalem in her appointed feasts, so shall the waste cities be filled with flocks of men; and they shall know that I am the LORD.”
The hand of the LORD was upon me, and the LORD brought me out by the Spirit and set me down in the midst of the valley, which was full of bones.
He led me all around among them, and, behold, there were very many on the surface of the valley, and, behold, they were exceedingly dry.
He said to me, "Son of man, can these bones live?" And I answered, "O Lord GOD, You know."
Then He said to me, "Prophesy over these bones and say to them, 'O dry bones, hear the word of the LORD.'
Thus says the Lord GOD to these bones: "Behold, I will cause breath to enter you, and you shall live.
I will put sinews upon you and bring flesh upon you and cover you with skin and put breath in you, and you shall live, and you shall know that I am the LORD."
So I prophesied as I was commanded; and as I prophesied, there was a sound, and, behold, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to its bone.
And I looked, and, behold, sinews were on them, and flesh had come up, and skin had covered them above; but there was no breath in them.
Then He said to me, "Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, Son of man, and say to the breath, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live.'
So I prophesied as He commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived and stood on their feet, an exceedingly great army.
Then He said to me, "Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. Behold, they say, 'Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost; we are cut off.'
Therefore prophesy and say to them, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I will open your graves and raise you from your graves, O My people, and I will bring you into the land of Israel.
And you shall know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves and raise you from your graves, O My people.
I will put My Spirit in you, and you shall live, and I will place you on your own land. Then you shall know that I am the LORD; I have spoken, and I will do it, declares the LORD.'
The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

"And you, Son of man, take for yourself one stick and write on it, 'For Judah and for the children of Israel, his companions'; then take another stick and write on it, 'For Joseph—the stick of Ephraim—and for all the house of Israel, his companions.'
And join them to one another into one stick, that they may become one in your hand."
And when the children of your people say to you, 'Will you not tell us what these things mean to you?'

say to them, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am taking the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel, his companions, and I will put them on the stick of Judah and make them one stick, and they shall be one in My hand.'
The sticks on which you write shall be in your hand before their eyes.

And say to them, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the nations to which they have gone, and I will gather them from all around and bring them into their own land.

I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and one king shall be king over all of them; they shall no longer be two nations, and they shall no longer be divided into two kingdoms.

They shall no longer defile themselves with their idols, their detestable things, and all their transgressions; and I will save them from all their dwelling places in which they have sinned, and I will cleanse them; and they shall be My people, and I will be their God.
And My servant David shall be king over them, and there shall be one shepherd over all of them; they shall walk in My judgments and keep My statutes and observe them.

They shall dwell in the land that I gave to My servant Jacob, in which your fathers dwelt; and they shall dwell in it, they, their children, and their children's children, forever; and My servant David shall be their prince forever.
I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them; and I will establish them and multiply them, and I will set My sanctuary in their midst forever.
My dwelling place shall be with them; I will be their God, and they shall be My people.
Then the nations shall know that I am the LORD who sanctifies Israel, when My sanctuary is in their midst forever.'
The word of the LORD came to me, saying:
"Son of man, set your face toward Gog, in the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him.
Say, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: "Behold, I am against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.

I will turn you about, fasten hooks in your jaws, and drag you forth with all your host—horses and riders, every one accoutred in panoply, a vast assemblage bearing buckler and shield, all of them wielding swords.
Persia, Cush, and Put are in their ranks, all equipped with shield and helmet.
Gomer and all its hordes, Beth-togarmah from the uttermost north and all its hordes—many peoples are allied with you.
Be at the ready; indeed, make yourself ready—you and all your company mustered about you—and assume command over them.'"

"After many days you will be summoned. In the latter years you will invade the land recovered from the sword, gathered from many peoples, upon the mountains of Israel, which had long been a desolation; yet its people were brought forth from the nations, and now they dwell in security, every one of them.
You will advance, coming like a tempest; you will be like a cloud enveloping the land—you and all your troops, and many peoples with you."
"Thus says the Lord GOD: On that day thoughts will arise in your heart, and you will devise a nefarious scheme.

You will say, "'I will march against a land of unfortified villages; I will come upon those who are tranquil, who dwell in security, all of them living without walls and having neither bars nor gates'—

"to seize spoil and carry off plunder, to turn your hand against the desolate places now inhabited, and against a people gathered from the nations, who have amassed livestock and goods and dwell in the heart of the earth.

Sheba, Dedan, and the merchants of Tarshish with all its villages will say to you, "'Have you come to seize spoil? Have you mustered your company to take plunder, to carry away silver and gold, to take away livestock and goods, to take great spoil?'"
"Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: On that day when My people Israel are dwelling in security, will you not take notice?
You will come from your place, from the farthest north, you and many peoples with you, all of them riding on horses—a vast company and a mighty army.

You will advance against My people Israel like a cloud covering the land. In the latter days, O Gog, I will bring you against My land, so that the nations may know Me when I am sanctified in you before their eyes.'"
"Thus says the Lord GOD: Are you the one of whom I spoke in former days through My servants, the prophets of Israel, who prophesied in those days for years that I would bring you against them?
On that day, when Gog comes against the land of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, My wrath will flare up in My anger.
For in My zeal and in the fire of My wrath I have spoken: Surely on that day there will be a great earthquake in the land of Israel.

The fish of the sea, the birds of the heavens, the beasts of the field, all creeping things that creep upon the earth, and all mankind upon the face of the earth will tremble at My presence. The mountains will be overturned, the cliffs will collapse, and every wall will fall to the ground.
I will summon a sword against him throughout all My mountains, declares the Lord GOD. Every man's sword will be against his brother.

I will enter into judgment with him by pestilence and bloodshed, and I will rain down upon him, upon his troops, and upon the many peoples who are with him torrential rain, hailstones, fire, and brimstone.
Thus I will magnify Myself and sanctify Myself, and I will make Myself known in the sight of many nations; and they will know that I am the LORD."
You, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say: Thus says the Lord GOD: Behold, I am against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
I will turn you about, urge you onward, bring you up from the remote recesses of the north, and bring you against the mountains of Israel.
I will strike your bow from your left hand and make your arrows fall from your right hand.
You shall fall on the mountains of Israel—you, all your hordes, and the peoples who are with you—and I will give you as food to every kind of bird of prey and to the beasts of the field.
You shall fall on the open field, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.
I will send fire upon Magog and upon those who dwell securely in the coastlands, and they shall know that I am the LORD.

I will make known My holy name in the midst of My people Israel, and I will no longer allow My holy name to be profaned among the nations; the nations shall know that I am the LORD, the Holy One in Israel.
Behold, it is coming and it shall come to pass, declares the Lord GOD. This is the day of which I have spoken.

Then the inhabitants of the cities of Israel will go out and set fire to and burn the weapons—shields and bucklers, bows and arrows, clubs and spears—and they will make fires with them for seven years.

They will not gather wood from the field or cut timber from the forests, for they will make fires with the weapons; they will plunder those who plundered them and despoil those who despoiled them, declares the Lord GOD.

On that day I will give Gog a burial place in Israel—the Valley of the Travelers east of the sea—and it will block the travelers; for there they will bury Gog and all his multitude, and they will call it the Valley of Hamon-gog.
For seven months the house of Israel will bury them, in order to cleanse the land.
All the people of the land will bury them, and it will redound to their renown on the day when I glorify Myself, declares the Lord GOD.
Men will be continually set apart to pass through the land to cleanse it, burying those who remain on the face of the land; at the end of seven months they will conduct a search.
Whenever travelers pass through the land and someone sees a bone, he shall set up a marker beside it, until the buriers have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog.
A city shall also be called Hamonah; thus they shall cleanse the land.

As for you, son of man, thus says the Lord GOD: Say to every bird and to every beast of the field, ‘Gather together and come; assemble from all around to My sacrifice that I am sacrificing for you, a great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel, and you shall eat flesh and drink blood.
You shall eat the flesh of the mighty and drink the blood of the princes of the earth—rams, lambs, goats, and bulls—all of them fatlings of Bashan.
You shall eat fat to satiety and drink blood to intoxication, from My sacrifice which I have sacrificed for you.
At My table you shall be filled with horses and charioteers, with mighty men and all the men of war,’ declares the Lord GOD.
I will set My glory among the nations, and all the nations shall see My judgment that I have executed and My hand that I have laid upon them.
From that day onward the house of Israel shall know that I am the LORD their God.

The nations shall know that the house of Israel went into exile because of their iniquity, because they acted treacherously against Me; so I hid My face from them and delivered them into the hand of their adversaries, and they all fell by the sword.
According to their uncleanness and according to their transgressions I dealt with them, and I hid My face from them.
Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Now I will restore the fortunes of Jacob and have compassion on the whole house of Israel, and I will be jealous for My holy name.
They shall bear their disgrace and all their treachery which they committed against Me, when they dwell securely in their own land with no one to make them afraid.
When I bring them back from the peoples and gather them out of the lands of their enemies, I will be sanctified through them in the sight of many nations.
Then they shall know that I am the LORD their God, for I sent them into exile among the nations and then gathered them to their own land; I will not leave any of them there any longer.
I will no longer hide My face from them, because I have poured out My Spirit upon the house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.

In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city had been struck down—on that very day—the hand of the LORD was upon me, and He brought me there.
In visions of God He brought me to the land of Israel and set me down upon a very high mountain, on whose southern side was something like the structure of a city.
He brought me there, and behold, a man whose appearance was like bronze, standing in the gate, with a linen cord and a measuring rod in his hand.

The man said to me, “Son of man, see with your eyes, hear with your ears, and set your heart upon all that I show you, for you have been brought here so that I may show it to you; declare to the house of Israel all that you see.”

And behold, a wall all around outside the temple; the measuring rod in the man’s hand was six cubits long, each cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth. He measured the thickness of the building, one rod, and its height, one rod.
Then he came to the gate facing east; he ascended its steps and measured the threshold of the gate, one rod wide, and the other threshold, one rod wide.
Each guardroom was one rod long and one rod wide, and between the guardrooms was five cubits; the threshold of the gate beside the portico of the gate toward the house was one rod.
He also measured the portico of the gate toward the house, one rod.
Then he measured the portico of the gate, eight cubits, and its jambs, two cubits; and the portico of the gate was toward the house.
The gate facing east had three guardrooms on either side; the three had one measurement, and the jambs on either side had one measurement.
He measured the width of the gate’s entrance, ten cubits, and the length of the gate, thirteen cubits.
There was a ledge of one cubit before the guardrooms, and a ledge of one cubit on the other side; and each guardroom was six cubits on either side.
He measured the gate from the roof of one guardroom to the roof of the other, a width of twenty-five cubits, door opposite door.
He made the jambs sixty cubits high, and the courtyard extended to the jamb on every side of the gate.
From the front of the entrance gate to the front of the inner portico of the gate was fifty cubits.
There were latticed windows to the guardrooms and to their jambs within the gate all around, and likewise to the porticos; windows all around on the inside, and palm trees on each jamb.
Then he brought me into the outer courtyard, and behold, chambers and a pavement made all around the courtyard; thirty chambers were upon the pavement.
The pavement ran along the side of the gates, corresponding to the length of the gates—the lower pavement.
He measured the width from the front of the lower gate to the front of the inner courtyard outside, one hundred cubits, eastward and northward.
As for the gate of the outer courtyard facing north, he measured its length and its width.
Its guardrooms—three on this side and three on that—its jambs, and its portico were according to the first measurement: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its windows, its portico, and its palm trees were according to the measurement of the gate facing east; and seven steps went up to it, with its portico before them.
There was a gate to the inner courtyard opposite the north gate and the east gate; he measured from gate to gate, one hundred cubits.
Then he led me southward, and behold, a gate toward the south; he measured its jambs and its portico according to these measurements.
There were windows in it and in its portico all around, like those windows; fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
There were seven steps going up to it, and its portico was before them; it had palm trees on its jambs, one on this side and one on that.
There was a gate to the inner courtyard toward the south; he measured from gate to gate toward the south, one hundred cubits.
Then he brought me to the inner courtyard through the south gate; he measured the south gate according to these measurements.
Its guardrooms, its jambs, and its portico were according to these measurements; and its portico had windows all around; fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
There were porticos all around, twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide.
Its portico faced the outer courtyard; palm trees were on its jambs; and eight steps led up to it.
He brought me to the inner courtyard toward the east; he measured the gate according to these measurements.
Its guardrooms, its jambs, and its portico were according to these measurements; and its portico had windows all around; fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its portico faced the outer courtyard; palm trees were on its jambs on this side and on that; and eight steps led up to it.
He brought me to the north gate; he measured it according to these measurements.
Its guardrooms, its jambs, and its portico; and it had windows all around; fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its jambs faced the outer courtyard; palm trees were on its jambs on this side and on that; and eight steps led up to it.
There was a chamber with its entrance by the jambs of the gates; there they rinsed the burnt offering.
In the portico of the gate were two tables on this side and two tables on that, on which to slaughter the burnt offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering.
Outside, at the side of the entrance to the north gate, were two tables; and on the other side of the portico of the gate were two tables.
Four tables on this side and four tables on that side of the gate—eight tables—on which they slaughtered.

There were four tables of hewn stone for the burnt offering, a cubit and a half long, a cubit and a half wide, and one cubit high; upon them they laid the instruments with which they slaughtered the burnt offering and the sacrifice.
Hooks, a handbreadth long, were fastened all around within; and upon the tables was the flesh of the offering.

Outside the inner gate were chambers for the singers in the inner courtyard, which was at the side of the north gate, and their faces were toward the south; one was at the side of the east gate, facing north.
He said to me, “This chamber whose face is toward the south is for the priests who keep charge of the temple.
And the chamber whose face is toward the north is for the priests who keep charge of the altar; these are the sons of Zadok, who, among the sons of Levi, draw near to the LORD to minister to Him.”
He measured the courtyard, a square, one hundred cubits long and one hundred cubits wide; and the altar was before the house.

He brought me to the portico of the house and measured the jambs of the portico, five cubits on this side and five cubits on that; and the width of the gate was three cubits on this side and three cubits on that.
The length of the portico was twenty cubits, and the width eleven cubits; and by the steps by which they went up to it, there were pillars by the jambs, one on this side and one on that.
Then he brought me to the outer sanctuary and measured the side pillars; they were six cubits in breadth on one side and six cubits on the other—the breadth of the tabernacle.
The entrance was ten cubits wide, and its shoulder walls were five cubits on either side. He measured the outer sanctuary: forty cubits in length and twenty cubits in breadth.
Then he entered the inner sanctuary and measured the jambs of the entrance: two cubits; the entrance itself: six cubits; and the breadth of the entrance: seven cubits.
He measured the inner sanctuary: twenty cubits in length and twenty cubits in breadth, corresponding to the outer sanctuary. And he said to me, “This is the Most Holy Place.”
Then he measured the wall of the temple: six cubits; and the breadth of each side chamber: four cubits, all around the temple.

The side chambers were arranged in three stories, thirty chambers to each story, stacked one above another. Ledges ran all around the wall of the temple to support the side chambers, so that the supports were not inserted into the wall of the temple itself.

The side chambers surrounding the temple grew wider at each successive level, because the surrounding structure was built in tiers; consequently, the width of the temple increased as one ascended, the upper chambers being formed from space taken from the lower and middle levels.
I observed that the temple had a raised base all around it; these were the foundations of the side chambers, a full rod—six cubits—in height.
The outer wall of the side chambers was five cubits thick, and the open area between the side chambers of the temple
and the outer chambers was twenty cubits wide all around the temple.
The side chambers opened onto this open area, one door facing north and another facing south, and the open area was five cubits wide all around.
The building facing the temple yard on the west was seventy cubits wide; its wall was five cubits thick all around, and its length was ninety cubits.
He measured the temple: one hundred cubits in length; and the separate place, the building, and its walls: one hundred cubits in length.
The separate place on the east, facing the temple, was one hundred cubits wide.

He measured the building facing the separate place at the rear, together with its galleries on either side: one hundred cubits. The outer sanctuary, the inner sanctuary, and the porticoes of the court

were paneled with wood all around, and the thresholds, the narrow windows, and the galleries around all three were likewise paneled with wood—everything from the threshold up to the windows, which were covered.
From the space above the door up to the inner sanctuary, and all around the outer and inner walls, everything was measured.
They were carved with cherubim and palm trees: a palm tree stood between two cherubim, and each cherub had two faces.
One face was human, turned toward the palm tree on one side, and the other was a lion’s face, turned toward the palm tree on the other side. These carvings ran all around the temple.
From the floor to the space above the door, cherubim and palm trees were carved on the walls of the sanctuary.
The outer sanctuary had a square doorframe, and the front of the sanctuary looked like
an altar of wood—three cubits high and two cubits long—with corners; its length and its walls were of wood. And he said to me, “This is the table that is before the LORD.”
The outer sanctuary and the inner sanctuary each had a double door,
and each door had two panels—two folding doors for one door and two for the other.
Cherubim and palm trees were carved on the doors of the sanctuary, as on the walls, and a canopy of wood stood over the front of the portico outside.
Narrow windows and palm trees appeared on either side of the portico’s shoulders, along with the side chambers of the temple and the canopies.

Then the guide conducted me outward through the northern gate into the outer court, bringing me to the suite of chambers situated opposite the segregated precinct and opposite the edifice on the north.
Along the northern façade of the outer structure extended a chamber one hundred cubits in length and fifty cubits in breadth.
The uppermost chambers were recessed in relation to those on the lower and middle levels, and they were withdrawn from the wall of the inner court.
Before these chambers lay a passage ten cubits wide and one hundred cubits long, with their entrances oriented toward the north.
The upper chambers were more contracted, because the galleries appropriated greater space from them than from the lower and middle floors.
For they were disposed in three stories and lacked columns such as those in the courts; consequently, the upper chambers were set back from the ground more than the lower and middle ones.
Before the chambers stood an outer wall fifty cubits long, running parallel to the chambers and the outer court.
Indeed, the chambers opening onto the outer court were fifty cubits long, whereas those facing the temple were one hundred cubits long.
Below these chambers was an entrance on the east side, as one enters them from the outer court.
On the south side, along the wall of the outer court, there were chambers facing the separate area and the building, with a passageway before them analogous to that of the northern chambers.
They possessed the same length and breadth, with comparable exits, entrances, and arrangements.
Corresponding to the doors of the southern chambers was an entrance at the beginning of the passageway, the passageway before the corresponding wall on the east, as one enters.

Then the man said to me, “The northern and southern chambers facing the temple precinct are holy chambers, where the priests who approach the LORD shall eat the most holy offerings. There they shall deposit the most holy offerings—the grain offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings—because the place itself is holy.”

When the priests enter, they must not depart from the holy area into the outer court without first relinquishing the garments in which they minister, for those garments are holy. They are to don other clothes before they approach the people.
Now when the man had completed measuring the inner temple, he led me out by way of the east gate and measured the surrounding area.
He measured the east side with the measuring rod: five hundred cubits.
He measured the north side: five hundred cubits.
He measured the south side: five hundred cubits.
He turned and measured the west side: five hundred cubits.
Thus he measured the area on all four sides; it had a wall all around, five hundred cubits in length and five hundred cubits in breadth, to demarcate the holy from the common.
He then conducted me to the gate—the gate that faces east.
And behold, the glory of the God of Israel was advancing from the east, His voice resonant as the sound of many waters, and the earth was irradiated by His glory.
The vision I beheld resembled the vision I had seen when the LORD came to destroy the city, and it recalled the visions I had seen by the Kebar River; whereupon I prostrated myself upon my face.
The glory of the LORD entered the temple by way of the gate facing east.
The Spirit bore me aloft and brought me into the inner court, and behold, the glory of the LORD pervaded the house.
A man stood beside me, and I heard a voice addressing me from within the temple.

He said to me, "Son of man, this is the locus of My throne and the place of the soles of My feet, where I shall dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel forever. The house of Israel—and their kings—shall no longer defile My holy name through their spiritual prostitution or through the corpses of their kings upon their high places.

When they placed their threshold beside My threshold and their doorpost beside My doorpost, with only a wall between Me and them, they defiled My holy name by the abominations they committed; therefore I consumed them in My wrath.
Now let them remove far from Me their spiritual prostitution and the corpses of their kings, and I will dwell among them forever."
"As for you, son of man, describe the temple to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities, and let them measure the plan.

If they are ashamed of all that they have done, make known to them the design of the temple—its arrangement, its exits and entrances, all its forms, all its statutes, every one of its designs, and the whole of its law—and write it before their eyes, so that they may preserve its entire design and all its statutes and put them into practice.
This is the law of the temple: its entire boundary all around, upon the summit of the mountain, is most holy. Behold, this is the law of the temple."

These are the measurements of the altar in cubits—the cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth: its base is one cubit high and one cubit wide, with a rim of one span around its edge; and this is the height of the altar.
From the base on the ground to the lower ledge is two cubits, with a width of one cubit; and from the smaller ledge to the larger ledge is four cubits, with a width of one cubit.
The altar hearth is four cubits high, with four horns rising from it.
The altar hearth is square on all four sides: twelve cubits long by twelve cubits wide.
The ledge is square on all four sides: fourteen cubits long by fourteen cubits wide, with a border of half a cubit all around, a base of one cubit all around, and a stairway facing east.
He said to me, "Son of man, thus says the Lord the LORD: These are the statutes of the altar on the day it is fashioned, for offering burnt offerings upon it and for sprinkling blood upon it.
You shall give a young bull as a sin offering to the Levitical priests of the line of Zadok, who draw near to Me to minister to Me—declares the Lord the LORD.
You shall take some of its blood and apply it to the four horns of the altar, to the four corners of the ledge, and to the border all around; thus you shall purify it and make atonement for it.
You shall take the sin-offering bull and burn it in the designated place of the temple, outside the sanctuary.
On the second day you shall offer an unblemished male goat as a sin offering, and they shall purify the altar just as they purified it with the bull.
When you have finished purifying it, you shall offer an unblemished young bull and an unblemished ram from the flock.
You shall present them before the LORD; the priests shall cast salt upon them and offer them up as a burnt offering to the LORD.
For seven days you shall offer a goat each day as a sin offering, together with an unblemished young bull and an unblemished ram from the flock; they shall offer these.
For seven days they shall make atonement for the altar, purify it, and consecrate it.

When these days are completed, on the eighth day and thereafter, the priests shall offer your burnt offerings and your peace offerings on the altar; and I will accept you, declares the Lord the LORD."
He brought me back by way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, the one facing east, and it was shut.

The LORD said to me, “This gate shall remain shut; it shall not be opened, and no man shall enter through it, because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it; therefore it shall remain shut.
As for the prince—he is indeed a prince—he shall sit in it to eat bread before the LORD; he shall enter by way of the vestibule of the gate, and by that same way he shall go out.”
Then he brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the house. I looked, and behold, the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD, and I fell upon my face.

The LORD said to me, “Son of Man, set your heart and see with your eyes, and hear with your ears everything that I am speaking to you concerning all the statutes of the house of the LORD and all its laws; and set your heart upon the entrance of the house, together with all the exits of the sanctuary.
And you shall say to the rebellious house of Israel, ‘Thus says the Lord the LORD: Enough of all your abominations, O house of Israel—

in that you brought in foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and flesh, to be in My sanctuary, to profane it, even My house, when you offered My food, the fat and the blood; and they broke My covenant in addition to all your abominations.
And you have not kept charge of My holy things, but you have set keepers of My charge in My sanctuary for yourselves.’”
Thus says the Lord the LORD: “No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and flesh, shall enter My sanctuary—not any foreigner who is among the sons of Israel.”
“But as for the Levites who went far from Me when Israel went astray after their idols, they shall bear their iniquity.

They shall be ministers in My sanctuary, having charge at the gates of the house, and ministering to the house; they shall slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they shall stand before them to serve them.

Because they served them before their idols and became a stumbling block of iniquity to the house of Israel, therefore I lifted My hand against them, and they shall bear their iniquity—declares the Lord the LORD.
They shall not approach Me to serve as priest, nor approach any of My holy things, to the most holy things; but they shall bear their shame and the abominations they committed.
Yet I will appoint them keepers of the charge of all the service of the house, and of all that is done in it.”

“But the priests, the Levites, the sons of Zadok, who kept charge of My sanctuary when the sons of Israel went astray from Me, they shall approach Me to serve Me; they shall stand before Me to offer Me the fat and the blood—declares the Lord the LORD.
They shall enter My sanctuary, and they shall approach My table to serve Me, and keep My charge.”
“When they enter the gates of the inner court, they shall wear linen garments; no wool shall come upon them while they serve at the gates of the inner court and within.
Linen turbans shall be on their heads, and linen undergarments upon their waists; they shall not gird themselves with anything that causes sweat.

When they go out to the outer court, to the people, they shall take off the garments in which they served, and leave them in the holy chambers, and put on other garments, so that they do not consecrate the people with their garments.
They shall not shave their heads, nor let their locks grow long; they shall only trim their heads.
No priest shall drink wine when he enters the inner court.
They shall not take widows or divorced women as wives, but only virgins of the seed of the house of Israel, or a widow who is the widow of a priest.
They shall teach My people the difference between the holy and the common, and cause them to discern between the unclean and the clean.
In a dispute they shall stand to judge, and they shall judge according to My judgments; they shall keep My laws and My statutes in all My appointed feasts, and they shall sanctify My Sabbaths.
They shall not defile themselves by going near a dead person, except for father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or a sister who has had no husband; for these they may defile themselves.
After he is cleansed, they shall count seven days for him.
On the day he goes into the sanctuary, into the inner court, to serve in the sanctuary, he shall offer his sin offering—declares the Lord the LORD.
It shall be to them for an inheritance: I am their inheritance; you shall give them no possession in Israel: I am their possession.
They shall eat the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering; and every devoted thing in Israel shall be theirs.

The first of all the firstfruits of every kind, and every contribution of every kind from all your contributions, shall be for the priests; you shall also give to the priest the first of your dough, to cause a blessing to rest upon your house.
The priests shall not eat any bird or beast that died of itself or was torn.”

When you cast lots to apportion the land as an inheritance, you shall set apart for the LORD a holy contribution from the land: a sacred district twenty-five thousand cubits in length and twenty thousand cubits in breadth, and the whole district shall be holy.
Within this district there shall be a square of five hundred cubits by five hundred cubits for the sanctuary, with an open border of fifty cubits encircling it.
From this holy portion you shall measure off a length of twenty-five thousand cubits and a width of ten thousand cubits, and within it shall stand the sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.

It shall be a holy portion of the land for the priests who minister in the sanctuary and draw near to minister before the LORD; it shall furnish them with dwellings and constitute a holy precinct for the sanctuary.
An area twenty-five thousand cubits long and ten thousand cubits wide shall belong to the Levites who minister in the temple, and they shall possess twenty chambers.
You shall allot to the city a tract five thousand cubits wide and twenty-five thousand cubits long, adjacent to the holy portion, and it shall belong to the whole house of Israel.

The prince shall hold a portion on both sides of the holy portion and the city, extending westward from its western side and eastward from its eastern side, running continuously from the western boundary to the eastern boundary.
This land shall be his possession in Israel; and My princes shall no longer oppress My people, but shall allot the remainder of the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes.

Thus says the Lord GOD: "You have gone quite far enough, O princes of Israel! Put away violence and oppression, execute justice and righteousness, and cease dispossessing My people," declares the Lord GOD.
You shall employ just balances, a just ephah, and a just bath.
The ephah and the bath shall be of one capacity: the bath shall contain a tenth of a homer, and the ephah a tenth of a homer, so that the homer shall be the standard measure.
The shekel shall comprise twenty gerahs; twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, and fifteen shekels shall constitute your mina.
This is the contribution that you shall offer: a sixth of an ephah from every homer of wheat, and a sixth of an ephah from every homer of barley.
The ordinance concerning oil, measured by the bath, shall be a tenth of a bath from each cor—a cor being ten baths, that is, one homer, since ten baths make a homer.

From Israel's well-watered pastures you shall take one sheep from every two hundred; these shall serve for the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make atonement for the people, declares the Lord GOD.
All the people of the land shall join in this contribution for the prince in Israel.

It shall be the prince's duty to furnish the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings for the festivals, the new moons, and the Sabbaths—for all the appointed feasts of the house of Israel. He shall provide the sin offering, the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make atonement on behalf of the house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord GOD: "On the first day of the first month you shall take a young bull without blemish and purify the sanctuary."
The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering and apply it to the doorposts of the temple, to the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and to the gateposts of the inner court.
You shall do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who has sinned through error or ignorance; so shall you make atonement for the temple.
On the fourteenth day of the first month you shall observe the Passover, a festival of seven days, during which unleavened bread shall be eaten.
On that day the prince shall provide a bull as a sin offering for himself and for all the people of the land.
Throughout the seven days of the festival, he shall provide seven bulls and seven rams without blemish as a burnt offering to the LORD each day, together with a male goat as a sin offering.
He shall provide as a grain offering an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram, along with a hin of oil for each ephah.
On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, during the festival, he shall make the same provision for seven days: the same sin offering, burnt offering, grain offering, and oil.
Thus says the Lord, the LORD: The gate of the inner court that faces east shall remain closed during the six working days, yet it shall be opened on the Sabbath and on the day of the New Moon.

The prince shall enter from without through the vestibule of the gate and stand beside the gatepost; the priests shall prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he shall worship at the threshold of the gate. Then he shall depart, but the gate shall not be closed until evening.
On the Sabbaths and on the New Moons, the people of the land shall worship at the entrance of that gate before the LORD.
The burnt offering that the prince is to present to the LORD on the Sabbath shall be six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram.
The grain offering accompanying the ram shall be an ephah, and the grain offering with the lambs shall be as much as he can afford, together with a hin of oil per ephah.
On the day of the New Moon, the offering shall be a bull from the herd without blemish, six lambs, and a ram, all of them without blemish.
He shall provide a grain offering of an ephah with the bull and an ephah with the ram, and with the lambs as much as he is able, together with a hin of oil per ephah.
When the prince enters, he shall come in by way of the vestibule of the gate, and he shall go out by the same way.

But when the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed festivals, whoever enters by the north gate to worship shall leave by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate shall leave by the north gate; no one shall turn back by the gate through which he entered, but each shall go out straight ahead.
When they enter, the prince shall enter among them, and when they depart, he shall depart.
At the festivals and appointed seasons, the grain offering shall be an ephah with a bull, an ephah with a ram, and with the lambs as much as one is able, together with a hin of oil per ephah.

When the prince makes a freewill offering, whether a burnt offering or peace offerings, as a freewill offering to the LORD, the gate that faces east shall be opened for him; he shall present his burnt offering and his peace offerings as he does on the Sabbath, and then he shall go out, after which the gate shall be closed.
You shall provide a year-old lamb without blemish as a burnt offering to the LORD each day; morning by morning you shall provide it.

And you shall provide a grain offering with it each morning: one-sixth of an ephah, with one-third of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour, as a grain offering to the LORD. This is a perpetual statute.
Thus they shall provide the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil every morning as a regular burnt offering.
Thus says the Lord, the LORD: If the prince gives a gift to any of his sons, it is his inheritance; it shall belong to his sons and remain their hereditary possession.

But if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall be his only until the year of emancipation, when it shall revert to the prince; only his sons may retain a permanent inheritance.

The prince shall not take any of the people's inheritance by dispossessing them of their property; he shall provide an inheritance for his sons from his own property, so that none of My people may be driven from his holding.
Then he brought me through the entrance at the side of the gate into the holy chambers for the priests, which face north, and behold, there was a place at the far western end.

And he said to me, "This is the place where the priests are to boil the guilt offering and the sin offering and to bake the grain offering, so that they need not bring them out into the outer court and sanctify the people."
Then he brought me out into the outer court and led me around to the four corners of the court; and behold, in each corner of the court there was a court.
In the four corners of the court were enclosed courts, forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide; the four were of the same dimensions.
A row of masonry ran all around them, around the four of them, and cooking hearths were fashioned beneath the rows all around.
And he said to me, "These are the kitchens where the ministers of the temple shall boil the sacrifices of the people."

He brought me back to the entrance of the temple, and behold, water was issuing from beneath the threshold of the temple toward the east, for the temple faced east; and the water was descending from beneath the south side of the temple, south of the altar.
Then he brought me out by way of the north gate and led me around on the outside to the outer gate facing east, and behold, water was trickling from the south side.
The man went out eastward with a measuring line in his hand, measured a thousand cubits, and led me through the water, which was ankle-deep.
He measured another thousand cubits and led me through the water, which was knee-deep; then he measured another thousand and led me through, and the water reached my waist.
He measured yet another thousand, but the river had become an impassable torrent, for the waters had risen into a current deep enough for swimming, a river that could not be forded.
He said to me, "Son of man, have you seen this?" Then he led me back to the bank of the river.
When I returned, behold, on the bank of the river there were very many trees on this side and on that.
He said to me, "These waters go out toward the eastern region and descend into the Arabah; they enter the sea, and when they flow into the sea, the waters are healed.

And wherever the river goes, every living creature that swarms shall live, and there shall be very many fish, because these waters go there and are healed; and everything shall live wherever the river goes."
Fishermen shall stand beside it from En-gedi to En-eglaim; it shall be a place for spreading nets, and its fish shall be of many kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea, exceedingly many.
But its swamps and marshes shall not be healed; they are given over to salt.

And on the bank of the river, on this side and on that, shall grow every tree for food; its leaf shall not wither, nor shall its fruit fail; it shall bear fresh fruit every month, because its waters flow from the sanctuary; and its fruit shall be for food, and its leaf for healing.
Thus says the Lord the LORD: "This is the border by which you shall inherit the land according to the twelve tribes of Israel; Joseph shall have two portions.
You shall inherit it, each one equally with his brother, concerning which I lifted up My hand to give it to your fathers; and this land shall fall to you as an inheritance.
"And this is the border of the land: on the north side, from the Great Sea by way of Hethlon to the entrance of Zedad.
Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim (which is between the border of Damascus and the border of Hamath), and Hazer-hatticon (which is by the border of Hauran).
The border from the sea shall be Hazar-enan at the north border of Damascus, with the border of Hamath to the north; this is the north side.
"On the east side, from between Hauran and Damascus, along the Jordan, between Gilead and the land of Israel, to the eastern sea, to Tamar; this is the east side.
On the south side, from Tamar to the waters of Meribah-kadesh, along the Brook of Egypt to the Great Sea; this is the south side toward the south.
And the west side shall be the Great Sea from the border as far as opposite the entrance of Hamath; this is the west side."
"So you shall divide this land among yourselves according to the tribes of Israel.

You shall allot it as an inheritance to yourselves and to the sojourners who reside among you and who have begotten children among you; they shall be to you as native-born among the children of Israel, and with you they shall fall by lot for an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
In whatever tribe the sojourner resides, there you shall give him his inheritance, declares the Lord the LORD."

These are the names of the tribes. Beginning at the northern boundary, Dan shall receive one portion, whose frontier runs from the road to Hethlon through Lebo-hamath to Hazar-enan and the border of Damascus, with Hamath to the north, extending from the eastern boundary to the sea.
South of Dan, Asher shall receive one portion, stretching from the eastern boundary to the western.
South of Asher, Naphtali shall receive one portion, from the eastern boundary to the western.
South of Naphtali, Manasseh shall receive one portion, from the eastern boundary to the western.
South of Manasseh, Ephraim shall receive one portion, from the eastern boundary to the western.
South of Ephraim, Reuben shall receive one portion, from the eastern boundary to the western.
South of Reuben, Judah shall receive one portion, from the eastern boundary to the western.

Bordering Judah on the south, from east to west, there shall be the special contribution you are to set apart: twenty-five thousand cubits in width, with a length equal to one tribal portion from the eastern boundary to the western, and with the sanctuary in its midst.
The contribution that you offer to the LORD shall be twenty-five thousand cubits in length and ten thousand cubits in width.

This shall be the holy portion for the priests: twenty-five thousand cubits on the north, ten thousand cubits on the west, ten thousand cubits on the east, and twenty-five thousand cubits on the south, with the sanctuary of the LORD in its midst.
It shall belong to the consecrated priests, the descendants of Zadok, who kept My charge and did not go astray as the Levites did when the Israelites went astray.
It shall be a special contribution for them from the land's contribution, a most holy portion adjoining the territory of the Levites.

Alongside the priests' territory, the Levites shall have an area twenty-five thousand cubits in length and ten thousand cubits in width; the whole length shall be twenty-five thousand cubits, and the width ten thousand cubits.
They shall not sell any part of it, nor exchange it, nor alienate the firstfruits of the land, because it is holy to the LORD.
The remaining area—five thousand cubits in width and twenty-five thousand in length—shall be common land for the city, for dwellings and pasture, and the city shall be in its midst.

These shall be the city's dimensions: four thousand five hundred cubits on the north, four thousand five hundred on the south, four thousand five hundred on the east, and four thousand five hundred on the west.
The city's pastureland shall extend two hundred fifty cubits to the north, two hundred fifty to the south, two hundred fifty to the east, and two hundred fifty to the west.
The remainder of the holy portion, bordering the holy allotment, shall be ten thousand cubits to the east and ten thousand to the west; its produce shall provide food for the city's workers.
The city's workers, drawn from all the tribes of Israel, shall cultivate it.
The entire portion shall be a square, twenty-five thousand cubits by twenty-five thousand cubits; you shall set apart the holy portion together with the city's property.

The remainder on both sides of the holy portion and the city's property shall belong to the prince: eastward from the twenty-five thousand cubits of the holy portion to the eastern boundary, and westward from the twenty-five thousand cubits to the western boundary, with the holy portion and the sanctuary of the temple in its midst.
Thus the Levitical property and the city's property shall lie in the center of the area belonging to the prince, whose territory shall lie between the borders of Judah and Benjamin.
As for the remaining tribes, Benjamin shall receive one portion, south of the prince's allotment, extending from the eastern boundary to the western.
South of Benjamin, Simeon shall receive one portion, from the eastern boundary to the western.
South of Simeon, Issachar shall receive one portion, from the eastern boundary to the western.
South of Issachar, Zebulun shall receive one portion, from the eastern boundary to the western.
South of Zebulun, Gad shall receive one portion, from the eastern boundary to the western.
Gad's southern boundary shall run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, then along the Brook of Egypt to the Great Sea.
“This is the land that you are to allot as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel, and these are their portions,” declares the Lord the LORD.
“These are the exits of the city: on the north side, which shall be four thousand five hundred cubits long,
the gates of the city shall be named after the tribes of Israel. There shall be three gates on the north: the gate of Reuben, the gate of Judah, and the gate of Levi.
On the east side, which shall be four thousand five hundred cubits long, there shall be three gates: the gate of Joseph, the gate of Benjamin, and the gate of Dan.
On the south side, which shall be four thousand five hundred cubits long, there shall be three gates: the gate of Simeon, the gate of Issachar, and the gate of Zebulun.
On the west side, which shall be four thousand five hundred cubits long, there shall be three gates: the gate of Gad, the gate of Asher, and the gate of Naphtali.
The perimeter shall be eighteen thousand cubits, and from that day the name of the city shall be: The LORD Is There.”
In the third year of Jehoiakim's reign over Judah, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, advanced upon Jerusalem and besieged it.

And the Lord delivered Jehoiakim, king of Judah, into his power, together with a portion of the vessels of the house of God; he conveyed them to the land of Shinar, to the temple of his deity, and deposited the vessels in the treasury of his god.
Then the king commanded Ashpenaz, the chief of his eunuchs, to select from among the Israelites—of royal lineage and of noble extraction—

youths in whom no physical defect was found, comely in appearance, sagacious in every branch of wisdom, conversant with knowledge, discerning in understanding, and endowed with the vigor requisite to stand in the king's palace, that he might instruct them in the literature and language of the Chaldeans.

The king allotted to them a daily ration from the royal viands and from the wine of his own table; they were to be nurtured for three years, and thereafter they were to present themselves before the king.
Among them were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, of the tribe of Judah.
The chief of the eunuchs assigned them appellations: Daniel he styled Belteshazzar; Hananiah, Shadrach; Mishael, Meshach; and Azariah, Abednego.
But Daniel resolved in his heart not to defile himself with the king's delicacies or with the wine of his banquets; therefore he petitioned the chief of the eunuchs to be exempted from defilement.
Now God granted Daniel favor and compassion in the sight of the chief of the eunuchs.

And the chief said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king, who has prescribed your food and your drink; for why should he behold your countenances more haggard than those of the youths of your own cohort? You would thereby render me culpable to the king.”
Then Daniel said to the steward whom the chief of the eunuchs had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
“I entreat you to test your servants for ten days; let us be furnished with vegetables to eat and water to drink.
Then compare our appearance with that of the youths who consume the king's delicacies, and deal with your servants in accordance with what you observe.”
So he hearkened to them in this matter and tested them for ten days.
At the end of ten days their appearance proved superior and their flesh more robust than that of all the youths who partook of the king's delicacies.
Thereupon the steward withdrew their prescribed food and the wine appointed for their drink, and furnished them with vegetables.
As for these four youths, God conferred upon them knowledge and proficiency in every branch of literature and wisdom; moreover, Daniel possessed discernment in all visions and dreams.
At the expiration of the days designated by the king for their presentation, the chief of the eunuchs escorted them into the presence of Nebuchadnezzar.
The king conversed with them, and among them all none was found comparable to Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah; consequently they were stationed before the king.
In every matter of wisdom and discernment upon which the king interrogated them, he discovered them tenfold superior to all the magicians and enchanters in his entire realm.
Daniel remained until the first year of King Cyrus.
In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams; his spirit was deeply agitated, and sleep fled from him.
The king commanded that the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and Chaldeans be summoned to declare to the king his dreams. They came and stood before the king.
The king said to them, “I have had a dream, and my spirit is disquieted to know the dream.”
The Chaldeans then addressed the king in Aramaic: “Long live the king! Tell your servants the dream, and we will declare its interpretation.”
The king answered the Chaldeans, “My decree is final: if you do not make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you shall be dismembered, and your houses reduced to rubble.
But if you show the dream and its interpretation, you shall receive gifts, lavish rewards, and great honor. Therefore show me the dream and its interpretation.”
They answered a second time, “Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will show its interpretation.”
The king answered, “I know with certainty that you are stalling for time, because you perceive that my decree is irrevocable.

If you do not make known the dream to me, there is one uniform sentence for you all; for you have agreed to speak lying and corrupt words before me until circumstances change. Therefore tell me the dream, and I shall know that you can show the interpretation.”
The Chaldeans answered the king, “There is no man on earth who can show the king’s matter, for no great and powerful king has ever asked such a thing of any magician, enchanter, or Chaldean.
The thing the king asks is arduous, and no one can show it except the gods, whose dwelling is not among mortals.”
Because of this the king was incensed and exceedingly wrathful, and he commanded that all the wise men of Babylon be destroyed.
The decree went out, and the wise men were being killed; and they sought Daniel and his companions, that they too might be put to death.
Then Daniel replied with prudence and tact to Arioch, the captain of the king’s guard, who had gone out to execute the wise men of Babylon.
He answered Arioch, the king’s officer, “Why is the king’s decree so urgent?” Then Arioch made the matter known to Daniel.
Daniel went in and requested of the king that he would grant him time, and that he would show the king the interpretation.
Then Daniel went to his house and made the matter known to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions,
that they might seek mercy from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his companions might not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a night vision. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
Daniel answered and said, “Blessed be the name of God from everlasting to everlasting, for wisdom and might are His.
He changes times and seasons; He removes kings and establishes kings; He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who have understanding.
He reveals deep and hidden things; He knows what is in darkness, and light dwells with Him.
To You, O God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, for You have given me wisdom and might, and have now made known to me what we asked of You, for You have made known to us the king’s matter.”

Therefore Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon; he went and said, “Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon; bring me before the king, and I will show the king the interpretation.”
Then Arioch brought Daniel before the king in haste and said, “I have found a man among the exiles of Judah who will make known to the king the interpretation.”
The king answered Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, “Are you able to make known to me the dream I saw and its interpretation?”
Daniel answered before the king, “No wise men, enchanters, magicians, or astrologers can show the king the mystery that the king asks.
But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, and He has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will be in the latter days. Your dream and the visions of your head upon your bed are these:”
“As for you, O king, your thoughts arose upon your bed as to what would come after this; and He who reveals mysteries made known to you what will be.

But as for me, this mystery has been revealed to me, not because I have more wisdom than all the living, but so that the interpretation may be made known to the king, and that you may know the thoughts of your heart.”
“You, O king, were looking, and behold, a great image. This image, mighty and of surpassing brightness, stood before you, and its appearance was terrifying.
The head of the image was fine gold; its breast and arms were silver; its belly and thighs were bronze;
its legs were iron; its feet were partly iron and partly clay.”
“You watched until a stone was cut out without hands, and it struck the image upon its feet of iron and clay and shattered them.

Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were crushed together and became like chaff from the summer threshing floors; the wind carried them away, and they vanished without a trace. But the stone that struck the image became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
This is the dream; now we will tell its interpretation before the king.”
“You, O king, are king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given the kingdom, the power, the strength, and the glory.
Wherever the sons of men dwell, the beasts of the field and the birds of the heaven He has given into your hand, and has made you ruler over them all. You are the head of gold.”
“After you another kingdom will arise, inferior to yours, and then a third kingdom of bronze, which shall rule over all the earth.
A fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron, because iron breaks in pieces and shatters all things; and like iron that crushes, it shall break in pieces and crush.”
“Whereas you saw the feet and toes, partly of baked clay and partly of iron, the kingdom shall be divided; yet the strength of iron shall be in it, just as you saw iron mixed with miry clay.
The toes of the feet, partly iron and partly clay: the kingdom shall be partly strong and partly brittle.
Whereas you saw iron mixed with miry clay, they shall mingle with the seed of men, but they shall not adhere one to another, just as iron does not mix with clay.”

“In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed; nor shall its sovereignty be left to another people; it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand forever.

Inasmuch as you saw that a stone was cut from the mountain without hands, and that it broke in pieces the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold—the great God has made known to the king what shall come after this. The dream is certain, and its interpretation is trustworthy.”
Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell upon his face and paid homage to Daniel, and commanded that an offering and incense be offered to him.
The king answered Daniel, “Truly your God is God of gods and Lord of kings and Revealer of mysteries, since you were able to reveal this mystery.”
Then the king made Daniel great, and gave him many great gifts, and made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon and chief prefect over all the wise men of Babylon.
Daniel requested of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the affairs of the province of Babylon; but Daniel was at the gate of the king.
King Nebuchadnezzar fashioned an image of gold, sixty cubits in height and six cubits in breadth, and he set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.

Then King Nebuchadnezzar sent to assemble the satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the other provincial officials, that they might attend the dedication of the image he had erected.
So the satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the provincial officials were gathered for the dedication of the image, and they stood before it.
Then a herald cried aloud: “To you, O peoples, nations, and languages, it is proclaimed
that at the moment you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and every kind of music, you are to fall down and worship the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
Whoever does not fall down and worship shall be cast immediately into a burning fiery furnace.”
