Therefore, as soon as all the peoples heard the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, and every kind of music, all the peoples, nations, and languages fell down and worshiped the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
At that time certain Chaldeans came near and maliciously accused the Jews.
They said to King Nebuchadnezzar, “O king, may you live forever!
You, O king, have made a decree that everyone who hears the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and every kind of music shall fall down and worship the golden image;
and whoever does not fall down and worship shall be cast into a burning fiery furnace.

There are certain Jews whom you have appointed over the administration of the province of Babylon—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. These men, O king, pay no heed to you; they do not serve your gods, and they do not worship the golden image that you have set up.”
Then Nebuchadnezzar, in furious rage, commanded that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego be brought; and these men were brought before the king.
Nebuchadnezzar answered them, “Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you do not serve my gods and do not worship the golden image that I have set up?

Now if you are ready, at the moment you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and every kind of music, and you fall down and worship the image that I have made, very good; but if you do not worship, you shall be cast immediately into a burning fiery furnace. And what god is there who can deliver you from my hand?”
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered the king, “O Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer you in this matter.
If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and He will deliver us from your hand, O king.
But even if He does not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden image that you have set up.”

Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and the aspect of his face was altered toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He spoke and commanded that the furnace be heated seven times more than it was usually heated.
And he commanded certain mighty men of his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and to cast them into the burning fiery furnace.
Then these men were bound in their cloaks, tunics, hats, and other garments, and they were cast into the burning fiery furnace.
Because the king’s command was urgent and the furnace exceedingly hot, the flame of the fire slew those men who carried up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell down bound into the burning fiery furnace.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar was astonished and rose up in haste. He said to his counselors, “Did we not cast three men bound into the fire?” They answered and said to the king, “True, O king.”
He answered and said, “Behold, I see four men unbound, walking in the midst of the fire, and they are not hurt; and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.”

Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the door of the burning fiery furnace and said, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out and come here.” Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out of the midst of the fire.

And the satraps, prefects, governors, and the king’s counselors gathered together and saw these men, that the fire had exercised no power over their bodies; the hair of their heads was not singed, their cloaks were not changed, and the smell of fire had not come upon them.

Nebuchadnezzar spoke and said, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who has sent His angel and delivered His servants who trusted in Him, and who have defied the king’s command and yielded their bodies rather than serve or worship any god except their own God.

Therefore I make a decree: Every people, nation, and language that speaks anything amiss against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego shall be cut in pieces, and their houses shall be reduced to rubble, because there is no other god who is able to deliver in this way.”
Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.
King Nebuchadnezzar to all peoples, nations, and languages dwelling throughout the whole earth: may your peace be multiplied.
It has seemed good to me to declare the signs and wonders that the Most High God has wrought toward me.
How great are His signs, and how mighty His wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and His dominion endures from generation to generation.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was tranquil in my house and flourishing in my palace.
I beheld a dream that terrified me, and the cogitations of my bed, together with the visions of my head, dismayed me.
Therefore I issued a decree summoning all the wise men of Babylon into my presence, that they might disclose to me the interpretation of the dream.
Then the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and astrologers entered, and I rehearsed the dream before them, yet they proved unable to disclose its interpretation to me.
At last Daniel—called Belteshazzar after my god, and in whom resides the spirit of the holy gods—came into my presence, and I recounted the dream to him.

“O Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, since I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you and that no secret is too arduous for you, declare to me the visions of my dream that I beheld, and their interpretation.”
The visions of my head upon my bed were these: I looked, and there stood a tree in the midst of the earth, exceedingly tall.
The tree grew mighty and robust, its crown reaching to the heavens, and it was visible to the ends of all the earth.

Its foliage was fair and its fruit abundant, and food for all was in it; beneath it the beasts of the field took shelter, the birds of the heavens nested in its branches, and all flesh was nourished from it.
As I lay upon my bed, in the visions of my head, I beheld a watcher—a holy one—descending from heaven.

He cried out with a mighty voice and declared, “Cut down the tree, lop off its branches, strip away its foliage, and scatter its fruit; let the beasts flee from beneath it and the birds from its branches.

Yet leave the stump of its roots in the earth, bound with a band of iron and bronze, amid the tender grass of the field; let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and let his lot be with the beasts among the grass of the earth.
Let his mind be altered from that of a man, and let the mind of a beast be given to him, and let seven times pass over him.

This sentence is decreed by the watchers, and the demand is pronounced by the holy ones, so that the living may know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity, grants it to whomever He wills, and exalts over it the lowliest of men.”

This dream I, King Nebuchadnezzar, beheld; and you, O Belteshazzar, declare its interpretation, for none of the wise men of my kingdom can disclose it to me, yet you are able, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you.

Then Daniel, whose name is Belteshazzar, stood appalled for a time, and his thoughts troubled him. The king answered and said, “Belteshazzar, let neither the dream nor its interpretation dismay you.” Belteshazzar answered and said, “My lord, would that the dream concerned your foes and its interpretation your enemies!
The tree that you saw, which grew and became strong, whose top reached to heaven and which was visible to the ends of all the earth—
whose foliage was fair and whose fruit was abundant, and in which was food for all; beneath it the beasts of the field took shelter, and in its branches the birds of the heavens dwelt—
it is you, O king, who have grown and become mighty: Your greatness has increased until it reaches heaven, and your dominion extends to the ends of the earth.

And inasmuch as the king beheld a watcher, a holy one, descending from heaven and saying, ‘Cut down the tree and destroy it, yet leave the stump of its roots in the earth, bound with iron and bronze, amid the tender grass of the field; let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and let his lot be with the beasts of the field, until seven times pass over him’—
this is the interpretation, O king: it is a decree of the Most High that has come upon my lord the king—

that you will be driven from among men, and your dwelling will be with the beasts of the field; you will be made to eat grass like an ox, and you will be drenched with the dew of heaven, and seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity and grants it to whomever He wills.
And as it was commanded that the stump of the tree's roots be left, so your kingdom will be preserved for you once you acknowledge that Heaven rules.

Therefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable to you: redeem your sins by righteousness and your iniquities by showing mercy to the oppressed, if perhaps there may be a prolonging of your tranquility.”
All of this befell King Nebuchadnezzar.
Twelve months later, he was strolling upon the roof of the royal palace in Babylon,
and the king declared, “Is this not Babylon the great, which I myself have built as a royal residence by the might of my power and for the glory of my majesty?”
While the word was yet upon the king's lips, a voice fell from heaven: “O King Nebuchadnezzar, to you it is declared: the kingdom has been taken from you,

and you will be driven from among men, and your dwelling will be with the beasts of the field; you will be made to eat grass like an ox, and seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity and grants it to whomever He wills.”

Immediately the word was fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar: he was driven from among men, ate grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven until his hair grew as long as eagles' feathers and his nails became like birds' claws.

At the end of those days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me; I blessed the Most High, and praised and honored Him who lives forever; His dominion is an everlasting dominion, and His kingdom endures from generation to generation.

All the inhabitants of the earth are reckoned as nothing; He does according to His will among the host of heaven and among the inhabitants of the earth, and none can restrain His hand or say to Him, “What have You done?”

At that very time my understanding returned to me, and for the glory of my kingdom my majesty and splendor were restored to me; my counselors and nobles sought me out, and I was re-established in my kingdom, with even greater greatness added to me.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise, exalt, and honor the King of heaven, for all His works are truth and His ways are justice; and those who walk in pride He is able to humble.
King Belshazzar prepared a lavish banquet for a thousand of his nobles, and he drank wine in their presence.

While exhilarated by the wine, Belshazzar gave orders to bring the gold and silver vessels that Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken from the temple in Jerusalem, so that the king, his nobles, his wives, and his concubines might drink from them.
Accordingly, they brought the gold vessels taken from the temple of the house of God in Jerusalem, and the king, his nobles, his wives, and his concubines drank from them.
They drank wine and extolled the gods of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
In that very hour the fingers of a human hand emerged and wrote upon the plaster of the wall opposite the lampstand, and the king beheld the part of the hand that was writing.
Then the king's countenance was altered, and his thoughts terrified him; the joints of his loins were loosened, and his knees smote one another.

The king cried out authoritatively for the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the astrologers to be brought in. He addressed the wise men of Babylon, saying, "Whoever reads this writing and reveals its interpretation shall be clothed in purple, shall wear a chain of gold upon his neck, and shall exercise authority as the third highest ruler in the kingdom."
Then all the king's wise men entered, yet they were unable to read the writing or to disclose its interpretation to the king.
Thereupon King Belshazzar was greatly dismayed, his countenance changed, and his nobles were confounded.

Because of the king's words and those of his nobles, the queen entered the banquet hall. The queen declared, "O king, live forever! Let not your thoughts terrify you, nor let your countenance be altered.

There is a man in your kingdom in whom resides the spirit of the holy gods; in the days of your father, illumination, understanding, and wisdom like that of the gods were found in him. King Nebuchadnezzar, your father, appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and astrologers.

Because an extraordinary spirit, together with knowledge and discernment—interpreting dreams, expounding riddles, and unraveling knotty problems—was found in Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar, let Daniel now be summoned, and he will reveal the interpretation."
Then Daniel was brought before the king. The king addressed Daniel, saying, "Are you Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah whom my father the king brought from Judah?
I have heard concerning you that the spirit of the gods is in you, and that illumination, understanding, and surpassing wisdom have been found in you.
Now the wise men, the enchanters, have been brought before me to read this writing and to make known its interpretation to me, yet they were unable to disclose the interpretation of the matter.

But I have heard concerning you that you can render interpretations and unravel knotty problems. Now if you can read the writing and make known to me its interpretation, you shall be clothed in purple, shall wear a chain of gold upon your neck, and shall exercise authority as the third highest ruler in the kingdom." "
Let your gifts remain yours, and let your recompense be bestowed upon another; nevertheless, I shall read the writing to the king and make known to him its interpretation.
O king, the Most High God granted to Nebuchadnezzar your father the kingdom, greatness, glory, and majesty.

Because of the greatness that He bestowed upon him, all peoples, nations, and languages quaked and feared before him. Whomever he willed, he put to death; whomever he willed, he spared; whomever he willed, he exalted; and whomever he willed, he abased. "
But when his heart was lifted up and his spirit grew insolent with pride, he was deposed from his royal throne, and his glory was taken from him.

He was driven out from human society, his mind was made like that of the beasts, and his dwelling was with the wild donkeys. He was fed grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until he acknowledged that the Most High God holds sovereignty over human kingdoms and appoints over them whomever He pleases. "
And you, his son Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, although you knew all this.

Rather, you have exalted yourself against the Lord of heaven. The vessels of His house were brought before you, and you, your nobles, your wives, and your concubines drank wine from them. You praised the gods of silver, gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone—gods that neither see, nor hear, nor know—yet the God in whose hand are your life-breath and all your ways you have not glorified.
Therefore, from His presence were sent the fingers of a hand, and this inscription was written.
This is the inscription that was written: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, and PARSIN.
This is the interpretation of the matter: MENE—God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to its close.
TEKEL—you have been weighed in the scales and found deficient.
PERES—your kingdom has been divided and given to the Medes and Persians."

Then Belshazzar gave the command, and Daniel was clothed in purple, a chain of gold was placed upon his neck, and proclamation was made concerning him that he should be the third highest ruler in the kingdom.
That very night Belshazzar, the king of the Chaldeans, was slain.
And Darius the Mede received the kingdom, being about sixty-two years old.
It pleased Darius to appoint one hundred twenty satraps over the kingdom, stationed throughout the entire realm,
and over them three chief administrators, among whom Daniel was one, so that these satraps might render account to them and the king suffer no loss.
Then this Daniel distinguished himself above the administrators and satraps, because an extraordinary spirit was in him, and the king contemplated establishing him over the whole kingdom.

Thereupon the administrators and satraps sought to discover a pretext against Daniel in the affairs of the kingdom, yet they could find neither corruption nor negligence, since he was faithful and no fault or corruption was found in him.
Consequently these men said, "We shall find no pretext against this Daniel unless we find it in the law of his God."
Then these administrators and satraps thronged to the king and addressed him thus: "O King Darius, live forever!

All the administrators of the kingdom, the prefects and satraps, the counselors and governors, have conferred together to establish a royal statute and to enforce an interdict: for thirty days, whoever petitions any god or human being except you, O King, shall be cast into the den of lions.
Now, O King, establish the interdict and sign the document, so that it cannot be altered, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which does not pass away."
Therefore King Darius signed the document and the interdict.

When Daniel learned that the document had been signed, he went to his house, where, in his upper chamber, with windows opened toward Jerusalem, he knelt three times each day, prayed, and gave thanks before his God, precisely as he had done before.
Then these men assembled and found Daniel petitioning and supplicating before his God.

They approached the king and said concerning the interdict, "Did you not sign an interdict, O King, that for thirty days any person who petitions any god or human being except you, O King, shall be cast into the den of lions?" The king answered, "The matter is established, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which does not pass away."
Then they answered before the king, "Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah, pays no heed to you, O King, nor to the interdict that you signed, but petitions his God three times a day."
When the king heard the matter, he was deeply distressed concerning Daniel, and he resolved to deliver him; he labored until sunset to rescue him.
Then these men thronged to the king and said, "Know, O King, that it is a law of the Medes and Persians that no interdict or statute which the king establishes may be changed."
Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel and cast him into the den of lions. The king said to Daniel, "May your God, whom you serve continually, deliver you!"
A stone was brought and placed over the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet and with the signets of his nobles, so that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel.
Then the king went to his palace and spent the night fasting; no entertainments were brought before him, and sleep fled from him.
Then at daybreak, as soon as it was light, the king arose and went in haste to the den of lions.

As he drew near to the den, he cried out to Daniel with an anguished voice; the king spoke and said, "Daniel, servant of the Living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to deliver you from the lions?"
Then Daniel spoke with the king, "O King, live forever!
My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions, so that they have not harmed me, because I was found innocent before Him; and also before you, O King, I have done no wrong."

Then the king was exceedingly glad concerning him, and commanded that Daniel be taken up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no injury was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

The king then commanded, and those men who had maliciously accused Daniel were brought and cast into the den of lions—they, their children, and their wives; and before they reached the bottom of the den, the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.
Then King Darius wrote to all peoples, nations, and languages dwelling in all the earth: "May your peace be multiplied.

I issue a decree that in every dominion of my kingdom people shall fear and tremble before the God of Daniel, for He is the Living God and endures forever; His kingdom shall not be destroyed, and His dominion shall be to the end.
He delivers and rescues; He performs signs and wonders in heaven and on earth; He has delivered Daniel from the power of the lions."
So this Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and during the reign of Cyrus the Persian.

In the first year of Belshazzar’s reign over Babylon, Daniel beheld a dream, and visions traversed his mind as he lay upon his couch; he then committed the dream to writing, distilling the essential purport of the affair.
Daniel declared, “In my nocturnal vision I looked, and behold, the four winds of heaven were churning the great sea.
Four great beasts ascended from the sea, each distinct from the others.

The first resembled a lion, yet it possessed the wings of an eagle; I watched until its wings were plucked away, whereupon it was lifted from the earth and made to stand upon its feet like a man, and a human heart was bestowed upon it.
And behold, a second beast, like a bear, raised itself on one side, and three ribs were clenched between its teeth; a voice commanded it, “Arise and devour flesh in abundance.”
After this I beheld another beast, like a leopard, with four wings of a bird upon its back; it had four heads, and dominion was granted to it.

Thereafter, in my nocturnal visions, I saw a fourth beast, dreadful and exceedingly terrifying, possessed of great iron teeth; it devoured, crushed, and trampled the remainder with its feet, and it differed from all the beasts that preceded it, for it had ten horns.

While I contemplated the horns, behold, another horn, small, sprang up among them, and three of the former horns were uprooted before it; and in this horn were eyes like the eyes of a man, together with a mouth uttering grandiose things.

I continued watching until thrones were set in place and the Ancient of Days took His seat. His garment was white as snow, and the hair of His head was like pure wool; His throne was flames of fire, and its wheels were burning fire.
A river of fire issued forth and flowed from before Him; thousands upon thousands served Him, and myriads upon myriads stood before Him. The court convened, and the books were opened.
I watched then because of the sound of the great words the horn was speaking; I watched until the beast was slain, its body destroyed, and given over to be burned with fire.
As for the other beasts, their dominion was removed, though a prolongation of life was granted to them for a season and a time.
In my nocturnal vision I continued to watch, and behold, One like a Son of Man came with the clouds of heaven; He approached the Ancient of Days and was brought before Him.

To Him was given dominion, glory, and a kingdom, so that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve Him; His dominion is an everlasting dominion that shall not pass away, and His kingdom is one that shall not be destroyed.”
I, Daniel, was grieved in spirit, and the visions of my head alarmed me.
I approached one of those standing by and sought from him the certain truth concerning all this, and he spoke to me and disclosed the interpretation of these matters.
“These four great beasts are four kings who shall arise from the earth.
But the saints of the Most High shall receive the kingdom and possess it forever—yes, forever and ever.”

Then I desired to ascertain the truth concerning the fourth beast, which differed from all the others, exceedingly dreadful, with teeth of iron and claws of bronze, devouring and crushing, and trampling the remainder with its feet;

and concerning the ten horns upon its head, and the other horn that came up, before which three fell, the horn that had eyes and a mouth speaking great things and appeared greater than its companions.
As I watched, that horn made war against the saints and prevailed against them,
until the Ancient of Days came and judgment was rendered in favor of the saints of the Most High, and the appointed time arrived for the saints to possess the kingdom.
This is what he said: “The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom that shall arise upon the earth, differing from all the kingdoms; it shall devour the whole earth, trample it down, and crush it.
The ten horns are ten kings who shall arise from this kingdom, and after them another shall arise, different from the former ones, and he shall subdue three kings.

He shall speak words against the Most High and wear out the saints of the Most High; he shall intend to alter the times and the law, and they shall be given into his hand for a time, times, and half a time.
But the court shall sit, and his dominion shall be taken away, to be destroyed and annihilated forever.

Then the kingdom, the dominion, and the greatness of the kingdoms under all heaven shall be given to the holy people of the Most High. His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey Him.”
Here is the end of the matter. I, Daniel, was greatly troubled by my thoughts, and my countenance changed; yet I kept the matter in my heart.
In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me—Daniel—after the one that had appeared to me at the first.
In the vision I was in Susa the citadel, in the province of Elam, and I was standing by the Ulai canal.
I lifted my eyes and looked, and behold, a ram was standing before the canal, and it had two horns; the horns were high, but one was higher than the other, and the higher one came up last.
I saw the ram goring westward, northward, and southward; no beast could withstand it, and none could deliver any from its hand; it acted according to its will and magnified itself.
As I was considering this, behold, a male goat came from the west, sweeping across the face of the whole earth without touching the ground; and the goat had a conspicuous horn between its eyes.
It came to the ram with the two horns, which I had seen standing before the canal, and it charged at it with the fury of its might.

I saw it reach the ram; enraged against it, it struck the ram and shattered its two horns, and the ram had no strength to stand before it; it hurled the ram to the ground and trampled it, and there was no one to rescue the ram from its power.
The male goat grew exceedingly great; but when it had become strong, the great horn was broken, and in its place four conspicuous horns sprang up toward the four winds of heaven.
From one of them came forth a little horn, which grew exceedingly toward the south, toward the east, and toward the Beautiful Land.
It grew up to the host of heaven, threw down some of the host and some of the stars to the earth, and trampled them.
It magnified itself even to the Prince of the host; it took away the daily sacrifice from Him, and His sanctuary was thrown down.
Because of transgression, a host was given over to it together with the daily sacrifice; it cast truth to the ground and prospered in all that it did.

I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to the one who was speaking, “How long will the vision last—the daily sacrifice, the desolating transgression, and the surrender of both the sanctuary and the host to be trampled underfoot?”
He said to me, “For two thousand three hundred evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary shall be restored to its rightful state.”
When I, Daniel, had seen the vision, I sought to understand it; and behold, there stood before me one whose appearance was like that of a man.
I heard a human voice calling across the Ulai, “Gabriel, make this man understand the vision.”
He came near where I stood, and when he came I was terrified and fell on my face. He said to me, “Understand, O son of man, that the vision concerns the time of the end.”
While he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep with my face to the ground; but he touched me and set me on my feet.
He said, “Behold, I will make known to you what is to happen at the end of the wrath, for it concerns the appointed time of the end.
The ram that you saw with its two horns represents the kings of Media and Persia.
The shaggy goat is the king of Greece, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king.
As for the horn that was broken, in whose place four arose, four kingdoms shall arise from that nation, but not with his power.
“In the latter part of their kingdom, when the transgressors have reached their full measure, a king of fierce countenance, adept in intrigue, shall arise.
His power shall be mighty, though not by his own strength; he shall work fearful destruction, prosper in all that he does, destroy mighty men, and afflict the holy people.

By his cunning he shall make deceit prosper under his control; in his heart he shall magnify himself; while men are at ease he shall destroy many; and he shall rise up against the Prince of princes, but he shall be broken by no human hand.
The vision of the evenings and mornings that has been declared is true; but seal up the vision, for it concerns days far in the future.”
And I, Daniel, was overcome and lay sick for several days; then I rose and attended to the king’s business, but I was appalled by the vision, and no one could explain it.
In the inaugural year of Darius, son of Ahasuerus, of Median lineage, who had been enthroned over the Chaldean realm,

in the opening year of his reign, I, Daniel, discerned from the sacred writings the tally of years concerning which the word of the LORD had come to Jeremiah the prophet: that Jerusalem's desolations were to fulfill seventy years.
I turned my countenance toward the Lord God, earnestly seeking Him through prayer and supplication, accompanied by fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.
I prayed to the LORD my God and confessed, saying, "O Lord, the great and awe-inspiring God, who keeps covenant and steadfast love with those who love Him and keep His commandments,
we have sinned, acted perversely, wrought wickedness, and rebelled; indeed, we have turned aside from Your precepts and Your judgments.
Nor have we heeded Your servants the prophets, who spoke in Your name to our kings, our princes, and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.

"O Lord, righteousness belongs to You, but to us belongs open shame, as it is this day—to the men of Judah, to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to all Israel, near and far, throughout all the lands to which You have driven them, because of the treachery by which they have acted treacherously against You.
O Lord, open shame belongs to us—to our kings, our princes, and our fathers—because we have sinned against You.
To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgiveness, though we have rebelled against Him.
"Nor have we obeyed the voice of the LORD our God, to walk in His laws, which He set before us by His servants the prophets.

Indeed, all Israel has transgressed Your law and turned aside, refusing to obey Your voice; therefore the curse and the oath written in the Law of Moses, the servant of God, have been poured out upon us, because we have sinned against Him.

And He has confirmed His words, which He spoke against us and against our judges who judged us, by bringing upon us a great calamity; for under the whole heaven nothing has been done like what has been done to Jerusalem.

"As it is written in the Law of Moses, all this calamity has come upon us; yet we have not entreated the favor of the LORD our God, that we might turn from our iniquities and gain insight into Your truth.
The LORD has kept watch over the calamity and brought it upon us, for the LORD our God is righteous in all His works that He has done, and we have not obeyed His voice.
"And now, O Lord our God, who brought Your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and made for Yourself a name, as it is this day—we have sinned, we have acted wickedly.

O Lord, according to all Your righteousness, let Your anger and Your wrath turn away from Your city Jerusalem, Your holy mountain; for because of our sins and the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and Your people have become a reproach to all around us.
"And now, our God, hear the prayer of Your servant and his supplications, and for the Lord's sake let Your face shine upon Your desolate sanctuary.

O my God, incline Your ear and hear; open Your eyes and behold our desolations and the city that is called by Your name; for we do not present our supplications before You because of our righteous deeds, but because of Your great mercies.
O Lord, hear; O Lord, forgive; O Lord, pay heed and act; do not delay, for Your own sake, O my God, for Your city and Your people are called by Your name."
While I was still speaking and praying, confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and presenting my supplication before the LORD my God concerning the holy mountain of my God,
indeed, while I was still speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the earlier vision, came to me in swift flight at the time of the evening offering.
And he instructed me and spoke with me, saying, "O Daniel, I have now come forth to impart to you insight and understanding.
"At the beginning of your supplications a word went forth, and I have come to declare it, for you are greatly beloved; therefore consider the word and understand the vision.

"Seventy weeks are decreed concerning your people and your holy city: to finish transgression, to put an end to sin, to atone for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the Most Holy Place.

"Know, therefore, and understand: from the issuing of the decree to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until the Anointed One, the Prince, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks; the plaza and the moat will be rebuilt, though in times of distress.

And after the sixty-two weeks, the Anointed One will be cut off and have nothing; and the people of the coming prince will destroy the city and the sanctuary; its end will come like a flood, and until the end there will be war; desolations are decreed.

He will enforce a covenant with many for one week; in the middle of that week he will bring sacrifice and offering to an end; and upon the wing of abominations will come a desolator, until the decreed consummation is poured out upon the desolate."

In the third year of King Cyrus of Persia, a revelation was granted to Daniel, who was called Belteshazzar. The message was true and concerned a great conflict, and understanding of the message was given to him in a vision.
In those days I, Daniel, was in mourning for three full weeks.
I ate no delicacies; no meat or wine passed my lips; I did not anoint myself with oil until the three weeks had run their course.
On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was standing beside the great river, the Tigris.
I lifted my eyes and looked, and there stood a man clothed in linen, belted about the waist with gold from Uphaz.
His body was like beryl, his face like lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and feet like burnished bronze, and the sound of his words like the roar of a multitude.
I, Daniel, alone saw the vision, for the men who were with me did not see it; nevertheless, a great dread fell upon them, and they fled to hide themselves.
So I was left alone and saw this great vision. No strength remained in me; my vigor was turned to ruin within me, and I retained no power.
Then I heard the sound of his words; and as I heard it, I fell into a deep sleep, my face to the ground.
Then a hand touched me and set me trembling upon my knees and the palms of my hands.
He said to me, “O Daniel, man greatly beloved, understand the words that I speak to you, and stand upright, for now I am sent to you.” When he had spoken this word to me, I stood trembling.

He said to me, “Do not be afraid, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come because of your words.
The prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me for twenty-one days, but Michael, one of the chief princes, came to my aid, for I had been left there with the kings of Persia.
Now I have come to make you understand what will befall your people in the latter days, for the vision concerns those days.”
While he was speaking these words to me, I turned my face to the ground and was speechless.

Then one resembling a man touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and spoke; I said to the one standing before me, “O my lord, because of the vision my anguish has overwhelmed me, and I have no strength.
How, then, can this servant of my lord speak with my lord? For now no strength remains in me, and no breath is left in me.”
Again one with the appearance of a man touched me and strengthened me.

He said, “Do not be afraid, O man greatly beloved. Peace be with you; be strong, yes, be very strong.” When he spoke to me, I was strengthened. And I said, “Speak, my lord, for you have strengthened me.”
Then he said, “Do you know why I have come to you? Now I will return to fight the prince of Persia, and when I leave, the prince of Greece will come.
But I will tell you what is inscribed in the book of truth, and no one strengthens me against these except Michael, your prince.”
In the first year of Darius the Mede, I arose to strengthen and fortify him.

Now I shall disclose to you the truth: three further kings will arise in Persia, and the fourth will amass wealth eclipsing all his predecessors; by the might of his riches he will rouse the whole realm against the kingdom of Greece.
Then a mighty king will emerge, wielding vast dominion and acting in accordance with his own volition.

Yet scarcely has he arisen before his kingdom is shattered and apportioned toward the four winds of heaven; it will not pass to his posterity, nor preserve the dominion he wielded, for his realm will be uprooted and conferred upon others.
The king of the South will wax powerful, yet one of his commanders will become still more formidable and govern a kingdom of vast extent.

After some years they will enter into an alliance, and the daughter of the king of the South will come to the king of the North to secure an equitable settlement; but she will not preserve her influence, nor will his power endure. She, together with her retinue, her child, and her partisan, will be surrendered.
Nevertheless, a descendant from her lineage will rise in his place, advance against the army, and penetrate the fortress of the king of the North; he will fight against them and prevail.
He will also carry off to Egypt their gods, together with their molten images and precious vessels of silver and gold; for several years he will refrain from assailing the king of the North.
Then the king of the North will invade the domain of the king of the South, but will withdraw to his own land.
His sons will wage war and muster an immense host—a multitude of troops that will advance like a deluge, overflow, and pass through; he will again wage war as far as his fortress.
The king of the South will be exasperated and march out to fight the king of the North, who will raise a great army, but it will be delivered into his hand.
When the multitude is carried away, the king of the South will be exalted, and he will cast down tens of thousands, yet he will not be victorious.
For the king of the North will return and raise a multitude greater than the first; after some years he will advance with a great army and abundant materiel.
In those times many will rise against the king of the South; violent men among your people will exalt themselves to fulfill a vision, but they will stumble.
Then the king of the North will come, erect a siege ramp, and capture a fortified city. The forces of the South will not stand; even its choicest troops will lack the strength to resist.
The invader will act according to his own pleasure, and no one will stand before him; he will establish himself in the Glorious Land, with ruin in his hand.

He will set his face to come with the strength of his entire kingdom, and upright allies with him; he will accomplish this, and give him a daughter in marriage to overthrow it, but she will not stand with him or belong to him.
Then he will turn his face toward the coastlands and capture many; but a commander will bring his insolence to an end and turn it back upon him.
He will turn his face back toward the strongholds of his own land, but he will stumble, fall, and be found no more.
In his place one will arise who will send an oppressor through the glorious kingdom; yet within a few days he will be broken, though not in open battle.
In his place a contemptible person will arise, upon whom royal splendor has not been conferred; he will come in a time of tranquility and seize the kingdom through intrigue.
Overwhelming forces will be swept away before him and shattered, together with the prince of the covenant.
After an alliance is made with him, he will act deceitfully and rise to power with a small following.

In a time of ease he will invade the richest provinces and do what neither his fathers nor his forefathers did; he will distribute plunder, spoil, and wealth among them, and he will devise plans against their strongholds—but only for a time.

He will stir up his power and courage with a great army against the king of the South, and the king of the South will wage war with an exceedingly great and mighty army, but he will not stand, because plots will be devised against him.
His own confidants will destroy him; his army will be swept away, and many will fall slain.
The two kings, with their hearts inclined to evil, will speak deceitfully at the same table, but it will come to nothing, for the end will still arrive at the appointed time.
He will return to his land with great wealth, but his heart will be set against the holy covenant; he will take action and then return to his own land.
At the appointed time he will invade the South again, but this time will not be like the first or the last.

Ships of Kittim will come against him, and he will lose heart; then he will turn back and vent his fury against the holy covenant, taking action. He will turn back and show favor to those who forsake the holy covenant.
Forces from him will arise, desecrate the sanctuary fortress, abolish the daily sacrifice, and set up the abomination that desolates.
With flattery he will corrupt those who violate the covenant, but the people who know their God will stand firm and act.
Those with insight will instruct many, though for a time they will fall by sword and flame, be taken captive, and be plundered.
In their stumbling they will receive a little help, and many will join them insincerely.
Some of the wise will fall, so that they may be refined, purified, and made spotless until the time of the end, for it is still for the appointed time.

Then the king will do as he pleases, exalt and magnify himself above every god, and speak astonishing things against the God of gods. He will prosper until the indignation is completed, for what is decreed will be done.
He will show no regard for the gods of his fathers, nor for the desire of women, nor for any god, for he will magnify himself above them all.
Instead, he will honor a god of fortresses—a god his fathers did not know—with gold, silver, precious stones, and valuables.
He will attack the strongest fortresses with the help of a foreign god; he will greatly honor those who acknowledge him, and he will distribute land at a price.

At the time of the end, the king of the South will engage him in battle, and the king of the North will storm against him with chariots, horsemen, and many ships. He will invade many countries and sweep through them like a flood.
He will also enter the Glorious Land, and many countries will fall, but Edom, Moab, and the leaders of the Ammonites will be delivered from his hand.
He will stretch out his hand against the countries, and the land of Egypt will not escape.
He will gain control of the hidden treasures of gold and silver and all the riches of Egypt, with the Libyans and Cushites in his train.
But reports from the east and the north will alarm him, and he will set out with great fury to destroy and annihilate many.
He will pitch his royal tent between the seas at the beautiful holy mountain; yet he will come to his end, and there will be no one to help him.

In that hour, Michael—the great prince who stands as guardian over the sons of your people—will arise; and there will be a time of distress such as has never occurred since nations first existed until that hour. Yet in that hour your people—every one found inscribed in the book—shall be delivered.
Multitudes who slumber in the dust of the earth will awaken: some to life everlasting, and others to shame and everlasting contempt.
The discerning will radiate like the splendor of the firmament, and those who lead many to righteousness will shine like the stars for ever and ever.
As for you, Daniel, conceal these words and seal the book until the time of the end; many will range to and fro, and knowledge will proliferate.
Then I, Daniel, looked and beheld two others standing—one on this bank of the river and one on the opposite bank.
One said to the man clothed in linen, who stood above the waters of the river, “Until when shall the consummation of these wonders be?”

The man clothed in linen, who stood above the waters of the river, raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven and swore by Him who lives forever that it would be for a time, times, and half a time, and that when the shattering of the power of the holy people had run its course, all these things would reach their consummation.
I heard, yet I did not comprehend; so I said, “My lord, what will be the latter end of these things?”
He said, “Proceed on your way, Daniel, for the words are sealed and shut up until the time of the end.”
Many will be purified, whitened, and refined; yet the wicked will persist in wickedness. None of the wicked will understand, but the discerning will understand.
From the moment the continual sacrifice is removed and the abomination of desolation is erected, there will be one thousand two hundred ninety days.
Blessed is the one who waits and attains to the one thousand three hundred thirty-fifth day.
As for you, proceed to the end; you will rest, and you will stand in your allotted inheritance at the end of the days.
The word of the LORD that came to Hosea, son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.

At the commencement of the LORD’s speaking through Hosea, the LORD said to Hosea, “Go, take for yourself a wife devoted to harlotry, together with children of harlotry, for the land itself has practiced egregious whoredom, forsaking the LORD.”
Accordingly, he went and took Gomer, daughter of Diblaim; and she conceived and bore him a son.
Then the LORD said to him, “Name him Jezreel, for in but a little while I will requite the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and I will terminate the kingdom of the house of Israel.
And on that day I will shatter the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel.”
She conceived again and bore a daughter. And He said to him, “Name her Lo-ruhamah, for I will no longer extend compassion to the house of Israel; indeed, I will not forgive them at all.
But I will have compassion upon the house of Judah, and I will deliver them by the LORD their God; I will not deliver them by bow, or by sword, or by warfare, or by horses, or by horsemen.”
When she had weaned Lo-ruhamah, she conceived again and bore a son.
And He said, “Name him Lo-ammi, for you are not My people, and I am not your God.”

Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, immeasurable and innumerable; and in the very place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ it shall be said to them, ‘Children of the living God.’

And the children of Judah and the children of Israel shall be gathered together, and they shall appoint for themselves one head, and they shall ascend from the land, for great shall be the day of Jezreel.
Tell your brothers, "You are My people," and your sisters, "You have been shown mercy."

Bring charges against your mother—bring charges—because she is no longer My wife, and I am no longer her husband. Let her remove her prostitution from her face and her adultery from between her breasts.
Otherwise I will strip her naked and expose her as on the day of her birth; I will make her like a desert, turn her into an arid wasteland, and slay her with thirst.
I will show no compassion to her children, for they are children of prostitution.

For their mother has prostituted herself; she who conceived them has acted shamefully. She said, "I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and water, my wool and flax, my oil and my beverages."
Therefore, behold, I will hedge her way with thorns; I will enclose her with a wall so that she cannot find her paths.
She will pursue her lovers but will not overtake them; she will seek them but will not find them. Then she will say, "I will go back to my first husband, for I was better off then than now."
Yet she did not know that I gave her grain, new wine, and oil, and lavished upon her silver and gold—wealth they then devoted to Baal.
Therefore I will take back My grain in its time and My new wine in its season; I will take away My wool and My flax that were given to cover her nakedness.
Now I will expose her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and no one will rescue her from My hand.
I will put an end to all her mirth—her festivals, her new moons, her Sabbaths, and all her appointed feasts.
I will destroy her vine and her fig tree, which she claimed as the wages her lovers had given her. I will turn them into a thicket, and the beasts of the field will devour them.
I will punish her for the days of the Baals, when she burned incense to them; she decked herself with rings and jewelry and went after her lovers, but Me she forgot," declares the the LORD.
Therefore, behold, I will allure her and lead her into the wilderness, and I will speak tenderly to her.
There I will give back her vineyards and make the Valley of Achor a door of hope. There she will respond as in the days of her youth, as in the day she came up from the land of Egypt.
"On that day," declares the the LORD, "you will call Me 'My Husband,' and you will no longer call Me 'My Master.'"
I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, and they will no longer be invoked.

On that day I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field, the birds of the air, and the creatures that crawl on the ground. I will abolish the bow, the sword, and war from the land, and I will make them lie down in safety.
I will betroth you to Me forever; I will betroth you to Me in righteousness and justice, in loving devotion and compassion.
I will betroth you to Me in faithfulness, and you will know the the LORD.
"On that day," declares the the LORD, "I will answer; I will answer the heavens, and they will answer the earth."
And the earth will respond to the grain, to the new wine and oil, and they will respond to Jezreel.
I will sow her for Myself in the land, and I will have compassion on "No Compassion," and I will say to "Not My People," "You are My people," and they will say, "You are my God."

The LORD said to me, "Go, love a woman who is still the beloved of a paramour and is an adulteress, even as the LORD loves the sons of Israel, though they turn toward other gods and are enamored of sacred raisin cakes."
So I acquired her for myself for fifteen shekels of silver, together with a homer and a lethech of barley.
And I said to her, "Remain with me for many days; you shall not be promiscuous, nor shall you belong to any man; and I, too, shall be yours."
For the sons of Israel shall dwell for many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or sacred pillar, and without ephod or household idols.
Afterward the sons of Israel shall return and seek the LORD their God and David their king; and they shall turn toward the LORD and toward His goodness with reverent dread in the latter days.
Hear the word of the LORD, O children of Israel, for the LORD has a case against the inhabitants of the land: “There is no truth, no steadfast love, and no knowledge of God in the land.”
Cursing, deception, murder, theft, and adultery proliferate, and bloodshed follows upon bloodshed.
Therefore the land mourns, and all who dwell in it languish; even the beasts of the field, the birds of the heavens, and the fish of the sea are swept away.
Yet let no one accuse, and let no one rebuke, for your people are like those who strive with the priest.
You will stumble in daylight, and the prophet will stumble with you by night; so I will destroy your mother.

My people are destroyed for want of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I reject you from serving as My priest; and because you have forgotten the law of your God, I will forget your children.
The more they multiplied, the more they sinned against Me; they exchanged their Glory for disgrace.
They feed upon the sin of My people and set their hearts upon iniquity.
So it shall be—like people, like priest: I will punish both alike for their ways and repay them according to their deeds.
They shall eat yet not be satisfied; they shall be promiscuous yet not multiply, because they have forsaken the LORD to devote themselves
to prostitution, to wine, and to new wine, which steal away understanding.
My people seek counsel from their wooden idols, and their divining rods answer them; for a spirit of prostitution has led them astray, and they have prostituted themselves against their God.

They offer sacrifices on the mountaintops and burn incense on the hills, beneath oak, poplar, and terebinth, because their shade is delightful; therefore your daughters prostitute themselves and your brides commit adultery.

I will not punish your daughters for their prostitution, nor your brides for their adultery, because the men themselves go aside with prostitutes and sacrifice with shrine prostitutes; thus a people without understanding is ruined.
Though you prostitute yourself, O Israel, let not Judah incur guilt. Do not go to Gilgal, do not ascend to Beth Aven, and do not swear, “As the LORD lives!”
For Israel is as stubborn as a refractory heifer; how, then, can the LORD shepherd them like a lamb in an open pasture?
Ephraim is bound to idols; let him alone.
Their drink is spent, then they turn to prostitution; their rulers dearly love disgrace.
The wind will wrap them in its wings, and their sacrifices will bring them to shame.
Hear this, O priests; attend, O house of Israel; give ear, O king—for judgment is upon you, because you have become a snare at Mizpah and a net spread over Tabor.
The rebels have sunk profoundly into slaughter, yet I remain a chastisement to them all.
I know Ephraim, and Israel is not concealed from Me; for now Ephraim has prostituted itself, and Israel is defiled.
Their deeds will not permit them to return to their God, for a spirit of promiscuity dwells within them, and they have no knowledge of the LORD.
Israel’s pride bears witness against him; Israel and Ephraim stumble in their iniquity, and Judah stumbles with them.
They go with their flocks and herds to seek the LORD, but they will not find Him; He has withdrawn from them.
They have dealt treacherously with the LORD; for they have begotten alien offspring. Now a single month will devour them together with their fields.
Sound the horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah; raise the battle cry in Beth-aven: “Behind you, Benjamin!”
Ephraim shall be desolate on the day of rebuke; among the tribes of Israel I have announced what is certain.
The princes of Judah are like those who displace boundary stones; I will pour out My wrath upon them like water.
Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment, because it willingly pursued a worthless decree.
I will be to Ephraim like a moth and to the house of Judah like rot.
When Ephraim perceived its sickness and Judah its wound, Ephraim went to Assyria and sent to the great king; yet he cannot heal you or cure your wound.
For I will be like a lion to Ephraim and like a young lion to the house of Judah; I Myself will tear and depart; I will carry away, and no one will rescue them.
I will go and return to My place until they acknowledge their guilt and seek My face; in their distress they will seek Me earnestly.
“Come, let us return to the LORD, for He has torn us, yet He will heal us; He has struck us, but He will bind us up.
After two days He will revive us; on the third day He will raise us up, that we may live in His presence.
Let us press on to know the LORD; His appearing is as certain as the dawn. He will come to us like the rains, like the spring showers that water the earth.”
“What shall I do with you, Ephraim? What shall I do with you, Judah? For your steadfast love is like a morning cloud, like the dew that vanishes at daybreak.
Therefore I have hewn them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of My mouth; and your judgments go forth like the light.
For I desire steadfast love rather than sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
But they, like Adam, transgressed the covenant; there they betrayed Me.”
Gilead is a city of evildoers, tracked with blood.
Like bandits lying in ambush for a man, so a company of priests murders along the road to Shechem, for they have committed an outrage.
“In the house of Israel I have seen an abomination: Ephraim's harlotry is there, and Israel is defiled.
And you too, Judah, have a harvest appointed for you, when I restore My people.”

Whenever I would bring healing to Israel, Ephraim's iniquity is disclosed and Samaria's depravities are uncovered; for they have perpetrated falsehood, and a thief breaks in, while a marauding band pillages the street.
Yet they do not reckon within their hearts that I remember all their evil; now their deeds have encircled them, and they stand exposed before My face.
They delight the king with their wickedness, and the princes with their falsehoods. “
They are all adulterers, resembling an oven heated by the baker, who ceases stoking from the kneading of the dough until it is leavened.
On the day of our king, the princes became inflamed with wine, and he stretched forth his hand in fellowship with scoffers.
For they have drawn near with hearts like an oven, while they lie in ambush; all night their baker slumbers, and by morning it blazes like a flaming fire.
They are all hot as an oven, and they devour their rulers; all their kings have fallen; there is none among them who calls upon Me. “
Ephraim mingles among the nations; Ephraim has become a cake left unturned—half-baked and worthless.
Foreigners have consumed his vigor, yet he does not know it; gray hairs are sprinkled upon him, yet he remains unaware.
Israel's arrogance bears witness against him; yet they have not returned to the the LORD their God, nor have they sought Him in all this.
Ephraim has become like a gullible dove, devoid of understanding; they call to Egypt, they make their way to Assyria. “
When they go, I will spread My net over them; I will bring them down like the birds of heaven; I will chastise them in accordance with the report given to their assembly.
Woe to them, for they have strayed from Me; ruin to them, for they have rebelled against Me! Though I would redeem them, they speak falsehoods against Me.
They do not cry out to Me from their hearts, but they wail upon their beds; for grain and new wine they slash themselves; they turn away from Me.
I indeed trained and strengthened their arms, yet they devise evil against Me.
They turn, but not to the Most High; they are like a faulty bow. Their leaders shall fall by the sword because of the insolence of their tongue; this shall be their mockery in the land of Egypt.”
Put the trumpet to your lips! Like an eagle swooping over the house of the LORD, because they have transgressed My covenant and rebelled against My law.
Israel cries out to Me, “My God, we know You!”
Yet Israel has rejected what is good, and an enemy shall pursue him.
They have set up kings, but not by Me; they have appointed princes, yet I did not acknowledge them. With their silver and gold they have fashioned idols for themselves, that they might be cut off.
Your calf, O Samaria, is rejected; My wrath burns against them. How long will they remain incapable of innocence?
For it is from Israel; a craftsman made it, and it is not God. It shall be broken to pieces—that calf of Samaria.
For they sow empty wind and reap a tempest of ruin; the standing grain has no heads and yields no flour. Should it produce, strangers would devour it.
Israel is swallowed up; now it is among the nations like a vessel in which no one delights.
For they have gone up to Assyria, like a wild donkey wandering alone; Ephraim has purchased alliances.
Though they traffic among the nations, I shall now gather them, and they shall begin to diminish beneath the burden of the king of princes.
Because Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning, those altars have become to him occasions for sin.
Though I wrote for him the great things of My law, they were regarded as something foreign.
They sacrifice flesh and eat it, but the LORD does not accept them. Now He will remember their iniquity and punish their sins; they shall return to Egypt.
For Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces; Judah too has multiplied fortified cities. But I will send fire upon his cities, and it shall consume his citadels.
Do not exult, O Israel, after the manner of the nations, for you have been unfaithful to your God; you have set your affection upon a harlot’s hire upon every threshing floor of grain.
Neither threshing floor nor winepress shall nourish them, and the new wine shall prove false to them.
They shall not remain in the land of the LORD; Ephraim shall return to Egypt, and in Assyria they shall consume that which is unclean.

They shall not pour out wine offerings to the LORD, nor shall their sacrifices be acceptable to Him. Their bread shall be as the bread of mourners; all who partake of it shall be defiled, for their bread is for their own sustenance and shall not enter the house of the LORD.
What will you do on the day of the appointed festival, on the day of the LORD’s feast?

For behold, they have departed because of devastation; Egypt shall gather them, and Memphis shall bury them. Their cherished silver shall be inherited by nettles, and thorns shall dwell in their tents.

The days of visitation have arrived, the days of recompense have arrived; Israel shall know it. The prophet is a fool, and the man of the spirit is mad, because of the magnitude of your iniquity and the abundance of your hostility.
Ephraim’s prophet is a watchman with my God, yet a snare of the fowler is upon all his ways, and hostility is in the house of his God.
They have sunk to the depths of corruption, as in the days of Gibeah; He will remember their iniquity and visit their sins upon them.

I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness; I beheld your fathers as the first-ripe fruit upon the fig tree in its first season. But they went to Baal-peor and consecrated themselves to Shame, and became abominations in proportion to their love.
Ephraim’s glory shall take wing like a bird—no birth, no pregnancy, no conception.
Even if they rear their children, I will bereave them of every one; yes, woe to them when I withdraw from them.
I have seen Ephraim, like Tyre, planted in a pleasant place; yet Ephraim shall lead forth his children to the slayer.
Give them, O LORD—what shall You give? Give them a womb that miscarries and breasts that yield no milk.
All their wickedness is in Gilgal, for there I hated them. On account of the evil of their deeds I will expel them from My house; I will no longer love them; all their princes are rebels.
Ephraim is stricken; their root has dried up; they shall produce no fruit. Even if they beget children, I will put to death the darlings of their womb.
My God will reject them, because they have not hearkened to Him; they shall become wanderers among the nations.
Israel is a luxuriant vine that bears fruit for itself; as its harvest multiplied, it multiplied altars in like measure, and as its land flourished, it made its sacred pillars ever more splendid.
Their hearts are divided; now they must bear their guilt. He will break down their altars and shatter their sacred pillars.
For now they will say, “We have no king, because we did not fear the LORD. What, then, could a king do for us?”
They utter empty words and make covenants by false oaths, so justice springs up like hemlock in the furrows of a field.
The inhabitants of Samaria will dread the calves of Beth-aven, for their people mourn over the idol, while its priests exult over its glory, since it has been carried away from them.
It too will be carried off to Assyria as tribute to the great king. Ephraim will be seized with shame, and Israel will be put to shame by its own counsel.
Samaria’s king will be cut off like foam upon the water.
The high places of Aven will be destroyed—the very sin of Israel. Thorns and thistles will overrun their altars, and they will cry to the mountains, “Cover us!” and to the hills, “Fall upon us!”
Since the days of Gibeah, O Israel, you have sinned, and there you have remained. Will not war at Gibeah overtake the sons of iniquity?
I will discipline them at My pleasure; nations will be gathered against them to bind them for their double transgression.
Ephraim is a trained heifer that loves to thresh; so I will put a yoke on her fair neck. I will harness Ephraim; Judah will plow, and Jacob will break up his fallow ground.
Sow righteousness for yourselves, reap according to steadfast love; break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek the LORD, until He comes and rains righteousness upon you.
You have plowed wickedness and reaped injustice; you have eaten the fruit of lies. Because you have trusted in your own way and in your many warriors,
a tumult will rise among your people, and all your fortresses will be devastated—as Shalman devastated Beth-arbel on the day of battle, when mothers were dashed to pieces along with their children.
Thus it will be done to you, O Bethel, because of your wickedness. At dawn the king of Israel will be utterly cut off.
When Israel was yet in its youth, I loved him, and out of Egypt I summoned My son.
They were summoned, yet they withdrew from those who summoned them; they sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to carved images.
Nevertheless, it was I who instructed Ephraim to walk, lifting him upon My arms; yet he failed to recognize that I was his healer.
I drew them with human cords, with bonds of love; I was to them as one who removes the yoke from the jaw; I stooped toward him and nourished him. “
He shall not return to the land of Egypt; rather, Assyria shall be his sovereign, because they refused to turn back.
The sword shall whirl through his cities, consuming their fortifications and devouring them because of their own counsels.
My people are resolutely bent upon apostasy from Me; though they cry out to the Most High, not one truly exalts Him. “
How could I surrender you, Ephraim? How could I give up you, Israel? How could I render you as Admah, or appoint you as Zeboiim? My heart turns within Me, and My compassions are kindled in concert.
I will not execute the heat of My anger; I will not again bring Ephraim to ruin, for I am God and not a man—the Holy One in your midst—and I will not come upon them in wrath. “
They shall follow the LORD, who will roar like a lion; when He roars, the children shall come trembling from the west.
They shall flutter like a bird from Egypt, and like a dove from the land of Assyria; and I will cause them to dwell in their homes, declares the LORD.
Ephraim has encircled Me with deceit, and the house of Israel with treachery; yet Judah still walks with God and remains faithful among the holy ones.”
Ephraim feeds on the wind and pursues the east wind; all day long he multiplies lies and violence. They make a covenant with Assyria, and oil is carried down to Egypt.
The LORD has an indictment against Judah, and He will punish Jacob according to his ways; according to his deeds He will repay him.
In the womb he seized his brother's heel, and in his vigor he contended with God.
He wrestled with the angel and prevailed; he wept and pleaded with Him. He found Him at Bethel, and there He spoke with us.
And the LORD God of Hosts—the the LORD is His memorial name.
So you, return to your God; keep steadfast love and justice, and wait continually for your God.
Canaan is a merchant; fraudulent balances are in his hand, and he loves to oppress.
Ephraim says, “Surely I have grown rich; I have amassed wealth for myself. In all my toil, no one will find in me any iniquity that constitutes sin.”
But I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt; I will again make you dwell in tents, as in the days of the appointed feast.
I have spoken to the prophets, and I have multiplied visions; and through the prophets I have set forth parables.
Is there iniquity in Gilead? They are indeed worthless. In Gilgal they sacrifice bulls, and their altars are like heaps of stones in the furrows of a field.
Jacob fled to the country of Aram; Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he tended sheep.
By a prophet the LORD brought Israel up out of Egypt, and by a prophet he was preserved.
Ephraim has provoked Him to bitter anger; therefore his bloodguilt shall remain upon him, and his Lord will repay him his reproach.
When Ephraim spoke, trembling ensued; he exalted himself in Israel, yet he incurred guilt through Baal and perished.
And now they add sin to sin, fashioning for themselves molten idols—skillfully wrought images of silver, the handiwork of artisans—and they declare, “Let those who offer sacrifice kiss the calves!”
Therefore they shall be like the morning cloud and like the dew that vanishes early, like chaff whirled from the threshing floor and like smoke from a window.
Yet I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt; you shall know no God but Me, and no Savior besides Me.
I knew you in the wilderness, in the land of drought.
When they had pasture, they were satisfied; when satisfied, their hearts grew proud; therefore they forgot Me.
So I will be to them like a lion; like a leopard I will lurk beside the road.
I will confront them like a bear robbed of her cubs; I will tear open the enclosure of their hearts; there I will devour them like a lion, and the beast of the field shall maul them.
Your destruction, O Israel, is that you are against Me—against your Helper.
Where, then, is your king, that he may save you in all your cities? And where are your judges, to whom you said, “Give me a king and princes”?
In My anger I gave you a king, and in My wrath I took him away.
Ephraim's iniquity is bound up; his sin is treasured up.
The pangs of childbirth seize him, yet he is an unwise son; for when the time comes, he does not present himself at the mouth of the womb.
I will ransom them from the hand of Sheol; I will redeem them from Death. O Death, I will be your plague; O Sheol, I will be your destruction; compassion is hidden from My eyes.

Though he may flourish among his brothers, an east wind will come—the wind of the LORD rising from the wilderness—so that his spring dries up and his fountain is parched; it will plunder the treasury of every precious thing.
Samaria shall be held guilty, because she has rebelled against her God; they shall fall by the sword; their little ones shall be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women shall be ripped open.
Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God, for you have stumbled through your iniquity.
Take words with you and return to the LORD. Say to Him, “Take away all iniquity, accept what is good, and we will offer the sacrifices of our lips.”
Assyria will not save us; we will not ride upon horses. Nor will we any longer call the work of our hands our god, for in You the fatherless finds mercy.
I will heal their apostasy; I will love them freely, for My anger has turned away from him.
I will be like the dew to Israel; he will blossom like the lily and take root like the cedars of Lebanon.
His shoots will spread; his splendor will be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like the cedars of Lebanon.
They will return and dwell in his shade; they will revive like grain and blossom like the vine. His renown will be like the wine of Lebanon.
Ephraim, what more have I to do with idols? I will answer and watch over him. I am like a green cypress; from Me comes your fruit.
Who is wise? Let him understand these things. Who is discerning? Let him know them. For the ways of the LORD are right, and the righteous walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them.
The word of the LORD that came to Joel, son of Pethuel.
Hear this, O elders, and give ear, all you inhabitants of the land: has anything comparable occurred in your days, or in the days of your fathers?
Recount it to your children, and let your children recount it to their children, and their children to another generation.

What the cutting locust has left, the swarming locust has devoured; what the swarming locust has left, the hopping locust has devoured; and what the hopping locust has left, the destroying locust has devoured.
Awake, you drunkards, and weep; wail, all you drinkers of wine, over the new wine, for it is snatched from your mouths.
For a nation has ascended against my land—mighty and beyond number—whose teeth are the teeth of a lion and whose fangs are those of a lioness.
It has made my vine a desolation and splintered my fig tree; it has stripped it utterly bare and cast it away, so that its branches are whitened.
Lament as a virgin girded in sackcloth for the bridegroom of her youth.
The grain offering and the libation are cut off from the house of the LORD; the priests mourn, the ministers of the LORD.
The field is ravaged, the soil mourns, because the grain is ruined, the new wine is withered, and the oil languishes.
Be confounded, you farmers; wail, you vinedressers, over the wheat and the barley, for the harvest of the field has perished.
The vine is withered, the fig tree languishes; the pomegranate, the palm, and the apple—indeed, all the trees of the field are dried up—because gladness is withered from the children of men.

Gird yourselves and lament, you priests; wail, you ministers of the altar. Come, spend the night in sackcloth, you ministers of my God, for the grain offering and the libation are withheld from the house of your God.
Sanctify a fast, proclaim a solemn assembly; gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land into the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.
Alas for the day! For the day of the LORD is near, and as devastation from the Almighty it comes.
Is not the food cut off before our eyes—gladness and joy from the house of our God?
The seed shrivels beneath their clods; the storehouses are desolate; the granaries are broken down, because the grain is withered.
How the beasts groan! The herds of oxen are bewildered, for they have no pasture; indeed, the flocks of sheep are made desolate.
To you, the LORD, I cry, for fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and flame has scorched all the trees of the field.
Even the beasts of the field pant after you, for the watercourses are dried up, and fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness.
Sound the shofar in Zion, and raise the alarm on My holy mountain; let all who dwell in the land tremble, for the Day of the LORD is coming—it is near.

It is a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness; like dawn spread over the mountains, there comes a great and mighty people, the like of which has not been from of old and will not be again after them through the generations.
Before them a fire devours, and behind them a flame blazes; the land before them is like the garden of Eden, but behind them a desolate waste, and nothing escapes them.
Their appearance is like that of horses, and like cavalry they charge.
Like the rumbling of chariots they leap upon the mountaintops, like the crackling of a fire consuming stubble, like a mighty army drawn up for battle.
Before them peoples writhe in anguish, and every countenance grows pale.
They charge like warriors; they scale walls like soldiers; each advances along his own course, and they do not break ranks.
They do not crowd one another; each proceeds along his own path; they burst through the defenses without being halted.
They surge into the city; they run along the walls; they climb into the houses; they enter through the windows like a thief.
Before them the earth quakes and the heavens tremble; the sun and moon grow dark, and the stars withdraw their light.
The LORD gives voice before His army, for His camp is exceedingly great and mighty in executing His word. Indeed, the Day of the LORD is great and exceedingly dreadful—who can endure it?
“Even now,” declares the LORD, “return to Me with all your heart, with fasting, weeping, and mourning.”
Rend your hearts and not your garments, and return to the LORD your God, for He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion, and He relents from sending calamity.
Who knows? He may turn and relent and leave behind Him a blessing—grain and drink offerings for the LORD your God.
Blow the trumpet in Zion; consecrate a fast; proclaim a solemn assembly.
Gather the people; sanctify the congregation; assemble the elders; gather the children and nursing infants. Let the bridegroom come out of his chamber and the bride from her canopy.

Let the priests, the ministers of the LORD, weep between the portico and the altar, and let them say: “Spare Your people, O LORD, and do not make Your inheritance a reproach, a byword among the nations. Why should they say among the peoples, ‘Where is their God?’”
Then the LORD will be jealous for His land and take pity on His people.
The LORD will answer and say to His people: “Behold, I am sending you grain, new wine, and oil, and you will be satisfied; I will never again make you a reproach among the nations.

I will drive the northern army far from you, banishing it to a barren and desolate land, its vanguard to the eastern sea and its rearguard to the western sea. Its stench will rise; its foul odor will ascend, for it has done great things.”
Do not be afraid, O land; rejoice and be glad, for the LORD has done great things.
Do not be afraid, O beasts of the field, for the pastures of the wilderness are green; the trees bear their fruit; the fig tree and vine yield their full strength.
Be glad, O children of Zion, and rejoice in the LORD your God, for He has given you the autumn rain in righteousness; He has poured down for you the rain, the autumn and spring rains, as before.
The threshing floors will be full of grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.
