“I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten—the young locust, the destroying locust, and the consuming locust—My great army that I sent among you.
You will eat in plenty and be satisfied, and you will praise the Name of the LORD your God, who has dealt wondrously with you; My people will never again be put to shame.
Then you will know that I am in the midst of Israel, that I am the LORD your God and there is no other; My people will never again be put to shame.”
“And afterward I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh; your sons and daughters will prophesy, your old men will dream dreams, and your young men will see visions.
Even on the male and female servants I will pour out My Spirit in those days.
I will show wonders in the heavens and on the earth—blood, fire, and columns of smoke.
The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the coming of the great and dreadful Day of the LORD.

And it will come to pass that everyone who calls on the Name of the LORD will be saved, for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, as the LORD has said, among the survivors whom the LORD calls.”
For behold, in those days and at that very time, when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem—

I shall gather all the nations and conduct them down into the Valley of Jehoshaphat, and there I shall contend with them in judgment on behalf of My people and My inheritance, Israel, whom they dispersed among the nations and whose land they partitioned.
They cast lots for My people; they bartered a boy for a harlot’s hire and sold a girl for wine, which they then drank.
And what claim have you upon Me, O Tyre and Sidon, and all the districts of Philistia? Are you requiting Me? If you are requiting Me, I shall swiftly return your recompense upon your own heads.
For you appropriated My silver and My gold, and conveyed My choicest treasures into your temples.
You sold the sons of Judah and the sons of Jerusalem to the Greeks, so as to exile them far from their native territory.
Behold, I shall rouse them from the place to which you sold them, and I shall return your recompense upon your own heads.
Moreover, I shall sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the sons of Judah, and they shall sell them to the Sabeans, to a nation far away, for the LORD has spoken.
Proclaim this among the nations: Consecrate a war; awaken the mighty men; let all the men of war draw near and ascend.
Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears; let even the weakling declare, “I am a mighty man.”
Hasten and come, all you nations from every side, and gather yourselves there. Bring down Your mighty ones, O the LORD.
Let the nations rouse themselves and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I shall sit in judgment over all the surrounding nations.
Put in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe; come and tread the grapes, for the winepress is full and the vats overflow, because their wickedness is great.
Multitudes, multitudes in the Valley of Decision! For the day of the LORD is near in the Valley of Decision.
The sun and the moon are darkened, and the stars withhold their radiance.
The LORD roars from Zion and utters His voice from Jerusalem, so that the heavens and the earth quake. Yet the LORD is a refuge for His people and a stronghold for the sons of Israel.
Thus you shall know that I am the LORD your God, dwelling in Zion, My holy mountain. Jerusalem shall be holy, and no stranger shall ever again pass through her.

And in that day the mountains shall drip with new wine, the hills shall flow with milk, and all the streambeds of Judah shall run with water; a fountain shall issue from the house of the LORD and irrigate the Valley of Shittim.
Egypt shall become a desolation, and Edom a desolate wilderness, because of the violence done to the sons of Judah, in whose land they shed innocent blood.
But Judah shall abide forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
I shall avenge their blood, blood that I have not yet avenged, for the LORD dwells in Zion.

The words of Amos, who was among the shepherds of Tekoa, which he beheld concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel—two years before the earthquake.
And he said, “The LORD roars from Zion and utters His voice from Jerusalem; the pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the summit of Carmel withers.”
Thus says the LORD: “For three transgressions of Damascus—and indeed for four—I will not revoke its punishment, because they threshed Gilead with iron threshing sledges.
So I will send fire into the house of Hazael, and it will devour the citadels of Ben-hadad.
I will shatter the gate-bar of Damascus, cut off the inhabitant from the Valley of Aven, and the scepter-bearer from Beth-eden; and the people of Aram shall be exiled to Kir,” declares the LORD.
Thus says the LORD: “For three transgressions of Gaza—and indeed for four—I will not revoke its punishment, because they deported an entire population in order to hand them over to Edom.
So I will send fire against the wall of Gaza, and it will consume her citadels.
I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod and the scepter-bearer from Ashkelon; I will turn My hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish,” declares the Lord the LORD.

Thus says the LORD: “For three transgressions of Tyre—and indeed for four—I will not revoke its punishment, because they delivered up an entire captivity to Edom and did not remember the covenant of brotherhood.
So I will send fire against the wall of Tyre, and it will consume her citadels,” declares the LORD.

Thus says the LORD: “For three transgressions of Edom—and indeed for four—I will not revoke its punishment, because he pursued his brother with the sword and stifled his compassion; his anger raged continually, and his wrath he nursed forever.
So I will send fire upon Teman, and it will devour the palaces of Bozrah,” declares the LORD.

Thus says the LORD: “For three transgressions of the Ammonites—and indeed for four—I will not revoke its punishment, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead in order to enlarge their territory.
So I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it will devour her palaces, amid shouting on the day of battle and a storm on the day of the whirlwind.
And their king shall go into exile, he and his princes together,” declares the LORD.
Thus says the LORD: "For three transgressions of Moab, and even for four, I will not revoke My judgment, because he burned the bones of Edom's king to lime.
I will send fire into Moab, and it shall devour the strongholds of Kerioth; Moab shall perish amid tumult, amid shouting, and amid the sound of the trumpet.
I will cut off the ruler from its midst, and I will slay all its officials together with him," declares the LORD.

Thus says the LORD: "For three transgressions of Judah, and even for four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they rejected the law of the LORD and did not keep His statutes, but their lies led them astray—the very falsehoods their ancestors followed.
I will send fire upon Judah, and it shall consume the palaces of Jerusalem."
Thus says the LORD: "For three transgressions of Israel, and even for four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they sell the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals.
They trample the heads of the poor into the dust of the earth and pervert the way of the humble; a man and his father consort with the same young woman, thereby profaning My holy name.
They recline beside every altar upon garments taken in pledge, and in the house of their god they drink wine exacted as fines."
"Yet I destroyed the Amorite before them, whose stature was like that of cedars and whose strength was like that of oaks; I destroyed his fruit from above and his roots from below.
I brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you forty years through the wilderness, to take possession of the land of the Amorite.
I raised up prophets from among your sons and Nazirites from among your young men. Is it not so, O children of Israel?" declares the LORD.
"But you made the Nazirites drink wine and commanded the prophets, 'You shall not prophesy.'"
"Behold, I will crush you in your place, as a cart laden with sheaves crushes.
Flight will be lost to the swift, the strong shall not retain his strength, and the mighty shall not save his life.
The archer shall not stand, the swift-footed shall not escape, and the horseman shall not save his life.
The stout-hearted among the mighty shall flee naked on that day," declares the LORD.
Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, O children of Israel, concerning the whole family that I brought up out of the land of Egypt, saying:
“You only have I known of all the families of the earth; therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities.”
Can two walk together unless they have agreed to meet?
Does a lion roar in the forest when it has no prey? Does a young lion give voice from its den unless it has made a catch?
Does a bird fall to the ground where no snare has been set for it? Does a trap spring up from the earth without securing a catch?
If a trumpet is sounded in a city, do not the people tremble? If calamity befalls a city, has not the LORD accomplished it?
Surely the Lord GOD does nothing without revealing His secret to His servants the prophets.
The lion has roared—who then will not fear? The Lord GOD has spoken—who then will not prophesy?

Proclaim upon the palaces of Ashdod and upon the palaces of the land of Egypt, and say, “Assemble yourselves upon the mountains of Samaria, and behold the great tumult within her and the oppressions in her midst.”
For they do not know how to do what is right, declares the LORD, those who store up violence and plunder in their palaces.
Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: An adversary shall encircle the land and strip you of your strength, and your palaces shall be plundered.

Thus says the LORD: “As a shepherd rescues from the mouth of the lion two legs or a piece of an ear, so the children of Israel who dwell in Samaria shall be rescued—with nothing more than the corner of a bed and a couch in Damascus.”
Hear and bear witness against the house of Jacob, declares the Lord GOD, the God of Hosts:
“On the day that I punish Israel for its transgressions, I will also punish the altars of Bethel; the horns of the altar shall be cut off and fall to the ground.
I will strike the winter house together with the summer house; the houses of ivory shall perish, and many houses shall vanish, declares the LORD.”
Hear this word, you indulgent matrons of Bashan on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor and crush the needy, who say to their lords, “Bring, and let us drink.”
The Lord, the the LORD, has sworn by His holiness: “Surely the days are coming upon you when they will take you away with hooks, and your posterity with fishhooks.
You will go out through the breaches, each woman straight before her, and you will be cast toward Harmon,” declares the the LORD.
“Come to Bethel and transgress; to Gilgal multiply transgression; bring your sacrifices in the morning, your tithes every three days.
Burn a thank offering of leaven, and proclaim freewill offerings—announce them! For this is what you love, O children of Israel,” declares the Lord, the the LORD.
“I also gave you famine in all your cities, and lack of bread in all your places; yet you did not return to Me,” declares the the LORD.

“I also withheld rain from you when three months yet remained before the harvest; I caused rain to fall on one city and withheld it from another; one field was rained upon, while the field on which it did not rain withered,” declares the the LORD.
“So two or three cities wandered to another city to drink water, but were not satisfied; yet you did not return to Me,” declares the the LORD.
“I struck you with blight and mildew; the locust devoured the abundance of your gardens and vineyards, your fig trees and your olive trees; yet you did not return to Me,” declares the the LORD.

“I sent among you a pestilence after the manner of Egypt; I killed your young men with the sword, along with your captured horses; I made the stench of your camps rise in your nostrils; yet you did not return to Me,” declares the the LORD.
“I overturned you as God overturned Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a brand plucked from the burning; yet you did not return to Me,” declares the the LORD.
“Therefore thus I will do to you, O Israel; and because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, O Israel!

For behold, He who forms the mountains and creates the wind, who declares to man what is his thought, who makes the morning darkness, and treads upon the high places of the earth—the the LORD, the God of hosts, is His name.”
Hear this word, O house of Israel—this dirge that I raise over you:
“Fallen is Virgin Israel; she shall rise no more. She lies forsaken upon her own land, and there is no one to raise her up.”
For thus says the Lord, the LORD: “The city that marches out a thousand strong shall have a hundred left, and the one that marches out a hundred strong shall have ten left to the house of Israel.”
For thus says the LORD to the house of Israel: “Seek Me, and you shall live.
Do not seek Bethel, nor enter Gilgal, nor cross over to Beersheba; for Gilgal shall surely go into exile, and Bethel shall come to nothing.”
Seek the LORD and live, lest He break out like fire in the house of Joseph and devour it, with no one to quench it for Bethel.
You who turn justice into wormwood and cast righteousness to the ground!

He who made the Pleiades and Orion, who turns deep darkness into morning and darkens day into night, who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out upon the face of the earth—the LORD is His name.
He flashes forth destruction against the strong, so that devastation comes upon the fortress.
You hate the one who reproves in the gate and abhor the one who speaks with integrity.

Therefore, because you trample on the poor and exact a tax of grain from him, though you have built houses of hewn stone, you shall not dwell in them; though you have planted pleasant vineyards, you shall not drink their wine.
For I know how many are your transgressions and how great are your sins—you who oppress the righteous, take bribes, and thrust aside the needy in the gate.
Therefore the prudent keep silent in such a time, for it is an evil time.
Seek good and not evil, that you may live; and so the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be with you, just as you say.
Hate evil and love good, and establish justice in the gate; perhaps the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.

Therefore thus says the LORD, the God of Hosts, the Lord: “There shall be wailing in all the squares, and in all the streets they shall cry, ‘Alas! Alas!’ They shall call the farmers to mourning and those skilled in lamentation to wailing.
In all the vineyards there shall be wailing, for I will pass through your midst,” says the LORD.
Woe to you who long for the Day of the LORD! Why do you long for the Day of the LORD? It is darkness and not light.
It will be as when a man flees from a lion and a bear meets him, or when he goes into the house and leans his hand against the wall and a serpent bites him.
Is not the Day of the LORD darkness and not light—gloom without any brightness?
“I hate, I despise your feasts, and I take no delight in your solemn assemblies.
Even though you offer Me burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them; and the peace offerings of your fattened cattle I will not regard.
Take away from Me the noise of your songs; to the melody of your harps I will not listen.
But let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.
Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness for forty years, O house of Israel?
You have lifted up Sikkuth, your king, and Kiyyun, your star god—images that you made for yourselves.
Therefore I will exile you beyond Damascus,” says the LORD, whose name is the God of Hosts.
Woe to those who are at ease in Zion and to those who feel secure on Mount Samaria—the distinguished of the foremost nation, to whom the house of Israel comes.
Cross over to Calneh and see; go from there to great Hamath; then descend to Gath of the Philistines. Are those realms superior to these, or is their territory more expansive than your own?
You defer the day of disaster and draw near a seat of violence.
You who recline on ivory couches and sprawl upon your divans, eating lambs from the flock and fattened calves from the stall,
who strum idle melodies on the harp and devise songs for yourselves as David did,
who drink wine from bowls and anoint yourselves with the choicest oils, yet feel no anguish over the ruin of Joseph.
Therefore they shall now be led away at the head of the exiles, and the carousing of the self-indulgent shall pass away.
The Lord the LORD has sworn by Himself—the the LORD, the God of Hosts, declares: "I abhor the arrogance of Jacob and hate his palaces; I will surrender the city and all that fills it."
If ten men remain in a single house, they shall die.

When a relative or the one who burns him carries the bones out of the house and says to the one in the inner chamber, "Is anyone still with you?" When he answers, "No," the relative will say, "Hush! For the name of the the LORD is not to be invoked."
For behold, the the LORD commands, and He will strike the great house into fragments and the small house into cracks.
Do horses run on rock? Does one plow there with oxen? Yet you have turned justice into venom and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood.
You who exult in emptiness, boasting, "Have we not gained power by our own strength?"
For behold, I am raising up a nation against you, O house of Israel, declares the the LORD, the God of Hosts, and they shall oppress you from the entrance of Hamath to the Brook of the Arabah.
Thus the Lord the LORD showed me: behold, He was fashioning locusts at the commencement of the latter growth's springing up; and behold, it was the latter growth after the king's mowings.
When they had finished devouring the grass of the land, I said, "O Lord the LORD, forgive, I beseech You! How can Jacob endure? For he is small."
The LORD relented concerning this: "It shall not be," said the LORD.
Thus the Lord the LORD showed me: behold, the Lord the LORD was calling for judgment by fire, and it consumed the great deep and devoured the allotted portion.
And I said, "O Lord the LORD, desist, I beseech You! How can Jacob endure? For he is small."
The LORD relented concerning this: "This also shall not be," said the Lord the LORD.
Thus He showed me, and behold, the Lord was standing by a wall constructed with a plumb line, with a plumb line in His hand.

And the the LORD said to me, "Amos, what do you see?" And I said, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "Behold, I am setting a plumb line in the midst of My people Israel; I will not pass by him again.
The high places of Isaac shall be desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword."
Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, "Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel; the land cannot endure all his words.
For thus Amos says, 'Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely go into exile from its land.'"
And Amaziah said to Amos, "O seer, go, flee to the land of Judah, and eat bread there, and prophesy there.
But never again prophesy at Bethel, for it is the king's sanctuary and a royal residence."
Then Amos answered and said to Amaziah, "I was not a prophet, nor was I a prophet's son; but I was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore figs.
And the the LORD took me from following the flock, and the the LORD said to me, 'Go, prophesy to My people Israel.'"
Now therefore hear the word of the the LORD: You say, "Do not prophesy against Israel, and do not speak against the house of Isaac."

Therefore thus says the the LORD: 'Your wife shall play the harlot in the city, and your sons and your daughters shall fall by the sword, and your land shall be divided by a measuring line, and you shall die in an unclean land; and Israel shall surely go into exile from its land.'"
This is what the Lord the LORD showed me: Behold, a basket of summer fruit.
He said, "Amos, what do you see?" I said, "A basket of summer fruit." Then the LORD said to me, "The end has come upon My people Israel; I will not spare them any longer."
"In that day," declares the Lord the LORD, "the songs of the temple will become wailings; many will be the dead bodies—cast out in every place. Silence!"
Hear this, you who trample the needy and bring the humble of the land to ruin,

saying, "When will the new moon be over, that we may sell grain? And the Sabbath, that we may put the wheat up for sale?—making the ephah small and the shekel large, and falsifying the scales with deceit—
so that we may buy the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, and sell the sweepings of the wheat?"
the LORD has sworn by the Pride of Jacob: "Surely I will never forget any of their deeds."
Will not the land tremble on account of this, and every inhabitant mourn? Indeed, all of it will rise like the Nile, surge, and subside again, like the river of Egypt.
"And on that day," declares the Lord the LORD, "I will make the sun set at noon and darken the land in broad daylight.

I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into dirges; I will put sackcloth on every waist and baldness on every head; I will make it like mourning for an only child, and its end like a bitter day."
"Behold, days are coming," declares the Lord the LORD, "when I will send a famine upon the land—not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD.
They will wander from sea to sea and from north to east; they will rove about seeking the word of the LORD, but they will not find it."
In that day the beautiful young women and the young men will faint from thirst.
Those who swear by the shame of Samaria and say, "As your god lives, O Dan," and, "As the way of Beersheba lives"—they will fall, never to rise again.

I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and He said, “Strike the tops of the pillars so that the thresholds shake, and shatter them on the heads of all; the rest of them I will slay with the sword. No one who flees will get away, and no survivor will escape them.
If they dig into Sheol, from there My hand will take them; if they climb to heaven, from there I will bring them down.

If they hide on the summit of Carmel, from there I will search and seize them; if they conceal themselves from My sight in the depths of the sea, from there I will command the serpent, and it will bite them.
If they go into captivity before their enemies, from there I will command the sword to slay them. I will fix My eyes upon them for evil and not for good.”
The Lord, the LORD of Hosts—He who touches the earth and it melts, and all who dwell in it mourn; it rises like the Nile and sinks like the Nile of Egypt—
He who builds His upper chambers in the heavens and founds His vault upon the earth, who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out over the face of the earth—the LORD is His name.
“Are you not like the Cushites to Me, O children of Israel?” declares the LORD. “Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Arameans from Kir?”
“Behold, the eyes of the Lord, the LORD, are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the face of the earth; yet I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,” declares the LORD.
“For behold, I am giving the command, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations as grain is sifted in a sieve, yet not a pebble will fall to the ground.
All the sinners among My people will die by the sword—those who say, ‘Disaster will not overtake us or confront us.’
“In that day I will raise up the fallen tent of David; I will repair its breaches, raise up its ruins, and rebuild it as in the days of old,
so that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations that are called by My name,” declares the LORD, “who will do this.

Behold, the days are coming,” declares the LORD, “when the harvest will be so abundant that the plowman will overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes the sower of seed; the mountains will drip with sweet wine, and all the hills will flow with it.
I will restore the fortunes of My people Israel; they will rebuild the ruined cities and inhabit them, plant vineyards and drink their wine, make gardens and eat their fruit.
I will plant them on their own land, and they will never again be uprooted from the land I have given them,” says the LORD your God.

The vision of Obadiah. Thus says the Lord the LORD concerning Edom: We have heard a report from the the LORD, and an envoy has been dispatched among the nations, saying, “Arise, and let us rise up against her in battle.”
Behold, I will reduce you to insignificance among the nations; you will be held in utter contempt.
The arrogance of your heart has beguiled you, O inhabitant of the clefts of the rock, whose dwelling is in the heights, who says in his heart, “Who shall bring me down to the earth?”
Though you exalt yourself like the eagle, and though you set your nest among the stars, from there I will bring you down, declares the the LORD.

If thieves were to come to you, if marauders by night—how utterly you would be ruined!—would they not steal only as much as they needed? If grape gatherers were to come to you, would they not leave gleanings?
How thoroughly Esau will be pillaged, his concealed treasures plundered!
All your allies have driven you to the border; your confederates have deceived and overpowered you; those who eat your bread have laid a snare beneath you; there is no discernment in him.
On that day, declares the the LORD, will I not destroy the wise out of Edom and discernment from Mount Esau?
Then your mighty men, O Teman, will be dismayed, and every man on Mount Esau will be cut down in the slaughter.
Because of the violence against your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be cut off forever.
On the day you stood aloof, on the day strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners entered his gates and cast lots for Jerusalem, you were like one of them.
But do not gloat over your brother in the day of his calamity; do not rejoice over the people of Judah in the day of their ruin; do not boast in the day of distress.
Do not enter the gate of My people in the day of their calamity; do not gloat over his disaster in the day of his calamity; do not loot his wealth in the day of his calamity.
Do not stand at the crossroads to cut off his fugitives; do not surrender his survivors in the day of distress.
For the day of the the LORD is near for all the nations. As you have done, it will be done to you; your recompense will return upon your own head.
For as you have drunk on My holy mountain, so all the nations will drink continually; they will drink and swallow, and they will be as though they had never been.
But on Mount Zion there will be deliverance, and it will be holy, and the house of Jacob will take possession of its inheritance.

The house of Jacob will be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble; they will burn and consume them, and there will be no survivor for the house of Esau, for the the LORD has spoken.
Those of the Negev will possess Mount Esau, and those of the lowland will possess the land of the Philistines; they will possess the fields of Ephraim and Samaria, and Benjamin will possess Gilead.
The exiles of the Israelites in Canaan will possess the land as far as Zarephath, and the exiles of Jerusalem in Sepharad will possess the cities of the Negev.
Deliverers will ascend Mount Zion to judge Mount Esau, and the kingdom will belong to the the LORD.
The word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai, saying,
“Arise, proceed to Nineveh, that great city, and cry out against it, for its wickedness has ascended before Me.”

Yet Jonah rose to flee toward Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD. Descending to Joppa, he found a vessel bound for Tarshish; he paid its fare and embarked with its company, intent on reaching Tarshish apart from the presence of the LORD.
Then the LORD hurled a violent wind upon the sea, and a tempest of extraordinary magnitude arose upon the waters, so that the ship seemed on the verge of disintegration.

The mariners, seized by terror, each cried out to his own god, and they cast the ship's cargo into the sea to lighten their burden; meanwhile Jonah had descended into the vessel's lowest recesses, lain down, and sunk into a profound slumber.
The shipmaster approached him and said, “What are you doing, sleeper? Arise and call upon your God! Perhaps God will consider us, so that we may not perish.”
They said to one another, “Come, let us cast lots, so that we may ascertain on whose account this calamity has befallen us.” They cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.
They said to him, “Tell us, we pray, on whose account this calamity has come upon us. What is your occupation? Whence do you come? What is your native land? And to what people do you belong?”
He said to them, “I am a Hebrew, and I revere the LORD, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”

The men were then seized by an exceedingly great fear, and they said to him, “What have you done?” For they knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the LORD, because he had disclosed it to them.
The sea was becoming increasingly tempestuous, so they said to him, “What shall we do to you, that the sea may be calm for us?”
He said to them, “Lift me up and cast me into the sea; then the sea will be calm for you, for I know that it is on my account that this great storm has come upon you.”
Nevertheless, the men rowed strenuously to bring the vessel back to land, but they could not, for the sea grew ever more tempestuous against them.

Therefore they cried out to the LORD and said, “Please, O the LORD, do not let us perish on account of this man's life, and do not charge us with innocent blood; for You, O the LORD, have done as You pleased.”
So they lifted Jonah up and cast him into the sea, and the sea ceased from its raging.
Then the men feared the LORD with great fear, and they offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows.
And the LORD appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah remained in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
Then Jonah prayed to the LORD his God from the belly of the fish.
He said, “Out of my distress I invoked the LORD, and He answered me; from the belly of Sheol I cried out, and You heard my voice.
You cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the current surrounded me; all Your breakers and Your waves passed over me.
And I said, ‘I am driven away from before Your eyes; yet I will look again toward Your holy temple.’
The waters closed over me, threatening my very life; the abyss surrounded me; seaweed was bound about my head.
“I descended to the roots of the mountains; the earth with its bars closed about me forever; yet You brought up my life from the pit, O the LORD my God.
When my soul fainted within me, I remembered the LORD; my prayer came to You, into Your holy temple.
Those who cling to worthless idols forfeit the mercy that could be theirs.
“But I, with shouts of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to you; what I have vowed I will pay. Deliverance belongs to the LORD.”
And the LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto dry land.
The word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time, saying,
“Arise, go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim to it the proclamation that I speak to you.”
So Jonah arose and went to Nineveh, according to the word of the LORD. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, a journey of three days.
Jonah began to enter the city, a day's journey, and he cried out, saying, “Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.”
The people of Nineveh believed in God; they proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from the greatest among them to the least.
When the report reached the king of Nineveh, he arose from his throne, removed his royal robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
“Let neither man nor beast, neither herd nor flock, taste anything; let them not feed, nor drink water;
but let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and let them cry mightily to God; let everyone turn from his evil way and from the violence that is in their hands.
Who knows? God may turn and relent, and turn away from His fierce anger, so that we do not perish.”
When God saw their deeds, that they turned from their evil way, God relented concerning the disaster that He had said He would bring upon them, and He did not do it.
But Jonah was greatly displeased and became angry.

So he prayed to the LORD and said, “Please, O the LORD, was this not what I said while I was still in my own country? That is why I fled beforehand to Tarshish, for I knew that You are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, and that You relent from bringing calamity.
And now, O the LORD, please take my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to live.”
And the LORD said, “Is it right for you to be angry?”
Then Jonah went out of the city and sat to the east of it. There he made himself a booth and sat under it in the shade, waiting to see what would become of the city.
the LORD God appointed a plant, and it grew up over Jonah to provide shade over his head and to deliver him from his discomfort; and Jonah was exceedingly glad because of the plant.
But when dawn came the next day, God appointed a worm, which attacked the plant so that it withered.
When the sun rose, God appointed a scorching east wind; the sun beat upon Jonah’s head, so that he grew faint and begged to die, saying, “It is better for me to die than to live.”
And God said to Jonah, “Is it right for you to be angry about the plant?” He said, “I am angry enough to die.”
And the LORD said, “You have been concerned about the plant, for which you did not labor and which you did not grow; it sprang up in a night and perished in a night.

And should I not have compassion on Nineveh, that great city, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand people utterly bereft of even the most elementary discernment, and also many animals?”
The word of the LORD that came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
Hear, all peoples; listen, O earth and all that is in it. Let the Lord, the LORD, be a witness against you—the Lord from His holy temple.
For behold, the LORD is coming out of His place; He will come down and tread upon the high places of the earth.
The mountains will melt beneath Him, and the valleys will split apart, like wax before the fire, like water poured down a slope.
All this is for the transgression of Jacob and for the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what is the high place of Judah? Is it not Jerusalem?
“Therefore I will make Samaria a heap of rubble in the open field, a planting place for vineyards; I will pour out her stones into the valley and expose her foundations.

All her carved images will be smashed to pieces; all her wages will be burned in the fire; and I will lay waste all her idols. Because she gathered them from a prostitute's wages, they will return to a prostitute's wages.”
Because of this I will lament and wail; I will go barefoot and naked. I will howl like a jackal and mourn like an ostrich.
For her wound is incurable, for it has reached Judah; it has come to the gate of my people, even to Jerusalem.
Do not tell it in Gath; do not weep at all. Roll in the dust at Beth-le-aphrah.
Pass on, O inhabitants of Shaphir, in naked shame. The inhabitant of Zaanan will not come out. Beth-ezel mourns; its support is taken from you.
For the inhabitant of Maroth waits in anguish for good, but disaster has come down from the LORD to the gate of Jerusalem.
Harness the chariot to the swift steed, O inhabitant of Lachish. She was the beginning of sin to the daughter of Zion, for the transgressions of Israel were found in you.
Therefore you shall give parting gifts to Moresheth-gath. The houses of Achzib will be a deception to the kings of Israel.
I will yet bring a conqueror against you, O inhabitant of Mareshah; the glory of Israel will come to Adullam.
Make yourself bald and cut off your hair for the children you delight in; enlarge your baldness like the eagle, for they have gone into exile from you.
Woe to those who contrive iniquity and perpetrate wickedness upon their couches! At the first blush of dawn they bring it to fruition, for it lies within their power.
They covet estates and seize them, together with houses, and carry them off; they crush a man together with his household, a man together with his patrimony.
Therefore thus says the the LORD: “Behold, I am devising against this family an evil from which you cannot extricate your necks; you shall not walk haughtily, for it is an evil time.”

In that day people will raise a taunt against you, and lament with a bitter lamentation, saying, “We are utterly ruined! He has changed the portion of my people; how utterly He has removed it from me; He has allotted our fields to traitors.”
Therefore you shall have no one to cast the measuring line by lot in the assembly of the the LORD.
“Do not prophesy!” they say. “Do not prophesy concerning these things; disgrace shall not overtake us.”
O house of Jacob, is the Spirit of the the LORD impatient? Are these His doings? Do not My words do good to him who walks uprightly?
But lately My people have risen as an enemy; you strip the robe from those who pass by securely, as men returning from war.
The women of My people you cast out from their pleasant houses; from their children you take away My glory forever.
Arise and depart, for this is no rest for you; because of uncleanness that destroys, with a grievous destruction.
If a man should walk in a false spirit and speak lies, saying, “I will prophesy to you of wine and strong drink,” he would be the prophet of this people.

I will surely gather all of you, O Jacob; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together like sheep of Bozrah, like a flock in the midst of its fold; they shall make a great noise because of the multitude of men.
The Breaker goes up before them; they break through and pass the gate, and go out by it; their king passes before them, with the the LORD at their head.
And I said: Hear now, heads of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel: Is it not for you to know justice?
Haters of good and lovers of evil, who strip the skin from them and the flesh from their bones—
who eat the flesh of My people, flay them and strip their skin from them, break their bones and chop them like meat in a pot, like flesh in a cauldron.
Then they will cry out to the LORD, but He will not answer them; at that time He will hide His face from them, because they have made their deeds evil.

Thus says the LORD concerning the prophets who lead My people astray, who proclaim peace so long as they have something to bite with their teeth, but declare war against anyone who puts nothing in their mouths.
Therefore night will come upon you, without vision, and darkness without divination; the sun will set on the prophets, and the day will blacken over them.
The seers will be ashamed, the diviners disgraced, and they will all cover their mouths in shame, for there is no answer from God.
But as for me, I am filled with power, with the Spirit of the LORD, and with justice and might, to declare to Jacob his transgression and to Israel his sin.
Hear this, you leaders of the house of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel, who abhor justice and pervert all that is straight.
They build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with iniquity.
Her leaders judge for a bribe, her priests teach for a price, and her prophets divine for money; yet they lean on the LORD, saying, "Is not the LORD among us? No disaster will come upon us."
Therefore, on account of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins, and the mount of the LORD's house a wooded height.
In the latter days, the mountain of the house of the LORD shall be established at the summit of the mountains, exalted above the hills, and peoples shall stream toward it.

Many nations will come and say, “Come, let us ascend to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, that He may teach us His ways, and we may walk in His paths.” For the law shall go forth from Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

He will judge between many peoples and decide for mighty nations far away; they shall beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks; nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war anymore.
But every man shall sit under his vine and under his fig tree, and no one shall make them afraid, for the mouth of the LORD of Hosts has spoken.
For every people walks in the name of its god, whereas we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever.
In that day, says the LORD, “I will gather the lame, I will assemble the exiled, and those whom I have afflicted.”
I will make the lame a remnant and the outcast a mighty nation; and the LORD will reign over them on Mount Zion from that time forth and forevermore.
And you, O tower of the flock, O stronghold of the daughter of Zion, to you shall come the former dominion, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.
Now why do you cry aloud? Is there no king in you? Has your counselor perished, that pangs have seized you like a woman in labor?

Writhe and groan, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in labor, for now you shall go forth from the city and dwell in the field; you shall go to Babylon. There you shall be rescued; there the LORD will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
Now many nations are gathered against you, saying, “Let her be defiled, and let our eyes gaze upon Zion.”
But they do not know the thoughts of the LORD, nor do they understand His counsel; for He has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor.

Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion, for I will make your horn iron and your hooves bronze; you shall beat in pieces many peoples, and I will devote their gain to the LORD, and their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.
Now marshal your troops, O daughter of troops, for a siege has been laid against us; with a rod they will strike the cheek of Israel's judge.
But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the thousands of Judah, out of you shall come forth for Me One to be ruler in Israel, whose origins are from of old, from days of eternity.
Therefore He will abandon them until the woman in labor has given birth; then the rest of His brothers will return to the children of Israel.
And He will stand and shepherd His flock in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD His God; and they will dwell, for then His greatness will reach the ends of the earth.
And He will be our peace. When Assyria comes into our land and treads upon our palaces, we will raise up against him seven shepherds and eight princes of men.
They will shepherd the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod at its gates; and He will deliver us when Assyria comes into our land and treads within our borders.
The remnant of Jacob will be among many peoples like dew from the LORD, like showers upon the grass, which neither waits for man nor tarries for the sons of men.

The remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the beasts of the forest, like a young lion among flocks of sheep, which tramples and tears as it passes through, with no one to rescue.
your hand will be lifted up against your adversaries, and all your enemies will be cut off.
And it shall be in that day, declares the LORD, that I will cut off your horses from your midst and destroy your chariots.
And I will cut off the cities of your land and tear down all your fortresses.
And I will cut off sorceries from your hand, and you will have no soothsayers.
And I will cut off your carved images and your pillars from your midst, and you shall no longer bow down to the work of your hands.
And I will uproot your Asherah poles from your midst and destroy your cities.
And I will execute vengeance in anger and wrath upon the nations that did not listen.
Hear now what the LORD says: “Arise, contend with the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.”
Hear, you mountains, the LORD’s indictment, and you, enduring foundations of the earth; for the LORD has a controversy with His people, and He will contend with Israel.
“O My people, what have I done to you? And how have I wearied you? Testify against Me!
For I brought you up from the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery; and I sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
O My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab devised, and what Balaam son of Beor answered him—from Shittim to Gilgal—that you may know the righteous acts of the LORD.”
“With what shall I come before the LORD, and bow down to the God of heaven? Shall I come before Him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?
Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?”
He has told you, O man, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
The voice of the LORD cries to the city—and it is sound wisdom to fear Your name: “Hear the rod and Him who appointed it!
Are there still in the house of the wicked treasures of wickedness, and the short ephah that is accursed?
Shall I acquit wickedness with dishonest scales, with a bag of deceitful weights?
For its rich men are full of violence, and its inhabitants speak lies, and their tongues are deceitful in their mouths.”
Therefore I, too, have struck you, making you desolate because of your sins.
You shall eat, but not be satisfied; and your hunger shall remain within you. You shall put away, but not preserve; and what you preserve, I will give to the sword.
You shall sow, but not reap; you shall tread olives, but not anoint yourself with oil; and you shall tread grapes, but not drink wine.

You have observed the statutes of Omri and all the works of the house of Ahab, and you have walked in their counsels, that I may make you a desolation, and its inhabitants a hissing; and you shall bear the reproach of My people.
Alas for me, for I have become like one who gathers the summer harvest, like a gleaner after the vintage; no cluster remains to be eaten, nor any first-ripe fig to gratify my longing.
The devout have vanished from the land, and among humankind no upright person remains; all lie in ambush for bloodshed, each hunting his brother with a net.
Their hands are consummately skilled in mischief: the prince and the judge solicit a bribe; the magnate proclaims the craving of his soul, and they concertedly pervert the matter.
The best of them is like a brier, and the most upright more noxious than a thorn hedge. The day foretold by your watchmen has arrived; now their perplexity shall overtake them.
Place no trust in a neighbor; repose no confidence in an intimate friend; guard the portals of your mouth from the woman who reclines in your embrace.
For a son treats his father with contempt, a daughter rises against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man's adversaries are the members of his own household.
But as for me, I shall watch for the the LORD; I shall wait for the God of my salvation; my God will hear me.
Do not exult over me, my enemy; though I have fallen, I shall rise again; though I sit in darkness, the the LORD shall be my light.

Because I have sinned against Him, I shall bear the indignation of the the LORD until He pleads my cause and executes judgment on my behalf; He will bring me forth into the light, and I shall behold His righteousness.
Then my enemy shall see it and be clothed with shame—she who said to me, “Where is the the LORD your God?” My eyes shall behold her; now she shall be trampled as mire in the streets.
A day shall come for rebuilding your walls; on that day the boundary shall be extended afar.
In that day they shall come to you from Assyria and from the cities of Egypt, from Egypt to the River, from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain.
Yet the earth shall become desolate because of its inhabitants, on account of the fruit of their deeds.
Shepherd Your people with Your staff, the flock of Your inheritance, who dwell alone in the forest, in the midst of Carmel; let them graze in Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old.
“As in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will show them My wonders.”
The nations shall see and be put to shame, despite all their might; they shall lay their hand upon their mouth, and their ears shall become deaf.

They shall lick the dust like a serpent, like crawling things of the earth; they shall come trembling out of their strongholds; they shall turn in dread to the the LORD our God, and they shall be afraid of you.
Who is a God like You, pardoning iniquity and passing over the transgression of the remnant of His inheritance? He does not retain His anger forever, because He delights in steadfast love.
He will again have compassion on us; He will tread our iniquities underfoot and cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
You will show faithfulness to Jacob and steadfast love to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from days of old.
An oracle concerning Nineveh: the book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
The LORD is a jealous and avenging God; the LORD is avenging and fierce in wrath. The LORD takes vengeance upon His adversaries, and He reserves indignation for His enemies.
The LORD is long-suffering and possessed of great might; the LORD will not at all acquit the guilty. His way is in the whirlwind and in the tempest, and the clouds are the dust of His feet.
He rebukes the sea and desiccates it, and He dries up all the rivers. Bashan and Carmel languish, and the blossom of Lebanon withers.
The mountains tremble before Him, and the hills dissolve; the earth heaves before Him, together with the world and all its inhabitants.
Who can stand before His indignation? Who can rise up amid the fierceness of His anger? His wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are shattered before Him.
The LORD is good—a stronghold in the day of distress—and He knows those who seek refuge in Him.
With an overflowing flood He will bring its place to an utter end, and darkness will pursue His enemies.
What do you devise against the LORD? He is effecting an utter end; affliction shall not rise up a second time.
For though they are entangled like thorns, and though they are drunk as drunkards, they shall be consumed like stubble fully dried.
From you has gone forth one who devises evil against the LORD, a counselor of worthlessness.
Thus says the LORD: “Though they stand intact and in great numbers, yet they shall be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.
And now I will break his yoke from upon you, and I will tear your bonds asunder.”

The LORD has commanded concerning you: “You shall have no descendants to bear your name. From the house of your gods I will cut off the carved image and the molten image. I will prepare your grave, for you are contemptible.”

Behold, upon the mountains, the feet of a messenger bringing good tidings, announcing peace! Celebrate your feasts, O Judah; fulfill your vows. For the wicked one shall no more pass through you; he has been utterly cut off.
The scatterer has pressed his assault against you; guard the rampart, watch the road, brace yourself for exertion, and summon every reserve of power.
For the LORD is restoring the majesty of Jacob as the majesty of Israel, though destroyers have laid them waste and ruined their vines.
The shields of his mighty men are crimson; his valiant warriors are clad in scarlet. The chariots flash like fire on the day he arrays them, and the cypress spears are brandished.
The chariots race through the streets and dash about the squares; they appear like torches and dart like lightning.
He summons his nobles, and they stumble as they advance; they rush to its wall, and the protective shield is set in place.
The river gates are thrown open, and the palace collapses.
It is decreed: she is exiled and carried away, while her maidservants moan like doves, beating their breasts.
Nineveh has been like a pool of water from her earliest days, but now they flee. “Stop! Stop!” they cry, yet no one turns back.
Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! There is no end to the treasure, an abundance of every precious thing.
She is emptied—yes, desolated and laid waste! Hearts melt, knees knock, bodies tremble, and every face grows pale.
Where is the lions’ den, the feeding ground of the young lions, where lion and lioness prowled with their cubs, with nothing to make them afraid?
The lion tore enough for his cubs and strangled prey for his lionesses; he filled his dens with prey and his lairs with torn carcasses.

Behold, I am against you, declares the LORD of Hosts. I will burn your chariots in smoke; the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voices of your messengers will be heard no more.
Woe to the blood-drenched city, teeming with falsehood and rapine, from which the prey never departs.
The crack of the whip and the rumble of wheels, the gallop of horses and the bounding of chariots;
the charging horseman, the flashing blade, the gleaming spear; heaps of the slain, masses of corpses, bodies beyond counting—they stumble over their own dead.
Because of the countless harlotries of the seductive harlot, mistress of sorceries, who sells nations by her seductions and families by her spells.
“Behold, I am against you, declares the LORD of Hosts; I will lift your skirts over your face and expose your nakedness to the nations and your shame to the kingdoms.
I will cast abominations upon you, treat you with contempt, and make a spectacle of you.”
And everyone who sees you will shrink from you and say, “Nineveh is laid waste—who will mourn for her?” Where shall I seek comforters for you?
Are you better than Thebes, seated among the rivers, with water surrounding her, whose rampart was the sea and whose wall was the water?
Cush and Egypt were her strength, beyond number; Put and Libya were her allies.
Yet she too went into exile, into captivity; her little ones were dashed to pieces at the head of every street; lots were cast for her nobles, and all her great men were bound in chains.
You too will be drunk; you will be hidden; you too will seek a stronghold against the enemy.
All your fortresses are like fig trees with first-ripe figs: if shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.
Behold, the people in your midst are like women; the gates of your land stand wide open to your enemies; fire has consumed your bars.
Draw water for the siege, strengthen your fortresses; go into the clay and tread the mortar, reinforce the brickkiln.
There fire will devour you; the sword will cut you off; it will consume you as the young locust consumes; multiply yourself like the young locust, multiply yourself like the locust.
You have multiplied your merchants more than the stars of heaven; the young locust strips the land and flies away.
Your crowned ones are like locusts, your marshals like swarms of grasshoppers that settle in the hedges on a cold day; when the sun rises they fly away, and no one knows where they have gone.
Your shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria; your nobles dwell in the dust; your people are scattered upon the mountains, and there is none to gather them.
There is no healing for your bruise; your wound is grievous. All who hear the report of you clap their hands over you, for upon whom has your wickedness not passed continually?
The prophetic oracle that Habakkuk the prophet beheld.
How long, O the LORD, must I cry for help, but You do not listen? I cry out to You, “Violence!” but You do not rescue?
Why do You cause me to behold iniquity and compel me to gaze upon misery? Ruin and violence confront me; strife and contention arise.
Therefore the law is enfeebled, and justice never emerges; for the wicked hem in the righteous, so judgment issues forth distorted.
“Look among the nations and observe; be confounded, utterly bewildered. For I am effecting a work in your days that you would not believe even if it were recounted.”
For behold, I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter and impetuous nation, who traverse the breadth of the earth to seize dwellings not their own.
They are dreaded and fearsome; their justice and sovereignty proceed from themselves.
Their horses are swifter than leopards, fiercer than wolves of the evening; their horsemen charge ahead, and their riders come from afar, flying like an eagle swooping to devour.
They all come for violence; their faces press eastward, and they gather captives like sand.
They scoff at kings, and rulers are a derision to them; they laugh at every fortress, for they heap up earth and capture it.
Then they surge onward like the wind and pass by—guilty men whose might is their god.
Are You not from everlasting, O the LORD my God, my Holy One? We shall not die. O the LORD, You have appointed them for judgment; O Rock, You have established them for chastisement.
Your eyes are too pure to behold evil, and You cannot gaze upon iniquity. Why do You regard the treacherous and remain silent while the wicked devours one more righteous than himself?
You make humankind like the fish of the sea, like crawling creatures without a ruler.
He draws them all up with a hook; he catches them in his net and gathers them in his dragnet; therefore he rejoices and exults.
Therefore he sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his dragnet, for by them his portion is fat and his food is rich.
Will he then empty his net and continue slaughtering nations without pity?
I will take my stand upon my watchtower and station myself upon the rampart, watching to see what He will say to me and what answer I shall return concerning my complaint.
The LORD answered me and said, "Write down the vision and inscribe it plainly upon the tablets, so that whoever reads it may run with it."
For the vision is yet for an appointed time; it testifies to the end and does not deceive. Though it tarry, wait for it, for it will surely come and will not be late.
Behold, his soul is puffed up within him and is not upright; but the righteous shall live by his faith.

Moreover, wine is treacherous; the arrogant man does not abide. He enlarges his appetite like Sheol, and like death he is never satisfied. He gathers all nations to himself and collects all peoples to himself.
Will not all these take up a taunt against him, and a mocking riddle, and say, "Woe to him who heaps up what is not his own—how long?—and burdens himself with pledges!"?
Will not your creditors suddenly arise, and those who make you tremble awake? Then you will become spoil for them.
Because you have plundered many nations, all the remnant of the peoples will plunder you, because of the blood of man and the violence done to the land, to the city, and to all its inhabitants.
Woe to him who gains evil profit for his house, setting his nest on high to be delivered from the hand of calamity!
You have devised shame for your house by cutting off many peoples, and you have sinned against your own soul.
For the stone will cry out from the wall, and the beam will answer it from the timber.
Woe to him who builds a city with blood and establishes a town by iniquity!
Behold, is it not from the the LORD of Hosts that peoples labor for fire, and nations weary themselves for nothing?
For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.
Woe to him who makes his neighbor drink, pouring out your venom and making them drunk, so that you may gaze upon their nakedness!
You are filled with shame rather than glory. Drink also, and be exposed! The cup in the the LORD's right hand will come around to you, and disgrace will cover your glory.
For the violence done to Lebanon will cover you, and the destruction of beasts will terrify you, because of the blood of man and the violence to the land, to the city, and to all its inhabitants.
What profit is an idol, when its maker has carved it—a metal image, a teacher of lies? For the craftsman trusts in his own handiwork when he makes mute idols.
Woe to him who says to wood, "Awake!" and to silent stone, "Arise!" Can this teach? Behold, it is overlaid with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all within it.
But the the LORD is in His holy temple; let all the earth keep silence before Him.
A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, set to Shigionoth.
The LORD, I have heard the report concerning You; I stand in awe, the LORD, of Your work. Revive it in the midst of the years; in the midst of the years make it known; in wrath remember mercy.
God comes from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His glory covers the heavens, and His praise fills the earth.
His radiance is like the light; rays flash from His hand, and there His power is hidden.
Plague goes before Him, and pestilence follows in His steps.
He stood and measured the earth; He looked and startled the nations. The ancient mountains crumbled; the everlasting hills collapsed. His ways are eternal.
I saw the tents of Cushan in distress; the curtains of Midian trembled.
Were You angry with the rivers, the LORD? Was Your wrath against the streams? Did You rage against the sea when You rode upon Your horses, Your chariots of salvation?
You bared Your bow; sworn were the rods of chastisement. Selah. You split the earth with rivers.
The mountains saw You and writhed; torrents of water swept by; the deep roared and lifted its hands on high.
Sun and moon stood still in their places at the flash of Your flying arrows, at the gleam of Your glittering spear.
In wrath You strode through the earth; in anger You threshed the nations.
You went out to save Your people, to save Your anointed. You crushed the head of the house of the wicked and stripped him from head to foot. Selah.
With his own spear You pierced his head when his warriors stormed out to scatter me, gloating as though to devour the poor in secret.
You trampled the sea with Your horses, churning the great waters.

I heard, and my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the sound; decay entered my bones; I trembled where I stood. Yet I will wait in quietness for the day of distress to come upon the nation that invades us.
Though the fig tree does not bud and no fruit is on the vines, though the olive crop fails and the fields produce no food, though the sheep are cut off from the fold and no cattle are in the stalls,
yet I will rejoice in the LORD; I will exult in the God of my salvation.
The LORD God is my strength; He makes my feet like those of a deer and enables me to walk on the heights. For the choirmaster, with stringed instruments.
The word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.
“I shall utterly extirpate all things from the face of the earth,” declares the LORD.

“I shall extirpate man and beast alike; I shall extirpate the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, together with the stumbling blocks and the wicked. I shall cut off humankind from the face of the earth,” declares the LORD.

“I shall stretch forth My hand against Judah and against all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and I shall cut off from this place the remnant of Baal, the name of the idolatrous priests together with the priests—
those who prostrate themselves upon the rooftops to the host of heaven, those who prostrate themselves and swear to the LORD while also swearing by Milcom,
and those who turn back from following the LORD, who neither seek the LORD nor inquire of Him.”
Be silent before the Lord the LORD, for the day of the LORD is near. The LORD has prepared a sacrifice; He has consecrated His guests.
“On the day of the LORD’s sacrifice I shall punish the officials, the king’s sons, and all who array themselves in foreign attire.
On that day I shall punish all who leap over the threshold, who fill their masters’ houses with violence and deceit.”
“On that day,” declares the LORD, “a cry shall be heard from the Fish Gate, a wail from the Second Quarter, and a great crash from the hills.”
Howl, O inhabitants of the Hollow! For all the people of Canaan are undone, and all who weigh out silver are cut off.
“At that time I shall search Jerusalem with lamps and punish the men who are complacent, who say in their hearts, ‘The LORD will not do good, nor will He do evil.’
Their wealth shall become spoil, and their houses desolation; though they build houses, they shall not dwell in them, and though they plant vineyards, they shall not drink their wine.”
The great day of the LORD is near—near and hastening swiftly. The sound of the day of the LORD is bitter; there the mighty warrior cries out.
That day is a day of wrath, a day of distress and anguish, a day of ruin and devastation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness,
a day of trumpet blast and battle cry against the fortified cities and against the lofty battlements.
I shall bring distress upon mankind, so that they shall walk as the blind, because they have sinned against the LORD; their blood shall be poured out like dust, and their flesh like dung.

Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them on the day of the wrath of the LORD. In the fire of His jealousy all the earth shall be consumed, for He will make a full and sudden end of all who dwell upon the earth.
Gather together, yes, gather, O shameless nation,
before the decree takes effect—before the day is borne away like chaff—before the fierce anger of the the LORD descends upon you, before the day of the the LORD overtakes you.
Seek the the LORD, all you humble of the land, who have performed His justice; seek righteousness, seek humility; perhaps you will be concealed in the day of the the LORD’s anger.
For Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon shall become a desolation; Ashdod shall be driven out at noon, and Ekron shall be uprooted.
Woe to you inhabitants of the seacoast, you nation of the Cherethites! The word of the the LORD is against you, O Canaan, land of the Philistines; I will destroy you, so that no inhabitant remains.
The seacoast shall become pastures, with meadows for shepherds and folds for flocks.

It shall belong to the remnant of the house of Judah; they shall pasture upon it, and in the houses of Ashkelon they shall lie down at evening, for the the LORD their God will visit them and restore their fortunes.
“I have heard the taunt of Moab and the revilings of the Ammonites, how they taunted My people and magnified themselves against their border.

Therefore, as I live,” declares the the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, “Moab shall be like Sodom, and the Ammonites like Gomorrah—a realm of nettles and salt pits, a desolation forever. The remnant of My people shall plunder them, and the survivors of My nation shall possess them.”
This shall be their recompense for their pride, because they taunted and magnified themselves against the people of the the LORD of Hosts.
The the LORD will be formidable against them, for He will famish all the gods of the earth; and all the coastlands of the nations shall bow down to Him, each in its own place.
You also, O Cushites, shall be slain by My sword.
He will stretch out His hand against the north and destroy Assyria; He will make Nineveh a desolation, dry as the wilderness.

Herds shall lie down in her midst—all kinds of beasts; even the owl and the hedgehog shall lodge among her capitals; a voice shall hoot in the window; devastation shall be on the threshold, for He has laid bare her cedar work.

This is the exultant city that dwelt in security, that said in her heart, “I am, and there is no one else.” How she has become a desolation, a lair for wild beasts! Everyone who passes by her hisses and shakes his fist.
Woe to the oppressing city, rebellious and defiled!
She has not heeded the voice; she has not accepted correction. She has not trusted in the LORD; she has not drawn near to her God.
Her officials within her are roaring lions; her judges are wolves that prowl at dusk and devour everything before dawn.
Her prophets are reckless, faithless men; her priests profane the sanctuary and do violence to the law.
The LORD within her is righteous; He does no wrong. Morning by morning He dispenses justice; at dawn He does not fail; yet the unjust know no shame.
“I have cut off nations; their corner towers are desolate. I have laid waste their streets, so that no one passes through. Their cities are destroyed, without inhabitant.
I said, ‘Surely you will fear Me and accept correction.’ Then her dwelling would not be cut off, nor all that I have appointed against her. Yet they were eager to corrupt all their deeds.

Therefore wait for Me,” declares the LORD, “until the day I rise up to plunder. For My determination is to gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, to pour out upon them My indignation—all My burning anger. For in the fire of My jealousy all the earth will be consumed.
For then I will restore to the peoples a pure language, that all of them may call upon the name of the LORD and serve Him with one accord.
From beyond the rivers of Cush My worshipers, My dispersed ones, will bring Me an offering.

On that day you will not be put to shame for any of the deeds by which you have rebelled against Me. For then I will remove from among you those who rejoice in their pride, and you will never again be haughty on My holy mountain.
And I will leave in your midst a people humble and lowly, and they will trust in the name of the LORD.
The remnant of Israel will not do wrong or speak lies, nor will a deceitful tongue be found in their mouths. For they will feed and lie down, and no one will make them afraid.”
Sing aloud, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel! Rejoice and exult with all your heart, O daughter of Jerusalem!
The LORD has taken away your judgments; He has cleared away your enemies. The King of Israel, the LORD, is in your midst; you will never again fear evil.
On that day it will be said to Jerusalem: “Do not fear, O Zion; do not let your courage fail.”
The LORD your God is in your midst, a mighty Savior. He will rejoice over you with gladness; He will quiet you with His love; He will exult over you with singing.
“I will gather those among you who grieve over the appointed feasts, so that they will no longer suffer reproach.
Behold, at that time I will deal with all your oppressors. I will save the lame and gather the outcast, and I will make them a praise and a name in all the earth, where they had been put to shame.

At that time I will bring you in; at that time I will gather you. For I will make you a name and a praise among all the peoples of the earth, when I restore your fortunes before your eyes,” says the LORD.

In the second year of King Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came by the hand of Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, saying:
"Thus says the LORD of Hosts: This people says, 'The time has not come—the time for the house of the LORD to be built.'"
Then the word of the LORD came by the hand of Haggai the prophet, saying:
"Is it time for you yourselves to dwell in your paneled houses while this house lies in ruins?"
Now therefore thus says the LORD of Hosts: "Set your hearts upon your ways.

You have sown much, but brought in little; you eat, yet are not satisfied; you drink, yet are not exhilarated; you clothe yourselves, yet are not warmed; and the wage earner earns wages only to put them into a purse full of holes."
Thus says the LORD of Hosts: "Set your hearts upon your ways.
Ascend the mountain, bring timber, and build the house, that I may take pleasure in it and be glorified, says the LORD.

You expected much, but behold, it came to little; and when you brought it home, I blew it away. Why? declares the LORD of Hosts. Because My house lies in ruins while each of you hastens to his own house.
Therefore the heavens above you have withheld the dew, and the earth has withheld its yield.
I have summoned a drought upon the land and upon the mountains, upon grain, new wine, oil, and all that the soil produces, upon human beings and beasts, and upon every labor of hands."

Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest, and all the remnant of the people heeded the voice of the LORD their God and the words of Haggai the prophet, according as the LORD their God had sent him; and the people revered the LORD.
Then Haggai, the messenger of the LORD, spoke to the people in the LORD's message, saying, "I am with you," declares the LORD.

And the LORD roused the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and labored upon the house of the LORD of Hosts, their God, on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.
On the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the word of the LORD came through the prophet Haggai, saying:
"Speak now to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the remnant of the people:
'Who among you remains who beheld this house in its former splendor? And how does it now appear to you? Is it not, in your estimation, as nothing beside that former magnificence?'"

"Now be strong, O Zerubbabel," declares the LORD, "and be strong, O Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and be strong, all you people of the land," declares the LORD, "and work, for I am with you," declares the LORD of Hosts.
"According to the covenant I established with you when you came forth from Egypt, My Spirit abides among you; do not fear."
For thus says the LORD of Hosts: "Yet once more—in a little while—I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
I will shake all nations, and the treasures of all nations will come in, and I will fill this house with glory," says the LORD of Hosts.
"The silver is Mine, and the gold is Mine," declares the LORD of Hosts.
"The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former," says the LORD of Hosts, "and in this place I will give peace," declares the LORD of Hosts.
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Haggai:
"Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Ask the priests concerning the law, saying,
'If a man carries consecrated meat in the fold of his garment, and with that fold touches bread, stew, wine, oil, or any food, does it become holy?' " And the priests answered, "No."
Then Haggai said, "If one who has become unclean through contact with a corpse touches any of these, does it become unclean?" And the priests answered, "It does become unclean."
Then Haggai answered and said, "So is this people, and so is this nation before Me," declares the LORD. "And so is every work of their hands; and what they offer there is unclean."
"Now set your hearts on this from this day forward, from before a stone was laid upon a stone in the temple of the LORD.
When you came to a heap of twenty measures, there were but ten; when you came to the wine vat to draw out fifty, there were but twenty.
I struck you and all the work of your hands with blight, mildew, and hail, but you did not return to Me," declares the LORD.
"Now set your hearts on this from this day forward, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day the foundation of the temple of the LORD was laid. Set your hearts on it.
Is the seed still in the barn? The vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive tree have not yet produced. But from this day on I will bless you."
A second time, on the twenty-fourth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to Haggai:
"Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, and say, 'I am about to shake the heavens and the earth.

I will overthrow the thrones of kingdoms and destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the nations. I will overturn chariots and their riders; horses and their riders will fall, each by the sword of his brother.

On that day,' declares the LORD of Hosts, 'I will take you, My servant Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel,' declares the LORD, 'and I will make you like My signet ring, for I have chosen you,' declares the LORD of Hosts."
In the eighth month of the second year of Darius’s reign, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, saying:
The LORD was intensely indignant with your fathers.
Therefore say to them, “Thus says the LORD of hosts: Return to Me, declares the LORD of hosts, and I will return to you, says the LORD of hosts.”

Do not be like your fathers, to whom the earlier prophets cried out, “Thus says the LORD of hosts: Turn now from your evil ways and your evil deeds.” Yet they did not listen, nor did they incline their ears to Me, declares the LORD.
Where are your fathers now? And the prophets—do they live forever?

But did not My words and My statutes, which I commanded My servants the prophets, overtake your fathers? Then they repented and said, “As the LORD of hosts purposed to do to us according to our ways and our deeds, so He has done to us.”
On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month—that is, the month of Shebat—in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah the prophet, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, saying:
I saw by night, and behold, a man riding on a red horse; he stood among the myrtle trees that were in the hollow, and behind him were red, sorrel, and white horses.
Then I said, “What are these, my lord?” And the angel who talked with me said to me, “I will show you what these are.”
And the man standing among the myrtle trees answered and said, “These are they whom the LORD has sent to patrol the earth.”
And they answered the angel of the LORD who stood among the myrtle trees and said, “We have patrolled the earth, and behold, all the earth sits tranquil and at rest.”
Then the angel of the LORD said, “O LORD of hosts, how long will You withhold compassion from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, against which You have been indignant these seventy years?”
And the LORD answered the angel who talked with me with good and comforting words.
So the angel who talked with me said to me, “Cry out, saying,” “Thus says the LORD of hosts: I am exceedingly jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion.
But I am very angry with the complacent nations; for while I was but a little angry, they compounded the calamity.
Therefore thus says the LORD: I have returned to Jerusalem with compassion; My house shall be built in it, says the LORD of hosts, and a surveyor’s line shall be stretched out over Jerusalem.”
