To these intruders we did not yield in subjection for so much as an hour, in order that the truth of the gospel might abide with you.
As for those who appeared to be persons of consequence—whatever they once were is immaterial to me, for God shows no partiality—these reputed leaders imparted nothing to me.
On the contrary, perceiving that I had been entrusted with the gospel for the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been for the circumcised,
they recognized that He who wrought in Peter unto an apostleship to the circumcised wrought in me also toward the Gentiles.

And James, Cephas, and John—those reputed pillars—recognizing the grace bestowed upon me, extended to Barnabas and me the right hand of fellowship, that we should labor among the Gentiles while they did so among the circumcised.
They asked only that we remember the poor, a charge I was already zealous to fulfill.
But when Cephas came to Antioch, I withstood him to his face, for he stood condemned.
For before the arrival of certain men from James, he dined with the Gentiles; yet when they appeared, he withdrew and set himself apart, apprehensive of those of the circumcision.
The other Jews joined him in this dissimulation, so that even Barnabas was swept along by their hypocrisy.

When I perceived that they were not walking uprightly in accordance with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in the presence of all, "If you, though a Jew, live as the Gentiles do and not as the Jews, how can you compel the Gentiles to live as Jews?"
We are Jews by birth, not sinners from among the Gentiles.

Yet knowing that a person is not justified by works of the law, except through faith in Jesus Christ, we also believed in Christ Jesus, that we might be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law; for by works of the law no flesh shall be justified.
But if, while seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves are discovered to be sinners, is Christ then an agent of sin? By no means!
For if I reconstruct what I once dismantled, I constitute myself a transgressor.
For through the law I died to the law, that I might live unto God.

I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me; and the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and delivered Himself up for me.
I do not nullify the grace of God; for if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died in vain.
O unreflective Galatians, who has bewitched you, before whose very eyes Jesus Christ was publicly placarded as crucified?
I would learn this alone from you: did you receive the Spirit from works of the Law, or from hearing with faith?
Are you so devoid of understanding? Having commenced in the Spirit, are you now being brought to completion in the flesh?
Have you suffered so much to no purpose—if, indeed, it was to no purpose?
Does He, then, who lavishly furnishes the Spirit to you and effects mighty works among you, do so from works of the Law, or from hearing with faith?
Just as Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness,
know, then, that those who are of faith are sons of Abraham.
And the Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, proclaimed the gospel in advance to Abraham: "In you shall all the nations be blessed."
So then those who are of faith are blessed together with Abraham, the man of faith.
For as many as are of works of the Law are under a curse; for it is written, "Cursed is everyone who does not abide by all things written in the book of the Law, so as to perform them."
Now it is evident that no one is justified before God by the Law, for "The righteous shall live by faith."
The Law is not of faith; rather, "The one who does them shall live by them."
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the Law, having become a curse for us—for it is written, "Cursed is everyone who is hanged on a tree"—
so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles, so that we might receive the promised Spirit through faith.
Brothers, I put this in human terms: even a covenant ratified by a man no one voids or amends.
Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his Seed. He does not say, "And to seeds," as referring to many, but "And to your Seed," as referring to one, who is Christ.
What I am saying is this: the Law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, does not invalidate a covenant previously ratified by God, so as to nullify the promise.
For if the inheritance is by the Law, it is no longer by promise; but God graciously granted it to Abraham by promise.
Why then the Law? It was added because of transgressions, until the Seed should come to whom the promise had been made; and it was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator.
Now a mediator is not for a single party, but God is one.
Is the Law, then, contrary to the promises of God? By no means! For if a law had been given that could impart life, then righteousness would indeed be by the Law.
But the Scripture imprisoned all things under sin, so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.
Now before faith came, we were held in custody under the Law, being shut up unto the faith that was to be revealed.
So then the Law has become our guardian to lead us to Christ, so that we might be justified by faith.
But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.
For you are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is no male and female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
And if you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to promise.
Now I say that for as long as the heir remains a minor, he differs in no respect from a slave, although he is lord of all;
rather, he is under guardians and stewards until the date appointed by the father;
so likewise we, when we were minors, were enslaved beneath the elemental principles of the world.
Yet when the fullness of time had come, God sent forth His Son, born of a woman, born under the law,
in order that He might redeem those under the law, in order that we might receive adoption as sons.
And because you are sons, God sent forth the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying, “Father, O Father!”
Consequently, you are no longer a slave, but a son; and if a son, then an heir through God.
But formerly, not knowing God, you were enslaved to beings that by nature are no gods;
but now, having come to know God—or rather, having been known by God—how is it that you turn back again to the weak and beggarly elemental principles, unto which you desire to be enslaved anew?
You observe days and months and seasons and years.
I fear for you, lest somehow I have labored among you in vain.
I entreat you, brothers, become as I am, because I also became as you are. You did me no wrong.
And you know that because of weakness of the flesh I formerly proclaimed the gospel to you.
And your ordeal occasioned by my bodily weakness you did not despise nor spit out, but received me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus.
Where, then, is your blessedness? For I testify to you that, if possible, having plucked out your eyes, you would have given them to me.
So have I become your enemy by speaking truth to you?
They zealously court you, yet not honorably; rather, they desire to shut you out, that you may be zealous for them.
But it is commendable to be zealous in a good cause always, and not only when I am present with you.
My little children, for whom I am again in travail until Christ is formed in you,
I could wish to be present with you now and to alter my voice, because I am perplexed concerning you.
Tell me, you who desire to be under the law: do you not hear the law?
For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the bondwoman and one by the free woman.
But the one by the bondwoman was born according to the flesh, whereas the one by the free woman was born through promise.
These things are to be taken allegorically: for these women are two covenants, one from Mount Sinai, bearing children unto slavery, which is Hagar.
Now Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and she corresponds to the present Jerusalem, for she serves together with her children.
But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.
For it is written: “Rejoice, barren woman who does not bear; break forth and cry aloud, you who do not travail; for more are the children of the desolate than of her who has the husband.”
And you, brothers, are children of promise according to Isaac.
But just as then the one born according to the flesh persecuted the one according to the Spirit, so also now.
But what does the Scripture say? “Cast out the bondwoman and her son, for the son of the bondwoman will not inherit with the son of the free woman.”
Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free woman.
For freedom Christ has emancipated us; stand firm, therefore, and do not permit yourselves to be entangled again in a yoke of servitude.
Mark well: I, Paul, declare to you that if you undergo circumcision, Christ will avail you nothing.
I solemnly attest once more to every man who submits to circumcision that he becomes obligated to observe the entire Law.
As for you who would be justified by the Law, you have been severed from Christ; you have fallen from grace.
For through the Spirit, by faith, we eagerly await the hope of righteousness.
For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision possesses any efficacy whatsoever; rather, faith energized through love is what counts.
You were progressing admirably; who impeded you from obeying the truth?
Such persuasion is not from the One who calls you.
A mere modicum of leaven leavens the entire mass.
I am confident in the Lord concerning you, that you will entertain no contrary conviction; yet whoever is agitating you shall bear his condemnation, whoever he may be.
And I, brothers, if I still proclaim circumcision, why am I still persecuted? In that case the scandal of the cross has been nullified.
Would that those who are unsettling you would go so far as to emasculate themselves!
For you, brothers, were called to freedom; only do not convert that freedom into an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another.
For the whole Law is fulfilled in one word, namely: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
But if you bite and devour one another, beware lest you be consumed by one another.
I say, then, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desire of the flesh.
For the flesh craves what is contrary to the Spirit, and the Spirit what is contrary to the flesh; these are antagonistic to each other, so that you do not do whatever you wish.
But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the Law.
Now the works of the flesh are evident: sexual immorality, impurity, and debauchery;
idolatry, sorcery, enmities, strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, rivalries, dissensions, factions;
envy, drunkenness, carousing, and the like. I forewarn you, just as I have forewarned you, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
gentleness, and self-control; against such things there is no law.
And those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh, together with its passions and desires.
If we live by the Spirit, let us also keep in step with the Spirit.
Let us not become conceited, provoking one another and envying one another.
Brethren, should any person be overtaken in a transgression, you who are spiritual must restore such a one in a spirit of meekness, scrutinizing yourself, lest you too be tempted.
Bear one another's burdens, and in this manner you will fulfill the law of Christ.
For if anyone reckons himself to be something while he is nothing, he beguiles himself.
Rather, let each person prove his own work, and then he shall have ground for exultation in himself alone, and not in comparison with another.
For each shall bear his own proper load.
Moreover, let the one instructed in the word share in all good things with the instructor.
Do not be deceived: God is not mocked, for whatever a person sows, that he shall also reap.
For whoever sows unto his own flesh shall reap from the flesh corruption; but whoever sows unto the Spirit shall reap from the Spirit life everlasting.
And let us not grow weary in well-doing, for at the appointed season we shall reap, if we do not lose heart.
Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us work good toward all, and especially toward those of the household of faith.
Behold with what prodigious script I have written to you by my own hand.
Those who wish to present a seemly appearance in the flesh compel you to be circumcised, solely that they may not be persecuted for the cross of Christ.
For not even those who are circumcised observe the law; rather, they desire that you be circumcised, that they may boast in your flesh.
But far be it from me to boast, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world is crucified to me, and I to the world.
For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision avails anything, but a new creation.
And as many as shall walk by this rule, peace and mercy rest upon them, and upon the Israel of God.
Henceforth let no one trouble me, for I bear in my body the marks of Jesus.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brethren. Amen.
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, to the saints who are in Ephesus and the faithful in Christ Jesus:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places,
just as He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless before Him in love,
having predestined us for adoption as sons through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of His will,
to the praise of the glory of His grace, which He lavished upon us in the Beloved.
In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of His grace,
which He lavished upon us in all wisdom and insight,
making known to us the mystery of His will, according to His good pleasure, which He purposed in Him,
as an economy for the fullness of the times, to recapitulate all things in Christ—things in heaven and things on earth—in Him.
In Him we have also obtained an inheritance, having been predestined according to the purpose of Him who accomplishes all things according to the counsel of His will,
so that we who were the first to hope in Christ might be to the praise of His glory.
In Him you also, when you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and believed in it, were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit,
who is the pledge of our inheritance until the redemption of the acquired possession, to the praise of His glory.
For this reason I too, having heard of your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love toward all the saints,
do not cease giving thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers,
that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of Him,
having the eyes of your heart enlightened, so that you may know what is the hope of His calling, what are the riches of the glory of His inheritance among the saints,
and what is the surpassing greatness of His power toward us who believe, according to the working of His mighty strength,
which He worked in Christ when He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly places,
far above all rule and authority and power and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this age but also in the one to come.
And He put all things under His feet and gave Him as head over all things to the church,
which is His body, the fullness of Him who fills all in all.
And as for you, who were dead in your trespasses and sins,
in which you formerly conducted yourselves according to the course of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, the spirit that is now at work among the sons of disobedience,

among whom we all also formerly conducted ourselves in the cravings of our flesh, indulging the inclinations of the flesh and of the mind, and were by nature children of wrath, as the rest of mankind.
But God, being rich in mercy, because of the great love with which He loved us,
even when we were dead in our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ—by grace you have been saved—
and raised us up together and seated us together in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus,
so that in the coming ages He might display the surpassing riches of His grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus.
For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not from yourselves; it is the gift of God,
not from works, so that no one may boast.
For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand so that we might conduct ourselves in them.
Therefore remember that formerly you, the Gentiles in the flesh, who are called “the uncircumcision” by those called “the circumcision” in the flesh, made by hands,
were at that time without Christ, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel and strangers to the covenants of the promise, having no hope and without God in the world.
But now in Christ Jesus, you who once were far off have become near by the blood of Christ.
For He Himself is our peace, who made both one and broke down the dividing wall of hostility,
by abolishing in His flesh the law of commandments expressed in ordinances, so that He might create in Himself one new man from the two, thus making peace,
and might reconcile both to God in one body through the cross, thereby putting to death the hostility in Himself.
And He came and preached peace to you who were far off and peace to those who were near.
For through Him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father.
So then you are no longer strangers and aliens, but fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God,
built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus Himself being the cornerstone,
in whom the whole building, being fitted together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord,
in whom you also are being built together into a dwelling place for God in the Spirit.
For this cause I, Paul, am held as a prisoner of Christ Jesus on behalf of you Gentiles—
if, indeed, you have heard of the stewardship of God’s grace entrusted to me for your benefit,
namely, that the mystery was disclosed to me through revelation, as I have cursorily noted before,
by means of which, upon your reading, you may apprehend my insight into the mystery of Christ,
a mystery that in earlier generations was not revealed to the sons of men, but has now been unveiled in the Spirit to His holy apostles and prophets:
that the Gentiles are co-heirs, co-members of the body, and co-participants in the promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel,
of which I became a minister in accordance with the gift of God’s grace bestowed upon me by the operative efficacy of His power.
To me, the least of all the saints, this grace was granted: to proclaim to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ,
and to illuminate for all people what is the administration of the mystery concealed for ages in God, who created all things,
so that now, through the church, the manifold wisdom of God might be made known to the rulers and authorities in the heavenly realms,
in accordance with the eternal purpose that He accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord,
in whom we possess boldness and confident access through faith in Him.
Therefore I entreat you not to be disheartened by my tribulations on your behalf, for they constitute your glory.
For this reason I bow my knees before the Father,
from whom every family in heaven and on earth derives its name,
that He would grant you, according to the riches of His glory, to be strengthened with power through His Spirit in the inner man,
so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith, you being rooted and grounded in love,
and that you may possess the strength to comprehend with all the saints what is the breadth and length and height and depth,
and to know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge, so that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
Now to Him who is able to do exceedingly abundantly beyond all that we ask or conceive, according to the power at work within us,
to Him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus throughout all generations, forever and ever. Amen.
As a prisoner in the Lord, therefore, I exhort you to conduct your lives in a manner worthy of the vocation to which you have been called,
with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
striving to preserve the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called to one hope in your calling;
one Lord, one faith, one baptism;
one God and Father of all, who is over all, through all, and in all.
Yet to each of us grace has been apportioned according to the measure of Christ’s gift.
Hence it is said, “When He ascended on high, He led captives in His train and gave gifts to humanity.”
Now what is the significance of “He ascended,” if not that He first descended into the lower regions of the earth?
The One who descended is Himself also the One who ascended far above all the heavens, so that He might fill all things.
And He Himself appointed some as apostles, some as prophets, some as evangelists, and some as pastors and teachers,
for the equipping of the saints for the work of ministry, toward the edification of the body of Christ,
until we all attain to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to mature adulthood, to the measure of the stature of Christ’s fullness.
Thus we are no longer to be infants, tossed to and fro and carried about by every wind of teaching, by the cunning and craftiness of people in their deceitful scheming.
Rather, speaking the truth in love, we are to grow up in all respects into Him who is the head—Christ Himself.
From Him the whole body, being fitted and held together by every supporting ligament, grows and builds itself up in love as each part does its work according to its proper measure.
So I declare and testify in the Lord that you must no longer live as the Gentiles do, in the futility of their thinking.
Their understanding is darkened; they are alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance within them, stemming from the hardness of their hearts.
Having lost all sensitivity, they have surrendered themselves to sensuality so as to indulge in every kind of impurity with insatiable greed.
But you did not so learn Christ,
assuming that you have heard Him and been taught in Him, as truth resides in Jesus.
You were instructed to put off the old self, which belongs to your former way of life and is being corrupted by deceitful desires,
and to be renewed in the spirit of your minds,
and to put on the new self, created in God’s likeness in true righteousness and holiness.
Therefore, having laid aside falsehood, let each of you speak truth with his neighbor, for we are members of one another.
“Be angry, yet do not sin; do not let the sun set upon your wrath.”
And give no opportunity to the devil.
Let the thief steal no longer; rather, let him toil, doing honest work with his own hands, so that he may have something to share with those in need.
Let no corrupt word proceed from your mouth, but only what is good for edification according to the need, that it may impart grace to those who hear.
And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
Let all bitterness, rage, anger, clamor, and slander be removed from you, together with all malice.
Rather, be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other, just as God in Christ forgave you.
Become, therefore, imitators of God, as His dearly beloved children,
and conduct yourselves in love, even as Christ loved us and surrendered Himself on our behalf—an offering and sacrifice to God, a fragrant aroma.
Yet among you, as befits the saints, let not even a whisper of sexual immorality, nor any impurity, nor covetousness be named;
neither obscenity, nor foolish discourse, nor scurrilous jesting—things unbecoming—but rather thanksgiving.
For you know this with certainty: that no sexually immoral person, nor impure person, nor covetous person—that is, an idolater—possesses any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.
Let no one beguile you with vain words, for on account of these things the wrath of God descends upon the sons of disobedience.
Therefore do not become co-participants with them.
For once you were darkness, but now you are light in the Lord; walk, therefore, as children of light,
for the fruit of the light is found in all goodness, righteousness, and truth,
discerning what is well-pleasing to the Lord.
And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather expose them;
for it is shameful even to recount the things wrought by them in secret.
Yet all things, when brought to light, are made manifest, for whatever is made manifest is light.
Hence it is said, “Awake, O sleeper, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall shine upon you.”
Look carefully, then, how you walk—not as the unwise, but as the wise—
making the most of your time, for the days are evil.
Wherefore do not be foolish, but apprehend what the will of the Lord is.
And do not be intoxicated with wine, wherein lies debauchery, but be filled with the Spirit,
addressing one another in psalms, hymns, and spiritual odes, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord;
always rendering thanks for all things, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to God the Father;
and submitting yourselves to one another in the reverence of Christ.
Wives, submit yourselves to your own husbands, as unto the Lord.
For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church, He Himself being the Savior of the body.
But as the church is subject to Christ, so also wives ought to be subject to their husbands in all things.
Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ loved the church and delivered Himself up for her,
that He might sanctify her, having cleansed her by the washing of water with the word,
that He might present her to Himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle or any such blemish, but that she should be holy and without blemish.
So too ought husbands to love their own wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife loves himself;
for no one ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it, even as Christ does the church,
for we are members of His body.
“For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall be joined to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh.”
This mystery is profound; yet I am speaking concerning Christ and the church.
Nevertheless, let each one of you love his own wife even as himself, and let the wife see that she reverence her husband.
Children, render obedience to your parents in the Lord, for this is the essence of righteousness.
“Honor your father and mother”—the first commandment that carries a promise—
that it may fare well with you and that you may be long-lived upon the earth.
And fathers, do not provoke your children to wrath; rather, nurture them in the discipline and admonition of the Lord.
Slaves, obey your earthly masters with reverential fear and trembling, in the sincerity of your heart, as unto Christ;
not as men-pleasers rendering service solely under scrutiny, but as slaves of Christ, executing the will of God from the soul;
serving with benevolence, as to the Lord and not to mortals,
knowing that whatever good each one performs, he will receive recompense from the Lord, whether slave or free.
And masters, act reciprocally toward them, relinquishing threats, cognizant that their Master and yours is in heaven, and that there is no partiality with Him.
Finally, be empowered in the Lord and in the might of His strength.
Clothe yourselves in the full armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the stratagems of the devil.

For our contest is not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against authorities, against the cosmic rulers of this darkness, against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly realms.
Therefore take up the full armor of God, that in the evil day you may be able to withstand, and having accomplished all, to stand.
Stand firm, therefore, having girded your loins with truth and having put on the breastplate of righteousness;
and having shod your feet with the preparation of the gospel of peace;
in all circumstances taking up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to quench all the flaming darts of the evil one;
and take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God;
praying in the Spirit at all times with every prayer and supplication, and to this end keeping alert with all perseverance and supplication for all the saints.
And for me, that utterance may be granted me in the opening of my mouth, to proclaim with boldness the mystery of the gospel,
for which I am an ambassador in chains, that I may speak boldly therein, as it behooves me to speak.
Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, will acquaint you with all things, so that you too may know my circumstances and what I am doing.
I have sent him to you for this very purpose, that you may know our affairs and that he may comfort your hearts.
Peace be to the brothers, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ with incorruptible love.
Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, together with the overseers and deacons:
grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I give thanks to my God for every remembrance of you,
always in every prayer of mine making my petition for all of you with joy,
on account of your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until the present.
Being convinced of this very proposition, that the One who inaugurated a good work in you will bring it to consummation until the day of Christ Jesus.

It is altogether just for me to entertain this conviction concerning all of you, because I cherish you in my heart, inasmuch as, both in my bonds and in the defense and vindication of the gospel, you are all co-participants with me in grace.
For God is my witness how I yearn for all of you with the tender mercies of Christ Jesus.
And this is my prayer: that your love may overflow yet more and more in full knowledge and in all discernment,
so that you may test and approve what is superior, in order that you may be pure and blameless until the day of Christ,
having been filled with the fruit of righteousness that is through Jesus Christ, unto the glory and praise of God.
Now I desire you to know, brothers, that my circumstances have rather conduced to the advancement of the gospel,
so that my bonds have become evident throughout the whole praetorium and to all others, as being in Christ;
and the majority of the brothers, having gained confidence in the Lord because of my bonds, are far more emboldened to proclaim the word without fear.
Some, to be sure, proclaim Christ from envy and contention, but others from goodwill.
The latter do so out of love, knowing that I am set for the defense of the gospel;
the former announce Christ out of selfish ambition, not with pure motives, imagining that they are adding affliction to my bonds.
What then? Only that in every manner, whether in pretense or in truth, Christ is proclaimed; and in this I rejoice—indeed, I will continue to rejoice.
For I know that this will result in my deliverance through your supplication and the provision of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,

in accordance with my earnest expectation and hope, that in nothing shall I be ashamed, but that with all boldness, as always, so now also Christ shall be magnified in my body, whether by life or by death.
For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
Yet if to live in the flesh means fruitful labor for me, then what I shall choose I know not.
For I am constrained between the two, having the longing to depart and be with Christ, for that is far better;
yet to abide in the flesh is more needful for your sake.
And being persuaded of this, I know that I shall remain and continue with all of you for your advancement and joy in the faith,
so that your glorying in Christ Jesus may overflow toward me through my coming to you again.

Only let your manner of life be worthy of the gospel of Christ, so that whether I come and see you or remain absent, I may hear of your circumstances, that you stand firm in one spirit, contending together with one soul for the faith of the gospel,
and in nothing terrified by the adversaries; which is to them an evident token of destruction, but to you of salvation, and that from God.
For to you it has been graciously granted on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for Him,
having the same struggle which you saw in me and now hear in me.
Therefore, if there is any encouragement in Christ, if any solace of love, if any communion of the Spirit, if any tender affections and mercies,
complete my joy by being of one mind, possessing the same love, being united in spirit and intent upon one purpose.
Do nothing from selfish ambition or vainglory, but in humility regard one another as surpassing yourselves.
Let each of you look not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others.
Have this mind among you which was also in Christ Jesus:
Who, though existing in the form of God, did not regard equality with God as something to be seized,
but emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, being born in the likeness of men.
And being found in appearance as a man, He humbled Himself and became obedient unto death—even death on a cross.
Therefore God exalted Him to the highest place and bestowed upon Him the name above every name,
so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven and on earth and under the earth,
and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence but now much more in my absence, work out your salvation with fear and trembling;
for it is God who works in you, both to will and to work, for His good pleasure.
Do all things without grumbling or disputing,
that you may be blameless and innocent, children of God without blemish in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation, among whom you shine as luminaries in the world,
holding fast the word of life, so that I may boast on the day of Christ that I did not run in vain nor labor in vain.
But even if I am being poured out as a libation upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice and share joy with all of you.
Likewise you also should rejoice and share joy with me.
Now I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I too may be encouraged when I learn of your circumstances.
For I have no one like-minded who will genuinely care for your concerns;
for all seek their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.
But you know his proven worth, that as a child serves a father, so he served with me in the gospel.
Therefore I hope to send him immediately, as soon as I see how things go with me.
And I am confident in the Lord that I myself will come soon.
But I deemed it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier, who is also your messenger and minister to my need,
since he was longing for all of you and was distressed because you heard that he was ill.
For indeed he was ill, near to death; but God had mercy on him, and not only on him but also on me, lest I should have sorrow upon sorrow.
Therefore I am the more eager to send him, so that when you see him again you may rejoice, and I may be less sorrowful.
Receive him, then, in the Lord with all joy, and hold such men in honor,
because for the work of Christ he drew near to death, risking his life to make up for your deficiency of service to me.
Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. It imposes no onerous burden upon me to reiterate these same admonitions to you; indeed, such repetition constitutes a safeguard for you.
Beware of the dogs; beware of the malevolent laborers; beware of the mutilation.
For we are the authentic circumcision—those who render worship by the Spirit of God, boast in Christ Jesus, and repose no confidence in the flesh.
Though I myself might repose confidence in the flesh—if any other presumes to repose confidence in the flesh, I possess still greater warrant:
circumcised on the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew sprung from Hebrews; as to the law, a Pharisee;
as to zeal, a persecutor of the church; as to righteousness derived from the law, blameless.
Yet whatever things were gains to me, these I have reckoned as loss for Christ’s sake.

Indeed, I count all things to be loss on account of the transcendent excellence of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord, for whose sake I have suffered the loss of all things and regard them as rubbish, that I may gain Christ.
and be found in Him, not possessing a righteousness of my own derived from the law, but that which is through faith in Christ—the righteousness that proceeds from God on the basis of faith—
that I may know Him and the power of His resurrection, and the fellowship of His sufferings, being conformed to His death,
if somehow I may attain to the resurrection from the dead.
Not that I have already obtained it or have already been perfected; but I press on, if indeed I may lay hold of that for which Christ Jesus also laid hold of me.
Brothers, I do not reckon myself to have laid hold of it; but one thing I do: forgetting the things behind and stretching forward to the things ahead,
I press on toward the goal for the prize of the upward calling of God in Christ Jesus.
Let as many of us as are mature hold this view; and if in anything you think differently, God will reveal even this to you.
Nevertheless, let us walk by the same standard to which we have attained.
Brothers, become fellow imitators of me, and observe those who walk in this manner, just as you have us as a pattern.
For many walk—of whom I have often told you, and now tell you even weeping—as enemies of the cross of Christ.
Whose end is destruction, whose god is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame—those who set their minds on earthly things.
For our citizenship is in heaven, from which we also eagerly await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ,
who will transform our lowly body to be conformed to His glorious body, according to the working of His power, by which He is able even to subject all things to Himself.
Consequently, my beloved and deeply longed-for brothers—my joy and crown—stand firm in the Lord in this manner, beloved.
I exhort Euodia, and I exhort Syntyche, to be of one mind in the Lord.

Yes, I also entreat you, my genuine yokefellow, to assist these women, who contended at my side in the gospel, together with Clement and my other fellow workers, whose names are inscribed in the book of life.
Rejoice in the Lord always; again I say, rejoice.
Let your gentleness be made known to all people. The Lord is near.
Be anxious about nothing; rather, in everything, by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
And the peace of God, which transcends all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.

Finally, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is just, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is commendable—if there is any excellence and if there is anything praiseworthy—give careful thought to these things.
What you have learned and received and heard and seen in me—practice these things, and the God of peace will be with you.
I have rejoiced greatly in the Lord that now, at last, you have renewed your concern for me; you were indeed mindful of me, yet you lacked opportunity.
Not that I speak from want, for I have learned to be content in whatever state I am.
I know how to be brought low, and I know how to abound; in every circumstance I have learned the secret of being well fed and of going hungry, of having abundance and of suffering want.
I can do all things through Him who strengthens me.
Nevertheless, you did well to share in my affliction.
And you Philippians know that in the beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church entered into partnership with me in the matter of giving and receiving except you alone.
For even in Thessalonica you sent more than once to supply my need.
Not that I seek the gift, but I seek the fruit that accrues to your account.
I have received all things and abound; I am fully supplied, having received from Epaphroditus what you sent, a fragrant aroma, an acceptable sacrifice, well-pleasing to God.
And my God will supply all your need according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
Now to our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen.
Greet every saint in Christ Jesus. The brothers with me greet you.
All the saints greet you, and especially those of Caesar's household.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother,
to the saints and faithful brothers in Christ who are in Colossae: grace and peace be to you from God our Father.
We always give thanks to God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying for you,
since we have heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and of the love you bear toward all the saints,
because of the hope reserved for you in heaven, which you first heard in the word of truth, the gospel,
which has come to you, just as it is bearing fruit and increasing throughout the whole world, as it also does among you from the day you heard it and truly apprehended the grace of God;
just as you learned it from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant, who is a faithful minister of Christ on your behalf,
who has also disclosed to us your love in the Spirit.
For this reason, we too, from the day we heard of it, have not ceased praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of His will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding,
so that you may walk in a manner worthy of the Lord, fully pleasing to Him, bearing fruit in every good work and increasing in the knowledge of God,
being strengthened with all power according to the might of His glory, unto all endurance and patience with joy,
giving thanks to the Father, who has qualified you to share in the inheritance of the saints in light.
He has delivered us from the authority of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of His beloved Son,
in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.
He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation;
for in Him all things were created, in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities—all things have been created through Him and for Him.
And He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together.
And He is the head of the body, the church; He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that He might be preeminent in all things.
For in Him all the fullness was pleased to dwell,
and through Him to reconcile all things to Himself, whether things on earth or things in heaven, having made peace through the blood of His cross.
And you, who once were alienated and hostile in mind, doing evil works,
He has now reconciled in the body of His flesh through death, in order to present you holy and blameless and above reproach before Him,

if indeed you continue in the faith, grounded and steadfast, and are not moved away from the hope of the gospel you heard, which has been proclaimed in all creation under heaven, of which I, Paul, became a minister.
Now I rejoice in my sufferings for your sake, and in my flesh I fill up what is lacking in the afflictions of Christ for the sake of His body, that is, the church,
of which I became a minister according to the stewardship of God given to me for you, to fulfill the word of God,
the mystery that has been hidden for ages and generations but now has been revealed to His saints.
To them God willed to make known the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.
Him we proclaim, admonishing every person and teaching every person in all wisdom, so that we may present every person perfect in Christ.
For this I labor, striving according to His working that works powerfully in me.
For I would have you know what an immense contest I sustain on your behalf, and on behalf of those in Laodicea, and on behalf of all who have never beheld my face in the flesh—

that their hearts may be consoled, being compacted together in love, and attaining unto the entire wealth of the full assurance of understanding, unto the recognition of the mystery of God, namely Christ,
in whom are concealed all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
I declare this lest anyone should beguile you with plausible discourse.
For although I am absent in flesh, nevertheless I am present with you in spirit, rejoicing and beholding your good order and the steadfastness of your faith in Christ.
Therefore, as you received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in Him,
rooted and edified in Him, and confirmed in the faith, even as you were instructed, abounding in thanksgiving.
Take heed lest anyone despoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, according to human tradition, according to the rudiments of the world, and not according to Christ.
For in Him dwells all the fullness of the Deity bodily,
and you are made full in Him, who is the head of every principality and authority.
In whom you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands, in the putting off of the body of the flesh, in the circumcision of Christ,
having been buried with Him in baptism, wherein you were raised together with Him through faith in the working of God, who raised Him from the dead.
And you, being dead in your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, He made alive together with Him, having graciously forgiven us all our trespasses,
having blotted out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and having removed it out of the midst, nailing it to the cross.
Having stripped off the principalities and powers, He made a public exhibition of them, triumphing over them in Him.
Let no one therefore judge you in food or in drink, or in respect of a feast day, or new moon, or Sabbaths,
which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is Christ’s.
Let no one beguile you of your reward, taking delight in humility and the worship of angels, dwelling upon things he has seen, being vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind,
and not holding fast the head, from whom the whole body, being supplied and knit together through joints and ligaments, grows with the growth of God.
If you died with Christ from the rudiments of the world, why, as though living in the world, do you submit to decrees—
“Do not handle, neither taste, nor touch”—
all which things are to perish in the using, according to the commandments and doctrines of men?
These things indeed have an appearance of wisdom in will-worship, and humility, and severity to the body, but are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh.
Therefore, if you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God.
Set your minds on the things above, not on terrestrial concerns.
For you died, and your life is concealed with Christ in God.
When Christ, who is your life, is manifested, then you also will be manifested with Him in glory.
Therefore, put to death your earthly members: sexual immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire, and greed—which is idolatry.
On account of these things the wrath of God is coming upon the sons of disobedience.
You once walked among them, when you were living in them.
But now you must also rid yourselves of all these: anger, wrath, malice, slander, and obscene language from your mouth.
Do not deceive one another, having stripped off the old self with its practices
and having clothed yourselves with the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge according to the image of its Creator.
In this renewal there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave or free, but Christ is all and in all.
Therefore, as God's chosen, holy and beloved, array yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, meekness, and patience.
Bear with one another and forgive one another; if anyone has a grievance against another, forgive as the Lord forgave you.
And above all these, put on love, which is the bond of perfection.
And let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, to which you were indeed called in one body; and be thankful.
Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly, as you teach and admonish one another in all wisdom, singing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with grace in your hearts to God.
And whatever you do, in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.
Wives, be subject to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.
Husbands, love your wives and do not grow bitter toward them.
Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is well-pleasing in the Lord.
Fathers, do not exasperate your children, lest they become discouraged.
Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything—not with eye-service, as people-pleasers, but in sincerity of heart, fearing the Lord.
Whatever you do, labor with your whole soul, as for the Lord and not for men,
knowing that from the Lord you will receive the inheritance as your reward; you serve the Lord Christ.
For the wrongdoer will receive back what he has done wrong, and there is no partiality.
Masters, furnish your slaves with what is just and equitable, recognizing that you too have a Master in heaven.
Devote yourselves steadfastly to prayer, remaining watchful therein with thanksgiving,
while concurrently interceding for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, so that we may proclaim the mystery of Christ, on account of which I am in chains.
And pray that I may disclose it with the clarity incumbent upon me.
Conduct yourselves with wisdom toward outsiders, making the most of the occasion.
Let your speech be invariably gracious and aptly seasoned, so that you may discern how you ought to respond to each person.
Tychicus will apprise you of all my circumstances; he is the beloved brother, a faithful minister, and a fellow servant in the Lord.
I have dispatched him to you for this very end, that you may learn of our circumstances and that he may console your hearts.
He is accompanied by Onesimus, the faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will disclose to you everything here.
Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, greets you, as does Mark, the cousin of Barnabas. (You have received instructions concerning him; if he comes to you, receive him.)
And Jesus, who is called Justus. These alone, being of the circumcision, are my fellow workers for the kingdom of God, and they have been a solace to me.
Epaphras, who is one of you and a servant of Christ Jesus, greets you. He is always wrestling in prayer on your behalf, that you may stand mature and fully assured in all the will of God.
For I bear witness to him that he exerts himself greatly on your behalf, and on behalf of those in Laodicea and Hierapolis.
Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas greet you.
Greet the brothers in Laodicea, and Nympha, and the church in her house.
And when this letter has been read among you, arrange for it to be read also in the church of the Laodiceans, and see that you yourselves read the one from Laodicea.
And tell Archippus, “See that you fulfill the ministry you have received in the Lord.”
The greeting is in my own hand—Paul. Remember my chains. Grace be with you.
Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy—to the church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace to you and peace.
We always give thanks to God for all of you, making mention of you in our prayers,
unceasingly remembering before our God and Father your work of faith, your labor of love, and your steadfastness of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ,
brothers beloved by God, knowing your election,
because our gospel came to you not only in word but also in power and in the Holy Spirit and in much full assurance, just as you know what manner of men we proved to be among you for your sake.
And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, having received the word with joy of the Holy Spirit in much affliction,
so that you became an example to all the believers in Macedonia and in Achaia.
For not only has the word of the Lord sounded forth from you in Macedonia and in Achaia, but your faith toward God has gone out in every place, so that we have no need to say anything.
For they themselves report concerning us what kind of reception we had among you, and how you turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God,
and to wait for His Son from heaven, whom He raised from the dead—Jesus, who delivers us from the wrath to come.
For you yourselves know, brothers, that our advent among you was not in vain.

As you are aware, having already endured affliction and suffered ignominious treatment at Philippi, we nevertheless found, in our God, the boldness to proclaim to you the gospel of God amid great contention.
For our exhortation does not issue from delusion, nor from impurity, nor from guile.
But, just as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the gospel, so we speak—not as men-pleasers, but as those who seek to please God, who scrutinizes our hearts.
For, as you know, we never resorted to flattering discourse, nor did we employ a pretext for avarice—God is our witness—
nor did we seek glory from human beings, whether from you or from others, though, as apostles of Christ, we might have imposed a burden.
On the contrary, we proved gentle in your midst, like a nursing mother cherishing her own children.
Thus, yearning for you, we were delighted to share with you not only the gospel of God but our very lives as well, because you had become exceedingly dear to us.
For you remember, brothers, our labor and toil: working night and day, so as not to impose a burden upon any of you, we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.
You are witnesses, as is God, of how devoutly, justly, and blamelessly we conducted ourselves among you who believe.
As you know, we exhorted, consoled, and solemnly charged each one of you, as a father does his own children,
so that you might walk in a manner worthy of God, who calls you into His own kingdom and glory.

And for this reason we too give thanks to God unceasingly: because, when you received the word of God that you heard from us, you accepted it not as the word of men, but, as it truly is, the word of God, which is also operative in you who believe.
For you, brothers, became imitators of the churches of God in Judea that are in Christ Jesus; for you suffered from your own countrymen the same things they suffered from the Jews,
who killed both the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and drove us out as well. They are displeasing to God and hostile to all people,
hindering us from speaking to the Gentiles so that they might be saved, with the result that they always fill up the measure of their sins; but wrath has come upon them at last.
But we, brothers, though torn away from you for a short time—in person, not in heart—were all the more eager, with intense longing, to see your face.
For we desired to come to you—I, Paul, indeed, more than once—but Satan obstructed us.
For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of boasting, if not you yourselves before our Lord Jesus at His coming?
For you are indeed our glory and joy.
Accordingly, when our fortitude could endure the separation no longer, we resolved to remain alone in Athens.
Moreover, we dispatched Timothy—our brother and God’s collaborator in proclaiming the gospel of Christ—to establish and console your faith,
so that no one might be agitated by these tribulations; for you yourselves know that we are destined for this.
Indeed, even while we were among you, we forewarned you that we were destined to suffer affliction, precisely as it has transpired, and you are aware.
Therefore, when my own endurance was exhausted, I dispatched inquiry concerning your faith, lest the tempter had somehow assailed you and our labor should be rendered vain.
But now Timothy has returned to us from you, bearing glad tidings of your faith and love, and of your perpetual favorable remembrance of us, longing to see us, even as we likewise long for you.
Thus, brethren, in the midst of every exigency and tribulation, we found consolation regarding you, by virtue of your faith.
For now we genuinely live, provided that you remain steadfast in the Lord.
For what adequate thanksgiving could we possibly offer to God on your behalf, for all the exultation with which we rejoice because of you in the presence of our God,
supplicating night and day with superabundant earnestness that we might behold your countenance and remedy the deficiencies of your faith?
Now may our God and Father Himself, together with our Lord Jesus, make straight our way unto you.
And may the Lord cause you to proliferate and superabound in love toward one another and toward all, even as we also toward you,
so that He may establish your hearts blameless in holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all His saints. Amen.
Finally, then, brothers, we request and exhort you in the Lord Jesus that, just as you received from us how you must walk and please God—indeed, as you are walking—so you may abound all the more.
For you know what injunctions we delivered to you through the Lord Jesus.
For this is the will of God: your sanctification, namely, that you abstain from sexual immorality;
that each of you know how to acquire his own body in sanctification and honor,
not in the passion of lust, as do the Gentiles who do not know God;
that no one transgress and defraud his brother in this matter, because the Lord is an avenger concerning all these things, as we also forewarned you and solemnly testified.
For God did not call us to impurity but in sanctification.
Therefore, whoever rejects this does not reject a human being but God, who also gives His Holy Spirit to you.
Now concerning brotherly love, you have no need for us to write to you, for you yourselves are taught by God to love one another.
Indeed, you are doing so toward all the brothers throughout Macedonia. But we exhort you, brothers, to abound still more,
and to aspire to live quietly, to mind your own affairs, and to work with your own hands, just as we instructed you,
so that you may walk decorously toward outsiders and be in need of nothing.
But we do not want you to be uninformed, brothers, concerning those who are asleep, so that you may not grieve as the rest do who have no hope.
For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, so too will God bring with Him those who have fallen asleep through Jesus.
For this we declare to you by a word of the Lord: we who are alive, who remain until the coming of the Lord, will not precede those who have fallen asleep.
For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a cry of command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God; and the dead in Christ will rise first.
Then we who are alive, who remain, will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and so we will always be with the Lord.
Therefore encourage one another with these words.
Now, concerning the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no necessity for anything to be inscribed for you,
for you yourselves know with meticulous precision that the day of the Lord arrives unexpectedly and furtively.
When they are declaring, “Peace and security,” then abrupt ruination overtakes them, just as the acute pangs of childbirth seize a woman heavy with child, and they shall in no wise elude it.
But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that that day should overtake you unawares;
for you are all sons of light and sons of day—we are not of night, nor of darkness.
Therefore let us not slumber, as the rest do, but let us keep watch and remain sober.
For those who slumber slumber by night, and those who are intoxicated are intoxicated by night.
But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, having put on the breastplate of faith and love, and, as a helmet, the hope of salvation.
For God did not appoint us to wrath, but to acquire salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,
who died for us, so that whether we are awake or asleep we might live together with Him.
Therefore encourage one another and edify one another, just as you are already doing.
Now we ask you, brothers, to acknowledge those who toil among you and exercise oversight over you in the Lord and admonish you,
and to regard them with superabundant esteem in love because of their work. Cultivate peace among yourselves.
We urge you, brothers, to admonish the unruly, to comfort the fainthearted, to sustain the infirm, and to be long-suffering toward all.
See to it that no one recompenses evil for evil, but always pursue what is good, both toward one another and toward all.
render thanksgiving in all circumstances, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
do not treat prophecies with contempt;
but scrutinize all things, and retain tenaciously that which is good.
Abstain from every species of evil.
Now may the God of peace Himself sanctify you completely, and may your whole spirit, soul, and body be kept irreproachable at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
The One who calls you is faithful, and He will assuredly bring it to pass.
Greet all the brothers with a sacred kiss.
I adjure you by the Lord that this epistle be recited to all the brothers.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ remain with you.
Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

We are bound to render thanks to God at all times for you, brothers, as is fitting, because your faith is increasing beyond measure and the love of each one of you all toward one another is abounding;
so that we ourselves boast of you among the churches of God for your perseverance and faith in all your persecutions and afflictions, which you endure.
This constitutes evidence of God’s righteous judgment, namely, that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you also suffer;
since it is indeed just with God to repay affliction to those who afflict you,
and to grant relief to you who are afflicted, along with us, at the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven with His mighty angels,
in flaming fire, inflicting vengeance upon those who do not know God and upon those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus.
They shall pay the penalty of eternal destruction, away from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of His might,
when He comes on that day to be glorified in His saints and to be marveled at among all who have believed, because our testimony to you was believed.
To this end we also pray always for you, that our God may count you worthy of His calling and may fulfill every good purpose and every work of faith with power,
so that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in Him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Now, regarding the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering unto Him, we entreat you, brothers;
do not be precipitously unsettled in mind, nor be terrified, whether by spirit, or by discourse, or by epistle as if from us, to the effect that the day of the Lord has already arrived.
Let no one beguile you in any manner, for that day shall not arrive unless the apostasy come first and the man of lawlessness be disclosed, the son of perdition,
who opposes and exalts himself above every so-called god or object of veneration, so that he seats himself in the temple of God, exhibiting himself as though he were God.
Do you not recollect that, while I was yet with you, I was declaring these things to you?
And you know what now restrains him, so that he may be disclosed in his appointed season.
For the mystery of lawlessness is already operative; only the one who now restrains will continue to do so until he is removed from the midst.
And then the lawless one will be disclosed, whom the Lord Jesus will slay with the breath of His mouth and annihilate by the epiphany of His coming—
the coming whose operation is according to Satan, with all power and spurious signs and portents,
and with every deceit of unrighteousness among those who are perishing, because they did not receive the love of the truth so as to be saved.
Therefore God sends them an operative delusion, that they should believe the lie,
in order that all may be judged who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in unrighteousness.

But we are bound always to give thanks to God for you, brothers beloved by the Lord, because God chose you from the beginning unto salvation through sanctification by the Spirit and belief in the truth,
unto which He also called you through our gospel, for the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So then, brothers, stand firm and hold fast the traditions which you were taught, whether by word or by our epistle.
Now may our Lord Jesus Christ Himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us everlasting consolation and good hope through grace,
comfort your hearts and establish them in every good word and work.
Finally, brothers, intercede on our behalf, that the word of the Lord might run swiftly and be glorified, even as it has been among you,
and that we may be rescued from perverse and malevolent persons, for faith is not the possession of all.
Yet the Lord is faithful, and He will establish you and guard you from the evil one.
Moreover, we have confidence in the Lord regarding you, that you are both practicing and will continue to practice the injunctions we lay upon you.
And may the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God and into the patient endurance of Christ.

Now we charge you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to withdraw from every brother who conducts himself in a disorderly manner and not in accordance with the tradition you received from us.
For you yourselves know how fitting it is for you to emulate us, because we did not conduct ourselves disorderly among you.
Nor did we partake of anyone's bread gratis, but labored with toil and hardship night and day, lest we should burden any of you.
Not because we lack authority, but in order to present ourselves as a paradigm for you, that you might emulate us.
For even when we were among you, we enjoined upon you this precept: “If anyone is unwilling to work, let him not eat.”
For we hear that certain individuals among you are conducting themselves in a disorderly fashion, doing no work, but meddling in others' affairs.
Now we charge and exhort such persons in the Lord Jesus Christ to work quietly and to eat their own bread.
But as for you, brothers, do not lose heart in doing good.
And if anyone refuses to heed our instruction conveyed through this epistle, mark that person and do not consort with him, so that he may be put to shame.
Yet do not esteem him as an adversary, but admonish him as a brother.
Now may the Lord of peace Himself grant you peace at all times and in every manner. The Lord be with all of you.
This salutation is by my own hand—Paul; this is a sign in every letter; thus I write.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you.
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the command of God our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope,
to Timothy, my genuine child in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
As I urged you while I was going into Macedonia, remain in Ephesus, so that you may command certain persons not to teach a different doctrine,
nor to devote themselves to myths and endless genealogies, which foster speculations rather than the stewardship of God that is by faith.
The aim of our charge is love that proceeds from a pure heart, a good conscience, and a sincere faith.
Certain persons, having strayed from these, have turned aside to vain discussion,
desiring to be teachers of the law, though they understand neither what they are saying nor the matters about which they make confident assertions.
Now we know that the law is good, if one uses it lawfully,

knowing this: that the law is not laid down for the righteous, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for patricides and matricides, for murderers,
for the sexually immoral, for men who practice homosexuality, for enslavers, for liars, for perjurers, and for whatever else is contrary to sound doctrine,
in accordance with the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, with which I have been entrusted.
I give thanks to Him who has strengthened me, Christ Jesus our Lord, because He judged me faithful by appointing me to His service,
though formerly I was a blasphemer, a persecutor, and an insolent opponent. But I received mercy because I had acted ignorantly in unbelief,
and the grace of our Lord overflowed for me with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
The saying is trustworthy and deserving of full acceptance: that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the foremost.
But I received mercy for this reason, that in me, as the foremost, Christ Jesus might display His perfect patience as an example to those who are to believe in Him for eternal life.
To the King of the ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
This charge I entrust to you, Timothy, my child, in accordance with the prophecies previously made concerning you, that by them you may wage the good warfare,
holding faith and a good conscience. By rejecting these, some have made shipwreck of their faith,
among whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have handed over to Satan that they may learn not to blaspheme.
First of all, then, I exhort that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and eucharistic thanksgivings be offered on behalf of all humanity;
on behalf of sovereigns and all who occupy positions of eminence, so that we may pass our days in an untroubled and tranquil existence, marked by comprehensive piety and dignified decorum.
This conduct is noble and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior,
who desires all people to be delivered and to arrive at a full epistemic apprehension of the truth.
For there is one God and one mediator between God and humankind—the man Christ Jesus—
who surrendered Himself as a ransom for all, a testimony rendered in its own appointed seasons.
For this purpose I was ordained a herald and apostle—I speak the truth and do not lie—a teacher of the nations in faith and truth.
I desire, therefore, that men in every locality pray, elevating holy hands, apart from wrath and contentious disputation.
Likewise, women ought to adorn themselves in modest apparel, with propriety and sobriety, not with elaborate braids, gold, pearls, or sumptuous garments,
but with the good works befitting women who profess reverence for God.
Let a woman learn in quietude, in full submission.
I do not, however, permit a woman to teach, nor to exercise authority over a man, but to remain in quietude.
For Adam was fashioned first, and then Eve;
and Adam was not deceived, but the woman, having been thoroughly beguiled, fell into transgression.
Yet she shall be saved through childbearing, provided that they abide in faith, love, and sanctification, accompanied by sobriety.
This is a trustworthy saying: if anyone aspires to oversight, he covets a noble work.
Consequently, an overseer must be irreproachable, devoted to a single wife, temperate, prudent, respectable, hospitable, and didactically competent;
he must not be addicted to wine, nor pugnacious, but forbearing, peaceable, and averse to avarice;
he must manage his own household admirably, keeping his children in submission with all gravity.
For if a man cannot preside over his own household, how shall he superintend the church of God?
He must not be a neophyte, lest, inflated with conceit, he fall into the devil's condemnation;
moreover, he must possess an estimable testimony from outsiders, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.
Likewise, deacons must be venerable, not duplicitous in speech, not devoted to copious wine, not sordidly avaricious;
they must hold the mystery of the faith with a pure conscience.
And let these too be examined first; then, being found blameless, let them minister.
Likewise, women must be venerable, not calumnious, sober, and faithful in all respects.
Deacons must be men of one wife, managing their children and their own households commendably.
For those who have ministered well acquire for themselves a noble rank and much boldness in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
Hoping to come to you soon, I write these things to you.
But if I am delayed, you may know how one must comport oneself in the household of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.

And, by common confession, great is the mystery of godliness: He was revealed in flesh, vindicated by the Spirit, seen by angels, heralded among the nations, believed upon in the world, and received up in glory.

The Spirit states with unmistakable clarity that in the latter times some will apostatize from the faith, devoting themselves to deceitful spirits and to demonic doctrines—disseminated through the hypocrisy of mendacious men whose consciences have been cauterized—
while forbidding marriage and enjoining abstinence from foods that God created to be received with gratitude by the faithful and by those who have come to know the truth.
For every creation of God is good, and nothing received with thanksgiving is to be rejected,
since it is consecrated by the word of God and by prayer.
If you set these matters before the brothers, you will prove yourself a good servant of Christ Jesus, being nourished by the words of the faith and by the sound doctrine that you have followed.
But shun profane and superstitious fables; instead, discipline yourself for godliness.
For physical training yields only limited benefit, whereas godliness is beneficial in every respect, since it carries the promise of both the present life and the life to come.
The saying is trustworthy and deserving of full acceptance.
For it is to this end that we labor and contend, because we have set our hope on the living God, who is the Savior of all humanity, and especially of those who believe.
Let no one treat your youth with contempt; rather, become a model for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, and in purity.
Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading, to exhortation, and to teaching.
Do not neglect the gift that resides in you, which was conferred upon you through prophecy together with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.
Ponder these matters; be absorbed in them, so that your advancement may be manifest to everyone.
Keep close watch over yourself and over the teaching; remain in them, for by doing so you will save both yourself and those who listen to you.
Do not rebuke an older man harshly, but exhort him as a father; address younger men as brothers,
older women as mothers, and younger women as sisters, with uncompromising purity.
Honor widows who are genuinely widows.

Yet if any widow has children or grandchildren, let these first learn to manifest piety in their own household and to render due recompense to their progenitors, for this is acceptable in the sight of God.
Now the widow who is truly bereft of support has set her hope upon God and persists in supplications and prayers night and day.
But she who lives in voluptuous indulgence is dead while she still lives.
Command these things, so that they may be irreproachable.
But if anyone does not provide for his own, and especially for those of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
Let a widow be enrolled only if she has reached at least sixty years, having been the wife of one husband,
and is attested by good works: whether she has reared children, shown hospitality, washed the feet of the saints, relieved the afflicted, and devoted herself to every good work.
But refuse younger widows; for when their passions draw them away from Christ, they desire to marry,
incurring condemnation because they have repudiated their first pledge.
At the same time they learn idleness, going from house to house; and not only idle, but gossips and busybodies, speaking what should not be spoken.
Therefore I wish younger widows to marry, bear children, manage their households, and afford the adversary no occasion for slander.
For some have already turned aside after Satan.
If any believing woman has widows, let her assist them, and let not the church be burdened, so that it may assist those who are truly widows.
Let elders who preside well be counted worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in word and teaching.
For the Scripture says, You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads out the grain, and, The laborer is worthy of his wages.
Do not receive an accusation against an elder except on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
Those who sin, rebuke before all, that the rest also may be seized by fear.
I charge you before God and Christ Jesus and the elect angels to keep these things without prejudice, doing nothing by partiality.
Do not lay hands on anyone hastily, nor share in others' sins; keep yourself pure.
No longer drink water only, but use a little wine because of your stomach and your frequent ailments.
The sins of some men are evident, going before them to judgment; but for others they follow after.
Likewise, good works are evident, and those that are otherwise cannot be concealed.
All who remain beneath the yoke of servitude must regard their own masters as meriting every species of honor, so that the name of God and the doctrine may not be subjected to blasphemy.

Those whose masters are believers are not to treat them with contempt on the pretext that they are brothers; rather, they are to render service all the more, precisely because those who partake of their beneficence are faithful and beloved. Teach and exhort these things.
If anyone propagates heterodox doctrine and refuses to acquiesce in the wholesome words of our Lord Jesus Christ and in the teaching consonant with piety,
he is inflated with conceit, knowing nothing, but is diseased with controversies and verbal strife, from which arise envy, contention, blasphemy, and baseless suspicions—
the chronic friction of people corrupted in mind and bereft of truth, who imagine that piety is a lucrative enterprise.
Yet piety accompanied by contentment constitutes a considerable gain,
