for we imported nothing into the world, and it is certain that we can export nothing from it;
and having sustenance and raiment, we shall be satisfied with these.

Those who are determined to become wealthy precipitate themselves into temptation and a snare, together with a multitude of senseless and deleterious cravings that submerge people in ruin and perdition.
For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil, and through their craving for it some have strayed from the faith and transfixed themselves with manifold anguish.
But you, O man of God, flee these things and pursue righteousness, piety, faith, love, endurance, and meekness.
Contend in the noble contest of the faith; lay hold of eternal life, to which you were summoned and concerning which you rendered the noble confession before many witnesses.
I charge you before God, who gives life to all things, and before Christ Jesus, who bore witness to the noble confession under Pontius Pilate,
that you keep the commandment unblemished and irreproachable until the manifestation of our Lord Jesus Christ,
which He will reveal in His own seasons—He who is the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of kings and Lord of lords,
who alone possesses immortality and inhabits light unapproachable, whom no human being has seen or is able to see; to Him be honor and everlasting dominion. Amen.
Charge those who are affluent in the present age not to be arrogant, nor to fix their confidence upon the instability of wealth, but upon God, who lavishly furnishes us with all things for enjoyment.
They are to perform beneficence, to be affluent in good works, to be munificent and disposed to share,
thereby amassing for themselves a noble foundation for the time to come, in order that they may lay hold upon what is truly life.
O Timothy, safeguard the deposit committed to your trust, shunning profane and empty discourses and the antitheses of what is mendaciously styled "knowledge,"
for by professing such, certain persons have deviated from the faith. Grace be with you.
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, according to the promise of life that is in Christ Jesus,
to Timothy, my beloved child: grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
I give thanks to God, whom I serve with a pure conscience, as my forebears did, since I retain an unceasing remembrance of you night and day in my prayers,
remembering your tears and longing to see you, so that I may be filled with joy.
I have been reminded of the unfeigned faith that dwells in you, which first took residence in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am persuaded that it dwells in you as well.
For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God that is in you through the laying on of my hands.
For God did not give us a spirit of cowardice, but of power, love, and self-discipline.
Therefore do not be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord, nor of me, His prisoner; rather, share in suffering for the gospel according to the power of God,
who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works but according to His own purpose and grace, granted to us in Christ Jesus before the ages began,
and now revealed through the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel.
For this gospel I was appointed a herald, an apostle, and a teacher.

For this reason I also suffer these things, yet I am not ashamed, for I know the One in whom I have placed my trust, and I am persuaded that He is able to guard the deposit entrusted to me until that day.
Hold fast the pattern of sound words that you heard from me, in the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
Guard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit, who dwells in us.
You know that all who are in Asia turned away from me, among whom are Phygelus and Hermogenes.
May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, for he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chain.
On the contrary, when he was in Rome, he searched diligently and found me.
May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord in that day—and you know better than I how many services he rendered in Ephesus.
You, my child, therefore, be strengthened by the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
Moreover, the things you heard from me in the presence of many witnesses, commit to faithful men who will be qualified to instruct others.
Join in hardship as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
No one engaged in military service entangles himself in the affairs of everyday life, so as to please the one who enlisted him.
Likewise, if anyone competes as an athlete, he is not crowned unless he has competed according to the rules.
The farmer who toils must be the first to partake of the fruits.
Reflect upon what I am saying, for the Lord will grant you discernment in all matters.
Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David, in accordance with my gospel,
for which I endure suffering, even to the point of imprisonment, as though I were a malefactor; yet the word of God is not shackled.
For this reason I endure everything for the sake of the elect, that they too may attain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, together with eternal glory.
This saying is trustworthy: if we died with Him, we shall also live with Him;
if we endure, we shall also reign with Him; if we disown Him, He will also disown us;
if we prove faithless, He remains faithful, for He cannot disown Himself.
Remind them of these things, solemnly charging them before God not to engage in verbal disputes, which serve no useful purpose and tend only to the ruin of those who listen.
Strive to present yourself to God as one approved, a workman who has no cause for shame, rightly handling the word of truth.
But avoid profane and empty chatter, for it will lead to further progress in ungodliness,
and their teaching will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
men who have deviated from the truth by asserting that the resurrection has already occurred, thereby overturning the faith of some.
Nevertheless, God’s firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Let everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord depart from wickedness.”
Now in a large household there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and earthenware, some for honorable use and some for dishonorable.
If, then, anyone cleanses himself from these things, he will be a vessel for honor, sanctified and useful to the Master, prepared for every good work.
Flee youthful passions, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, along with those who invoke the Lord from a pure heart.
Reject foolish and uneducated speculations, knowing that they beget quarrels.
And the Lord’s servant must not be quarrelsome, but must be gentle toward all, able to teach, and forbearing,
with gentleness correcting those who oppose him, in the hope that God may grant them repentance leading to a full knowledge of the truth,
and that they may come to their senses and escape from the snare of the devil, having been captured by him to do his will.
But know this: in the last days grievous times will come.
For people will be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, blasphemous, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, and unholy;
unloving, unforgiving, slanderous, without self-control, brutal, and averse to goodness;
treacherous, rash, conceited, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God.
They will maintain an outward semblance of piety while repudiating its power; and from such persons you must turn away.
For among them are those who insinuate themselves into households and make captives of susceptible women burdened with sins, swayed by manifold cravings,
perpetually learning yet never arriving at a knowledge of the truth.
Just as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so these men likewise withstand the truth; their minds are corrupted, and they are reprobate concerning the faith.
But they will not progress much further, for their folly will be manifest to everyone, as the folly of those men was.
You, however, have closely followed my teaching, my way of life, my purpose, my faith, my patience, my love, and my steadfastness,
together with my persecutions and sufferings, such as befell me at Antioch, at Iconium, and at Lystra—persecutions I endured, yet the Lord delivered me from all of them.
Indeed, everyone who wishes to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
But wicked people and charlatans will progress from bad to worse, deceiving others and being deceived themselves.
But as for you, abide in what you have learned and of which you have been assured, knowing from whom you learned it,
and that from infancy you have known the sacred Scriptures, which are able to impart wisdom unto you for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
All Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness,
so that the man of God may be thoroughly equipped, furnished for every good work.
I solemnly charge you before God and Christ Jesus, who is destined to judge the living and the dead, and in view of His appearing and His kingdom:
proclaim the word; stand ready whether the occasion is opportune or inopportune; expose error, censure, and exhort, exercising complete forbearance and doctrinal instruction.

For a season will arrive in which they will no longer tolerate wholesome teaching; rather, their ears, craving pleasing novelties, will prompt them to amass for themselves instructors consonant with their own cravings.
They will avert their ears from the truth and be diverted into fables.
But as for you, maintain sober-mindedness in every circumstance, endure affliction, perform the labor of an evangelist, and discharge your ministry in full.
For I am already being poured out as a libation, and the season of my dissolution is at hand.
I have waged the noble contest, completed the course, and preserved the faith.
Consequently, the crown of righteousness is reserved for me, which the Lord—the righteous Judge—will bestow upon me in that day, and not solely upon me but upon all who have cherished His appearing.
Strive to come to me without delay.
For Demas, enamored of the present age, has abandoned me and departed for Thessalonica; Crescens has gone to Galatia; and Titus to Dalmatia.
Luke alone remains with me. Retrieve Mark and bring him along with you, for he proves serviceable to me in ministry.
Tychicus I have dispatched to Ephesus.
When you arrive, bring the cloak I left with Carpus in Troas, together with the books—above all, the parchments.
Alexander the coppersmith inflicted considerable injury upon me; the Lord will recompense him commensurate with his works.
You likewise must be on guard against him, since he vehemently resisted our message.
At my initial defense, no one stood by me; rather, all forsook me. May it not be reckoned against them.
Yet the Lord stood beside me and empowered me, so that through me the proclamation might be brought to full fruition and all the nations might hear it; and I was delivered from the lion's mouth.
The Lord will deliver me from every malevolent work and will usher me safely into His heavenly kingdom; to Him belongs glory unto the ages of ages. Amen.
Convey my greetings to Prisca and Aquila, and to the household of Onesiphorus.
Erastus stayed behind in Corinth, while I left Trophimus ailing in Miletus.
Strive to arrive before winter. Eubulus sends you greetings, as do Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brethren.
The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you.
Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, in accordance with the faith of God’s elect and the knowledge of the truth that accords with godliness,
in hope of eternal life, which God, who cannot lie, promised before the ages began,
and at the proper time manifested His word through proclamation—a trust committed to me by the command of God our Savior—
to Titus, my genuine child in a common faith: Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
For this reason I left you in Crete, that you might set in order what remained unfinished and appoint elders in every city, just as I directed you,
if anyone is above reproach, the husband of one wife, with children who are faithful and not accused of dissipation or insubordination.
For an overseer, as God’s steward, must be above reproach—not self-willed, not quick-tempered, not given to wine, not violent, not greedy for dishonest gain—
but hospitable, devoted to goodness, self-controlled, upright, holy, and disciplined,
clinging to the trustworthy word as taught, so that he may be competent both to exhort by sound doctrine and to refute those who contradict it.
For there are many insubordinate people—empty talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision—
whose mouths must be silenced, since they subvert entire households by teaching what they ought not, all for sordid gain.
One of their own prophets has said, “Cretans are always liars, vicious beasts, lazy gluttons.”
This testimony is true; therefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith,
paying no heed to Jewish myths or to human commandments issued by those who turn away from the truth.
To the pure, all things are pure; but to the defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure—indeed, both their mind and their conscience are defiled.
They profess to know God, yet by their deeds they deny Him; they are abominable, disobedient, and disqualified for every good work.
But you must articulate what is consonant with salubrious doctrine:
older men are to be temperate, venerable, discreet, and robust in faith, in love, and in endurance;
older women, in like manner, are to be reverent in deportment, not calumnious, not enslaved to copious wine, but instructors of what is noble;
so that they may admonish the young women to be affectionate toward their husbands and children,
discreet, chaste, domestic, beneficent, and submissive to their own husbands, lest the word of God be blasphemed.
Likewise, exhort younger men to be self-controlled.
In all things, present yourself as a paradigm of noble works; in teaching, exhibit incorruptibility and gravity,
together with sound speech beyond reproach, so that any adversary may be put to shame, having no malignancy to allege concerning us.
Slaves are to be subject to their own masters in everything, to be well-pleasing, not contentious,
not pilfering, but demonstrating all good fidelity, so that in every respect they may adorn the doctrine of God our Savior.
For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all humanity,
training us to renounce impiety and worldly desires, and to live soberly, righteously, and devoutly in the present age,
while we await the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ,
Who gave Himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for Himself a people for His own possession, zealous for noble works.
Speak these things, exhort, and reprove with all authority; let no one despise you.
Admonish them to be subject to magistrates and authorities, to be obedient, and to remain prepared for every beneficent undertaking;
to calumniate no one, to be pacific and equitable, exhibiting complete forbearance toward all humanity.
For we ourselves were formerly insensate, recalcitrant, and led astray, enslaved to multifarious cravings and pleasures, conducting our lives in malice and envy, detestable and mutually abhorrent.
Yet when the benignity of God our Savior and His philanthropy toward humankind was disclosed,
He delivered us—not by deeds of righteousness that we had performed, but in accordance with His own mercy—through the laver of regeneration and the renovation wrought by the Holy Spirit,
whom He lavished upon us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior,
in order that, having been justified by His grace, we might become heirs in hope of life everlasting.

This saying is trustworthy, and I desire that you affirm these matters with conviction, so that those who have placed their trust in God may be solicitous to take the lead in noble works; for such pursuits are honorable and advantageous to humankind.
But shun foolish disputations, genealogies, contentions, and legalistic quarrels, for they are otiose and vain.
After a first and second admonition, have nothing to do with a divisive person,
knowing that such an individual is perverted and sinful, being self-condemned.
When I dispatch Artemas or Tychicus to you, endeavor to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have resolved to winter there.
Expedite the departure of Zenas the jurist and Apollos, so that they may lack nothing.
Moreover, let our own people learn to take the lead in noble works for pressing necessities, lest they be fruitless.
All who are with me send greetings to you. Greet those who cherish us in faith. Grace be with all of you.
Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy, our brother, to Philemon, our beloved fellow worker,
and to Apphia, our sister, and to Archippus, our fellow soldier, and to the church that meets in your house:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I always thank my God, making mention of you in my prayers,
because I hear of your love and faith toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the saints,
so that the sharing of your faith may become effective in the knowledge of every good thing that is in us for Christ.
For I have derived much joy and encouragement from your love, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, brother.
Therefore, although in Christ I possess abundant boldness to prescribe to you what is fitting,
yet, for love's sake, I prefer to appeal, being such a one as Paul, now an aged man and also a prisoner of Christ Jesus.
I appeal to you on behalf of my child Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my chains,
who was formerly useless to you, but now is useful both to you and to me.
I am sending him back to you; receive him, for he is my own heart.
I wished to retain him with me, so that on your behalf he might serve me in the chains of the gospel,
but without your consent I resolved to do nothing, in order that your good deed might not be as though by compulsion but of your own free will.
For perhaps for this reason he was separated from you for a while, that you might receive him back forever,
no longer as a slave, but more than a slave—a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
If, then, you regard me as a partner, receive him as you would me.
If he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge it to my account.
I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I will repay it—not to mention that you owe me even your own self.
Yes, brother, let me have some benefit from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in Christ.
Confident of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I say.
At the same time, prepare a guest room for me, for I hope that through your prayers I shall be granted to you.
Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends you greetings,
as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
In antiquity, God spoke to the fathers through the prophets in a multiplicity of portions and modes;
yet in these last days He has spoken to us in His Son, whom He appointed heir of all things and through whom He also constituted the ages.

He, being the radiance of glory and the exact imprint of His being, and upholding all things by the word of His power, having made purification for sins, sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high,
having become so much superior to the angels as the name He has inherited is more distinguished than theirs.
For to which of the angels did He ever say, "You are My Son; today I have begotten You"? And again, "I will be to Him a Father, and He will be to Me a Son"?
And again, when He brings the firstborn into the world, He says, "Let all God's angels worship Him."
And concerning the angels He says, "He makes His angels spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire."
But to the Son He says, "Your throne, O God, is forever and ever, and the scepter of uprightness is the scepter of Your kingdom.
You have loved righteousness and hated lawlessness; therefore God, Your God, has anointed You with the oil of gladness beyond Your companions."
And, "In the beginning, Lord, You laid the foundation of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.
They will perish, but You remain; and they all will grow old like a garment.
Like a cloak You will roll them up, and like a garment they will be changed. But You are the same, and Your years will not fail."
But to which of the angels has He ever said, "Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet"?
Are they not all ministering spirits sent out for service for the sake of those who are about to inherit salvation?
Consequently, it behooves us to attend with exceptional vigilance to the tidings we have received, lest we should drift away from them.
For if the discourse promulgated through angels attained firm validity, and every transgression and act of disobedience received a commensurate retribution,
how shall we possibly escape, having neglected so great a salvation, a salvation that, having first been announced through the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard Him,
while God Himself bore corroborative witness through signs, portents, and manifold miracles, together with distributions of the Holy Spirit apportioned according to His sovereign volition?
For it was not to angels that He subjected the inhabited world that is yet to come, the realm concerning which we are discoursing.
But somewhere a witness attests, saying,

"What is man, that You should be mindful of him? Or the son of man, that You should visit him with Your solicitude? You have made him a little lower than the angels; You have crowned him with glory and honor.
You have subjected all things beneath his feet." For in subjecting everything to him, He left nothing outside his dominion; yet at present we do not behold all things as having been subjected to him.

But we do behold Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor on account of His having suffered death, so that, by the grace of God, He might taste death on behalf of all.

For it was eminently fitting for Him—for whom all things exist and through whom all things are accomplished—in bringing many sons to glory, to perfect through sufferings the pioneer of their salvation.
For both the One who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all of one origin; for which cause He is not ashamed to call them brothers,
saying, "I will proclaim Your name to My brothers; in the midst of the assembly I will sing hymns of praise to You."
And again, "I will place My confidence in Him." And again, "Behold, I and the children whom God has bestowed upon Me."

Since, then, the children are participants in flesh and blood, He Himself in like manner partook of the same nature, in order that through death He might render powerless the one who holds the dominion of death—that is, the devil—
and might emancipate those who, through dread of death, had been held in bondage throughout the entirety of their lives.
For assuredly He does not assist angels, but He assists the offspring of Abraham.

Therefore it was incumbent upon Him to be made like His brothers in every respect, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in the things pertaining to God, to make propitiation for the sins of the people.
For because He Himself has suffered, having been subjected to temptation, He is able to succor those who are being tempted.
Consequently, holy brothers, fellow participants in a heavenly summons, fix your attention upon Jesus, the apostle and high priest of our confession,
who proved faithful to Him who appointed Him, even as Moses was throughout His entire household.
For this One has been deemed worthy of glory surpassing that of Moses, inasmuch as the founder of a household commands greater esteem than the household itself.
For every dwelling is constructed by someone, yet the Architect of all things is God.
Indeed, Moses was faithful throughout God's household as a servant, bearing witness to the things destined to be declared afterward,
whereas Christ is faithful as a Son over His household; and we ourselves constitute that household, provided we retain our boldness and the exultation of our hope steadfast to the end.
Accordingly, as the Holy Spirit declares, "Today, if you heed His voice,
do not harden your hearts as in the provocation, on the day of trial in the wilderness,
where your fathers tested Me and tried Me, and beheld My works for forty years.
Therefore I was indignant with that generation, and I said, 'They are perpetually wandering in their heart; they have not come to know My ways.'
Hence I swore in My wrath, 'They shall not enter My rest.'"
Take heed, brothers, lest an evil heart of unbelief should arise in any one of you, turning away from the living God.
Rather, exhort one another day by day, as long as it is called 'Today,' so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
For we have become partakers of Christ, if we hold fast the beginning of our confidence firm to the end,
as it is said, "Today, if you heed His voice, do not harden your hearts as in the provocation."
For who, after hearing, rebelled? Was it not indeed all those who came out of Egypt under Moses?
And with whom was He indignant for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose carcasses fell in the wilderness?
And to whom did He swear that they should not enter His rest, if not to the disobedient?
Thus we perceive that they were unable to enter because of unbelief.
Therefore, since the promise of entering His rest still stands, let us fear lest any of you should seem to have fallen short of it.
For we too have had good news proclaimed to us, just as they did; yet the word that was heard did not profit them, because those who heard it did not unite it with faith.
For we who have believed are entering that rest, just as He has said, “As I swore in My wrath, they shall not enter My rest,” although His works were finished from the foundation of the world.
For somewhere He has spoken concerning the seventh day in this way: “And God rested on the seventh day from all His works.”
And again in this passage: “They shall not enter My rest.”
Since, then, it remains for some to enter it, and those to whom the good news was first proclaimed did not enter because of disobedience,
He again designates a certain day, calling it “Today,” when, long afterward, He speaks through David, as has been said beforehand: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.”
For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not afterward speak of another day.
So there remains a Sabbath rest for the people of God.
For whoever has entered His rest has himself also ceased from his works, just as God ceased from His.
Let us therefore strive to enter that rest, so that no one may fall by following the same pattern of disobedience.
For the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing to the division of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
And no creature is hidden from His sight, but all things are naked and exposed to the eyes of Him to whom we must give account.
Therefore, since we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens—Jesus, the Son of God—let us hold fast our confession.
For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but One who has been tempted in every respect as we are, yet without sin.
Let us then approach the throne of grace with boldness, that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.
Indeed, every high priest is appointed from among human beings and acts on their behalf in matters relating to God, so that he may present both gifts and sacrifices for sins.
He is able to deal gently with those who are ignorant and astray, since he himself is likewise encompassed by weakness.
Consequently, he is obligated to offer sacrifices for sins on his own behalf as well as on behalf of the people.
Moreover, no one arrogates this honor to himself; rather, one receives it only when summoned by God, just as Aaron was.
In like manner, Christ did not arrogate to Himself the glory of becoming High Priest; instead, He was so designated by the One who declared to Him, "You are My Son; today I have begotten You."
And, as He likewise declares in another place, "You are a Priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek."

During the days of His earthly flesh, He offered up prayers and entreaties, accompanied by vehement cries and tears, to the One who was able to save Him from death; and He was heard on account of His reverence.
Although He was the Son, He learned obedience through the things He suffered.
And, having been made perfect, He became the source of eternal salvation for all who obey Him,
having been designated by God a High Priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
Concerning Him we have a great deal to say, and it is difficult to articulate, since you have become sluggish in hearing.
For though by this time you ought to be teachers, you have need again for someone to teach you the elementary principles of the oracles of God, and you have come to need milk and not solid food.
For everyone who partakes of milk is unskilled in the word of righteousness, for he is an infant.
But solid food belongs to the mature, whose faculties, through habitual exercise, have been trained to distinguish good from evil.

Therefore, leaving behind the elementary teaching concerning Christ, let us be carried onward toward maturity, without repeatedly laying a foundation of repentance from dead works and faith toward God,
of instruction concerning baptisms, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
And this we shall do, if God permits.
For it is impossible, in the case of those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift and have become partakers of the Holy Spirit,
who have tasted the good word of God and the powers of the age to come,
and then have fallen away, to renew them again to repentance, since they are crucifying the Son of God afresh for themselves and holding Him up to public contempt.
For land that has drunk the rain frequently falling upon it and brings forth vegetation useful to those for whose sake it is cultivated receives blessing from God;
but if it bears thorns and thistles, it is worthless and near to being cursed, and its end is to be burned.
But although we speak in this way, beloved, we are convinced of better things concerning you—things that accompany salvation.
For God is not so unjust as to forget your work and the love that you showed for His name in having served and in continuing to serve the saints.
And we desire that each one of you show the same earnestness so as to realize the full assurance of hope to the end,
in order that you may not become indolent but may become imitators of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
For when God made a promise to Abraham, since He had no one greater by whom to swear, He swore by Himself,
saying, “Surely I will bless you abundantly and multiply you greatly.”
And thus, having patiently endured, he obtained the promise.
For people swear by the greater, and an oath is for them a confirmation that puts an end to every dispute.
In the same way, when God desired to show more abundantly to the heirs of the promise the unchangeableness of His purpose, He guaranteed it with an oath,
so that by two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled for refuge may have strong encouragement to seize the hope set before us.
We have this hope as an anchor of the soul, both sure and steadfast, which enters into the inner sanctuary beyond the veil,
where Jesus has entered as a forerunner on our behalf, having become a high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
For this Melchizedek—king of Salem, priest of the Most High God—who encountered Abraham as he returned from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,
and to whom Abraham apportioned a tenth of all things, is first, by interpretation, “King of Righteousness,” and thereafter also “King of Salem,” that is, “King of Peace”;
bereft of father, mother, and genealogy, having neither commencement of days nor consummation of life, but rendered like unto the Son of God, he abides a priest in perpetuity.
Now contemplate the magnitude of this figure, to whom even the patriarch Abraham tendered a tenth of the spoils.
For those among the sons of Levi who receive the priesthood possess, according to the law, a mandate to tithe the people—that is, their brethren—although they too have issued from Abraham’s loins;
yet this One, whose lineage is not reckoned from among them, tithed Abraham and blessed him who possessed the promises.
And it is without any contradiction that the inferior is blessed by the superior.
Moreover, whereas here mortal men receive tithes, there it is attested that he lives;
and, to speak approximately, Levi himself, who receives tithes, was tithed through Abraham,
for he was still in the loins of his father when Melchizedek met him.

Hence, if perfection had been attainable through the Levitical priesthood—for upon it the people were given the law—what further necessity would there be for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, rather than according to the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is transposed, a transposition of the law necessarily follows.
For the One concerning whom these things are spoken partakes of another tribe, from which no one has ever attended the altar;
for it is manifest that our Lord sprang from Judah, a tribe concerning which Moses spoke nothing regarding priests.
And this becomes still more abundantly manifest if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who became such not according to a law of carnal commandment but according to the power of an indissoluble life.
For it is testified, “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For, on the one hand, there occurs an annulment of the preceding commandment by reason of its infirmity and uselessness—for the law perfected nothing—and,
on the other hand, an introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And inasmuch as this was not without an oath—for those who formerly became priests were made so without an oath—
but He with an oath through the One saying to Him, “The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind: You are a priest forever”—
by so much also Jesus has become the surety of a better covenant.
Furthermore, there have been many priests, because death hindered them from remaining;
but He, because He abides forever, possesses an untransferable priesthood,
whence He is able to save to the uttermost those who approach God through Him, since He ever lives to make intercession for them.
For such a High Priest was befitting for us: holy, guileless, undefiled, separated from sinners, and exalted above the heavens,
who has no need, like those high priests, to offer sacrifices daily—first for His own sins and then for those of the people—for He accomplished this once for all when He offered up Himself.
For the law appoints men as high priests who possess infirmity, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son who has been perfected forever.
The cardinal point, then, of what we are asserting is this: we possess a high priest of such a kind, who has taken His seat at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
and who ministers in the sanctuary and in the true tabernacle that the Lord erected, not a human being.
For every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices; hence it is necessary that this one also have something to offer.
Now if He were on earth, He would not be a priest at all, since there are already those who offer gifts according to the law—

those who serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, just as Moses was divinely warned when he was about to complete the tabernacle: “See that you make everything according to the pattern that was shown to you on the mountain.”
But now He has obtained a more excellent ministry, inasmuch as He is also the mediator of a better covenant, which has been enacted upon better promises.
For if that first covenant had been faultless, no place would have been sought for a second.
For in finding fault with them, He says, “Behold, days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will establish a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah—

not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not remain in My covenant, and I disregarded them,” declares the Lord.

“For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days,” declares the Lord: “I will put My laws into their minds and inscribe them on their hearts, and I will be their God, and they shall be My people.
And no longer shall each person teach his neighbor and each his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ for they shall all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.
For I will be merciful toward their iniquities, and I will remember their sins no more.”
In saying “new,” He has made the first obsolete; and what is becoming obsolete and growing old is near to vanishing away.
Now even the first covenant possessed regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tabernacle was prepared—the first section—in which were the lampstand, the table, and the bread of the Presence; this is called the Holy Place.
Behind the second curtain stood a tabernacle called the Most Holy Place,

having the golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant, overlaid on every side with gold, in which was a golden urn containing the manna, Aaron’s staff that had budded, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were the cherubim of glory, overshadowing the mercy seat; concerning these things, however, we are not now to speak in detail.
These arrangements having been thus completed, the priests enter the first section continually, performing the sacred services;
but into the second section the high priest alone enters, and that only once a year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s unwitting sins.
The Holy Spirit thereby signified that the way into the holy places was not yet disclosed while the first tabernacle still maintained its standing,
which constitutes a figure for the present age, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the conscience of the worshiper.
They pertain only to food and drink and various washings—bodily ordinances imposed until the time of reformation.
But when Christ appeared as High Priest of the good things that have come, He entered through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands—that is, not of this creation—
and not through the blood of goats and calves, but through His own blood, He entered once for all into the holy places, having secured eternal redemption.
For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the sprinkling of those defiled with the ashes of a heifer, sanctifies them for the purification of the flesh,
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself without blemish to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God.

And for this reason He is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who have been called may receive the promised eternal inheritance, a death having occurred for the redemption of the transgressions committed under the first covenant.
For where a covenant exists, it is necessary to establish the death of the one who made it.
For a covenant is valid only upon death, since it is never in force while the one who made it lives.
Hence not even the first covenant was ratified without blood.

For when every commandment had been spoken by Moses to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and goats, with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the scroll itself and all the people,
saying, “This is the blood of the covenant that God commanded for you.”
And in the same manner he sprinkled with the blood both the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry.
Indeed, according to the law, almost everything is purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness of sins.
It was therefore necessary for the copies of the heavenly realities to be purified with these rites, whereas the heavenly things themselves required better sacrifices than these.
For Christ did not enter holy places made by hands, which are mere copies of the true ones, but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God on our behalf.
Nor did He offer Himself repeatedly, as the high priest enters the holy places year by year with blood not his own;

otherwise He would have had to suffer repeatedly since the foundation of the world. But now, at the consummation of the ages, He has appeared once for all to put away sin through the sacrifice of Himself.
And just as it is appointed for people to die once, and after that comes judgment,
so Christ, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, not to deal with sin, but to save those who are eagerly awaiting Him.

For the law, though it possesses merely a shadow of the good things to come rather than the very image of those realities, can never, by the same sacrifices that are offered year after year, render perfect those who draw near.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, since the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in these sacrifices there is an annual remembrance of sins.
For it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to remove sins.
Therefore, when He enters the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but a body You have prepared for Me.
In burnt offerings and offerings for sin You took no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Behold, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written concerning Me—to do Your will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and burnt offerings and offerings for sin You did not desire, nor did You take pleasure in them,” which are offered according to the law,
He then says, “Behold, I have come to do Your will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily ministering and offering repeatedly the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.
But this One, having offered a single sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
waiting from that time until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also bears witness to us, for after saying,
“This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days,” declares the Lord: “I will put My laws upon their hearts, and I will write them on their minds.”
“And their sins and their lawless deeds I will remember no more.”
Now where there is forgiveness of these things, there is no longer an offering for sin.
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence to enter the holy places by the blood of Jesus,
by a new and living way that He opened for us through the veil—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for He who promised is faithful.
And let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works,
not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day drawing near.
For if we sin deliberately after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins,
but only a fearful expectation of judgment and a fury of fire that will consume the adversaries.
Anyone who has rejected the law of Moses dies without mercy on the evidence of two or three witnesses.

How much more severe a punishment do you suppose will be deserved by the one who has trampled underfoot the Son of God, and has profaned the blood of the covenant by which he was sanctified, and has outraged the Spirit of grace?
For we know Him who said, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay,” says the Lord. And again, “The Lord will judge His people.”
It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
But recall the former days, when, after you were enlightened, you endured a great struggle of sufferings,
partly by being made a public spectacle through reproaches and afflictions, and partly by becoming partners with those who were so treated.
For you sympathized with the prisoners, and you accepted joyfully the plundering of your possessions, knowing that you have a better and enduring possession.
Therefore do not throw away your confidence, which has a great reward.
For you have need of endurance, so that, having done the will of God, you may receive the promise.
For yet “a very little while, and the Coming One will come and will not delay.
But My righteous one shall live by faith; and if he shrinks back, My soul takes no pleasure in him.”
But we are not of those who shrink back to destruction, but of those who have faith to the preserving of the soul.
Now faith is the hypostatic reality of things hoped for and the rigorous demonstration of realities unseen.
For by it the elders received their attestation.
By faith we apprehend that the ages were divinely framed by the utterance of God, so that what is visible did not come into being from things apparent.

By faith Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, through which he was attested to be righteous, God Himself bearing witness to his gifts; and through that faith he still speaks, although he is dead.
By faith Enoch was translated so that he should not see death, and he was not found, because God had translated him; for before his translation he had been attested to have pleased God.
And without faith it is impossible to please Him, for whoever approaches God must believe that He exists and that He becomes a rewarder of those who diligently seek Him.

By faith Noah, having been warned concerning things not yet seen, moved with reverent fear, prepared an ark for the salvation of his household, by which he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness that is according to faith.
By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out to a place that he was to receive as an inheritance, obeyed and went out, not knowing where he was going.
By faith he sojourned in the land of promise as in a foreign country, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, fellow heirs of the same promise;
for he was looking forward to the city that has foundations, whose architect and builder is God.
By faith Sarah herself, though barren and past the season of age, received power to conceive seed, because she judged Him faithful who had promised.
Therefore from one man—and he, moreover, as good as dead—there were born descendants as numerous as the stars of heaven and as innumerable as the sand upon the seashore.
All these died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them and greeted them from afar, and having confessed that they were strangers and sojourners upon the earth.
For those who speak in this manner make it manifest that they are seeking a homeland.
And if indeed they had been mindful of that country from which they had gone out, they would have had opportunity to return;
but now they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God, for He has prepared for them a city.
By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac, and he who had received the promises offered up his only begotten son,
concerning whom it had been spoken, "In Isaac shall your seed be called,"
having reasoned that God is able to raise up even from the dead, from which he also received him back in a figure.
By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.
By faith Jacob, as he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff.
By faith Joseph, when he was dying, made mention of the exodus of the sons of Israel and gave commandment concerning his bones.
By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they were not afraid of the king's decree.
By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter,
choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God than to enjoy the passing pleasures of sin,
esteeming the reproach borne for Christ greater riches than the treasures of Egypt; for he looked to the recompense.
By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king, for he endured as seeing Him who is invisible.
By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, lest the destroyer of the firstborn should touch them.
By faith they passed through the Red Sea as through dry land, but the Egyptians, when they attempted to do so, were swallowed up.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they had been encircled for seven days.
By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who were disobedient, having received the spies with peace.
And what more shall I say? For time will fail me if I recount Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets,
who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,
quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were strengthened out of weakness, became mighty in war, and put to flight foreign armies.
Women received back their dead by resurrection; and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance, that they might obtain a better resurrection.
Others experienced trial of mockings and scourgings, yes, moreover of bonds and imprisonment.

They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were slain with the sword; they went about in sheepskins and goatskins, being destitute, afflicted, and mistreated—of whom the world was not worthy—wandering in deserts and mountains and in dens and caves of the earth.
of whom the world was not worthy—wandering in deserts and mountains and in dens and caves of the earth.
And all these, having been attested through faith, did not receive the promise,
since God had foreseen something better concerning us, that they should not be made perfect apart from us.
Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight and the sin that so easily entangles, and let us run with endurance the race set before us,
fixing our eyes on Jesus, the Author and Perfecter of our faith, who, for the joy set before Him, endured the cross, despising the shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
Consider Him who endured such hostility from sinners against Himself, so that you may not grow weary and lose heart.
You have not yet resisted to the point of shedding blood in your struggle against sin.
And you have forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not regard lightly the discipline of the Lord, nor lose heart when you are rebuked by Him;
for the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and He chastises every son whom He receives.”
If you endure discipline, God is dealing with you as sons; for what son is there whom a father does not discipline?
If you are without discipline, in which all have shared, then you are illegitimate children and not sons.
Moreover, we had earthly fathers to discipline us, and we respected them; should we not much more be subject to the Father of spirits and live?
For they disciplined us for a short time as seemed best to them, but He disciplines us for our good, that we may share His holiness.
No discipline seems pleasant at the time, but painful; yet afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
Therefore strengthen the hands that hang down and the feeble knees,
and make straight paths for your feet, so that the lame may not be put out of joint but rather healed.
Pursue peace with everyone, and holiness, without which no one will see the Lord.
See to it that no one falls short of the grace of God, and that no root of bitterness springs up to cause trouble and defile many.
See that no one is sexually immoral or profane like Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal.
For you know that afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected; for he found no opportunity for repentance, though he sought it with tears.
For you have not come to a mountain that can be touched, blazing with fire, and to darkness, gloom, and storm,
and to the blast of a trumpet and the sound of words, which those who heard begged that no further word be added to them.
For they could not bear what was commanded: “If even a beast touches the mountain, it shall be stoned.”
The spectacle was so terrifying that Moses said, “I am terrified and trembling.”
But you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to innumerable angels in festal gathering,
and to the assembly of the firstborn enrolled in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of the righteous made perfect,
and to Jesus, the Mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.
See that you do not refuse Him who speaks. For if they did not escape when they refused Him who warned them on earth, how much less will we escape if we turn away from Him who warns from heaven?
His voice then shook the earth, but now He has promised, saying, “Yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also the heaven.”
The phrase “Yet once more” signifies the removal of the things that are shaken—that is, the things that have been made—so that the things that cannot be shaken may remain.
Therefore, since we are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us be thankful, and through that grace serve God acceptably with reverence and awe;
for our God is a consuming fire.
Do not be remiss in hospitality, for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.
Remember the imprisoned as though you were shackled alongside them, and the maltreated as though you yourselves were sharing their suffering.
Let marriage be held in honor among all, and let the marriage bed remain undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers.
Keep your conduct free from avarice and be content with what you have, for God Himself has said, “Never will I leave you; never will I forsake you.”
Hence we may say with confidence, “The Lord is my helper; I shall not fear. What can man do to me?”
Remember your leaders, who proclaimed to you the word of God; and, contemplating the outcome of their manner of life, imitate their faith.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
Do not be swept away by diverse and foreign doctrines, for it is good that the heart be established by grace, not by foods, which have conferred no benefit upon those who partake of them.
We possess an altar from which those who minister at the tabernacle have no authority to partake.
For the bodies of those animals whose blood the high priest bears into the sanctuary as an offering for sin are burned outside the camp.
Therefore Jesus likewise suffered outside the gate, that He might sanctify the people through His own blood.
Let us therefore go forth unto Him outside the camp, bearing His reproach.
For we have here no abiding city, but we seek the city that is to come.
Through Jesus, therefore, let us continually offer up to God a sacrifice of praise, that is, the fruit of lips confessing His name.
And do not be forgetful of doing good and of sharing, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.

Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they watch over your souls as those who must render an account, so that they may do this with joy and not with groaning—for that would be unprofitable to you.
Pray for us, for we are persuaded that we have a good conscience, desiring to conduct ourselves honorably in all things.
And I exhort you the more abundantly to do this, that I may be restored to you the sooner.
Now may the God of peace, who brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, the great Shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the eternal covenant,
equip you with every good thing to do His will, working in us what is pleasing in His sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
I beseech you, brethren, to bear with this word of exhortation, for I have written to you in brief.
Know that our brother Timothy has been set at liberty; if he comes shortly, I shall see you with him.
Salute all your leaders and all the saints; those from Italy greet you.
James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered throughout the Dispersion: greetings.
Regard it as unalloyed joy, my brothers, whenever you encounter trials of manifold kinds,
for you know that the testing of your faith produces steadfastness.
And let steadfastness complete its work, so that you may be mature and entire, lacking nothing.
If any of you lacks wisdom, let him petition God, who gives generously to all without reproach, and it will be given to him.
But let him ask in faith, doubting nothing, for the doubter is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind.
For that person must not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord;
he is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.
Let the brother of lowly station boast in his exaltation,
and the rich man in his humiliation, because he will pass away like a blossom of the grass.
For the sun rises with scorching heat and withers the grass; its flower falls, and the beauty of its face perishes. So also the rich man will fade away in the midst of his pursuits.
Blessed is the man who remains steadfast under trial, for when he has been approved he will receive the crown of life, which God has promised to those who love Him.
Let no one say when he is tempted, “I am being tempted by God,” for God cannot be tempted by evil, and He Himself tempts no one.
But each one is tempted when he is drawn away and enticed by his own desire.
Then desire, when it has conceived, gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is fully grown, brings forth death.
Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers.
Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of change.
Of His own will He brought us forth by the word of truth, that we might be a kind of firstfruits among His creatures.
Know this, my beloved brothers: let every person be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger,
for the anger of man does not produce the righteousness of God.
Therefore, putting away all filthiness and the abundance of wickedness, receive with meekness the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
But be doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.
For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man who looks at his natural face in a mirror;
for he looks at himself and goes away, and at once forgets what he was like.
But the one who looks into the perfect law, the law of liberty, and continues in it—not being a forgetful hearer but a doer who acts—he will be blessed in his doing.
If anyone thinks himself religious, yet does not bridle his tongue but deceives his heart, that person's religion is worthless.
Pure and undefiled religion before God and the Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained from the world.
My brethren, do not hold the faith of our glorious Lord Jesus Christ with partiality.
For if a man enters your assembly wearing a gold ring in resplendent raiment, while a poor man in sordid raiment also enters,
and you look with favor upon the one wearing the splendid raiment and you say, “Sit here in a seemly place,” and you say to the poor man, “Stand there,” or, “Sit beneath my footstool,”
have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges animated by evil reasonings?
Listen, my beloved brethren: Has not God chosen the poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom that He promised to those who love Him?
Yet you have dishonored the poor man. Do not the rich oppress you and drag you into courts?
Do they not blaspheme the good name that was invoked over you?
If you indeed fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you do well.
But if you show partiality, you commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.
For whoever keeps the whole law yet stumbles in one point has become guilty of all.
For He who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not murder.” Now if you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.
So speak and so do as those who are about to be judged by the law of liberty.
For judgment is merciless to the one who has shown no mercy; mercy triumphs over judgment.
What is the benefit, my brethren, if someone says he has faith but does not have works? Can that faith save him?
If a brother or sister is naked and lacking daily food,
and one of you says to them, “Go in peace, be warmed and be filled,” yet does not give them the things needed for the body, what is the benefit?
So also faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead.
But someone will say, “You have faith and I have works.” Show me your faith apart from works, and I will show you my faith by my works.
You believe that God is one; you do well. Even the demons believe and shudder.
But are you willing to know, O foolish man, that faith apart from works is useless?
Was not Abraham our father justified by works when he offered up his son Isaac upon the altar?
You see that faith was working together with his works, and by works faith was perfected.
And the Scripture was fulfilled which says, “Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness,” and he was called a friend of God.
You see that a man is justified by works and not by faith alone.
And likewise was not Rahab the prostitute justified by works when she received the messengers and sent them out by another way?
For as the body apart from the spirit is dead, so also faith apart from works is dead.
Let not many of you aspire to the office of teacher, my brethren, for you are well aware that we who teach shall incur a more stringent judgment.
For we all lapse in a multitude of ways; yet if a man never stumbles in speech, he is a consummate human being, endowed with the capacity to bridle his entire corporeal frame.
When we insert bits into the mouths of horses in order to secure their obedience, we thereby redirect their entire bodily frame.

Consider, moreover, the ships: though they be of prodigious magnitude and driven by tempestuous gales, they are steered by a rudder of the most diminutive scale, whithersoever the helmsman's volition directs.
Even so, the tongue, though a diminutive member, vaunts itself with grandiose pretensions; behold how a mere spark may ignite an immense expanse of timber.
The tongue, moreover, is a fire—a veritable world of iniquity situated among our members; it sullies the entire body, sets ablaze the wheel of nativity, and is itself ignited by Gehenna.
For every species of beast and bird, of reptile and marine creature, is subdued and has been subdued by the human constitution.
Yet no human being can subdue the tongue; it is an unruly malefactor, replete with lethal venom.
By means of it we bless the Lord and Father, while by the same instrument we invoke curses upon human beings who have been fashioned after the likeness of God.
From one and the same mouth proceed benediction and malediction. My brethren, such incongruity ought not to obtain.
Can a spring yield from a single aperture both the sweet and the bitter?
My brethren, can a fig tree bear olives, or a vine bear figs? Neither is saline water capable of yielding sweetness.
Who among you is wise and discerning? Let such a one evince, through an honorable mode of life, his deeds in the meekness of wisdom.
But if you harbor bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not vaunt yourselves, nor prevaricate against the truth.
Such wisdom is not that which descends from above; rather, it is terrestrial, naturalistic, and demoniacal.
For wherever jealousy and selfish ambition obtain, there one finds tumult and every species of depraved practice.
But the wisdom that is from above is, in the first instance, pure; thereafter peaceable, gentle, tractable, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial and unfeigned.
Moreover, the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who are peacemakers.
Whence arise wars, and whence quarrels among you? Do they not spring from the very passions that wage war within your members?
You covet and yet do not possess; you kill and envy, yet cannot attain; you contend and wage war. You have not, because you do not ask.
You ask and receive nothing, since you ask amiss, intending to squander it upon your pleasures.
You adulteresses! Do you not know that friendship with the world constitutes enmity toward God? Consequently, whoever resolves to be a friend of the world constitutes himself an enemy of God.
Or do you suppose that Scripture speaks in vain when it declares that the Spirit, whom He caused to dwell within us, yearns with envy?
But He gives greater grace; therefore it says, “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
Submit yourselves, then, to God; resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded.
Lament, mourn, and weep; let your laughter be turned to mourning, and your joy to dejection.
Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will exalt you.

Brothers, do not speak evil against one another. Whoever speaks against a brother or judges his brother speaks against the law and judges the law; and if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge.
There is one Lawgiver and Judge, the One able to save and to destroy; but who are you to judge your neighbor?
Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city, spend a year there, trade, and make a profit.”
You do not even know what tomorrow will bring. What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.
Instead, you ought to say, “If the Lord is willing, we will live and do this or that.”
As it is, you boast in your arrogance; all such boasting is evil.
Therefore, to one who knows to do good and does not do it, to him it is sin.
Come now, you who are rich—weep and wail over the miseries that are bearing down upon you.
Your wealth has putrefied, and your garments have become moth-eaten.
Your gold and silver have corroded, and their rust shall stand as testimony against you, devouring your flesh as though it were fire; you have amassed treasure in the final days.
Behold, the wages of the laborers who mowed your fields, which you withheld by fraud, are crying out against you, and the cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the LORD of Hosts.
Upon the earth you have reveled in luxury and wanton indulgence; you have nourished your hearts for a day of slaughter.
You have condemned and slain the righteous one, who does not resist you.

Be patient, therefore, brethren, until the advent of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman awaits the precious produce of the soil, enduring patiently for it until it has received the early and the latter rains.
You too must be patient; fortify your hearts, for the Lord's coming is near.
Do not murmur against one another, brethren, lest you be judged; behold, the Judge stands at the doors.
As an exemplar of suffering and endurance, brethren, take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
Behold, we deem blessed those who have endured. You have heard of Job's perseverance, and you have beheld the consummation wrought by the Lord, that the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.
But above all, my brethren, do not swear, neither by heaven nor by earth nor by any other oath; let your "yes" be yes and your "no" be no, lest you fall under judgment.
Is anyone among you afflicted? Let him pray. Is anyone of good cheer? Let him sing psalms.
Is anyone among you ill? Let him summon the elders of the congregation, and let them pray over him, having anointed him with oil in the name of the Lord.
And the prayer of faith shall deliver the ailing one, and the Lord will raise him up; and if he has committed sins, they shall be forgiven him.
Therefore confess your transgressions to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The petition of a righteous person, being effectual in its operation, is mighty.
Elijah was a man of like nature with us, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain, and no rain fell upon the land for three years and six months.
And again he prayed, and the heavens yielded rain, and the earth brought forth its fruit.
My brethren, if any among you should stray from the truth, and one should turn him back,
let him know that he who turns a sinner from the error of his way shall save a soul from death and shall cover a multitude of sins.
Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the elect sojourners of the Dispersion throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in the sanctification of the Spirit, for obedience to Jesus Christ and sprinkling with His blood: may grace and peace be multiplied to you.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who, according to His abundant mercy, has begotten us anew to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
to an inheritance imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, reserved in heaven for you,
who are being guarded by the power of God through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
In this you exult, though now for a little while, if necessary, you have been grieved by various trials,
so that the tested genuineness of your faith—more precious than gold that perishes, though it is tested by fire—may be found to result in praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
Though you have not seen Him, you love Him; and though you do not now see Him, yet believing, you rejoice with joy inexpressible and full of glory,
obtaining as the outcome of your faith the salvation of your souls.
Concerning this salvation, the prophets who prophesied about the grace that was to come to you searched and inquired carefully,
investigating what person or epoch the Spirit of Christ in them was indicating when He predicted the sufferings of Christ and the subsequent glories.

It was revealed to them that they were serving not themselves but you, in these things that have now been announced to you through those who preached the gospel to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, things into which angels long to look.
Therefore, preparing your minds for action, being sober-minded, set your hope fully on the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
As obedient children, do not be conformed to the passions of your former ignorance,
but as He who called you is holy, you also be holy in all your conduct,
since it is written, "You shall be holy, for I am holy."
And if you call on Him as Father, who judges impartially according to each one's deeds, conduct yourselves with fear throughout the time of your exile,
knowing that you were ransomed from the futile ways inherited from your forefathers, not with perishable things such as silver or gold,
but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without blemish or spot.
He was foreknown before the foundation of the world but was made manifest in the last times for the sake of you.
Through Him you believe in God, who raised Him from the dead and gave Him glory, so that your faith and hope are in God.
Having purified your souls by your obedience to the truth for a sincere brotherly love, love one another earnestly from a pure heart,
since you have been born again, not of perishable seed but of imperishable, through the living and abiding word of God;
for "All flesh is like grass and all its glory like the flower of grass. The grass withers, and the flower falls,"
but the word of the Lord remains forever. And this is the word that was preached to you.
Having therefore laid aside every species of malice, all deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and every form of slander,
as newborn infants, yearn for the unadulterated and rational milk, that by it you may mature unto salvation—
if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is good.
As you come to Him—a living stone, indeed rejected by men, yet chosen and precious in the sight of God—
you yourselves, as living stones, are being edified into a spiritual house, to constitute a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices well-pleasing to God through Jesus Christ.
For it stands in Scripture: "Behold, I lay in Zion a stone—chosen, precious, a cornerstone—and whoever believes in Him shall not be put to shame."
To you who believe, therefore, belongs the honor; but to those who disbelieve, "The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone,"
and, "A stone of stumbling and a rock of offense." They stumble because they disobey the word, as indeed they were appointed.

But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for His own possession, so that you may proclaim the excellencies of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.
Once you were not a people, but now you are the people of God; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.
Beloved, I entreat you, as sojourners and exiles, to abstain from fleshly desires, which campaign against your soul.

Maintain an excellent mode of life among the Gentiles, so that, in the very matter in which they malign you as malefactors, they may, by beholding your good works, glorify God in the day of visitation.
For the Lord's sake, submit yourselves to every human institution—whether to the king as supreme
or to governors as those sent by him to punish evildoers and to praise those who do good.
For this is the will of God: that by doing good you may muzzle the ignorance of foolish men.
Live as free people, not using your freedom as a cloak for malice, but as slaves of God.
Honor everyone; love the brotherhood; fear God; honor the king.
Household servants, be subject to your masters with all reverence—not only to the good and gentle, but also to the perverse.
For this is grace: if, for conscience toward God, anyone endures sorrows while suffering unjustly.
For what glory is it if, when you sin and are beaten for it, you endure? But if, when you do good and suffer for it, you endure, this is grace in the sight of God.
For to this you have been called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you might follow in His steps.
He committed no sin, nor was deceit found in His mouth.
When He was reviled, He did not revile in return; when He suffered, He did not threaten, but entrusted Himself to Him who judges justly.
He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree, that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. By His wounds you have been healed.
For you were straying like sheep, but have now returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.
Likewise, wives, submit yourselves to your own husbands, so that even if some are disobedient to the word, they may be won without a word by the conduct of their wives,
when they behold your pure and reverent comportment.
Do not let your adornment be merely external—elaborate braiding of the hair, the wearing of gold, or the putting on of fine garments—
but let it be the hidden person of the heart, with the imperishable beauty of a gentle and tranquil spirit, which is of great worth in the sight of God.
For in this manner the holy women of former times, who hoped in God, adorned themselves, submitting to their own husbands,
as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord; and you have become her children if you do good and are not intimidated by any terror.
Husbands, likewise, dwell with them in an understanding way, bestowing honor upon the woman as the weaker vessel, and as co-heirs of the grace of life, so that your prayers may not be hindered.
Finally, all of you, be harmonious, sympathetic, loving as brothers, tenderhearted, and humble-minded;
do not render evil for evil or insult for insult, but, on the contrary, bless, for to this you were called, that you may inherit a blessing.
For “Whoever desires to love life and to see good days, let him restrain his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit;
let him turn away from evil and do good; let him seek peace and pursue it.
For the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears are open to their supplication, but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.”
And who is there to harm you if you are zealous for what is good?
But even if you should suffer for righteousness' sake, you are blessed; do not fear their threats, nor be distressed.
But in your hearts sanctify Christ as Lord, always being prepared to make a defense to everyone who asks you for a reason concerning the hope that is in you, yet with gentleness and reverence;
keep a good conscience, so that, when you are slandered, those who revile your good conduct in Christ may be put to shame.
For it is better to suffer for doing good, if such be God's will, than for doing evil.
For Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, that He might bring you to God, having been put to death in the flesh but made alive in the Spirit,
in which He also went and proclaimed to the spirits in prison,
who formerly were disobedient when God's patience waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was being prepared, in which a few—that is, eight souls—were brought safely through water.
And baptism, which corresponds to this, now saves you—not as a removal of filth from the flesh, but as an appeal to God for a good conscience—through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, with angels, authorities, and powers having been subjected to Him.

Consequently, since Christ suffered in the flesh, you yourselves must likewise arm yourselves with the identical disposition, for anyone who has suffered in the flesh has definitively ceased from sin,
so that you no longer live the remainder of your mortal sojourn according to human cravings, but according to the will of God.
