For the time already elapsed has been more than adequate for accomplishing the purpose of the Gentiles, inasmuch as you formerly conducted yourselves in licentiousness, passions, inebriation, revelries, carousals, and execrable idolatries.
In regard to which they are astonished that you do not rush with them into the same deluge of profligacy, and they heap abuse upon you.
They will give account to Him who stands ready to judge the living and the dead.
For this is why the gospel was proclaimed even to those who are now dead, so that, though judged in the flesh according to human standards, they might live in the spirit according to God.
Now the consummation of all things has drawn near; therefore exercise sound judgment and be sober-minded, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer.
Above all, maintain an earnest love for one another, because love covers a multitude of sins.
Show hospitality to one another without murmuring.
As good stewards of God’s varied grace, let each of you employ whatever gift he has received to serve one another.

If anyone speaks, let him do so as one uttering the oracles of God; if anyone serves, let him do so from the strength that God supplies, so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen.
Beloved, do not be astonished at the fiery ordeal that has come upon you to test you, as though some alien calamity were befalling you.
Rather, rejoice to the extent that you participate in the sufferings of Christ, so that you may also be overjoyed and exult when His glory is revealed.
If you are reviled for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory, even the Spirit of God, rests upon you.
For let no one among you suffer as a murderer, a thief, a malefactor, or a busybody in others’ affairs.
But if anyone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; instead, let him glorify God in that name.
For the time has come for judgment to commence at the household of God; and if it begins first with us, what will be the outcome for those who do not obey the gospel of God?
And if the righteous is saved only with difficulty, where will the ungodly and the sinner stand?
Therefore let those who suffer according to the will of God entrust their souls to a faithful Creator while continuing to do good.
I exhort the elders among you, being myself a fellow elder and witness to the sufferings of Christ, and likewise a participant in the glory that is about to be disclosed.
Shepherd the flock of God that is among you, exercising oversight not under compulsion but willingly, in accordance with God’s will, and not for sordid gain but with eager readiness.
Do not lord it over those allotted to your charge, but become patterns for the flock.
And when the Chief Shepherd is manifested, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.
Likewise, you who are younger, be subject to the elders; and all of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.
Humble yourselves, therefore, under the mighty hand of God, so that He may exalt you in due time.
casting all your anxiety upon Him, because He cares for you.
Be sober-minded; be watchful. Your adversary the devil prowls about like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.
Resist him, firm in faith, knowing that the same sufferings are being endured by your brethren throughout the world.
And after you have suffered a little while, the God of all grace, who called you to His eternal glory in Christ, will Himself restore, confirm, strengthen, and establish you.
To Him be the dominion forever and ever. Amen.
Through Silvanus, whom I regard as a faithful brother, I have written to you briefly, exhorting and testifying that this is the true grace of God; stand firm in it.
The fellow-chosen one in Babylon greets you, and so does my son Mark.
Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace to all of you who are in Christ.
Simon Peter, a bondservant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have been allotted a faith of equal honor with ours through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ—
may grace and peace be multiplied to you in the full knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.
His divine power has bestowed upon us everything requisite for life and godliness through the knowledge of Him who summoned us by His own glory and excellence,

through which He has granted to us the precious and exceedingly great promises, so that through them you may become participants in the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.
For this very reason, apply all diligence to furnish your faith with virtue, and virtue with knowledge,
and knowledge with self-control, and self-control with perseverance, and perseverance with godliness,
and godliness with brotherly affection, and brotherly affection with love.
For if these things are present in you and abound, they render you neither idle nor unfruitful in the full knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
For whoever lacks these qualities is blind—nearsighted, indeed—having fallen into forgetfulness of the purification of his former sins.
Therefore, brothers, be all the more diligent to make your calling and election sure; for by practicing these things you shall never stumble.
For in this manner an entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ will be richly supplied to you.
Therefore I shall always be ready to remind you of these things, although you know them and have been established in the truth that is presently yours.
I consider it right, as long as I remain in this bodily tabernacle, to stir you up by way of reminder,
knowing that the laying aside of my tent is imminent, just as our Lord Jesus Christ has made clear to me.
And I shall also be diligent that, after my departure, you may at any time call these things to remembrance.
For we did not follow cunningly devised fables when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we became eyewitnesses of His majesty.
For He received honor and glory from God the Father when a voice was borne to Him by the Majestic Glory, saying, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."
And we ourselves heard this voice borne from heaven, for we were with Him on the holy mountain.
And we have the prophetic word made more sure, to which you do well to pay heed, as to a lamp shining in a murky place, until the day dawns and the morning star arises in your hearts,
knowing this first, that no prophecy of Scripture originates from a person's own private interpretation.
For prophecy never came by human volition, but men spoke from God as they were borne along by the Holy Spirit.

But just as false prophets arose among the people, so too false teachers will arise among you, who will surreptitiously introduce destructive factions, even repudiating the Master who ransomed them, thereby precipitating swift ruin upon themselves.
Many will emulate their licentiousness, on account of whom the way of truth will be traduced;
and in their avarice they will exploit you with fabricated discourses, whose judgment from antiquity is not inert, nor does their destruction slumber.
For if God did not spare angels who sinned, but consigned them to Tartarus, delivering them to chains of gloom to be reserved for judgment;
and did not spare the antediluvian cosmos, but preserved Noah, a herald of righteousness, together with seven others, when He brought a deluge upon a world of the impious;
and condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to devastation, reducing them to ashes, and set them forth as an exemplar for the impious who are to come;
and rescued righteous Lot, who was vexed by the wanton conduct of the lawless—
for that righteous man, dwelling among them, tormented his righteous soul day by day through the lawless deeds he observed and heard—
then the Lord knows how to deliver the devout from trial and to reserve the unrighteous for punishment until the day of judgment.
And especially those who proceed in the defiling desire of the flesh and disdain lordship: audacious and self-willed, they do not tremble as they blaspheme glorious beings,
whereas angels, though superior in might and power, do not bring against them a reviling judgment before the Lord.
But these men, like irrational beasts, born as natural creatures for capture and corruption, reviling what they do not comprehend, shall likewise be corrupted in their own corruption,

receiving the wages of unrighteousness as the recompense of wrongdoing. They account revelry in broad daylight a pleasure; they are spots and blemishes, carousing in their deceptions while they feast with you,
having eyes brimming with adulterous desire and insatiable for sin, enticing unstable souls, accursed offspring, their hearts exercised in covetousness.
Abandoning the straight path, they have wandered, following the way of Balaam son of Beor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness,
but received a rebuke for his own transgression: a mute beast of burden, speaking with a human voice, restrained the prophet's madness.
These are waterless springs and mists driven by a tempest; the blackness of darkness has been reserved for them.
For uttering bombastic vanities, they entice, through the lusts of the flesh, those who have only barely escaped from those who live in error,
promising them liberty while they themselves are slaves of corruption; for by whatever one is overcome, by that he is enslaved.

For if, after escaping the defilements of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein and overcome, their last condition has become worse than the first.
For it would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than, having known it, to turn back from the holy commandment delivered to them.
The true proverb has befallen them: "A dog returns to its own vomit," and "a sow, after washing, returns to wallowing in the mire."
Beloved, I am now composing for you this second epistle, in which, by way of reminder, I am stirring up your sincere disposition of mind,
so that you may remember the words spoken beforehand by the holy prophets, and the commandment of your Lord and Savior, delivered through His apostles.
First of all, you must understand this: that in the last days scoffers will come, walking in derision and indulging their own lusts,
and saying, “Where is the promise of His coming? For ever since the fathers fell asleep, all things have continued unchanged from the beginning of creation.”
For this escapes their notice deliberately: that by the word of God the heavens existed long ago, and the earth was formed out of water and through water;
and by means of these the world that then existed was deluged and destroyed.
But by the same word the present heavens and earth are reserved for fire, being kept for the day of judgment and the destruction of ungodly people.
But do not let this one fact escape you, beloved: that with the Lord one day is as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.
The Lord is not slow concerning His promise, as some reckon slowness, but is patient toward you, not wishing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

But the day of the Lord will come like a thief, in which the heavens will pass away with a roar, and the elements will be dissolved as they burn with fervent heat, and the earth and its works will not be found.
Since all these things are to be dissolved, what sort of people ought you to be in holy conduct and godliness,
looking for and hastening the coming of the day of God, because of which the heavens will be set on fire and dissolved, and the elements will melt as they burn!
But, according to His promise, we are waiting for new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.
Therefore, beloved, since you are waiting for these things, be diligent to be found by Him in peace, spotless and blameless.
And count the patience of our Lord as salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul wrote to you according to the wisdom given to him,

as he does in all his letters when he speaks in them of these matters. There are some things in them that are hard to understand, which the ignorant and unstable distort to their own destruction, as they do the rest of the Scriptures.
You therefore, beloved, knowing this beforehand, take care that you are not carried away with the error of lawless people and fall from your own steadfastness.
But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To Him be glory both now and to the day of eternity. Amen.
That which was from the beginning—what we have heard, what we have seen with our own eyes, what we beheld and what our hands have touched—concerning the Word of life:
and the life was manifested, and we have seen it and bear witness and proclaim to you the eternal life, which was with the Father and was manifested to us—
that which we have seen and heard we proclaim to you, so that you too may have fellowship with us; and indeed our fellowship is with the Father and with His Son Jesus Christ.
And these things we write, so that our joy may be made complete.
And this is the message that we have heard from Him and proclaim to you: God is light, and in Him there is no darkness whatsoever.
If we claim that we have fellowship with Him while walking in the darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth.
But if we walk in the light, as He Himself is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin.
If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
If we say that we have not sinned, we make Him a liar, and His word is not in us.
My dear little ones, I am inscribing these admonitions for you, lest you fall into sin; yet should any among you transgress, we possess an Advocate before the Father—Jesus Christ, the Righteous One.
He Himself constitutes the propitiation for our transgressions—not solely for ours, but likewise for the sins of the entire world.
By this we ascertain that we have attained intimate knowledge of Him: whenever we observe His commandments.
Whoever professes, “I have known Him,” yet fails to observe His commandments, is a mendacious figure in whom the truth does not dwell.
Conversely, whoever keeps His word has the love of God truly perfected within him; by this we recognize that we abide in Him.
He who alleges that he abides in Him is obligated to order his life precisely as that One Himself did.
Beloved, I am not promulgating a novel injunction for you, but rather an antiquated commandment which you have possessed from the inception; this venerable mandate is the very word you have heard.
Yet again I inscribe for you a new commandment—something veracious in Him and in you—because the darkness is passing away and the genuine light already shines.
Whoever professes to dwell in the light while harboring hatred toward his brother remains, even now, in darkness.
But he who cherishes his brother abides in the light, and no occasion for stumbling exists within him.
Conversely, whoever hates his brother inhabits darkness and conducts himself therein; he is unaware of his destination, for darkness has blinded his eyes.
I inscribe this to you, little children, because your sins have been remitted for the sake of His name.

I write to you, fathers, because you have come to know Him who exists from the beginning; I write to you, young men, because you have prevailed over the evil one; I have written to you, little children, because you have come to know the Father.

I have written to you, fathers, because you have known Him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, the word of God resides within you, and you have conquered the evil one.
Do not set your affection upon the world, nor upon the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father does not dwell within him.
For everything that belongs to the world—the craving of the flesh, the craving of the eyes, and the vainglory of life—does not originate from the Father, but is derived from the world.
Moreover, the world is passing away, and with it its desires; yet the one who performs the will of God abides forever.
Little ones, it is the final hour; and as you have heard that an antichrist is coming, so now many antichrists have arisen; hence we recognize that it is indeed the final hour.

They departed from our fellowship, yet they were never truly of us; for had they been of us, they would have persisted with us. Rather, their exodus serves to manifest that not all of them belonged to us.
Yet you possess an anointing from the Holy One, and you all possess knowledge.
I did not write to you on account of your ignorance of the truth, but because you are acquainted with it, and because no falsehood derives from the truth.
Who, then, is the liar, if not the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? Such a person is the antichrist—one who denies both the Father and the Son.
Everyone who denies the Son is devoid of the Father; conversely, whoever confesses the Son possesses the Father also.
As for you, let that which you heard from the beginning abide in you; if it does, you too will abide in the Son and in the Father.
And this is the promise which He Himself pledged to us—life everlasting.
I have committed these words to writing for you concerning those who seek to lead you astray.

As for you, the anointing which you received from Him abides within you, and you have no need for anyone to instruct you; rather, as His anointing instructs you concerning all things—and it is authentic, not fallacious—so, having been taught by it, remain in Him.
And now, little children, abide in Him, so that whenever He is manifested we may possess boldness and not be put to shame before Him at His advent.
If you know that He is righteous, you also recognize that everyone who practices righteousness has been begotten of Him.
Behold what manner of love the Father has bestowed upon us, that we should be called children of God—and so we are. For this reason the world does not recognize us, because it did not recognize Him.
Beloved, we are now children of God, and what we shall be has not yet been disclosed; yet we know that when He is disclosed, we shall be like Him, for we shall see Him as He is.
And everyone who entertains this hope in Him purifies himself, even as He is pure.
Everyone who commits sin commits lawlessness as well, for sin is lawlessness.
And you know that He was manifested to take away sins, and in Him there is no sin.
Everyone who abides in Him does not sin; everyone who sins has neither seen Him nor known Him.
Little children, let no one deceive you: the one who practices righteousness is righteous, just as He is righteous.
The one who practices sin is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. The Son of God was manifested for this purpose: to destroy the works of the devil.
Everyone born of God does not sin, because His seed abides in him; and he cannot sin, because he has been born of God.
In this the children of God and the children of the devil are manifest: everyone who does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is the one who does not love his brother.
For this is the message that you heard from the beginning: that we should love one another,
not as Cain, who was of the evil one and murdered his brother. And why did he murder him? Because his works were evil, whereas his brother’s were righteous.
Do not marvel, brothers, if the world hates you.
We know that we have passed from death into life, because we love the brothers. The one who does not love abides in death.
Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.
By this we have known love: that He laid down His life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers.
But whoever has the world’s goods and sees his brother in need, yet closes his heart against him—how does the love of God abide in him?
Little children, let us not love in word or in tongue, but in deed and in truth.
And by this we shall know that we are of the truth, and we shall set our hearts at rest before Him,
for if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart and knows all things.
Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence toward God,
and we receive from Him whatever we ask, because we keep His commandments and do what is pleasing in His sight.
And this is His commandment: that we believe in the name of His Son, Jesus Christ, and love one another, just as He gave commandment to us.
And the one who keeps His commandments abides in Him, and He in him; and by this we know that He abides in us: by the Spirit whom He gave us.

Beloved, do not accord credence to every spirit; rather, subject the spirits to rigorous discernment, ascertaining whether they emanate from God, for a multitude of false prophets have gone forth into the world.
By this you may recognize the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ as having come in the flesh is from God;

yet every spirit that withholds confession of Jesus is not from God. This, moreover, is the spirit of the antichrist, concerning which you have heard that it is impending and is even now operative within the world.
You are from God, little children, and you have overcome them, because greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world.
They are from the world; therefore they speak as the world speaks, and the world listens to them.
We are from God. Whoever knows God listens to us, whereas whoever is not from God does not listen to us. By this we discern the Spirit of truth from the spirit of error.
Beloved, let us love one another, for love is from God, and everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.
The one who does not love does not know God, because God is love.
In this the love of God was manifested among us: God sent His only begotten Son into the world, so that we might live through Him.
In this is love—not that we have loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as the propitiation for our sins.
Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another.
No one has ever seen God; if we love one another, God abides in us, and His love is perfected in us.
By this we know that we abide in Him and He in us: He has given us of His Spirit.
And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent the Son as Savior of the world.
Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God—God abides in him, and he in God.
We have come to know and have believed the love that God has in us. God is love, and the one who abides in love abides in God, and God abides in him.
In this, love is perfected among us, so that we may have confidence in the day of judgment, because as He is, so also are we in this world.
There is no fear in love; rather, perfect love casts out fear, because fear involves punishment, and the one who fears has not been perfected in love.
We love because He first loved us.
If anyone says, “I love God,” yet hates his brother, he is a liar; for the one who does not love his brother whom he has seen cannot love God whom he has not seen.
And we have this commandment from Him: that the one who loves God should love his brother as well.
Every person who believes that Jesus is the Messiah has been begotten of God; and everyone who cherishes the One who begat also cherishes the one begotten from Him.
By this we discern that we cherish the offspring of God: whenever we cherish God and execute His precepts.
For this constitutes the love of God—that we preserve His commandments; and His commandments are by no means onerous.
For every offspring begotten of God vanquishes the world; and this is the triumph that has subdued the world—our faith.
And who is the conqueror of the world, if not the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?
This is He who came through water and blood—Jesus Christ—not through water alone, but through water and through blood; and the Spirit is the witness, inasmuch as the Spirit is truth itself.
the Spirit, the water, and the blood—and these three concur as one.
If we accept human testimony, the testimony of God is greater still, because this is God's testimony: He has borne witness concerning His Son.

Whoever believes in the Son of God possesses that testimony within himself; whoever does not believe God has rendered Him a liar, because he has not trusted the testimony that God bore concerning His Son.
Moreover, this is the testimony: God has conferred upon us life everlasting, and that life resides in His Son.
Whoever possesses the Son possesses life; whoever lacks the Son of God is devoid of life.
I have inscribed these words for you who trust in the name of the Son of God, that you may be assured you possess life everlasting.
And this is the boldness we possess before Him: that if we petition Him for anything consonant with His will, He hearkens to us.
And if we know that He hears us in whatever we petition, we know that we possess the petitions we have requested from Him.

Should anyone perceive his brother committing a transgression not incurring death, let him petition, and God will grant life to that brother—not, however, for transgressions incurring death. There is a transgression incurring death; concerning that, I do not enjoin him to inquire.
All unrighteousness is sin, yet there is sin that does not incur death.
We know that everyone begotten of God does not persist in sin; rather, the One begotten of God guards him, and the evil one cannot lay hold of him.
We know that we derive from God, whereas the whole world is enthralled to the evil one.

Moreover, we know that the Son of God has come and has imparted to us discernment, so that we may know the True One; and we abide in the True One, in His Son Jesus Christ. This One is the true God and life everlasting.
Little children, keep yourselves unblemished from idols.
The elder to the elect lady and her children, whom I love in the truth—not I alone, but likewise all who have come to know the truth—
on account of the truth abiding in us and destined to remain with us in perpetuity.
Grace, mercy, and peace shall be with us from God the Father and from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.
I rejoiced exceedingly upon discovering that some of your children conduct themselves in the truth, precisely as we received commandment from the Father.
And now I entreat you, lady, not as though I were inscribing a novel injunction for you, but rather the one we have possessed from the beginning: that we love one another.
And this is love, that we walk according to His commandments; this is the commandment, even as you heard from the beginning, that you walk in it.
For many deceivers have issued forth into the world, those who do not confess Jesus Christ as coming in flesh; this one is the deceiver and the antichrist.
Take heed to yourselves, that you do not forfeit what we have labored to accomplish, but that you may receive a complete recompense.
Everyone who advances beyond and does not abide in the teaching of Christ possesses no God; the one who abides in the teaching—this one possesses both the Father and the Son.
If anyone comes to you and does not bear this teaching, do not receive him into your house, and do not extend a salutation to him.
For the one who extends a salutation to him participates in his wicked works.
Having numerous matters to inscribe to you, I was disinclined to do so through paper and ink; instead, I hope to arrive and discourse face to face, so that our joy may be made full.
The children of your elect sister extend greetings to you.
The elder to the beloved Gaius, whom I cherish in the truth.
Beloved, I pray that in every respect you may flourish and enjoy bodily health, even as your soul flourishes.
For I rejoiced exceedingly when brethren came and bore witness to your truth, just as you walk in the truth.
I have no greater joy than this: to hear that my children are walking in the truth.
Beloved, you are acting faithfully in whatever you accomplish for the brethren—and that even for strangers—
who have testified before the church to your love. You will do well to send them onward in a manner befitting God.
For they have gone forth for the sake of the Name, accepting nothing from the Gentiles.
Therefore we ought to receive such men, so that we may become fellow workers for the truth.
I wrote something to the church, but Diotrephes, who covets primacy among them, refuses to receive us.

Therefore, if I come, I will call to mind his deeds, which he perpetrates, prating against us with malicious words; and not content with these, he neither receives the brethren, nor suffers those who would, and casts them out of the church.
Beloved, do not imitate evil, but good. Whoever does good is from God; whoever does evil has not seen God.
Demetrius has received testimony from everyone, and from the truth itself; we too testify, and you know that our testimony is true.
I had much to write to you, but I am unwilling to write to you with pen and ink.
I hope to see you soon, and we shall speak face to face. Peace to you. The friends greet you. Greet the friends by name.
Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, to the called—those beloved in God the Father and preserved for Jesus Christ:
May mercy, peace, and love be multiplied to you.

Beloved, although I was exerting every effort to write to you concerning our common salvation, I found it necessary to write, exhorting you to contend earnestly for the faith once for all delivered to the saints.

For certain men have crept in unnoticed—ungodly men who were long ago designated for this condemnation—perverting the grace of our God into licentiousness and denying our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.
Now I wish to remind you, though you once fully knew these things, that Jesus, having saved a people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who did not believe.
And the angels who did not keep their own sphere of authority but abandoned their proper dwelling—He has kept them in eternal bonds under darkness for the judgment of the great day.
Just as Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them, having indulged in sexual immorality and pursued unnatural desire, are set forth as an example, undergoing the penalty of eternal fire.
Yet in the same way these dreamers also defile the flesh, reject authority, and blaspheme glorious beings.
But when the archangel Michael contended with the devil and disputed about the body of Moses, he did not presume to pronounce a blasphemous judgment, but said, "The Lord rebuke you."
But these men revile what they do not understand, and the things they know by instinct, like unreasoning animals, they use to corrupt themselves.
Woe to them! For they have walked in the way of Cain, have rushed headlong into the error of Balaam for gain, and have perished in the rebellion of Korah.

These are hidden reefs at your love feasts, feasting with you without fear, shepherds feeding themselves; waterless clouds carried along by winds; fruitless trees in late autumn, twice dead, uprooted.
They are wild waves of the sea, foaming up their own shame; wandering stars, for whom the blackest darkness has been reserved forever.
It was also about these that Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied, saying, "Behold, the Lord comes with ten thousands of His holy ones,

to execute judgment upon all, and to convict all the ungodly of all their ungodly deeds that they have committed in an ungodly way, and of all the harsh words that ungodly sinners have spoken against Him."
These are grumblers and malcontents, following their own desires; their mouths speak bombastic words, and they show favoritism to gain advantage.
But you, beloved, remember the words spoken beforehand by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ,
for they said to you, "In the last time there will be scoffers, following their own ungodly passions."
These are the ones who cause divisions, worldly-minded, devoid of the Spirit.
But you, beloved, building yourselves up in your most holy faith and praying in the Holy Spirit,
keep yourselves in the love of God, waiting for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ leading to eternal life.
And have mercy on those who doubt;
save others, snatching them out of the fire; and to still others show mercy with fear, hating even the garment stained by the flesh.
Now to Him who is able to keep you from stumbling and to present you blameless before the presence of His glory with great joy,
to the only God our Savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory, majesty, dominion, and authority, before all time and now and forever. Amen.
The revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to disclose to His servants the things that must shortly come to pass; He signified it by dispatching His angel to His servant John.
He bore witness to all that he beheld—namely, the word of God and the testimony of Jesus Christ.
Blessed is the one who reads aloud the words of this prophecy, and blessed are those who hear and heed what is written in it, for the time is at hand.
John, to the seven churches in Asia: Grace and peace to you from Him who is, and who was, and who is to come, and from the seven Spirits before His throne.
And from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the firstborn from the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth. To Him who loves us and has freed us from our sins by His blood,
and has made us to be a kingdom and priests to His God and Father—to Him be glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen.
Behold, He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see Him, even those who pierced Him; and all the tribes of the earth will mourn over Him. Yes, amen.
“I am the Alpha and the Omega,” says the Lord God, “who is and was and is to come, the Almighty.”

I, John—your brother and companion in the tribulation, the kingdom, and the patient endurance that are in Jesus—was on the island called Patmos on account of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus.
On the Lord’s Day I was in the Spirit, and I heard behind me a loud voice like a trumpet,
saying, “Write in a book what you see, and send it to the seven churches—to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea.”
Then I turned to see the voice that was speaking with me, and upon turning I beheld seven golden lampstands.
And in the midst of the lampstands I saw one like a Son of Man, clothed in a long robe and girded with a golden sash across His chest.
His head and hair were white like wool, as white as snow, and His eyes were like a flame of fire.
His feet were like burnished bronze refined in a furnace, and His voice was like the roar of many waters.
In His right hand He held seven stars, and from His mouth came a sharp two-edged sword, and His face was like the sun shining in full strength.
When I saw Him, I fell at His feet as though dead. Then He placed His right hand on me and said, “Do not be afraid. I am the First and the Last,
and the Living One. I died, and behold, I am alive forevermore; and I hold the keys of Death and Hades.
Write, therefore, what you have seen, what is, and what is to take place after these things.

The mystery of the seven stars that you saw in My right hand, and of the seven golden lampstands, is this: the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches.”
“To the angel of the church in Ephesus write: These are the words of Him who holds the seven stars in His right hand and walks among the seven golden lampstands:
I know your deeds, your toil, and your perseverance; I know that you cannot tolerate the wicked, that you have tested those who claim to be apostles but are not, and have found them to be liars.
You have persevered and endured hardship for My name, and you have not grown weary.
“But I have this against you: you have abandoned your first love.
Remember therefore from where you have fallen, repent, and do the works you did at first; otherwise, I am coming to you, and I will remove your lampstand from its place, unless you repent.
“Yet you have this: you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.
He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who overcomes I will grant to eat of the tree of life, which is in the paradise of God.”
“And to the angel of the church in Smyrna write: These are the words of the First and the Last, who died and came to life:
I know your tribulation and your poverty—though you are rich—and the blasphemy of those who say they are Jews and are not, but are a synagogue of Satan.

“Do not be afraid of what you are about to suffer. Behold, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison, that you may be tested, and you will have tribulation for ten days. Be faithful unto death, and I will give you the crown of life.
He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. The one who overcomes will not be hurt by the second death.”
“And to the angel of the church in Pergamum write: These are the words of Him who has the sharp, double-edged sword:

I know where you dwell, where Satan’s throne is; yet you hold fast My name, and you did not deny My faith, even in the days of Antipas My faithful witness, who was killed among you, where Satan dwells.

“But I have a few things against you: you have there some who hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to place a stumbling block before the sons of Israel, so that they would eat food sacrificed to idols and practice sexual immorality.
So also you have some who hold the teaching of the Nicolaitans.
Therefore repent; otherwise, I am coming to you soon, and I will wage war against them with the sword of My mouth.

“He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who overcomes I will give some of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone, with a new name written on it that no one knows except the one who receives it.”
“And to the angel of the church in Thyatira write: These are the words of the Son of God, whose eyes are like a flame of fire and whose feet are like burnished bronze:
I know your works, your love and faith, your service and perseverance, and that your last works are greater than your first.

“But I have this against you: you tolerate that woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess and teaches and leads My servants astray to practice sexual immorality and to eat food sacrificed to idols.
I gave her time to repent, but she refuses to repent of her immorality.
Behold, I will throw her onto a bed of suffering, and those who commit adultery with her into great tribulation, unless they repent of her works.
And I will strike her children dead, and all the churches will know that I am He who searches minds and hearts, and I will give to each of you according to your works.
“But to the rest of you in Thyatira, to those who do not hold to this teaching and have not known what some call the deep things of Satan, I say: I am not laying on you any other burden,
except to hold fast what you have until I come.
The one who overcomes and keeps My works until the end, to him I will give authority over the nations,
and he will rule them with an iron rod, as when earthen vessels are shattered, just as I received authority from My Father.
I will also give him the morning star.
He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.”
“To the angel of the church in Sardis write: Thus says the One who holds the seven Spirits of God and the seven stars: I know your deeds—you bear a reputation for being alive, yet you are dead.
Become alert and fortify what remains, which is about to die, for I have not found your works complete in the sight of My God.
Remember, then, how you received and heard; keep it, and repent. If you do not stay alert, I will come like a thief, and you will not know at what hour I will come upon you
“Yet you have a few people in Sardis who have not soiled their garments; and because they are worthy, they will walk with Me in white.
Thus the one who conquers will be clothed in white garments, and I will never blot his name from the Book of Life; indeed, I will confess his name before My Father and before His angels
“Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.”
“To the angel of the church in Philadelphia write: Thus says the Holy One, the True One, who has the key of David—He who opens and no one shuts, and shuts and no one opens.
I know your deeds. Behold, I have set before you an open door that no one can shut, because you have but little power, yet you have kept My word and have not denied My name.
Behold, I will cause those of the synagogue of Satan—who claim to be Jews yet are not, but lie—to come and prostrate themselves before your feet, and to know that I have loved you
“Because you have kept My word of patient endurance, I too will keep you from the hour of trial that is coming upon the whole inhabited world, to test those who dwell on the earth.
I am coming soon; hold fast to what you have, so that no one may rob you of your crown

“The one who conquers I will make a pillar in the temple of My God, never to leave it again; and I will inscribe upon him the name of My God, and the name of the city of My God—the new Jerusalem descending from heaven from My God—and My own new name.
Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.”
“To the angel of the church in Laodicea write: Thus says the Amen, the faithful and true Witness, the origin of God’s creation.
I know your deeds: you are neither cold nor hot. Would that you were either cold or hot!
So, because you are lukewarm—neither hot nor cold—I am about to vomit you out of My mouth
“For you say, ‘I am wealthy, I have grown rich, and I lack nothing,’ yet you do not know that you are wretched, pitiable, impoverished, blind, and naked.

I advise you to purchase from Me gold refined by fire, that you may become truly rich; and white garments, that you may clothe yourself and keep the shame of your nakedness from being exposed; and eye salve to anoint your eyes, that you may see.
Those whom I love I reprove and discipline; therefore be earnest and repent
“Behold, I stand at the door and knock; if anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in to him and dine with him, and he with Me.
To the one who conquers I will give the right to sit with Me on My throne, just as I conquered and sat down with My Father on His throne.
Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.”

After these things I beheld, and lo, a portal stood ajar in heaven, while the voice I had first heard discoursing with me—resonant as a trumpet—declared, “Ascend hither, and I shall disclose unto you the things that must needs come to pass hereafter.”
Forthwith I found myself in the Spirit, and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, with One seated upon it.
And He who sat there presented an appearance like jasper and carnelian, while a rainbow, resembling an emerald in appearance, encircled the throne in its entirety.
And round about the throne were twenty-four thrones, upon which sat twenty-four elders, arrayed in white raiments, with golden crowns upon their heads.
And from the throne proceeded lightnings, voices, and thunders; moreover, before the throne burned seven lamps of fire, which are the seven Spirits of God.
Before the throne lay something like a sea of glass, resembling crystal; and in the midst of the throne, and round about it, stood four living creatures, replete with eyes before and behind.
The first creature resembled a lion, the second a calf, the third bore a face as of a man, and the fourth was like an eagle in flight.

And each of the four living creatures, having six wings, was full of eyes within and without; and they rest not day nor night, saying, “Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, who was, and who is, and who is to come.”
And whenever the living creatures render glory, honor, and thanksgiving to Him who sits upon the throne, who lives unto the ages of ages,
the twenty-four elders prostrate themselves before Him who sits upon the throne, and worship Him who lives unto the ages of ages, casting their crowns before the throne, saying,
“Worthy are You, our Lord and God, to receive glory, honor, and power, for You created all things, and by Your will they existed and were created.”
And I saw in the right hand of Him who sat on the throne a scroll written within and on the back, sealed with seven seals.
And I saw a mighty angel proclaiming with a loud voice, “Who is worthy to open the scroll and break its seals?”
And no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth was able to open the scroll or to look into it.
And I wept profusely because no one was found worthy to open the scroll or to look into it.
And one of the elders said to me, “Do not weep. Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has conquered, so that He can open the scroll and its seven seals.”

And I saw, and behold, in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures and in the midst of the elders, a Lamb standing as though it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God sent out into all the earth.
And He came and took the scroll from the right hand of Him who sat on the throne.

And when He had taken the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each holding a harp and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.

And they sang a new song, saying, “Worthy are You to take the scroll and to open its seals, for You were slain, and by Your blood You ransomed for God people from every tribe and tongue and people and nation,
and You have made them a kingdom and priests to our God, and they shall reign on the earth.”
Then I looked, and I heard around the throne and the living creatures and the elders the voice of many angels, numbering myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands,
saying with a loud voice, “Worthy is the Lamb who was slain to receive power and wealth and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and blessing!”

And I heard every creature in heaven and on earth and under the earth and in the sea, and all that is in them, saying, “To Him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be blessing and honor and glory and might forever and ever!”
And the four living creatures said, “Amen!” and the elders fell down and worshiped.
And I beheld when the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures cry out, in a voice like thunder, “Come!”
And I looked, and behold, a white horse; and its rider carried a bow, and a crown was given to him, and he went forth conquering, and bent upon further conquest.
And when He had opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature say, “Come!”
And another horse came forth, fiery red; and to its rider it was granted to take peace from the earth, that men should slaughter one another; and a great sword was given to him.
And when He had opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature say, “Come!” And I looked, and behold, a black horse; and its rider held a pair of scales in his hand.

And I heard, as it were, a voice in the midst of the four living creatures, saying, “A choenix of wheat for a denarius, and three choenixes of barley for a denarius; and do not harm the oil and the wine.”
And when He had opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature say, “Come!”

And I looked, and behold, a pale horse; and the name of its rider was Death, and Hades followed with him. And authority was given to them over a fourth of the earth, to kill with sword, and with famine, and with pestilence, and by the beasts of the earth.
And when He had opened the fifth seal, I saw beneath the altar the souls of those who had been slain because of the word of God and because of the testimony which they maintained.
And they cried out with a loud voice, saying, “How long, O Master, holy and true, until You judge and avenge our blood upon those who dwell on the earth?”

And to each of them was given a white robe; and it was said to them that they should rest a little while longer, until their fellow servants and their brothers, who were destined to be killed even as they had been, should be brought to their full number.
And I saw when He opened the sixth seal, and there came a great earthquake; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the whole moon became like blood.
And the stars of heaven fell to the earth, as a fig tree casts its unripe figs when it is shaken by a great wind.
And the sky was parted like a scroll being rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved out of its place.
And the kings of the earth, and the great ones, and the commanders, and the rich, and the strong, and every slave and free man, hid themselves in the caves and in the rocks of the mountains.
And they said to the mountains and to the rocks, “Fall on us and hide us from the face of Him who sits on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb,
for the great day of Their wrath has come, and who is able to stand?”
Thereafter I beheld four angels stationed at the four corners of the earth, restraining the earth’s four winds, so that no wind should blow upon the land, nor upon the sea, nor upon any tree.

And I saw another angel ascending from the east, where the sun rises, bearing the seal of the living God; and he cried out with a mighty voice to the four angels to whom it had been granted to harm the earth and the sea,
saying, “Do not harm the earth, nor the sea, nor the trees, until we have sealed upon their foreheads the servants of our God.”
And I heard the number of the sealed: one hundred forty-four thousand, sealed out of every tribe of the sons of Israel.
From the tribe of Judah, twelve thousand were sealed; from Reuben, twelve thousand; from Gad, twelve thousand;
from Asher, twelve thousand; from Naphtali, twelve thousand; from Manasseh, twelve thousand;
from Simeon, twelve thousand; from Levi, twelve thousand; from Issachar, twelve thousand;
from Zebulun, twelve thousand; from Joseph, twelve thousand; and from Benjamin, twelve thousand were sealed.

After these things I looked, and behold, a vast multitude that no one could enumerate, drawn from every nation and tribe and people and tongue, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, arrayed in white robes, holding palm branches in their hands.
And they cried out with a loud voice, saying, “Salvation belongs to our God, who is seated upon the throne, and to the Lamb!”
And all the angels stood encircling the throne and the elders and the four living creatures, and they prostrated themselves before the throne upon their faces and worshiped God,
saying, “Amen! Blessing and glory and wisdom and thanksgiving and honor and power and might belong to our God forever and ever! Amen.”
Then one of the elders addressed me, “These who are clothed in white robes—who are they, and whence have they come?”
And I said to him, “Sir, you know.” And he said to me, “These are the ones who are coming out of the great tribulation; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
Therefore they are before the throne of God, and they serve Him day and night in His temple; and He who sits upon the throne will spread His tabernacle over them.
They shall hunger no more, neither shall they thirst any more; nor shall the sun strike them, nor any scorching heat.
For the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne will shepherd them and will guide them to springs of living water; and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.”
When the Lamb opened the seventh seal, silence fell upon heaven for about half an hour.
I beheld the seven angels standing before God, to whom seven trumpets were entrusted.

Another angel, bearing a golden censer, approached and took his place at the altar; abundant incense was given to him, that he might present it with the prayers of all the saints upon the golden altar before the throne.
The smoke of the incense, ascending with the prayers of the saints, rose before God from the angel's hand.
The angel then took the censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and cast it upon the earth; whereupon there followed thunderclaps, rumblings, flashes of lightning, and an earthquake.
The seven angels who held the seven trumpets then made ready to sound them.

The first angel sounded, and there came hail and fire mingled with blood, and it was cast upon the earth; a third of the earth was consumed by fire, as were a third of the trees and all the green grass.
The second angel sounded, and as it were a great mountain blazing with fire was hurled into the sea, so that a third of the sea became blood.
A third of the living creatures in the sea perished, and a third of the ships were destroyed.
The third angel sounded, and a great star, blazing like a torch, fell from heaven upon a third of the rivers and upon the springs of water.
The star's name is Wormwood, and a third of the waters became wormwood; many people died from the waters, because they had been made bitter.

The fourth angel sounded, and a third of the sun, a third of the moon, and a third of the stars were struck, so that a third of them were darkened; a third of the day was deprived of light, and the night as well.

Then I looked, and I heard an eagle flying in midheaven, crying out in a loud voice, "Woe, woe, woe to the inhabitants of the earth, because of the remaining trumpet blasts that the three angels are about to sound!"
When the fifth angel sounded his trumpet, I beheld a star that had fallen from heaven to earth, and to it was given the key to the shaft of the abyss.
It opened the shaft of the abyss, and smoke ascended from the shaft like the smoke of a great furnace, so that the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke rising from the shaft.
Out of the smoke came locusts upon the earth, and to them was granted authority commensurate with that possessed by the scorpions of the earth.
They were instructed not to harm the grass of the earth, nor any green plant, nor any tree, but only those human beings who do not bear the seal of God upon their foreheads.
They were not permitted to kill them; rather, they were to torment them for five months, and their torment was like the torment inflicted when a scorpion strikes a person.
In those days people will seek death and will not find it; they will long to die, and death will flee from them.
The locusts resembled horses prepared for battle; upon their heads were something like golden crowns, and their faces were like human faces.
They had hair like women's hair, and their teeth were like lions' teeth.
They wore breastplates like iron breastplates, and the sound of their wings was like the sound of many horses and chariots rushing into battle.
They had tails and stings like scorpions, and in their tails lay their power to harm people for five months.
They have over them a king, the angel of the abyss, whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon and in Greek is Apollyon.
The first woe has passed; two more woes are still to come.
When the sixth angel sounded his trumpet, I heard a voice from the four horns of the golden altar before God,
saying to the sixth angel who held the trumpet, "Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates."
So the four angels, who had been prepared for that hour, day, month, and year, were released in order to kill a third of humanity.
The number of the mounted troops was two hundred million; I heard their number.

And this is how I saw the horses and their riders in the vision: they had breastplates of fire, hyacinth, and sulfur; the horses' heads were like lions' heads; and from their mouths came fire, smoke, and sulfur.
A third of humanity was killed by these three plagues—by the fire, the smoke, and the sulfur that issued from their mouths.
For the power of the horses resides in their mouths and in their tails, for their tails are like serpents with heads, and with them they inflict injury.

The rest of humanity, who were not killed by these plagues, did not repent of the works of their hands—namely, their worship of demons and idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood, which cannot see or hear or walk.
Nor did they repent of their murders, their sorceries, their sexual immorality, or their thefts.
Then I saw another mighty angel descending from heaven, clothed in a cloud, with a rainbow upon his head; his face was like the sun, and his feet were like pillars of fire.
He held in his hand a little scroll that was open, and he set his right foot upon the sea and his left foot upon the earth.
He cried out with a loud voice, like a lion roaring; and when he cried, the seven thunders spoke with their own voices.
When the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to write, but I heard a voice from heaven saying, "Seal what the seven thunders have said, and do not write it down."
The angel whom I had seen standing on the sea and on the land raised his right hand toward heaven
and swore by Him who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and everything in it, the earth and everything in it, and the sea and everything in it, that there would be no more delay.
Instead, in the days when the seventh angel is about to sound his trumpet, the mystery of God will be fulfilled, just as He announced to His servants the prophets.
Then the voice that I had heard from heaven spoke to me again, saying, "Go, take the open scroll in the hand of the angel standing on the sea and on the land."
So I went to the angel and said to him, "Give me the little scroll." He said to me, "Take it and eat it; it will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be sweet as honey."
I took the little scroll from the angel's hand and ate it; in my mouth it was sweet as honey, but after I had eaten it, my stomach became bitter.
They said to me, "You must prophesy again concerning many peoples, nations, languages, and kings."
I was given a measuring rod resembling a staff, and I heard the command, "Rise and measure the temple of God, the altar, and those who worship within it.
But exclude the outer court of the temple; do not measure it, for it has been given to the nations, and they will trample the holy city for forty-two months."
And I will commission My two witnesses, and they will prophesy for 1,260 days, clothed in sackcloth.
These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth.
If anyone seeks to injure them, fire proceeds from their mouths and consumes their enemies; and if anyone should seek to injure them, he must be slain in that manner.

These have authority to shut heaven, so that rain may not fall during the days of their prophesying; and they have authority over the waters to turn them into blood and to strike the earth with every plague, as often as they desire.
And when they have completed their testimony, the beast that ascends from the Abyss will make war against them, overcome them, and kill them.
Their dead bodies will lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also their Lord was crucified.
For three and a half days, peoples, tribes, tongues, and nations will gaze upon their dead bodies and will not permit them to be placed in a tomb.
And those who dwell on the earth will rejoice over them and celebrate, and they will send gifts to one another, because these two prophets tormented those who dwell on the earth.
And after the three and a half days, the spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet, and great fear fell upon those who beheld them.
And they heard a great voice from heaven saying to them, "Come up here." And they ascended into heaven in the cloud, and their enemies looked on.
And in that hour there was a great earthquake, and a tenth of the city fell, and seven thousand people were killed in the earthquake; and the rest were terrified and gave glory to the God of heaven.
The second woe has passed; behold, the third woe is coming quickly.

And the seventh angel sounded his trumpet, and there were loud voices in heaven, saying, "The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ, and He shall reign forever and ever."
And the twenty-four elders, who sit on their thrones before God, fell upon their faces and worshiped God,
saying, "We give thanks to You, Lord God Almighty, who is and who was, because You have taken Your great power and have begun to reign.

The nations were enraged, but Your wrath has come, and the time has come to judge the dead and to reward Your servants the prophets, the saints, and those who fear Your name, both small and great, and to destroy those who destroy the earth."
Then the temple of God in heaven was opened, and the ark of His covenant was seen within His temple; and there were flashes of lightning, voices, thunders, an earthquake, and great hail.
A prodigious sign manifested itself in the heavens: a woman arrayed in solar splendor, with the moon beneath her feet and a coronet of twelve stars upon her head.
She was gravid and cried aloud in the throes of parturition, tormented by the anguish of bringing forth.
Then another sign appeared in heaven: behold, a great crimson dragon, possessing seven heads and ten horns, with seven diadems upon his heads.

His tail swept away a third of the stars of heaven and cast them to the earth; and the dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, in order that, when she delivered, he might devour her offspring.
She bore a male son, destined to rule all the nations with an iron scepter; and her child was snatched away to God and to His throne.
The woman fled into the wilderness, where God had prepared for her a place, that they might nourish her there for one thousand two hundred and sixty days.
Then war erupted in heaven: Michael and his angels waged battle against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back.
But he was not strong enough, nor was any place found for them in heaven any longer.
The great dragon was hurled down—the ancient serpent, called the Devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole inhabited world; he was cast to the earth, and his angels were cast down with him.

And I heard a loud voice in heaven, saying, “Now have come the salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God, and the authority of His Christ, because the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down, the one who accuses them day and night before our God.
They conquered him through the blood of the Lamb and through the word of their testimony, and they did not cherish their lives even unto death.
Therefore rejoice, O heavens, and those who dwell in them! Woe to the earth and the sea, for the devil has descended to you in great wrath, knowing that his time is brief.”
When the dragon perceived that he had been cast to the earth, he pursued the woman who had brought forth the male child.

The woman was given the two wings of the great eagle, so that she might fly from the presence of the serpent into her place in the wilderness, where she is nourished for a time, and times, and half a time.
From his mouth the serpent spewed water like a river after the woman, to sweep her away with the flood.
But the earth came to the woman's aid and opened its mouth, swallowing the river that the dragon had disgorged from his mouth.

Enraged at the woman, the dragon departed to make war against the rest of her offspring, those who keep the commandments of God and hold the testimony of Jesus. And he took his stand upon the sand of the sea.
I beheld a beast ascending from the sea, endowed with ten horns and seven heads; upon its horns rested ten diadems, and upon its heads were inscribed blasphemous names.
The beast I witnessed resembled a leopard, its feet evoked those of a bear, and its maw was like that of a lion; the dragon conferred upon it his own power, his throne, and expansive dominion.
One of its heads appeared to have sustained a mortal wound, yet the lethal injury was healed, whereupon the entire earth stood in awestruck admiration of the beast.

The populace prostrated themselves before the dragon, since he had delegated dominion to the beast, and they likewise prostrated themselves before the beast, exclaiming, “Who can be likened unto this beast, and who possesses the martial capacity to contend with it?”
To this creature was granted a mouth uttering grandiose and blasphemous pronouncements, together with jurisdiction to act for a span of forty-two months.
It opened its maw in blasphemous imprecations against God, reviling His name, His tabernacle, and those who sojourn in heaven.
Moreover, it was empowered to wage war against the saints and to overcome them, and jurisdiction was conferred upon it over every tribe, people, language, and nation.
All who dwell upon the earth will worship it—everyone whose name has not been written in the book of life of the Lamb, the Lamb who was slain from the foundation of the world.
If anyone is endowed with hearing, let him hear.

“If anyone is destined for captivity, into captivity he shall be led; if anyone is appointed to perish by the sword, by the sword he must perish.” Herein resides the steadfast endurance and the fidelity of the saints.
Then I beheld another beast ascending from the earth, possessing two horns resembling those of a lamb, yet speaking with the voice of a dragon.
It exercises the entirety of the first beast’s authority in its presence, and it induces the earth and its inhabitants to worship the first beast, whose mortal wound had been healed.
It performs prodigious signs, even causing fire to descend from heaven to earth in the presence of humanity.
By the signs it was empowered to perform before the beast, it deceives the inhabitants of the earth, instructing them, “Fashion an image for the beast that received the sword-wound and yet lived.”
It was granted the capacity to animate the image of the beast, so that the image might speak and orchestrate the execution of all who refused to worship it.
It compels everyone—small and great, rich and poor, free and enslaved alike—to receive a mark upon the right hand or upon the forehead,
so that no one may engage in commerce, buying or selling, unless bearing the mark, which is either the name of the beast or the numerical cipher of its name.
Herein lies wisdom: let the discerning mind compute the beast’s number, for it is a human number, and its sum is six hundred sixty-six.
I saw, and behold, the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, accompanied by one hundred forty-four thousand who bore His name and the name of His Father inscribed upon their foreheads.
And I heard a voice from heaven resembling the roar of many waters and the crash of great thunder; and the voice I heard was like that of harpists playing upon their harps.

And they sing a new song before the throne, before the four living creatures, and before the elders; nor could anyone learn that song except the one hundred forty-four thousand who had been purchased from the earth.
These are they who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins; these follow the Lamb wherever He goes; these were purchased from among men as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb.
And no lie was found in their mouths; they are blameless.
Then I saw another angel flying through mid-heaven, possessing an everlasting gospel to proclaim to the inhabitants of the earth and to every nation, tribe, language, and people.
He cried with a loud voice, “Fear God and give Him glory, for the hour of His judgment has come; worship Him who made heaven and earth, the sea, and the springs of water.”
And another angel, a second, followed, saying, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, who has made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath born of her fornication.”
And a third angel followed them, crying with a loud voice, “If anyone worships the beast and its image and receives a mark on his forehead or on his hand,

he too shall drink of the wine of God’s wrath, poured undiluted into the cup of His indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and sulfur in the presence of the holy angels and in the presence of the Lamb.
And the smoke of their torment ascends forever and ever; and day and night they have no rest—those who worship the beast and its image, and whoever receives the mark of its name.”
Here is the patient endurance of the saints, those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.
And I heard a voice from heaven saying, “Write: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on.” “Yes,” says the Spirit, “that they may rest from their labors, for their works accompany them.”
And I looked, and behold, a white cloud, and seated on the cloud One like the Son of Man, having a golden crown upon His head and a sharp sickle in His hand.

And another angel came out of the temple, crying with a loud voice to Him who sat on the cloud, “Send your sickle and reap, for the hour has come to reap, because the harvest of the earth has ripened.”
And He who sat on the cloud cast His sickle upon the earth, and the earth was reaped.
And another angel came out of the temple in heaven, and he too had a sharp sickle.

And another angel came out from the altar, having authority over fire, and he called with a loud voice to him who had the sharp sickle, saying, “Send your sharp sickle and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth, for its grapes are fully ripe.”
And the angel cast his sickle into the earth and gathered the vine of the earth and threw it into the great winepress of the wrath of God.
And the winepress was trodden outside the city, and blood came out of the winepress, up to the bridles of the horses, for a distance of one thousand six hundred stadia.
And I beheld another sign in heaven, great and wondrous: seven angels having the seven last plagues, in which the wrath of God is brought to its completion.

And I saw, as it were, a sea of glass mingled with fire, and those who had triumphed over the beast, and over its image, and over the number of its name, standing upon the glassy sea, bearing the harps of God.
And they sing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying, “Great and marvelous are Your works, Lord God Almighty! Just and true are Your ways, King of the nations!
Who shall not fear You, O Lord, and glorify Your name? For You alone are holy. All the nations shall come and worship before You, for Your righteous acts have been made manifest.”
And after these things I looked, and the temple of the tabernacle of testimony in heaven was opened.
And out of the temple came forth the seven angels who had the seven plagues, arrayed in pure, radiant linen, and girded about their breasts with golden sashes.
And one of the four living creatures gave to the seven angels seven golden bowls brimming with the wrath of God, who lives forever and ever.
And the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from His power, and no one was able to enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels should be accomplished.
Then I heard a mighty voice from the sanctuary saying to the seven angels, “Go and pour out upon the earth the seven bowls of the wrath of God.”
The first angel departed and poured out his bowl upon the land, and a foul, malignant ulcer broke out upon the people who bore the beast’s mark and worshipped its image.
The second angel poured out his bowl into the sea, and it became blood like that of a corpse, and every living soul in the sea perished.
The third angel poured out his bowl into the rivers and the springs of water, and they became blood.
Then I heard the angel of the waters declare, “You are righteous, O Holy One, who is and who was, because You have judged these things;
for they have poured out the blood of saints and prophets, and You have given them blood to drink—they are worthy of it.”
And I heard the altar reply, “Yes, Lord God Almighty, true and just are Your judgments.”
The fourth angel poured out his bowl upon the sun, and it was given power to scorch people with fire.
The people were scorched by the fierce heat, and they blasphemed the name of God, who possesses authority over these plagues; yet they did not repent and give Him glory.
The fifth angel poured out his bowl upon the throne of the beast, and its realm was plunged into darkness; and they gnawed their tongues in anguish.
They blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and they did not repent of their deeds.
The sixth angel poured out his bowl upon the great river Euphrates, and its water was dried up, so that the way might be prepared for the kings from the east.
Then I saw three unclean spirits, like frogs, issuing from the mouth of the dragon, from the mouth of the beast, and from the mouth of the false prophet.
For they are spirits of demons, performing signs, and they go out to the kings of the whole world to muster them for battle on the great day of God Almighty.
“Behold, I am coming like a thief. Blessed is the one who stays awake and keeps his garments, so that he may not walk naked and his shame be seen.”
And they gathered them into the place called in Hebrew Armageddon.
The seventh angel poured out his bowl into the air, and a loud voice came forth from the throne, out of the temple, saying, “It is done!”

Then there were flashes of lightning, voices, and peals of thunder, and there was a great earthquake, such as had never occurred since humanity came to be on the earth—so colossal was that earthquake.
The great city was split into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell; and Babylon the great was remembered before God, that she might be given the cup of the wine of the fury of His wrath.
Every island fled away, and no mountains were to be found.
And great hail, weighing about a talent, fell from heaven upon the people; and the people blasphemed God because of the plague of hail, for its plague was exceedingly great.

Then one of the seven angels bearing the seven bowls approached and addressed me, saying, “Come, and I will disclose to you the judgment decreed against the great prostitute, who is enthroned over many waters.
With her the kings of the earth engaged in sexual immorality, and those dwelling on the earth were intoxicated with the wine of her debauchery.”
Then he transported me in the Spirit into a desolate place, where I beheld a woman seated upon a scarlet beast, a creature replete with blasphemous names and possessing seven heads and ten horns.

The woman was arrayed in purple and scarlet, adorned with gold, precious stones, and pearls; in her hand she held a golden cup brimming with abominations and with the impurities of her sexual immorality.
Upon her forehead was inscribed a mysterious name: BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF PROSTITUTES AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.
I beheld the woman intoxicated with the blood of the saints and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus, and I was seized with profound astonishment at the sight of her.
And the angel said to me, “Why do you marvel? I myself will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her, the one endowed with seven heads and ten horns.

The beast that you saw was, and is not, and is about to ascend from the abyss and is destined for destruction. Those who dwell on the earth, whose names have not been written in the Book of Life from the foundation of the world, will marvel when they behold the beast, because it was, and is not, and yet will come.
“This calls for a mind endowed with wisdom: the seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman is seated;
they are also seven kings, of whom five have already fallen, one is presently reigning, and the other has not yet come, and when he comes he must remain but a short time.
As for the beast that was, and is not, it is itself also an eighth king, and it belongs to the seven, and it is destined for destruction.
“The ten horns that you saw are ten kings who have not yet received royal power, but for one hour they receive authority as kings in concert with the beast.
These share a single purpose and consign their power and authority to the beast.
These will make war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will overcome them, because He is Lord of lords and King of kings, and those who are with Him are called and chosen and faithful.
“The waters that you saw, where the prostitute is seated, are peoples, multitudes, nations, and languages.
The ten horns and the beast that you saw will hate the prostitute; they will render her desolate and naked, and they will devour her flesh and burn her with fire.
For God has put it into their hearts to carry out His purpose, to be of one mind, and to give their kingdom to the beast until the words of God are fulfilled.
The woman that you saw is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth.”
After these things, I beheld another angel descending from heaven, endowed with prodigious authority, and the earth was illumined by the radiance of his glory.

And he cried out with a mighty voice, saying, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great! She has become a habitation of demons, a dungeon for every unclean spirit, a cage for every unclean bird, and a prison for every unclean and abhorred beast.

For all the nations have imbibed the wine of the wrath of her fornication, and the kings of the earth prostituted themselves with her, and the merchants of the earth amassed wealth through the potency of her luxury.”
And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, “Come out of her, My people, lest you participate in her sins and lest you receive of her plagues.
For her sins have been heaped up even to heaven, and God has remembered her iniquities.
Render to her as she rendered, and double to her a twofold recompense according to her works; in the cup in which she mixed, mix for her a double portion.

In proportion to the glory and luxury with which she glorified herself, give to her torment and mourning; for in her heart she says, ‘I sit as queen, and I am no widow, and mourning I shall never see.’
Therefore her plagues shall arrive in a single day—death, mourning, and famine—and she shall be consumed by fire, because mighty is the Lord God who judged her.”
And the kings of the earth, who committed fornication and lived in luxury with her, will weep and lament over her when they behold the smoke of her burning,
standing afar off because of the fear of her torment, saying, “Woe, woe, the great city, Babylon the mighty city! For in one hour your judgment has come.”
And the merchants of the earth weep and mourn over her, because no one buys their cargo any longer:

cargo of gold and silver and precious stones and pearls and fine linen and purple and silk and scarlet, and every kind of citron wood and every ivory vessel and every vessel of most precious wood and bronze and iron and marble,
and cinnamon and spice and incense and perfume and frankincense and wine and oil and fine flour and wheat and cattle and sheep and horses and chariots and slaves and human souls.
And the fruit of your soul’s desire has departed from you, and all the opulent and resplendent things have perished from you, and they shall not find them anymore.
The merchants of these things, who grew rich from her, will stand afar off because of the fear of her torment, weeping and mourning,
